*nix.gloss: Unix and various other similar or compatible operating systems.

.dat.gloss: An extension for a data file.

.ovl.gloss: An overlay file. From the extension for an overlay file. A file used in memory limited systems to overwrite portions of program execution space (code and data) to enable other operations; such as found in 8-/10-/12-/16-bit systems.

1-connected.gloss: Having a singleton as its fundamental group.

10-foot user interface.gloss: A graphical user interface designed for televisions and thus requiring much larger visual elements than those used on computers and smartphones, as well as the ability to be operated by a simple remote control.

10-gon.gloss: Synonym of decagon (“a polygon with ten sides and ten angles”).

100-gon.gloss: Synonym of hectogon: A polygon having a hundred sides.

1000-gon.gloss: Synonym of chiliagon: A polygon with a thousand vertices and a thousand edges.

10000-gon.gloss: Synonym of myriagon: A polygon with 10,000 sides.

1000000-gon.gloss: Synonym of megagon: A polygon with one million sides.

10base2.gloss: An early thin form of Ethernet cable

10base5.gloss: An early form of Ethernet cable

11-gon.gloss: Synonym of hendecagon: A polygon with eleven edges and eleven angles.

12-gon.gloss: Synonym of dodecagon: A polygon with twelve edges and twelve angles.

120-cell.gloss: A four-dimensional polytope, analogous to a dodecahedron, whose 120 bounding facets are dodecahedra.

13-gon.gloss: Synonym of tridecagon: A polygon having thirteen sides and thirteen angles.

14-gon.gloss: Synonym of tetradecagon (“a polygon having fourteen sides and fourteen angles”).

15-gon.gloss: Synonym of pentadecagon: A polygon with fifteen sides.

16-cell.gloss: A four-dimensional polytope, analogous to an octahedron, whose sixteen bounding facets are tetrahedra.

16-gon.gloss: Synonym of hexadecagon: A polygon with sixteen sides and sixteen angles.

17-gon.gloss: Synonym of heptadecagon: A polygon with seventeen sides and seventeen angles.

18-gon.gloss: Synonym of octadecagon: A polygon with 18 sides and 18 vertices.

19-gon.gloss: Synonym of enneadecagon: A polygon with nineteen sides and nineteen angles.

1gl.gloss: Initialism of first-generation language, i.e. machine language.

1mms.gloss: Initialism of one megabyte modem system.

2-3 tree.gloss: A tree data structure whose every node with children (internal node) has either two children and one data element, or three children and two data elements; a B-tree of order 3.

2-3-4 tree.gloss: A tree data structure whose every node with children (internal node) has either two, three or four child nodes: a 2-node has one data element, and if internal has two child nodes; a 3-node has two data elements, and if internal has three child nodes; and a 4-node has three data elements, and if internal has four child nodes.

2-omino.gloss: Synonym of domino (“a polyomino consisting of two squares”)

2.5d.gloss: Halfway between two-dimensional and three-dimensional; typically limited to a two-dimensional plane with only limited access to the third dimension.

20-gon.gloss: Synonym of icosagon: A polygon with twenty sides and twenty angles.

200-gon.gloss: Synonym of dihectagon (“a polygon with two hundred sides and two hundred angles”).

21-gon.gloss: Synonym of icosihenagon: A polygon with twenty-one edges and twenty-one angles.

22-gon.gloss: Synonym of icosidigon (“a polygon with twenty-two sides and twenty-two angles”).

23-gon.gloss: Synonym of icositrigon: A polygon with 23 sides and 23 angles.

24-cell.gloss: A four-dimensional polytope whose twenty-four bounding facets are octahedra and which has no three-dimensional analogue.

24-gon.gloss: Synonym of icositetragon: A polygon with 24 sides and 24 angles.

2gl.gloss: Initialism of second-generation language, i.e. assembly language.

3-2-1.gloss: Following the mnemonic "3-2-1 rule" for data archiving and protection: three copies of a piece of data are created, using two different types of media, and one is stored offsite.

30-gon.gloss: Synonym of triacontagon (“a polygon with thirty sides”).

32-gon.gloss: Synonym of triacontadigon (“a polygon with thirty-two sides and thirty-two angles”).

34-gon.gloss: Synonym of triacontatetragon (“a polygon with thirty-four sides and thirty-four angles”).

3des.gloss: Abbreviation of Triple DES, a cipher formed from the Data Encryption Standard (DES) cipher by using it three times.

4-cube.gloss: A cube in four dimensions or four-dimensional space; a tesseract, 8-cell or octachoron; made of eight cubical cells or eight cubes.

4-gon.gloss: Synonym of quadrilateral (“a polygon with four sides”).

40% keyboard.gloss: A compact computer keyboard that improves ergonomics by omitting the numeric keypad, function keys, etc. and relying on additional modifier keys to access certain functions.

404.gloss: Not found, especially of a web page on the Internet.
An error indicating that a web page could not be found.
To return an error indicating that a web page could not be found.

42-gon.gloss: Synonym of tetracontadigon (“a polygon with forty-two sides and forty-two angles”).

46-gon.gloss: Synonym of tetracontakaihexagon (“a polygon with forty-six sides and forty-six angles”).

4gl.gloss: Initialism of fourth-generation language, characterized by having its own operating environment (e.g., Foxpro, Mathematica, AMPL).

4ktro.gloss: An intro that can be stored in four kilobytes of memory (intended to challenge the programmer, who must write compact and efficient code to achieve this).

5-cell.gloss: A four-dimensional polytope, analogous to a tetrahedron, whose five bounding facets are tetrahedra.

5-gon.gloss: Synonym of pentagon (“a polygon with five sides and five angles”).

5gl.gloss: Initialism of fifth-generation language: a high-level, constraint-based programming language (e.g. Prolog).

5k.gloss: A display device or item of content with approximately 5,000 pixels in the horizontal axis.

6-gon.gloss: Synonym of hexagon (“a polygon with six sides and six angles”).

600-cell.gloss: A four-dimensional polytope, analogous to an icosahedron, whose 600 bounding facets are tetrahedra.

7-bit.gloss: Of a word size or an integer, represented using 7 bits (ASCII).

7-gon.gloss: Synonym of heptagon (“a polygon with seven sides and seven angles”).

70-gon.gloss: Synonym of heptacontagon: A polygon with seventy edges.

8-bit.gloss: Of a word size or an integer, represented using units of 8 bits (1 byte).
Originating from or resembling the art or music of the 8-bit computer era.
Originating from or resembling the art or music of the 8-bit computer era and subsequent eras.
A computer that processes data in groups of 8 bits (binary digits).

8-cell.gloss: A four-dimensional polytope, analogous to a cube, whose eight bounding facets are cubes; a tesseract.

8-gon.gloss: Synonym of octagon (“a polygon with eight sides and eight angles”).

80-gon.gloss: Synonym of octacontagon (“a polygon with eighty sides and eighty angles”).

8514/a.gloss: 8514/Adapter, a video interface card and 4:3 display standard for computers, made obsolete in 1990 by the XGA video standard.

8n1.gloss: Abbreviation of eight data bits, no parity, one stop bit: the most common configuration for serial lines, e.g. EIA-232.

9-gon.gloss: Synonym of nonagon (“a polygon with nine sides”).

90-gon.gloss: Synonym of enneacontagon: A polygon with 90 sides and 90 angles.

96-gon.gloss: Synonym of enneacontahexagon: A polygon with ninety six sides and ninety six angles.

a fortiori.gloss: With stronger or greater reason; as a corollary implied by a stronger claim; even more so; all the more so; so much the more.
With stronger or greater reason; as a corollary implied by a stronger claim.

a posteriori.gloss: Involving induction of theories from facts.
In a manner that deduces theories from facts.

a priori.gloss: Based on hypothesis and theory rather than experiment or empirical evidence.
In a way based on theoretical deduction rather than empirical observation.

a*.gloss: A best-first graph search algorithm for finding a lowest-cost path to a goal.

a/b testing.gloss: The use of a randomized experiment with two variants (termed A and B) which differ in a single particular.

a20 gate.gloss: A gate on x86 microprocessors restricting access to the memory beyond 1 MB.

aa tree.gloss: A form of balanced binary tree used for storing and retrieving ordered data efficiently, a variation of the red-black tree.

aba problem.gloss: In multithreaded computing, a case in which a program erroneously considers the equality of a variable at two times to mean it has never changed in between.

abandonware.gloss: A software product that is no longer updated or maintained, or whose copyright is no longer defended or which is no longer marketed even by the company who made it.

abbreviate.gloss: To reduce to lower terms, as a fraction.

abbreviation.gloss: Reduction to lower terms, as a fraction.

abc.gloss: A keyboard layout in which all keys are arranged in alphabetical order in English.

abc conjecture.gloss: Given coprime positive integers a, b and c, such that a + b = c, and d the radical of abc (the product of its distinct prime factors), the conjecture that d is usually not much smaller than c (in other words, that if a and b are divisible by large powers of primes, then c usually is not).

abduction.gloss: A syllogism or form of argument in which the major premise is evident, but the minor is only probable.

abductive.gloss: Being or relating to a logical process of abduction or inference.

abel polynomial.gloss: Any member of a certain polynomial sequence whose nth term is of the form p_n(x)=x(x-an)ⁿ⁻¹.

abel sum.gloss: Given a power series f(x)=∑ₙ₌₀ ᪲a_nxⁿ that is convergent for real x in the open interval (0, 1), the value lim _(x→1⁻)∑ₙ₌₀ ᪲a_nxⁿ, which is assigned to f(1)=∑ₙ₌₀ ᪲a_n by the Abel summation method (or A-method).

abel-jacobi map.gloss: A construction of algebraic geometry that relates an algebraic curve to its Jacobian variety.

abelian.gloss: Of an algebraic structure (usually a group or algebra), having a commutative defining operation.

abelian algebra.gloss: Any algebra in which multiplication (or its equivalent) is commutative.

abelian category.gloss: A pre-abelian category such that all monomorphisms are kernels of some morphism, and all epimorphisms are cokernels of some morphism.

abelian group.gloss: A group in which the group operation is commutative.

abelianization.gloss: A homomorphism that transforms a group into an abelian group.

abelianize.gloss: to transform into an abelian group

abend.gloss: The abnormal termination of a program.

aberrancy.gloss: The deviation of a curve from circular form.

abliterate.gloss: To uncensor a large language model by modifying specific model internals to remove refusal behaviours or unwanted traits, while aiming to preserve the model's other capabilities.

abliteration.gloss: The process of uncensoring a large language model by modifying internal functions to eliminate refusal behaviors while preserving the remaining functions of the model.

abort.gloss: The function used to abort a process.
An event in which a process is aborted.
To terminate a process prior to completion.

about box.gloss: A window displaying information about an application, such as its version number and copyright or other licence.

abscissa.gloss: The first of the two terms by which a point is referred to, in a system of fixed rectilinear coordinate (Cartesian coordinate) axes.
The horizontal line representing an axis of a Cartesian coordinate system, on which the abscissa (sense above) is shown.

absolute.gloss: As measured using an absolute value.
Indicating an expression that is true for all real numbers, or of all values of the variable; unconditional.
In a plane, the two imaginary circular points at infinity; in space of three dimensions, the imaginary circle at infinity.

absolute address.gloss: A numerical value that identifies a fixed location in real storage in terms of the number of bytes from the beginning, or in a peripheral device in terms of disks, sectors and bytes.

absolute assembler.gloss: An assembler that generates code that uses only absolute addresses.

absolute code.gloss: Code which uses only absolute addresses.

absolute complement.gloss: The set that contains exactly those elements belonging to the universal set but not to a given set.

absolute constant.gloss: A constant that maintains the same value wherever it occurs; such as π.

absolute deviation.gloss: The absolute value of the difference between a given value (such as mean or expected value) and a variate value (usually an observed value).

absolute differential calculus.gloss: Ricci calculus; the rules of index notation and manipulation for tensors and tensor fields, as developed by Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro.

absolute error.gloss: The difference (sometimes defined to be the absolute difference) between the measured or inferred value of a quantity and its true value.

absolute frequency.gloss: the number of data points satisfying something

absolute geometry.gloss: The single (up to logical equivalence) geometry whose axiomatic system is equivalent to that of Euclidean geometry without the parallel postulate or any alternative.
Any geometry whose axiomatic system extends that of absolute geometry (in the singular sense) and neither assumes nor contradicts the parallel postulate.

absolute instruction.gloss: An assembly language instruction that uses only absolute addresses.

absolute loader.gloss: A loader that places absolute code into main memory beginning with the initial address assigned by the assembler. No address manipulation is performed.

absolute mean.gloss: The mean of the absolute magnitude of a function that has both positive and negative values.

absolute path.gloss: A path or address that identifies a file or web page which includes all the information necessary to find the file or web page with no assumptions based on local context.

absolute value.gloss: For a complex number a+bi, the principal square root of the sum of the squares of its real and imaginary parts, √(a²+b²). Denoted by vertical bars |,|.

absolutely convergent.gloss: Of an infinite series, convergent even if the absolute value is taken of each term; a stronger condition than ordinary convergence.

absolutely flat.gloss: Synonym of regular (“a von Neumann regular”).

absolutely summable.gloss: Of an infinite series: such that the sum of the absolute values of its summands converges.

absorber.gloss: A set that, under suitable transformations, can contain any set from a given class within a topological space.

absorbing.gloss: Allowing a process to enter it, but not to leave it.

abstract.gloss: To separate; to disengage. To consider abstractly; to contemplate separately or by itself; to consider theoretically; to look at as a general quality. To produce an abstraction, usually by refactoring existing code. Generally used with "out".

abstract algebra.gloss: The branch of mathematics concerned with algebraic structures, such as groups, rings, and fields.

abstract analytic number theory.gloss: A branch of number theory in which suitable ideas and techniques from analytic number theory are generalised and applied to a variety of mathematical fields.

abstract data type.gloss: A data type defined only by data properties and operations to be performed on the data without any specification as to how the data will be represented or the operations performed.

abstract factory class.gloss: A class that has an abstract method to create an object.

abstract factory pattern.gloss: A creational design pattern that decouples the object creation by providing a group of individual factories by defining an abstract factory class.

abstract harmonic analysis.gloss: A branch of harmonic analysis dealing with generalised Fourier transforms that act on functions defined on Hausdorff locally compact topological groups.

abstract model.gloss: A model that contains an abstraction or abstractions of the reality.

abstract nonsense.gloss: Details which are straightforward but so tedious that an author or lecturer would rather skip them (especially those of a category theoretical nature).

abstract polyhedron.gloss: A type of abstract polytope where the connections between its points correspond to the faces, edges, and vertices of a polyhedron.

abstract polytope.gloss: A partially ordered set that captures the dyadic properties of a normal polytope without specifying its geometric properties.

abstract type.gloss: a type in a nominative type system that cannot be instantiated.

abstraction.gloss: Hiding implementation details from the interface of a component, to decrease complexity through interdependency and improve modularity; a construct that serves as such.

abundancy index.gloss: The divisor function of an integer divided by the integer.

abundant.gloss: Being an abundant number, i.e. less than the sum of all of its divisors except itself.

abundant number.gloss: A number that is less than the sum of its proper divisors (all divisors except the number itself).

abuse of notation.gloss: The use of a mathematical notation in a way that is not formally correct but seems likely to simplify the exposition or suggest the correct intuition.

accelerated graphics port.gloss: A high-speed port used to attach a display adapter to a personal computer.

accelerator.gloss: A computer component using dedicated hardware to accelerate the processing and display of graphics.

accelerator card.gloss: A graphics card with its own GPU and memory, for greater performance.

accentus.gloss: Ambiguity arising when the meaning of a sentence is changed by placing an unusual prosodic stress, or when, in a written passage, it is left unclear which word the emphasis was supposed to fall on.

acceptor.gloss: A kind of finite-state machine whose binary output indicates whether or not a received input was accepted.

access.gloss: The process of locating data in memory.
Connection to or communication with a computer program or to the Internet.

access control.gloss: Permitting or denying the use of a particular resource.

access control list.gloss: A security scheme for file-level security (as opposed to traditional user, group levels, or the somewhat stricter role levels). Abbreviated ACL.

access method.gloss: A method or means, usually a software or hardware component of a mainframe, to access data on an external storage device.

access point.gloss: A device, such as an Internet modem, that permits wireless devices to connect to a network.

access specifier.gloss: A keyword applied to a variable, method, etc. that indicates which other parts of the program are permitted to access it.

access time.gloss: The time interval between the issuing of a request to read data from or write data to a storage device and the completion of this action.
An item of metadata indicating when a file was last accessed.

access token.gloss: An object that describes the security context of a process or thread, such as the user's identity and privileges.

accessibility.gloss: Features that increase software usability for users with certain impairments.

accession number.gloss: A unique identifier given to a biological polymer sequence (DNA, protein) when it is submitted to a sequence database.

accidens.gloss: Synonym of accident (“a property, fact, or relation that is the result of chance or is nonessential or nonsubstantive”).

accidental.gloss: Being a double point with two distinct tangent planes in 4-dimensional projective space.

accordion.gloss: A vertical list of items that can be individually expanded and collapsed to reveal their contents.

accounting machine.gloss: A business machine, generally a combined calculator and printer, that tabulates, adds, subtracts, and totals.

accountless.gloss: Not using or possessing an account.

accumulation point.gloss: Given a subset S of a topological space X, a point x whose every neighborhood contains at least one point distinct from x that belongs to S.

accumulator.gloss: A register or variable used for holding the intermediate results of a computation or data transfer.

achilles number.gloss: An integer that is a powerful number but not a perfect power.

achiral.gloss: Superimposable on its mirror image; amphichiral.

achirality.gloss: The characteristic of being achiral; the absence of chirality.

achromatic number.gloss: The largest possible number of colors in any coloring for a given graph.

acid.gloss: Acronym of atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability, a set of properties that guarantee database transactions are processed reliably.

ack.gloss: An acknowledgement either of a packet or a message received from a network.
To acknowledge a packet or a message received from a network.

acknowledgment.gloss: A response (ACK) sent by a receiver to indicate successful receipt of a transmission (See Wikipedia article on transmission).

acnode.gloss: An isolated point not upon a curve, but whose coordinates satisfy the equation of the curve so that it is considered as belonging to the curve.

acquire.gloss: To sample signals and convert them into digital values.

acquisition.gloss: The process of sampling signals that measure real world physical conditions and converting these signals into digital numeric values that can be manipulated by a computer.

act.gloss: To possess an action onto (some other structure). Examples include the group action of a group on a set, the action of a ring on a module by scalar multiplication, and the action of a group or algebra on a vector space via a representation.

action.gloss: A way in which each element of some algebraic structure transforms some other structure or set, in a way which respects the structure of the first. Formally, this may be seen as a morphism from the first structure into some structure of endomorphisms of the second; for example, a group action of a group G on a set S can be seen as a group homomorphism from G into the set of bijections on S (which form a group under function composition), while a module M over a ring R can be defined as an abelian group together with a ring homomorphism from R into the ring of group endomorphisms of M (which is also called the action of R on M).

activate.gloss: To remove the limitations of demoware by providing a license; to unlock.

activation function.gloss: A function that defines the output of a particular node in an artificial neural network on the basis of its inputs.

activation record.gloss: A data structure containing subroutine state information located on the call stack.

active.gloss: Eligible to be processed by a compiler or interpreter.

actor.gloss: The entity that performs a role (in use case analysis).

actual parameter.gloss: A value supplied to a method or function, as opposed to a formal parameter.

actuator.gloss: The mechanism that moves the head assembly on a disk drive.

acute.gloss: Having all three interior angles measuring less than 90 degrees.

acute angle.gloss: An angle greater than 0 degrees and less than 90 degrees.

acute triangle.gloss: A triangle all of the angles of which are acute.

acute-angled.gloss: Of a triangle: having three acute angles.

acyclic digraph.gloss: A directed acyclic graph, a finite directed graph that contains no directed cycles.

ad hoc.gloss: Independent of previously instated network structure, like routers or access points.

ad hocery.gloss: Arbitrary decision rules sometimes included in artificially intelligent software to simulate the unexpectedness in human reasoning.

ad&d.gloss: Initialism of application development and delivery.

ad-hoc polymorphism.gloss: A kind of polymorphism where polymorphic functions can be applied to arguments of different types, as they can denote a number of distinct and potentially heterogeneous implementations depending on the types of argument to which they are applied.

adaptee.gloss: A class that is converted to another class using a so-called adapter class.

adapter pattern.gloss: A structural design pattern that translates one interface for a class into a compatible interface.

adaptive tile refresh.gloss: A sidescrolling technique for video games, making unusual use of the EGA graphics hardware to minimize redrawing.

adaptive-control function.gloss: That part of a control system that dynamically updates the parameters of an optimizing control function or a direct control function

adbot.gloss: A bot (automated software agent) that displays advertisements.

add.gloss: To perform the arithmetical operation of addition.
An act or instance of adding.

add-on.gloss: A software extension or hardware peripheral that provides additional functions or customization for a core application or system.

addend.gloss: Addendum, any one of two or more numbers or other terms that are to be added together.

additive.gloss: Pertaining to addition; that can be, or has been, added.
Whose operator is identified as addition.

additive category.gloss: A preadditive category in which all finite biproducts (including the empty biproduct, which by definition must be a zero object) exist.

additive combinatorics.gloss: A subbranch of combinatorics that concerns additive problems expressed using sumsets.

additive function.gloss: A unary function that preserves the addition operation; a unary function f such that for any x and y: f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y).

additive group.gloss: Any group, or algebraic object that can be regarded as a group, whose binary operation is called addition and denoted +; specifically: Any (often, but not necessarily, abelian) group whose binary operation is called addition.

Any group, or algebraic object that can be regarded as a group, whose binary operation is called addition and denoted +; specifically: Any of certain algebraic objects (ring, field or vector space, etc., whose definition includes a commutative operation called addition) regarded as a group under addition.

Any group, or algebraic object that can be regarded as a group, whose binary operation is called addition and denoted +; specifically: Any group object (such as a group functor, group scheme, etc.), whose binary operation is called addition.

additive identity.gloss: An element of an algebraic structure, generally denoted 0, which is an identity for an additive operation (generally denoted +). That is, x + 0 = 0 + x = x for any x in the structure.

additive inverse.gloss: The inverse with respect to addition; the opposite.

additive number theory.gloss: The subfield of number theory concerning the behaviour of sumsets (integer sets added to each other elementwise).

additive operation.gloss: An operation, written using the symbol +, that produces the sum of two operands

address.gloss: Direction. A number identifying a specific storage location in computer memory.
Direction. A string of characters identifying a node or range of nodes on a network (especially the Internet), such as an e-mail address, IP address or URL.
To refer to a location in computer memory.

address assignment.gloss: The process of assigning a numerical address to a component of a computer system.

address bar.gloss: A bar in a web browser that displays the address (uniform resource identifier) of the page or resource being displayed.

address book.gloss: A computerized storage area for contact information such as e-mail addresses.

address bus.gloss: A bus that is used to specify a physical address.

address of record.gloss: The SIP or SIPS URI that points to a domain with a location service that can map the URI to another URI where the user might be available, frequently thought of as the "public address" of the user.

address space.gloss: A range of discrete addresses, all the address locations available in a particular, named, subset of a computer's (virtual or real) memory.

addressability.gloss: The capability of a microprocessor etc. to deal with values of a certain size using a single instruction.
The capability of a display surface or storage device to accommodate a specified number of uniquely identifiable points.

addressing.gloss: Any of several methods of locating and accessing information within storage

adele.gloss: An infinite sequence consisting of a real number and a p-adic number for every prime number p, such that all but finitely many of them are p-adic integers. More generally, a member of a self-dual topological ring built on any algebraic number field, and involving in a symmetric way all the completions of the field.

adelic.gloss: Of or pertaining to an adele ring.

adespota.gloss: Literary works not attributed to (or claimed by) an author. (Originally used as a title of collections of anonymous Greek poetry.)

adf.gloss: Initialism of Application Development Framework (of Oracle)

adfected.gloss: Having different powers of the unknown quantity in its various terms.

adic.gloss: Carrying the I-adic topology for some ideal I of the ring.

adicity.gloss: The number of arguments or operands a function or operation takes. For a relation, the number of domains in the corresponding Cartesian product.

adjacency list.gloss: A collection of unordered lists (each representing the neighbours of a vertex) that represents a finite graph.

adjacency matrix.gloss: A matrix showing which vertices of a graph are adjacent to which other vertices.

adjacent angle.gloss: Either of a pair of angles that share a common side

adjoin.gloss: To extend an algebraic object (e.g. a field, a ring, etc.) by adding to it an element not belonging to it and then ensuring closure, for example by also adding all finite power series of the element.

adjoint.gloss: Used in certain contexts, in each case involving a pair of transformations, one of which is, or is analogous to, conjugation (either inner automorphism or complex conjugation).
That is related to another functor by an adjunction.
Having a relationship of the nature of an adjoint (adjoint curve); sharing multiple points with.
qualifiers: of one curve to another curve

adjoint.gloss: The transpose of the cofactor matrix of a given square matrix.
A functor related to another functor by an adjunction.

A curve A such that any point of a given curve C of multiplicity r has multiplicity at least r–1 on A. Sometimes the multiple points of C are required to be ordinary, and if this condition is not satisfied the term sub-adjoint is used.

adjoint functor.gloss: One of a pair of functors such that the domain and codomain of one of them are identical to the codomain and domain of the other one, respectively, and such that there is a pair of natural transformations which turns the pair of functors into an adjunction.

adjugate.gloss: The transpose of the respective cofactor matrix, for a given matrix. One of the factors in calculating the inverse of a matrix. Commonly notated as adj(A), where A is the given matrix.

adjunct.gloss: One of a pair of morphisms which relate to each other through a pair of adjoint functors.

adjunction.gloss: The process of adjoining elements to an algebraic structure (usually a ring or field); the result of such a process.
A relationship between a pair of categories that makes the pair, in a weak sense, equivalent.

A natural isomorphism between a pair of functors satisfying certain conditions, whose existence implies a close relationship between the functors and between their (co)domains; the natural isomorphism, functors, and their (co)domains thought of as a single object.

A natural isomorphism between a pair of functors satisfying certain conditions, whose existence implies a close relationship between the functors and between their (co)domains; the natural isomorphism, functors, and their (co)domains thought of as a single object. A natural isomorphism Φ: operatorname Hom_( mathcal )C(G·,·)→ operatorname Hom_( mathcal )D(·,F·) (where the hom-functors are understood as bifunctors from 𝒟^( operatorname )op×𝒞 to mathbf Set). See Adjoint functors on Wikipedia.Wikipedia .

adjunctive.gloss: The property of two operations x and y, such that ax(ayb) = a, and ay(axb) = a.

adl.gloss: Initialism of argument-dependent lookup, a feature of C++ in which the compiler chooses a function based on its arguments.

adlet.gloss: A small app or active document that can be embedded in a Web page.

admin.gloss: A systems administrator (one who maintains a computer system or network).
To serve as an administrator for or of.

administrate.gloss: the act or function of providing maintenance and general housekeeping for computer systems, networks, peripheral equipment, etc.

administrator.gloss: One who is responsible for software installation, management, information and maintenance of a computer or network.

adminship.gloss: The role of an administrator; administratorship.

admm.gloss: Initialism of alternating direction method of multipliers.

adobe.gloss: Any file, document or program that is associated with Adobe Inc.

adoption.gloss: The transfer from an old system to another (usually better) system.

adorner.gloss: A visual element used to decorate or enhance another element to which it is attached.

adverb.gloss: In the Raku programming language, a named parameter that modifies the behavior of a routine.

advice.gloss: In aspect-oriented programming, the code whose execution is triggered when a join point is reached.
