asa character.gloss: A standard carriage control character added to the start of each line of text to be printed on a line printer

asc.gloss: ASC (“an ASCII-encoded text file”): Ellipsis of ASC file

ascending.gloss: Rising or increasing to higher levels, values, or degrees. (e.g. of a sequence) That causes a sequence to follow an ascending order.

ascending chain condition.gloss: A property of a partially ordered set that states that any increasing sequence of elements must eventually become constant.

ascii art.gloss: A form of computer letter art that uses only ASCII characters.
Any type of text-based visual art in general, even that which uses non-ASCII characters.

asciibetical.gloss: According to the order of the ASCII table, with uppercase and lowercase letters grouped separately.

asciify.gloss: To convert into ASCII or, more generally, into 7-bit data.

ash.gloss: The resultant remaining more stable patterns that emerge from the evolution of a soup or a similarly random pattern.

asl.gloss: Initialism of arithmetic shift left, a type of bitwise operation.

aspect.gloss: In aspect-oriented programming, a feature or component that can be applied to parts of a program independent of any inheritance hierarchy.

aspect-oriented.gloss: Describing a system which has been written so that different subsystems appear to add themselves to the main business logic without that logic having to include them explicitly.

aspect-oriented language.gloss: A programming language that aims to increase modularity by allowing the separation of cross-cutting concerns.

aspect-oriented programming.gloss: A programming paradigm that aims to increase modularity by allowing the separation of cross-cutting concerns.

aspectualize.gloss: To use as an implementation for aspects.

assassin.gloss: An associated prime of a module.

assemble.gloss: To translate from assembly language to machine code.

assembler.gloss: A program that reads source code written in assembly language and produces executable machine code, possibly together with information needed by linkers, debuggers and other tools.

assembly.gloss: A building block of an application, similar to a DLL, but containing both executable code and information normally found in a DLL's type library. The type library information in an assembly, called a manifest, describes public functions, data, classes, and version information.

assembly language.gloss: A programming language in which the source code of programs is composed of mnemonic instructions, each of which corresponds directly to a machine instruction for a particular processor.

assembly programming.gloss: The act of writing human-readable code using a low-level programming language that directly corresponds to a computer architecture's binary machine code instructions.

assembly time.gloss: The amount of time required for a computer to translate symbolic computer language into instructions of a machine language.

assert.gloss: To declare that a condition or expression must be true at a certain point in the source code (in some cases causing the program to fail if it is not, as a safeguard).

assertion.gloss: A statement in a program asserting a condition expected to be true at a particular point, used in debugging.

assertoric.gloss: Stating that which is actual, usually in contrast with modal sentences.

asset.gloss: Any component, model, process or framework of value that can be leveraged or reused.

assign.gloss: To give (a value) to a variable.

assignment.gloss: An operation that assigns a value to a variable.

assignment operator.gloss: An operator that sets the value stored in the storage location(s) denoted by a variable name.

associahedron.gloss: A convex polytope in which each vertex corresponds to a way of correctly inserting opening and closing parentheses in a word of n letters and the edges correspond to a single application of the associativity rule.

associate.gloss: One of a pair of elements of an integral domain (or a ring) such that the two elements are divisible by each other (or, equivalently, such that each one can be expressed as the product of the other with a unit).

associated prime.gloss: An ideal of R which is the annihilator of some prime submodule of M.
qualifiers: of a module M over a ring R

associated prime.gloss: An ideal of R which is the annihilator of some prime submodule of M. If the ring R is commutative, equivalently: A prime ideal of R which is the annihilator of some element of M.
qualifiers: of a module M over a ring R

association.gloss: Any relationship between two measured quantities that renders them statistically dependent (but not necessarily causal or a correlation).

association fallacy.gloss: a formal fallacy that asserts that properties of one thing must also be properties of another thing if both things belong to the same group

association link.gloss: A device that is used to group multiple words or concepts.

association list.gloss: A data structure that associates keys with data; implemented as a list whose members are paired storage locations (cons cells), one element of which (the car) contains the key and the other element of which (the cdr) contains the keyed data.

associative.gloss: Such that, for any operands a,b and c, (a*b)*c=a*(b*c); (of a ring, etc.) whose multiplication operation is associative.
Addressable by a key more complex than an integer index.

associative algebra.gloss: An algebra over a ring (or more narrowly, an algebra over a field) whose bilinear product is associative.

associative array.gloss: An array-like data structure where the indices (called keys) are not limited to integers.

associativity.gloss: The property of an operator which determines how it is grouped with operators of the same precedence in the absence of parentheses.

associator.gloss: A multilinear map, given by [x, y, z] = xy(z) − x(yz), that measures the degree of nonassociativity of a ring or algebra.

assortativity.gloss: The extent to which nodes of a graph link to others of the same degree.

assosymmetric.gloss: (more or less) associative and also symmetric

assumption.gloss: The minor or second proposition in a categorical syllogism.

astonisher.gloss: An exclamation mark, the punctuation mark “!”.

astral plane.gloss: A Unicode plane (range of code points) above the Basic Multilingual Plane; any plane beyond U+FFFF.

astrobot.gloss: a robot designed to work in space.

astroinformatics.gloss: The processing of large amounts of astronomical data

astromathematics.gloss: The branches of mathematics used in the study of astronomy, astrophysics and cosmology.

astrostatistics.gloss: The application of statistics to the study and analysis of astronomical data.

asvs.gloss: Initialism of Application Security Verification Standard, a standard to performing application-level security verifications.

asymmetric.gloss: Not involving a mutual exchange of keys between the sender and receiver.
Of a relation R on a set S: having the property that for any two elements of S (not necessarily distinct), at least one is not related to the other via R.

asymptote.gloss: A straight line which a curve approaches arbitrarily closely as it goes to infinity. The limit of the curve; its tangent "at infinity".
To approach, but never quite touch, a straight line, as something goes to infinity.

asymptotic.gloss: Pertaining to values or properties approached at infinity.
Coming into consideration as a variable tends to a limit, usually infinity.

asymptotic analysis.gloss: Any of several methods for describing and analyzing the behaviour of a system at its limits

asymptotic throughput.gloss: The value of the maximum throughput for a communication network when the incoming traffic approaches infinity, either due to the size of a message or data sources.

asymptotically.gloss: In an asymptotical manner, in the way of an asymptote, toward an asymptote.
As the variable tends to infinity; in the long term.

asynchronous.gloss: Allowing the node, program or thread of interest to continue during processing.
qualifiers: of a request or a message

asynchronous.gloss: Having many actions occurring at a time, in any order, without waiting for each other.

at sign.gloss: The symbol @, used in e-mail addresses to separate the user name from the domain name.

ata.gloss: Advanced Technology Attachment; a computer bus technology primarily designed for transfer of data to and from a hard disk. (Renamed PATA when SATA came into existence to more clearly distinguish the two.)

atlas.gloss: A family of coordinate charts that cover a manifold.
An image or texture containing a number of other images or textures, so as to reduce the cost of loading them separately.

atom.gloss: An individual number or symbol, as opposed to a list; a scalar value.
An integer representing a particular string.
A non-zero member of a partially ordered set that has only zero below it (assuming that the poset has a least element, its "zero").
An element of a set that is not itself a set; an urelement.

atomic.gloss: Unable to be split or made any smaller. Containing a single change, as opposed to involving numerous unrelated changes.
qualifiers: of a commit in a VCS

atomic.gloss: Unable to be split or made any smaller. Lacking logical operators; unable to be made simpler in logical form.
Unable to be split or made any smaller. Such that for every element b>0 there exists an atom a such that b≥a>0.
qualifiers: of a partially ordered set with a least element 0

atomic.gloss: Guaranteed to complete either fully or not at all while waiting in a pause, and running synchronously when called by multiple asynchronous threads.

atomic authorization.gloss: (A digitally signed document containing) published rights with cryptographically verifiable integrity, secured independently of the applications that use them and entities to which they apply.

atomic formula.gloss: A formula which does not have smaller subformulas.

atomic operating system.gloss: A type of system architecture where the core file system is read-only and system updates are applied as a single, indivisible, transactional unit.

atomicity.gloss: The state of a system (often a database system) in which either all stages complete or none complete.

atomless.gloss: Not assigning strictly positive probability to any single outcome.

attachment.gloss: A file sent along with a message, usually an email.

attack.gloss: An attempt to exploit a vulnerability in a computer system.

attack vector.gloss: A path or method used by a hacker to gain access to a target system, such as a computer or network server.

attractor.gloss: A set of points or states to which a dynamical system evolves after a long enough time. That is, points that get close enough to the attractor remain close even if slightly disturbed.

attribute.gloss: That which is predicated or affirmed of a subject; a predicate; an accident.
An option or setting belonging to some object.
A semantic item with which a method or other code element may be decorated.
A numeric value representing the colours of part of the screen display.

attribute-oriented.gloss: Of or pertaining to a technique that adds metadata, or attributes, to program code, which affect the system's semantics.

attribute-oriented programming.gloss: A development technique that embeds metadata (attributes or annotations) within source code to declare behavior or configuration, extending the semantics of a program without altering its core logic.

audio file.gloss: A digital record of sound, such as music, speech, or other noises.

audio mining.gloss: A technique that involves automatically analyzing and searching the content of an audio signal, often for speech recognition.

audioactive.gloss: Being or relating to the look-and-say sequence.

audioboard.gloss: A circuit board used for audio processing.

augmented assignment.gloss: An assignment by which an operator takes a variable as one of its arguments and then assigns the result back to this variable.

augmented matrix.gloss: A matrix obtained by appending the columns of two given matrices, usually for the purpose of performing the same elementary row operations on each of the given matrices.

augmented reality.gloss: The merging of a view of the real-world environment upon a digital image in real time.

augmented sphenocorona.gloss: A polyhedron, one of the Johnson solids, whose faces are composed of 16 equilateral triangles and one square.

auslander-reiten theory.gloss: The study of the representation theory of Artinian rings using techniques such as Auslander-Reiten sequences (almost split sequences) and Auslander-Reiten quivers.

authentication.gloss: Proof of identity required by a user to log on to some network or access some resource.

authoring program.gloss: Software that can combine text with other multimedia to make an integrated package.

authorized term.gloss: A term prescribed by a controlled vocabulary as the one preferable to its synonyms, such as frequency preferable to pitch.

auto-forwarding.gloss: The capability of forwarding incoming messages from one user account to another user account or from one domain to another.

auto-reply.gloss: A feature in e-mail software that sends automatic replies, used for instance when the recipient of a message is on holiday.
A message sent by this means.

auto-shuffle.gloss: A feature that automatically randomly reorders something, such as tracks in a playlist or the cards held in a game.

auto-tagging.gloss: The automated process of assigning metadata, taxonomy terms, or tracking parameters to digital content.

auto-tiering.gloss: The automatic movement of data between storage locations based on how often it has been accessed, in order to optimize performance.

autoabstract.gloss: An abstract (abridgement or summary of a publication) generated automatically by a computer.

autoalgorithm.gloss: An algorithm that is invoked automatically

autoaway.gloss: An instant messaging feature that automatically marks a user as being away if the user does not interact with the computer or device in a set period of time.

autobiographical number.gloss: A number in which the first digit counts the number of zeroes in the number, the second digit counts the number of ones, etc. (i.e. the nᵗʰ digit counts the number of the digit n-1).

autoblock.gloss: (An) automatic blocking (inhibition of a feature etc.).

autoboot.gloss: The automatic booting of a system.

autocapitalize.gloss: To convert (text) to upper case automatically.

autochanger.gloss: An automatic tape loader, for switching automatically between several computer backup tapes.

autoclick.gloss: A software feature that simulates the click of a mouse button.
To simulate a click without direct user input.

autoclicker.gloss: A program that simulates the click of a mouse, typically used to automate commands in a graphical user interface.

autocode.gloss: Any of several early assembly languages.

autocommit.gloss: To commit (“to make a set of changes permanent”) automatically.

autocomplete.gloss: A software feature that predicts the rest of a word a user is typing.

autocompletion.gloss: A software feature permitting form fields, etc., to be autocompleted.
An input or entry produced by such a feature.

autoconcurrency.gloss: The situation where two instances of the same actions occur simultaneously and in parallel.

autoconcurrent.gloss: Exhibiting or relating to autoconcurrency; occurring simultaneously and in parallel.

autocorrect.gloss: A software feature that attempts to correct presumed errors as soon as they are generated.

autocorrelation.gloss: The cross-correlation of a signal with itself: the correlation between values of a signal in successive time periods.

autocovariance.gloss: The covariance of a signal with another part of the same signal

autodarwinate.gloss: To kill oneself in a foolish manner.

autodeletion.gloss: Automatic deletion; the process of autodeleting.

autodependency.gloss: The dependency of the value of a variable on its value at a previous time

autodialer.gloss: malicious software, embedded in a website, that routes dial-up Internet connections to a different telephone number charged at a premium rate

autodifferentiation.gloss: The automatic differentiation of a function by a computer.

autodiscovery.gloss: Automatic discovery, as of newsfeeds for a website or changes to the configuration of machines on a network.

autoequivalence.gloss: An equivalence between an object and itself.

autoescape.gloss: To escape (cause a text character to be interpreted literally) automatically.

autoextend.gloss: To extend automatically (when the allocated storage space is exhausted).

autoextension.gloss: The automatic growth of a data file when the allocated storage space is exhausted.

autofill.gloss: Any software feature that fills in (fields of a form, cells of a spreadsheet, etc.) automatically.

autofocus.gloss: The automatic setting of the focus on an input element.

autoformat.gloss: To automatically prepare (a mass storage medium) for initial use, erasing any existing data in the process, without requiring a prompt from the user to do so.

autoindexing.gloss: The programmed retrieval of words from a document for use in building an index

autojoin.gloss: A type of join from a table to itself.

autokey.gloss: Being a cipher that incorporates the plaintext into the key.

autoload.gloss: To load (data or storage media) automatically.

autoloader.gloss: A mechanical device that automatically loads storage media (such as tapes or disks) into the device that can read them.
A software mechanism that automatically locates and loads classes etc. as required at run time.

autoloading.gloss: The capability of loading and linking portions of a program from mass storage automatically when needed.

autologin.gloss: A feature that automatically logs in to a system.

autologistic.gloss: Pertaining to a logistic model that is based on autocorrelation.

automagical.gloss: Automatic, but with an apparent element of magic. Commonly referring to complex technical processes hidden from the view of users or operators, resulting in technology that "just works".

automask.gloss: A mask created automatically by analyzing pixel data.

automatic.gloss: Automatically added to and removed from the stack during the course of function calls.
Having one or more finite-state automata.

automatic differentiation.gloss: Exact differentiation of functions represented in program code by inspecting the code (as opposed to mere evaluation) and repeated application of the chain rule.

automatic programming.gloss: The automated derivation of a computer program, or program fragment, from a higher-level representation of requirements, behavior, constraints, examples, or intent, with the objective of reducing the amount of implementation detail that must be explicitly supplied by a human programmer.

autometry.gloss: An isometry of a metric space to itself

automoderate.gloss: To automatically moderate (a discussion forum, etc.).

automoderation.gloss: Automatic moderation (of a discussion forum, etc.).

automoderator.gloss: A bot that automatically moderates (a discussion forum, etc.).

automorphic.gloss: Describing a number whose square ends in the number itself; circular.
Of or pertaining to automorphy or an automorphism.

automorphic number.gloss: A number whose decimal representation of its square ends in itself.

automorphism.gloss: An isomorphism of a mathematical object or system of objects onto itself.

automorphism group.gloss: The group of automorphisms of a given set or other mathematical object, with the group operation being function composition.

automount.gloss: The automatic mounting of a file system.

automounter.gloss: A software system that handles automounting.

autonomics.gloss: The use of self-correcting software systems that automatically detect and fix certain types of error without intervention by a software engineer.

autoparallel.gloss: A curve having a parallel tangent vector field.
Having a parallel tangent vector field.

autopartitioning.gloss: automatic partitioning (of a network, database, etc.)

autoplay.gloss: Any software feature that plays (a video, a compact disc, etc.) automatically.

autopopulate.gloss: To populate (a database with data, a form with text, etc.) automatically.

autopopulation.gloss: automatic population (of a database with data, a form with text, etc.)

autoprojector.gloss: A system that carries out autoprojection.

autoprompt.gloss: A prompt generated by a program itself via a previous command.

autoreceive.gloss: A feature (of telecommunication software etc.) that receives automatically.

autoreducibility.gloss: The state or quality of being autoreducible.

autoreducible.gloss: Of a set, that can be reduced to itself by a Turing machine that does not ask for its own input.

autorefresh.gloss: Any feature that automatically refreshes a screen display.

autoregression.gloss: An autoregressive process that is used to model many types of natural behaviour

autoregressive.gloss: Employing autoregression, using a weighted sample of past data to predict future results

autoresolve.gloss: To resolve (a system conflict etc.) automatically.

autoresponder.gloss: A computer program that automatically sends a certain message or messages in response to incoming e-mail.

autorun.gloss: Any feature that runs a program, etc. automatically.

autosave.gloss: A software facility that saves an open document (or progress in a game, etc.) periodically to avoid the risk of data loss.
A copy of a file or document saved automatically by such a facility.

autoscaler.gloss: A system that automatically increases or decreases the resources available to a process depending on need and availability.

autosend.gloss: A feature (of telecommunication software etc.) that sends automatically.

autostart.gloss: A program or application set to start automatically.

autosuggest.gloss: Any feature that makes automatic suggestions to the user.

autotopism.gloss: A full group fixing any ordered pair of components of the spread of a vector space over a prime field.

autotransformation.gloss: A transformation such that the distribution of the mapped values is the same as the distribution of the original values.

autotype.gloss: A function that completes the typing of a field using a prediction based upon the characters entered so far.

autovacuum.gloss: To vacuum (physically remove deleted tuples from) a table or database automatically.

autovector.gloss: An interrupt vector representing a priority level, from which the processor determines the actual target address.

autovivify.gloss: In the Perl programming language, to create an array or hash automatically when a previously undefined value is dereferenced.

autowire.gloss: To resolve and inject a dependency automatically, without explicit configuration.

avalanche effect.gloss: A property of some cipher systems in which a small change in the input results in a very large change in the output.

average.gloss: Any measure of central tendency, especially any mean, the median, or the mode.
Any measure of central tendency, especially any mean, the median, or the mode. The arithmetic mean.

average access time.gloss: The average amount of time required for a storage device to transfer data to the CPU.

average seek time.gloss: Of a hard drive, the average of all possible seek times equivalent to the time of all possible seeks divided by the number of all possible seeks.

avl tree.gloss: A self-balancing binary search tree, where, for each node, the heights of the two child subtrees differ only by at most one.

awaitable.gloss: Able to be executed in an asynchronous manner, with the caller receiving any result at a later stage.
An operation that can be executed in an asynchronous manner, with the caller receiving any result at a later stage.

awaiter.gloss: An object that waits for the completion of an asynchronous task.

axial point.gloss: Any point that lies on any of the axes of a coordinate system

axiom.gloss: A fundamental assumption that serves as a basis for deduction of theorems; a postulate (sometimes distinguished from postulates as being universally applicable, whereas postulates are particular to a certain science or context).

axiom of choice.gloss: One of the axioms of set theory, equivalent to the statement that an arbitrary direct product of non-empty sets is non-empty; any version of said axiom, for example specifying the cardinality of the number of sets from which choices are made.

axiom of countable choice.gloss: A weaker form of the axiom of choice that states that every countable collection of nonempty sets must have a choice function; equivalently, the statement that the direct product of a countable collection of nonempty sets is nonempty.

axiom of extensionality.gloss: One of the axioms in axiomatic set theory, equivalent to the statement that two sets are equal if and only if they contain the same elements.

axiom of infinity.gloss: One of the axioms in axiomatic set theory that guarantees the existence of an infinite set.

axiom of pairing.gloss: One of the axioms in axiomatic set theory, equivalent to the statement that if two sets exist, there exists a set with those two sets as its sole elements.

axiom of regularity.gloss: One of the axioms in axiomatic set theory, equivalent to the statement that every non-empty set contains a member that is disjoint from that set.

axiom of union.gloss: One of the axioms in axiomatic set theory, equivalent to the statement that a union exists for any set, containing exactly all the elements contained within the sets within that set.

axiom schema.gloss: A formula in the language of an axiomatic system, in which one or more schematic variables appear, which stand for any term or subformula of the system, which may or may not be required to satisfy certain conditions.

axiom schema of abstraction.gloss: The axiom schema stating that for any clearly stated condition Sx, there exists a set B whose elements are exactly those objects which satisfy Sx.

axiom schema of separation.gloss: The axiom schema stating that for every set A and every condition Sx, there exists a set B whose elements are exactly those members of A for which Sx holds.

axiom scheme.gloss: A formula in the language of an axiomatic system, in which one or more schematic variables appear, which stand for any term or subformula of the system, which may or may not be required to satisfy certain conditions.

axiomatic system.gloss: A set of axioms from which theorems can be derived.

axis.gloss: An imaginary line around which an object spins (an axis of rotation) or is symmetrically arranged (an axis of symmetry).

A fixed one-dimensional figure, such as a line or arc, with an origin and orientation and such that its points are in one-to-one correspondence with a set of numbers; an axis forms part of the basis of a space or is used to position and locate data in a graph (a coordinate axis)

axis of symmetry.gloss: Any of one or more lines about which a geometric figure is symmetric

ayt.gloss: Initialism of are you there?: a telnet command sequence sent from client to server to verify that the connection is still active.

azdo.gloss: Initialism of approaching zero driver overhead (“a set of techniques aimed at reducing the CPU overhead in preparing and submitting rendering commands in the OpenGL pipeline”).

azumaya algebra.gloss: A generalization of central simple algebras to R-algebras where R need not be a field.

b+ tree.gloss: An m-ary tree data structure with a variable but often large number of children per node. It can be viewed as a B-tree in which each node contains only keys (not key–value pairs), and to which an additional level is added at the bottom with linked leaves.

b-frame.gloss: A compressed video frame which is reconstructed based on its differences from both the previous and the subsequent frame.

b-heptomino.gloss: A particular seven-cell methuselah in Conway's Game of Life.

b-sheaf.gloss: A kind of partial, simpler to describe sheaf which can be extended into a sheaf (and which is, in a technical sense, equivalent to that sheaf). For a formal definition, see B-sheaf on Wikipedia.Wikipedia .

b-tree.gloss: An indexed data structure suitable for storage of a large number of items in a balanced fashion, with very few disk accesses required for locating the correct record block.

baas.gloss: Acronym of backup as a service.
Acronym of backend as a service.

baby duck syndrome.gloss: The tendency of computer users to think the system (software or usage paradigm) they originally started using is better than others.

baby monster group.gloss: A sporadic simple group, B, and one of the 26 sporadic groups of the second highest order.

back buffer.gloss: A buffer used to store graphics while they are being drawn, and later copied to the display in a single operation.

back channel.gloss: A real-time online discussion that occurs simultaneously with a verbal presentation.

back end.gloss: That part of a hardware or software system that is farthest from the user; the internals rather than the user interface.

back out.gloss: To exit a mode or function.

back pointer.gloss: A pointer that reciprocates another structure's pointer to its own containing structure, typically found in doubly linked lists and trees.

back substitution.gloss: A method of solving linear systems that have been transformed into row echelon form.
A method of solving recurrence relations.

back up.gloss: To copy (data) so that it can be restored if the main copy is lost.

back-end.gloss: Relating to the back end part of a hardware or software system.

backcalculation.gloss: A form of calculation in which input parameters are adjusted until the calculated result coincides with the actual result found.

backchain.gloss: To perform inferences, starting with a list of goals (or a hypothesis) and working backwards from the consequent to the antecedent.

backface.gloss: The back side of a face of a mesh, which typically will never face the camera and can thus be culled (discarded) from the list of items to be rendered.

background.gloss: The image or color over which a computer's desktop items are shown (e.g. icons or application windows).
A type of activity on a computer that is not normally visible to the user.

background process.gloss: A process that is not currently able to receive input from its controlling terminal.

background processing.gloss: The execution of a subsidiary operation by a computer while the user works with another application.

backing bean.gloss: A bean managed by JavaServer Faces that acts as a server-side data model and controller for a specific UI view (page).

backjump.gloss: A jump from one level of an algorithm to another, used in backjumping.

backjumping.gloss: A form of backtracking that may move more than one level at a time, used to improve the efficiency of certain algorithms.

backlink.gloss: A reference to an object on another server, allowing it to be updated periodically.
A link to another page that links to the current one, often in an automatically assembled list of links to all other such pages, allowing for bidirectional navigation.

backlinker.gloss: A program or process that maintains backlinks (references to objects on another server).

backoff.gloss: The situation where an algorithm or process refrains from taking an action it would otherwise have taken.

backpatch.gloss: To update (partially compiled code) with jump addresses that were previously left as placeholders because they had not yet been encountered in the source code.

backport.gloss: To retroactively supply to a previous version of a software product a fix or a new feature at the same time or after supplying it to the current version.
To re-release software on its original or a previous platform with new features, after its release on a different platform.
A software program that has been backported.

backpressure.gloss: The buildup of unprocessed data due to a bottleneck; a technique to control the flow of data between producers and consumers.

backprime.gloss: The ⟨‵⟩ or ⟨`⟩ symbol; a reversed prime.

backpropagation.gloss: An error correction technique used in neural networks.

backquote.gloss: The symbol `, resembling a reversed quotation mark.

backscatter.gloss: The sending of IP packets to essentially random addresses in response to incoming packets that have a spoofed origin.

backshift.gloss: A function on a stochastic process whose value on any random variable is the preceding random variable in the process.

backslash.gloss: The punctuation mark /; a slash, forward slash.
To escape (a metacharacter) by prepending a backslash that serves as an escape character, thereby forming an escape sequence.

backspace.gloss: A keyboard key used for removing a character behind the cursor, and moving the cursor one position backwards.
A non-printable text character representing a backspace.
To remove a character behind a cursor.
To move a magnetic tape to a previous block.

backstore.gloss: A back end data storage; a backing store device.

backtab.gloss: A software-defined key combination to do the reverse of pressing the Tab key, usually Shift+Tab.
An instance of pressing this key combination.

backtick.gloss: The symbol `, resembling a reversed quotation mark and also being, or being homoglyphic to (depending on mental model), a grave accent mark in isolation. (Common uses include (1) use as a dead key in composing grave-accented characters, (2) use as an escape character to mark literals, and (3) many other uses as defined by contexts.)

backtracking.gloss: The act of building all possible solutions to a problem incrementally, abandoning any candidate solution if it cannot lead to a valid solution.

backup.gloss: A copy of a file or record, stored separately from the original, that can be used to recover the original if it is damaged or destroyed.
That is intended as a backup.

backup copy.gloss: A duplicate instance of an application, datafile, server or system created as a means to restore the original data in case it is deleted, corrupted or lost.

backupability.gloss: The capability of being backed up.

backus-naur form.gloss: A formal notation for context-free grammars.

backward compatibility.gloss: The capability of an electronic device, a piece of software, etc., to interoperate with older systems; (countable) an instance of this.

backward compatible.gloss: Capable of interoperating with older systems.

backward incompatibility.gloss: The incapability of interoperating with older systems.

backward incompatible.gloss: Incapable of interoperating with older systems.

backward induction.gloss: The process of reasoning backwards in time, from the end of a problem or situation, to determine a sequence of optimal actions.

backwrap.gloss: A word wrap feature that restores a word to the preceding line when space is made for it by deletion.
To restore a word to the preceding line when space is made for it by deletion.

bad.gloss: Causing a problem rendering the current task impossible.

badge.gloss: A small overlay on an icon that shows additional information about that item, such as the number of new alerts or messages.

bag.gloss: A collection of objects, disregarding order, but (unlike a set) in which elements may be repeated.

bag of words.gloss: The collection of words from an unprocessed text without regard to grammar; a collection of word unigrams.

bagplot.gloss: A method for visualizing two- or three-dimensional statistical data, analogous to the one-dimensional box plot.

baire function.gloss: A function obtained from a continuous function by transfinite iteration of the operation of forming pointwise limits of sequences of functions.

baitware.gloss: Freeware of deliberately poor quality with some, but generally not all, of the features of a software application, intended to entice those who download the freeware to buy the complete application.

bake.gloss: To fix (lighting, reflections, etc.) as part of the texture of an object to improve rendering performance.

baksmal.gloss: Converting a Dalvik executable file (.dex file) to smali language (a human-readable representation of the binary Dalvik bytecode).

balanced category.gloss: A category in which every bimorphism is an isomorphism.

balayage.gloss: A method for reconstructing a harmonic function.

balayaged.gloss: Of a harmonic function: reconstructed by the balayage method.

ball.gloss: Homologue or analogue of a disk in the Euclidean plane. In 3-dimensional Euclidean space, the volume bounded by a sphere.
Homologue or analogue of a disk in the Euclidean plane. The set of points in a metric space of any number of dimensions lying within a given distance (the radius) of a given point.
Homologue or analogue of a disk in the Euclidean plane. The set of points in a topological space lying within some open set containing a given point.

ballean.gloss: The asymptotical counterpart of a ball (inside surface of a sphere)

banach algebra.gloss: An associative algebra over the real or complex numbers (or over a non-Archimedean complete normed field) that is also a Banach space.

banana.gloss: A catamorphism (from the use of banana brackets in the notation).

band printer.gloss: A type of impact line printer in which a metal band, etched with character shapes and timing marks, moves horizontally across the print area, allowing hammers to strike and transfer characters from the band through a ribbon onto paper.

bandelet.gloss: An orthonormal basis that is adapted to geometric boundaries, used in image processing.

bandwidth.gloss: The rate of data flow in digital networks typically measured in bits per second; the bitrate.
The minimum, over all orderings of vertices of a given graph, of the length of the longest edge.

bang.gloss: A factorial, in mathematics, because the factorial of n is written as n!

bang path.gloss: An early form of e-mail address with the components separated by exclamation marks, naming the sequence of networked computers that the mail should be routed through.

bank.gloss: A contiguous block of memory that is of fixed, hardware-dependent size, but often larger than a page and partitioning the memory such that two distinct banks do not overlap.

bank switching.gloss: A method to increase the usable memory beyond what the processor normally supports by switching between different areas of memory ("banks") at runtime.

bannerware.gloss: software that contains banner advertising for other software by the same maker

banzhaf power index.gloss: An index defined by the probability of changing an outcome of a vote where voting rights are not necessarily equally divided among the voters or shareholders.

bar.gloss: The sign indicating that the characteristic of a logarithm is negative, conventionally placed above the digit(s) to show that it applies to the characteristic only and not to the mantissa.
A metasyntactic variable representing an unspecified entity, often the second in a series, following foo.

barcode reader.gloss: An electronic device that can read and output printed barcodes to a computer.

bare board.gloss: A printed circuit board before it has any electronic components or holes added.

bare metal.gloss: A runtime environment where little to no abstraction is available: usually employing a low-level programming language, without access to any operating system facilities, and interfacing hardware directly.
Physical hardware, as opposed to virtualised.

bare-bones.gloss: Describes a computer sold preassembled, but without certain essential components, such as a processor, memory, and hard drive.

bareword.gloss: A sequence of text characters in source code that do not form a keyword nor part of a quoted string, and may potentially be interpreted in various ways.

barfmail.gloss: electronic mail automatically sent in reply to a sender whose original message cannot be delivered

barnacle.gloss: A deprecated or obsolete file, image or other artifact that remains with a project even though it is no longer needed.

barnes integral.gloss: A contour integral involving a product of gamma functions, closely related to generalized hypergeometric series.

barnsley fern.gloss: A fern-like fractal involving four affine transformations.

barrel file.gloss: A JavaScript or TypeScript module which does nothing except import various files and then export them together, for the convenience of other developers who only need to know about and work with that single barrel file.

barrel shifter.gloss: A digital circuit that can shift a word by a specified number of bits using only combinational logic, without any sequential logic.

barycenter.gloss: The centroid, the geometric center of a plane figure

barycentre.gloss: The point at the centre of a system; an average point, weighted according to mass or other attribute. The term is usually used in astronomy for the centre of mass about which a system rotates, for example, the moon and the earth rotate about a common point within the earth but not near the centre. Jupiter and the Sun rotate about a common point just outside the surface of the Sun.

base.gloss: The lowest side of a triangle or other polygon, or the lowest face of a cone, pyramid or other polyhedron laid flat.
A number raised to the power of an exponent.
The set of sets from which a topology is generated.
A topological space, looked at in relation to one of its covering spaces, fibrations, or bundles.
A sequence of elements not jointly stabilized by any nontrivial group element.

base address.gloss: An address serving as a point of reference for calculating other addresses.

base angle.gloss: Either of the two angles that intersect with the base of a triangle.

base character.gloss: A character whose appearance is modified by one or more combining characters.

base memory.gloss: The first 640 kilobytes of RAM (random access memory) in an IBM-compatible PC.
The amount of RAM installed on a new computer, before any optional upgrades.

base station.gloss: A radio receiver/transmitter that serves as the hub of the local wireless network, and may also be the gateway between a wired network and the wireless network.

base year.gloss: a year chosen for comparison with other years, in statistical analysis and various indices, such as a price index. It usually has an arbitrary value of 100 to make percentage comparisons easier. A new base year can be chosen as the years progress.

base-2.gloss: Synonym of binary (“concerning numbers and calculations using the binary number system”).

basebean.gloss: A foundational utility or base class (a JavaBean or data object) from which specialized classes inherit common properties and methods.

baseline.gloss: To provide a baseline for measurement.

basename.gloss: A filename without any path or directory information.

basepoint.gloss: A point that marks the beginning and the end of a topological loop

bashism.gloss: A shell command specific to the Bash interpreter.

basin of attraction.gloss: Informally, a set of points from which a dynamical system spontaneously moves to a particular attractor.

basinhopping.gloss: A particular Monte Carlo method of optimization

basis.gloss: In a vector space, a linearly independent set of vectors spanning the whole vector space.

A collection of subsets ("basis elements") of a set, such that this collection covers the set, and for any two basis elements which both contain an element of the set, there is a third basis element contained in the intersection of the first two, which also contains that element.

basis spline.gloss: A spline function that has minimal support with respect to a given degree, smoothness, and domain partition. Any spline function of given degree can be expressed as a linear combination of basis splines of that degree.

basis vector.gloss: A vector that forms part of a basis for a vector space.

bastard operator from hell.gloss: A rogue system administrator who abuses users of the system.

batch.gloss: A group or collection of things of the same kind, such as a batch of letters or the next batch of business. A set of data to be processed at one time.
To handle a set of input data or requests as a batch process.

batch file.gloss: A file containing a series of instructions to be carried out by the operating system.

batch job.gloss: A series of instructions executed by the operating system.

batch process.gloss: A series of commands or programs that are executed without human intervention; the execution of such a series.

batch processing.gloss: the execution of a series of programs on a computer, called jobs, without manual intervention

batch queue.gloss: A system software data structure maintained by job scheduler software.

batch up.gloss: To line up multiple tasks to be executed at once in order to improve efficiency.

batchable.gloss: Capable of being run as a batch (a set of data processed at one time).

batteries-included.gloss: Including all possible components required for full usability.

battery-backed.gloss: Using a battery to maintain volatile memory when powered off.

battle of the sexes.gloss: A situation in which two people want to do different things, but do them together.

baud.gloss: A unit of data transmission symbol rate; the number of signalling events per second.
bps (bits per second), regardless of how many bits are represented by each symbol.

baxterization.gloss: A method for finding spectral dependent solutions to the Yang-Baxter equations.

bayesian.gloss: Of or pertaining to Bayes' theorem and its applications.

bayesian network.gloss: A directed acyclic graph whose vertices represent random variables and whose directed edges represent conditional dependencies. Each random variable can fall into any of at least two mutually disjoint states, and has a probability function which takes as inputs the states of its parent nodes and returns as output the probability of being in a certain state for a given combination of the states of its parent nodes. A node without parent nodes just has an unconditioned probability of being in some given state.

bayesianism.gloss: An approach to probability which quantifies expectations based on given data, following Bayes' theorem.

baz.gloss: A metasyntactic variable used to stand for some unspecified entity; typically the third in a series after foo and bar.

bazeries cylinder.gloss: A cryptographic device similar to the Jefferson disks.

bbstro.gloss: An intro created to publicize a bulletin board system.

bdfl.gloss: Initialism of benevolent dictator for life.

bdrf.gloss: Initialism of bidirectional reflectance distribution function.

bduf.gloss: Initialism of Big Design Up Front.

beach ball.gloss: A spinning wait cursor in macOS.

beachball.gloss: To hang; to stop responding to user input.

beaconing.gloss: gerund of beacon A continuous signaling of error conditions on a LAN, or small packets on a wireless LAN (WLAN).
gerund of beacon In a token ring network, the process of isolating a fault domain with signals, so that recovery actions can take place.

beam.gloss: To transmit, especially by direct wireless means such as infrared.

beamspace.gloss: A beam of particles treated as a mathematical space.

beanplot.gloss: An alternative form of boxplot in which individual observations are shown as small lines in a one-dimensional scatter plot.

bebugging.gloss: A technique for measuring test coverage by adding bugs to a program and tasking the tester with finding them.

beckett-gray code.gloss: A mathematical structure based on Samuel Beckett's play Quad.

bed.gloss: A place, or flat surface or layer, on which something else rests or is laid. The flat surface of a scanner on which a document is placed to be scanned.

bedmas.gloss: An acronym for arithmetic order of precedence, with B first and AS last: Brackets, exponents, division, multiplication, addition, subtraction.

beehive.gloss: In Conway's Game of Life, a particular still life pattern with a rounded appearance.

beerware.gloss: Software that can be used under a relaxed licence, with the user encouraged to pay for the software by donating to its author enough money to buy a beer.

before image journal.gloss: A transaction log acting as a version of a database entry before an update is recorded.

beg the question.gloss: To engage in the logical fallacy of begging the question (petitio principii).

beggarware.gloss: freeware that encourages the user to make an optional donation to its author

behavioral subtyping.gloss: A subtype relation of the form that each subtype object satisfies the specification of the supertype.

behavioural pattern.gloss: A design pattern which specifies how the entities of a software communicate with each other.

behrens-fisher problem.gloss: The problem of interval estimation and hypothesis testing concerning the difference between the means of two normally distributed populations when the variances of the two populations are not assumed to be equal, based on two independent samples.

beige box.gloss: A desktop computer in the style typical of personal computers of the 1980s and 1990s, having a boxy off-white case and CRT monitor.

beknottedness.gloss: The measure or degree to which a knot is complicated, i.e., a knot's complexity; the number of times that it is necessary to pass one part of the curve of the knot projected upon a plane through another in order to untie the knot.

belinkedness.gloss: The number of times one branch of a link must be passed through the other in order to undo it.

bell character.gloss: A control character with the value seven (Unicode code point U+0007, ASCII 0x07), originally used to ring a bell on telegraphy equipment to alert the operator to an incoming message; on modern computers, it generally causes a beep or buzzer to sound when printed to a terminal window, or, as a silent visual alternative, may cause the terminal window to flash briefly.

bell curve.gloss: The bell-shaped curve that is typical of the normal distribution.

bell number.gloss: Any member of a sequence of numbers that count the possible partitions of a set, such that the nth number Bₙ is the number of different ways to partition a set that has exactly n elements.

bell polynomial.gloss: Any member of a certain class of polynomials used in the study of set partitions, and related to Stirling numbers and Bell numbers.

bellman-ford algorithm.gloss: An algorithm that computes single-source shortest paths in a weighted digraph, capable (unlike the faster Dijkstra's algorithm) of handling graphs with negative edge weights.

belong.gloss: (followed by to) To be an element of (a set). The symbol ∈ means belongs to.

bem.gloss: Initialism of block, element, modifier, a convention for authoring CSS.

benchmark.gloss: A computer program that is executed to assess the performance of the runtime environment.

benevolent dictator for life.gloss: The leader of an open-source software project, typically project founders, who retains the final say in disputes or arguments within the community.

bent function.gloss: A Boolean function f: Z ₂ⁿ→ Z ₂ whose Walsh transform has constant absolute value.

bento.gloss: A menu icon of nine squares in a grid.
A layout consisting of cards arranged in a modular, irregularly partitioned grid.

beowulf cluster.gloss: A cluster of standard personal computers linked by a local area network, usually on the order of 10 nodes.

bernoulli distribution.gloss: A discrete probability distribution that represents the result of a single trial, taking value 1 with "success" probability p and value 0 with "failure" probability q=1-p.

bernoulli number.gloss: Any one of the rational numbers in a sequence of such that appears in numerous contexts, including formulae for sums of integer powers and certain power series expansions.

bernoulli polynomial.gloss: Any member of a certain group of polynomials remarkable in that the number of crossings of the x-axis in the unit interval does not go up as the degree of the polynomials goes up.

bernoulli process.gloss: A series of independent trials, analogous to repeatedly flipping a coin to determine whether it is fair.

bernoulli trial.gloss: A random experiment with exactly two possible outcomes.

bernoulli umbra.gloss: In umbral calculus, a kind of umbra corresponding to the Bernoulli numbers.

bernstein basis polynomial.gloss: Any polynomial of the form b_i,n(t)=n choose itⁱ(1-t)ⁿ⁻ⁱ!!, being the iᵗʰ term of the binomial expansion of (t+(1-t))ⁿ!.

bernstein polynomial.gloss: The linear combination of a set of Bernstein basis polynomials.

besicovitch set.gloss: Synonym of Kakeya set (“set of points in Euclidean space that contains a unit line segment in every direction”).

bessel function.gloss: Any of a class of functions that are solutions to a particular form of differential equation (a Bessel equation) and are typically used to describe waves in a cylindrically symmetric system.

beta.gloss: The phase of development after alpha testing and before launch, in which software, while not complete, has been released to potential users for testing.
Software in such a phase; a preliminary version.
Any kind of content from early development that was not used in the final product.
Preliminary; prerelease. Refers to an incomplete version of a product released for initial testing.
To preliminarily release computer software for initial testing prior to final release.

beta distribution.gloss: Any of a family of continuous probability distributions defined on the interval [0, 1] whose shape is parametrised by two positive parameters, denoted α and β, which appear as exponents in the associated random variable.

beta function.gloss: A mathematical function that is also called the Euler integral of the first kind; it is a symmetric special function.

beta reduce.gloss: To syntactically replace a function call by the result of calling that function.

beta reduction.gloss: One of the three rewrite rules of the lambda calculus, which states that the application of a lambda abstraction (λx.t) to a term s yields an expression t[s/x], "t with s instead of x", where all free instances of x in t have been replaced by s.

beta testing.gloss: A form of software testing, after the alpha testing stage, involving a limited audience of external users.

beta version.gloss: An early version of a program or application that contains most of the major features, but is not yet complete. Sometimes these versions are released only to a select group of people, or to the general public, for testing and feedback. This is the second major stage of development following the alpha version, and comes before the release candidate.

betaish.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a beta version.

bethe lattice.gloss: A kind of connected cycle-free graph.

betti number.gloss: Any of a sequence of numbers, denoted bₙ, which characterise a given topological space K by giving, for each dimension, the number of holes in K of said dimension; (formally) the rank of the nth homology group, Hₙ, of K.

betweenness.gloss: A measure of the number of geodesic paths through a node or edge.

bevan circle.gloss: The circle through the centers of the three excircles of a triangle.

bevan point.gloss: A triangle center, defined as the center of the Bevan circle.

bfi.gloss: Initialism of brute force and ignorance. Reliance on raw computing power (rather than, for example, an efficient algorithm).

bfile.gloss: LOB datatype accessible directly from the operating system, without using the DBMS.

bi-endian.gloss: Supporting both big-endian and little-endian processing.

biadjacency.gloss: The adjacency of a bipartite graph

bialgebra.gloss: A particular form of vector space that is a compatible form of two algebras.

bialtitude.gloss: A perpendicular to two opposite edges of a tetrahedron.

biangular.gloss: Having exactly two angular structures, operations, coordinates, or relative positions.

bias.gloss: The difference between the expectation of the sample estimator and the true population value, which reduces the representativeness of the estimator by systematically distorting it.

bias-robust.gloss: Describing statistics that are relatively unbiased even when some assumptions about the data or the model do not hold true.

biased.gloss: Exhibiting a systematic distortion of results due to a factor not allowed for in its derivation; skewed.

biautomaton.gloss: A finite automaton which arbitrarily alternates between reading the input from the left and from the right

biaxial.gloss: Having two axes of rotation and two planes of symmetry (e.g. having the shape of a spheroid)

białynicki-birula decomposition.gloss: A T-stable cellular decomposition of a smooth T-variety.

bibd.gloss: Initialism of balanced incomplete block design.

bibundle.gloss: A generalized bundle in a Lie group

bicanonical.gloss: Canonical on both the left and the right.

bicapped.gloss: Having a cap (in the shape of a pyramid) at each end

bicartesian closed category.gloss: A Cartesian closed category which also has an initial object and such that for any pair of objects, A and B, in the category, the category has another object which is their coproduct, A∐B.

bicategorical.gloss: Of or pertaining to a bicategory

bicategory.gloss: A particular construct in category theory, used to extend the notion of category to handle the cases where the composition of morphisms is not (strictly) associative, but only associative up to an isomorphism.

bicharacter.gloss: A type of bilinear complex number

bicharacteristic.gloss: Describing a line of tangency of two characteristics

bichromatic.gloss: Describing a graph with edges of two possible colours.

bicircular.gloss: Having nodes at the two circular points at infinity.

biclique.gloss: A special kind of bipartite graph where every vertex of the first set is connected to every vertex of the second set.

biclosed.gloss: Of a monoidal category: both left-closed and right-closed.

bicluster.gloss: A subset of rows or columns of a matrix produced by biclustering

biclustering.gloss: The simultaneous clustering of the rows and columns of a matrix

bicoherence.gloss: A squared normalised form of a bispectrum.

bicombing.gloss: A selection of a path for which two points moving simultaneously along lines that begin and end at a distance less than or equal to 1 apart always remain within a specified bounded distance of each other, independent of the lengths of the paths.

bicommutant.gloss: A double commutant (that commutes with the elements of two subgroups)

bicompletion.gloss: The process that makes a category bicomplete.

bicomplex.gloss: Composed of a pair of complex numbers having certain defined properties

bicomplex number.gloss: A pair (w,z) of complex numbers constructed by the Cayley–Dickson process that defines the bicomplex conjugate (w,z)^*=(w,-z), and the product of two bicomplex numbers as (u,v)(w,z)=(uw-vz,uz+vw).

biconditional.gloss: An "if and only if" conditional wherein the truth of each term depends on the truth of the other

bicone.gloss: The three-dimensional shape swept by revolving an isosceles triangle around its edge of unequal length, or by joining two identical right circular cones, base to base.

biconnected.gloss: Describing a connected graph from which two vertices must be removed for it to become disconnected.

biconservative.gloss: Satisfying the equation A(grad H) = -H grad H for the mean curvature function H and the Weingarten operator A.

bicorn.gloss: A plane curve having two cusps.

bicorrelation.gloss: The correlation between two sets of variables

bicriterion.gloss: Either of a pair of related criteria

bicritical.gloss: Describing a graph, the removal of two of whose vertices leaves a subgraph the edges of which can be coloured with only three colours

bicrossproduct.gloss: A group constructed from two subgroups by generalization of the direct and semidirect products.

bicupola.gloss: A solid formed from two cupolas joined at the base.

bicursal.gloss: Used to describe a curve composed of two moving points; e.g. a hyperbola.

bicylinder.gloss: A solid formed by two intersecting cylinders.

bidegree.gloss: An extension of the degree (or order) of a polynomial in certain geometries

bidegreed.gloss: Whose vertices have exactly two degrees

biderivation.gloss: A bilinear mapping which is a derivation in each variable separately.

bidiagonal.gloss: Describing a matrix that has non-zero entries along the main diagonal and either the diagonal above or the diagonal below.

bidiagonalization.gloss: A particular form of matrix decomposition

bidirected.gloss: Describing a graph, each of whose edge has an independent orientation at each end

bidisc.gloss: A polydisc of the second order

bidouble.gloss: Acting as a finite flat Galois morphism with Galois group (Z/2)²-.

bielliptic.gloss: Being a branched double cover of an elliptic curve.

biequivalent.gloss: Both left equivalent and right equivalent; Having the property that there exists a pair of mappings M₁ (A->B) and M₂ (B->A) such that M₁M₂(A) is equivalent to applying the unity operator to A and M₂ M₁(B) is equivalent to applying the unity operator to B.
qualifiers: of two entities A and B

bifid cipher.gloss: A classical cipher that combines the Polybius square with transposition, and uses fractionation to achieve diffusion.

bifolium.gloss: A quartic plane curve whose equation in Cartesian coordinates is (x²+y²)²=ax²ʸ.

bifunction.gloss: A function of a pair of values

bifunctor.gloss: A functor whose domain is a product of categories.
The analog to a functor in a bicategory.

bifundamental.gloss: Describing a tensor product of two representations.
A tensor product of two representations.

bifurcation.gloss: The change in the qualitative or topological structure of a given family as described by bifurcation theory.
A command that executes one block or other of commands depending on the result of a condition.

bifurcation theory.gloss: A branch of mathematics concerned with dynamical systems which suffer sudden qualitative changes from an infinitesimal change in a parameter.

big agile.gloss: The application of agile principles and practices to larger, complex projects, often with teams working from multiple locations.

big ball of mud.gloss: A complex system designed in a haphazard manner, without coherent architecture.

big bang testing.gloss: A form of integration testing in which the individual modules are linked together and tested as a whole, without first being tested independently.

big box.gloss: Software supplied in a large box made from card, typical of the 1990s.

big iron.gloss: Large, expensive, powerful computers such as mainframes.

big o.gloss: Upper bound function; see big O notation.

big o notation.gloss: A particular notation, useful in the analysis of algorithms, which describes the limiting behavior of a function when the argument tends towards a particular value or infinity, usually in terms of simpler functions.

big-endian.gloss: Storing the most significant byte of a multibyte number at a lower address than the least significant byte; that is, "big end" first.
Transmitting the most significant byte of a multibyte number before transmitting the least significant byte; that is, "big end" first.

bigenus.gloss: The second plurigenus P₂ of a surface.

bigluing.gloss: A category of quadruples related to the gluing construction.

bignum.gloss: A number whose digits of precision are limited only by available memory (as opposed to the usual fixed-point arithmetic).

bigraded.gloss: indexed by a pair of integers

bigrassmannian.gloss: Pertaining to a permutation such that there is at most one left and one right descent (at most one index i and one index j, such that wsᵢ < w and sⱼw < w).

bihamiltonian.gloss: Describing any system that may be described by a pair of hamiltonian structures

biharmonic.gloss: Describing a class of fourth-order partial differential equations which arises in areas of continuum mechanics

bihermitian.gloss: Hermitian in x for every y and hermitian in y for every x.

biholomorphic.gloss: Of, pertaining to, or exhibiting biholomorphism

biholomorphism.gloss: A bijective holomorphism whose inverse is also holomorphic

biinfinite.gloss: Infinite in both directions, having neither a first nor a last element.

bijection.gloss: A one-to-one correspondence, a function which is both a surjection and an injection.

bijective.gloss: Associating to each element of the codomain exactly one element of the domain; establishing a perfect (one-to-one) correspondence between the elements of the domain and the codomain; (formally) both injective and surjective.
Having a component that is (specified to be) a bijective map; that specifies a bijective map.

bijective numeration.gloss: A numeral system that uses digits to establish a bijection between finite strings and the positive integers, especially by k-adic notation such as unary and decimal without a zero.

bikeshed.gloss: A topic that is attracting debate out of proportion to its actual importance.
To discuss a minor detail rather than focusing on more important issues.

bilanguage.gloss: A language that has a regular treelike structure

bilattice.gloss: A structure B = (S,⊑₁ ,⊑₂) in which S is a non-empty set, and ⊑₁ and ⊑₂ are partial orderings each giving S the structure of a lattice, determining thus for each of the two lattices the corresponding operations of meet and join.

bilevel.gloss: A binary image, one that has only two possible values for each pixel (usually black and white).

bilimit.gloss: A generalization of the concept of a limit that is an equivalence class rather than a unique value.

bilinear.gloss: Linear (preserving linear combinations) in each variable.
qualifiers: of a function in two variables

bilinear.gloss: Of or pertaining to a Möbius transformation (type of conformal map representable as the ratio of two linear functions).

bilinear form.gloss: A function of two arguments from the same vector space which maps onto a field of scalars, which acts like a linear form with respect to either one of its arguments when the other one is held constant.

bilinearization.gloss: A process that makes a function bilinear.

billboard.gloss: A sprite that always faces the screen, no matter which direction it is viewed from.

billboarding.gloss: A technique in three-dimensional graphics in which a sprite is rendered perpendicular to the camera without respect to camera movement.

bilogarithmic.gloss: Based on two logarithms; logarithmic in two directions

bilunabirotunda.gloss: A polyhedron, one of the Johnson solids, having 8 triangular, 2 square, and 4 pentagonal faces.

bim.gloss: Abbreviation of Beginning of Information Mark.

bimagic.gloss: Of a magic cube: remaining magic even if all its numbers are replaced by their kth power for 1 ≤ k ≤ 2.

bimagic square.gloss: A magic square that remains magic when all of its numbers are replaced by their squares.

bimap.gloss: A map that is also a comap.

bimedial.gloss: Being the sum of two lines commensurable only in power (such as the side and diagonal of a square).

bimedian.gloss: A line that joins the midpoints of opposite sides of a quadrilateral or tetrahedron

bimetric.gloss: Describing any system that may be described using two metrics.

bimodule.gloss: An abelian group that is both a left and a right module, such that the left and right multiplications are compatible

bimonoid.gloss: A monoid that is also a comonoid

bimorphism.gloss: A morphism which is both a monomorphism and an epimorphism.

bin.gloss: Any of the discrete intervals in a histogram, etc
To convert continuous data into discrete groups.

binarion.gloss: An element in the second level of associative composition algebra being a composition of two unarions.

binarization.gloss: Conversion of a tree to one with at most two children per node.

binary.gloss: Concerning logic whose subject matter concerns such states.
Concerning numbers and calculations using the binary number system.
Of an operation, function, procedure, or logic gate, taking exactly two operands, arguments, parameters, or inputs; having domain of dimension 2.
Of data, consisting coded values (e.g. machine code) not interpretable as plain or ASCII text (e.g. source code).
The bijective base-2 numeral system, which uses only the digits 0 and 1.

binary blob.gloss: A piece of software which is only available as a binary file (as opposed to being open-source), thus making the program very difficult to audit or modify.

binary chop.gloss: The use of binary search to eliminate a subset of values from a possible set.

binary code.gloss: A code that uses the binary digits (1 and 0), usually in groups of eight, to represent characters, machine instructions or other data.

binary digit.gloss: Either of the characters 0 and 1, used in the binary numeral system.

binary distribution.gloss: A distribution of software containing executable binaries, without source code.

binary file.gloss: A computer file that is not a text file, consisting of data other than human-readable text.

binary function.gloss: a function of the type f:V×V→V, or more generally, a function of the type f:U_1×U_2×...×U_n→V in which exactly two of the sets Uᵢ are equal to V.

binary large object.gloss: A data type that allows storage of binary data often of indeterminate length, used for example to embed multimedia within a database table.

binary number.gloss: A number represented by the binary digits 0 and 1.

binary numeral system.gloss: A system for representing numbers in which a radix of two is used; that is, each digit in a binary numeral may have either of two different values.

binary one.gloss: A fundamental unit of data in computing that represents an "on" state, a true condition, or the number 1 in the base-2 binary system.

binary operator.gloss: A symbol representing binary operation; an operator taking two operands.

binary point.gloss: A symbol that separates the integer and fractional parts of a number in a binary representation.

binary relation.gloss: A subset of the Cartesian product A×A (the set of ordered pairs (a, b) of elements of A, alternatively written as A²).

binary system.gloss: A numeric system with a base of 2, using only the numerals 0 and 1.

binary tree.gloss: A data structure in which each node has at most two children, each node but the root has one parent, and there are no cycles.

binary zero.gloss: A fundamental digital value (0) that represents an "off" state in hardware.

binary-coded decimal.gloss: A decimal number encoded in such a way that each decimal digit is represented by its own binary sequence, simplifying conversion between binary and decimal, and allowing exact representation of decimal fractions.

binary-compatible.gloss: able to run the same binary code intended to be run on another computer

binary-safe.gloss: Guaranteed not to corrupt or alter binary data.

bincount.gloss: A count of the number of things in each element of an array

bind.gloss: To associate an identifier with a value; to associate a variable name, method name, etc. with the content of a storage location.

binder.gloss: A software mechanism that performs binding.

bindful.gloss: Having the limitation of requiring textures to be bound by the CPU to a particular slot in a fixed-size table before the GPU can use them.

binding.gloss: The association of a named item with an element of a program.

binding number.gloss: The smallest possible ratio of the number of neighbours of a proper subset of vertices to the size of the subset.

binding time.gloss: The point in time when symbolic references to data are converted into physical machine addresses.

bindless.gloss: Not having the limitation of requiring textures to be bound by the CPU to a particular slot in a fixed-size table before the GPU can use them.

binning.gloss: A data pre-processing technique in which original data values fall into a small interval ("bin") and are replaced by a value representative of that interval, often the central value.

binode.gloss: A double point of a surface whose tangent cone consists of two different planes.

binomial.gloss: Of or relating to the binomial distribution.
A quantity expressed as the sum or difference of two terms.

binomial coefficient.gloss: a coefficient of any of the terms in the expansion of the binomial (x+y)ⁿ, defined by n choose k=(n!)/(k!(n-k)!), read as "n choose k"

binomial distribution.gloss: The discrete probability distribution of the number of successes in a sequence of n independent trials, each of which yields success with probability p.

binomial expansion.gloss: The rewriting of a binomial as a longer equivalent sum.

binomial random variable.gloss: The number of successes in n repeated experiments.

binomial series.gloss: The Maclaurin series expansion of the function f(x) = (1 + x)^α, for arbitrary complex α; the series ∑ₖ₌₀ ᪲α choose kxᵏ, where α choose k=(α(α-1)(α-2)…(α-k+1))/(k!).

binormal.gloss: A line that is at right angles to both the normal and the tangent of a point on a curve and, together with them, forms three orthogonal axes.

binsize.gloss: The number of things in each element of an array

binwidth.gloss: The numerical width of a bin

bio-inspired.gloss: Ideas inspired by mechanisms or laws operating in biological organisms, e.g. neural networks.

biochip.gloss: A microchip made from biological macromolecules (especially DNA) rather than a semiconductor.

biocompiler.gloss: The analogue of a compiler in synthetic biology.

biocomputer.gloss: Any of several proposed systems using DNA, proteins, or other biological materials to perform data processing (in synthetic biology).

biocomputing.gloss: The design and construction of computers containing biological components.
The application of computing to the biological sciences; bioinformatics.

bioctonion.gloss: An element of the tensor product of the algebra of octonions and the algebra of complex numbers

biocuration.gloss: The organization, representation and making accessible of biological data to both humans and computers

bioinformatics.gloss: A field of science in which biology, computer science, and information technology merge into a single discipline to analyse biological information using computers and statistical techniques.

biomathematics.gloss: The application of mathematics to the study of biological systems and processes

biometamorphic.gloss: That has a biological form and is metamorphic

biorthogonal.gloss: Describing a pair of topological vector spaces that are in duality with a pair of indexed subsets in a specific manner.

biorthonormal.gloss: Orthonormal and having elements that are each orthogonal to all but exactly one element in the other set.

bios.gloss: any firmware user interface that provides similar functionality as BIOS, such as UEFI.

biosimulation.gloss: The computer simulation of a biological system

biostatistics.gloss: The application of statistics to the study and analysis of biological and medical data

biparavector.gloss: A particular function of two paravectors.

bipartient.gloss: Involving an operation on two equal values.

bipartite.gloss: Having vertices that can be divided into two independent sets (see bigraph)

bipartization.gloss: The removal of vertices from a graph in order to make it bipartite

bipower.gloss: An alternative to variance; a measure of variability based on summing the product of adjacent data points rather than summing the squares of data points.

biprimality.gloss: The condition of being a biprime number

biprism.gloss: A fusion of two triangular prisms.

biproduct.gloss: An object which is simultaneously the product and the coproduct of some collection of objects.

biquadrate.gloss: The fourth power; the square of a square.

biquadratic.gloss: Of a polynomial expression, involving only the zeroth, second, and fourth powers of a variable, as x⁴ + 3x² + 2. Sometimes extended to any expression involving the biquadrate or fourth power (but no higher powers), as x⁴ − 4x³ + 3x² − x + 1.

biquandle.gloss: A generalisation of a quandle that is a form of a birack

biquaternion.gloss: Any of the numbers w+xi+yj+zk! where w, x, y, and z are complex numbers and the elements of {1, i, j, k} multiply as in the quaternion group.

biquinary.gloss: Employing, or relating to, an arithmetical system and notation in which each decimal digit is represented by a coefficient of five and a coefficient of one

biquotient.gloss: The base space of a principal bundle with a homogeneous space as total space.

birack.gloss: A rack in which the two operations are invertible.

birational.gloss: Describing a rational geometric function that has a rational inverse

birational geometry.gloss: A field of algebraic geometry in which the aim is to determine under what conditions two algebraic varieties are isomorphic outside lower-dimensional subsets.

birds-of-a-feather session.gloss: An informal discussion group, typically at a conference, based on a shared interest and without any fixed agenda.

biregular.gloss: Being a regular map with regular inverse.

bireversible.gloss: reversible under the action of two linear involutions

birthday attack.gloss: A covert method of decryption exploiting the so-called birthday paradox.

birthday effect.gloss: A statistical phenomenon where an individual's likelihood of death appears to increase on or close to their birthday, variously attributed to alcohol consumption, psychological stress, increased suicide risk, and other factors.

biscribed.gloss: Both circumscribed and inscribed, i.e. having vertices that lie on a curve and sides that are tangent to the curve.

bisecant.gloss: A secant that cuts a curve at exactly two points

bisect.gloss: To cut or divide into two parts. To divide an angle, line segment, or other figure into two equal parts.

bisector.gloss: A line or curve that bisects or divides a line segment, angle, or other figure into two equal parts.

bisegment.gloss: One of two equal parts of a line segment, circle, polygon, or other entity.

biserial.gloss: Having a correlation between one series and another that is divided into two types

biset.gloss: A pair of ordered sets of the same magnitude.

bisimilar.gloss: Of two state transition systems, such that a bisimulation exists between the two.

bisimulation.gloss: an equivalence relation between state transition systems, associating systems which behave in the same way in the sense that one system simulates the other and vice-versa

bispace.gloss: A set with both left and right morphisms.

bispanning.gloss: Having a partition of the edge set into two spanning trees.

bispectrum.gloss: A statistic used in the study of nonlinear interactions.

bisquare.gloss: An extension of the least squares method that removes or downweights extreme outliers

bistatistics.gloss: Pairs of statistics on the same set.

bisymmetric.gloss: Symmetric about both of its main diagonals.

bit.gloss: A binary digit, generally represented as a 1 or 0.

Any datum that may take on one of exactly two values.
A unit of measure for information entropy.

bit array.gloss: An array structure which store bit (0,1) values.

bit bashing.gloss: Any programming technique manipulating bits (binary digits). instead of whole words.

bit depth.gloss: The number of bits (binary digits) used to represent the colour of a single pixel.

bit interval.gloss: The time required to send one signal bit.

bit rot.gloss: The putative tendency of content in storage to become corrupt over time.
