bit slice.gloss: Any of a group of variable-length words that may be combined to form computable lengths of bits of any length

bit time.gloss: The amount of time it takes for one bit to be ejected from a network interface card operating at a predefined standard speed.

bit-compressed.gloss: Represented by the minimum number of bits that can represent the maximum value (of an integer variable)

bit-paired.gloss: Of a keyboard: having the layout of shifted keys corresponding to columns in the ASCII table.

bitangent.gloss: A line that is tangent to a curve at two points

bitangential.gloss: Meeting a curve at the tangency points of its bitangents.

bitarray.gloss: An array (or list) of bits (representing Boolean variables)

bitcoin.gloss: A unit of the bitcoin (proper noun proper noun sense 1) cryptocurrency.

bitensor.gloss: A tensorial function of pairs of points.

biter.gloss: Something (a data unit, machine etc.) with a width of a specified amount of bits.

biternary.gloss: Having three variables and their duals

bitfield.gloss: A sequence of bits (binary digits) which can be toggled individually as flags.

bitfilter.gloss: A specified subset of a sequence of bits.

bitflag.gloss: A bit (binary digit) whose value acts as a flag to enable or disable some behaviour.

bitflip.gloss: The switching of a bit's value (from 1 to 0, or vice versa).

bitlock.gloss: To encrypt (something) using the BitLocker encryption software for Microsoft Windows.

bitmap.gloss: A series of bits that represents a rasterized graphic image, each pixel being represented as a group of bits.

bitmask.gloss: A pattern of bits indicating which bits in a second pattern are to be modified.

bitonic.gloss: Having the property x_0≤⋯≤x_k≥⋯≥x_n-1 for some k,0≤k<n, or being a circular shift of such a sequence.

bitopological.gloss: Equipped with two distinct arbitrary topologies.

bitrade.gloss: Either of two elements of a permutation group that trade places with each other.

bitruncation.gloss: An operation on a regular polytope in which every edge is lost and every face is reduced in size.

bitscore.gloss: A normalised numerical score used to determine the similarity of two lists.

bitstate.gloss: The state (0 or 1) of a particular bit (binary digit).

bitwise.gloss: Treating a value as a series of bits rather than a numerical quantity.

biunique.gloss: that have a one-to-one correspondence in each direction

bivariate.gloss: Having or involving exactly two variables.
A polynomial or function with exactly two variables.

bivariate normal distribution.gloss: The joint probability distribution of two variables that are both individually normally distributed.

bivector.gloss: An antisymmetric tensor of second rank.

bixen.gloss: Users of the Byte Information Exchange (BIX) system, which ran from the mid-1980s until 2001.

bixie.gloss: A type of emoticon such as <@_@>, which represents an unrotated expression, unlike a smiley.

bksp.gloss: Abbreviation of backspace, on a computer keyboard.

black chamber.gloss: A government or royal court's cryptanalyst department.

black hat.gloss: A malicious hacker, one who violates computer security out of malice or for personal gain.

black midi.gloss: A style of music composition involving the creation of MIDI files where extreme numbers of musical notes are played simultaneously.

black room.gloss: A governmental facility for intercepting and decrypting communications.

black screen of death.gloss: A critical system error encountered by computer operating systems, characterized by the display of a completely black screen and the cessation of device functionality.

black-box testing.gloss: Any form of testing in which knowledge of the internals of the system being tested are unknown and unimportant.

blacklist.gloss: A list or set of people or entities to be shunned or banned, disallowed or blocked.

blade.gloss: An exterior product of vectors. (The product may have more than two factors. Also, a scalar counts as a 0-blade, a vector as a 1-blade; an exterior product of k vectors may be called a k-blade.)

blame.gloss: A source control feature that can show which user was responsible for a particular portion of the source code.

blancmange curve.gloss: A self-affine curve constructible by midpoint subdivision.

blindable.gloss: Such that, given an encrypted bit (binary digit), anybody can create a random ciphertext decrypting to the same bit.

blink.gloss: A text formatting feature that causes text to disappear and reappear as a form of visual emphasis.

blinkenlights.gloss: The flashing lights on an electronic device such as a modem, router, or network hub (originally the front-panel lights on old computers).

blinker.gloss: In Conway's Game of Life, an arrangement of three cells in a row that switches between horizontal and vertical orientations in each generation.

blit.gloss: A logical operation in which a block of data is rapidly moved or copied in memory, most commonly used to animate two-dimensional graphics.

blivet.gloss: A program that has messy source code.

bll.gloss: Initialism of business logic layer, a software architecture layer.

bloated.gloss: Excessively overloaded with features, like bloatware.

blob.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of BLOB: acronym of binary large object.

bloch function.gloss: Any of the elements of the Bloch space.

bloch space.gloss: The space, denoted by ℬ or ℬ, of holomorphic functions f defined on the open unit disc D in the complex plane, such that the function (1-|z|²)|f^′(z)| is bounded.

block.gloss: A substantial, often approximately cuboid, piece of any substance. In Conway's Game of Life, a still life consisting of four living cells arranged in a two-by-two square.

A logical extent or region; a grouping or apportionment of like things treated together as a unit. A region of code in a program that acts as a single unit, such as a function or loop.
A logical extent or region; a grouping or apportionment of like things treated together as a unit. A fixed-length group of bits making up part of a message.

A logical extent or region; a grouping or apportionment of like things treated together as a unit. A contiguous range of Unicode code points used to encode characters of a specific type; can be of any size evenly divisible by 16, up to 65,536 (a full plane).

To wait for some condition to become true.

block-scoped.gloss: whose scope is limited to a block

Agent noun of block (“obstruct or prevent”); something that blocks something else. An application or feature that stops or impedes something.
Agent noun of block (“obstruct or prevent”); something that blocks something else. A bug or issue that prevents software from being released.

blocklist.gloss: A list of websites or other material to be blocked.
A list or set of people or entities to be shunned or banned.

blockmodeling.gloss: The modeling of data using block models

blocksize.gloss: The size of a block of data (in a file or a transmission)

blockwise.gloss: In terms of blocks of data.

In terms of blocks; one block of data at a time.

blogcast.gloss: A short video aor audio clip published within a blog.

blogging.gloss: The design and editing of a blog; weblogging.

blort.gloss: A metasyntactic variable, similar to foo and bar.

blue screen.gloss: Ellipsis of blue screen of death.

boehm collector.gloss: A kind of mark-and-sweep garbage collector .

bofh.gloss: Initialism of bastard operator from hell.

bookmarklet.gloss: A small piece of JavaScript code stored as a URL within a bookmark.

bookware.gloss: Software that is published in, or distributed with, a book.

bool.gloss: A Boolean variable (one whose value is either true or false).

boole's inequality.gloss: The statement that the probability that at least one of a finite or countable set of events happens is no greater than the sum of the probabilities of the individual events.

boolean.gloss: Pertaining to data items that can have “true” and “false” (or, equivalently, 1 and 0 respectively) as their only possible values and to operations on such values.
A variable that can hold a single true/false (1/0) value.

boolean algebra.gloss: An algebraic structure (Σ,∨,∧,∼,0,1) where ∨ and ∧ are idempotent binary operators, ∼ is a unary involutory operator (called "complement"), and 0 and 1 are nullary operators (i.e., constants), such that (Σ,∨,0) is a commutative monoid, (Σ,∧,1) is a commutative monoid, ∧ and ∨ distribute with respect to each other, and such that combining two complementary elements through one binary operator yields the identity of the other binary operator. (See Boolean algebra (structure)#Axiomatics.)
Specifically, an algebra in which all elements can take only one of two values (typically 0 and 1, or "true" and "false") and are subject to operations based on AND, OR and NOT
The study of such algebras; Boolean logic, classical logic.

boolean atom.gloss: A logical proposition that cannot be derived from other logical propositions by a Boolean operation.

boolean circuit.gloss: A directed acyclic graph whose internal nodes are Boolean functions.

boolean derivative.gloss: With respect to a Boolean variable x_i: The XOR-sum of the positive and negative Shannon cofactors of the given derived function with respect to x_i. In symbols: ∂f/∂x_i(⃑x)=f_x_i(⃑x)⊕f_̄x_i(⃑x).

boolean function.gloss: Any function based on the operations AND, OR and NOT, and whose elements are from the domain of Boolean algebra

boolean lattice.gloss: The lattice corresponding to a Boolean algebra.

boolean logic.gloss: A system of symbolic logic that is the basis of Boolean algebra

boolean ring.gloss: A ring whose multiplicative operation is idempotent.

boolean variable.gloss: Any variable, from the domain of Boolean algebra, having one of only two values

boom.gloss: To rapidly adjust the evaluation of a position away from zero, indicating a likely win or loss.

boot.gloss: To disconnect forcibly; to eject from an online service, conversation, etc.
The act or process of bootstrapping; the starting or re-starting of a computing device.
To bootstrap; to start a system, e.g. a computer, by invoking its boot process or bootstrap.

boot block.gloss: A dedicated block usually at the beginning (first block on first track) of a storage medium that holds special data used to start a system. Some systems use a boot block of several physical sectors, while some use only one boot sector. Other manufacturers use the terms boot block and boot sector interchangeably.

boot disk.gloss: A computer disk holding a bootstrap loader and an operating system.

boot loader.gloss: A small program that initiates the bootstrap process by loading the operating system proper.

boot loop.gloss: A faulty condition in which the system repeatedly reboots itself.

boot sector.gloss: A dedicated sector, usually at the beginning (first sector on first track) of a storage medium, that holds special data used to start a system.

boot storm.gloss: The situation where many users attempt to boot their computers at the same time, causing excessive demand on the network.

boot time.gloss: The amount of time required to load the kernel of an operating system, its device drivers, and the initialization of the hardware.

bootability.gloss: The state or condition of being bootable.

bootable.gloss: That can be booted; from which one can boot the system.
A disk or other medium from which the system can be booted.

bootblock.gloss: A block of storage on disk that holds the code for booting the operating system.

booter.gloss: A program or process that boots.
A game that is launched by booting directly from the floppy disk containing the game program, rather than starting the program from within the computer's standardized operating system.
The floppy disk used to launch a game in such a manner.

bootflash.gloss: A flash memory used at bootstrap time for a device, commonly containing a bootloader and simple configuration information.

boothian.gloss: Of or relating to a tangential coordinate system invented by James Booth.

booting.gloss: The act by which a computer is booted.

bootload.gloss: The work done by a boot loader; the startup of an operating system.

bootrom.gloss: A read-only memory used for the initial boot process of a computer or device.

bootscan.gloss: An antivirus scan that takes place before the operating system has loaded.

bootsplash.gloss: A splash screen displayed at bootup.

bootstrap.gloss: The process by which the operating system of a computer is loaded into its memory.
The process necessary to compile the tools that will be used to compile the rest of the system or program.
Any method or instance of estimating properties of an estimator (such as its variance) by measuring those properties when sampling from an approximating distribution.
To load the operating system into the memory of a computer. Usually shortened to boot.
To compile the tools that will be used to compile the rest of a system or program.

border.gloss: A string that is both a prefix and a suffix of another particular string.

bordism.gloss: The property of two closed manifolds whose disjoint union is the boundary of a compact manifold

borel.gloss: being a member of a Borel σ-algebra; being a Borel set

borel function.gloss: A function which is Borel measurable.

borel measurable.gloss: Such that the inverse image of any open set in its codomain is a Borel set of its domain.

borel measure.gloss: A measure whose domain is the Borel σ-algebra of a locally compact Hausdorff space.

borel set.gloss: Any of the members of a Borel σ-algebra.

borel summation.gloss: A summation method for divergent series, particularly useful for summing divergent asymptotic series, and in some sense giving the best possible sum for such series.

borel transform.gloss: A transform used in Borel summation.
A generalization of this in Nachbin's theorem.

borel σ-algebra.gloss: The smallest σ-algebra which contains the topology of a given topological space.

borelian.gloss: Of or pertaining to a Borel set.

born digital.gloss: Created in an electronic format; never having existed in a physical edition.

bornological.gloss: Describing a form of locally convex space which, in some sense, possesses the minimum amount of structure needed to address questions of boundedness of sets and functions.

bornology.gloss: A structure which generalizes the set of all bounded subsets of a topological vector space

borrow.gloss: In Rust and some other programming languages, the situation where the ownership of a value is temporarily transferred to another region of code.

bot.gloss: A piece of software designed to perform a task (often a minor but repetitive one) automatically or on command, especially when operating with the appearance of a (human) user profile or account.

botless.gloss: Without bots; without a bot participating or running. (a piece of software designed to perform a task (often a minor but repetitive one) automatically or on command, especially when operating with the appearance of a (human) user profile or account.)

botlessness.gloss: The state or quality of being botless.

bottom type.gloss: The type that is a subtype of all other types.

botty.gloss: Resembling a bot (automated software process); botlike.
A term of address for a bot.

bounce.gloss: To turn power to (a device) off and back on; to reset; to reboot.

bound.gloss: A value which is known to be greater or smaller than a given set of values.

bound property.gloss: A property of an object that transmits notification of any changes to an adapter or event handler.

bound variable.gloss: A variable that is associated with a value, and therefore a variable that has an allocated storage location. If the programming language implements a representation of a canonical unknown value, infinity, etc., the value bound to the variable may be one of these.

boundary.gloss: (of a set) The set of points in the closure of a set S, not belonging to the interior of that set.

boundary condition.gloss: Any of a set of constraints that limit the solutions of a differential equation

boundary group.gloss: The image of the (k + 1)ᵗʰ boundary homomorphism (for a given chain complex).

boundary homomorphism.gloss: A group homomorphism on the group of simplicial k-chains induced by mapping each oriented k-simplex to a particular formal sum of its faces.
A homomorphism that operates on the kth element in a chain complex.

boundary term.gloss: A term that must be added to an equation to represent a boundary condition.

bounded.gloss: That can be enclosed within a ball of finite radius.
with bounded range when restricted to the unit ball
That contains a least element, a, and a greatest element, b, such that for all x ∈ X, a ≤ x ≤ b.
qualifiers: of a poset X with partial order ≤

bounded function.gloss: Any function whose values remain bounded by some constant.

bounded lattice.gloss: Any lattice (type of partially ordered set) that has both a greatest and a least element.

bounding.gloss: Containing all points of a given set within it.

bouquet of circles.gloss: A graph with only one vertex.

bouquet of spheres.gloss: A wedge product of two or more spheres joined at a distinguished point, usually the equator.

bourbakian.gloss: Any of the mathematicians involved in the formulation of Bourbakism.

box.gloss: Senses relating to a three-dimensional object or space. A computer, or the case in which it is housed.
A rectangular object in any number of dimensions.

box and whiskers plot.gloss: A graphical summary of a numerical data sample through five statistics — median, upper quartile, lower quartile, and upper extreme and lower extreme values — by depiction as a box with its edges at the quartile marks and an internal line at the median and with lines protruding from the box as far as the extremal values.

box plot.gloss: A graphical summary of a numerical data sample through five statistics: median, lower quartile, upper quartile, and some indication of more extreme upper and lower values.

box-cox distribution.gloss: The distribution of a random variable X for which the Box-Cox transformation on X follows a truncated normal distribution.

box-drawing character.gloss: A text character used for creating geometric frames and boxes.

boxcar.gloss: To reduce to a boxcar function.

boxcar function.gloss: Any function whose value is zero except for a finite part of its argument for which it has a constant non-zero value.

boxel.gloss: Any of a set of axis-aligned boxes that do not overlap, used to represent a 2.5D data set.

boxicity.gloss: The minimum dimension in which a graph may be represented as a specific intersection of boxes

boyce-codd normal form.gloss: A stage in the normalization of a relational database in which a database is in third normal form and all determinants are candidate keys.

bozosity.gloss: The behaviour of a bozo; idiocy.

bpaas.gloss: Acronym of business process as a service.

bpl.gloss: Initialism of broadband over power line.

bpon.gloss: Initialism of broadband passive optical network, or ITU-T G.983.

bps.gloss: Initialism of bit per second, a measure of speed of digital communication.

bqp.gloss: Initialism of bounded-error quantum polynomial time.

bra.gloss: One of the two vectors in the standard notation for describing quantum states in quantum mechanics, the row vector; the other (column) vector being its complex conjugate, the ket.

brachistochrone.gloss: A cycloid; the curve of fastest descent between two points.

bracket.gloss: A pair of values that represent the smallest and largest elements of a range.

braid.gloss: Given two sets of n points on corresponding positions on two parallel lines, a braid is a unique set of crossings (over or under) between n strands that connect each point on one line to a point on the other line such that all points represent the terminus of one and only one strand and the traversal of any strand from a starting point to an ending point never moves further away from the from the ending point.

braid group.gloss: A group whose elements represent ways to weave some number of strings into braids.

braid statistics.gloss: A generalization of the statistics of bosons and fermions based on the concept of braid group.

bramble.gloss: A collection of mutually touching connected subgraphs, where two subgraphs touch if they share a vertex or each includes one endpoint of an edge.

branch.gloss: One of the portions of a curve that extends outwards to an indefinitely great distance.
A sequence of code that is conditionally executed.
A group of related files in a source control system, including for example source code, build scripts, and media such as images.
A path of vertices of degree 2, ending at vertices whose degree is not 2.
To jump to a different location in a program, especially as the result of a conditional statement.

branch cut.gloss: A curve in the complex plane such that it is possible to define a single analytic branch of a multi-valued function on the plane minus that curve.

branch predictor.gloss: A digital circuit that tries to predict which way a branch structure will go, so as to improve the flow in the instruction pipeline.

branch-decomposition.gloss: An unrooted binary tree that represents the hierarchical clustering of the edges of an undirected graph.

brancher.gloss: That which branches, or jumps to another instruction location within a program.

branching process.gloss: A stochastic process which typically models reproduction of objects, with the assumption that the reproductions of individual particles are mutually independent.

branchwidth.gloss: The minimum width of a branch-decomposition.

brauer group.gloss: For a field K, an abelian group whose elements are Morita equivalence classes of central simple algebras over K, with addition given by the tensor product of algebras.

bravais lattice.gloss: An infinite array of discrete points generated by a set of discrete translation operations mathbf R=n_1 mathbf a₁+n_2 mathbf a₂+n_3 mathbf a₃, where nᵢ are any integers and aᵢ are known as the primitive vectors which lie in different directions and span the lattice.

brazilian logic.gloss: A form of paracomplete logic that is the dual of intuitionistic logic.

brdf.gloss: Initialism of bidirectional reflectance distribution function.

breadcrumb.gloss: A single link in a chain indicating the hierarchical location of a directory, web page or similar, used as a navigation aid.
A fragment of data that serves to log the actions taken by a program, used in debugging.
To add navigational breadcrumbs to (a web page or user interface).

breadth.gloss: The length of the longest path between two vertices in a graph.

breadth-first search.gloss: A search algorithm that begins at the root node and explores all the neighboring nodes.

break.gloss: To change a steady state abruptly. To cause, or allow the occurrence of, a line break.
To stop, or to cause to stop, functioning properly or altogether. To terminate the execution of a program before normal completion.
To stop, or to cause to stop, functioning properly or altogether. To suspend the execution of a program during debugging so that the state of the program can be investigated.
The separation between lines, paragraphs or pages of a written text.
A keystroke or other signal that causes a program to terminate or suspend execution.

break movie.gloss: A crude form of text-based animation created in ATASCII, using special control characters to move the cursor and overwrite previous animation frames.

break the internet.gloss: To overwhelm a web server through organic user-driven demand, such that the server goes offline or is in danger of doing so.
To deliberately overwhelm a web server through a cyberattack such as a DDOS, such that the server goes offline or is in danger of doing so.

breakdown point.gloss: The number or proportion of arbitrarily large or small extreme values that must be introduced into a batch or sample to cause the estimator to yield an arbitrarily large result.

breaking change.gloss: A change in one part of a software system that potentially causes other components to fail; occurs most often in shared libraries of code used by multiple applications.

breakpoint.gloss: A point in a program at which operation may be interrupted during debugging so that the state of the program at that point can be investigated.

breeder.gloss: A pattern that exhibits quadratic growth by generating multiple copies of a secondary pattern, each of which then generates multiple copies of a tertiary pattern.

brianchon hexagon.gloss: A nonplanar hexagon whose three diagonals meet.

brick.gloss: An electronic device, especially a heavy box-shaped one, that has become non-functional or obsolete.
To make (an electronic device) non-functional and usually beyond repair, as a result of software or configuration issues.
Of an electronic device, to become non-functional, especially in a way beyond repair, as a result of software or configuration issues.

brickable.gloss: Able to be bricked (rendered inoperative through incorrect configuration).

bricking.gloss: The state of an electronic device being rendered completely unusable by a failed or corrupted firmware or software change.

bridge.gloss: A connection, real or abstract. A device which connects two or more computer buses, typically in a transparent manner.
A connection, real or abstract. A software component connecting two or more separate systems.
A connection, real or abstract. A system which connects two or more local area networks at layer 2 of OSI model.
A connection, real or abstract. An edge which, if removed, changes a connected graph to one that is not connected.
To connect two or more computer buses, networks etc. with a bridge.

bridge pattern.gloss: A structural design pattern that decouples an abstraction from its implementation so that the two can vary independently.

bridgeness.gloss: A measure of connectivity in certain networks

briefcase.gloss: In Microsoft Windows, a folder that supports file synchronization between itself and another folder.

brillouin zone.gloss: A uniquely defined primitive cell forming part of the reciprocal lattice, involved in calculations regarding waves in a periodic medium given by Bloch's theorem.

bring radical.gloss: Synonym of ultraradical (“root of the polynomial x⁵ + x + a, where a is a complex number”).

brittle.gloss: Poorly error- or fault-tolerant; having little in the way of redundancy or defense in depth; susceptible to catastrophic failure in the event of a relatively-minor malfunction or deviance.

broadcaster.gloss: A piece of equipment used to transmit data over a computer network.

brocard circle.gloss: A circle that passes through the circumcenter and symmedian of a given triangle, and is centered at the midpoint of the line segment joining them.

brocard point.gloss: The point inside a triangle at the intersection of the lines through each vertex such that the angle between the line and the side of the triangle when moving clockwise is the same for each vertex.

brocard triangle.gloss: The triangle formed by joining the points of intersection of the lines from each vertex of a triangle to its Brocard points.

broken diagonal.gloss: In the theory of magic squares, a set of n cells forming two parallel diagonal lines in the square.

broken source.gloss: Open source computer software that is buggy, unstable, or lacking features.

broker.gloss: An agent involved in the exchange of messages or transactions.

broket.gloss: An angle bracket: either of the symbols < and > when used as an enclosing pair.

broking.gloss: The action of a broker agent; exchange of messages or transactions involving a software agent.

brouter.gloss: A network device that acts as both a bridge and a router by routing packets for known protocols and forwarding all others, as a bridge would.

brownfield.gloss: Being a development that has to integrate with legacy systems.

browse.gloss: To navigate through hyperlinked documents on a computer, usually with a browser.

browser.gloss: Any other type of information browser.

browserify.gloss: To adopt (a script or screen element, etc.) to work inside the web browser.

browserish.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a web browser.

brun sieve.gloss: A technique for estimating the size of sifted sets of positive integers that satisfy a set of conditions expressed by congruences.

brunnian braid.gloss: A braid that becomes trivial upon removal of any one of its strings.

brunnian link.gloss: A nontrivial link that becomes a set of trivial unlinked circles if any one component is removed. In other words, cutting any loop frees all the other loops.

brush.gloss: An on-screen tool for "painting" a particular colour or texture.
A set of defined design and parameters that produce drawn strokes of a certain texture and quality.

brute force.gloss: A method of computation wherein the computer is let to try all permutations of a problem until one is found that provides a solution, in contrast to the implementation of a more intelligent algorithm.
To break a password, encryption, or any other protection mechanism by brute force.

brute-forcer.gloss: A program that performs a brute force computation.

brzozowski derivative.gloss: The set of all strings obtainable from a given set of strings by cutting off a prefix. For example, for the set { cat, cow, dog }, the Brzozowski derivative with respect to c is { at, ow }. They have applications in regular expressions.

bsc.gloss: Initialism of Basic Spacing between Centers: Used in integrated circuits to specify package mechanical dimensions. This is a theoretical true position dimension and has no tolerance.

bsde.gloss: Initialism of backward stochastic differential equation.

bsod.gloss: Initialism of blue screen of death.
Initialism of black screen of death.
To fail critically and display a blue screen of death.

bsp.gloss: Initialism of board support package (“device driver”).

btpan.gloss: Abbreviation of Bluetooth Personal Area Network.

bubble.gloss: Any of the small magnetized areas that make up bubble memory.
To apply a filter bubble, as to search results.

bubble memory.gloss: A type of non-volatile computer memory that uses a thin film of magnetic material to hold small magnetized areas, known as bubbles or domains, each storing one bit of data.

bubble sort.gloss: A sorting algorithm in which pairs of neighboring values are compared and swapped into the right order if necessary in the innermost loop.

bucket.gloss: A storage space in a hash table for every item sharing a particular key.
To categorize (data) by splitting it into buckets, or groups of related items.

bucket list.gloss: A data structure containing buckets used in a hashing algorithm.

bucket rendering.gloss: The rendering of a graphical scene in a number of portions ("buckets") that can be assigned to different processors to take advantage of parallelism.

bucket sort.gloss: A sorting algorithm that partitions an array into a number of buckets (groups of elements) which are then individually sorted, either recursively or using some other algorithm.

bucky bit.gloss: A bit (binary digit) in the binary representation of a text character that is set by means of a modifier key on the keyboard, allowing numerous characters to be produced by different combinations of keypresses.

buddy block.gloss: A block of memory associated with another block and able to be merged with it, in the system of buddy memory allocation.

buddy memory allocation.gloss: A form of memory allocation that divides memory into partitions to try to satisfy a memory request as suitably as possible.

buddy system.gloss: The use of buddy memory allocation.

buffer.gloss: Anything used to isolate or minimize the effect of one thing on another. A portion of memory set aside to temporarily store data, often before it is sent to an external device or as it is received from an external device.
To store (data) in memory temporarily while it is awaiting processing.

buffer underrun.gloss: A state occurring when a buffer used to communicate between two devices or processes is fed with data at a lower speed than the data is being read from it.

bufferbloat.gloss: Excessive buffering of packets which may cause delays (latency) or jitter (latency variation) in packet-switched networks, particularly during high load.
Delay caused by such excessive buffering.

bufferful.gloss: The amount of data that fills a buffer.

bufferize.gloss: To buffer; to store in a buffer.

bug check.gloss: An error that occurs when an operating system halts, because it has reached a condition where it can no longer operate safely.

bug compatibility.gloss: The compatibility between two systems down to the specific bugs exhibited by the implementations.

bug scrub.gloss: A regular meeting to discuss and triage unfixed problems in the software.

bugdoor.gloss: A security vulnerability caused by a bug that was intentionally added by the vendor.

bugfix.gloss: A patch or change that fixes the unwanted behaviour caused by a bug.

buglet.gloss: A minor bug in a program.

build.gloss: To construct (software) by compiling its source code.
To be converted into software by compilation, usually with minimal human intervention.
Any of various versions of a software product as it is being developed for release to users.

build artifact.gloss: Any of the files that result from a compilation process and are deployed for use.

builder pattern.gloss: A creational design pattern that intends to abstract steps of construction of objects so that different implementations of these steps can construct different representations of objects.

built-in.gloss: A function that is built into a system.

built-in function.gloss: Any function that is provided as part of a high-level language and can be executed by a simple reference with specification of arguments

built-in type.gloss: A data type provided by a programming language as a basic building block, such as integer, character or Boolean, but in some languages also list, hash table or first class function.

bulk-add.gloss: To add or input many items at once, instead of entering or creating them one by one.

bulletin board system.gloss: A type of computer system, now largely obsolete, used to exchange messages and data over a telecommunications network.

bump mapping.gloss: A technique where a perturbation to the surface normal of the object being rendered is applied to each pixel, based on a texture map, prior to calculating the illumination, so as to produce a richer, more detailed surface representation.

bundle.gloss: A directory containing related resources such as source code; application bundle.
Topological space composed of a base space and fibers projected to the base space.
To sell hardware and software as a single product.

bundle adjustment.gloss: A process used in the reconstruction of a three-dimensional model from a set of photographs, simultaneously refining the coordinates describing the scene geometry as well as the parameters of the relative motion and the optical characteristics of the cameras that took the pictures.

bundler.gloss: One who bundles software, etc. with another product.

bundleware.gloss: Software that is bundled with something else.

burn.gloss: The act or action of burning something with fire, or by analogous means; the quality or nature of an act of burning. The writing of data to a permanent storage medium like a compact disc or a ROM chip.

To cause to be consumed by fire; to destroy or otherwise impact with fire or flames. To make or produce by the application of real or figurative fire, light or burning heat. To write data to a permanent storage medium like a compact disc or a ROM chip.

To cause to be consumed by fire; to destroy or otherwise impact with fire or flames. To make or produce by the application of real or figurative fire, light or burning heat. To render subtitles into a video's content while transcoding it, making the subtitles part of the image (hardsubs).

burndown.gloss: In agile software development, a chart showing how much work remains to be completed.

burner.gloss: A device that records data or music to an optical disc, such as a CD-R or DVD-RW.
An app that creates temporary phone numbers for a user.

burrows-wheeler transform.gloss: An algorithm used in data compression that rearranges a character string into runs of similar characters.

burstable.gloss: Having the ability to exceed the normal maximum bandwidth for short periods.

burstiness.gloss: The degree to which something occurs in abrupt bursts

bursty.gloss: Occurring in abrupt bursts, especially of information

bus.gloss: A network topology with each computer connected to a single cable.

bus bridge.gloss: A device for connecting two disparate hardware buses.

bus mastering.gloss: A feature supported by many bus architectures that enables a device connected to the bus to initiate transactions.

bus stop.gloss: "⟌": The two-lined right-angled symbol used to separate quotient, divisor and dividend in long division and short division

bus topology.gloss: A (computer) network topology in which the nodes are all connected at different points to a line called a bus.

busable.gloss: capable of being used with a bus (electrical conductor or interface)

business logic.gloss: Algorithms in a software system that model real-life business objects and their interactions.

business object.gloss: An entity, in a multitiered software application, that represents a particular entity within the business, such as a customer or an order.

bustle.gloss: A cover to protect and hide the back panel of a computer or other office machine.

busy beaver.gloss: A Turing machine that attains the maximum number of steps performed, or number of non-blank symbols finally on the tape, among all Turing machines in a certain class.

busy beaver function.gloss: The mathematical function, denoted by Σ(n), that maps each positive integer n to the number of steps required for the busy beaver among machines with two colors and n states to terminate.

busy loop.gloss: A loop that actively consumes CPU cycles while waiting for an event.

butterfly keyboard.gloss: A kind of computer keyboard consisting of two separate halves, intended to facilitate typing with two hands.
A kind of computer keyboard where each key is activated by means of a scissor switch.

butterworth filter.gloss: A kind of filter designed to have as flat a frequency response as possible in the passband.

buttery smooth.gloss: Having a high refresh rate so that the subjective experience does not include flickers or pauses as the video changes frames.

button.gloss: An on-screen control that can be selected as an activator of an attached function.

buttonize.gloss: To apply bevelled edges to (a visual element), giving it the appearance of a push-button.

buzzword compliance.gloss: The practice of ensuring that a product supports a set of features considered important for marketing, regardless of whether they are valuable features.

buzzword compliant.gloss: Supporting all features considered important by marketing, regardless of their actual value.

bye.gloss: A command to exit a session.

byob.gloss: Initialism of bring your own buffer.

byoc.gloss: Initialism of bring your own container.

byok.gloss: Initialism of bring your own key; a system which allows a customer to encrypt their data using an encryption key on a cloud provider's hardware.

byol.gloss: Initialism of bring your own license (“a system by which software licenses can be used either on premises or in the cloud”).

byte.gloss: A short sequence of bits (binary digits) that can be operated on as a unit by a computer; the smallest usable machine word.
A unit of computing storage equal to eight bits, which can represent any of 256 distinct values.

byte order.gloss: Order in which bytes are written or read, in memory or through a transmission; choices being big-endian or little-endian.

byte order mark.gloss: A character indicating the endianness of a string of text.
A character indicating the endianness of a string of text. The Unicode character U+FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE.

byte pair encoding.gloss: A lossless data compression algorithm that iteratively replaces the most frequent pair of adjacent bytes in a sequence with a new byte not already present in the data.

bytecode.gloss: P-code (various forms of instruction sets designed for efficient execution by a software interpreter as well as being suitable for further compilation into machine code).

byter.gloss: A chunk of data having a size of so many bytes.

bytesexual.gloss: Capable of operating in either big-endian or little-endian mode.

bytestring.gloss: A text string treated as a series of single bytes rather than a series of characters of possibly varying storage size.

bytewise.gloss: In terms of bytes, or one byte at a time.

byzantine fault tolerance.gloss: The dependability of a fault-tolerant (distributed) computer system, where components may fail without perfect information about the state of the components.

bézier curve.gloss: A type of parametric curve defined by a set of control points, two of which are the ends of the curve, while the others determine its shape.

bézier spline.gloss: A spline consisting of a series of joined Bézier curves.

bézier surface.gloss: A type of spline that is stretched towards its defined set of control points.

bézier triangle.gloss: A type of Bézier surface created by the interpolation of a given number of values.

bézout domain.gloss: An integral domain in which the sum of two principal ideals is also a principal ideal.

büchi automaton.gloss: A type of ω-automaton that extends a finite automaton to infinite inputs. It accepts an infinite input sequence if there exists a run of the automaton that visits (at least) one of the final states infinitely often.

c family.gloss: Any one of the several programming languages which share significant features of the C programming language.

c-style comment.gloss: A (possibly multiline) comment enclosed by the symbol sequences /* and */.

c-style string.gloss: A string which uses a null value to mark its own end.

cab.gloss: Clipping of cabinet file (“a compressed library archive file”).

cabalize.gloss: To encode as a Haskell package with the ".cabal" extension, which can then be installed and interpreted using the cabal command.

cable theory.gloss: The use of mathematical models to calculate the electric current and accompanying voltage along passive neurites, particularly the dendrites that receive synaptic inputs at different sites and times.

cablegami.gloss: A technique used in the building of computer systems that involves the complex folding of flat ribbon cables as if they were origami, or the routing and organization of non-flat cables.

caccioppoli set.gloss: A set whose boundary is measurable and has (at least locally) finite measure.

cache.gloss: A store, protected and often hidden in some way, of things that may be required in the future, such that they can be retrieved rapidly. A fast temporary storage where recently or frequently used information is stored to avoid having to reload it from a slower storage medium.
To store data in a cache.

cache buster.gloss: A tag or value included in a request (such as a URL) purely to differentiate it from previous requests and thus avoid receiving a cached response.

cache language model.gloss: A type of statistical language model that assigns probabilities to word sequences based on a probability distribution.

cache stampede.gloss: A cascading failure that may occur when massively parallel systems with caching mechanisms come under very high load, leading to multiple threads of execution attempting to perform the same operation simultaneously.

cactoid.gloss: A locally connected continuum that is the closure of the union of an at most countable number of spheres and simple arcs, of which every simple closed contour is contained in one and only one of the spheres.

cactus stack.gloss: An in-tree data structure when used to implement a set of stacks.

cad/cam.gloss: The combination of computer-aided design and computer-aided manufacturing.

cadam.gloss: Acronym of computer-augmented design and manufacturing.

cadd.gloss: Initialism of computer-aided design and drafting.

caddr.gloss: Car of the cdr of the cdr in Lisp. The third element in a list.

cadence.gloss: The frequency of regular product releases.

cadlag.gloss: A function that is right continuous and has a left limit.

cadr.gloss: Car of the cdr in Lisp. The second element in a list.

caesar cipher.gloss: A simple form of encryption in which each letter in the plaintext is shifted through the alphabet a number of positions (for example A→D, B→E, C→F, etc.).

cage.gloss: A regular graph that has as few vertices as possible for its girth.

cake number.gloss: For some number n, the maximum number of regions into which a cube can be partitioned by exactly n planes.

cake-cutting.gloss: A theoretical framework for the fair division of resources which studies algorithms and rules that ensure multiple parties receive a fair or "envy-free" share of a continuous, heterogeneous good when they have different preferences for its various parts.

calabi-yau manifold.gloss: A kind of manifold having properties, such as Ricci flatness, that yield applications in theoretical physics.

calculate.gloss: To determine the value of something or the solution to something by a mathematical process.
To determine values or solutions by a mathematical process; reckon.

calculation.gloss: The act or process of calculating.

calculus.gloss: Any formal system in which symbolic expressions are manipulated according to fixed rules.

calculus of variations.gloss: The form of calculus that deals with the maxima and minima of definite integrals of functions of many variables.

calendar versioning.gloss: A versioning scheme where each release number is based on the build date, usually in the ISO 8601 format, allowing for easy sorting.

calendaring.gloss: The use of a computerized calendar to schedule events or appointments.

cali or bust.gloss: Expressing a desire to work for a company in Silicon Valley, California (especially a FAANG company).

call.gloss: To jump to (another part of a program); to perform some operation, returning to the original point on completion.
The act of jumping to a subprogram, saving the means to return to the original point.

call by sharing.gloss: An evaluation strategy where arguments passed to a function can be mutated in a way that is visible to the caller (unlike call-by-value) but access is not given to the specific variables passed as arguments (unlike call-by-reference).

call graph.gloss: A directed graph that represents relationships between called and calling subroutines in a computer program, used in code analysis.

call site.gloss: The section of code from which another section is called.

call stack.gloss: A stack that stores details of the functions called by a program in sequence, so that each function can return on completion to the code that called it.

call-by-future.gloss: An evaluation strategy in which the arguments to a function are evaluated concurrently with the function body.

call-by-name.gloss: An evaluation strategy whereby an argument to a function is evaluated each time its value is used in the function, and is not evaluated at all if its value is never used.

call-by-need.gloss: An evaluation strategy in which the arguments to a function are evaluated the first time they are used in that function.

call-by-reference.gloss: An evaluation strategy in which the arguments to a function are evaluated first, and a pointer to the result is passed to the function.

call-by-value.gloss: An evaluation strategy in which the arguments to a function are evaluated first, and the result is passed into the function.

call-with-current-continuation.gloss: A programming language operation that captures the current state of execution (the continuation) and provides it as a function that can be invoked to return to or replace that state of execution at any later time.

callable.gloss: An object of a type that can be called, such as a function.

callback.gloss: A function pointer passed as an argument to another function.

callback hell.gloss: The situation (chiefly in JavaScript) where callbacks are nested within other callbacks several levels deep, making it difficult to understand and maintain the code.

caller.gloss: A function that calls another (the callee).

calligraphic projection.gloss: A system for displaying or projecting an image composed of a beam of light or electrons directly tracing the image, as opposed to sweeping in raster order over the entire display surface.

calloc.gloss: A subroutine in the C programming language's standard library for performing dynamic memory allocation.
To allocate memory using the C programming language calloc subroutine.

callout.gloss: The invocation of an external third-party component.

calltip.gloss: A pop-up reminder of the signature of a function or method, to aid the programmer while writing code.

camel case.gloss: Especially in computer programming, and in the names of brands and organizations: a style of typography in which several words are concatenated together without any spaces between them, with the first letter of each word (sometimes excluding the first word) capitalized.

camelize.gloss: To change a variable or object name that consists of several words into camel case.

camera.gloss: The viewpoint in a three-dimensional game or simulation.

camera roll.gloss: The collection of images and videos taken on a smartphone.

canadian traveller problem.gloss: A generalization of the shortest path problem to graphs that are only partially observable (i.e. the graph is revealed while it is being explored).

canary.gloss: A value placed in memory such that it will be the first data corrupted by a buffer overflow, allowing the program to identify and recover from it.
A change that is tested by being rolled out first to a subset of machines or users before rolling out to all.
To test a software change by rolling out to a small set of machines or users before making it available to all.

canary release.gloss: A deployment strategy performed in order to reduce the risk of introducing a new software version in production by slowly rolling out the change to a small subset of users.

cancel.gloss: To remove a common factor from both the numerator and denominator of a fraction, or from both sides of an equation.

cancellation.gloss: The operation of striking out common factors, e.g. in both the dividend and divisor.

cancellative.gloss: Said of a magma that has the cancellation property.

candidate key.gloss: In the design of a database table, a column (or an irreducible group of them) able to identify every row of the table, having a unique value or set of values in each row. One of the candidate keys (abbreviated CKs) will be the primary key.

canned benchmark.gloss: A computer program designed for the sole purpose of benchmarking the hardware it's being run on.

cannot-link.gloss: The property of data points that must not be clustered into the same chunklet.

canny edge detection.gloss: The use of the Canny edge detector algorithm.

canny edge detector.gloss: An operator that uses a multistage algorithm, involving the calculus of variations, to detect the edges in an image.

canonical.gloss: Distinguished among entities of its kind, so that it can be picked out in a way that does not depend on any arbitrary choices.

canonical conjunctive normal form.gloss: Conjunctive normal form with the additional property that all of the terms of the product contain the same literals, so that the terms differ from each other only in their patterns of complementation (of their literals).

canonical disjunctive normal form.gloss: Disjunctive normal form with the additional property that all of the terms of the sum contain the same literals, so that the terms differ from each other only in their patterns of complementation (of their literals).

canonical form.gloss: A standard or normal presentation of a mathematical entity or a text string, etc.

canonical formalism.gloss: A formalism for a physical theory which is based upon the canonical equations of Hamiltonian dynamics.

canoniser.gloss: a software component, algorithm, or process that converts data with multiple possible representations into a single, standard, or "canonical" form

canonizant.gloss: A covariant that is the catalecticant of the penultimate emanant

cantellated.gloss: Generated or modified by a cantellation.

cantellation.gloss: An operation in any dimension that cuts a regular polytope at its edges and its vertices, creating a new facet in place of each edge and each vertex.

cantitruncated.gloss: Generated or modified by a cantitruncation.

cantor dust.gloss: A multidimensional version of the Cantor set, formed by taking a finite Cartesian product of the Cantor set with itself.

cantor set.gloss: A subset of an interval formed by recursively removing an interval in the middle of every connected component of the set.

cantorian.gloss: Smaller than its own power set; satisfying Cantor's theorem.

canvas.gloss: A region on which graphics can be rendered.

cap.gloss: A portion of a spherical or other convex surface.

cap off.gloss: To glue a relatively uncomplicated compact manifold to a manifold of the same dimension along (a component of the latter's boundary).

cap product.gloss: A method of adjoining a chain of degree p with a cochain of degree q, such that q ≤ p, to form a composite chain of degree p − q.

capability.gloss: A digital token allowing a user or process to interact in a specified way with an object that is subject to access control.

capacitate.gloss: To reach maximum throughput on at least part of a constrained network.

capacitated.gloss: Constrained by maximum throughput, often applied to physical networks transporting flows.

capped collection.gloss: In MongoDB, a fixed-size collection that, once the size limit has been reached, replaces the oldest record whenever a new one is added.

capping.gloss: The conversion of a polyhedron into a stellated polyhedron by raising a pyramid on each face.

caps lock.gloss: An input mode in which all letters of bicameral scripts are generated in capital letters.
A lock key on a computer keyboard that activates this mode.

captcha.gloss: A computerized test requiring the human user to perform a task deemed to be difficult to automate, such as entering a displayed series of distorted characters or describing images, to demonstrate that they are a human and not a computer program.

captive portal.gloss: A web page shown to new users of an access point before they can access the greater Internet.

capture.gloss: A particular match found for a pattern in a text string.

capture card.gloss: A circuit board allowing a computer to record video from an external source.

captureless.gloss: (of a lambda function) That has an empty capture list.

car.gloss: The first part of a cons in Lisp. The first element of a list.

card.gloss: A removable electronic device that may be inserted into a powered electronic device to provide additional capability.
Any of a set of pages or forms that the user can navigate between, and fill with data, in certain user interfaces.
A graph formed from a given graph by deleting one vertex.

card punch.gloss: A machine that punches holes in a punch card

card reader.gloss: A data input device that reads data from a card-shaped storage medium.

cardan grille.gloss: A sheet of card or thin metal, etc., used in composing secret messages. The words of the message are written through a number of holes cut arbitrarily in the sheet, and the remaining paper is then filled with irrelevant words to disguise it.

cardinal.gloss: Ellipsis of cardinal number, a number indicating quantity, or the size of a set (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3). (See Cardinal_number.)

cardinal number.gloss: A generalized kind of number used to denote the size of a set, including infinite sets.

cardinal spline.gloss: A series of curves joined to form a larger one, defined by a set of control points and an amount of tension.

cardinality.gloss: The number of elements a given set contains.
The property of a relationship between a database table and another one, specifying whether it is one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, or many-to-many.

cardioid.gloss: An epicycloid with exactly one cusp; the plane curve with polar equation ρ=1+ cos ,θ - approximately heart-shaped

cardware.gloss: The software and hardware supporting a smart card system.

caret notation.gloss: A notation where each control character is represented by a caret followed by a letter or symbol.

cargo culting.gloss: An approach that copies an existing successful approach without properly analysing and understanding it.

caricature.gloss: In facial recognition systems, a face that has been modified to look less like the average face, and thus more distinctive.

carlson symmetric form.gloss: Any of a canonical set of elliptic integrals to which all others may be reduced. They are a modern alternative to the Legendre forms, and unlike the Legendre forms they are unchanged by the exchange of certain subsets of their arguments.

carlyle circle.gloss: A certain circle in a coordinate plane associated with a quadratic equation, having the property that the solutions of the equation are the horizontal coordinates of the intersections of the circle with the horizontal axis.

carmichael number.gloss: A composite number n that satisfies the modular arithmetic congruence relation bⁿ⁻¹≡1(mod n) for all integers 1<b<n that are relatively prime to n.

carol prime.gloss: A Carol number that is also a prime number.

carousel.gloss: A visual component that displays a horizontal series of items one at a time.
A visual component that displays a horizontal series of items one at a time. Ellipsis of carousel post.
Synonym of jukebox (“automated carousel for the storage and retrieval of tapes, CD-ROMs, etc.”).

carputer.gloss: A form of personal computer or similar device designed to be installed in the dashboard of a car

carriage control character.gloss: A character, added to the beginning of each line of text to be printed on a line printer, that controls the movement of paper through the printer before each new line is printed

carriage return.gloss: The control character (0x0D in ASCII, abbreviated as CR) that originally signaled a device to perform a carriage return, but now merely indicates the end of a line of text (newline).

carrier hotel.gloss: A colocation facility for retail customers.

carrier set.gloss: the underlying set of an algebraic structure

carrier wave.gloss: Synonym of soliton (“a self-reinforcing pulse or travelling wave caused by any non-linear effect”).

carry.gloss: The bit or digit that is carried in an addition operation.

carry-in.gloss: A command that adds a carry (bit or digit that is carried in an addition operation) to an accumulator for the current digit in an addition operation.

carry-lookahead.gloss: A command that checks whether there will be a carry (bit or digit that is carried in an addition operation) for the current digit in an ongoing addition operation.

carry-out.gloss: A command that exports a carry (bit or digit that is carried in an addition operation) from the current column of an addition operation.

carryless.gloss: In which no figures are carried over.

cart.gloss: A cartridge for a computer or video game system.
Acronym of classification and regression tree.

cartan integer.gloss: Any of the scalar products a_ij=2(r_i,r_j)/(r_i,r_i) that make up the Cartan matrix of a simple Lie algebra.

cartan subalgebra.gloss: A certain kind of nilpotent subalgebra of a Lie algebra.

cartesian.gloss: Of, or pertaining to, co-ordinates based on mutually orthogonal axes.

cartesian closed category.gloss: A category which has a terminal object and which for every two objects A and B has a product A × B and an exponential object Bᴬ.

cartesian coordinate.gloss: The coordinates of a point measured from an origin along a horizontal axis from left to right (the x-axis) and along a vertical axis from bottom to top (the y-axis). This can be extended to three-dimensions by the z-axis perpendicular to the x- and y-axes.

cartesian coordinates.gloss: The coordinates of a point measured as its perpendicular distance to the right of a vertical axis (the y-axis) and its perpendicular distance above a horizontal axis (the x-axis).

cartesian equation.gloss: An equation that describes a line or plane in terms of the relationship between the coordinates on the axes involved.

cartesian grid.gloss: a regular grid consisting of squares, cubes, or more generally unit hypercubes

cartesian natural transformation.gloss: A natural transformation whose naturality squares are pullbacks.

cartesian plane.gloss: A coordinate plane, with an applied Cartesian coordinate system.

cartesian product.gloss: The set of all possible ordered pairs of elements, the being first from X, the second from Y, written X×Y. Formally, the set (x,y);|;x∈X;and;y∈Y.
qualifiers: of two sets X and Y

cartesian product.gloss: All possible combinations of rows between all of the tables listed.

An (m+n)-dimensional space, formally composed of all possible ordered pairs of points from X and Y, but thought of as an independent (m+n)-dimensional space (in the sense that if, e.g. X and Y are vector spaces, the elements of X×Y are thought of as (m+n)-tuples instead of ordered pairs) and written X×Y.
qualifiers: of an m-dimensional space X and an n-dimensional space Y

cartesian product.gloss: Any of several generalizations of the set-theoretic sense, especially one which shares the geometrical intuition outlined above, i.e. one such that the product can be thought of as an object in its own right and not just as a set of pairs.

cartesian space.gloss: Euclidean space described by Cartesian coordinates.

cartesian square.gloss: For a set X, the Cartesian product X² = X × X.

cartridge.gloss: A vessel which contains the ink or toner for a computer printer and can be easily replaced with another.
Magnetic tape storage, used for storing (backup) copies of data.
A removable enclosure containing read-only memory devices, used for rapid loading of software onto a home computer or video game console.

cascading style sheet.gloss: A stylesheet in Cascading Style Sheets format.

case.gloss: A section of code representing one of the actions of a conditional switch.

case fatality rate.gloss: A percentage derived by the division of the number of fatalities by the number of confirmed (diagnosed) cases (sufferers) of a disease.

case folding.gloss: Text normalization where uppercase and lowercase characters are treated as equivalent.

case insensitive.gloss: Treating or interpreting upper- and lowercase letters as being the same.

case mod.gloss: A modification to the outer case of a computer or video game console, to change its appearance or improve its performance.

case sensitive.gloss: Distinguishing upper- and lower-case letters. Often used in computer science to indicate a distinction is made in comparison or equality of letters based on case. For example, a case-sensitive password will not recognize "Password" and "password" as the same, but a case insensitive comparison would.

case sensitivity.gloss: The characteristic of being case sensitive; having different reactions to typed letters based on whether the letters are uppercase or lowercase.

case-based reasoning.gloss: The process of solving new problems based on the known solutions of similar problems encountered in the past.

case-sensitivity.gloss: The characteristic of being case sensitive; having different reactions to typed letters based on whether the letters are uppercase or lowercase.

casing.gloss: The state of letter case across a whole phrase or whole lines of text; the collective state/arrangement of uppercase and lowercase letters.

cassette drive.gloss: A cassette tape interface unit for computers, used to read and/or write data to/from a minicassette.

cassini oval.gloss: A plane curve defined as the set (or locus) of points in the plane such that the product of the distances to two fixed points is constant (related to an ellipse, for which the sum of the distances is constant).

cast.gloss: To change a variable type from, for example, integer to real, or integer to text.

cast away.gloss: To eliminate by means of a cast operation.

castable.gloss: Able to be cast. In particular: Capable of being cast to another data type.

casting.gloss: The act of converting between data types.

casus.gloss: A possible world, as a starting point for reasoning.

cat.gloss: A program and command in Unix that reads one or more files and directs their content to the standard output.

To dump large amounts of data on (an unprepared target), usually with no intention of browsing it carefully.

cat 5.gloss: A twisted pair cable for carrying signals, particularly for Ethernet-based computer networks.

catalan solid.gloss: The dual polyhedron of any Archimedean solid.

catalan surface.gloss: A ruled surface whose rulings are all parallel to a fixed plane.

catalecticant.gloss: A polynomial in the coefficients of a form of even degree that vanishes when the form is a sum of an unusually small number of powers of linear forms.

catastrophe.gloss: A type of bifurcation, where a system shifts between two stable states.

catastrophe theory.gloss: The branch of mathematics dealing with dynamical systems which can undergo abrupt irreversible qualitative changes due to a tiny change in parameters.

catastrophic backtracking.gloss: An excessively large amount of backtracking that occurs with certain regular expressions, due to an exponentially large number of possible matching paths to check.

catcall.gloss: In the Eiffel programming language, a run-time error caused by use of the wrong data type.

catch.gloss: To seize hold of. To handle an exception.

categorematic.gloss: Capable of being employed alone as a term.

categorical dual.gloss: For a given category C, its dual category Cᵒᵖ is obtained by reversing the direction of each one of the arrows of C.

categorical product.gloss: The limit of two (or more) objects, considered without regard to any arrows between them.

categorical proposition.gloss: A proposition that asserts or denies that members of one category (the subject term) belong to another (the predicate term). There are four types: "all S are P", "all S are not P", "some S are P", and "some S are not P".

categorification.gloss: A procedure that defines theorems in terms of category theory by mapping concepts from set theory to category theory.

categorify.gloss: To define a theorem in terms of category theory

category.gloss: A collection of objects, together with a transitively closed collection of composable arrows between them, such that every object has an identity arrow, and such that arrow composition is associative.

category reference.gloss: A reference that specifies within some taxonomy or text typology one or more defined categories into which the referenced article, computer file etc. belongs.

category theory.gloss: A branch of mathematics which deals with spaces and maps between them in abstraction, taking similar theorems from various disparate more concrete branches of mathematics and unifying them.

catenarian.gloss: Shaped like a catenary; following the curve made by a chain or rope when suspended from both ends.

catenary.gloss: The curve described by a flexible chain or a rope if it is supported at each end and is acted upon by no other forces than a uniform gravitational force due to its own weight and variations involving additional and non-uniform forces. It is described by the hyperbolic cosine function.

catenet.gloss: A system of packet-switched communication networks interconnected via gateways.

catenoid.gloss: A three-dimensional surface formed by rotation of a catenary

catenoidal.gloss: Relating to, or having the form of a catenoid

caterpillar.gloss: A set of subtrees of a tree.

caterpillar tree.gloss: A tree consisting of only a path (the spine or stalk of the tree) and vertices directly connected to (i.e. one edge away from) that path; a tree whose vertices with a degree of at least 3 are all surrounded by at most two vertices of degree two or greater.

caterpillarization.gloss: The process or the result of caterpillarizing a tree.

caterpillarize.gloss: To visualize (a tree) as a group of subtrees.

cathetus.gloss: A line perpendicular to a surface (or line); in particular, either of the sides of a right triangle other than its hypotenuse.

cauchy.gloss: Of a sequence in a metric space, whose terms become arbitrarily close to one another.

cauchy distribution.gloss: A symmetric continuous probability distribution with fat tails, with probability density function that is

cauchy problem.gloss: For a given m-order partial differential equation, the problem of finding a solution function u on ℝⁿ that satisfies the boundary conditions that, for a smooth manifold S⊂ℝⁿ, u(x)=f_0(x) and (∂ᵏu(x))/(∂nᵏ)=f_k(x), ∀x∈S, k=1…m-1, given specified functions f_k defined on, and vector n normal to, the manifold.

cauchy sequence.gloss: Any sequence x_n in a metric space with metric d such that for every ϵ>0 there exists a natural number N such that for all k,m>N, d(x_k,x_m)<ϵ.

cauchy space.gloss: A space for which notions of a Cauchy sequence and completeness exist.

cauchyan.gloss: Of or pertaining to Augustin-Louis Cauchy.

cayley table.gloss: The analogue for a group of a multiplication table.

cayley tree.gloss: A type of tree graph in which every nonleaf vertex (node) has the same constant number of branches.

cayleyan.gloss: A variety associated to a hypersurface.

cbow.gloss: Initialism of continuous bag of words.

ccaas.gloss: Acronym of call center as a service.

cddr.gloss: Cdr of the cdr in Lisp. The remainder of a list if the first two elements are removed.

cdram.gloss: Initialism of cached dynamic random-access memory.

ceiling.gloss: The smallest integer greater than or equal to a given number.

ceiling effect.gloss: The phenomenon where an independent variable no longer has an effect on a dependent variable, or the level above which variance in an independent variable is no longer measurable.

ceiling function.gloss: A function that maps a real number to the smallest integer that is no smaller than it.

cel shading.gloss: A style of non-photorealistic rendering suggesting the flat, hand-drawn appearance of a comic or cartoon.

cel-shaded.gloss: Produced using the technique of cel shading.

cell.gloss: The minimal unit of a cellular automaton that can change state and has an associated behavior.

The unit in a statistical array (a spreadsheet, for example) where a row and a column intersect.

cell-oriented programming.gloss: A programming paradigm where the fundamental unit of computation is a self-contained cell that can process and store data and communicate with other cells.

cellular automaton.gloss: An automaton consisting of cells arranged in a regular grid, in one or more dimensions. Each application of an associated rule creates a new generation, where the cells have a new configuration of values.

censor.gloss: An algorithm that approves or rejects something on grounds of taste or morality etc.

censoring.gloss: A partial obscuring of data points.

censorware.gloss: Software or hardware used to filter content on the Internet or block Internet access or restrict the running of applications or computer usage, on the basis of content being regarded as objectionable.

census.gloss: A count of the number of individual patterns within a larger pattern, most often the ash of a soup or a methuselah.

center.gloss: The point on a line that is midway between the ends.

A point on a triangle's plane that is in some sense in its middle.

The set of those elements (of a given algebraic structure) that commute with every other element, usually denoted Z(G). In the case of (semi-)groups, it is required that they commute under the (semi-)group operation; in the case of rings and (Lie) algebras, under multiplication (i.e. the bracket for Lie algebras)

centerless.gloss: Whose center is trivial (contains only the identity element).

centerpoint.gloss: A generalization of the median to data in higher-dimensional Euclidean space.

centipawn.gloss: One hundredth of the value of a pawn, especially for calculation purposes in computer chess.

centipede game.gloss: An extensive form game in which two players take turns choosing either to take a slightly larger share of an increasing pot, or to pass the pot to the other player. The payoffs are arranged so that if one passes the pot to one's opponent and the opponent takes the pot on the next round, one receives slightly less than if one had taken the pot on this round, but after an additional switch the potential payoff will be higher. Therefore, although at each round a player has an incentive to take the pot, it would be better for them to wait.

clock cycle.gloss: The time between two adjacent pulses of the oscillator that regulates the tempo of the computer processor.

clock generator.gloss: a circuit that produces a timing signal for use in synchronizing a circuit's operation.

clock speed.gloss: The rate, measured in hertz, at which a processor performs its fundamental operations.

clockable.gloss: Of an ordinal such that an infinite-time Turing machine can complete in so many steps of computation.

clocksource.gloss: A source of time used by an application, such as a hardware clock.

cloner.gloss: A software program that duplicates media.

cloop.gloss: A compression technology for Linux files stored on a read-only block device that allows files to be decompressed on the fly.

Lacking endpoints. For parametric curves, with the same image for the ends of the domain.

closed beta.gloss: A testing arrangement in which a beta test version of software is distributed to a small group of testers.

closed formula.gloss: A formula which has no free occurrences of variables; or equivalently, in which all occurrences of variables are bound.

closed interval.gloss: an interval in the real number line which contains its supremum and infimum.

closed loop.gloss: A path whose initial point is equal to its terminal point.

closed-source.gloss: Whose constituent makeup, or source code, is not made publicly available.

closeness.gloss: The shortest path between two vertices in a graph.

closing.gloss: In morphology, the erosion of the dilation of a set.

closing form.gloss: A method to end an implemented functionality.

clothoid.gloss: A plane curve whose curvature at any point is proportional to distance along it.

cloud-native.gloss: Able to take full advantage of running on public, private, or hybrid cloud computing environments.

club.gloss: A set which is both closed and unbounded.

clubsuit.gloss: A family of combinatorial principles that is a weaker version of the corresponding diamond principle.

cluebat.gloss: A bat (club) with which someone clueless is struck (figuratively or in one's imagination).

clui.gloss: Acronym of command line user interface.

cluon.gloss: The imaginary elementary particle of cluefulness; the anti-particle to the bogon.

cluster.gloss: A bunch or group of several discrete items that are close to each other. A group of computers that work together.

A bunch or group of several discrete items that are close to each other. clustered.gloss: Used as the clustering key of a clustered index.

clusterer.gloss: That which divides data etc. into clusters.

clustering.gloss: The undesirable contiguous grouping of elements in a hash table.

clustering coefficient.gloss: A quantitative measure of how often the nodes of a graph cluster together, defined as the ratio of the number of links among the nodes to the maximum possible number of links.

clustering illusion.gloss: The tendency to erroneously perceive random streaks and clusters arising in small samples from random distributions as being non-random.

clustering key.gloss: A database field whose values serve as the keys of a clustered index.

cmdlet.gloss: A specialized .NET class implementing a particular operation in Windows PowerShell.

cmyk.gloss: Initialism of cyan, magenta, yellow, key: the subtractive primary colour model used in colour printing.

cnc.gloss: Initialism of computer numerical control or computerized numerical control.

cnile.gloss: A C programmer, especially one who dismisses newer programming languages.

cnoidal.gloss: Describes a travelling wave whose amplitude is constricted; e.g. a wave in shallow water.

co-host.gloss: To store data on a shared server (as in web hosting).

co-occurrence network.gloss: A text analysis method that visually represents relationships among entities based on their co-occurrence in electronic text.

coalesce.gloss: To convert a null value to a defined value.

coamoeba.gloss: The graph of the real part of the logarithms of a polynomial equation under the argument mapping.

coassociative.gloss: Describing the relationship, in a coalgebra, that is the dual of an associative one.

coassociativity.gloss: A relationship that is the dual of associativity.

coaster.gloss: Something that coasts or is used to coast. A useless compact disc or DVD, such as one that was burned incorrectly or has become corrupted.

coatom.gloss: In a partially ordered set, a non-unit element that has no element above it other than the unit (assuming that the poset has a top element, its "unit").

coatomistic.gloss: Of a set: such that every element is the greatest lower bound of a set of coatoms.

coaugmentation.gloss: A natural transformation from the identity functor to a certain endofunctor.

coaxis.gloss: One of the directional motion vectors perpendicular to a cocone.

cob.gloss: Initialism of chip on board (an LED module or integrated circuit bonded to a circuit board)

cobwebbing.gloss: A graphical technique for solving discrete-time systems, useful in finding the stationary points.

cocommutative.gloss: Describing the relationship, in a coalgebra, that is the equivalent of a commutative one.

cocomplete.gloss: In which all small colimits exist.

code-first.gloss: Of a software development approach, where the database schema is created based on code written by developers rather than designing the database first.

code-lift.gloss: To copy an entire function without understanding it to use outside a secured system

codebase.gloss: The body of source code used to create a particular computer program or software component.

coding time.gloss: The amount of time required from the first commit, to a branch, eventually the submission of a pull request.

codirection.gloss: An equation for a hyperplane in the tangent space modulo a factor that is a positive constant; cotangent direction.

coercion.gloss: Conversion of a value of one data type to a value of another data type.

coevent.gloss: A particular form of truth function associated with quantum mechanics.

coflow.gloss: Any of a series of flows that have a common source and destination

The dual of a free structure.

cofunction.gloss: The trigonometric function of the complement of the supplied angle.
A costatement that takes the form of a function and can accept parameters and return a value.

cofunctionality.gloss: The condition of being a cofunction

cogalois.gloss: Pertaining to the correspondence between subfields of a radical field extension with subgroups of a cogroup that is a Galois group.
