cogredient.gloss: Describing two or more variables that undergo the same linear transformations.

coincidence.gloss: A fixed point of a correspondence; a point of a variety corresponding to itself under a correspondence.

coloop.gloss: An element in a matroid that belongs to no circuit or (equivalently) belongs to every basis.

column vector.gloss: An n×1 matrix that represents a vector.

comatrix.gloss: Adjoint; The transposed matrix of the cofactors of the entries of a matrix.

command processing overhead time.gloss: The amount of processing time which a device requires, prior to the execution of a command.

command-line interface.gloss: Alternative form of command line interface.

command-line interpreter.gloss: A computer program that reads lines of text entered by a user and interprets them in the context of a given operating system or programming language.

commensurable.gloss: (of two or more numbers) Divisible by the same number ᵂᴾ

commensurate.gloss: Describing two numbers within the same Archimedean class, so that neither is infinitely larger than the other.

commensurator.gloss: The number by which two commensurable numbers are divisible an integral number of times

comment.gloss: A remark embedded in source code in such a way that it will be ignored by the compiler or interpreter, typically to help people to understand the code.
To comment out (code); to disable by converting into a comment.

comment out.gloss: To disable a section of source code by converting it into a comment.

commentable.gloss: Capable of being marked with a comment.

commentation.gloss: The use of comments in source code.

commify.gloss: To insert commas into (a piece of code).

commit.gloss: To make a set of changes permanent.
To integrate new revisions into the public or master version of a file in a version control system.
The act of committing (e.g. a database transaction), making it a permanent change; such a change.
The submission of source code or other material to a source control repository.

commit point.gloss: In a DBMS, a point in time at which all updates to a database, or group of records in a database, are guaranteed to have been written to disk, and the journal or log records of that action have also been so committed. Future updates may be undone to that point if necessary.

committable.gloss: Able to be committed as a transaction; able to be implemented as a whole or rolled back as a whole, so that no partial implementation can occur.

committer.gloss: A person who is authorized to make changes to source code or other material in a repository.

commodorian.gloss: An employee of the computer company Commodore International, or a fan of its products.

common antilogarithm.gloss: A base-ten antilogarithm; ten raised to a certain power.

common coupling.gloss: a form of coupling in which multiple modules share the same global data

common denominator.gloss: Any integer that is a common multiple of the denominators of two or more fractions.

common difference.gloss: The constant added to each element of an arithmetic progression to obtain the next.

common factor.gloss: A number that can divide two different numbers, without leaving a remainder.

common knowledge.gloss: A special kind of knowledge for a group of agents, such that when all the agents in a group G know p, they all know that they know p, they all know that they all know that they know p, and so on ad infinitum.

common multiple.gloss: A number which may be divided by any of a given set of numbers without a remainder.

common ratio.gloss: The ratio of each term of a geometric progression to the term preceding it.

communality.gloss: A measure of variance in factor analysis.

communication theory.gloss: A field that studies the technical process of information.

commutant.gloss: The subset of all elements of a semigroup that commute with the elements of a given subset

commutate.gloss: To commute; to be invariant under a reversal of the positions of operands.

commutative.gloss: Such that the order in which the operands are taken does not affect their image under the operation.
Such that any two sequences of morphisms with the same initial and final positions compose to the same morphism.

commutative algebra.gloss: The branch of algebra concerned with commutative rings and objects related to them (such as ideals and modules).
Any algebra (mathematical structure) in which the multiplication operation is commutative.

commutative ring.gloss: A ring whose multiplicative operation is commutative.

commutator.gloss: A binary map in a given group G, given by [g, h] = ghg⁻¹h⁻¹, where g and h are elements of G, which yields the group's identity if and only if the group operation commutes for g and h.

commutator subgroup.gloss: The subgroup of a specified group generated by the larger group's commutators.

commute.gloss: Of an operation, to be commutative, i.e. to have the property that changing the order of the operands does not change the result.

comodernism.gloss: The property of being the dual of something modernistic.

comonad.gloss: A monad of the opposite category.

comonotonic.gloss: Of a random vector, having components that can be represented as increasing functions of a single random variable.

comorphism.gloss: A mapping associated with a morphism that, when applied to every member of the morphism, results in the same value as the morphism applied to the image of every member.

compact.gloss: Of a topological space: Such that every open cover has a finite subcover. In a metric space, this is equivalent to being sequentially compact. In metric spaces with the Heine-Borel property, this is equivalent to being closed and bounded.
Of a topological space: Compact in the above sense and moreover Hausdorff.

compact space.gloss: Any topological subset of Euclidean space that is a compact set

compactification.gloss: Any of various procedures of enlarging a topological space to make it compact.
The space resulting from any such procedure.

compactify.gloss: To enlarge (a topological space) in order to render it compact.

companion.gloss: A knot in whose neighborhood another, specified knot meets every meridian disk.

comparable.gloss: Constituting a pair in a particular partial order.

comparable function.gloss: Either of a pair of functions that have the same domain and that the values of one are equal to or greater than the other for all points in that domain.

comparand.gloss: A thing to which something is compared.

comparate.gloss: One of two things being compared.

comparator.gloss: An application or program that compares prices, rates, tariffs of flights, smartphones, cars, etc.

compare.gloss: An instruction or command that compares two values or states.

comparison operator.gloss: a binary operator that tests for equality or inequality and evaluates to true or false

compartmentalization.gloss: The act or process of dividing a complex task or structure into smaller, often more manageable pieces. The act of dividing complex code into libraries with common functionality to help make the process of programming more manageable and reusable.

compass error.gloss: The combination of variation and deviation which is the horizontal angle between the direction indicated by a magnetic compass and true north.

compatibility.gloss: the ability to execute a given program on different types of computers without modification of the program or the computers. See backward compatibility and forward compatibility.

the capability that allows the substitution of one subsystem (storage facility), or of one functional unit (e.g., hardware, software), for the originally designated system or functional unit in a relatively transparent manner, without loss of information and without the introduction of errors.

compiland.gloss: A file or other single unit of program source code that can be compiled.

compilate.gloss: To use a compiler to process source code and produce executable code.

compilation.gloss: Translation of source code into object code by a compiler.

compile.gloss: To use a compiler to process source code and produce executable code.
To be successfully processed by a compiler into executable code.

compile-and-go.gloss: Having compilation, assembly and linking steps performed as an initial stage of program execution, and not as distinct separate processes.

compile-time.gloss: Operations performed by a compiler (the “compile-time operations”).
Programming language requirements that must be met by source code for it to be successfully compiled (the “compile-time requirements”).
Properties of the program that can be reasoned about during compilation.

compiler.gloss: A computer program that transforms source code into object code.

complement.gloss: An angle which, together with a given angle, makes a right angle.
Given two sets, the set containing one set's elements that are not members of the other set (whether a relative complement or an absolute complement).
An expression related to some other expression such that it is true under the same conditions that make other false, and vice versa.
A bit with the opposite value to the given one; the logical complement of a number.
The diminished radix complement of a number; the nines' complement of a decimal number; the ones' complement of a binary number.
The radix complement of a number; the two's complement of a binary number.
The numeric complement of a number.

complementary angle.gloss: An angle that, when added to another referenced angle, produces a right angle.

complementary angles.gloss: A pair of angles that sum to a right angle.

complementary function.gloss: For a nonhomogeneous linear differential equation a_ny⁽ⁿ⁾+a_n-1y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾+⋯+a_1y'+a_0y=g(x), the general solution of the associated homogenous linear differential equation a_ny⁽ⁿ⁾+a_n-1y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾+⋯+a_1y'+a_0y=0.

complementary nondeterministic polynomia.gloss: The set, or property, of a problem with a yes/no answer in which the complementary yes/no problem calls for nondeterministic polynomial time.

complementary region.gloss: A connected component of the complement in a manifold of a lamination of that manifold.

complementation.gloss: The replacement of a set by its complement

completable.gloss: That can be expanded to a total algebra.

complete.gloss: In which every Cauchy sequence converges to a point within the space.
qualifiers: of a metric space or topological group

complete.gloss: In which every set with a lower bound has a greatest lower bound.
In which all small limits exist.
In which every semantically valid well-formed formula is provable.
qualifiers: of a proof system of a formal system with respect to a given semantics

complete.gloss: That is in a given complexity class and is such that every other problem in the class can be reduced to it (usually in polynomial time or logarithmic space).

complete bipartite graph.gloss: A biclique, a bipartite graph such that every vertex of one set is connected to every vertex of the other.

complete graph.gloss: A graph where every pair of vertices is connected by an edge.

complete lattice.gloss: A partially ordered set in which all subsets have both a supremum (join) and an infimum (meet).

complete measure.gloss: A measure such that, for every set of measure zero belonging to its domain, all subsets of that set are also assigned measure zero by the given measure.

complete partial order.gloss: Three similar yet distinct classes of partially ordered sets, characterized by their completeness.

complete the square.gloss: To write a quadratic polynomial in terms of the square of a binomial.

completely metrizable.gloss: Of a set, that it is metrizable and, under such given metric, complete.

completeness.gloss: The property of a logical theory that whenever a wff is valid then it must also be a theorem. Symbolically, letting T represent a theory within logic L, this can be represented as the property that whenever T⊨ϕ is true, then T⊢ϕ must also be true, for any wff φ of logic L.

completeness axiom.gloss: The following axiom (applied to an ordered field): for any subset of the given ordered field, if there is any upper bound for this subset, then there is also a supremum for this subset, and this supremum is an element of the given ordered field (though not necessarily of the subset).

completion.gloss: The act of making a metric space complete by adding points.
The space resulting from such an act.

completory.gloss: Serving to fulfil or complete (e.g. complete a set).

complex.gloss: Having the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i is (by definition) the imaginary square root of −1.
Whose range is a subset of the complex numbers.
Whose coefficients are complex numbers; defined over the field of complex numbers.
A curve, polygon or other figure that crosses or intersects itself.

complex analysis.gloss: The branch of mathematics that studies holomorphic functions.

complex conjugate.gloss: Of a complex number x, the complex number ◌̅x formed by changing the sign of the imaginary part: The complex conjugate of a + bi is a - bi.

complex conjugation.gloss: The unary operation which maps complex numbers to their complex conjugates.

complex fraction.gloss: Any fraction in which either or both of the numerator or denominator are themselves fractions.

complex function.gloss: A function whose range is a subset of the set of complex numbers.

complex geometry.gloss: The study of complex manifolds, complex algebraic varieties, and functions of several complex variables.

complex line.gloss: A 1-dimensional affine subspace of a vector space over the complex numbers.

complex measure.gloss: A function whose domain is a σ-algebra, whose codomain is the set of complex numbers, and which is countably additive.

complex number.gloss: A number of the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i denotes the imaginary unit.

complex plane.gloss: A representation of the space of complex numbers.

complex projective line.gloss: A complex line (especially, the set of complex numbers regarded as such) endowed with a point at infinity (thus becoming a projective line); (more formally) the set of equivalence classes of ordered pairs (α, β) of complex numbers, not both zero, with respect to the equivalence relation "(α, β) ≡ (λα, λβ) for all nonzero complex λ".

complex-differentiable.gloss: That is differentiable and satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann equations on a subset of the complex plane.

complexification.gloss: An extension from a basis on real numbers to a basis on complex numbers.

complexity.gloss: The smallest number of ones that can be used to represent a given integer, using no other digits and any number of additions, multiplications, and parentheses.

complexity function.gloss: A function that counts the number of distinct factors (substrings of consecutive symbols) in a string of symbols;

A function that counts the number of distinct factors (substrings of consecutive symbols) in a string of symbols;
(of a formal language) a function that counts the number of words of a given length. a function that counts the number of words of a given length.
A function representing the computational complexity an algorithm.

complexity theory.gloss: The study and classification of decision problems by the computational resources—such as time and space—needed by the programs that solve the problems.

component.gloss: A connected subgraph that is not part of any larger connected subgraph.

component-oriented.gloss: Of or pertaining to a software development approach that focuses on building components that are loosely-coupled and reusable.

composability.gloss: The condition of being modular in a variety of ways.

composite.gloss: Having factors other than itself and one; not prime and not one.

composite function.gloss: A function of one or more independent variables, at least one of which is itself a function of one or more other independent variables; a function of function(s).

composite key.gloss: A key constituted by several fields, including one which is not a superkey.

composite number.gloss: A (nonzero) natural number that is expressible as the product of two (or more) natural numbers other than itself and 1.

composite pattern.gloss: A structural (and partitioning) design pattern where a group of objects are to be treated in the same way as a single instance of an object.

composite type.gloss: A data type that can be constructed in a programming language out of that language's primitive types and other composite types; exemplified by array, structure, and class.

composition.gloss: Applying a function to the result of another.

composition algebra.gloss: A non-associative (not necessarily associative) algebra, A, over some field, together with a nondegenerate quadratic form, N, such that N(xy) = N(x)N(y) for all x, y ∈ A.

compositor.gloss: A system that puts images together in a buffer (such as individual windows on a desktop) to generate a final display image.

compositorial.gloss: The product of all composite numbers less than or equal to a particular number.

compositum.gloss: Given a field extension F/K and subextensions A and B, the smallest subextension that contains both A and B.

compound.gloss: Dealing with numbers of various denominations of quantity, or with processes more complex than the simple process.

compound key.gloss: A key which is constituted by several fields.

compound pattern.gloss: A design pattern that combines at least two patterns into a solution that solves a recurring or general problem.

compound symbol.gloss: A symbol made by joining two or more others with punctuation (normally a period/full stop).

comprehension.gloss: The totality of intensions, that is, attributes, characters, marks, properties, or qualities, that the object possesses, or else the totality of intensions that are pertinent to the context of a given discussion.
A compact syntax for generating a collection in some programming languages, traditionally lists in functional programming languages.

compress.gloss: To make digital information smaller by encoding it using fewer bits.

compressed sensing.gloss: A signal processing technique for efficiently acquiring and reconstructing a signal, by finding solutions to underdetermined linear systems.

compressible.gloss: Able to be compressed. Of a surface embedded in a 3-dimensional manifold, containing a circle that does not serve as the boundary of a disk that lies in the surface, but does serve as boundary of a disk that lies in the ambient manifold.

compression.gloss: The process by which data is compressed.

compression ratio.gloss: The ratio of the size of compressed data to the size of the original uncompressed data.

compressor.gloss: A program or algorithm for compressing data.

compspec.gloss: Abbreviation of completion specification, the file read by a shell that allows to tab-complete arguments for specific commands.

computability.gloss: The property of being computable by purely mechanical means.

computability theory.gloss: The branch of the theory of computation that studies which problems are computationally solvable using different models.

computable.gloss: Of a problem, solvable by a Turing machine or any thereto Turing-equivalent model; Turing-computable.
of a number, able to be approximated to arbitrary precision by a computable function
Of a countably infinite set, having a computable indicator function.

computable analysis.gloss: Mathematical analysis of computable numbers and functions.

computable function.gloss: A mathematical function that can be computed using an abstract computation machine such as Turing machine.

computation history.gloss: a sequence of steps taken by an abstract machine in the process of computing its result.

computation time.gloss: The total amount of time required by a computer to perform a computational process.

computation tree logic.gloss: A particular modal logic of branching time with operators "next", "globally", "finally" or "eventually", "until", and "weak until".

computational chemistry.gloss: The use of computation to predict the structure, properties and reactions of molecules

computational complexity theory.gloss: A theory focusing on classifying computational problems according to their resource usage, and relating these classes to each other.

computational design.gloss: The development of a computational theory of design.
The design of products and processes through the use of digital means, integrating digital technology.

computational fluid dynamics.gloss: The study of computational algorithms to solve mathematical problems in the field of fluid dynamics.

computational geometry.gloss: A field of study, within computer science, devoted to algorithms that solve problems formulated in geometric terms.

computational humor.gloss: A field within computational linguistics and artificial intelligence that leverages computers for research on humor.

computational intelligence.gloss: A field of study that covers traditional artificial intelligence together with neural networks and fuzzy systems etc.

computational lexicology.gloss: The use of computers to analyze lexicons, especially machine-readable dictionaries.

computational linguistics.gloss: An interdisciplinary field dealing with the statistical and/or rule-based modeling of natural language from a computational perspective. This modeling is not limited to any particular field of linguistics.

computational semantics.gloss: The study of automating the creation and interpretation of meaning representations in natural language expressions.

computational social choice.gloss: A field of study examining collective decision-making processes (social choice) using computational methods.
A specific social choice or decision reached by a computational process.

computationally secure.gloss: Not decodable with all available computer power.

computer architecture.gloss: The conceptual structure around which a given computer is designed.

computer core.gloss: a computer processing center or central computer

computer graphics.gloss: The representation and manipulation of pictorial data by a computer.
The various technologies used to create and manipulate such pictorial data.
A sub-field of computer science which studies methods for digitally synthesizing and manipulating visual content.

computer illiteracy.gloss: The inability to use a personal computer.

computer illiterate.gloss: Unable to operate a personal computer.

computer language.gloss: A language that is used internally by computers, including programming languages, machine languages, query languages, markup languages, etc.

computer literacy.gloss: The ability to operate a personal computer, including its associated hardware and software (but not necessarily to understand the underlying electronics or a programming language).

computer literate.gloss: Able to operate a personal computer and its associated software and hardware, and to understand most of the underlying concepts (but not necessarily the electronics, or a programming language).

computer model.gloss: A computer program, or network of computers, that attempts to simulate an abstract model of a particular system.

computer network.gloss: A group of computers that use a set of common communication protocols over digital interconnections for the purpose of sharing resources located on or provided by the network nodes.

computer programming.gloss: The process of designing, writing, testing, debugging, and maintaining the source code of computer programs.

computer system.gloss: A system for computing that includes the physical computing unit itself and its peripherals.
Any system based around computer technology, such as a software package.

computer technician.gloss: A person who repairs computers, typically both hardware and software.

computer virus.gloss: A program which can covertly transmit itself between computers via networks (especially the Internet) or removable storage such as disks and USB drives by inserting its code into other executable files, often causing damage to systems and data.

computerize.gloss: To convert a manual function or system into a computer system.
To equip with a computer or a computer system.
To enter data into such a system.

comultiplication.gloss: The equivalent of multiplication in a coalgebra.

conatural.gloss: Being the dual of a natural entity.

concatenation.gloss: The operation of joining multiple character strings.
A character string formed by joining multiple character strings.

concatenation tree.gloss: A tree data structure whose internal nodes represent the concatenation of their child branches.

concave.gloss: Not convex; having at least one internal angle greater than 180 degrees.

concave envelope.gloss: For a given set S⊆ℝⁿ and real-valued function f defined on the convex hull conv(S), the lowest-valued concave function that overestimates or equals f over S.
qualifiers: of a function on a set

concave function.gloss: The negative of the convex function.

concavifiability.gloss: Capability of being concavified (being made concave).

concavifiable.gloss: Capable of being concavified (being made concave).

concavification.gloss: The process of converting to concave form.

concept drift.gloss: The tendency of a statistical model to become less and less accurate over time in real-world conditions.

concern.gloss: Any set of information that affects the code of a computer program.

conchoid.gloss: Any of a family of curves defined as the locus of points p, such that each p is on a line that passes through a given fixed point P and intersects a given curve, C, and the distance from p to the point of intersection with C is a specified constant (note that for nontrivial cases two such points p satisfy the criteria, and the resultant curve has two parts).

conchoidal.gloss: Of or pertaining to a conchoid; that may be defined as a conchoid.

conclude.gloss: to deduce, to infer (develop a causal relation)

conclusion.gloss: In an argument or syllogism, the proposition that follows as a necessary consequence of the premises.

conclusion indicator.gloss: A word or phrase that signals a conclusion in an argument, such as: therefore, thus, so, hence, consequently, accordingly, for this reason, as a result, which shows that, ergo, etc.

concolic.gloss: Having elements of both concrete (normal) and symbolic processing.

concomitant.gloss: An invariant homogeneous polynomial in the coefficients of a form, a covariant variable, and a contravariant variable.

concordance.gloss: A listing, often lemmatized and alphabetized, showing the places in a text, especially the Bible, where each word or phrase may be found, and its immediate context in each place. A listing, usually tokenized, where every word or phrase in a corpus can be found alongside its immediate context in each usage.

concrete.gloss: Real, actual, tangible. Analogous to the categories of algebraic objects which category theory was created to generalize, in the sense of having objects which can be thought of as sets equipped with some additional structure. Formally, equipped with a faithful functor to the category of sets.
A term designating both a quality and the subject in which it exists; a concrete term.

concurrency.gloss: A property of systems where several processes execute at the same time.

concurrency pattern.gloss: A design pattern that deal with the multi-threaded programming paradigm.

concurrent.gloss: Designed to run independently, rather than sequentially, using various mechanisms, such as threads, event loops or time-slicing.

concurvity.gloss: The condition of having the same curvature

condensation.gloss: For a given directed graph G, a directed acyclic graph with one vertex for each strongly connected component of G, and an edge connecting pairs of components that contain the two endpoints of at least one edge in G.

condensation point.gloss: (said to be "of" a given subset of a topological space) a point whose every neighborhood contains uncountably many points belonging to the given subset

conditional.gloss: Stating that one sentence is true if another is true.
A statement that one sentence is true if another is.
An instruction that branches depending on the truth of a condition at that point.

conditional assembly language.gloss: The section of an assembly language that is used to write macros.

conditional comment.gloss: A comment in source code that can be interpreted as a directive by some systems, but is ignored by those others that are not aware of the convention; formerly used to overcome compatibility issues between web browsers.

conditional entropy.gloss: The portion of a random variable's own Shannon entropy which is independent from another, given, random variable.

conditional logic.gloss: A set of rules that lets a computer make decisions and run different blocks of code based on whether specific conditions are true or false.

conditional probability distribution.gloss: The probability distribution of a random variable given the known outcome of another random variable.

conditional proof.gloss: A proof showing that if an assumption A is true then a consequent statement or conclusion B must also be true, i.e. B is true on the condition that A is true.

conducible.gloss: Able to be decomposed into a direct sum of ideals, such that each ideal corresponds to a certain structure or property.

conductor.gloss: An ideal of a ring that measures how far it is from being integrally closed

conduit.gloss: A channel or pathway through which something is conducted, carried, etc. Any pattern, typically composed of still lifes or oscillators, used to transfer an active region to another location without being destroyed or permanently modified in the process.

cone.gloss: A surface of revolution formed by rotating a segment of a line around another line that intersects the first line.
A solid of revolution formed by rotating a triangle around one of its altitudes.
A space formed by taking the direct product of a given space with a closed interval and identifying all of one end to a point.

An object V together with an arrow going from V to each object of a diagram such that for any arrow A in the diagram, the pair of arrows from V which subtend A also commute with it. (Then V can be said to be the cone’s vertex and the diagram which the cone subtends can be said to be its base.)
A set of formal languages with certain desirable closure properties, in particular those of the regular languages, the context-free languages and the recursively enumerable languages.

cone tracing.gloss: A variation of ray tracing that uses cones instead of rays.

conference matrix.gloss: A square matrix C with 0 on the diagonal and +1 and −1 off the diagonal, such that CᵀC is a multiple of the identity matrix I.

confidence interval.gloss: A range defined such that there is a fixed probability that the value of the measured parameter will fall within the range.

confidence level.gloss: The probability that a measured quantity will fall within a given confidence interval.

confidence limits.gloss: For a statistical sample a pair of values that delimit the interval for which there is a certain probability that the true value of some deduced variable lies between those values.

configuration.gloss: A finite set of points and lines (and sometimes planes), generally with equal numbers of points per line and equal numbers of lines per point.
The way a computing environment (physical or software) is set up or customized to the needs of its users.
The process of customizing a computing environment in this way.

configuration language.gloss: A specialized language designed to define and manage the settings, parameters, and operational behavior of software applications, systems, or infrastructure.

configuration section.gloss: The part of the environment division of a COBOL program that specifies the computer that the compiled code is to run on, and hence the instruction set that the compiler should use.

configurator.gloss: A small software application intended to assist in the configuration of a particular part of the system.

confirmshaming.gloss: A dark pattern that encourages the user to make a choice by presenting the alternative as confirming a negative trait (e.g. "No thanks, I don't want to help by donating").

confluence.gloss: A property describing which terms can be rewritten with other, equivalent terms.

confluent.gloss: Exactly the same size as another triangle.

Given a binary operation →_β on a set A, and its reflexive, transitive closure ↠_β , then, for all a1, a2, and a3 in A, if a1 →_β a2 and a1 →_β a3, then there must exist an a4 in A such that a2 ↠_β a4 and a3 ↠_β a4.

conformal.gloss: That preserves angles between intersecting curves.

conformal geometry.gloss: The study of conformal (angle-preserving) transformations on a space;

The study of conformal (angle-preserving) transformations on a space;
(formally) an ordered pair comprising a space and the group of conformal transformations that act on the space. an ordered pair comprising a space and the group of conformal transformations that act on the space.

conformal mapping.gloss: A mapping, between points of one coordinate system and another, in which the angles of intersection between pairs of curves are preserved.

conformality.gloss: The condition (of a map) of being conformal.

confounder.gloss: A factor, in data analysis, that causes the effects of two distinct processes to be indistinguishable; a confounding variable.

confounding variable.gloss: An extraneous variable in a statistical model that correlates (positively or negatively) with both the dependent variable and the independent variable.

confused deputy.gloss: A computer program that is innocently fooled by some other party into misusing its authority.

congruence.gloss: A relation between two numbers indicating they give the same remainder when divided by some given number.
The quality of being isometric — roughly, the same measure and shape.
Matrix similarity by an orthogonal matrix.
Any equivalence relation defined on an algebraic structure which is preserved by operations defined by the structure.

congruence class.gloss: An equivalence class of an equivalence relation that is a congruence.

congruent.gloss: Having a difference divisible by a modulus.

congruential.gloss: That uses congruency (division by a modulus)

conharmonic.gloss: Related through a harmonic division; having a cross-ratio of -1.

conic section.gloss: Any of the four distinct shapes that are the intersections of a cone with a plane, namely the circle, ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola.

conic section directrix.gloss: A fixed straight line that, along with the focus, defines the set of points on a conic section.

conical.gloss: Of or relating to a cone or cones.

conical surface.gloss: Synonym of cone (“a surface of revolution formed by rotating a segment of a line around another line that intersects the first line or a solid of revolution formed by rotating a triangle around one of its altitudes”).

conics.gloss: The branch of geometry which treats of the cone and the curves which arise from its sections.

conifold.gloss: A certain generalization of a manifold, capable of containing conical singularities.

conjecture.gloss: A statement likely to be true based on available evidence, but which has not been formally proven.

conjoin.gloss: To combine two sets, conditions, or expressions by a logical AND; to intersect.

conjugacy.gloss: The condition or state of being conjugate.

conjugacy class.gloss: A subset of a group which is an equivalence class in the quotient set of the group divided by conjugation as equivalence relation.

conjugate.gloss: To multiply on the left by one element and on the right by its inverse.
More generally, any of a set of irrational or complex numbers that are zeros of the same polynomial with integral coefficients.
Given a field extension L / K and an element α ∈ L, any other element β ∈ L that is another root of the minimal polynomial of α over K.
qualifiers: of an element of an extension field

conjugate.gloss: Presenting themselves simultaneously and having reciprocal properties; said of quantities, points, lines, axes, curves, etc.

conjugate angles.gloss: A set of angles that sum to 360 degrees.

conjugate axis.gloss: Either of two axes in a conic section, such that each is parallel to the tangent at the extremity of the other.

conjugate transpose.gloss: The transpose of a matrix, after replacing each element with its complex conjugate.

conjugation.gloss: A mapping sending x to gxg⁻¹, where g and x are elements of a group; an inner automorphism.
A function which negates the non-real part of a complex or hypercomplex number; a complex conjugation.

conjugator.gloss: A function g, such that there is a conjugation mapping x to gxg⁻¹.

conjunction.gloss: The proposition resulting from the combination of two or more propositions using the ∧ ( and ) operator.

conjunctive.gloss: Of or relating to logical conjunction.

conjunctive normal form.gloss: The form of a Boolean formula that the formula has if the formula is a conjunction of disjunctions of literals, such as “(A or B or C) and (D or E or not F)”.

connascence.gloss: A relationship between two or more elements of software in which changing one necessitates changing the others in order to maintain overall correctness; a metric for such a relationship.

connect time.gloss: The total amount of time spent by a user of a computer connected to a network.
The amount of time during which a user of a remote terminal is connected with a time-sharing system.

connectance.gloss: The fraction of all possible links in a network that are realized.

connected.gloss: That cannot be partitioned into two nonempty open sets.
Having a path, either directed or undirected, connecting every pair of vertices.

connected component.gloss: A connected subset that is, moreover, maximal with respect to being connected.

connected graph.gloss: A graph in which there is a route of edges and nodes connecting any two nodes.

connected space.gloss: Any topological space which cannot be written as the disjoint union of two or more nonempty open spaces.

connecting homomorphism.gloss: The homomorphism constructed by the snake lemma, leading to a particular exact sequence of kernels and cokernels. Such a homomorphism in the context of exact sequences of chain complexes, leading to a long exact sequence of homology groups.

connection.gloss: A set of sets that contains the empty set, all one-element sets for any element that is included in any of the sets, and the union of any group of sets that are elements where the intersections of those sets is non-empty.

connection string.gloss: A text string that specifies information about a database or other data source and the means of connecting to it.

connectionless.gloss: Without the use of a constant connection; sending and receiving data arbitrarily as needed, usually with less reliability than if a connection were held open.

connective.gloss: A function that operates on truth values to give another truth value.

connectivity.gloss: In a graph, a measure of concatenated adjacency (the number of ways that points are connected to each other)

connector.gloss: A line connecting two shapes in presentation software.
A software component that provides access from an application program to an external database or data source, such as a JDBC connector.
A map which can be defined for a linear connection.

connex.gloss: A correspondence between a projective space and its dual.
Such that, for all x and y in X, and for a binary relation R, either or both of xRy and yRx hold(s).

connotation.gloss: The attribute or aggregate of attributes connoted by a term, as contrasted with a denotation.

conoid.gloss: A Catalan surface all of whose rulings intersect some fixed line
A solid formed by the revolution of a conic section about its axis

conormal.gloss: Whose corresponding vector field (covector) is normal

cons.gloss: A data structure in Lisp that is a pair of pointers, car and cdr, used mainly for lists.

To obtain a list from a cons or a nesting of conses; to prepend an element to a list by forming a cons of that element and the list; to obtain a list from a smaller one by repeated application of such kind of prepending.

consecution.gloss: The relation of consequent to antecedent.

consensus.gloss: An agreement on some data value that is needed during computation.

consequent.gloss: The second half of a hypothetical proposition; Q, if the form of the proposition is "If P, then Q."
The second term of a ratio, i.e. the term b in the ratio a:b, the other being the antecedent.

conservative.gloss: That is the gradient of a function.

conservative extension.gloss: An extension of a logical theory such that every theorem expressible in the original theory is also derivable within the original theory.

consilience.gloss: The concurrence of multiple inductions drawn from different data sets.

consistency.gloss: Freedom from contradiction; the state of a system of axioms such that none of the propositions deduced from them are mutually contradictory.

consistent.gloss: Of a set of statements: such that no contradiction logically follows from them.

const.gloss: A variable whose value cannot be changed directly.
Whose value cannot be changed directly.
Which cannot change the value of its class’s attributes.

const correctness.gloss: The proper declaration of objects as immutable in contexts where they are not expected to be modified.

constant.gloss: A quantity that remains at a fixed value throughout a given discussion or operation.
An identifier that is bound to an invariant value; a fixed value given a name to aid in readability of source code.

constant function.gloss: A function whose value is the same for all the elements of its domain.

constant morphism.gloss: A morphism which yields the same morphism when post-composed with either one of a parallel pair of morphisms.

constant of integration.gloss: An unspecified constant term added to a particular antiderivative to make it represent its whole family of antiderivatives, usually denoted with C.

constant problem.gloss: The problem of deciding whether a given expression is equal to zero.

constant term.gloss: A term in an algebraic expression that does not contain any variables.

constant time.gloss: An algorithm, also written as O(1) time) where the value of T(n) (the complexity of the algorithm) is bounded by a value that does not depend on the size of the input.

constantive.gloss: Composed of elements that are each expressible by a unary polynomial.

constness.gloss: The declaration of variables or objects as immutable.

constraint.gloss: A condition that a solution to an optimization problem must satisfy.
A linkage or other restriction that maintains database integrity.

constraint cluster.gloss: A cluster of data points in a set conforming to the must-link and cannot-link constraints specified for each pair of data points.

construct.gloss: To draw (a geometric figure) by following precise specifications and using geometric tools and techniques.

constructible.gloss: That can be constructed in a plane using only a pair of compasses and a straightedge.
Such that the line segment joining it to the origin can be constructed using only a pair of compasses and a straightedge.
Admitting description as a finite union of locally closed (with respect to the Zariski topology) sets.
qualifiers: of a subset of the spectrum of a noetherian ring

construction.gloss: A geometric figure of arcs and line segments that is drawable with a straightedge and compass.

construction language.gloss: A programming language that is used to write actual software applications, in contrast to a language used mainly for specification, modeling or prototyping.

constructive logic.gloss: Any kind of logic in which any proof of existence can be converted into an algorithm that constructs the mathematical object which it claims to exist.

constructivism.gloss: A philosophy that asserts the need to construct a mathematical object to prove it exists.

constructivize.gloss: To convert into a framework that is consistent with constructivism.

contact manifold.gloss: A smooth manifold of odd dimensionality in contact geometry.

contactization.gloss: Conversion to, or description using a contact manifold

contactomorphic.gloss: Describing a pair of contact manifolds that have a diffeomorphism

contactomorphism.gloss: An isomorphism in the contact category.

contain.gloss: To have as an element or subset.

container.gloss: Someone who contains; something that contains. A file format that can hold various types of data.
Someone who contains; something that contains. An abstract data type whose instances are collections of other objects.
Someone who contains; something that contains. Any user interface component that can hold further (child) components.
Someone who contains; something that contains. A web container.

Someone who contains; something that contains. A bundle consisting of operating system, application code and dependencies to be run sandboxed inside a virtualized environment; (by extension) the environment itself.

containerization.gloss: Software virtualization at the level of the operating system.

containerize.gloss: To run an application in a software container.

content.gloss: The n-dimensional space contained by an n-dimensional polytope (called volume in the case of a polyhedron and area in the case of a polygon); length, area or volume, generalized to an arbitrary number of dimensions.

The greatest common divisor of the coefficients; (of a polynomial with coefficients in an integral domain) the common factor of the coefficients which, when removed, leaves the adjusted coefficients with no common factor that is noninvertible.
qualifiers: of a polynomial with coefficients in a GCD domain

content coupling.gloss: A form of coupling where one module relies on the internal workings of another module.

content determination.gloss: The process of selecting and organizing information within a generated text.

content management system.gloss: A computer software system for organizing and facilitating collaborative creation of documents and other content, especially for loading to a website.

content repository.gloss: The main repository of a content management system.

content wrangling.gloss: All the various tasks associated with content management systems, especially the preparation of documents for posting on a website.

contention.gloss: Competition by parts of a system or its users for a limited resource.

context.gloss: For a formula: a finite set of variables, which set contains all the free variables in the given formula.
The data (register contents, program counter value, etc.) needed to switch to another thread of execution.

context-free grammar.gloss: A formal grammar in which every production rule is such that the left-hand side is exactly one non-terminal symbol and the right-hand side is zero or more terminal symbols and/or nonterminal symbols.

context-sensitive.gloss: Sensitive to context; exhibiting different behaviour depending on a task or situation.

contingency.gloss: A statement which is neither a tautology nor a contradiction.

contingency table.gloss: A table presenting the joint distribution of two categorical variables.
An arrangement of data containing the joint distribution of two or more categorical variables, usually in a database, a series of tables, or a special visualization.

continuant.gloss: A determinant formed from a tridiagonal matrix.

continuation.gloss: A representation of an execution state of a program at a certain point in time, which may be used at a later time to resume the execution of the program from that point.

continuation-passing style.gloss: A style of programming in which every user function f takes an extra argument c known as a continuation. Whenever f would normally return a result r to its caller, it instead returns the result of applying the continuation to r.

continued fraction.gloss: A compound numerical expression consisting of an integer plus a fraction whose numerator is a positive integer and whose denominator is a continued fraction (an integer plus a fraction), and so on, with finite or infinite recursion.

continuity.gloss: A characteristic property of a continuous function.

continuous.gloss: Such that, for every x in the domain, for each small open interval D about f(x), there's an interval containing x whose image is in D.
Such that each open set in the target space has an open preimage (in the domain space, with respect to the given function).
qualifiers: of a function between two topological spaces

continuous bag of words.gloss: A bag of words comprised of the words in the vicinity of a specific target.

continuous delivery.gloss: An approach where teams produce software in short cycles, ensuring that the software can be reliably released at any time.

continuous delivery pipeline.gloss: An automated series of steps that moves software code from the development stage through building, testing, and deployment to a production environment.

continuous function.gloss: a function whose value at any point in its domain is equal its limit at the same point
a function from one topological space to another, such that the inverse image of any open set is open

continuous integration.gloss: The practice of merging all branches to a shared mainline several times a day.

continuous time.gloss: A framework which views variables as having a particular value only for an infinitesimally short amount of time.

continuous variable.gloss: A variable that has a continuous distribution function, such as temperature.

continuous wavelet transform.gloss: A tool used for analyzing the time and frequency domain of a signal simultaneously.

continuum.gloss: The nondenumerable set of real numbers; more generally, any compact connected metric space.

continuum hypothesis.gloss: The hypothesis which states that any infinite subset of ℝ must have the cardinality of either the set of natural numbers or of ℝ itself.

continuum theory.gloss: The branch of topology devoted to the study of continua, a type of metric space.

contour integral.gloss: The integral of a function around a contour on the complex plane.

contractible.gloss: (of a topological set) Able to be reduced to one of its points by a continuous deformation

contradiction.gloss: A proposition that is false for all values of its propositional variables or Boolean atoms.

contradictionism.gloss: A worldview according to which contradictory statements can both be true.

contradictory.gloss: Either of a pair of propositions, that cannot both be true or both be false.

contragredient.gloss: Generally, denoting an object inversed and transposed (to another).
Of a representation in linear algebra: being the transpose of the former representation of an inverse object.
Of a matrix: being a transpose of an inverse matrix.

contraharmonic mean.gloss: A type of average calculated as the arithmetic mean of the squares of the values divided by the arithmetic mean of the values, i.e. C=(x_1²+x_2²+...+x_n²)/n/(x_1+x_2+...+x_n)/norC(x_1,x_2,...,x_n)=x_1²+x_2²+...+x_n²/x_1+x_2+...+x_n

contraponend.gloss: The original proposition involved in a contraposition.

contraposition.gloss: The statement of the form "if not Q then not P", given the statement "if P then Q".

contrapositive.gloss: The inverse of the converse of a given logical implication.

contrapositively.gloss: By the inverse of the converse of a given proposition.

contrary.gloss: One of a pair of propositions that cannot both be simultaneously true, though they may both be false.

contravariance.gloss: Of vectors, the property of scaling inversely with a change of basis, as opposed to covariance.

contravariant.gloss: Which reverses the order of morphism composition: formally, which associates each morphism f:X→Y to a morphism F(f):F(Y)→F(X).
Scaling inversely with a change of basis.
A bihomogeneous polynomial in dual variables of x, y, ... and the coefficients of some homogeneous form in x, y, ... that is invariant under some group of linear transformations.

contravariant functor.gloss: A functor which maps a morphism f:X → Y to a morphism F(f):F(Y) → F(X), such that if h=g∘f, then F(h)=F(f)∘F(g).

control.gloss: (construed with for) To design (an experiment) so that the effects of one or more variables are reduced or eliminated.
An interface element that a computer user interacts with, such as a window or a text box.

control bus.gloss: A part of the system bus that is used by CPUs for communicating with other devices within the computer.

control character.gloss: A character which does not have a direct visual appearance as a glyph, but rather causes some other action to occur, such as a transition to a new line.

control code.gloss: A numeric value or string of such values that triggers a specific command or action to occur, rather than displaying a text character.

control coupling.gloss: A form of coupling where one module controls the flow of another by passing information on what to do.

control flow.gloss: The order in which individual statements, instructions or function calls of an imperative program are executed or evaluated.

control function.gloss: A function that controls the recording, processing, transmission, or interpretation of data.

control key.gloss: A key on a personal computer or terminal keyboard used in combination to modify the function of other keys.

control panel.gloss: A computer display offering a number of controls or options.

control plane.gloss: The part of a network that handling network topology and signalling, as opposed to the parts carying user traffic.

control point.gloss: Any of a series of points defining the shape of a curve, etc.

control structure.gloss: A structure used to direct the flow of execution of a program.

control unit.gloss: The part of a central processing unit that directs its operation, converting instructions stored in memory into signals that determine the operation of the data path and other components.

control-flow graph.gloss: A representation, using graph notation, of all paths that might be traversed through a program during its execution.

controlled vocabulary.gloss: A carefully selected set of terms, such as words and phrases, such that each concept from the domain of discourse is described using only one term in the set and each term in the set describes only one concept.

controller.gloss: A mechanism that controls or regulates the operation of a machine, especially a peripheral device in a computer.
In software applications using the model-view-controller design pattern, the part or parts of the application that treat input and output, forming an interface between models and views.

conventional memory.gloss: The first 640 kilobytes of RAM in an IBM-compatible PC.

conventional pci.gloss: PCI (the computer bus), as opposed to the newer PCI Express.

converge.gloss: (said of a sequence or series) To have a (finite, proper) limit.
(said of an iterative process) To reach a stable end point.

convergence.gloss: The process or property of approaching some limiting value; typically of an infinite series.

convergent.gloss: Of a (typically infinite) sequence or series in a topological space, converging to a (finite, proper) limit.
The rational number obtained when a continued fraction is terminated after a finite number of terms.

convergent series.gloss: An infinite series whose partial sums converge.

conversation.gloss: The protocol-based interaction between systems processing a transaction.

conversational.gloss: Involving a two-way exchange of messages, such as between a client and a server.

converse.gloss: Of a proposition or theorem consisting of a statement of the form "If A is true, then B is true", the statement "If B is true, then A is true" which need not be equivalent to the first one.

conversion.gloss: A software product converted from one platform to another.
The act of interchanging the terms of a proposition, as by putting the subject in the place of the predicate, or vice versa.
A change or reduction of the form or value of a proposition.

convert.gloss: To change (one proposition) into another, so that what was the subject of the first becomes the predicate of the second.

convertend.gloss: Any proposition which is subject to the process of conversion; so called in its relation to itself as converted, after which process it is termed the converse.

converter.gloss: A person or thing that converts. A program that converts one file format to another one, or which converts between different units of measurement, such as miles to meters.

convertible.gloss: Able to be converted Able to undergo conversion (i.e., inversion) without falsehood.
A computer able to be converted between laptop and tablet form factors.

convex.gloss: having no internal angles greater than 180 degrees.
arranged such that for any two points in the set, a straight line between the two points is contained within the set.
qualifiers: of a set in Euclidean space

convex combination.gloss: A linear combination (of vectors in Euclidean space) in which the coefficients are non-negative and all add up to one.

convex envelope.gloss: For a given set S⊆ℝⁿ and real-valued function f defined on the convex hull conv(S), the highest-valued convex function that underestimates or equals f over S.
qualifiers: of a function on a set

convex function.gloss: A mathematical function where the line segment between any two points on the graph of the function lies above the graph in a vector space of at least two dimensions.

convex hull.gloss: The smallest convex set of points in which a given set of points is contained.

convex set.gloss: A set which contains any convex combination of any (finite) subset of its points.

convexifiability.gloss: Capability of being convexified (being made convex).

convexifiable.gloss: Capable of being convexified (being made convex).

convexification.gloss: The process of converting to convex form.

convolution.gloss: A mathematical operation on two functions that produces a third that expresses how the shape of one is modified by the other; the integral of the product of the two functions after one is reflected about the y-axis and shifted along the x-axis.
A function which maps a tuple of sequences into a sequence of tuples.

convolve.gloss: To form the convolution of something with something else

convolver.gloss: An algorithm that performs convolution on a signal.

conway knot.gloss: A particular knot with 11 crossings, related by mutation to the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot.

coobservable.gloss: Of a behaviour in a distributed system: such that decisions can be made by each site based on what it observes, without the need for input from other sites.

cook reduction.gloss: A Turing reduction that runs in polynomial time.

cooked.gloss: Corrupted by conversion through a text format, requiring uncooking to be properly listenable.

cooked mode.gloss: The mode of a device driver in which input data is processed or preprocessed.

cookie.gloss: To send a cookie to (a user, computer, etc.).

cookied.gloss: (of an HTTP request, a transferred file, a user) That has cookies.

cookieless.gloss: Without the use of HTTP cookies.

cooperad.gloss: One of a set of composed operads

cooperative game.gloss: Informally, a game formalized using a function (called the characteristic function) that assigns to each coalition of players a real number representing the payoff that the coalition can gain if it is formed, without specifying how the outcome is divided among the participants of the coalition; upon the execution of the game, each player can be a member of at most one coalition.

cooperon.gloss: A special Green's function used in modelling superconductivity.

coorbit theory.gloss: A theory for atomic decomposition of a range of Banach spaces of distributions, including among others the wavelet transform and the short-time Fourier transform.

coordinate.gloss: A number representing the position of a point along a line, arc, or similar one-dimensional figure.

coordinate axis.gloss: One of the lines in the coordinate system that represents one of the dimensions.

coordinate plane.gloss: A Euclidean plane with a system of coordinates.

coordinate system.gloss: A method of representing the position of any individual point in a space of given dimensionality as a tuple of numerical coordinates.

coordinatewise.gloss: By or with respect to coordinates or an individual coordinate.

coordinatization.gloss: The application of coordinates to a system

coordinatize.gloss: to apply coordinates to a system

cop number.gloss: For a given undirected graph, the minimum number of cops that suffices to ensure a win (i.e. a capture of the robber) in a certain pursuit–evasion game on the graph.

copartition.gloss: A partition of data streams such that the data in each of the streams has the same partition configuration.
A set of subsets such that the set of complementary subsets forms a partition.
To ensure that two streams of partitioned data have matching partition configurations.

copier.gloss: A program or process that copies.

coplanarity.gloss: The state or characteristic of being within the same plane.

copositive.gloss: Of a real matrix A: such that xᵀᴬˣ≥0 for every non-negative vector x≥0.

copower.gloss: The dual object of a power.

copperbar.gloss: An animated horizontal bar of colour that extends into the overscan area of the display.

coprime.gloss: Having no positive integer factors in common, aside from 1.
qualifiers: of two or more positive integers

coprime.gloss: Having no positive integer factors, aside from 1, in common with one or more specified other positive integers.
Whose greatest common divisor is a nonzero constant (i.e., polynomial of degree 0).

coprocess.gloss: A process that explicitly yields control to other processes or to the operating system.

coprocessor.gloss: An additional microprocessor used to supplement the functionality of the central processing unit, performing tasks such as floating-point arithmetic (floating-point unit) or graphics calculations (graphics processing unit).

coproduct.gloss: The colimit of two (or more) objects, without regard to any morphisms between them.

copula.gloss: A function that represents the association between two or more variables, independent of the individual marginal distributions of the variables.

copunctual.gloss: Having a common set of points

copy.gloss: To place a copy of an object in memory for later use.

copy elision.gloss: An optimisation technique where a value is transferred to the final target address, instead of being copied and then destroyed.

copy-on-write proxy.gloss: A proxy that controls the copying of an object by deferring the copy until it is required by a client.

copy-paste.gloss: The action of duplicating (text, an object, etc.) by copying it and later pasting somewhere else.
Material incorporated into another work with minimal or no changes.
To copy (text, an object, etc.) and later paste it somewhere else.

copy-pasto.gloss: An error caused by incorrect copy-pasting, often resulting in unintended text (or other content) being inserted.

copybook.gloss: A series of instructions or data definitions copied into multiple programs from a shared library; boilerplate.

copyparty.gloss: An event where people meet to swap software (often pirated copies of commercial releases), a forerunner of the demoparty.

copypasta.gloss: Code or documentation that has been copied and pasted, often erroneously.

copywronged.gloss: Having copy protection that is broken or inoperable.

coquaternion.gloss: Any of a group of elements of a type of four-dimensional vector space

coquecigrue.gloss: A certain mathematical object in connection with Leibniz algebras.

corank.gloss: The dimension of the left nullspace of a matrix.
The dimension of the cokernel of a linear transformation of a vector space
The number of elements of a matroid minus its rank.

cordership.gloss: A class of engineered spaceships in Conway's Game of Life based on the switch engine that move at a speed of c/12 diagonally.

core.gloss: The most important part of a thing or aggregate of things wherever located and whether of any determinate location at all; the essence. A technical term for classification of things denoting those parts of a category that are most easily or most likely understood as within it. The set of feasible allocations that cannot be improved upon by a subset (a coalition) of the economy's agents.
particular parts of technical instruments or machines essential in function: Ellipsis of core memory (“magnetic data storage”).

particular parts of technical instruments or machines essential in function: An individual computer processor, in the sense when several processors (called cores or CPU cores) are plugged together in one single integrated circuit to work as one (called a multi-core processor).

core dump.gloss: The recorded state of the memory of a computer program at a specific time, generally when the program has terminated abnormally.

core memory.gloss: A type of non-volatile random-access rewritable electronic memory using ferrite cores to magnetically store binary digits (bits).

core switch.gloss: A high-capacity switch usually at the core or backbone of a computer network, aggregating network traffic to the Internet or a WAN.

coreachable.gloss: Mutually reachable, that is, for any two nodes n1 and n2, they are coreachable iff n1 is reachable from n2 and n2 is reachable from n1.

corelet.gloss: Any of various applications resident in the memory of a mobile phone or similar device.

coreset.gloss: A small set of points that approximates the shape of a larger point set, in the sense that applying some geometric measure to the two sets (such as their minimum bounding box volume) results in approximately equal numbers.

coresidual.gloss: Any of four points on the common chord of a cubic curve intercepted by a cone.

coresolution.gloss: An object in a comodule or other dual to an abelian object that has a specified property.

cornell box.gloss: A physical box with variously coloured walls and an inner light source, photographed and used to gauge the accuracy of a computer rendering of the same scene.

corner solution.gloss: A solution to a minimization or maximization problem where an interior solution is infeasible.

corollary.gloss: A proposition which follows easily from the statement or proof of another proposition.
A proposition which follows easily from the statement or proof of another proposition. A product or byproduct of an assertion following easily from another stated or proven assertion.

coroutine.gloss: A piece of code that performs a task, and that can be passed new input and return output more than once.

corpus linguistics.gloss: A branch of linguistics that studies large samples (corpora) of real-world text, usually with the aid of computer software.

corpus manager.gloss: A sophisticated tool for analyzing multilingual corpora.

correctness.gloss: The state of an algorithm that correctly mirrors its specification.

correlation.gloss: One of the several measures of the linear statistical relationship between two random variables, indicating both the strength and direction of the relationship.
An isomorphism from a projective space to the dual of a projective space, often to the dual of itself.

correlation coefficient.gloss: Any of the several measures indicating the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two random variables.

correlation function.gloss: function giving the statistical correlation between random variables at two different points in space or time

correlator.gloss: A type of device used to compare two signals

correlogram.gloss: A graph that shows the correlation between two variables.

correntropy.gloss: A nonlinear measure of the similarity between two random variables

correspondence.gloss: Congruity or similarity between different things, people, etc: A relation.

corruption.gloss: The destruction of data by manipulation of parts of it, either by deliberate or accidental human action or by imperfections in storage or transmission media.

cosecant.gloss: In a right triangle, the reciprocal of the sine of an angle. Symbols: cosec, csc

cosection.gloss: The left inverse of a morphism.

coset.gloss: The set that results from applying a group's binary operation with a given fixed element of the group on each element of a given subgroup.

cosilting.gloss: Describing a generalization of cotilting modules

cosine.gloss: In a right triangle, the ratio of the length of the side adjacent to an acute angle to the length of the hypotenuse. Symbol: cos

cosine curve.gloss: A curve that has the equation y=acos(x) in Cartesian coordinates.

cosinusoidal.gloss: Having the form of a cosine.

coslice category.gloss: The category opposite to that of a slice category.

cost-free.gloss: Of software, content, or materials, without any monetary payment or licensing fees.

costate.gloss: An equation or variable related to the state equation of an optimal control problem in a dynamical system.

costatement.gloss: A list of statements that effectively execute together (though not simultaneously), such that each can yield execution to the others to avoid delaying the program. They are used to implement cooperative multitasking.

costructure.gloss: The structure produced by the intersection of multiple related curves or shapes.

cosymplectic.gloss: Symplectic and having a closed contact form as well.

cosysop.gloss: A user granted some of the administrative privileges of a sysop.

cotangent.gloss: In a right triangle, the reciprocal of the tangent of an angle. Symbols: cot, ctg, or ctn

coterminal.gloss: Differing only by a whole number of complete circles.
Describing an object in a category, such that there is precisely one morphism that maps that object to every object in the category.

cotilting.gloss: dual to a tilting class, module, or functor.
