cycloid.gloss: The locus of a point on the circumference of a circle that rolls without slipping on a fixed straight line.

cyclomatic.gloss: Used to describe the number of edges that must be removed from a graph to ensure that no graph cycle remains; equal to the number of edges, minus the number of nodes plus one.
Of or relating to a software metric that measures the complexity of a program based on the number of linearly independent paths through the source code.

cyclomatic complexity.gloss: A quantitative measure of the number of linearly independent paths (branches) through a program's source code which indicates the complexity of a program or a function.

cyclometric.gloss: Of or pertaining to the inverse trigonometric functions: arcsine, arccosine, arctangent, arccotangent, arcsecant, and arccosecant.

cyclometry.gloss: The measurement of circles, including calculating circumference, arcs, angles etc.

cyclotomic.gloss: of, or relating to the complex roots of unity

cyclotomic field.gloss: A number field obtained by adjoining a primitive root of unity to the field of rational numbers.

cyclotomic polynomial.gloss: For a positive integer n, a polynomial whose roots are the primitive nᵗʰ roots of unity, so that its degree is Euler's totient function of n. That is, letting ζₙ=e^(i 2π/n) be the first primitive nᵗʰ root of unity, then Φₙ(x)=∏_( stackrel )1<m<ngcd (n,m)=1(x-ζₙᵐ) is the nᵗʰ such polynomial.

cyclotomics.gloss: The branch of mathematics concerned with the complex roots of unity; cyclotomy.

cyclotomy.gloss: the historical problems of dividing the circle into a given number of equal segments, and of constructing regular polygons
the analytical extraction of the complex roots of unity; a de Moivre number

cylinder.gloss: A surface created by projecting a closed two-dimensional curve along an axis intersecting the plane of the curve.
A solid figure bounded by a cylinder and two parallel planes intersecting the cylinder.
The corresponding tracks on a vertical arrangement of disks in a disk drive considered as a unit of data capacity.

cylinder function.gloss: Any function that is a solution of the Bessel equation

cylinder-head-sector.gloss: An addressing system of hard drives where the hard drive is addressed by its cylinders, heads, and sectors.

cylindricity.gloss: A three-dimensional geometric tolerance that controls how much a feature can deviate from a perfect cylinder.

cylindroid.gloss: A certain three-dimensional surface described by a moving straight line, used to illustrate the motions of a rigid body and the forces that act upon it.

cylindroidal.gloss: Having the form of a cylindroid.

cypherpunk.gloss: A person with an interest in encryption and privacy, especially one who uses encrypted email.

cyrus–beck algorithm.gloss: A generalized algorithm for line clipping.

d-frame.gloss: A low-quality intraframe containing only DC components, used for high-speed previews.

d2t.gloss: Initialism of disk-to-tape: a method of data backup where information is copied from a disk (usually the hard disk of a computer) to a magnetic tape.

daas.gloss: Acronym of data as a service.
Acronym of desktop as a service.
Acronym of device as a service.

dacl.gloss: Initialism of discretionary access control list.

daemon.gloss: A process (a running program) that does not have a controlling terminal.

daemonize.gloss: Of a computer program or script, to prepare to go in to the background and become a daemon.

dag.gloss: A directed acyclic graph; an ordered pair (V,E) such that E is a subset of some partial ordering relation on V.

daisy chain.gloss: A thing resembling a daisy chain (noun sense 1) in having several elements connected together, often in a circle. A bus wiring scheme in which a series of devices are connected in sequence: A to B, B to C, C to D, etc.

daisy-chain.gloss: To connect (several computer devices or peripherals, or other components) in sequence with each other, usually such that the output of one component forms the input of another; also (followed by to), to connect (a computer device, peripheral, or other component) to another component in such a sequence.
Especially of a computer device, peripheral, or other component: to be capable of being connected with other components in sequence.

daisywheel printer.gloss: A printer that operates by striking the page with moulded characters from a rotating circular arrangement, obsolete since the late 1980s.

dal.gloss: Initialism of data access layer, a software architecture layer.
Initialism of database abstraction layer, a software architecture layer.

dammit operator.gloss: The operator ! in the C# programming language, used to indicate to the compiler that a possibly null reference will not be null at that point.

damn.gloss: Acronym of distributed architecture for mobile navigation.

damping ratio.gloss: A dimensionless measure of the damping in second-order linear dynamic system, appearing as the term ζ in the generalised equation of motion for such a system, ̈q+2ζωₙ̇q+ωₙ²q=F.

dancing links.gloss: A technique for reverting the deletion of a node from a circular doubly-linked list, particularly useful for efficiently implementing backtracking algorithms.

dangling else.gloss: A potential ambiguity in a programming language that occurs when an else clause can be associated with either a nested conditional or with the clause that encloses the nested conditional.

dangling pointer.gloss: A pointer (variable that holds the address of a memory location) that does not reference a valid object.
A pointer referencing memory that was previously deallocated.

dantzig-wolfe decomposition.gloss: An algorithm for solving linear programming problems with special structure, relying on delayed column generation for improving the tractability of large-scale linear programs.

dao.gloss: Initialism of disk-at-once, an optical disk recording mode.
Initialism of data access object, a design pattern.

dark figure.gloss: The estimated number of unreported criminal cases.

dark pattern.gloss: A user interface that is intentionally designed to trick users into doing things that are not in their own best interest, such as giving up more information, or agreeing to unfavourable terms.

dart.gloss: A concave quadrilateral similar in shape to a chevron or arrowhead.

dasd.gloss: Initialism of direct access storage device, such as a USB drive or hard drive.

dash.gloss: Any of the following symbols: ‒ (figure dash), – (en dash), — (em dash), or ― (horizontal bar). A hyphen or minus sign.

dashboard.gloss: A graphical user interface for changing settings.
A data visualization that summarizes reports from multiple disparate sources at a glance.

dasherize.gloss: To convert (a string) to use hyphens as word separators.

dat.gloss: Digital Audio Tape, a digital data storage tape format using a dual-spooled cartridge and magnetic tape, used for digital audio and data storage.

data.gloss: A representation of information in a computer (as symbols, quantities, sound, images or videos) which is stored, processed or transmitted in the form of electrical signals, records on magnetic tape or punched cards, etc.

data access object.gloss: An object in programming that provides an abstract interface to some type of persistence mechanism, providing some specific data operations without exposing details of the persistence layer.

data acquisition.gloss: The process of sampling signals that measure real-world physical conditions and converting the resulting samples into digital numeric values that can be manipulated by a computer.

data array.gloss: A fundamental programming structure that stores a collection of items or elements under a single variable name.

data binding.gloss: A general technique that binds together two data sources (or two separate representations of the same data) and keeps them synchronized.

data bus.gloss: A hardware subsystem that transfers data between components inside a computer, or between computers.

data circuit-terminating equipment.gloss: A device interconnecting data terminal equipment (DTE) and a data transmission circuit.

data collection.gloss: The process of gathering and measuring information on targeted variables in an established system.

data collection tree.gloss: A network topology used to gather and aggregate data from a collection of sensor nodes into a single node, which then propagates the aggregated data on.

data communications.gloss: The movement of data between computers, or between central computers (especially mainframes) and remote terminals.

data compression.gloss: Any of several techniques for reducing the number of bits needed to represent an item of digital data, either to save storage or to use less bandwidth when transmitting it

data controller.gloss: A clerk who scheduled batch jobs on a mainframe computer, and who distributed printed output

data coupling.gloss: a form of coupling when modules share data through objects like parameters

data cube.gloss: A very large three-dimensional array or table.

data dictionary.gloss: A document or repository that describes the data and metadata within a system.

data division.gloss: The part of a COBOL program in which the format and layout of external files and databases, and internally-used variables and constants are defined

data entry.gloss: The act of inputting data into a computer, such as by typing out handwriting, capturing data from scanned documents, taking responses from telephone interviews, etc.

data feed.gloss: A mechanism for a user to receive updated data from data sources.

data flow.gloss: The route between origin, via nodes, to a destination taken by a packet of data
The transfer of data between the components of a computer

data glove.gloss: A glove containing sensors to detect movement of the hand and fingers, used to control a computer-generated virtual reality environment.

data lakehouse.gloss: A hybrid architecture combining data lake and data warehouse principles.

data mining.gloss: A technique for searching large-scale databases for patterns; used mainly to find previously unknown correlations between variables that may be commercially useful.

data model.gloss: A result of applying a data modeling to some particular application, using a database model such as relational.
A database model, such as relational or hierarchical.

data object.gloss: A self-contained unit of information that represents a specific entity or interaction within a system.

data path.gloss: The part of a central processing unit that stores data to be immediately operated on and performs logic and arithmetic operations on it based on signals from the control unit.

data plane.gloss: The part of a network that carries user traffic, as opposed to those parts handling network topology and signalling.

data processing machine.gloss: An accounting machine or tabulating machine.

data race.gloss: A problematic situation where one thread could potentially read or write a memory location while another thread is writing to it.

data record.gloss: A section of the database consisting of several uniquely named components known as data fields.

data recovery.gloss: The process of retrieving deleted, inaccessible, lost, corrupted, damaged, or formatted data from secondary storage, removable media or files, when the data stored in them cannot be accessed in the usual way.

data room.gloss: A space used for housing data, usually of a secure or privileged nature in the context of mergers and acquisitions.

data scraping.gloss: A technique in which a computer program extracts data from human-readable output coming from another program.

data scrubbing.gloss: An error-correction technique that periodically inspects main memory or storage for errors, then correct detected errors using redundant data in the form of different checksums or copies of data.

data set.gloss: A file of related records on a computer-readable medium such as a disk, especially one on a mainframe computer.
A set of data to be analyzed.

data sink.gloss: A device or computer program that collects and stores data from other devices or programs.

data smoothing.gloss: The mathematical process of fitting a smooth curve to dispersed data points.

data store.gloss: A data repository of a set of integrated objects.

data stream.gloss: a sequence of digitally encoded coherent signals used in a transmission

data structure.gloss: Any form of storing and organizing data in a computer so that it can be accessed efficiently.

data synchronization.gloss: The establishment of equivalence between data collections (typically on different servers, and sometimes between trading partners), where each data element in one item maps to a data item in the other, and their data is equivalent.

data table.gloss: Any display of information in tabular form, with rows and/or columns named
A table stored in, or derived from, a database.

data terminal equipment.gloss: an end instrument that converts user information into signals or reconverts received signals.

data transfer object.gloss: A design pattern used to transfer data between software application subsystems.

data transfer rate.gloss: The transmission speed of a communications channel; measured in bits or bytes per second.

data type.gloss: A classification or category of various types of data, that states the possible values that can be taken, how they are stored, and what range of operations are allowed on them.

data warehouse.gloss: A collection of data, from a variety of sources, organized to provide useful guidance to an organization's decision-makers.

data wipe.gloss: The process of deleting all data from a device or account.

data-bound.gloss: Synchronised with a data source by means of data binding.

data-driven programming.gloss: A programming paradigm where data, rather than explicit control flow logic, guides a program's behavior.

data-oriented.gloss: Of or pertaining to a software engineering approach that focuses on data as the central point of an application.

database.gloss: A set of tables and other objects (queries, reports, forms) in the form of a structured data set.
A software program (application) for storing, retrieving and manipulating such a structured data set.
A combination of such data sets and the programs for using them.

database administrator.gloss: A person who is responsible for the logical and physical design of databases, and normally for all aspects of their recoverability, integrity, security, availability and performance.

database analyst.gloss: a person who is responsible for the logical and physical design of databases

database dump.gloss: The bulk transfer or release of a large amount of raw information from one database, system, or person to another. The act of exporting the contents and structure of an entire database into a single file to create a backup or migrate to a new system.

The bulk transfer or release of a large amount of raw information from one database, system, or person to another. Stolen information published by hackers or malicious actors (such as user credentials, emails, or intellectual property), publicly on the internet.

The bulk transfer or release of a large amount of raw information from one database, system, or person to another. The action of passing a massive amount of information, instructions, or project details to someone all at once.

database engine.gloss: The underlying component that a database management system uses to create, retrieve, update and delete data.

database key.gloss: A unique identifier in the database management system IDMS, which indicates the record occurrence's physical location in the database.

database management system.gloss: A suite of interrelated computer programs designed to manage message processing and database update in a tightly controlled manner.

database publishing.gloss: the production of catalogues, price lists etc, using data from a database

database transaction.gloss: A unit of interaction in a database management system.

database-first.gloss: Of a software development approach, where an existing database schema is first designed or used.

datafile.gloss: A computer file that stores data for use by an application or system.

dataframe.gloss: A two-dimensional array of data items, rather like a spreadsheet.

datagram.gloss: A packet of data passed across a network.

datahub.gloss: An administrative building centre with access to multiple, independent (often remote) databases

datalink.gloss: The protocol layer that transfers data between adjacent network nodes in a wide area network or between nodes on the same local area network segment.

datasheet.gloss: A display of the records in a table, arranged in rows and columns.

datasource.gloss: A source of data; typically a database

datastack.gloss: A stack (LIFO data structure) of data items

datathon.gloss: A kind of hackathon focusing on the use of large data sets.

date-time.gloss: Of or pertaining to the datetime variable or data type.

datestamp.gloss: The date on which an event occurred, often included in a log to track the sequence of events.

datetime.gloss: A variable or data type that can hold both date and time components.

dative.gloss: Given in advance; not needed to be calculated.

daughterboard.gloss: A circuit board that is an extension of a motherboard or other card.

dawg.gloss: Initialism of directed acyclic word graph.

dbaas.gloss: Acronym of database as a service.

dbal.gloss: Initialism of database abstraction layer, a software architecture layer.

dbd.gloss: Initialism of Database Driver (“the database driver of Perl DBI”).

dbm.gloss: Initialism of DataBase Manager, a family of key-value databases originating in early Unix.

dc.gloss: To become disconnected from a network.

ddd.gloss: Initialism of domain-driven design (“methodology and set of priorities for object oriented programming”).

ddo.gloss: Initialism of dynamic drive overlay, a type of computer software; a form of driver.

de bruijn graph.gloss: A kind of directed graph representing overlaps between sequences of symbols.

de bruijn index.gloss: A notation for representing terms in the lambda calculus with the purpose of eliminating the names of the variables from the notation.

de bruijn notation.gloss: A certain syntax for terms in the lambda calculus.

de bruijn sequence.gloss: A cyclic sequence (of order n on a size-k alphabet A) in which every possible length-n string on A occurs exactly once as a substring (i.e. a contiguous subsequence). Such a sequence is denoted by B(k, n).

de bruijn torus.gloss: An array of symbols from an alphabet (often just 0 and 1) that contains every m-by-n matrix exactly once.

de longchamps point.gloss: A triangle center defined as the reflection of the orthocenter of the triangle about the circumcenter.

de moivre number.gloss: Any of several complex numbers that are coordinates of the vertices of a regular polygon of unit radius

de morgan algebra.gloss: A bounded distributive lattice equipped with an involution (typically denoted ¬ or ~) which satisfies De Morgan's laws.

de morgan's law.gloss: Either of two laws in formal logic which state that: The negation of a conjunction is the disjunction of the negations; expressed in propositional logic as: ¬ (𝑝 ∧ 𝑞) ⇔ (¬ 𝑝) ∨ (¬ 𝑞)
Either of two laws in formal logic which state that: The negation of a disjunction is the conjunction of the negations; expressed in propositional logic as: ¬ (𝑝 ∨ 𝑞) ⇔ (¬ 𝑝) ∧ (¬ 𝑞)
Either of two laws in set theory which state that: The complement of a union is the intersection of the complements; as expressed by: (𝐴 ∪ 𝐵)′ = 𝐴′ ∩ 𝐵′
Either of two laws in set theory which state that: The complement of an intersection is the union of the complements; as expressed by: (𝐴 ∩ 𝐵)′ = 𝐴′ ∪ 𝐵′
Any of various laws similar to De Morgan’s laws for set theory and logic; for example: ¬∀𝑥 𝑃(𝑥) ⇔ ∃𝑥 ¬𝑃(𝑥)

de-archive.gloss: To render a file that has been archived available for editing.

dead click.gloss: A click on an element of a user interface which does not lead to any action.

dead code.gloss: Instructions that, when executed, have no effect on the running of the program.
A portion of source code that will never be executed as part of the running program.

dead flesh.gloss: The rubber chiclet keyboard of the ZX Spectrum computer.

dead pixel.gloss: a miscolored pixel on an image where it is otherwise not intended to be.

deadband.gloss: In the domain of a transfer function, the band of input values where the output is zero. "(the output is 'dead' - no action occurs)"

deadlock.gloss: An inability to continue due to two programs or devices each requiring a response from the other before completing an operation.

deadlockable.gloss: Capable of entering a state of deadlock.

deallocation.gloss: The release of a portion of storage that had previously been allocated to a specific task.

deauth.gloss: A deauthentication frame in IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi.

deauthenticate.gloss: To revoke the authentication of; to cause no longer to be authenticated.

deauthentication.gloss: The invalidation of an existing authentication.

deblock.gloss: To separate the logical records that have been combined into a physical block for storage.
To process (digital video) so as to remove block-shaped artifacts of encoding.

debounce.gloss: To discard events or signals that should not be processed because they occurred too close together.

debug.gloss: To search for and eliminate malfunctioning elements or errors in something, especially a computer program or machinery.

debug mode.gloss: The mode of a compiler or IDE that allows for debugging, with the availability of information such as variable names and line numbers from the source code.

debuggee.gloss: A process or application being debugged.

debugger.gloss: A computer program that helps the user to test and debug other programs, by enabling their step-by-step execution controlled by the user, setting of breakpoints, and monitoring values of variables.

debugging.gloss: The process of finding and resolving bugs or defects that prevent correct operation of computer software or a system.

decagon.gloss: A polygon with ten sides and ten angles.

decal.gloss: A texture overlaid on another texture to provide extra details.

decangle.gloss: Synonym of decagon (“a polygon with ten sides and ten angles”).

decategorification.gloss: The reverse process of categorification: The mapping of a category theoretic category to a set by using a systematic process in which isomorphic objects in a category are identified as equal.

decategorified.gloss: Not represented in terms of category theory

decay.gloss: To deteriorate, to get worse, to lose strength or health, to decline in quality. To undergo software rot, that is, to fail to be updated in a changing environment, so as to eventually become legacy or obsolete.
Of an array: to lose its type and dimensions and be reduced to a pointer, for example when passed to a function.

decic.gloss: Of the tenth degree or order; e.g. for a polynomial

decidability.gloss: The state or condition of being decidable.

decidable.gloss: describing a set for which there exists an algorithm that will determine whether any element is or is not within the set in a finite amount of time.
in intuitionistic logic, a proposition P is decidable in a given theory if it can be proven from the theory that "either P or not P", i.e. in symbols: P∨¬P.

decide.gloss: Of a Turing machine: to return a correct answer (for some yes-or-no problem) on every possible input.

decider.gloss: A Turing machine that halts regardless of its input.

decigrade.gloss: An angular measure equal to one tenth of a grade

decile.gloss: Any of the values in a series that divides the distribution of individuals in that series into ten groups of equal frequency.

decimal.gloss: Concerning numbers expressed in decimal or mathematical calculations performed using decimal.

decimal number.gloss: A number expressed in a decimal system (base ten), (particularly) fractional numbers so represented.

decimal system.gloss: A numerical system of counting in tens.

decimate.gloss: To replace (a high-resolution model) with another of lower but acceptable quality. (Usually algorithmically)

decimation.gloss: The creation of a new sequence comprising only every nth element of a source sequence.
The creation of a new sequence comprising only every nth element of a source sequence. A digital signal-processing technique for reducing the number of samples in a discrete-time signal; downsampling

decision problem.gloss: A question in some formal system with a yes-or-no answer, depending on the values of input parameters.

decision tree.gloss: A visualization of a complex decision-making situation in which the possible decisions and their likely outcomes are organized in the form of a graph that resembles a tree.

deck.gloss: A collection of cards (pages or forms) in systems such as WML (Wireless Markup Language) and HyperCard.
The multiset of graphs formed from a single graph by deleting a single vertex in all possible ways.

declaration.gloss: The specification of an object, such as a variable or function, establishing its existence but not necessarily describing its contents.

declarative.gloss: Of or relating to declarative programming.

declarative programming.gloss: a programming paradigm that expresses the logic of a computation instead of its control flow

declarator.gloss: A construct in source code that declares something, such as a variable.

declare.gloss: To explicitly establish the existence of (a variable, function, etc.) without necessarily describing its content.

declarer.gloss: A statement that declares the properties of a variable or contributes to doing so.

decloud.gloss: To transfer data off of the cloud and onto local storage.

decodable.gloss: Of a code, having a non-singular extension; being a lossless encoding.

decode.gloss: Output from a program or device used to interpret communication protocols

decollate.gloss: To separate the copies of a multipart computer printout.

decollator.gloss: a machine that decollates (separates) the parts of multipart computer printout and discards the carbon paper

decomino.gloss: A polyomino made up of ten squares.

decompactor.gloss: A program or algorithm for decompressing data.

decompile.gloss: To recreate the original source code from a compiled executable.

decompiler.gloss: A computer program performing the reverse operation to that of a compiler.

decompress.gloss: To restore (compressed data) to its original form.

decompression bomb.gloss: A usually malicious file with a very high compression ratio, thus expected to consume a large amount of memory and disk space when decompressed.

deconfigure.gloss: To remove or cancel the configuration of; to reset.

deconflict.gloss: To resolve contradictory conclusions or responses to queries in a rule-based or deductive reasoning system.

deconfusion.gloss: A statistical technique, similar to independent component analysis, for separating correlated data.

deconvolution.gloss: The inversion of a convolution equation; does not normally have unique solution

decorate.gloss: To extend a method, etc. by attaching some further code item.

decorator pattern.gloss: A structural (and partitioning) design pattern that allows behaviour to be added to an existing object dynamically.

decreasing function.gloss: Any function of a real variable whose value decreases (or is constant) as the variable increases.

decrementer.gloss: Any device or circuit that carries out a decrementation operation

decrunch.gloss: To decompress (data) previously compressed by crunching.

decruncher.gloss: A program or algorithm that performs decrunching.

decycling.gloss: The removal of cycles from a graph
Describing the smallest number of vertices that can be removed from a graph such that no cycles remain

dedecoration.gloss: Decimation (the elimination of points from a lattice); the inverse of decoration.

dedekind cut.gloss: Any partition of the set of rational numbers into non-empty sets A and B such that all elements of A are less than all elements of B and A contains no greatest element; intended as a construction of a real number.

dedekind domain.gloss: An integral domain in which every proper ideal factors into a product of prime ideals which is unique (up to permutations).

dedent.gloss: To outdent; to remove an indent from.

dedentation.gloss: The reversal of indentation, moving the text cursor back out from its indented position.

dedimensionalize.gloss: To remove dimensions, typically from an equation

deduction.gloss: A process of reasoning that moves from the general to the specific, in which a conclusion follows necessarily from the premises presented, so that the conclusion cannot be false if the premises are true. A conclusion; that which is deduced, concluded or figured out.

A process of reasoning that moves from the general to the specific, in which a conclusion follows necessarily from the premises presented, so that the conclusion cannot be false if the premises are true. The ability or skill to deduce or figure out; the power of reason

deduction theorem.gloss: A procedure for "discharging" assumptions from an inference, causing them to become antecedents of the conclusion; or vice versa. Symbolically, the conversion of an inference of the form P,A⊢C to an inference of the form P⊢A→C or vice versa, where ⊢ is the turnstile symbol. The validity of the procedure is a metatheorem of the given logical theory.

deductive.gloss: Based on inferences from general principles.

dedup.gloss: Deduplication; elimination of redundant duplicate data.

deduplication.gloss: The elimination of redundant duplicate data.

deduplicator.gloss: A process or system that deduplicates.

deep color.gloss: Graphics with 30 or more bits of storage per pixel, allowing for billions of distinct colors.

deep copy.gloss: A copy of a data structure duplicating not only the structure itself, but all structures to which it is linked.

deep embedding.gloss: The act of representing one language, typically a logic or programming language, with another by modeling expressions in the former as data in the latter.

defactor.gloss: To modify source code to remove design patterns and structure, for example to make it harder to reverse-engineer.

default.gloss: the original software programming settings as set by the factory
To assume a value when none was given; to presume a tentative value or standard.

default gateway.gloss: The node in a computer network using the Internet Protocol suite serving as the forwarding host to other networks when no other route specification matches the destination IP address of a packet.

defeasible.gloss: Capable of being defeated, terminated, annulled, voided or invalidated.

defeater.gloss: a belief which, if proved to be true, would imply outright or indirectly that another belief were false.

defect.gloss: A part by which a figure or quantity is wanting or deficient.

defective matrix.gloss: A square (n×n) matrix that has fewer than n linearly independent eigenvectors, and is therefore not diagonalisable.

defenestrate.gloss: To remove a Windows operating system from (a computer).

defenestration.gloss: The act of removing the Microsoft Windows operating system from a computer in order to install an alternative one.

defensive copy.gloss: A copy of a mutable object made for the purpose of preserving the current state of the object.

defensive copying.gloss: The design pattern of using defensive copies.

defensive design.gloss: The practice of planning for contingencies in the design stage of a project so as to make the misuse of the software impossible, or to minimise the negative consequences.

defensive programming.gloss: A form of defensive design aiming to ensure the continuing functioning of a piece of software in spite of unforeseeable usage of it.

deferred.gloss: Synonym of promise (“object representing delayed result”).

deferred time.gloss: The time when a deferred operation eventually takes place.

deficiency.gloss: The amount by which the number of double points on a curve is short of the maximum for curves of the same degree.
The codimension of a linear system in the corresponding complete linear system.

deficient.gloss: Of a number n, Having the sum of divisors σ(n) < 2n, or, equivalently, the sum of proper divisors (or aliquot sum) s(n) < n.

deficient number.gloss: A number that is greater than the sum of all of its divisors except itself.

defiddle.gloss: To clean up an automatically pixelated artwork so that it looks presentable.

define.gloss: To establish the referent of a term or notation.
A kind of macro in source code that replaces one text string with another wherever it occurs.

definite clause.gloss: A Horn clause with exactly one positive literal.

definite integral.gloss: The integral of a function between an upper and lower limit

definition.gloss: A statement which provides a previous declaration with a value or body of a subroutine (in the case of function).
A statement that establishes the referent of a term or notation.

definitive description.gloss: A phrase that designates an object by providing a description that is satisfied by exactly one object.

deflate.gloss: To compress (data) according to a particular algorithm.

deflationary.gloss: Belonging or relating to a family of theories claiming that assertions that predicate truth of a statement do not attribute a property called truth to such a statement.

defloat.gloss: To cause (a visual element such as a tool palette) no longer to float over the rest of the application.

deforestation.gloss: A transformation to eliminate intermediate data structures within a program.

deformation retract.gloss: A subspace such that there is a retraction onto it of the ambient space homotopic to the identity function on the ambient space.

deformatter.gloss: Something that deformats; a remover of formatting.

defragment.gloss: To run a process that collects fragments of files and sorts them into contiguous sections on one or more hard disks or hard disk partitions, thus speeding up file management.

dictionary.gloss: An associative array; a data structure where each value is referenced by a particular key, analogous to words and definitions in a dictionary (noun sense 1).

dictionary attack.gloss: An attempt to illegally access a computer network, website, etc., that uses a list of words (from a dictionary) to try to guess decryption keys or passwords.

diddle.gloss: To manipulate a value at the level of individual bits (binary digits).

didodecahedron.gloss: A solid with 24 faces consisting of scalene triangles.

didonia.gloss: The curve which on a given surface and with a given perimeter contains the greatest area.

diehard test.gloss: Any of a collection of statistical tests for gauging the randomness of a random number generator.

diff.gloss: Any program which compares two files or sets of files and outputs a description of the differences between them.
The output of a diff program, a diff file.
To run a diff program on (files or items) so as to produce a description of the differences between them, as for a patch file.
To compare two files or other objects, manually or otherwise.

diff eq.gloss: A college course in differential equations, usually as part of a standardized calculus curriculum.

diff file.gloss: A file produced by a diff program.
A file describing changes made to a computer file or files.

diffable.gloss: Suitable for processing by a diff program in order to show differences.

diffeomorphism.gloss: A differentiable homeomorphism (with differentiable inverse) between differentiable manifolds.

differ.gloss: A program that diffs, a diff.

difference.gloss: The quality or attribute which is added to those of the genus to constitute a species; a differentia.
The set of elements that are in one set but not another ( scriptstyle A◌̅B).

difference engine.gloss: A mechanical special-purpose computer used to generate tables of values of polynomials.

difference equation.gloss: An equation involving an ordered sequence of real numbers (a_nₙ₌₁ ᪲) and some of its differences, where the first difference is defined as Δ(a_n)=a_n+1-a_n, and the kᵗʰ difference is defined recursively as Δᵏ(a_n)=Δᵏ⁻¹(a_n+1)-Δᵏ⁻¹(a_n),.

difference of two squares.gloss: The identity x²-y²=(x+y)(x-y), that holds for all real numbers.

difference quotient.gloss: A mathematical quantity of the form (f(a+h)-f(a))/h for some function f(x), having two main interpretations: The average rate of change of the function f(x) over the interval [a,,a+h]. As h approaches zero, the value of (f(a+h)-f(a))/h approaches the derivative or instantaneous rate of change of f(x) at x=a.

A mathematical quantity of the form (f(a+h)-f(a))/h for some function f(x), having two main interpretations: The slope of the secant line passing through the points (a,,f(a)) and (a+h,,f(a+h)). As the horizontal distance h>0 between the points approaches zero, the slope of this secant line approaches the slope of the tangent line to f(x) at x=a, which is equal to the derivative of f(x) at x=a.

difference set.gloss: A subset of a group such that any element of the group can be expressed as the difference (or the quotient) of two elements in such subset.

different ideal.gloss: A measure of the lack of duality in the ring of integers of an algebraic number field K with respect to the field trace.

differentia.gloss: A distinguishing feature which marks a species off from other members of the same genus.

differentiable.gloss: Having a derivative, said of a function whose domain and codomain are manifolds.

differential.gloss: Of or pertaining to differentiation or the differential calculus.

A quantity representing an infinitesimal change in a variable, now only used as a heuristic aid except in nonstandard analysis but considered rigorous until the 20th century; a fluxion in Newtonian calculus, now usually written in Leibniz's notation as operatorname d!x.

A function giving the change in the linear approximation of f at a point x over a small interval Δx or operatorname d!x, the function being called the differential of f and denoted operatorname d!f(x,Δx), operatorname d!f(x), or simply operatorname d!f.
qualifiers: of a univariate differentiable function f(x)

differential.gloss: A function giving the change in the linear approximation of f at a point x over a small interval Δx or operatorname d!x, the function being called the differential of f and denoted operatorname d!f(x,Δx), operatorname d!f(x), or simply operatorname d!f. Any of several generalizations of this concept to functions of several variables or to higher orders: the partial differential, total differential, Gateaux differential, etc.
qualifiers: of a univariate differentiable function f(x)

differential.gloss: Any of several generalizations of the concept(s) above: e.g. the Kähler differential in the setting of schemes, the quadratic differential in the theory of Riemann surfaces, etc.

differential calculus.gloss: The calculus that deals with instantaneous rates of change.

differential equation.gloss: An equation involving the derivatives of a function.

differential geometry.gloss: The study of geometry, especially geometric structures on differentiable manifolds, using techniques from calculus, linear algebra and multilinear algebra.

differential operator.gloss: An operator defined as a function of the differentiation operator (the operator which maps functions to their derivatives).

differential structure.gloss: A structure defined for a (topological) manifold so that it supports differentiation of functions defined on it.

differential topology.gloss: Field dealing with differentiable functions on differentiable manifolds.

differentiatable.gloss: For which a derivative or differential can be calculated.

differentiate.gloss: To calculate the derivative of a function.
To calculate the differential of a function of multiple variables.

differentiation.gloss: The process of applying the derivative operator to a function; of calculating a function's derivative.

differintegral.gloss: Any type of mathematical operator which combines the properties of the fractional derivative and the fractional integral.

diffogram.gloss: A diagram that uses diagonal lines to display the results of multiple pairwise difference of means tests.

diffuson.gloss: A mathematical object relating to diffusive motion, used in the theory of electron transport in disordered systems.

digamma function.gloss: The first of the polygamma functions, being the logarithmic derivative of the gamma function.

digest.gloss: The result of applying a hash function to a message.

digit.gloss: A position in a sequence of numerals representing a place value in a positional number system.
A distinct symbol representing a natural number in a positional number system.
Synonym of degree: ¹⁄₃₆₀ of a circle.

digit sum.gloss: the number obtained when repeatedly applying above described operation until arriving at a single-digit number.

digitaddition.gloss: The addition of all the digits of a number; the sum so obtained. The repetition of this process eventually leads to a single digit: the digital root of the original number.

digital computer.gloss: A computing device that processes signals that change in discrete, quantized, steps; as opposed to an analog computer.

digital dark age.gloss: The lack of historical information in the digital age as a direct result of outdated file formats, software, or hardware that becomes corrupt, scarce, or inaccessible as technologies evolve and data decays.

digital divide.gloss: The gap between those with regular, effective access to digital technologies (and the computer literacy to use them) and those without it.

digital rights management.gloss: A set of access control technologies that restrict the use of proprietary hardware and digital files by an end user, so as to enforce copyright restrictions.

digital root.gloss: The single digit obtained from a number by repetitive digitaddition

digital storage.gloss: The recording or storing of information (data) in a digital, machine-readable medium.

digital watermark.gloss: Auxiliary data embedded in a datafile for subsequent identification and verification of the file.

digitization.gloss: The conversion of data or information from analog to digital or binary.
Hence, the transformation of a process or system from mainly analogue form to digital form

digitize.gloss: To represent something (such as an image or sound) as a structured sequence of binary digits.

digon.gloss: A polygon having two edges and two vertices.
A pair of parallel undirected edges in a multigraph.
A pair of antiparallel edges in a directed graph.

digonal.gloss: symmetrical about a 180° turn about an axis

digraph.gloss: A two-character sequence used to enter a single conceptual character.

digraphoid.gloss: A dual pair of regular matroids.

digraphon.gloss: The object obtained as the limit of a convergent sequence of directed graphs.

dihectagon.gloss: A polygon with two hundred sides and two hundred angles.

dihedral.gloss: An angle between two plane surfaces
Consisting of, relating to or contained between two plane surfaces.

dihedral group.gloss: a group of symmetries of a regular polygon

dilation.gloss: In morphology, a basic operation (denoted ⊕) that usually uses a structuring element for probing and expanding the shapes contained in the input image.

dilemma.gloss: A type of syllogism of the form "if A is true then B is true; if C is true then D is true; either A or C is true; therefore either B or D is true".

dilogarithm.gloss: The form of polylogarithm having a base of two

dimension.gloss: The number of independent coordinates needed to specify uniquely the location of a point in a space; also, any of such independent coordinates.
The number of elements of any basis of a vector space.
Any of the independent ranges of indices in a multidimensional array.
To specify the size of (an array or similar data structure); to allocate.

dimensional.gloss: Having dimension or dimensions; three-dimensional. Appended to cardinal numbers or algebraic symbols to form adjectives meaning "having the stated number of dimensions".

dimensional analysis.gloss: The study of the dimensions of physical quantities; used to obtain information about large complex systems, and as a means of checking mathematical and physics equations.

dimensionality.gloss: The number of dimensions something has.

dimm.gloss: Initialism of dual in-line memory module.

dinatural.gloss: That can be transformed in two related ways.

dioperad.gloss: An operad having multiple inputs and multiple outputs

diophantine.gloss: Of or pertaining to Diophantus, the Greek mathematician.

diophantine equation.gloss: A polynomial equation whose variables are only permitted to assume integer values.

diophantine geometry.gloss: A developing branch of mathematics in which techniques of algebraic geometry are applied to number theory (specifically the theory of Diophantine equations), in particular being concerned with algebraic varieties over fields that are finitely generated over their prime fields and over local fields.

dip switch.gloss: A miniature switch designed to be attached to a circuit board to customize the behavior of the circuit.

dirac comb.gloss: A periodic tempered distribution constructed from Dirac delta functions for some given period. It allows both continuous and discrete phenomena to be represented in a single framework.

dirac delta.gloss: A function-like symbol denoted as δ, with the property ∫f(t)δ(x-t)dt=f(x), informally understood as a function with an infinite value at 0 and zero elsewhere, and formally as a distribution or a measure.

dirac delta function.gloss: A function of one real argument, whose value is zero when the argument is nonzero, and whose integral is one over any interval that includes zero.

direct.gloss: Not employing the law of the excluded middle or argument by contradiction.

direct buffer.gloss: A portion of native memory that is shared with Java and can be used for direct reads.

direct limit.gloss: A set of equivalence classes which partition the disjoint union of the members of a direct system; each equivalence class being a sort of “drainage basin” of the mappings (of the morphisms) of the direct system, if these are analogically considered as “rivers”. direct product.gloss: The set of all possible tuples whose elements are elements of given, separately specified, sets.

Such a set of tuples formed from two or more groups, forming another group whose group operation is the component-wise application of the original group operations and of which the original groups are normal subgroups.
A topological space analogously formed from two or more (up to an infinite number of) topological spaces.
Any of a number of mathematical objects analogously derived from a given ordered set of objects.
A high-level generalization of the preceding that applies to objects in an arbitrary category and produces a new object constructable by morphisms from each of the original objects.

direct sum.gloss: coproduct in some categories, like abelian groups, topological spaces or modules

A linear sum in which the intersection of the summands has dimension zero. Equivalently, a linear sum of two subspaces, any vector of which can be expressed uniquely as a sum of two vectors: one vector belonging to the first subspace, and the other vector belonging to the second subspace.
A block diagonal matrix interpreted as having its non-zero blocks (which are square matrices) as summands.

direct system.gloss: A set of algebraic structures (which are part of a concrete category; e.g., modules) and a set of morphisms between them (e.g., module homomorphisms) which all together form a small category which is the image of a covariant functor whose domain is a directed poset.

directed.gloss: Having the properties of a directed graph.
Having the properties of a directed set.

directed acyclic graph.gloss: A finite directed graph that contains no directed cycles.

directed acyclic word graph.gloss: A data structure that represents a set of strings and allows for a query operation that tests whether a given string belongs to the set in time proportional to its length (thus more efficient in some situations than a trie).

directed edge.gloss: An edge of a directed graph.

directed graph.gloss: A graph in which the edges are ordered pairs, so that, if the edge (a, b) is in the graph, the edge (b, a) need not be in the graph and is distinct from (a, b) if it is.

directed path.gloss: In a directed graph, a path in which the edges are all oriented in the same direction.

directed set.gloss: A set equipped with a preorder such that for any two elements a and b there is an element c such that a ≤ c and b ≤ c.

direction vector.gloss: A unit vector used to represent spatial direction, commonly denoted as d.

directional derivative.gloss: A function which measures the rate of change of some other function at any point in a particular direction; formally, the directional derivative of a scalar function f( mathbf x)=f(x_1,x_2,…,x_n) along a vector mathbf v=(v_1,…,v_n) is the function ∇_(mathbf v)f defined by the limit ∇_(mathbf v)f( mathbf x)= lim _(h→0)(f( mathbf x+h mathbf v)-f( mathbf x))/h.

directive.gloss: A construct in source code that indicates how it should be processed but is not necessarily part of the program to be run.

directly proportional.gloss: Proportional to a constant multiple of an independent variable.

director circle.gloss: A circle formed by all 90° crossings of tangents of an ellipse or hyperbola.

directory.gloss: A structured listing of the names and characteristics of the files on a storage device.
A virtual container in a computer's file system, in which files and other directories may be stored. The files and subdirectories in a directory are usually related.

directory service.gloss: The software system that stores, organizes and provides access to information in a map between names and values.

directrix.gloss: A line used to define a curve or surface; especially a line, the distance from which a point on a conic has a constant ratio to that from the focus.

dirichlet character.gloss: A complex-valued arithmetic function χ:ℤ→ℂ that satisfies the following conditions for some positive integer m and all integers a and b

dirichlet distribution.gloss: Any of a family of continuous multivariate probability distributions parameterized by a vector of positive reals.

dirichlet energy.gloss: A quadratic functional which, given a real function defined on an open subset of ℝⁿ, yields a real number that is a measure of how variable said function is.

dirichlet problem.gloss: The problem of finding a function that solves a specified partial differential equation in the interior of a given region that takes prescribed values on the boundary of the region.

dirichlet process.gloss: Any of a family of stochastic processes whose realizations are probability distributions.

dirichlet series.gloss: Any infinite series of the form ∑ₙ₌₁ ᪲(a_n)/(nˢ), where s and each a_n are complex numbers.

dirigent.gloss: The line of motion of a describent line or surface that in so moving defines a plane or solid figure; a directrix.

dirimens copulatio.gloss: Mentioning a balancing or opposing fact to prevent the argument from being one-sided or unqualified.

dirty.gloss: Containing data needing to be written back to memory or disk.

dirty code.gloss: Software code that has had many editors with conflicting styles, making it nearly impossible to maintain.

disable.gloss: To deactivate, to make inoperational (especially of a function of an electronic or mechanical device).

disambiguator.gloss: A program that determines the meaning of a term from the context in which it is used

disassemble.gloss: To convert machine code to a human-readable, mnemonic form.

disassembler.gloss: A computer program that examines another computer program and attempts to generate assembly language source code that would, in theory, reproduce the target program.

disassembly.gloss: The code generated by a disassembler.

disassortative.gloss: Describing a graph (or network) in which nodes of low degree are more likely to connect with nodes of a high degree

disattenuation.gloss: A correction to account for attenuation

discard.gloss: A temporary variable used to receive a value of no importance and unable to be read later.

discharge.gloss: To release (an auxiliary assumption) from the list of assumptions used in arguments, and return to the main argument.

disconjugate.gloss: Having at most one fewer zeros (including multiplicities) than the dimension of the problem space.

disconnected.gloss: That can be partitioned into two nonempty subsets which are both open and closed.

discontinuity.gloss: A point in the range of a function at which it is undefined or discontinuous.

discordant.gloss: Of figures, etc.: having opposite signs (for example, positive and negative).

discrete.gloss: Consisting of or permitting only distinct values drawn from a finite, countable set.
Having each singleton subset open: said of a topological space or a topology.

discrete category.gloss: A category whose morphisms are all identity morphisms.

discrete choice analysis.gloss: The analysis of a model whose dependent variable is a binary (two-valued) variable.

discrete fourier transform.gloss: The process of converting a discrete time-based function into its frequency-based representation.

discrete mathematics.gloss: Collectively, most discrete or computer science-related branches of mathematics, such as graph theory and combinatorics.

discrete metric.gloss: a metric d such that for any pair of points x and y, d(x,y)=0 if x=y and d(x,y)=1 if x ne y.

discrete set.gloss: A set of points of a topological space such that each point in the set is an isolated point, i.e. a point that has a neighborhood that contains no other points of the set.

discrete time.gloss: A framework which views values of variables as occurring at distinct, separate points in time, or equivalently as being unchanged throughout each nonzero region of time.

discrete topology.gloss: A topology on a set consisting of all subsets of that set.

discrete valuation.gloss: A valuation (on some field) that takes integer values (including infinity).

discrete valuation ring.gloss: A local principal ideal domain whose unique maximal ideal is not the zero ideal.

discrete variable.gloss: A variable that takes values from a finite or countable set, such as the number of legs of an animal.

discrete wavelet transform.gloss: Any wavelet series in which the wavelets are discretely sampled.

discrete-time markov chain.gloss: A sequence of random variables, known as a stochastic process, in which the value of the next variable depends only on the value of the current variable, and not any variables in the past.

discrete-time signal.gloss: A time series consisting of a sequence of quantities.

discretive.gloss: Disjunctive with the additional characteristic that the conjoined clauses, while exhibiting a disjunct, are both asserted as true.

discretive proposition.gloss: A compound proposition in which contrasting judgments are made, connected by a word such as "but" or "though".

discretization.gloss: The act of discretizing, or dividing a continuous object or spectrum into a finite number of discrete elements

discretize.gloss: To convert (a continuous space) into an equivalent discrete space, often for the purposes of easier calculation.

discriminant.gloss: An expression that gives information about the roots of a polynomial; for example, the expression D = b² - 4ac determines whether the roots of the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 are real and distinct (D > 0), real and equal (D = 0) or complex (D < 0).
The invariant (on the vector space of forms of degree d in n variables) that vanishes exactly when the corresponding hypersurface in Pⁿ⁻¹ is singular.

discriminant function.gloss: A function used to predict a categorical dependent variable by one or more continuous or binary independent variables.

disdyakis triacontahedron.gloss: A Catalan solid with 120 scalene triangle faces, 180 edges and 62 vertices, being the dual of the truncated icosidodecahedron.

disentailed.gloss: In constraint programming: inconsistent with the set of constraints.

disjoint.gloss: Of two or more sets, having no members in common; having an intersection equal to the empty set.
Of two or more elements in a lattice, having a meet equal to the bottom element.

disjoint set.gloss: A family of sets sharing no elements in common; sets whose intersection is the empty set.
A data structure used to store such sets and perform operations on them efficiently.

disjoint union.gloss: A union of sets forced to be disjoint by attaching information referring to the original sets to their elements (i.e., by using indexing).
A union of sets which are already pairwise disjoint.
The disjoint union of the underlying sets of a given family of topological spaces, equipped with a topology.

disjoint union topology.gloss: A topology which is applicable to the disjoint union of a given set of topological spaces and is the largest (most inclusive) topology that preserves the continuity of each contributing space as represented in the union.

disjunct.gloss: One of multiple propositions, any of which, if true, confirm the validity of another proposition (a disjunction).

disjunction.gloss: The proposition resulting from the combination of two or more propositions using the or operator.
A logical operator that results in “true” when any of its operands are true.

disjunctive.gloss: Of or related to a disjunction.

disjunctive normal form.gloss: The form of a boolean formula that the formula has if the formula is a disjunction of conjunctions of literals, such as “(A and B and C) or (D and E and not F)”.

disjunctive syllogism.gloss: A logical argument of the form that if there are only two possibilities, and one of them is ruled out, then the other must take place. In symbols: P∨Q,¬P⊢Q

disk.gloss: A two-dimensional geometric region, the set of points bounded by a circle.

disk access time.gloss: The total amount of time required for an operating system to process a read-write request involving disk storage.

disk buffer.gloss: A buffer onboard a secondary storage device (disk) used to temporarily hold data being read from or written to it.

disk drive.gloss: A computer drive that reads disks.

disk image.gloss: A copy of all or part of a disk drive retained for backup or replication purposes.

disk operating system.gloss: A type of computer operating system that requires a disk drive for secondary storage to manage files and load programs.

disk pack.gloss: A rigid cylindrical device having a center spindle and one or more steel plates with a magnetic coating, used to store and retrieve computer files.

diskcyclic.gloss: Describing a form of cyclicity operator having criteria midway between a hypercyclic and a supercyclic operator.

diskette.gloss: A small, flexible, magnetic disk for storage and retrieval of data.

disklabel.gloss: A record on a hard disk or other storage device, holding information about the location of the partitions on the disk.

diskless.gloss: Without the use of floppy disks.

diskspace.gloss: storage space available on a computer disk

dismantlable.gloss: The property of an ordered set such that its elements can be listed in an order such that, for every element, the element is irreducible (has exactly one upper or lower cover) in the subset consisting of that element and all subsequent elements.

The property of a graph such that its vertices can be listed in an order such that, for every vertex, the vertex is a subdominant vertex (has an adjacent vertex that is adjacent to every other vertex that it is adjacent to) in the induced subgraph generated by that vertex and all subsequent vertices.

dismount.gloss: To make (a mounted drive) unavailable for use.

disocclude.gloss: To cause to be no longer occluded.

disocclusion.gloss: The situation where a previously occluded object becomes visible.

disordinal.gloss: Describing a situation in which the rank order of two contributory factors changes at some value

disown.gloss: To detach (a job or process) so that it can continue to run even when the user who launched it ends his/her login session.

dispatch.gloss: To pass on for further processing, especially via a dispatch table (often with to).
The passing on of a message for further processing, especially through a dispatch table.

dispatch table.gloss: A table of pointers to functions or methods, commonly used to implement dynamic binding.

dispatcher.gloss: A piece of software responsible for assigning priorities and resources to tasks waiting to be scheduled.

disperser.gloss: A particular kind of bipartite graph.

disphenocingulum.gloss: A polyhedron, one of the Johnson solids, having 20 triangular and 4 square faces.

disphenoid.gloss: A non-regular tetrahedron whose four faces are congruent acute-angled triangles.

displacement mapping.gloss: A method for adding detail to surfaces by subdivision and displacement of the resulting vertices from a heightmap.

display.gloss: An electronic screen that shows graphics or text.
The presentation of information for visual or tactile reception.

display list.gloss: A sequence of commands that define a graphical output.

distance fog.gloss: A gradient that progressively obscures objects as they get further from the camera, typically used to avoid the processing overhead of rendering distant objects.

distance function.gloss: a function used to calculate the distance between two points.

distance vector.gloss: A class of routing protocol based on sending global state between neighbouring nodes.

distantial.gloss: Pertaining to the difference between items.

distinguished open set.gloss: A particularly basic kind of set, generalizing the notion of the complement of a hypersurface, originating in the study of algebraic varieties but in modern mathematics also extending to the setting of affine schemes. Formally: (in the context of affine or projective varieties) the complement of the zero locus of a polynomial in affine or projective space; (in scheme theory) the subset of prime ideals of a commutative ring which do not contain some element of the ring.

distributable.gloss: A software component that can be distributed.

distribute.gloss: To employ (a term) in its whole extent; to take as universal in one premise.

distributed.gloss: Involving numerous separate computers or entities, rather than the traditional one.

distributed hash table.gloss: A decentralised distributed system that performs the functions of a hash table.

distributed ray tracing.gloss: A form of ray tracing that averages a number of rays across an interval, allowing for the rendering of soft or blurry phenomena.

distribution.gloss: A probability distribution; the set of relative likelihoods that a variable will have a value in a given interval.
A subset of the tangent bundle of a manifold that satisfies certain properties; used to construct the notions of integrability and foliation of a manifold.
A set of bundled software components.
The resolution of a whole into its parts.

distribution curve.gloss: A graphical representation, usually as a curve, that shows how values in a data set are distributed.

distribution function.gloss: A function of seven variables of the form f(x,y,z,t;v_x,v_y,v_z) that gives the number of particles per unit volume in single-particle phase space.

distribution server.gloss: a network server that stores the installation files for distribution over a network.

distribution-free.gloss: Free of specific assumptions about the shape of the probability distribution generating the sample.

distributional semantics.gloss: A field of research focused on quantifying and categorizing the semantic similarities between linguistic items.

distributional–relational database.gloss: A type of database management system that enhances the semantics of structured data by using distributional word-vector representations.

distributive.gloss: A property of functions that have a rule describing how the function can be performed to the individual components of another operation.
Assigning the species of a general term.

distributive lattice.gloss: A lattice in which the "meet" and the "join" operations are distributive with respect to each other.

distro.gloss: A set of software components, often open source, that have been packaged into a larger product or component for distribution to end-users.

distro-hopping.gloss: The process of frequently changing the operating system of one's computer to a different distribution of Linux.

dither.gloss: To apply an algorithm to digital data to minimize the effects of quantization: To use dot patterns in an image or graphic to simulate colors or shades not in the system palette.
To apply an algorithm to digital data to minimize the effects of quantization: To intentionally add noise to a signal to remove artifacts caused by digitization.
Any algorithm applied to digital data to minimize the effects of quantization: A form of noise intentionally added to remove artifacts caused by digitization.
Any algorithm applied to digital data to minimize the effects of quantization: The use of dot patterns in an image or graphic to approximate colors not available in the system palette.

dithered.gloss: Produced by dithering; consisting of bits in different colors placed side by side to simulate an intermediate color that is not in the palette, or the somewhat banded or mottled look that this can produce.

ditopology.gloss: A dichotomous topology; A topology that includes two structures: one describing the properties related to openness of sets, the other describing the properties related to closedness of sets.

div.gloss: A function, implemented in many programming languages, that returns the result of a division of two integers.
A section of a web page, or the div element that represents it in HTML code.

diverge.gloss: Not to converge: to have no limit, or no finite limit.

divergence.gloss: The operator which maps a function F=(F₁, ... Fₙ) from a n-dimensional vector space to itself to the function ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ(∂F_i)/(∂x_i).

divergent.gloss: (said of a sequence or series) Diverging; not approaching a limit.

divergent series.gloss: An infinite series whose partial sums are divergent.

divide and choose.gloss: A procedure for envy-free fair cake-cutting in which one person divides a heterogeneous resource in two and the other person chooses one of those two.

divide and conquer.gloss: An algorithm design technique that solves a problem by splitting it recursively into smaller problems until all of the remaining problems are trivial.

divisibility sequence.gloss: Any sequence of integers {aₙ}, indexed by the natural numbers, such that if n is divisible by m then aₙ is divisible by aₘ.

division.gloss: Any of the four major parts of a COBOL program source code.

division algebra.gloss: A linear algebra such that its non-zero vectors form a multiplicative group.
An algebra over a field such that every non-zero element of it has a multiplicative inverse. (It is not required to have a unity element.)

division ring.gloss: A ring with 0 ≠ 1, such that every non-zero element a has a multiplicative inverse, meaning an element x with ax = 1.

division sign.gloss: Any symbol (in particular ÷, / or : ) used to denote the operation of division.

division slash.gloss: The symbol (∕) used to denote the operation of division.

divisor.gloss: An integer that divides another integer an integral number of times, the former being called a divisor of the latter. domain.gloss: The set of input (argument) values for which a function is defined.

echoable.gloss: Capable of, or suitable for, being echoed to the display.

echoback.gloss: A test where data is transmitted from one system to another system and back again.

eigencoefficient.gloss: Any of the coefficients of an eigenstate.

eigencurve.gloss: A rigid analytic curve that parametrizes certain p-adic families of modular forms.

eigendecompose.gloss: To form the eigendecomposition of a matrix.

epsilon.gloss: An arbitrarily small quantity. A small child.

epsilon number.gloss: Any (necessarily transfinite) ordinal number α such that ω^α = α; (by generalisation) any surreal number that is a fixed point of the exponential map x → ωˣ.

epsilon-machine.gloss: A deterministic automaton consisting of a system of causal states and the transitions between them, functioning as the smallest possible maximally predictive model of a stochastic process

epsilonize.gloss: To convert small errors to zero or to treat them as arbitrarily small

epsilontic.gloss: Pertaining to mathematical analysis using explicit error bound estimation and the epsilon-delta definition of a limit, especially as opposed to using infinitesimals.

epsilontics.gloss: An approach to mathematical analysis using the epsilon-delta definition of a limit, i.e. with explicit estimation of error bounds, as opposed to using infinitesimals.
An instance of reasoning performed using this approach.

epstein class.gloss: A family of real-analytic interval maps that have a particularly well-controlled extension to the complex plane, used to study renormalization, especially for unimodal maps and critical circle maps.

equal.gloss: The same in one or more respects. Exactly identical, having the same value.
To be equal to, to have the same value as; to correspond to.

equal detour point.gloss: A triangle center characterized by the property that, if one travels from any vertex of the triangle to another by taking a detour through some inner point, then the additional distance traveled is constant.

equality.gloss: The fact of being equal, of having the same value.

equalize.gloss: to precompose with each of a parallel pair of morphisms so as to yield the same composite morphism.
To adjust the balance between frequency components within an electronic signal.

equalizer.gloss: A set of arguments where two or more functions have equal values; the solution set of an equation.

A morphism whose codomain is the domain of a parallel pair of morphisms and which forms part of the limit of that parallel pair. Equivalently, a morphism which equalizes a parallel pair of morphisms in a limiting way, which is to say that any other morphism which equalizes that parallel pair factors through this limiting morphism; and moreover such factorization is unique.

equate.gloss: A statement in assembly language that defines a symbol having a particular value.

equation.gloss: An assertion that two expressions are equal, expressed by writing the two expressions separated by an equal sign; in mathematical problems, equations describe various essential aspects of the problem, each of which contributes to the resolution of the problem in part.

equational class.gloss: Synonym of variety (“an equational class in universal algebra”).

equational variety.gloss: Synonym of variety (“an equational class in universal algebra”).

equiaffine.gloss: Being an affine transformation that preserves area.

equiaffinity.gloss: An affine transformation that preserves area.

equiangular.gloss: Of a polygon, having all interior angles equal. This is not necessarily a regular polygon, since that would also be equilateral; a rectangle is equiangular but not equilateral, unless it is a square.

equianharmonic.gloss: equally anharmonic; specifically, whose anharmonic ratio is a cube root of unity
A set of four points whose cross ratio (or anharmonic ratio) is a cube root of 1.

equibipartite.gloss: Having vertices that can be divided into two equal independent sets

equibounded.gloss: Having the property that there exists a positive number M such that for all functions f in the family of functions F defined on X, |f(x)| ≤ M for all x in X.

equicharacteristic.gloss: Of a ring: such that the ring and its residue field have the same characteristic.

equicontinuous.gloss: Such that all members are continuous, with equal variation in a given neighborhood.

equiconvergent.gloss: Of two series: such that the sum of all the terms in both series is convergent to zero.

equidecomposable.gloss: Capable of being decomposed into a number of pieces that can be reassembled into either of the two.

equidiagonal.gloss: Of a convex quadrilateral: having the two diagonals of equal length.

equidissectable.gloss: Of a polygon: able to be divided into triangles of equal area.

equidissection.gloss: The division of a polygon into triangles of equal area.

equidistant.gloss: Any of a set of points or figures that are equidistant.

equifrequency.gloss: Having, or concerning the same frequencies

equijoin.gloss: A join whose predicate uses only equality comparisons.
To join with a predicate using only equality comparisons.

equilateral triangle.gloss: A triangle having all three sides equal.

equilogical.gloss: Pertaining to topological spaces that are Cartesian closed categories.

equimax.gloss: Describing a compromise between varimax and quartimax criteria.

equimultiple.gloss: One of the products arising from the multiplication of two or more values by the same value.
Multiplied by the same number or quantity.

equinormality.gloss: Having a normal distribution and equal variance.

equinumerosity.gloss: The state or quality of being equinumerous.

equioscillation.gloss: An oscillation of equal to other oscillations amplitude or phase.

equipartition.gloss: The partition of its vertex set into sets whose sizes differ from each other by no more than 1.

equipollence.gloss: Sameness of signification of two or more propositions which differ in language.

equipollent.gloss: able to be deduced from the other

equipotent.gloss: Of two sets, having a bijection with one another.

equiprobable.gloss: Having equal probability, such as any number from 1 to 6 being the equiprobable outcome of the fair toss of fair dice.

equiradical.gloss: Of surds: arising from the extraction of the same nth root.

equiregular.gloss: Containing elements that are both outer regular and inner regular and which have inverses that are also both outer regular and inner regular.
Having both all sides equal length and all angles equal.

equisatisfiable.gloss: Of a pair of formulas, where one formula is satisfiable whenever the other is satisfiable (either both formulas are satisfiable or both are not).

equisummable.gloss: Of two or more series: such that their difference is summable.

equitangential.gloss: Of a curve: having tangential segments that are all of the same length.

equivalence.gloss: The relationship between two propositions that are either both true or both false.
A Boolean operation that is TRUE when both input variables are TRUE or both input variables are FALSE, but otherwise FALSE; the XNOR function.
A number in intersection theory. A positive-dimensional variety sometimes behaves formally as if it were a finite number of points; this number is its equivalence.

equivalence class.gloss: Any one of the subsets into which an equivalence relation partitions a set, each of these subsets containing all the elements of the set that are equivalent under the equivalence relation.

equivalence of categories.gloss: An adjunction whose unit and counit are both natural isomorphisms.

equivalence relation.gloss: A binary relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

equivalent.gloss: Of two sets, having a one-to-one correspondence.
Relating to the corresponding elements of an equivalence relation.

Of two categories, (informally) such that one is essentially a relabeling of the other; (formally) related by a pair of functors such the composition of the one with the other is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor.
Equal in measure but not admitting of superposition; applied to magnitudes.

equivariant.gloss: Not affected by a specified group action.

equivelar.gloss: In which each face and vertex has the same number of edges

equivocation.gloss: A logical fallacy resulting from the use of multiple meanings of a single expression.

eraser.gloss: An overwriter program used to prevent data recovery.

eraser dust.gloss: A font that simulates wide hand-drawn letters with a slightly mottled appearance and irregular edges.

erasure code.gloss: A forward-error-correction (FEC) code for the binary erasure channel, which transforms a message of k symbols into a longer message with n symbols such that the original message can be recovered from a subset of the n symbols.

ercp.gloss: Initialism of embedded Rich Client Platform.

erdős number.gloss: A number describing the degree of collaboration between a mathematician and Paul Erdős, defined such that a mathematician who has written a paper with Erdős has an Erdős number of 1, a mathematician who has written a paper with somebody having an Erdős number of 1 has an Erdős number of two, and so on.

ergodic.gloss: Of or relating to certain systems that, given enough time, will eventually return to a previously experienced state.
Of or relating to a process in which every sequence or sample of sufficient size is equally representative of the whole.
Of or relating to a literary work that requires nontrivial effort on the reader's part to traverse.

ergodic theory.gloss: The study of the properties of dynamical systems over large timescales.
Any of a number of different formulations or schools of thought within ergodic theory as a whole.

erosion.gloss: One of two fundamental operations in morphological image processing from which all other morphological operations are derived.
In morphology, a basic operation (denoted ⊖); see Erosion (morphology).

errno.gloss: A value or variable that identifies the kind of error (or lack thereof) that has occurred during the execution of a program or subroutine.

error.gloss: A failure to complete a task, usually involving a premature termination.
The difference between a measured or calculated value and a true one.
To function improperly due to an error, especially accompanied by error message.

error diffusion.gloss: A form of halftoning in which the quantization residual is distributed to neighbouring pixels that have not yet been processed.

error function.gloss: A sigmoid function giving the probability that a measurement, under the influence of normally distributed errors with standard deviation, is within a certain distance from the mean value.

error message.gloss: A message displayed when a failure condition occurs, usually on a computer or device.

esc key.gloss: A key used to ɡenerate the escape character.

escape.gloss: To cause (a single character, or all such characters in a string) to be interpreted literally, instead of with any special meaning it would usually have in the same context, often by prefixing with another character.
To halt a program or command by pressing a key (such as the "Esc" key) or combination of keys.
The text character represented by 27 (decimal) or 1B (hexadecimal).

escape character.gloss: A single metacharacter, usually a control code, which in a sequence of characters signifies that what is to follow takes an alternative interpretation. The term escape sequence refers to the escape character and the subsequent character or characters so modified.

escape key.gloss: A key on a computer keyboard that can be used to cancel an operation.

escape sequence.gloss: An escape character together with subsequent characters, not output as written, but specifying a particular behaviour.
