escaper.gloss: A program or algorithm for escaping text.

escribe.gloss: To draw outside of; designating a circle that touches one of the sides of a given triangle, and also the extensions of the other two sides.

esoteric programming language.gloss: A programming language with highly unconventional syntax or operation, designed as an experiment or as a joke rather than for the serious development of software.

ess.gloss: Initialism of explained sum of squares.

essential.gloss: Such that each complementary region is irreducible, the boundary of each complementary region is incompressible by disks and monogons in the complementary region, and no leaf is a sphere or a torus bounding a solid torus in the manifold.

essential infimum.gloss: The infimum (greatest lower bound) of a function which holds almost everywhere. In symbols, ess inf f= sup m:μ(x:f(x)<m)=0.

essential supremum.gloss: The supremum (least upper bound) of a function which holds almost everywhere. In symbols, ess sup f= inf M:μ(x:f(x)>M)=0

estate.gloss: An organization's collective information technology resources.

estimator.gloss: A function of a random sample of a population used to estimate some parameter of the whole population

eta conversion.gloss: One of the three rewrite rules of lambda calculus, which expresses a sort of tautology about function application. The rule says that a lambda abstraction of the form (λx.(fx)) may be rewritten as simply f, provided that x does not occur freely in f (considered by itself).

ethernet card.gloss: A hardware component that connects a computer or other device to an Ethernet network.

eubouliatic.gloss: Pertaining to the modality of safety or prudence.

euclid's lemma.gloss: The proposition that if a prime number p divides an arbitrary product ab of integers, then p divides a or b or both;

euclidean.gloss: Adhering to the principles of traditional geometry, in which parallel lines are equidistant.

euclidean algorithm.gloss: Specifically, a method, based on a division algorithm, for finding the greatest common divisor (gcd) of two given integers; any of certain variations or generalisations of said method.

euclidean distance.gloss: The distance between two points defined as the square root of the sum of the squares of the differences between the corresponding coordinates of the points; for example, in two-dimensional Euclidean geometry, the Euclidean distance between two points a = (aₓ, a_y) and b = (bₓ, b_y) is defined as

The distance between two points defined as the square root of the sum of the squares of the differences between the corresponding coordinates of the points; for example, in two-dimensional Euclidean geometry, the Euclidean distance between two points a = (aₓ, a_y) and b = (bₓ, b_y) is defined as:
 d( textbf a, textbf b)=√(( textbf aₓ- textbf bₓ)²+( textbf a_y- textbf b_y)²) d( textbf a, textbf b)=√(( textbf aₓ- textbf bₓ)²+( textbf a_y- textbf b_y)²)

euclidean domain.gloss: an integral domain in which division with remainder is possible

euclidean geometry.gloss: The familiar geometry of the real world, based on the parallel postulate.

euclidean group.gloss: the set of rigid motions that are also affine transformations.

euclidean metric.gloss: In the space ℝⁿ, the metric d(⃑x,⃑y)=√((x_1-y_1)²+(x_2-y_2)²+...+(x_n-y_n)²) where ⃑x=(x_1,...,x_n) and ⃑y=(y_1,...,y_n).

euclidean norm.gloss: A norm of an ordinary Euclidean space, for which the Pythagorean theorem holds, defined by ‖x‖=√(∑ⱼx_j²)

euclidean space.gloss: Any real vector space on which a real-valued inner product (and, consequently, a metric) is defined.

euler angle.gloss: Any one of three angles which together describe the orientation of a rigid body with respect to a fixed three-dimensional coordinate system, according to a formalism introduced by Leonhard Euler.

euler characteristic.gloss: The sum of even-dimensional Betti numbers minus the sum of odd-dimensional ones.

euler genus.gloss: The minimal integer n such that the given graph can be drawn without crossing itself on a sphere with n cross-caps or with n/2 handles.

euler line.gloss: A line that, for a given triangle, passes through several important points, including the circumcentre, orthocentre and centroid; an analogous line for certain other 2- and 3-dimensional geometric figures.
An Eulerian path, a looped path through a graph that passes along every edge exactly once.

eulerian circuit.gloss: An Eulerian trail that begins and ends at the same node.

eulerian graph.gloss: a graph containing an Eulerian circuit.

eulerian path.gloss: A walk that uses every edge of a graph exactly once.

eulerian trail.gloss: A trail that contains each edge exactly once.

eumorphism.gloss: A surjective homomorphism F on a group X which preserves certain metrics such as ones of distance.

eureka step.gloss: A flash of insight that cracks a problem and paves the way to a solution.

eurocard.gloss: A printed circuit board card in a standard European format, designed to plug into a standardized subrack.

eval.gloss: To evaluate (or execute) source code held in a string during run time.

evaluate.gloss: To compute or determine the value of (an expression).
To return or have a specific value.

evaluation.gloss: A completion of a mathematical operation; a valuation.
Determination of the value of a variable or expression.

evanescent.gloss: Disappearing, vanishing. Of a number or value: diminishing to the point of reaching zero as a limit; infinitesimal.

evectant.gloss: A contravariant constructed from an invariant by acting on it with a differential operator called an evector.

evector.gloss: A differential operator that allows a contravariant to be constructed from an invariant.

even.gloss: Of an integer, divisible by two.

even function.gloss: Any function whose value is unchanged if the independent variable changes sign i.e. f(x) = f(-x)

even number.gloss: An integer that is divisible by two.

evenly.gloss: In a manner that leaves no remainder.

event.gloss: A possible action that the user can perform that is monitored by an application or the operating system (event listener). When an event occurs an event handler is called which performs a specific task.
A set of some of the possible outcomes; a subset of the sample space.

event handler.gloss: A method or subroutine that handles an event.

event loop.gloss: A programming construct that waits for and dispatches events or messages.

event sink.gloss: A class or function that receives events from another object or function.

event-driven.gloss: Of a program: such that the program flow is determined by events.

event-driven architecture.gloss: A software architectural pattern promoting the production, detection, consumption of, and reaction to events.

event-driven programming.gloss: A programming paradigm where the flow of the program is determined by events.

eventing.gloss: The ability of one system or part of a program to send notifications to another, by raising events.

eventology.gloss: The branch of statistics that deals with random, vague events

eventually.gloss: For some tail; for all terms beyond some term; with only finitely many exceptions.

evergreen.gloss: Continually fresh or self-renewing. Of a document, a piece of software, or a data set: kept continually up to date (as opposed to being published at regular intervals and outdated in the meantime)

evict.gloss: To eject from a memory cache to reduce the cache's size.

evidence-gathering.gloss: The collection of potential evidence, which may be present in computer or network logs, on deprecated websites, or the collection of data that is forensically extracted from a computer hard drive.

evil twin.gloss: A rogue wireless access point installed near a legitimate one for purposes of eavesdropping or phishing.

evolute.gloss: A curve comprising the centres of curvature of another curve.

evolution.gloss: An unfolding. The opening out of a curve; now more generally, the gradual transformation of a curve by a change of the conditions generating it.
An unfolding. The extraction of a root from a given power.

evolutionarily stable strategy.gloss: A strategy that, when adopted by a population, is effective and not foreseeably likely to be replaced by another strategy.

eworld.gloss: Cyberspace and its penetration into the nonvirtual world.

exabit.gloss: One quintillion (10¹⁸, or 1,000,000,000,000,000,000) bits or 1,000 petabits.

exabyte.gloss: One quintillion (10¹⁸, or 1,000,000,000,000,000,000) bytes or 1,000 petabytes.

exact cover.gloss: Given a collection S of subsets of a set X, a subcollection S^* of S such that each element of X is contained in exactly one subset in S^*.

exact sequence.gloss: A sequence of modules (or groups, vector spaces, etc.; most generally, objects of an abelian category) with adjacent objects connected by homomorphisms (generally, morphisms) such that the image of one homomorphism is the kernel of the next.

exascale.gloss: Used as a metric to signify 10¹⁸

exbibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2⁶⁰ (1024⁶, 1,152,921,504,606,846,976) bytes or 2¹⁰ (1024) pebibytes, as opposed to an exabyte.

excedance.gloss: A position in a permutation occupied by a value greater than the position number.

exception.gloss: An interruption in normal processing, typically caused by an error condition, that can be raised ("thrown") by one part of the program and handled ("caught") by another part.

exception handler.gloss: A method or subroutine that handles an exception.

exception handling.gloss: The process of responding to an exception.

exceptional.gloss: Corresponding to something of lower dimension under a birational correspondence.

exceptional space.gloss: A space in which a generalization of quantum mechanics is described in terms of a system with a finite number of degrees of freedom

exceptionless.gloss: Without the use of an exception-handling mechanism.

excess.gloss: Spherical excess, the amount by which the sum of the three angles of a spherical triangle exceeds two right angles. The spherical excess is proportional to the area of the triangle.

excess kurtosis.gloss: Kurtosis minus 3; the difference between the kurtosis of a given distribution and the kurtosis of a normal distribution.

excircle.gloss: An escribed circle; a circle outside a polygon (especially a triangle, but also sometimes a quadrilateral) that is tangent to each of the lines on which the sides of the polygon lie.

excision.gloss: The fact that, under certain hypotheses, the homology of a space relative to a subspace is unchanged by the identification of a subspace of the latter to a point.

exclusive disjunction.gloss: A disjunction which is true if only one, but not both, of its disjuncts is true.

exclusive or.gloss: Exclusive disjunction: the use of or to indicate that of two predicates, one is true and one is false (without specifying which is which); contrasted with inclusive or, which does not imply that one must be false.

Exclusive disjunction: the use of or to indicate that of two or more predicates, an odd number are true (without specifying which or how many); contrasted with inclusive or, which indicates only that one or more is true.
An exclusive disjunction; the result of applying the above-described exclusive or to two or more predicates; contrasted with an inclusive or, which is the result of applying an inclusive or.

excosecant.gloss: The trigonometric function csc(x) − 1. Abbreviation: excsc

exe.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of exe (“a Windows executable file”).

executable.gloss: A file that can be run directly by a computer's hardware or a p-code interpreter with no further processing.

executable code.gloss: Instructions for a computer in a form the computer can directly use (i.e. which it can execute). Derived from source code by compiling or assembling and linking.

execution.gloss: The carrying out of an instruction, program or program segment by a computer.

execution time.gloss: The amount of time required for a program or task to complete a single instruction on a computer system.

executive.gloss: A process that coordinates and governs the action of other processes or threads; supervisor.

executor.gloss: A component of a system that executes or runs something.

exeter point.gloss: The point of concurrence of the rays DA’, EB’ and FC’.

exfat.gloss: Initialism of extended file allocation table, a 64-bit derivative of the FAT family of file systems.

exinscribed.gloss: inscribed inside a polygon (and touching every side of it)

existential.gloss: Of or relating to existence. Concerning the very existence of something, especially with regard to evading extinction.
Of or relating to existence. Of an assertion, etc.: assuming or suggesting the existence of something.
Of or relating to existentialism (“a philosophical movement emphasizing the uniqueness of each human existence in freely making its self-defining choices”).
Ellipsis of existential type (“in a type system: a type that hides the underlying concrete type(s)”).

existential instantiation.gloss: In predicate logic, an inference rule of the form ∃x P(x) ⊢ P(c), where c is a new symbol (not part of the original domain of discourse, but which can stand for an element of it (as in Skolemization)).

existential quantifier.gloss: The operator, represented by the symbol ∃, used in predicate calculus to indicate that a predicate is true for at least one member of a specified set. Verbal equivalents include "there exists" and "there is".

existential type.gloss: In a type system: a type that hides the underlying concrete type(s).

exit.gloss: To end or terminate (a program, subroutine, etc.)

exit node.gloss: A server that allows traffic to leave a secure network and enter the public internet.

exit program.gloss: A computer program which exits cleanly from an application, or on computer shutdown

exit time.gloss: The point in time in which a process completes its execution and exits from the system.

exogenous.gloss: Having an external cause. Having no meaning in itself, such as an automatically generated sequential identifier.

exokernel.gloss: A very low-level kernel that avoids abstractions.

exotype.gloss: A type (of object) that is defined programmatically at runtime based on external data.

expand.gloss: To rewrite (an expression) as a longer, yet equivalent, sum of terms.
To become, by rewriting, a longer, yet equivalent, sum of terms.
In a hierarchical list (such as a directory tree or table of contents), to show the subentries of (an entry).

expanded memory.gloss: On x86-compatible PCs, a way to increase available memory beyond the 640 kilobytes usable by DOS, through use of bank switching.

expander.gloss: A control that expands to show more options or commands, keeping them hidden until needed.
A kind of sparse graph with strong connectivity properties.

expando.gloss: A property added to an object at run-time.

expansion.gloss: An act, process, or instance of expanding. Stretching of geometric objects with flat sides.
An act, process, or instance of expanding. The rewriting of an expression as a longer but equivalent sum of terms.

expansion card.gloss: A circuit board that connects to the motherboard of a computer in order to allow additional capabilities.

expansion pack.gloss: A module that adds new content to an existing piece of software.

expansion slot.gloss: A slot for additional hardware, cards, etc. for the purpose of expanding a computer system.

expansivity.gloss: The formal notion of points moving away from one another under the action of an iterated function.

expectation.gloss: The first moment; the expected value; the long-run average value of a variable over many independent repetitions of an experiment.

expected value.gloss: The weighted average of outcome values, using probability as the weighting function.

expensive.gloss: Taking a lot of system time or resources.

experimental probability.gloss: The probability that a certain outcome will occur, as determined through experiment.

expire.gloss: To cause to lapse; to invalidate.

explanator.gloss: A variable that predicts or explains the variation in another variable; an explanatory variable.

explementary.gloss: Of or relating to the explement

explementary angles.gloss: A pair of angles that sum to 360 degrees.

explicandum.gloss: That which is to be explained or explicated

explicit function.gloss: Any function whose value may be directly calculated from the independent variable.

explode.gloss: To break (a delimited string of text) into several smaller strings by removing the separators.
To decompress (data) that was previously imploded.

exploit.gloss: A program or technique that takes advantage of a vulnerability in other software.

explorer.gloss: A visual representation of a file system etc. through which the user can navigate.

explosive.gloss: Having the character of an explosion. Of a specific cellular automaton rule, tending to exhibit infinite and unpredictable growth when starting from finite random patterns.

exponent.gloss: The number by which a value (called the base) is said to be raised to a power in exponentiation: for example, the 3 in 2³=8.
The degree to which the root of a radicand is found, for example, the 2 in √r=b.
The part of a floating-point number that represents its exponent value.

exponential.gloss: Expressed in terms of an exponent (power of a base), the base often being 10 or e.

Characterised by a rate of change that is proportional to the value of the varying quantity, or, equivalently, by a doubling or halving over successive fixed intervals of time or other parameter, described as exponential growth or exponential decay.
Any function that has an exponent as an independent variable.

exponential distribution.gloss: Any of a class of continuous probability distributions used to model the time between events that occur independently at a constant average rate.

exponential equation.gloss: A type of equation which includes a variable located in the exponent; for example, eˣ=1,.

exponential function.gloss: Any function in which an independent variable is in the form of an exponent; they are the inverse functions of logarithms

exponential generating function.gloss: A formal power series with one indeterminate, whose coefficients are fractions with factorial denominators (of index corresponding to the power of the indeterminate) and numerators which represent a sequence of numbers that is to be studied.

exponential growth.gloss: The growth in the value of a quantity in which the rate of growth is proportional to the instantaneous value of the quantity; for example, when the value has doubled, the rate of increase will also have doubled. The rate may be positive or negative.

exponential object.gloss: An object which indexes a family of arrows between two given objects in a universal way, meaning that any other indexed family of arrows between the same given pair of objects must factor uniquely through this universally-indexed family of arrows.

exponential smoothing.gloss: a rule-of-thumb technique for smoothing time series data using the exponential window function.

exponential time.gloss: An algorithm whose running time increases as an exponential function of the size of its input.

exponentiate.gloss: To raise (a number or mathematical expression) to a power; to apply an exponent to a mathematical expression.
To apply a mathematical exponentiation function.

exponentiation.gloss: The process of calculating a power by multiplying together a number of equal factors, where the exponent specifies the number of factors to multiply.

exponentiator.gloss: Any device or circuit that carries out an exponentiation operation.

export.gloss: To send (data) from one program to another.

exportation.gloss: Either the logical law ((P∧Q)→R)⇒(P→(Q→R)), or the rule of replacement ((P∧Q)→R)⇔(P→(Q→R)).

expose.gloss: To make available to other parts of a program, or to other programs.

expression.gloss: An arrangement of symbols denoting values, operations performed on them, and grouping symbols.
A piece of code in a high-level language that returns a value.

expression template.gloss: A template that builds structures representing a computation at compile time, where expressions are evaluated only as needed to produce efficient code.

expressive.gloss: Able to represent a number of ideas or concepts.

exptime.gloss: The set of all decision problems that are solvable by a deterministic Turing machine in exponential time.

expunge.gloss: To delete permanently (e-mail etc.) that was previously marked for deletion but still stored.

exsecant.gloss: The trigonometric function sec(x) − 1. Abbreviation: exsec

extended memory.gloss: The extent of memory above the first megabyte in the address space of later PCs

extended real number system.gloss: The real number system adjoined with two extra symbols: ∞ and −∞, inheriting the ordering of the real number system, and defining −∞ to be less than any real number, and ∞ to be larger than any real number.

extended static checking.gloss: A range of techniques used for statically checking the correctness of some program constraints.

extensibility.gloss: The capability of being extended. A quality of design that takes possible future advances into consideration and attempts to accommodate them.

extension.gloss: A short exact sequence 1→H→E→G→1, or the group E therein.
qualifiers: of a group G by a group H

extension.gloss: A short exact sequence 0→B→E→A→0, or the object E therein.
qualifiers: of an object A by an object B in an abelian category

extension.gloss: An optional software component that adds functionality to an application.
The set of tuples of values that, used as arguments, satisfy the predicate.

extension field.gloss: A field L which contains a subfield K, called the base field, from which it is generated by adjoining extra elements.

extensionality.gloss: The principle, codified in the axiom of extensionality, that sets are equal if and only if they contain the same elements.

extensive form game.gloss: Informally, a representation of a game as a tree of decision nodes, with the game beginning at a unique initial node, and flowing through the tree along a path determined by the players until a terminal node is reached, where play ends and payoffs are assigned to all players; each non-terminal node belongs to a player; that player chooses among the possible moves at that node, each possible move is an edge leading from that node to another node.

extent.gloss: A contiguous area of storage in a file system.

exterior angle.gloss: An angle formed between one side of a polygon and an extension of an adjacent side.

exterior derivative.gloss: A differential operator which acts on a differential k-form to yield a differential (k+1)-form, unless the k-form is a pseudoscalar, in which case it yields 0.

exterior product.gloss: A kind of product between vectors and/or multivectors which is associative, linear, and alternating.

extern.gloss: In the C and C++ programming languages, a variable that can be separately declared in many places, all of them referring to the same variable.

external.gloss: Not contained in the main computer.
Using a disk or tape drive rather than the main memory.
A variable that is defined in the source code but whose value comes from some external source.

external coupling.gloss: A coupling where two modules share an externally imposed communication protocol, data format, or device interface.

extrabinomial.gloss: Relating to unexpected variability arising from overdispersion.

extractor.gloss: A particular kind of bipartite graph.

A function which, being applied to output from a weakly random entropy source, together with a short, uniformly random seed, generates a highly random output that appears independent from the source and uniformly distributed.

extragradient.gloss: Obtaining strong convergence without strong monotonicity by projecting twice on the underlying set of constraints.

extraneous variable.gloss: A random variable that is not an independent variable and may bear any effect on the behaviour of the subject being studied.

extranet.gloss: A private computer network that uses Internet protocols and can be accessed by authorized individuals via the Internet.

extrapolate.gloss: To estimate the value of a variable outside a known range from values within that range by assuming that the estimated value follows logically from the known ones

extrapolation.gloss: A calculation of an estimate of the value of some function outside the range of known values.

extraregular.gloss: Meeting stricter criteria than those which define a regular (object, function, space, etc)

extraspecial.gloss: Being an analogue of the Heisenberg group over a finite field whose size is a prime.

extremal.gloss: Any solution to a variety of equations in the calculus of variations.

extreme.gloss: Either of the two numbers at the ends of a proportion, as 1 and 6 in 1:2=3:6.

extreme point.gloss: A point in a convex set which does not lie in any open line segment joining two points in the set.
The maximum or minimum of a function.
A leaf vertex of a tree data structure.

extreme programmer.gloss: A computer programmer who uses extreme programming techniques.

extreme programming.gloss: A software engineering methodology that promotes agility and simplicity, typically involving pair programming and a cycle of frequent testing and feedback.

extremizer.gloss: A function that returns an extremum.

extremum.gloss: A point, or value that is a maximum or a minimum.

f distribution.gloss: A probability distribution of the ratio of two variables, each with a chi-square distribution; used in analysis of variance, especially in the significance testing of a correlation coefficient (R squared).

f lock.gloss: A lock key that toggles the behaviour of the function keys between their traditional (application-defined) behaviours and a set of new commands.

f-algebra.gloss: A kind of generalization of the notion of algebraic structure.

faas.gloss: Acronym of function as a service.

fabric.gloss: Interconnected nodes that look like a textile fabric when diagrammed.

facade.gloss: An object serving as a simplified interface to a larger body of code, as in the facade pattern.

facade pattern.gloss: A structural design pattern that provides an object that is a simplified interface to a larger body of code, such as a class library.

face.gloss: Any of the flat bounding surfaces of a polyhedron; more generally, any of the bounding pieces of a polytope of any dimension.

facemail.gloss: Face-to-face communication, as opposed to other non-personal forms of communication.

facepile.gloss: A stack of images (photographs, initials, etc.) each representing a person.

facet.gloss: A face of codimension 1 of a polytope.
A criterion that can be used to sort and filter, such as the colour or size of products in an online store.

facet name.gloss: A technical name that identifies a facet in code, such as in a shortcode.

facient.gloss: One of the variables of a quantic as distinguished from a coefficient.

fact.gloss: An individual value or measurement at the lowest level of granularity in a data warehouse.

fact table.gloss: A database table consisting of the measurements, metrics or facts of a business process.

factor.gloss: Any of various objects multiplied together to form some whole.

factor analysis.gloss: A statistical method used to describe variability among observed correlated variables in terms of one or more unobserved variables (called factors).
A statistical study performed using the method.

factor graph.gloss: A bipartite graph representing the factorization of a function.

factor ideal.gloss: For given ring R, any ideal I such that Q = R / I, the set of cosets of elements of I in R, is a ring (the quotient ring of I in R).

factor out.gloss: To isolate a common factor from an expression.

factor space.gloss: A space obtained from another by identification of points that are equivalent to one another in some equivalence relation.
A space which is a factor (multiplicand) in a product space.

factor through.gloss: Said of a morphism: to be equal to a composition of two morphisms, one of which is the given morphism (that is being said to be "factored through").

factorable.gloss: Capable of being factored. For integers synonyms are composite, non-prime.

factoradic.gloss: Relating to or involving the factorial number system (a mixed radix numeral system adapted to numbering permutations).

factored.gloss: Expressed in terms of factors (values that are multiplied together to form a whole)
Having been subjected to, or resulting from a factor analysis.

factorial.gloss: The result of multiplying a given number of consecutive integers from 1 to the given number. In equations, it is symbolized by an exclamation mark (!). For example, 5! = 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 = 120.
Of or pertaining to a factor or factorial.

factorial prime.gloss: A prime number that is one more or one less than a factorial. For example, 7 is a factorial prime, since 3! + 1 = 7.

factorial table.gloss: A tabular presentation of data used to show the influence of two independent categorical variables on a dependent variable.
An arrangement of data showing the effect of more than two categorical variables on a dependent variables.

factorialize.gloss: To perform factor analysis on (a set of data).

factorially.gloss: According to a factorial series or ratio.

factoring.gloss: The process of rewriting an expression as the product of its factor.

factorion.gloss: A number that is equal to the sum of the factorials of its digits.

qualifiers: of an integer or polynomial etc

factorization.gloss: The process of creating a list of factors.
An expression listing items that, when multiplied together, will produce a desired quantity.

factorize.gloss: To create a list of the factors of.
To divide an expression into a list of items that, when multiplied together, will produce the original quantity.

factory.gloss: In a computer program or library, a function, method, etc. which creates an object.

factory class.gloss: A class that creates an object having a non-trivial creation process, implementing the factory method pattern.

factory method pattern.gloss: A creational design pattern that decouples the object creation by using an abstract method in the class.

factory reset.gloss: A process that restores an electronic device to its factory setting by erasing all user data and personalized configurations.
To perform a factory reset of (a device).

factory setting.gloss: The default configuration of a device when it is first manufactured and sold.

factum.gloss: A product (result of multiplying two numbers).

facultative.gloss: At which a given function is positive.

fade time.gloss: The time during which a wireless signal is too faint to be accurately received.

fader.gloss: A program or algorithm for fading out colors.

fagan inspection.gloss: A structured process of trying to find defects in source code, specifications, and other design documents.

fail fast.gloss: To report immediately any condition likely to cause a failure, rather than attempting to continue.

fail over.gloss: To automatically switch processing from a failed component in a critical system to its live spare or backup component.

fail-soft.gloss: Able to proceed even after an error condition by selectively skipping parts of the processing.

failback.gloss: The restoration of a system in a state of failover back to its original state (before the failure occurred).

failover.gloss: An automatic switch to a secondary system on failure of the primary system, such as a means for ensuring high availability of some critical resource (such as a computer system), involving a parallel backup system which is kept running at all times, so that, upon detected failure of the primary system, processing can be automatically shifted over to the backup.

failsoft.gloss: Supporting graceful degradation, so that a partial failure does not bring down the entire system.

fair.gloss: Of a coin or die, having equal chance of landing on any side, unbiased.

fair cake-cutting.gloss: A kind of fair division problem in which there is a divisible heterogeneous resource that must be divided among several partners in a subjectively fair way.

fair coin.gloss: A sequence of independent Bernoulli trials (a Bernoulli process) with probability 1/2 of success on each trial.

fair division.gloss: the problem of dividing a set of resources among several people who have an entitlement to them, such that each person receives their due share

faithful.gloss: Injective in specific contexts, e.g. of representations in representation or functors in category theory.

faithful functor.gloss: A functor which maps morphisms from its source to its target category in such a way that the restriction of that mapping to any source hom-set is injective into the corresponding target hom-set.

fall over.gloss: Of a computer program or system, to crash.

fall-through.gloss: In certain programming constructs, the situation where execution passes to the next condition in a list unless explicitly redirected.

fallacy.gloss: An argument, or apparent argument, which professes to be decisive of the matter at issue, while in reality it is not; a specious argument.

fallacy fallacy.gloss: The formal fallacy of inferring that if an argument contains a fallacy, its conclusion must be false.

false.gloss: Of a state in Boolean logic that indicates a negative result.

false analogy.gloss: An informal fallacy applying to inductive arguments, in which the similarity in one respect of two concepts, objects, or events is taken as sufficient to establish that they are similar in another respect in which they actually are dissimilar.

false cause.gloss: The fallacy of stating as a cause what is not actually the cause; the fallacy of non causa pro causa.

false negative.gloss: A type II error (“accepting the null hypothesis when it is false”).

false sharing.gloss: A performance-degrading usage pattern where the size of units in a cache means that the system may reload entire units even when it is not necessary.

falsiness.gloss: The property of being falsy, i.e. evaluating to false in a Boolean context.

falsy.gloss: Evaluating to false in a Boolean context.

family.gloss: Any group or aggregation of things classed together as kindred or related from possessing in common characteristics which distinguish them from other things of the same order. A collection of sets, especially of subsets of a given set.

family tree.gloss: A data structure that organizes resources or machines in a distributed system, consisting of nodes connected by edges, in which each node may also contain a subnode.

familywise.gloss: In terms of a family of related inferences.

fan.gloss: A section of a tree having a finite number of branches.

fang.gloss: Either of the two factors that make a number a vampire number.

fanin.gloss: The degree to which a component has separate inputs entering it.

fano plane.gloss: The finite projective plane of order 2, having the smallest possible number of points and lines, 7 each, with 3 points on every line and 3 lines through every point.

fanout.gloss: The degree to which something fans out, or splits into separate sections.

far.gloss: Outside the currently selected segment in a segmented memory architecture.

farey sequence.gloss: For a given positive integer n, the sequence of completely reduced fractions between 0 and 1 which, when in lowest terms, have denominators less than or equal to n, arranged in order of increasing size.

farkled.gloss: Not working correctly; ruined; broken; hosed.

fast.gloss: Able to transfer data in a short period of time.

fat.gloss: Acronym of file allocation table. Any of a series of file systems that use one or more FATs. FAT16 or FAT16B.
Acronym of file allocation table. Any of a series of file systems that use one or more FATs. FAT12.
Acronym of file allocation table. Any of a series of file systems that use one or more FATs. FAT12 or FAT16, without drawing a distinction between the two.

fat arrow.gloss: The => symbol, which has specific meanings in various programming languages.

fat client.gloss: A complex client that does not rely on the server to carry out most of its processing.

fat comma.gloss: The operator =>, used in declaring hashes.

fat tail.gloss: A tail of a probability distribution with significantly higher kurtosis than a normal distribution (which has kurtosis = 0).
A tail of a probability distribution with infinite variance.

fat12.gloss: The version of the FAT series of file systems which uses a 12-bit file allocation table.

fat16.gloss: The version of the FAT series of file systems which uses a 16-bit file allocation table. The original version of this file system, storing both the number of (real or virtual) disk sectors and the number of sector clusters in a volume as 16-bit integers.

The version of the FAT series of file systems which uses a 16-bit file allocation table. FAT16B, the version of this file system storing the number of clusters in a volume as a 16-bit integer but using a 32-bit integer to represent the total number of sectors in a volume, allowing for larger volume and file sizes.

fat32.gloss: The version of the FAT series of file systems which uses a 32-bit file allocation table.

fat64.gloss: A version of the FAT series of file systems which uses a 64-bit file allocation table. exFAT.

A version of the FAT series of file systems which uses a 64-bit file allocation table. A hypothetical FAT filesystem using a 64-bit file allocation table, but without the additional data structures found in exFAT.

fatal.gloss: Causing a sudden end to the running of a program.
A fatal error; a failure that causes a program to terminate.

father.gloss: The archived older version of a file that immediately precedes the current version, and was itself derived from the grandfather.

fatou component.gloss: A component of the Fatou set.

fatou set.gloss: A set that is complementary to the Julia set, and that informally consists of values with the property that all nearby values behave similarly under repeated iteration of the function.

fatx.gloss: Abbreviation of Xbox file allocation table: the version of the FAT file system used on Xbox consoles and compatible storage peripherals.

fault.gloss: A mistake or error. An exception within a software program or process.

fault injection.gloss: A technique for testing a computer system by subjecting it to unusual stresses, such as high voltage or temperature, or the deliberate mutation of software code.

fault-tolerant.gloss: Tolerating a fault or faults such that no cessation to operation occurs.

favicon.gloss: An icon associated with a particular website, and typically displayed in the address bar of a browser viewing the site.

feather.gloss: To intergrade or blend the pixels of an image with those of a background or neighboring image.

feature.gloss: An important or main item. A beneficial capability of a piece of software.
An individual measurable property or characteristic of a phenomenon being observed; the input of a model.

feature envy.gloss: The situation where one class in a program makes excessive use of parts of other classes.

federated.gloss: Interconnected, as a federation or supernetwork of independent and interoperable services.

federation.gloss: A collection of network or telecommunication providers that offer interoperability.

federator.gloss: A component that integrates access to various services.

feechur.gloss: An undesirable or misimplemented feature (software or hardware capability).

feed drive.gloss: A drive mechanism for CD-ROMs etc in which no tray is used; the medium is inserted in a slot and is pulled in

feedreader.gloss: A software program that gathers content from newsfeeds.

feigenbaum constant.gloss: Either of two mathematical constants that express ratios in a bifurcation diagram for a nonlinear map.

feistel cipher.gloss: A symmetric structure used in the construction of block ciphers. It is an iterated cipher with an internal function called a round function.

fencepost error.gloss: An off-by-one error arising from the fencepost problem.

fencepost problem.gloss: A problem dealing with how to treat the initial or boundary values of a discrete problem.

fenwick tree.gloss: A data structure that maintains prefix sums over a list of numbers while allowing dynamic updates and queries in logarithmic time.

fermat curve.gloss: The algebraic curve in the complex projective plane defined in homogeneous coordinates (X:Y:Z) by the Fermat equation.

fermat number.gloss: An integer which is one more than two raised to a power which is itself a power of two (i.e., is expressible in the form 2^(2ⁿ)+1 for some n>0); equivalently, a number that is one more than two raised to some power (is expressible as 2ⁿ+1) and is prime.

fermat point.gloss: A point such that the sum of the three distances from each of the three vertices of a given triangle to that point is the smallest possible; equivalently, the geometric median of the three vertices.

fermat prime.gloss: A Fermat number that is prime.

fermat pseudoprime.gloss: With respect to an integer base b, with b > 1, a composite integer n such that bⁿ⁻¹ is congruent to one modulo n.

fermi-dirac distribution function.gloss: A function that states the probability of one of a set of independent fermions will occupy a given energy level when thermal equilibrium exists.

ferrers diagram.gloss: A diagram that shows the possible partitions of a positive integer as rows of dots.

ferrite core.gloss: A magnetic core made of ferrite.

fetch.gloss: An act of fetching, of bringing something from a distance. An act of fetching data.

feuerbach point.gloss: A kind of triangle center, defined as the point at which the incircle and nine-point circle of the triangle are internally tangent to each other.

fiber.gloss: The preimage of a given point in the range of a map.
The pullback of a morphism along a global element (called the fiber of the morphism over the global element).
A kind of lightweight thread of execution.

fiber bundle.gloss: An abstract object in topology where copies of one object are "attached" to every point of another, as hairs or fibers are attached to a hairbrush. Formally, a topological space E (called the total space), together with a topological space B (called the base space), a topological space F (called the fiber), and surjective map π from E to B (called the projection or submersion), such that every point of B has a neighborhood U with π⁻¹(U) homeomorphic to the product space U × F (that is, E looks locally the same as the product space B × F, although its global structure may be quite different).

fiberwise.gloss: Of or pertaining to the fiber of a map.
With regard to the fiber of a map.

fibonacci.gloss: Of or pertaining to the Fibonacci sequence.

fibonacci number.gloss: Any number in a Fibonacci sequence (being the sum of the preceding two numbers).

fibonacci polynomial.gloss: Any member of a polynomial sequence which can be considered as a generalization of the Fibonacci numbers.

fibonacci sequence.gloss: The sequence of integers, each of which is the sum of the preceding two, the first and second numbers both being 1.
Any sequence of numbers such that each is the sum of the preceding two.

fibonacci spiral.gloss: An approximation of the golden spiral created by drawing circular arcs connecting the opposite corners of squares in a Fibonacci tiling; a spiral formed by connecting quarter-circles whose radii are Fibonacci number multiples of the initial radius.

fiboquadratic.gloss: Describing an extension of Fibonacci sequences involving quadratic numbers

fibral.gloss: Having the form of a fiber or fibril

fibration.gloss: A continuous mapping satisfying the homotopy lifting property with respect to any space.

fibrational.gloss: Of or pertaining to a fibration.

fibre.gloss: The preimage of a given point in the range of a map.
Said to be of a morphism over a global element: The pullback of the said morphism along the said global element.
A kind of lightweight thread of execution.

fiducially.gloss: Pertaining to or based on the correspondence between a parameter in a sample and the same parameter in the population from which the sample was drawn.

field.gloss: Any of various figurative meanings, often dead metaphors. Any of certain structures serving cognition. A non-zero commutative ring in which all non-zero elements are invertible; a simple commutative ring.

Any of various figurative meanings, often dead metaphors. A physical or virtual location for the input of information in the form of symbols. An area of memory or storage reserved for a particular value, subject to virtual access controls.

field axiom.gloss: Any of the several axioms that an object should meet to be considered a mathematical field.

field axioms.gloss: the requirements for an object to be considered a field

field extension.gloss: Any pair of fields, denoted L/K, such that K is a subfield of L.

field of fractions.gloss: The smallest field in which a given ring can be embedded.

field of quotients.gloss: A field all of whose elements can be represented as ordered pairs each of whose components belong to a given integral domain, such that the second component is non-zero, and so that the additive operator is defined like so: (a,b)+(a',b')=(ab'+a'b,bb'), the multiplicative operator is defined coordinate-wise, the zero is (0,1), the unity is (1,1), the additive inverse of (a,b) is (-a,b), equivalence is defined like so: (a,b)≡(a',b') if and only if ab'=a'b, and multiplicative inverse of a non-zero–equivalent element (a,b) is (b,a).

fieldbus.gloss: A member of a family of industrial digital communication networks used for real-time distributed control.

fifo.gloss: Acronym of first in first out.

fifteener.gloss: A book or other printed item that was printed in the 15th century (thus, during the first half-century of printing).

fifth normal form.gloss: A stage in the normalization of a relational database in which a database is in fourth normal form and every join dependency is implied by the candidate keys.

figural.gloss: Of numbers, describing a geometrical figure.

figurate number.gloss: A number equal to the number of dots in a geometric figure formed of dots. The series begins with unity and is formed so that subtracting each from the following, and treating the series so formed in the same way, by a continuation of the process, yields equal differences.

figure.gloss: The form of a syllogism with respect to the relative position of the middle term.

file.gloss: An aggregation of data on a storage device, identified by a name.

file allocation table.gloss: A table used internally by the operating system to keep track of the structure of a disk and where files are stored on it.

file association.gloss: The association of a file type with a program, so that the chosen program is the default for opening files of that type.

file carving.gloss: The process of reassembling computer files from fragments in the absence of file system metadata, based on the extrapolation of a file's probable type from its contents.

file descriptor.gloss: A process-unique identifier for a file or other input/output resource, such as a pipe or network socket.

file format.gloss: A standard structure according to which data is encoded in a file.

file handle.gloss: The descriptor used to access a file in a file system.

file manager.gloss: A computer program that provides a user interface to manage files and folders.

file section.gloss: The part of the data division of a COBOL program that describes the format of the logical records associated with external files to be accessed by the progrem

file sharing.gloss: The process of making files available to others to download from the Internet.
The use of a file sharing network, or peer-to-peer software.

file shredder.gloss: A software program designed to overwrite the contents of a data file (or other space on a disk) to prevent recovery of the file contents.

file size.gloss: The length of a file, often specified in bytes.

file system.gloss: A method of organizing blocks of data on a storage device into files and directories.
A set of blocks that are organized in this way.

filegroup.gloss: A collection of files that, in some database systems, are managed together as a group.

filemark.gloss: A special value used on computer tape to separate individual files.

filemask.gloss: A text pattern that matches certain filenames.

filename.gloss: The name assigned to a file in a file system.

filepath.gloss: The location of a file in a directory structure. Also known as the path of a file. A path can be absolute or relative.

filer.gloss: A software program for managing files.

fileserver.gloss: A server used to share files with other computers.

filespace.gloss: The space where files are stored.

filespec.gloss: A file identifier consisting of path and filename.

filestore.gloss: A conceptual space where files are stored.

filestream.gloss: A data stream providing access to the contents of a file.

filetype.gloss: An identifier indicating the type of information contained in an electronic format.

filf.gloss: Initialism of fuzzy integrated logical forecasting.

fill-in.gloss: An intermediate result that must be stored temporarily during the course of a sparse matrix computation.

filler.gloss: In COBOL, the description of an unnamed part of a record that contains no data relevant to a given context (normally capitalised when in a data division).

fillet.gloss: A rounded relief or cut at an edge, especially an inside edge, added for a finished appearance and to break sharp edges.

fillrate.gloss: A measurement of the number of pixels a video card can render in a certain time period.

filmstrip.gloss: A file containing a sequence of images or video frames.

filter.gloss: A non-empty upper set (of a partially ordered set) which is closed under binary infima (a.k.a. meets).

filter bank.gloss: An array of band-pass filters that separates the input signal into multiple components, each one carrying a single frequency subband of the original signal.

filtered-popping recursive transition ne.gloss: An extension of recursive transition networks.

filterware.gloss: Software that filters out objectionable material.

filtration.gloss: A totally ordered collection of subsets.

fin gripper.gloss: A gripper designed to act similarly to how a fish fin wraps around an object that pushes into it

final topology.gloss: Given a set X, a family of topological spaces (M#95;i,T#95;i)#95;#123;i#92;inI#125; and a family of functions f#95;i#58;M#95;i#92;toX, the final topology is the finest topology on X such that all f#95;i are continuous.

finalize.gloss: To prepare (an object) for garbage collection by calling its finalizer.

finalizer.gloss: A function that runs when an object is garbage collected, similar to a destructor.

findability.gloss: The quality of a particular object being locatable.
The quality of a whole system being navigable.

finger.gloss: Something similarly extending, (especially) from a larger body A leaf in a finger tree data structure.

finger tree.gloss: A purely functional tree-like data structure offering amortized constant time access to its "fingers" (leaves), used for the efficient implementation of other purely functional data structures.

finger-friendly.gloss: Designed to work well with touch-screen input, as well as or instead of mouse, trackball, etc.

fingerprint.gloss: A unique identification for a public key in asymmetric cryptography.

finitary.gloss: Of a function, taking a finite number of arguments to produce an output.
Pertaining to finite-length proofs, each using a finite set of axioms.

finite continued fraction.gloss: A continued fraction which terminates after a certain number of steps.

finite element.gloss: Any of a finite number of discrete elements of a system, interconnected at discrete nodes, used to model a physical system

finite geometry.gloss: Any geometric system that has only a finite number of points.
The branch of geometry that concerns geometric systems with only a finite number of points.

finite set.gloss: A set with only finitely many members. This includes the empty set.

finite-dimensional.gloss: (of a vector space) having a basis consisting of a finite number of elements.

finite-state machine.gloss: A formalism for describing computation, consisting of a finite set of states and a transition function describing when to move from one state to another.

finitely generated.gloss: In any of several specific senses, such that all its elements can be created using (or described by reference to) a finite set of elements, usually called generators: Such that the functor operatorname Hom_( mathcal )C(X,·) preserves those filtered colimits of monomorphisms.
qualifiers: of an object X in a locally small category 𝒞 that admits filtered colimits of monomorphism

finitely generated.gloss: In any of several specific senses, such that all its elements can be created using (or described by reference to) a finite set of elements, usually called generators: Being a quotient object of a free object over a finite set, i.e. being the target of a regular epimorphism from an object which is free on a finite set.
qualifiers: of an object X in a concrete category

finitely generated.gloss: In any of several specific senses, such that all its elements can be created using (or described by reference to) a finite set of elements, usually called generators: Having a finite set of generators, i.e. having a finite set of elements from which all other elements can be created in finitely many steps under the permitted operations (viz. the group operation for groups, addition and scalar multiplication for modules, addition and multiplication for rings, etc.)

In any of several specific senses, such that all its elements can be created using (or described by reference to) a finite set of elements, usually called generators: Finitely generated as a (left) module over R.
qualifiers: of a (left) ideal in a ring R

finitely generated.gloss: In any of several specific senses, such that all its elements can be created using (or described by reference to) a finite set of elements, usually called generators: Equipped with an Alexandrov topology (i.e. one where the intersection of every family of open sets is open).

finitely presented.gloss: Isomorphic to the kernel of a morphism of free modules; such that there exists an exact sequence Rᵐ→Rⁿ→M→0 for some integers m,n.
qualifiers: of a module M over a ring R

finitism.gloss: An extreme form of constructivism, according to which a mathematical object does not exist unless it can be constructed from natural numbers in a finite number of steps.

fioa.gloss: Initialism of fetch instruction operand address.

fir.gloss: Initialism of finite impulse response; that has impulse response (or response to any finite length input) of finite duration.

fire.gloss: To initiate an event (by means of an event handler).

fire and forget.gloss: The practice of transmitting or raising something, such as an event, and then proceeding without checking for any result or response.

fire hose.gloss: A feed of all updates to a website.

firebrick.gloss: The X11 color name of RGB hexadecimal value #B22222.

firehose cursor.gloss: A cursor that permits fast enumeration of rows but can only move forward.

firm error.gloss: A type of error where a signal or datum becomes wrong and remains wrong until the equipment is power-cycled, but does not physically damage the equipment's hardware.

firm link.gloss: A kind of link within a file system having aspects of both hard links and soft links.

firmware.gloss: A permanent form of software that provides a low-level control of computing device hardware.
Software that is intended for such embedded computer applications.

first class.gloss: Of or relating to a treatment like that for a first-class object.

first exit time.gloss: From A, the first hit time for S \ A, the complement of A in S.

first in first out.gloss: A type of queue data structure in which the oldest added items are retrieved first.

first normal form.gloss: A stage in the normalization of a relational database in which repeating groups and attributes have been eliminated by putting each into a separate table connected by a primary-key/foreign-key relationship.

first return time.gloss: The first hit time for the singleton set {X₀(ω)}, which is usually a given deterministic element of the state space, such as the origin of the coordinate system.

first-chance exception.gloss: An exception (error condition) when handled by a debugger, such that the programmer has the first chance to study it; such an exception would otherwise proceed to a handler or (in its absence) crash the program.

first-class continuation.gloss: A continuation that can be used like any other value in a programming language, granting it a powerful ability to control the flow of execution.

first-class object.gloss: An entity that can be constructed at run-time, passed as a parameter, returned from a function, or assigned into a variable.

An entity that can pass a value as a parameter, can be returned from a subroutine, and can be assigned into a variable. (This is the definition according to Raphael Finkel, who uses the terms of second- and third-class objects.)

first-fit.gloss: Of or relating to a fast but non-optimal algorithm for the Bin packing problem, placing each item into the first bin in which it will fit.

first-order.gloss: Of one of a series of models, languages, relationship, forms of logical discourse, etc., being the simplest one or the first in a sequence.

first-order logic.gloss: A formal deductive system extended from propositional logic with the possibility to quantify over individuals of the domain of discourse.

first-party.gloss: Of products, created or published by the company responsible for the platform on which it is released (or its internal developers), as opposed to third-party.

first-party cookie.gloss: A small text file that a website creates and stores on a user's browser.

first-passage time.gloss: The time taken for a random walker to reach a specified target.

fisher information.gloss: A measure of the amount of information that an observable random variable X carries about an unknown parameter θ of a distribution that models X. Formally, it is the variance of the score, or the expected value of the observed information.

fisher-yates shuffle.gloss: A particular algorithm for generating an unbiased random permutation of a set. It selects elements randomly from the initial set until none remain.

fit and finish.gloss: Those features that are not essential functionality of the software, but are otherwise important or useful, such as localization or improving the user interface.

fitness model.gloss: A mathematical model for evaluating the development of a system.

fitting subgroup.gloss: For a finite group G: the unique largest normal nilpotent subgroup of G, which intuitively represents the smallest subgroup that "controls" the structure of G when G is solvable.

five lemma.gloss: A particular lemma that claims the existence of a particular isomorphism in a commutative diagram given certain other homomorphisms in the diagram.

five-dimensional.gloss: Of a space, represented by five coordinates.

fix.gloss: To map (a point or subset) to itself.

fixed field.gloss: A subfield of a given field which contains all of the fixed points that are common to all of the automorphisms of some subgroup of the automorphism group of that given field.

fixed point.gloss: A fractional-number representation with a fixed number of digits after the decimal point. Compare floating point and integer.
A value which is unchanged by a function or other mapping. Formally: a value x for which f(x)=x.
Pertaining to fixed point representations or operations.

fixed set.gloss: A set which is unchanged by a function or other mapping. Formally: a set, S, is a fixed set of a function, f, if and only if for all x in S, f(x)=x.

fixed-point.gloss: Being or using an internal number representation with a fixed number of decimal places (as opposed to floating-point).

fixed-point number.gloss: A representation of fractional numbers by storing a fixed number of digits of their fractional part.

fixity.gloss: The position of an operator relative to its operand (prefix, postfix) or operands (infix).

fixme.gloss: A comment explaining that a section of code requires fixing in some way.

fixture.gloss: A state that can be recreated, used as a baseline for running software tests.

flabby.gloss: Which forms a surjection from the domain to every open subset of the codomain.

flag.gloss: A variable or memory location that stores a Boolean true-or-false, yes-or-no value, typically either recording the fact that a certain event has occurred or requesting that a certain optional action take place.
In a command line interface, a command parameter requesting optional behavior or otherwise modifying the action of the command being invoked.

A sequence of faces of a given polytope, one of each dimension up to that of the polytope (formally, though in practice not always explicitly, including the null face and the polytope itself), such that each face in the sequence is part of the next-higher dimension face.

A sequence of subspaces of a vector space, beginning with the null space and ending with the vector space itself, such that each member of the sequence (until the last) is a proper subspace of the next.
To set a program variable to true.

flag complex.gloss: A simplicial complex where every collection of pairwise adjacent vertices spans a simplex.

flag day.gloss: A day designated for changing to an incompatible system.
A change which is neither forward nor backward compatible.

flamegraph.gloss: A visual representation of hierarchical data used to analyze system and application performance metrics.

flamer.gloss: One who flames, or posts vitriolic criticism.

flap.gloss: A connected component of the induced subgraph formed by deleting a set of vertices.
To be advertised as being available and then unavailable (or available by different routes) in rapid succession.
qualifiers: of a resource or network destination

flapping.gloss: The situation where a resource, a network destination, etc., is advertised as being available and then unavailable (or available by different routes) in rapid succession.

flash.gloss: To write to the memory of (an updatable component such as a BIOS chip or games cartridge).

flash drive.gloss: A small, portable, nonvolatile storage device that uses flash memory and a USB interface to store, transport, and retrieve digital data.

flash memory.gloss: A rewritable memory chip that retains its data without a power supply.

flashable.gloss: Capable of being flashed (having its memory rewritten).

flashback.gloss: A query that operates against data from an earlier time, before it was changed.

flasher.gloss: A software developer who uses the Flash multimedia technology.

flat.gloss: Such that its target, regarded as a module over its source, is flat (as above).
Such that the induced map on every stalk is flat (as a map of rings).
A subset of n-dimensional space that is congruent to a Euclidean space of lower dimension.

flat design.gloss: A user interface style that that is characterized by the lack of shadows, giving a flat, two-dimensional look

flat file.gloss: A data file containing usually one record per line.

flat space.gloss: Any Riemann space in which the metric tensors are constants throughout

flatbed.gloss: A document scanner with a flat bed.

flatten.gloss: To reduce (a data structure) to one that has fewer dimensions, e.g. a 2×2 array into a list of four elements.
To combine (separate layers) into a single image.

flecnode.gloss: A double point that is also a point of inflexion of one branch.

fleeceware.gloss: Malware whose functionality works as advertised but that manipulates users into subscribing instead of using free or much cheaper alternatives (i.e. “fleeces” them out of their money).

fleflecnode.gloss: A double point that is also a point of inflexion of both branches.

fleiss' kappa.gloss: A statistical measure for assessing the reliability of agreement between a fixed number of raters.

fleissner grille.gloss: A kind of cryptographic grille that can be rotated for greater complexity.

fletcher's checksum.gloss: A kind of position-dependent checksum intended to provide error-detection properties approaching those of a cyclic redundancy check but with less computation.

flexagon.gloss: A flat model made from folded strips of paper that can be folded, or flexed, to reveal a number of hidden faces.

flic.gloss: A data file containing computer animations.

flicker fixer.gloss: A piece of computer hardware that deinterlaces an output video signal, resulting in a less flickery display on some systems.

flip.gloss: To invert a bit (binary digit), changing it from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0.

flip-flop.gloss: A bistable; an electronic switching circuit that has either two stable states (switching between them in response to a trigger) or a stable and an unstable state (switching from one to the other and back again in response to a trigger), and which is thereby capable of serving as one bit of memory.

flip-flop operator.gloss: An operator specifying a range of conditions, such that the related code executes only if the first condition is true, and only until the second condition becomes true.

flippy disk.gloss: An 8-inch or 5.25-inch floppy diskette that has been modified to be double-sided, allowing data storage on both sides of the disk.

flippy-floppy.gloss: A two-sided floppy disk; a flippy disk.

flit.gloss: A flow control unit or flow control digit.

float.gloss: To cause (an element within a document) to float above or beside others.
A floating-point number, especially one that has lower precision than a double.
A visual style on a web page that causes the styled elements to float above or beside others.

floating point.gloss: Of a number, written in two parts as a mantissa (also called significand, the value of the significant digits) and characteristic (order of magnitude / the power of a number base) e.g. 0.314159 × 10¹.
Of the internal representation of such a number as a pair of integers.

floating point operation.gloss: Any simple operation, such as addition, multiplication or division, performed on floating point numbers using a single operation.

floating-point number.gloss: A real number held as a pair of integers, one representing the mantissa and the other representing the exponent. The base is normally 10, 16 or 256 depending on the computing system.

floating-point unit.gloss: A microprocessor that performs floating-point arithmetic. In older models of computer the FPU was not integrated into the central processing unit, but rather as a coprocessor if included at all.

floer homology.gloss: A tool for studying symplectic geometry and low-dimensional topology. It is a novel invariant that arises as an infinite-dimensional analog of finite-dimensional Morse homology.

flood fill.gloss: A means of filling a discrete area with colour, based on colouring every pixel that can be recursively reached from a starting point.
To fill (an area) in this manner.

floor.gloss: The largest integer less than or equal to a given number.

floor effect.gloss: The phenomenon in which a data-gathering instrument has a lower limit to the data values it can reliably specify.

floor function.gloss: A function that maps a real number to the largest integer that is not greater than it.

flop.gloss: One floating-point operation per second, a unit of measure of processor speed.

floppy disk.gloss: A removable disk used for storing digital data, measuring between 2 and 8 inches diagonally and storing between 80 KB and 240 MB.

floppy disk drive.gloss: A floppy drive; a disk drive for floppy disks.

floppyful.gloss: The amount (of data) that a floppy disk can hold.

floptical.gloss: Using a combination of magnetic and optical technology.

floptical disk.gloss: A form of floppy disk whose head tracking was optically controlled (superseded by compact disc technology).

flotilla.gloss: A spaceship made of one or more central mutually stabilizing overweight spaceships flanked by lightweight, middleweight, or heavyweight spaceships that prevent the formation of destructive eggs.

flow.gloss: A formalization of the idea of the motion of particles in a fluid, as a group action of the real numbers on a set.
The sequence of steps taken in a piece of software to perform some action.
To arrange (text in a wordprocessor, etc.) so that it wraps neatly into a designated space; to reflow.

flow control.gloss: The management of the data transmission rate between two nodes to prevent a fast sender from outrunning a slow receiver.

flow network.gloss: A directed graph where each edge has a capacity and each edge receives a flow.

flowcharting.gloss: The design and construction of flowcharts.

flower box.gloss: A comment in source code that spans several lines, serving to introduce the source code that follows, and bordered by asterisks.

flowmap.gloss: A kind of diagram indicating flow through a process or system.

floydian.gloss: Of or pertaining to the work of Robert Floyd, American mathematician and computer scientist.

fluent.gloss: Being or relating to a fluent interface.
A continuous variable, especially one with respect to time in Newton's Method of Fluxions.

fluent interface.gloss: An object-oriented application programming interface whose design relies extensively on chaining methods together, with the aim of improving code legibility.

flush.gloss: The process of clearing the contents of a buffer or cache.
To clear (a buffer or cache) of its contents.
To write (the data) to primary storage, clearing it from the buffer or cache.
qualifiers: of data held in a buffer or cache

flyaround.gloss: The animated passage of the camera around a model, to show it from different angles.

flyby.gloss: A three-dimensional animated sequence in which the camera moves past an object or scenery.

flying mouse.gloss: An input device like a mouse that can be lifted from a surface and moved in three dimensions.

flyout.gloss: A popup menu that branches off some other visual element.

flype.gloss: A transformation of a knot involving a 180° rotation of a tangle

flyweight pattern.gloss: A structural design pattern in which an object contains no pointers to data type methods.

fnord.gloss: A metasyntactic variable, similar to foo and bar.

focal.gloss: One of two lines perpendicular to the axis of a cone such that the cosine of the angle between the line and the axis is equal to the ratio of the cosines o the semiangles of the cone.

focal point.gloss: A solution that people will tend to use in the absence of communication, because it seems natural, special, or relevant.

focaloid.gloss: A shell bounded by two concentric, confocal ellipses (in two dimensions) or ellipsoids (in three dimensions).

fock space.gloss: An algebraic system used in quantum mechanics to describe quantum states with a variable or unknown number of particles.

focus.gloss: A point of a conic at which rays reflected from a curve or surface converge.
The status of being the currently active element in a user interface, often indicated by a visual highlight.
To transfer the input focus to (a visual element), so that it receives subsequent input.

focusable.gloss: Able to receive the input focus.

foil.gloss: To expand a product of two or more algebraic expressions, typically binomials.

foistware.gloss: Software that is installed without the user's knowledge or consent, often bundled with another product.

fold.gloss: To split (a line of text) across multiple lines, to obey line length limitations.

That which is folded together, or which enfolds or envelops. The division between the top and bottom halves of a broadsheet: headlines above the fold will be readable in a newsstand display; usually the fold. The division between the part of a web page visible in a web browser window without scrolling; usually the fold.
A section of source code that can be collapsed out of view in an editor to aid readability.

folder.gloss: A virtual container in a computer's file system, in which files and other folders may be stored. The files and subfolders in a folder are usually related.

folderlike.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a folder (directory on disk).

folding.gloss: Code folding: a source code display technique that can hide the contents of methods, classes, etc. for easier navigation.

foliate.gloss: Shaped like or otherwise resembling a leaf; leaflike. Of a curve: having two infinite branches with a common asymptote, and a leaf-shaped loop.

foliation.gloss: A set of submanifolds of a given manifold, each of which is of lower dimension than it, but which, taken together, are coextensive with it.

folio.gloss: A protective case with a flap that folds to cover the screen of a mobile device.

folium.gloss: A curve of the third order, consisting of two infinite branches having a common asymptote. The curve has a double point, and a leaf-shaped loop.

folium of descartes.gloss: An algebraic curve defined by the implicit equation x³+y³-3axy=0.

folklore.gloss: The collective of proofs or techniques which are widely known among mathematicians, but have never been formally published.

fond.gloss: A group of records having shared provenance.

font.gloss: A computer file containing the code used to draw and compose the glyphs of one or more typographic fonts on a computer display or printer.

font name.gloss: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see font, name: the name of a font (typeface).

font stack.gloss: The list of fonts a CSS stylesheet instructs a web browser to use.

fontology.gloss: The study of fonts, or electronic typefaces.

foo.gloss: A metasyntactic variable used to represent an unspecified entity. If part of a series of such entities, it is often the first in the series, and followed immediately by bar.

foobar.gloss: A metasyntactic variable name, a place holder for words; compare foo, bar.

foot.gloss: The point of intersection of one line with another that is perpendicular to it.

footer.gloss: A line of information printed at the bottom of a page to identify the contents or number pages. (Compare foot in printing.)

footgun.gloss: Any feature likely to lead to the programmer or user shooting themselves in the foot.

footprint.gloss: The amount of hard drive space required for a program.
The audit trail left by a crashed program.

for loop.gloss: A section of code in which an instruction or group of instructions is executed a specific number of times depending on the value of a loop counter.

force.gloss: The annualized instantaneous rate of change at a particular timepoint.

forced update.gloss: An update required before the user is allowed to continue using the software.

forcing.gloss: A technique used to prove the consistency of certain axioms in set theory. See forcing (mathematics).

forcing function.gloss: A function in a system of differential equations that is only a function of time, unaffected by the other variables; or, more generally, any non-homogeneous source function in any variable.
An aspect of interface design that restricts a user's abilities in order to streamline completion of a task.

ford circle.gloss: Any one of a class of circles with centre at (p/q, 1/(2q²)) and radius 1/(2q²), where p/q is an irreducible fraction (i.e., p and q are coprime integers).

foreach loop.gloss: A section of code similar to a for loop, but repeating a series of instructions for every item in a collection.

forebeam.gloss: The support section of a robot arm that goes from the main body of the robot to the gripper.

forecolour.gloss: A prominent colour, especially one that is superimposed and visible over other colours.

foreground.gloss: The application the user is currently interacting with; the application window that appears in front of all others.

foreign key.gloss: A column (or group of columns) in a relational table that identifies another table, so that items in the two tables can be conceptually linked.

forest.gloss: A graph with no cycles; i.e., a graph made up of trees.
A group of domains that are managed as a unit.

forest plot.gloss: A graphical display used in meta-analysis designed to illustrate the relative strength of treatment effects in multiple quantitative scientific studies addressing the same question.

forge.gloss: A web-based collaborative platform for developing and sharing software.

forgetful.gloss: Dropping some of the input's structure or properties before producing an output.

forgetful functor.gloss: A functor that forgets or drops some or all of its input's structure or properties before mapping to the output.

forgiving.gloss: User-friendly, such that harmful mistakes are not easily made.

fork.gloss: (software development, content management, data management) A departure from having a single source of truth (SSOT), sometimes intentionally but usually unintentionally. The launch of one or more separate software development efforts based upon a modified copy of an existing project, especially in free and open-source software.

(software development, content management, data management) A departure from having a single source of truth (SSOT), sometimes intentionally but usually unintentionally. The launch of one or more separate software development efforts based upon a modified copy of an existing project, especially in free and open-source software. Any of the software projects resulting from the launch of such separate software development efforts based upon a copy of the original project.
A set of data associated with an individual file in some file systems.
To divide into two or more branches or copies. To spawn a new child process by duplicating the existing process.

To divide into two or more branches or copies. To launch a separate software development effort based upon a modified copy of an existing software project, especially in free and open-source software.
To divide into two or more branches or copies. To create a copy of a distributed version control repository.

fork bomb.gloss: A program that creates a large number of self-replicating tasks or processes in a computer system in order to cause a denial of service.

fork-join.gloss: A pattern for parallel computing where execution parallelizes (or forks) at designated points in the program, to later merge (join) again for sequential computation.

forkable.gloss: Capable of being split into separate processes.
Capable of being split into separate projects.

form feed.gloss: A control character traditionally used to cause the printer to eject the current page of output and start a new page, more recently equivalent to a carriage return.

formal.gloss: In accordance with a methodological framework with well-defined rules or laws; rigorous.
Relating to mere manipulation and construction of strings of symbols, without regard to their meaning.

formal fallacy.gloss: A pattern of reasoning which is always wrong, due to a flaw in the structure of the argument.
