formal grammar.gloss: A precise mathematical description of a formal language, consisting of terminal symbols, nonterminal symbols, a nonterminal symbol serving as start symbol, and a set of production rules that control the expansion of nonterminal symbols into strings consisting of both terminal and nonterminal symbols.

formal language.gloss: A set of finite strings (called words) made of symbols (from a finite set of symbols, called an alphabet).

formal parameter.gloss: An abstract representation, typically including a name and a type, of a parameter expected to be passed to a method or function.

formal power series.gloss: Any finite or infinite series of the form a_0+a_1x+a_2x²…=∑ᵢa_ixⁱ, where the aᵢ are numbers, but it is understood that no value is assigned to x.

formal semantics.gloss: the rigorous mathematical study of the meaning of programming languages

formal sum.gloss: An expression which looks like a sum but where the symbol + has a purely symbolic role, in the sense that the summands cannot be meaningfully combined. An element of a free abelian group or vector space regarded as a sum of basis elements.

An expression which looks like a sum but where the symbol + has a purely symbolic role, in the sense that the summands cannot be meaningfully combined. A sum of an infinite sequence of numbers considered as an indeterminate object, in the sense of being subject to certain algebraic manipulations but not necessarily convergent.

formal system.gloss: The grouping of a formal language and a set of inference rules and/or axioms.

formal validity.gloss: An argument's property of being valid due to being an instance of an argument form.

formalism.gloss: One of several alternative computational paradigms for a given theory.
A particular mathematical or scientific theory or description of a given state or effect.

A formal expression of a grammar; a formal grammar; a set of rules of syntax that, without reference to semantics, determine whether a sequence of symbols is a well-formed sentence in a given formal language.

formalize.gloss: To rigorously prove a mathematical result.

format.gloss: To prepare a mass storage medium for initial use, erasing any existing data in the process.

format string.gloss: A string of text characters serving as a template for other strings, such as dd/MM/yyyy for a date.

formation.gloss: A structure made of two categories, two functors from the first to the second category, and a transformation from one of the functors to the other.

formation rule.gloss: Any of a set of rules used to construct well-formed formulas of a formal language.

formatted.gloss: That has been physically arranged to be in a state ready for the storage of data

formfactor.gloss: The ratio of energy radiating out from one patch to the energy absorbed by another patch, used in the calculation of radiosity.

formula.gloss: A syntactic expression of a proposition, built up from quantifiers, logical connectives, variables, relation and operation symbols, and, depending on the type of logic, possibly other operators such as modal, temporal, deontic or epistemic ones.

forty weepy weepy.gloss: The cryptanalysis of an Enigma message which was a continuation of a previous message sent at a known time.

forward compatibility.gloss: The capability of an electronic device, a piece of software, etc., to interoperate with anticipated future systems.

forward compatible.gloss: Capable of interoperating with anticipated future systems.

forward declaration.gloss: The declaration of an identifier before it is given a complete definition, so that the compiler can know its data type and memory size.

forward proxy.gloss: A server that routes traffic between a client and another system, which is in most occasions external to the network.

forward reference.gloss: The actual use of an entity before any declaration.

forward rendering.gloss: A traditional three-dimensional rendering pipeline that sorts light sources applicable to models in world space prior to rasterization.

foss.gloss: Initialism of Free and Open Source Software.

fosser.gloss: A user or advocate of free open source software.

fossie.gloss: An advocate of free open source software.

foundation model.gloss: An AI model trained on comprehensive data, enabling its application across various use cases such as chatbots and generative AI.

four color problem.gloss: The problem of coloring a map with no more than four colors, such that no two adjacent regions have the same color.

four-dimensional.gloss: Having four dimensions; being measurable along four mutually perpendicular axes.

four-russians.gloss: Method of Four Russians: a technique for speeding up certain matrix operations by partitioning the matrix into smaller blocks associated with lookup tables.

four-vector.gloss: A vector in four-dimensional vector space, especially one having three spatial dimensions and one temporal dimension.

fourgon.gloss: A polygon with four sides; a quadrilateral.

fourier analysis.gloss: A field of study concerned with the representation or approximation of general functions, such as arbitrary waveforms, by sums of trigonometric functions.

fourier coefficient.gloss: A coefficient arising from the Fourier transform of a function or signal.

fourier series.gloss: Any series resulting from the decomposition of a periodic function into terms involving cosines and sines (or, equivalently, complex exponentials).

fourier transform.gloss: A particular integral transform that when applied to a function of time (such as a signal), converts the function to one that plots the original function's frequency composition; the resultant function of such a conversion.

fourier-mukai transform.gloss: A functor Φ_K between derived category of coherent sheaves D(X) → D(Y) for schemes X and Y, which is, in a sense, an integral transform along a kernel object K ∈ D(X×Y).

fourth dimension.gloss: The fourth coordinate indicating a position along the fourth axis.

fourth normal form.gloss: A stage in the normalization of a relational database in which a database is in Boyce-Codd normal form and all multi-valued dependencies are functional dependencies.

fpdp.gloss: Initialism of Front Panel Data Port.

fractal.gloss: A mathematical set that has a non-integer and constant Hausdorff dimension, corresponding to a geometric figure or object that is self-similar at arbitrarily small scales and thus has infinite complexity.
Having the form of a fractal; having to do with fractals.

fractal dimension.gloss: A dimension in which it is the most suitable to make measurements on a fractal set.

fractile.gloss: The value of a distribution for which some fraction of the sample lies below.

fraction bar.gloss: The line separating the numerator from the denominator, whether horizontal, oblique, or diagonal.

fractional calculus.gloss: The branch of mathematics that studies generalisations of calculus to allow noninteger (i.e., real or complex) powers of the differentiation operator D and the integration operator J; (countable) any one of said generalisations of calculus.

fractional ideal.gloss: Given an integral domain R and its field of fractions K = Frac(R), an R-submodule I of K such that for some nonzero r∈R, rI ⊆ R.

fractionate.gloss: To divide each plaintext symbol into several ciphertext symbols as a preliminary stage of encryption.

fractionation.gloss: A preliminary stage of encryption that divides each plaintext symbol into several ciphertext symbols.

fraggle attack.gloss: A particular variation of the smurf attack, using UDP traffic bearing the victim's spoofed IP address sent to certain standard ports.

fraglet.gloss: A fragment of distributed code in a bio-inspired network.

fragment.gloss: To break up and disperse (a file) into non-contiguous areas of a disk.

fragmentation.gloss: The breaking up and dispersal of a file into non-contiguous areas of a disk.
The breaking up of a data packet when larger than the transmission unit of a network.

frame.gloss: An independent chunk of data sent over a network.
A form of knowledge representation in artificial intelligence.
A complete lattice in which meets distribute over arbitrary joins.

frame problem.gloss: The problem of finding an adequate collection of axioms making up a viable description of the world for a robot or artificial intelligence.

frame rate.gloss: The measurement of how quickly an imaging device can produce unique consecutive images called frames, most often expressed in frames per second (often abbreviated "fps") or, equivalently, hertz (Hz).

framebuffer.gloss: A video output device that drives a display from a memory buffer containing a complete frame of graphical data.

frameproof.gloss: Describing a specific type of code that cannot be exploited by a user claiming to have been framed by others.

frameskip.gloss: A software feature that skips the display of certain frames of animation to improve performance at the expense of visual smoothness.

framework.gloss: A reusable piece of code (and, sometimes, other utilities) providing a standard environment within which an application can be implemented.

frankenstein pc.gloss: A custom-built or heavily repaired PC (type of computer) assembled from a mix of mismatched, repurposed, or discarded spare parts rather than brand-new, standardized components.

frankenswitch.gloss: A switch for a mechanical keyboard made by combining components from different standard switches.

frecency.gloss: Any heuristic that combines the frequency and recency into a single measure, typically used to predict page revisits in a web browser.

fredholm theory.gloss: A theory of integral equations, concerning itself in the narrowest sense with the solution of the Fredholm integral equation.

free.gloss: Unconstrained. With no or only freedom-preserving limitations on distribution or modification.
Unconstrained. Intended for release, and omitting debugging diagnostics, as opposed to a checked version.
Unconstrained. In any of various technical senses generic, universal. Left adjoint to a forgetful functor G; such that any map f:X→G(A) induces a universal map ̄f:F(X)→A.
Unconstrained. In any of various technical senses generic, universal. Belonging to the image of some free functor.

Unconstrained. In any of various technical senses generic, universal. Having a set of generators which satisfy no non-trivial relations; equivalently, being the group of reduced words on a set of generators.
Unconstrained. In any of various technical senses generic, universal. Having a linearly independent set of generators (called a basis).
Unconstrained. Unconstrained of identifiers, not bound.
To relinquish (previously allocated memory) to the system.

free abelian group.gloss: A free module over the ring of integers.

free boolean algebra.gloss: A field of sets whose elements are equivalent to Boolean formulas (or, perhaps more precisely, equivalence classes of Boolean formulas). Starting with a set of n variables which are independent of each other and are called generators, the power set of this set has 2ⁿmembers which may be called atoms and are valuations of the n variables: a valuation can be considered to be a set of variables which are "true" under that valuation, or a conjunction of generators (such that variables not included in that set are included in negated form in the equivalent conjunction). Then the power set of the set of atoms yields a set of 2^(2ⁿ) members which are the elements of the said field of sets. These elements correspond to Boolean formulas: a formula can be considered to be a set of valuations which make the formula true, or a linear combination (i.e., a disjunction) of atoms.

free category.gloss: A category that is induced by a multidigraph thus: it has as its objects the vertices of the multidigraph and its morphisms are paths in the multidigraph; composition of morphisms is concatenation of paths, as long as the end of one path coincides with the beginning of the other path; an identity morphism of an object is an “empty path” at that vertex.

free group.gloss: A group that has a presentation without relators; equivalently, a free product of some number of copies of ℤ.

free list.gloss: A data structure, used in dynamic memory allocation, that connects free (unallocated) regions of memory together in a linked list.

free module.gloss: A module that has a basis. Equivalently, a module consisting of n-tuples of ring elements with no extra identities. (Then the number n is said to be its rank.) Equivalently, a direct sum whose summands are all the same ring. (The quantity of summands may be more than two.)

free monoid.gloss: A monoid whose underlying set is the Kleene closure of some set of generators, and whose operator is concatenation.

free product.gloss: A group formed from others by concatenating their presentations (when those presentations are written with disjoint sets of generators).

free software.gloss: Software that can be freely copied, redistributed and modified, including source code; software that is libre.
Any software that is free of charge, such as freeware.

free store.gloss: A region of memory used for dynamic memory allocation, often synonymous with the heap.

free ultrafilter.gloss: An ultrafilter which contains all cofinite subsets of the set which is being "filtered" by it.

free variable.gloss: A variable that is not bound to a storage location.

A variable (occurring within some expression or well-formed formula) which is not bound by a quantifier or analogous symbol (such as a lambda abstractor, the "differential d" near the end of an integral or differential form, or a summation symbol).

freebooting.gloss: Software piracy, or stealing or unauthorized rehosting of digital content.

freecam.gloss: A camera (a viewpoint) that can be manipulated without restrictions.

freedomware.gloss: Free software (with source code available), distinguished from freeware.

freestanding.gloss: Of a computer program: that runs directly on a computer's hardware, without being managed by an operating system.

freeware.gloss: Complete and functional software that does not require payment or other compensation (such as viewing advertising) for its use. Freeware may be a proprietary license with no access to the source code.

freeze.gloss: Of a machine or system, to come to a sudden halt, to stop working (functioning).
The state when either a single computer program, or the whole system ceases to respond to inputs.

freezer.gloss: A hardware device that can freeze the state of the system to allow it to be inspected, saved or modified.

frequency.gloss: number of times an event occurred in an experiment (absolute frequency)

frequency distribution.gloss: a structured representation that summarizes how often values or categories occur within a dataset by organizing quantitative data into class intervals and categorizing qualitative data into distinct groups, thus revealing patterns, trends, and distributions, often showed in a list, table, or graph that displays the frequency of various outcomes in a sample.

frequency domain.gloss: The analysis of mathematical functions or signals with respect to frequency, and possibly a phase, rather than time.

frequency polygon.gloss: A frequency distribution curve made of only straight lines.

frequentaneous.gloss: Related to frequency and phase (of a wave)

frequently.gloss: For infinitely many terms of the sequence.

frey curve.gloss: The elliptic curve associated with a solution of Fermat's equation.

friable.gloss: Of a number: smooth, that factors completely into small prime numbers.

friction.gloss: Any obstacle or hindrance that makes a system less convenient or desirable to use.

friend-to-friend.gloss: Describing a restricted type of peer-to-peer network in which only persons who know each other participate.

friendly.gloss: Being or relating to two or more natural numbers with a common abundancy.

friendly name.gloss: The everyday name of a hardware device, displayed to the user instead of the internal or technical designation.

frieze group.gloss: Any of seven symmetry groups of infinitely long ornamented bands.

frink ideal.gloss: A certain kind of subset of a partially ordered set.

fritterware.gloss: Software with unnecessary features that encourage timewasting and experimentation.

frob.gloss: To manipulate in some ill-defined way; to tweak or mess about with.
To transform and obscure in a trivial fashion with memfrob(3).

frobenioid.gloss: A category with some extra structure that generalizes the theory of line bundles on models of finite extensions of global fields.

frobenius.gloss: Used attributively to attribute a concept to the work of Ferdinand Georg Frobenius or more directly to associate it with the Frobenius endomorphism (commutative algebra, field theory) or Frobenius morphism (category theory).

frobenius covariant.gloss: Any of a set of special polynomials for a square matrix A, namely projection matrices Aᵢ associated with the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A.

frobenius endomorphism.gloss: Given a commutative ring R with prime characteristic p, the endomorphism that maps x → xᵖ for all x ∈ R.

frobnicate.gloss: Synonym of frob (“manipulate in some ill-defined way; tweak”).

front controller pattern.gloss: A structural (and partitioning) design pattern that provides a centralized entry point for handling requests and is an extension to the model-view-controller design pattern.

front door.gloss: The normal portal page to a website.

front end.gloss: That part of a hardware or software system that is conceptually closest to the user; the user interface.

front-end.gloss: Relating to the front end or user interface of a hardware or software system.

front-end processor.gloss: A small computer that interfaces with the host computer and handles operations such as network access or peripheral control.

front-side bus.gloss: A bus that conducts data between a CPU and a memory controller.

fréchet derivative.gloss: An extension of the concept of the derivative from real-valued functions of one real variable to functions on normed spaces.

fréchet surface.gloss: An equivalence class of parametrized surfaces in a metric space.

frölicher spectral sequence.gloss: A tool in the theory of complex manifolds, for expressing the potential failure of the results of cohomology theory that are valid in general only for Kähler manifolds.

fsck.gloss: A *nix file system check to detect damage to, or corruption of, files or filesystem structures.
To run fsck on; to perform a fsck on.

fsvo.gloss: Initialism of for some values of.

ftbfs.gloss: Initialism of fails to build from source: said of a computer program that cannot be built from its source code due to errors.

ftp.gloss: To transfer using File Transfer Protocol.

fuchsian group.gloss: Any discrete group of isometries of the hyperbolic plane.

fuckings.gloss: Public abuse directed at rival demosceners, often included in the scrolltext of a demo; the negative equivalent of greets.

full.gloss: Complete; with nothing omitted. Surjective as a map of morphisms
qualifiers: of a functor between locally small categories

full.gloss: Complete; with nothing omitted. Including all morphisms. Formally: Such that for every pairs of objects (X, Y) in S, the hom-sets operatorname Hom_S(X,Y) and operatorname Hom_C(X,Y) are equal.
qualifiers: of a subcategory S of C

full binary tree.gloss: A binary tree in which each node has exactly two or zero children.

full disclosure.gloss: The disclosure of all security flaws in a product.

full functor.gloss: A functor which maps morphisms from its source to its target category in such a way that the restriction of that mapping to any source hom-set is surjective into the corresponding target hom-set.

full outer join.gloss: A join yielding a set of records for two tables, where all rows of the "left" table are enlisted with all rows of the "right" table, even if the join condition does not find any matching row on the "left" or on the "right" table.

full rank.gloss: Having the highest possible rank for its size; having a rank (dimension) equal to the number of columns or the number of rows.

full screen.gloss: Of a window occupying all the available display surface of a screen.

fullscreen.gloss: To make a window occupy the entire screen.

fullwidth.gloss: Of a text character, occupying the space of two alphanumeric characters in a monospace font, or two "normal" text columns.

fully faithful.gloss: Of a functor, injective and surjective on hom-sets.

fully qualified domain name.gloss: A domain name that specifies its exact location in the tree hierarchy of the Domain Name System.

fully qualified hostname.gloss: An Internet domain name that identifies a computer.

function.gloss: A relation in which each element of the domain is associated with exactly one element of the codomain.
A routine that receives zero or more arguments and may return a result.

function code.gloss: Any character used to specify a function of a piece of software or hardware (such as carriage return of a printer)

function key.gloss: Any of a set of keys on a personal computer or terminal keyboard used to activate a predefined or programmable function, especially a numbered row of keys (F1, F2, etc.) above the alphanumeric keys.

function pointer.gloss: a pointer that points to a function

function space.gloss: Any metric space whose elements are functions

function table.gloss: A printed tabulation of selected values of a function corresponding to selected independent variables; e.g. a table of logarithms.

function value.gloss: An element of the range of a function. (Or, employing the "machine" metaphor, it is one of the "outputs" of a function.)

function-evaluation routine.gloss: A program, module or subroutine etc that returns the value of a defined function

functional.gloss: Of or relating to a function or functions.
Having semantics defined purely in terms of mathematical functions, without side-effects.

A function that takes a function as its argument; more precisely, a function whose argument varies in a space of (real- or complex-valued) functions and whose value belongs to a monodimensional space.
A scalar-valued linear function on a vector space.
An object encapsulating a function pointer (or equivalent).

functional graph.gloss: A directed graph whose every vertex has outdegree 1.

functional programming.gloss: Programming in a style that, in lieu of assignment, uses procedure calls to bind variables to values, so that referential transparency is preserved.

functional requirement.gloss: Any of the functions of a software system, described formally.

functional root.gloss: A function which, when applied a given number of times, equals another given function.

functionalize.gloss: To adapt into a form that uses functional programming.

functionally complete.gloss: Capable of computing any recursive function.

functionhood.gloss: The state or quality of being a function.

functoid.gloss: A tool that transforms data from one form to another as it is routed from a source to a destination.

functor.gloss: A category homomorphism; a morphism from a source category to a target category which maps objects to objects and arrows to arrows (either covariantly or contravariantly), in such a way as to preserve morphism composition and identities.

functor category.gloss: A category whose objects are functors (from some fixed given domain category to some fixed given codomain category) and whose morphisms are natural transformations.

functorial.gloss: Able to be described as a functor.

fundamental group.gloss: For a specified topological space, the group whose elements are homotopy classes of loops (images of some arbitrary closed interval whose endpoints are both mapped to a designated point) and whose group operation is concatenation.

fundamental theorem.gloss: A theorem (or, in non-mathematical fields, a commonly accepted hypothesis) considered to be of central importance to a specified field.

funnel plot.gloss: A scatterplot of effect size against a measure of study size or variability, used primarily as a visual aid to detecting and displaying bias or systematic heterogeneity.

furps.gloss: Acronym of functionality, usability, reliability, performance, supportability; used to help remember the major requirements of software.

fuse.gloss: An otherwise stable arbitrarily long repeating pattern that, when perturbed from one end, destructively carries that perturbation at a constant speed to the other end.

fusker.gloss: A program or algorithm that downloads images or media from a web site that have not been publicly linked, based on guessing at similar URLs.

fusking.gloss: The use of a fusker to download private images or media.

futex.gloss: A mechanism for basic locking, based on an atomic integer in userspace that may be operated upon from multiple processes or threads.

future.gloss: An object that retrieves the value of a promise.

fuzz.gloss: The random data used in fuzz testing.
To test a software component by running it on randomly generated input.

fuzz test.gloss: Any test that uses the fuzz testing methodology.

fuzz testing.gloss: A testing methodology in which random data (“fuzz”) is supplied as input to a program.

fuzzable.gloss: Able to be fuzzed, i.e. tested with randomly generated input.

fuzzer.gloss: A software program that performs fuzz testing.

fuzzification.gloss: The addition of fuzziness to data in fuzzy logic.

fuzzy.gloss: Employing or relating to fuzzy logic.

fuzzy controller.gloss: A controller that uses a fuzzy logic ruleset.

fuzzy logic.gloss: A form of reasoning, derived from fuzzy set theory, whereby a truth value need not be exactly zero (false) or one (true), but rather can be zero, one, or any value in between.

fuzzy math.gloss: A form of logic based on the concept of a fuzzy set.

fuzzy measure.gloss: A kind of generalized measure in which the additive property is replaced by the weaker property of monotonicity.

fuzzy search.gloss: A type of search algorithm that includes results similar to the query (but not necessarily exactly matching), such as words with similar spelling, root form, pronunciation, or meaning, or results that contain the search term as a subsequence.

fuzzyism.gloss: Of a state or condition pertaining to fuzzy math.

fvu.gloss: Abbreviation of fraction of variance unexplained

følner sequence.gloss: For a given group, a sequence of sets satisfying a particular condition.

g-buffer.gloss: A screen space representation of geometry and material information, generated by an intermediate rendering pass in deferred shading rendering pipelines.

gabor atom.gloss: A kind of function used in the analysis proposed by Dennis Gabor in 1946 in which a family of functions is built from translations and modulations of a generating function.

gabor filter.gloss: A linear filter used for image texture analysis.

gabor transform.gloss: A special case of the short-time Fourier transform, used to determine the sinusoidal frequency and phase content of local sections of a signal as it changes over time.

gabor wavelet.gloss: A form of wavelet designed so as to minimize the product of its standard deviations in the time and frequency domain.

gadget.gloss: A technique for converting a part of one problem to an equivalent part of another problem, used in constructing reductions.

gadt.gloss: Initialism of generalized algebraic data type.

gallery.gloss: A browsable collection of images, font styles, etc.

galois connection.gloss: A type of correspondence between partially ordered sets (posets), also applicable to preordered sets.

galois extension.gloss: An algebraic extension that is both a normal and a separable extension; equivalently, an algebraic extension E/F such that the fixed field of its automorphism group (Galois group) Aut(E/F) is the base field F.

galois field.gloss: A finite field; a field that contains a finite number of elements.

galois group.gloss: The automorphism group of a Galois extension.

galois theory.gloss: The branch of mathematics dealing with Galois groups, Galois fields, and polynomial equations. It provides a link between field theory and group theory: it permits certain problems in the former to be reduced to the latter, which in some respects is simpler and better understood.

gambler's ruin.gloss: The fact that a gambler playing a game with negative expected value will eventually go broke, regardless of the betting system used.

game of chance.gloss: A game in which the outcome is at least partly determined by random variables (chance and luck) rather than strictly by strategy.

game port.gloss: An I/O port, on earlier PCs, used for the attachment of a joystick or similar hardware

game theory.gloss: A branch of applied mathematics that studies strategic situations in which individuals or organisations choose various actions in an attempt to maximize their returns.

game-theoretical.gloss: Of, relating to, or defined in terms of game theory.

gamebot.gloss: A bot (automated user) that takes part in a game or offers gaming functionality.

gameport.gloss: A hardware port for communication with a game controller.

gamma.gloss: The Gamma function, symbolized by Γ.
A constant approximately equal to 0.57721566, symbolized by γ (also known as the Euler–Mascheroni constant).

gamma correction.gloss: A nonlinear operation used to encode and decode luminance or tristimulus values in video or still image systems.

gamma distribution.gloss: Any of a family of two-parameter continuous probability distributions, of which the common exponential distribution and chi-square distribution are special cases.

gamma function.gloss: A meromorphic function which generalizes the notion of factorial to complex numbers and has singularities at the nonpositive integers; any of certain generalizations or analogues of said function, such as extend the factorial to domains other than the complex numbers.

gammoid.gloss: A certain kind of matroid, describing sets of vertices that can be reached by vertex-disjoint paths in a directed graph.

gap buffer.gloss: A dynamic array that allows efficient insertion and deletion operations clustered near the same location.

garbage.gloss: Allocated memory which is no longer in use but has not yet been deallocated.
Data that are misinterpreted as another kind of data.

garbage collect.gloss: To reclaim resources which are no longer in use; to run a garbage collector.
To destroy (an object that is no longer in use) during the process of garbage collection

garbage collection.gloss: An automatic mechanism that frees up resources (such as allocated memory) that are no longer in use.

garbage collector.gloss: An algorithm, procedure or thread dedicated to garbage collection: reclaiming resources which are no longer in use.

garch.gloss: Initialism of generalised autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity

garden of eden.gloss: A pattern that can only exist as an initial state and is not attainable from any other state.

gate.gloss: A logical pathway made up of switches which turn on or off. Examples are and, or, nand, etc.

gatekeeper.gloss: A provider of core platform services with specific characteristics (Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 of the European Parliament and of the Council)

gateware.gloss: Logic implemented in configurable digital logic gates.

gateway.gloss: In wireless internet, an access point with additional software capabilities such as providing NAT and DHCP, which may also provide VPN support, roaming, firewalls, various levels of security, etc.

gatewaying.gloss: The action or use of a gateway or access point; the connection or transmission using one or more gateways.

gating.gloss: The control of the flow of signals based on certain conditions or criteria.

gauge.gloss: A semi-norm; a function that assigns a non-negative size to all vectors in a vector space.

gauss map.gloss: A map from a given oriented surface in Euclidean space to the unit sphere which maps each point on the surface to a unit vector orthogonal to the surface at that point.

gauss-codazzi equation.gloss: Any of a group of fundamental formulas in Riemannian and pseudo-Riemannian geometry that link together the induced metric and second fundamental form of a submanifold of (or immersion into) a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold.

gauss-jordan elimination.gloss: A method of reducing an augmented matrix to reduced row echelon form.

gaussian.gloss: Of or pertaining to Carl Friedrich Gauss.
A holographic element, a fuzzy volume of a specified shape with view-direction dependent coloration.

gaussian elimination.gloss: A method of reducing an augmented matrix to row echelon form.

gaussian function.gloss: A function of the form f(x)=a· exp (-((x-b)²)/(2c²)) for arbitrary real-number constants a, b and non-zero c; used in statistics, signal processing, etc.

gaussian integer.gloss: Any complex number of the form a + bi, where a and b are integers.

gaussian moat.gloss: The maximum difference between consecutive numbers in a sequence of distinct Gaussian prime numbers.

gaussian prime.gloss: A Gaussian integer a + bi such that either one of a, b is zero and the absolute value of the other is a prime number of the form 4n + 3 (with n a nonnegative integer); or both are nonzero and a² + b² is a prime number (which will never be of the form 4n + 3).

gaussian splat.gloss: A holographic scene, object, image, video, formed out of individual Guassians splotched together as the splat.

gaussianity.gloss: The extent to which something is Gaussian.

gbps.gloss: gigabits per second, a measure of data transfer rate equal to 1,000 megabits per second.

gdal.gloss: Initialism of Geospatial Data Abstraction Library (a computer software library for reading and writing raster and vector geospatial data formats.)

gem.gloss: A package containing programs or libraries for the Ruby programming language.

general availability.gloss: A release of software which is good enough to be made available outside the originating company, to the general public.

general linear group.gloss: For given field F and order n, the group of invertible n×n matrices, with the group operation of matrix multiplication.

generalization.gloss: A proof, axiom, problem, or definition that includes another's cases, and also some additional cases; a conclusion reached by inferring from specific cases to more general cases or principles.

generalized circle.gloss: A circle or a line, the two being regarded as types of a single form.

generalized continued fraction.gloss: A continued fraction were the numerators and denominators can assume arbitrary values.

generalized continuum hypothesis.gloss: The hypothesis that, for each ordinal α, there is no cardinal number strictly between א_α and 2^(א_α), i.e. 2^(א_α)=א_(α+1).

generalized element.gloss: A morphism whose codomain is some specified object.

generalized search tree.gloss: A type of search tree that features data and query extensibility.

generate.gloss: To form a figure from a curve or solid.

generating function.gloss: A formal power series with one indeterminate, whose coefficients encode a sequence that can be studied by algebraic manipulation of the series; any one of several generalizations, such as to encode more than one sequence or use more than one indeterminate.

generation.gloss: The formation or production of any geometrical magnitude, as a line, a surface, a solid, by the motion, in accordance with a mathematical law, of a point or a magnitude, by the motion of a point, of a surface by a line, a sphere by a semicircle, etc.
A single iteration of a cellular automaton rule on a pattern.

generative art.gloss: An artwork created, in whole or in part, through an autonomous system; instead of painting or drawing manually, the artist writes rules, algorithms, or computer code that dictate how shapes, colors, and patterns interact; the system then runs independently to produce the final piece.

generative lexicon.gloss: A linguistic semantics theory that challenges purely verb-centric approaches to compositionality.

generator.gloss: One who, or that which, generates, begets, causes, or produces. An element of a group that is used in the presentation of the group: one of the elements from which the others can be inferred with the given relators.
One who, or that which, generates, begets, causes, or produces. One of the lines of a ruled surface; more generally, an element of some family of linear spaces.
One who, or that which, generates, begets, causes, or produces. A subordinate piece of code which, given some initial parameters, will generate multiple output values on request.

generatrix.gloss: A curve that, when rotated about an axis, produces a solid figure.

generic.gloss: Of a procedure, written so as to operate on any data type, the type required being passed as a parameter.
Of a point, having coordinates that are algebraically independent over the base field.

generic element.gloss: The identity element of an object when thought of as a generalized element of that object.

generic programming.gloss: A style of computer programming in which algorithms are written in terms of to-be-specified-later types that are then instantiated when needed for specific types provided as parameters.

generic property.gloss: A property that is true almost everywhere in a given set (i.e., the set of points at which the property is not true is either of measure zero or a subset of a set of measure zero).
A property that is true in some dense open subset of a given set.

genericize.gloss: To make generic. To make more generic: to be usable in more contexts.

generics.gloss: The use of templates, etc., to create generic source code that can be used in many situations.

generification.gloss: The process of making generic; the conversion to use generics.

genetic algorithm.gloss: A search heuristic that is based on biological evolution.

genetic memory.gloss: An artificial neural network combination of genetic algorithm and the mathematical model of sparse distributed memory.

genetic programming.gloss: A search heuristic that explores the space of computer programs and is based on biological evolution.

genned in.gloss: Having had certain characteristics generated or installed.

genome assembly.gloss: The process of taking a large number of short DNA sequences and putting them back together to create a representation of the original chromosomes from which the DNA originated.

genon.gloss: A branch cut between two complex planes.

genus.gloss: A natural number representing any of several related measures of the complexity of a given manifold or graph.

geo-block.gloss: To deny access to content to users from certain regions based on geolocation.

geo-blocking.gloss: The use of geolocation software to deny access to content to users from certain regions or countries.

geoadditive.gloss: Obtained by the addition of multiple geographically separate models

geocomplexity.gloss: The use of mathematical techniques to model complex geological systems (such as earthquakes)

geocomputation.gloss: The mathematical analysis of complex spatial problems

geocomputing.gloss: The use of computing in the geographic sciences

geodatabase.gloss: A database containing geographical and spatial data

geodesic.gloss: The shortest curve between two points on a specific surface.
A course allowing the parallel-transport of vectors along a course that causes tangent vectors to remain tangent vectors throughout that course (a straight curve, a line that is straight).

geodesicity.gloss: The property of a smooth curve being a geodesic or of a vector field to be geodesic in the context of differential geometry.
The characterisation of a differentiable manifold in terms of its geodesics, such as the quality of a submanifold being totally geodesic.

geoenabled.gloss: Supporting geographic features such as mapping.

geofacet.gloss: A technique for visualising data for a range of geographic regions, in which a series of identically-sized plots (for instance, bar charts) are arranged in a way that mimics the real-world geographical configuration of the regions.

geofence.gloss: A virtual perimeter around a geographic area, typically enforced by monitoring the positions of trackable mobile devices inside or outside the area, and determining if they cross the "fence".
To provide a geofence around (an area).

geolocked.gloss: restricted to a specific geographical region

geomathematics.gloss: The application of mathematics to the geosciences

geometric analysis.gloss: A branch of mathematics in which techniques from differential geometry are used in the analysis and solution of partial differential equations, and vice versa.

geometric mean.gloss: A measure of central tendency of a set of n values computed by extracting the nth root of the product of the values.

geometric multiplicity.gloss: The dimension of the eigenspace of a given eigenvalue (of a given square matrix).

geometric pen.gloss: A configurable drawing tool for creating lines that has a width specified in logical units, as opposed to device units (pixels), and therefore scales when the resulting image is zoomed in or out.

geometric progression.gloss: A sequence in which each term except the first is obtained from the previous by multiplying it by a constant value, known as the common ratio of the geometric progression.

geometric series.gloss: Any infinite series whose terms are in geometric progression; any series of the form a+ar+ar²+ar³⋯=a∑ᵢ₌₀ ᪲rⁱ, where a≠0, r≠0, and r≠1.

geometricity.gloss: The condition of being geometric, or of having been geometricized.

geometrization.gloss: The description of a space as a geometry.

geometry.gloss: The branch of mathematics dealing with spatial relationships.
A mathematical system that deals with spatial relationships and that is built on a particular set of axioms; a subbranch of geometry which deals with such a system or systems.
A mathematical object comprising representations of a space and of its spatial relationships.

geometry of numbers.gloss: The subbranch of number theory which applies techniques from geometry to the study of algebraic numbers.

geometry shader.gloss: A type of shader that can process three-dimensional model geometry, for example by turning one primitive into another.

georedundant.gloss: Operating at more than one geographical location, as a form of redundancy in case one site fails.

georemote.gloss: Geographically remote; taking place over a significant physical distance.

georestriction.gloss: The deliberate limitation of a (digital) product or service so that it is only available to users in certain geographic regions.

geospatial.gloss: Describing the combination of spatial software and geographic data.

geostatistics.gloss: The application of statistics to geological observations

gepon.gloss: Initialism of gigabit ethernet passive optical network.

gerbe.gloss: An abstract construction in homological algebra and geometry providing a certain type of generalisation for a sheaf.

gergonne point.gloss: A certain triangle center. Given a triangle ∆ABC and its Gergonne triangle (with the touchpoint opposite A denoted by T_A, etc.), the Gergonne point is the intersection of the three lines AT_A, BT_B, and CT_C.

gergonne triangle.gloss: A triangle defined by the three touchpoints of the incircle on the three sides of a given triangle.

germ.gloss: An equivalence class that includes a specified function defined in an open neighborhood.

gerschenkron effect.gloss: The theory that changing the base year for an index determines the growth rate of the index.

gesture.gloss: A motion made with a pointing device, or on a touchscreen, that is recognised by the system as a command.

gevrey class.gloss: The Gevrey classes on a domain #92;Omega#92;subseteq#92;Rⁿ are spaces of functions 'between' the space of analytic functions C#92;omega(#92;Omega) and the space of smooth (infinitely differentiable) functions C#92;infty(#92;Omega). They are used in control engineering for trajectory planning.

ggev.gloss: A routine in LAPACK for computing eigenvalues.

ghost.gloss: A copy of a file or record.
A formerly nonexistent character that was at some point mistakenly encoded into a character set standard, which might have since become used opportunistically for some genuine purpose.
To gray out (a visual element) to indicate that it is unavailable.
To forcibly disconnect (an IRC user) who is using one's reserved nickname.

ghost character.gloss: A kanji included erroneously in the JIS X 0208 character set (not traceable to the sources used to compile JIS X 0208).

ghost image.gloss: A copy of all the contents of a hard drive, used as a backup.

ghost imaging.gloss: The process of creating a ghost image of all the contents of a hard drive as a backup that may be stored and later retrieved if needed.

ghosting.gloss: A problem with a keyboard where certain simultaneous keypresses trigger the action of a further key that was not in fact pressed.

giant.gloss: An Ethernet packet that exceeds the medium's maximum packet size of 1,518 bytes.

gibbs measure.gloss: A generalization of the canonical ensemble to infinite systems, giving the probability of a given system being in a given state (or, equivalently, of a given random variable having a given value).

gibbs sampling.gloss: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for obtaining a sequence of observations which are approximated from a specified multivariate probability distribution, when direct sampling is difficult.

gibbs state.gloss: An equilibrium probability distribution which remains invariant under future evolution of the system.

gibibit.gloss: Strictly, 2³⁰ (1024³, or 1,073,741,824) bits or 2¹⁰ (1024) mebibits, as opposed to a gigabit.

gibibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2³⁰ (1024³, or 1,073,741,824) bytes or 2¹⁰ (1024) mebibytes, as opposed to a gigabyte.

gif.gloss: A bitmap image in a particular format with support for multiple images per file or animations, and up to 256 distinct colors per frame, including a fully transparent color.

gigabinary.gloss: Relating to the units prefixed gibi-, such as the gibibyte as opposed to the gigabyte.

gigabit.gloss: One billion (10⁹, or 1,000,000,000) bits or 1,000 megabits.

gigabyte.gloss: One billion (10⁹, or 1,000,000,000) bytes or 1,000 megabytes.

gigaflop.gloss: A unit of measure for the calculating speed of a computer equal to one billion (10⁹) floating point operations per second.

gigaword.gloss: A unit of storage or capacity equal to (or 2³⁰ = 1,073,741,824) words. It is given the "giga" prefix because of the relative proximity of this value to 10⁹.

gigo.gloss: Acronym of garbage in, garbage out (“the integrity of the output is dependent on the integrity of the input”).

gilt.gloss: Acronym of globalization, internationalization, localization, and translation

gimped.gloss: Modified by means of the GIMP image editor.

gingerbreadman map.gloss: In dynamical systems theory, a chaotic two-dimensional map given by the piecewise linear transformation

gini coefficient.gloss: A measure of the inequality of a statistical distribution, ranging from 0 (total equality) to 1 (maximal inequality), used in various disciplines but especially in economics to compare incomes or wealth.

girth.gloss: The length of the shortest cycle in a graph.

gis.gloss: Initialism of geospatial information system or initialism of geographic information system (“computer-based system to analyse and present spatial data”).

gist.gloss: A sharable snippet of source code, especially on the version controlled pastebin-hosting site GitHub Gist.

glassmorphism.gloss: A user interface style characterized by panels with a blurred translucency effect over background elements, mimicking frosted glass.

glenzed.gloss: Displayed with a simulation of translucency by means of glenzing.

glenzing.gloss: A technique for simulating translucency by storing extra colour values in the palette that represent the combined colours of intersecting objects in a scene.

glide reflection.gloss: A transformation consisting of a reflection followed by a translation along the same line.

glider.gloss: In the Game of Life, a particular configuration of five cells that recurs periodically at fixed offsets and appears to "walk" across the grid.

In the Game of Life, a particular configuration of five cells that recurs periodically at fixed offsets and appears to "walk" across the grid. Any spaceship in a cellular automaton, especially one which exhibits glide reflection.

glider gun.gloss: In the Game of Life, any pattern that "fires" out gliders.

glissette.gloss: The locus described by any point attached to a curve that moves continuously along another fixed curve, the movable curve having no rotation at any instant.

glitchfest.gloss: A situation involving numerous glitches or bugs.

glob.gloss: A limited pattern matching technique using wildcards, less powerful than a regular expression; such a pattern.
To carry out pattern matching using a glob.

global.gloss: Pertaining to the whole of something; total, universal: Of a variable, accessible by all parts of a program.

global element.gloss: A morphism from the terminal object to a given object (to which it is said to belong).

global illumination.gloss: The realistic lighting of a rendered scene by means of algorithms that take into account not only the direct illumination from light sources but also the indirect cases where light is reflected between surfaces in the scene.

global maximum.gloss: An element in a function's domain where the function assumes its highest value.

global minimum.gloss: An element in a function's domain where the function assumes its lowest value.

global scope.gloss: A type of scope that has an effect throughout an entire computer program.

globoid.gloss: A spherical representation or projection of a sphere or ellipsoid.
Of, or pertaining to, a globe

glome.gloss: A hypersphere in 4-dimensional Euclidean space defined as the set of all points that are at a given distance from a given point, also called a 3-sphere.

glue code.gloss: Code that serves to connect separate parts of a program for compatibility or interoperability.

gluing.gloss: A connection between the edges of two planes, or between the points at the ends of two lines.
Any of various processes for producing some structure (e.g. a sheaf or scheme) by combining smaller structures that are in some way compatible with each other.

glvalue.gloss: A value that is either an xvalue or an lvalue.

glyph.gloss: A visual representation of a letter, character, or symbol, in a specific font and style.

gnisrap.gloss: The cognitive process of creating a mental model of a computer program by reading the code.

gnome sort.gloss: A variation of the insertion sort that does not use nested loops.

gnomon.gloss: A plane figure formed by removing a parallelogram from a corner of a larger parallelogram.
A number representing the increment between two figurate numbers (“numbers equal to the numbers of dots in geometric figures formed of dots”).

go down.gloss: To stop functioning, to go offline.

go gold.gloss: To be released to manufacturing in its final form, so that copies can be made and shipped.

go into.gloss: To divide, to be a factor of.

god class.gloss: The class serving as a template for a God object.

god object.gloss: A poorly designed object that that references a large number of distinct types, has too many unrelated or uncategorized methods, or some combination of both, thereby violating the single responsibility principle of SOLID.

god ray.gloss: A crepuscular ray; a visible beam of light such as a sunbeam or moonbeam.

god-king.gloss: A tyrannical maintainer of a collaborative project.

goguen category.gloss: A fuzzy kind of category in which membership is determined not in binary (true-or-false) fashion but by a more general interval.

gold.gloss: In a finished state, ready for manufacturing.

goldbach number.gloss: A positive even integer that can be expressed as the sum of two odd primes; involved in Goldbach's conjecture.

goldbach partition.gloss: The expression of a given even number as the sum of two primes; involved in Goldbach's conjecture.

golden image.gloss: The master disk image used in the initialization of VMs, hard disks, etc.

golden ratio.gloss: The irrational number (approximately 1.618), usually denoted by the Greek letter φ (phi), which is equal to the sum of its own reciprocal and 1, or, equivalently, is the square root of the sum of itself and 1.

golden record.gloss: A single authoritative record on an individual customer etc. that draws from various other data sources.

golden section.gloss: The division of a whole into two parts such that the ratio of the smaller part to the larger is equal to the ratio of the larger part to the whole.

golden spiral.gloss: A logarithmic spiral whose growth factor is φ, the golden ratio.

golden triangle.gloss: An isosceles triangle whose duplicated side is in the golden ratio to the distinct side.

golf.gloss: To write something in as few characters as possible (e.g. in code golf, regex golf)

golfed.gloss: Having had its source code made as short as possible, as in code golf.

golfer.gloss: One who takes part in code golf or regex golf.

golflang.gloss: An esoteric programming language designed for code golf.

golygon.gloss: A serial isogon of 90 degrees; any polygon with all right angles, whose sides are consecutive integer lengths.

golyhedron.gloss: A three-dimensional generalization of a golygon.

gompertz curve.gloss: Any of a family of curves, describing demographic growth, that increase exponentially at first before reaching a plateau.

gompertz distribution.gloss: A continuous probability distribution, often used to describe adult lifespans.

gompertzian.gloss: Having the form of, or some characteristics of the form of, a Gompertz curve.

gon.gloss: One hundredth of a right angle: a gradian.

gonality.gloss: The "angularity" of a curve (See the Wikipedia article for a more rigorous definition)

gonihedric.gloss: of or pertaining to the generalization of the Feynman path integral to an integral over random surfaces

goodman and kruskal's gamma.gloss: A particular measure of rank correlation, i.e., the similarity of the orderings of the data when ranked by each of the quantities.

goodman and kruskal's lambda.gloss: A particular measure of proportional reduction in error in cross tabulation analysis.

goodput.gloss: Application-level throughput, i.e. the number of useful bits per unit of time forwarded by a network from source to destination, excluding protocol overhead such as retransmissions.

goodstein sequence.gloss: A sequence of natural numbers generated from an initial value m, starting with that value, and proceeding by performing certain operations on it. Although such sequences rapidly produce very large numbers, they always terminate at zero.

googolbyte.gloss: A unit of digital storage equal to a googol (10¹⁰⁰) bytes.

googolgon.gloss: A polygon with a googol number of sides (virtually indistinguishable from a circle)

goroutine.gloss: A lightweight communicating process in the Go programming language.

goshwow.gloss: Of or pertaining to a sense of wonder; awe inspiring; amazement causing.

gosper curve.gloss: A particular fractal object, a space-filling curve that can tile the plane.

gosper island.gloss: The space filled by the Gosper curve.

gossip.gloss: Communication done using a gossip protocol.
To communicate using a gossip protocol.

gotcha.gloss: A potential problem or source of trouble. A feature of a system or a program that works in the way it is documented but is counter-intuitive and almost invites mistake or non-function.

goto.gloss: Any construct which produces an unstructured jump in the flow of execution.
To reach (a point in a program) by means of a GOTO instruction.

gouraud shading.gloss: A method of simulating the effects of light and colour across the surface of an object, based on estimates of the surface normal of each vertex in a polygonal 3D model.

gowers norm.gloss: In the field of additive combinatorics, a class of norms on functions on a finite group or group-like object which quantify the amount of structure or randomness present.

gpf.gloss: Initialism of general protection fault, a type of interrupt produced by IA32 CPUs.

gpgpu.gloss: Initialism of general-purpose computing on graphics processing units.

gpio.gloss: Initialism of general-purpose input/output, a pin on an integrated circuit whose behavior can be controlled by the user at run time.

gpon.gloss: Initialism of gigabit-capable passive optical network, standardized as ITU-T G.984.

gpu.gloss: Initialism of graphics processing unit (an electronic circuit dedicated to generating graphics and displaying images).

grab handle.gloss: A visual cue indicating where a displayed object can be activated for resizing, etc. using the pointing device.

graceful degradation.gloss: The ability of a system to maintain at least some of its functionality when portions are not working, or when certain features are not available.

grade.gloss: In a linear system of divisors on an n-dimensional variety, the number of free intersection points of n generic divisors.

gradian.gloss: A unit of angle equal to 0.9 degree, so that there are 100 gradians in a right angle.

gradient.gloss: The ratio of the rates of change of a dependent variable and an independent variable, the slope of a curve's tangent.
A differential operator that maps each point of a scalar field to a vector pointed in the direction of the greatest rate of change of the scalar. Notation for a scalar field φ: ∇φ
Using the gradient to solve a problem.

gradient descent.gloss: A first-order iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function.

gradual typing.gloss: A type system where some variables are statically-typed and some are dynamically-typed.

graduate.gloss: To approve (a feature) for general release.

grammar.gloss: A formal system specifying the syntax of a language.
A formal system defining a formal language.
A set of component patterns, along with the rules for connecting them, which can be combined to form more complex patterns such as large still lifes, oscillators, and spaceships.

grammar checker.gloss: A software application, like a spell checker, that attempts to verify the grammar in a document.

grammar induction.gloss: The process of constructing a model that captures the characteristics of observed objects by learning a formal grammar.

grammar-oriented programming.gloss: A software development paradigm that involves creating a custom, domain-specific language (DSL) to capture the logic of a specific business domain.

grand 600-cell.gloss: A regular star 4-polytope with Schläfli symbol {3,3,5/2}

grand mean.gloss: The mean (average) of all numbers observed, rather than that of a subsample.

grandfather.gloss: The archived older version of a file that immediately preceded the father file.

granocentric.gloss: Describing the formulation of a packing problem based on the free space around a grain (individual particle)

graph.gloss: A data chart (graphical representation of data) intended to illustrate the relationship between a set (or sets) of numbers (quantities, measurements or indicative numbers) and a reference set, whose elements are indexed to those of the former set(s) and may or may not be numbers.

A set of points constituting a graphical representation of a real function; (formally) a set of tuples (x_1,x_2,…,x_m,y)∈ R ᵐ⁺¹, where y=f(x_1,x_2,…,x_m) for a given function f: R ᵐ→ R . See also Graph of a function on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

A set of vertices (or nodes) connected together by edges; (formally) an ordered pair of sets (V,E), where the elements of V are called vertices or nodes and E is a set of pairs (called edges) of elements of V. See also Graph (discrete mathematics) on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

A topological space which represents some graph (ordered pair of sets) and which is constructed by representing the vertices as points and the edges as copies of the real interval [0,1] (where, for any given edge, 0 and 1 are identified with the points representing the two vertices) and equipping the result with a particular topology called the graph topology.

A morphism Γ_f from the domain of f to the product of the domain and codomain of f, such that the first projection applied to Γ_f equals the identity of the domain, and the second projection applied to Γ_f is equal to f.
To draw a graph of a function.

graph antihole.gloss: The complement of a graph hole

graph directrix.gloss: A fixed straight line used to define and construct a parabola.

graph hole.gloss: A cycle, in a graph, that has no cycle chord

graph homomorphism.gloss: A mapping between two graphs that respects their structure.

graph minor.gloss: A graph which can be formed from some specified graph by performing vertex deletions, edge deletions, and edge contractions on the specified graph.

graph theorist.gloss: A mathematician or computer scientist who specializes in graph theory

graph theory.gloss: The branch of mathematics dealing with the properties of graphs (networks of vertices and edges).

graph toughness.gloss: A measure, expressed by a positive integer (with the exception of complete graphs), of the connectivity of a graph.

graph-theoretical.gloss: Relating to or using graph theory.

graph-theoretically.gloss: In a manner which uses graph theory
In the sense of graph theory

grapheme-phoneme correspondence.gloss: The relationship between graphemes and phonemes.

grapheme-to-phoneme.gloss: The task of converting graphemes into phonemes.

graphette.gloss: A generalisation of a (possibly disconnected) graphlet

graphical.gloss: Of, related to, or using graphics.

graphical user interface.gloss: A type of user interface which allows people to interact with a computer through a metaphor of direct manipulation of graphical images and widgets in addition to text.

graphician.gloss: A designer of graphics for computer software.

graphics.gloss: The pictorial representation and manipulation of data; the process by which a computer displays data.
The art or visual representations displayed by a computer.

graphics card.gloss: A circuit board that generates and controls the visual display on a computer screen.

graphics engine.gloss: Software engine in an application responsible for all functions pertaining to the graphics.

graphics processing unit.gloss: A specialized electronic circuit designed to accelerate the creation of images in a frame buffer intended for output to a display device.

graphics tablet.gloss: An input device that enables a user to draw images by hand, as if with a pencil, and import them into a computer system.

graphing calculator.gloss: A hand-held (usually programmable) electronic calculator which is capable of solving equations, plotting graphs and performing other tasks with variables.

graphlet.gloss: A small, connected, non-isomorphic, induced subgraph of a large network

graphoid.gloss: A matroid that has two collections of nonempty subsets called circuits and cocircuits such that the intersection of any circuit and cocircuit is not only the identity matroid, no circuit properly contains another circuit, no cocircuit properly contains another cocircuit, and for any painting of M that colors exactly one element green and the rest either red or blue there exists either a circuit containing the green element and no red elements or a cocircuit containing the green element and no blue elements.

A set of statements of the form, "X is irrelevant to Y given that we know Z" where X, Y and Z are sets of variables, which can be manipulated by a set of axioms concerning informational irrelevance and its graphical representation.

graphon.gloss: The completion of the metric space of the set of finite graphs endowed with the cut metric.

grassmann algebra.gloss: A direct sum with an exterior product of multivector spaces which are all based on a same underlying finite-dimensional vector space. The associative algebra of sums and exterior products of scalars, vectors, blades, multivectors, and hybrid (i.e., non-homogeneous) sums of multivectors of different grades.

grassmannian.gloss: A space which parameterizes all linear subspaces of a vector space of a given dimension.

gray hat.gloss: A hybrid between a white hat and a black hat hacker, who hacks for no personal gain, and does not have malicious intentions, but does sometimes commit crimes.

gray out.gloss: To make (a visual element) gray or lighter in colour to indicate that it is disabled or unavailable.

great bit bucket in the sky.gloss: Synonym of bit bucket (“notional resting place of lost or missing digital information”).

great circle.gloss: A circle defined as the intersection of the surface of a sphere and a plane which passes through the centre of the sphere.

great cubicuboctahedron.gloss: A nonconvex uniform polyhedron that has faces of eight triangles, six squares and six octagrams

great dodecahedron.gloss: A Kepler solid, with the Schläfli symbol {5,5/2}.

great icosahedron.gloss: One of four Kepler-Poinsot polyhedra with Schläfli symbol {3,5⁄2}.

great icosihemidodecahedron.gloss: A polyhedron having 26 faces, 30 vertices, 60 edges, six self-intersected faces, and six nonconvex faces.

great rhombicuboctahedron.gloss: An Archimedean solid that is isogonal and has twenty-six regular faces (twelve square, eight hexagonal and six octagonal).

great-circle arc.gloss: a segment of a great circle

greatest common divisor.gloss: The largest positive integer (respectively polynomial, element of a given ring) that is a divisor of each of a given set of integers (respectively polynomials, elements of a given ring).

greedoid.gloss: A particular type of set system.

greedy.gloss: That tries to find the global optimum by finding the local optimum at each stage.

greedy property.gloss: The property of being globally solvable optimally by making optimal decisions locally.

greek.gloss: To display a placeholder (instead of text), especially to optimize speed in displaying text that would be too small to read.
To fill a template with nonsense text (particularly the Lorem ipsum), so that form can be focused on instead of content.

greeking.gloss: Nonsense text or graphics inserted into a document as a placeholder to create a dummy layout, or to demonstrate a type font; the practice of using such placeholder text or graphics.

green thread.gloss: A thread of execution that is scheduled by a virtual machine, not natively by the underlying operating system.

green's function.gloss: a type of function used in the analysis of inhomogeneous differential equations.

greenfield.gloss: Of a completely new development, without the need to integrate with legacy systems, etc.

greets.gloss: Greetings sent to other demosceners, often included in the scrolltext of a demo.

grep.gloss: To use a program such as grep to search in a file.

greppable.gloss: In a format suitable for searching with the program grep; able to be grepped.

grey-box testing.gloss: A combination of black-box testing and white-box testing, where knowledge about the internal data structures and algorithms is used to design tests while executing those tests at the user, or black-box, level.

greyware.gloss: Software that is not outright malicious but is generally undesirable or annoying, such as adware.

grid.gloss: A system or structure of distributed computers working mostly on a peer-to-peer basis, used mainly to solve single and complex scientific or technical problems or to process data at high speeds (as in clusters).

grid method.gloss: A visual approach to the multiplication of polynomials through the use of a grid-like structure to represent the multiplicand terms

gridline.gloss: A line that forms part of a grid.

gridpoint.gloss: Any point in the Cartesian plane with integer coordinates.

grille.gloss: A rectangular stencil allowing words to be written, then read, through its apertures, with the text further disguised by filling the remaining space with irrelevant words.

grim trigger.gloss: A strategy that always cooperates as long as the opponent does not defect, in which case thereafter the strategy always defects.

grind.gloss: To automatically format and indent code.

grip.gloss: A visual component on a window etc. enabling it to be resized and/or moved by dragging with a mouse or finger.

gripper.gloss: A visual component on a window etc. enabling it to be resized and/or moved.

groin.gloss: The surface formed by two such vaults.

gromov-witten invariant.gloss: A rational number that, in certain situations, counts pseudoholomorphic curves meeting prescribed conditions in a given symplectic manifold. They have applications in string theory.

gronk.gloss: Of a floppy disk drive: to produce mechanical sounds of operation.
To fail; to crash or go wrong.

groom.gloss: In agile software development, to review and prioritize the items in the development backlog.

grooming.gloss: In agile software development, the reviewing and prioritization of items in the development backlog.

grossone.gloss: A proposed form of integer notation that would be able to handle arithmetic of infinities

grothendieck group.gloss: An abelian group constructed from a commutative monoid in a universal way.

grothendieck topology.gloss: A structure on a category which makes the category's objects act like the open sets of a topological space.

grothendieck universe.gloss: A kind of universal set whose elements follow the rules of Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory, and for which, with respect to an arbitrary set, an instance of its kind which has that set as a member may be posited to exist through an additional Tarski–Grothendieck axiom (which is not part of ZF but augments it, yielding Tarski–Grothendieck set theory).

groud.gloss: A heap, or mathematical generalization of a group, in abstract algebra.

ground set.gloss: The underlying set of mathematical structures such as posets and matroids.

ground truthing.gloss: In machine learning, the process of gathering objective (provable) data in order to test the system.

groundset.gloss: A vector space upon which matroids may be paved

group.gloss: A set with an associative binary operation, under which there exists an identity element, and such that each element has an inverse.
An effective divisor on a curve.
A number of users with the same rights with respect to accession, modification, and execution of files, computers and peripherals.

group action.gloss: A mapping of a mathematical group to the permutations of an object that is compatible with the group operation.

group box.gloss: A rectangular control that can contain other controls, intended for grouping similar items visually.

group functor.gloss: A group object that is an object in a category of functors; a functor with certain properties that generalise the concept of group.

group object.gloss: Given a category C, any object X ∈ C on which morphisms are defined corresponding to the group theoretic concepts of a binary operation (called multiplication), identity and inverse, such that multiplication is associative and properties are satisfied that correspond to the existence of inverse elements and the identity element.

group of lie type.gloss: Usually, a finite group that is closely related to the group of rational points of a reductive linear algebraic group with values in a finite field.

group operation.gloss: A binary operation that combines two elements of a set to produce a third element in a group.

group ring.gloss: Given ring R with identity not equal to zero, and group G=g_1,g_2,...,g_n, the group ring RG has elements of the form a_1g_1+a_2g_2+...+a_ng_n (where a_i isin R) such that the sum of a_1g_1+a_2g_2+...+a_ng_n and b_1g_1+b_2g_2+...+b_ng_n is (a_1+b_1)g_1+(a_2+b_2)g_2+...+(a_n+b_n)g_n and the product is ∑ₖ₌₁ⁿ(∑_(g_ig_j=g_k)a_ib_j)g_k.

group scheme.gloss: A group object that is an object in a category of schemes; a scheme that has certain properties that generalise the concept of group.

grouplike.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a group.

groupoid.gloss: A magma: a set with a total binary operation.
A set with a partial binary operation that is associative and has identities and inverses.

groupware.gloss: software designed to be used collaboratively by multiple users on a network

growl.gloss: To send a user a message via the Growl software library.

grubbs' test.gloss: A statistical test for deciding whether a data point is an outlier.

grötzsch graph.gloss: A triangle-free graph with 11 vertices, 20 edges, chromatic number 4, and crossing number 5. It is a member of an infinite sequence of triangle-free graphs, each the Mycielskian of the previous graph in the sequence.

gskew.gloss: A form of branch predictor that implements multiple prediction mechanisms with different indexing functions.

guard.gloss: A Boolean expression that must evaluate to true for a branch of program execution to continue.

guard band.gloss: A virtual area of the screen, bordering the real screen, to which any rendering is ignored, used to simplify clipping.

guardrailed.gloss: Of an automated process, script, language model application, or algorithmic framework: restricted to operate strictly within predefined policy boundaries, scopes, or execution parameters to eliminate operational failures.

guest.gloss: A user given temporary access to a system despite not having an account of their own.

guilt by association.gloss: A fallacy where a person or idea is judged guilty or discredited solely due to their connection to someone or something that is viewed negatively, rather than based on their own merits or actions.

guiltware.gloss: Software that attempts to convince the user to fulfil some obligation (such as registration or donation to a charity) by eliciting feelings of guilt.

gulp.gloss: An unspecified small number of bytes, often two.

gumbel distribution.gloss: A model of the distribution of the maximum (or the minimum) of a number of samples of various distributions.

gun.gloss: A pattern that "fires" out other patterns.

gunter's line.gloss: A logarithmic line on a Gunter's scale, which is used to perform the multiplication and division of numbers mechanically with only dividers.

gunzip.gloss: To decompress using the gzip program.

gweep.gloss: To work on a minicomputer late at night.
A nighttime hacker on early minicomputers.

gyroaverage.gloss: The average over a gyroperiod; a gyrophase average.

gyrobicupola.gloss: A bicupola in which the bases have the opposite orientation.

gyrobirotunda.gloss: A birotunda in which the bases have the opposite orientation.

gyrocenter.gloss: The center of an object in gyrovector space.

gyrocircle.gloss: A hyperbolic circle in gyrovector space.

gyrocommutative.gloss: Whose binary operation obeys a ⊕ b = gyr[a, b](b ⊕ a).

gyrocupolarotunda.gloss: A cupolarotunda in which the bases have the opposite orientation.

gyroelongated.gloss: Of a polyhedron, having been elongated by placing an antiprism in the middle of the polyhedron.

gyrogroup.gloss: A groupoid whose binary operation satisfies certain axioms, used with gyrovectors.

gyroid.gloss: An infinitely connected periodic minimal surface containing no straight lines.

gyroparallelogram.gloss: A hyperbolic quadrilateral whose two gyrodiagonals intersect at their gyromidpoints, analogous to a parallelogram in Euclidean space.

gyrotrigonometry.gloss: The use of gyroconcepts to study hyperbolic triangles.

gyrovector.gloss: A type of vector for which addition is defined by a formula that satisfies the axioms for a gyrogroup.

gzip.gloss: To compress using the gzip program.

gödel number.gloss: A number uniquely assigned to each symbol, and to each well-formed formula of some formal language.

gödel numbering.gloss: A function assigning a Gödel number to each well-formed formula of some formal language.

gödel sentence.gloss: An arithmetic statement that can be metatheoretically shown to not be provable or refutable in a formal system.

gömböc.gloss: A convex shape which, if made of a uniformly dense material, has one stable equilibrium orientation and one unstable equilibrium orientation.

h-space.gloss: A topological space X (generally assumed to be connected) together with a continuous map μ : X × X → X with an identity element e such that μ(e, x) = μ(x, e) = x for all x in X.

habtm.gloss: Acronym of has and belongs to many, a many-to-many relationship in a database.

hack.gloss: To make a quick code change to patch a computer program, often one that, while being effective, is inelegant or makes the program harder to maintain.
To accomplish a difficult programming task.
To work with something on an intimately technical level.
To hack into; to gain unauthorized access to (a computer system, e.g., a website, or network) by manipulating code.
To gain unauthorized access to a computer or online account belonging to (a person or organisation).
An expedient, temporary solution, such as a small patch or change to code, meant to be replaced with a more elegant solution at a later date; a workaround.
A computer programmer who makes quick but inelegant changes to computer code to solve problems or add features.
A computer programmer, particularly a veteran or someone not immediately expected to be capable of programming.
An interesting technical achievement, particularly in computer programming.
The illegal accessing of a computer network.
A video game or any computer software that has been altered from its original state.

hack up.gloss: To quickly and simply create (a piece of code).

hackable.gloss: That can be hacked or broken into; insecure, vulnerable.

hackaround.gloss: A hacky workaround; an unattractive but expedient solution.

hackathon.gloss: An event where programmers and others meet for collaborative software development, usually over several days.

hackbot.gloss: A bot (automated user) designed to hack into a system.

hackday.gloss: The day when a hackathon is held.

hackee.gloss: The victim of a hacking attack; one whose computer system has been compromised.

hacker.gloss: Someone who hacks. One who is expert at programming and solving problems with a computer.

Someone who hacks. One who is expert at programming and solving problems with a computer. One who applies a novel method, shortcut, skill, or trick to something to increase ease, efficiency, or productivity.

hackerish.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a hacker (malicious user who breaks into computer systems).

hackery.gloss: The use of hacks (ingenious but inelegant techniques).

hacking.gloss: Playful solving of technical work that requires deep understanding, especially of a computer system.
Unauthorized attempts to bypass the security mechanisms of an information system or network.

hacking run.gloss: A hacking session extended long outside normal working times, especially one longer than 12 hours; sometimes an all-nighter.

hackintosh.gloss: A computer other than a Macintosh that has been configured to run the Macintosh operating system (OS X or macOS).

hackish.gloss: Using, or characterised by, hacks: poorly designed workarounds.

hackware.gloss: Software used for hacking (circumventing security measures).

hacky.gloss: Using, or characterised by, hacks: poorly designed workarounds.

hacoversed sine.gloss: The trigonometric function equal to half the coversed sine. Abbreviation: hacoversin

hadamard regularization.gloss: A method of regularizing divergent integrals by dropping some divergent terms and keeping the finite part.
