internet address.gloss: Any address that is used to identify a place or resource on the Internet, such as a URL, an IP address, or a domain name.

internetting.gloss: gerund of internet The act of entwining or linking things together so as to form a network; interconnecting, networking.
gerund of internet The act of connecting a computer, an electronic device, etc., into a computer network (in particular, the Internet).
gerund of internet The act of connecting multiple computer networks together; internetworking.
gerund of internet The act of using the Internet; specifically, searching for information using the Internet.

interning.gloss: Practice of always using references instead of copies of equal objects.

interoperable.gloss: (of a system or device) Able to communicate, and exchange data with another system or device.

interoperate.gloss: To work reliably with another system.

interpenetrative.gloss: Mutually penetrative (overlapping each other in space)

interpolant.gloss: A function used to generate interpolation

interpolary.gloss: Relating to, or by means of, interpolation.

interpolate.gloss: To estimate the value of a function between two tabulated points.
During the course of processing some data, and in response to a directive in that data, to fetch data from a different source and process it in-line along with the original data.

interpolation.gloss: The process of estimating the value of a function at a point from its values at nearby points.
The process of interpolating: including and processing externally-fetched data in a document or program.

interpret.gloss: To analyse or execute (a program) by reading the instructions as they are encountered, rather than compiling in advance.

interpretation.gloss: An assignment of a truth value to each propositional symbol of a propositional calculus.

interpreted.gloss: Executed directly, rather than via a compiled binary representation.
qualifiers: of a programmign language or code

interpreter.gloss: A person or thing that interprets the meaning of something for another A machine that reads the pattern of holes on a punch card and prints its meaning along the top of the card.
A person or thing that interprets the meaning of something for another A program that converts commands into machine language in real time rather than compiling it in advance.

interprime.gloss: The mean of two consecutive odd primes

interprocess communication.gloss: A set of techniques for the exchange of data among two or more threads in one or more processes.

interquartile.gloss: Between quartiles. Specifically between the first and third quartiles.
The range or content of an interquartile.

interquartile range.gloss: The difference between the first and third quartiles; a robust measure of sample dispersion.

interreducible.gloss: Describing matrices that are mutually reducible

interrogate.gloss: To query (something); to request information from (something).

interrupt.gloss: To assert to (a computer) that an exceptional condition must be handled.
An event that causes a computer or other device to temporarily cease what it was doing and attend to a condition.

interrupt request.gloss: The act of interrupting any of several hardware processes in a computer.

intersect.gloss: Of two sets, to have at least one element in common.

intersection.gloss: The point or set of points common to two geometrical objects (such as the point where two lines meet or the line where two planes intersect).
The set containing all the elements that are common to two or more sets.
The pullback of a corner of monics.

intersphere.gloss: A sphere that is tangent to every edge of a given polyhedron.

intertwiner.gloss: A mapping between two equivariant maps

intertwingle.gloss: Of documents, information, etc.: to interconnect or interrelate in a complex way.

interval.gloss: A connected section of the real line which may be empty or have a length of zero.

interval variable.gloss: An ordinal variable with the additional property that the magnitudes of the differences between two values are meaningful.

intervalize.gloss: To cause to occur at regular time intervals.

intractable.gloss: Not able to be solved in polynomial time; too difficult to attempt to solve.

intraforest.gloss: Within a single forest (group of domains).

intraframe.gloss: A video frame that does not depend on any other frame for rendering, but simply presents a fixed image. Usually subject to spatial compression.

intranet.gloss: A private computer network, typically one that uses the protocols of the Internet.

intransitive.gloss: Of a set of dice: containing three dice A, B, and C, with the property that A rolls higher than B more than half the time, and B rolls higher than C more than half the time, but lacking the property that A rolls higher than C more than half the time. See intransitive dice and intransitive game.

intraobserver.gloss: Describing variation in the scores, responses etc obtained by the same observer on different occasions

intrinsic.gloss: A built-in function that is implemented directly by the compiler, without any intermediate call to a library.

intro.gloss: A small demo produced to promote one's demogroup or for a competition.

introspect.gloss: To examine by means of type introspection.

introspectability.gloss: The quality of being subject to introspection. The quality of supporting type introspection.

introspective sort.gloss: A sorting algorithm that begins with quicksort and switches to heapsort when the recursion depth exceeds a level based on (the logarithm of) the number of elements being sorted.

intrusive.gloss: Designating a type of collection in which each item keeps track of what collection it is in, rather than the more conventional approach of a collection keeping track of what items it contains. An intrusive collection does not "own" its contents and a single item can be part of multiple intrusive collections.

intuitionism.gloss: An approach to mathematics/logic which avoids proof by contradiction, and which requires that, in order to prove that something exists, one must construct it.

intuitionistic.gloss: Dealing strictly in constructive proofs, abstaining from proof by contradiction

intuitionistic logic.gloss: A type of logic which rejects the axiom law of excluded middle or, equivalently, the law of double negation and/or Peirce's law. It is the foundation of intuitionism.

invariant.gloss: Unaffected by a specified operation, especially by a transformation.

invariant section.gloss: A section that will not vary through changing state.
A property that does not change through a program's execution.

invariant theory.gloss: The branch of algebra concerned with actions of groups on algebraic varieties from the point of view of their effect on functions.

invariantly.gloss: In a manner that is invariant (without variation). In a manner that is invariant; unaffected by some operation.

inverse.gloss: Having the properties of an inverse; said with reference to any two operations, which, when both are performed in succession upon any quantity, reproduce that quantity.
That has the property of being an inverse (the result of a circle inversion of a given point or geometrical figure); that is constructed by circle inversion.
Whose every element has an inverse (morphism which is both a left inverse and a right inverse).
The result of an inversion A ratio etc. in which the antecedents and consequents are switched.
The result of an inversion The result of a circle inversion; the set of all such points; the curve described by such a set.
The result of an inversion The non-truth-preserving proposition constructed by negating both the premise and conclusion of an initially given proposition.

A second element which negates a first; in a binary operation, the element for which the binary operation—when applied to both it and an initially given element—yields the operation's identity element, specifically: The negative of a given number.

A second element which negates a first; in a binary operation, the element for which the binary operation—when applied to both it and an initially given element—yields the operation's identity element, specifically: One divided by a given number.

A second element which negates a first; in a binary operation, the element for which the binary operation—when applied to both it and an initially given element—yields the operation's identity element, specifically: A second function which, when combined with the initially given function, yields as its output any term inputted into the first function.
A morphism which is both a left inverse and a right inverse.

inverse fourier transform.gloss: A mathematical operation that transforms a function for a discrete or continuous spectrum into a function for the amplitude with the given spectrum; an inverse transform of the Fourier transform.

inverse function.gloss: For a given function f, another function, denoted f⁻¹, that reverses the mapping action of f; (formally) given a function f:X→Y, a function g:Y→X such that, ∀x∈X,f(x)=y⟹g(y)=x.

inverse limit.gloss: A subset of the Cartesian product of all the members of an inverse system, such that a member M of the subset is a sort of “cross section” of the inverse system (as fiber bundle) induced by the morphisms of it. (If i<j in the indexing poset then f_ij:A_j→A_i in the inverse system and if a_i∈A_i, a_j∈A_j are components of M then f_ij(a_j)=a_i).

inverse matrix.gloss: Of a matrix A, another matrix B such that A multiplied by B and B multiplied by A both equal the identity matrix.

inverse proportion.gloss: The property of being inversely proportional.

inverse semigroup.gloss: A semigroup in which every element x has an inverse y, such that x = xyx and y = yxy.

inverse system.gloss: A set of algebraic structures (which are part of a concrete category; e.g., groups) and a set of morphisms between them (e.g., group homomorphisms) which all together form a small category which is the image of a contravariant functor whose domain is a directed poset.

inverse trigonometric function.gloss: A function that is the inverse of an appropriate restriction of a trigonometric function.

inverse video.gloss: A display technique whereby background and foreground colours are interchanged, typically used for highlighting.

inversely proportional.gloss: Proportional to the reciprocal of the independent variable.

inversion.gloss: An operation on a group, analogous to negation.

inversion of control.gloss: Abstract principle describing an aspect of some software architecture designs in which the flow of control of a system is inverted in comparison to the traditional architecture, getting the flow of control from a generic code part.

inversion pair.gloss: a pair of integers (i,j) is an inversion pair of some permutation σ if iσ(j).

inversive geometry.gloss: The branch of geometry concerned with inversion transformations, specifically circle inversions in the Euclidean plane, but also as generalised in non-Euclidean and higher-dimensional spaces.

inverted index.gloss: An indexing algorithm which indexes a document based on the keywords being searched for.

invertible.gloss: Able to be inverted, having an inverse.

invertible matrix.gloss: Any n×n square matrix for which there exists a corresponding inverse matrix (i.e., a second (or possibly the same) matrix such that when the two are multiplied by each other, in either order, the result is the n×n identity matrix).

invex.gloss: Of a differentiable function f:ℝⁿ→ℝ, being such that there exists a vector valued function g such that f(x)-f(u)≥g(x,u)·∇f(u),, for all x and u.

invitro.gloss: An intro that provides details of a forthcoming demoparty to which viewers are invited.

invocation.gloss: The act of invoking, such as a function call.

invoke.gloss: To cause (a program or subroutine) to execute.

invoker.gloss: That which causes a program or subroutine to execute.

involutant.gloss: Given two matrices M, N of order w, the involutant is the resultant of the w² scalar equations obtained by equating to zero a linear function with scalar coefficients of the w² matrices which result from multiplying 1, m m², ... mʷ⁻¹ into 1, n, n², ... nʷ⁻¹.

involute.gloss: A curve that cuts all tangents of another curve at right angles; traced by a point on a string that unwinds from a curved object.

involution.gloss: An endofunction whose square is equal to the identity function; a function equal to its inverse.
A power: the result of raising one number to the power of another.

involutory.gloss: Of a mapping or transformation: being its own inverse; being an involution.
A linear transformation that is its own inverse, i.e., that has period two.

involve.gloss: To multiply (a number) by itself a given number of times; to raise to any assigned power.

iommu.gloss: Initialism of input–output memory management unit.

iosapic.gloss: Input/Output Streamlined Advanced Programmable Interrupt Controller.

iot.gloss: Initialism of index-organized table, a type of database's table where the data is stored in a B-tree index structure.
Initialism of input-output transfer, instructions for computers as in the PDP-8.
Initialism of interoperability testing, a process of testing to determine the interoperability of a software product.

ip.gloss: Initialism of insertion point (where text, etc. will be added in a document).

ip set.gloss: A set of natural numbers that contains all finite sums of some infinite set.

ip tracker.gloss: Software that converts an IP address into a hostname and provides location and other information.

ipa.gloss: A kind of archive containing a software package for certain Apple devices. Originally an initialism of iPhone Archive, later redefined as iOS App Store Package.

irrational.gloss: Of a real number, that cannot be written as the ratio of two integers.
A real number that can not be expressed as the quotient of two integers, an irrational number.

irrational number.gloss: Any real number that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers.

irrationality.gloss: The quality or state of being irrational. The property of being an irrational number.

irreducible.gloss: Unable to be factorized into polynomials of lower degree, as (x² + 1).
Whose numerator and denominator share no common factor greater than 1.
Unable to be factored into smaller integers; prime.
Whose only divisors are units and associates.
qualifiers: of an element of a ring

irreducible.gloss: Inexpressible as the union of two proper algebraic subvarieties.
Not containing a sphere of codimension 1 that is not the boundary of a ball.
Impossible to divide further into representations of lower dimension by means of any similarity transformation.

irreflexive.gloss: Of a binary relation R on X: such that no element of X is R-related to itself.

irregular.gloss: Of a polygon, not regular; having sides that are not equal or angles that are not equal.
Of a polyhedron, whose faces are not all regular polygons (or are not equally inclined to each other).

irregular prime.gloss: Any odd prime number that is not a regular prime.

irregular prism.gloss: a prism whose cross section is an irregular polygon
a solid that is like a prism but whose cross section is not (necessarily) a polygon

irrotational field.gloss: A vector field that has a irrotational vector value at any point, i.e. one that has zero curl everywhere in the domain.

irrotational flow.gloss: A flow that at any point in time is a irrotational field, i.e. one that has zero curl everywhere in the domain.

is-a.gloss: The relationship between two entities in which one entity inherits from the other.
Such a relationship expressed as an ontology component (regardless of whether the OOP paradigm per se is implemented).

iscii.gloss: Indian Script Code for Information Interchange

isms.gloss: Initialism of Information Security Management System.

isoaddition.gloss: The effect of the addition of two or more similar agents

isocapacitary.gloss: Having the same capacity; applied to the problem of finding an extremum for an integral over a space of a specified capacity.

isochron.gloss: A collection of points (such as a manifold), each point representing a set of initial conditions for a given dynamical system, such that every set results in the same long-term behaviour of the system.

isochronous.gloss: Of or pertaining to the use of clocks derived from the same clock reference.
Of or pertaining to data associated with time-sensitive applications.

isocline.gloss: A line, curve or function on a graph or map linking points with the same slope or gradient.

isocontour.gloss: level set; an isoline (2D) or isosurface (3D)

isocrystal.gloss: A kind of p-adic analogue of a sheaf.

isocrystalline.gloss: Of or pertaining to an isocrystal

isodynamic.gloss: In Euclidean geometry, being or relating to certain points associated with a triangle, with the properties that an inversion centered at one of these points transforms the given triangle into an equilateral triangle, and that the distances from the isodynamic point to the triangle vertices are inversely proportional to the opposite side lengths of the triangle.

isogeny.gloss: An epimorphism of group schemes that is surjective and has a finite kernel.

isohedral.gloss: Describing a polyhedron or a tiling all of whose faces are the same.

isolated.gloss: Minimal with respect to inclusion (among associated primes).
qualifiers: of an associated prime of a module

isolation.gloss: A database property that determines when and how changes made in one transaction are visible to other concurrent transactions.

isometric space.gloss: Either of two spaces between which an isometry exists.

isometry.gloss: A function between metric spaces (or on a single metric space) having the property that the distance between two images is equal to the distance between their preimages.

isomorphic.gloss: Related by an isomorphism; having a structure-preserving one-to-one correspondence.
Able to run either client-side or server-side.

isomorphism.gloss: A one-to-one correspondence a one-to-one correspondence between all the elements of two sets, e.g. the instances of two classes, or the records in two datasets.

A one-to-one correspondence A morphism which has a two-sided inverse; the composition of the morphism and such an inverse yields either one of two identity morphisms (depending on the order of composition).

isoparametric.gloss: Having the same parameters (under different coordinate systems)

isoperimeter.gloss: A figure that has the same perimeter as another

isoperimetric.gloss: Having the same perimeter; applied to the problem of finding a plane figure of the largest possible area whose boundary has a specified length

isophote.gloss: A contour of equal luminance in an image.

isoptic.gloss: The set of points for which two tangents of a given curve meet at a given angle.

isoradial.gloss: Of a planar graph: where each face is inscribable in a circle of common radius.

isosceles.gloss: Having (at least) two sides of equal length, used especially of a triangle or trapezoid.

isosceles triangle.gloss: A triangle having at least two sides equal.

isostick.gloss: A flash drive that can load ISO disk images into a computer.

isosurface.gloss: A surface that represents points of a constant value within a volume of space

isosynchronous.gloss: of a communications system in which the source and target are each synchronized but each transmission contains a start bit and a stop bit.

isotope.gloss: To define or demonstrate an isotopy of (one map with another).

isotopic.gloss: Of two presemifields 𝕊 and 𝕊' of characteristic p, when there exists three linear maps g_1, g_2, and g_3 from 𝕊 to 𝕊' such that g_1(x·y)=g_2(x)∘g_3(y) for all x,y∈𝕊.

isotopism.gloss: An instance of an isotopic state.

isotopy.gloss: A form of homotopy that is always an embedding.

isotoxal.gloss: That has symmetries which act transitively on its edges.

isotrivial.gloss: Describing a smooth projective surface having a morphism onto a curve such that all smooth fibres are isomorphic to each other

isotropic.gloss: Having the same components in all rotated coordinate systems

isotropy.gloss: The property of being identical, or having the same physical properties, in all directions.

isovariant.gloss: That commutes with the actions of a group on the domain and codomain, and preserves isotropy subgroups of elements that fix points in the domain and codomain.

isovector.gloss: A form of vector associated with isospin

isp.gloss: Initialism of Interface Segregation Principle, one of the five SOLID principles of programming.

issue tracking system.gloss: A software program that manages and maintains a list of issues.

isthmoid.gloss: A set of vertices of a graph after whose deletion the graph is no longer connected.

isthmus.gloss: An edge in a graph whose deletion increases the number of connected components of the graph.

isv.gloss: Initialism of independent software vendor (organization specializing in making and selling software; a software publisher)

it's not a bug, it's a feature.gloss: What one user may consider a software bug, other users may consider to be a useful feature or an intentional consequence of the system's design.

item set.gloss: A set of production rules which have an identical sequence of symbols between the right arrow (→) and the dot (•).

iterable.gloss: An object that can be iterated over.

iterate.gloss: To perform or repeat an action on each item in a set.
To perform or repeat an action on the results of each such prior action.
An n-fold self-composition of a function.
The image of a certain value under such a function.

iterated function system.gloss: A collection of transformations, which, when applied sequentially, can be used to construct a fractal. Formally: a finite set (or tuple) of contraction mappings on a complete metric space.

iterated integral.gloss: In multivariable calculus, the result of applying integrals to a function of more than one variable in such a way that each of the integrals considers some of the variables as given constants.

iteratee.gloss: In functional programming, a composable abstraction for incrementally processing sequentially-presented chunks of data in a purely functional fashion.

iteration.gloss: The use of repetition in a computer program, especially in the form of a loop.
A single repetition of the code within such a repetitive process.

iterative deepening search.gloss: A type of depth-first search in which each row of the tree is searched incrementally, simulating a breadth-first search with less memory usage.

iterative programming.gloss: A programming approach in which a process is executed by repeating a block of instructions until a stopping condition is met, typically using loop constructs such as for or while.

iterator.gloss: A method capable of performing the same action on every item in a collection.

iterator pattern.gloss: A behavioural design pattern that uses an iterator to traverse a container and access the container's elements, thus decoupling algorithms from containers.

ith.gloss: Occurring at position i in a sequence.

iverson bracket.gloss: A notation that denotes a number that is 1 if the condition in square brackets is satisfied, and 0 otherwise, i.e. (where P is a true or false statement)

iwahori-hecke algebra.gloss: A deformation of the group algebra of a Coxeter group.

i²c.gloss: Initialism of Inter-Integrated Circuit, a standard for integrated circuit communication using two lines.

j.gloss: An alternative version of i, the positive square root of -1; used in the context of electronics.
The second unit vector, after i

jaccard distance.gloss: A measure of dissimilarity between two sets.

jaccard index.gloss: A statistic for gauging the similarity and diversity of sample sets, based on the size of the intersection between the sets divided by the size of the union of the sets.

jack in.gloss: To insert an electronic coupling into a receptacle; to connect to something, whether involving a physical medium or not.

jackknife.gloss: A resampling method that applies estimators to all subsamples that each omit a single different group (possibly of a single datapoint) of the original sample to provide a sample distribution of the estimate.

jackson derivative.gloss: A q-analog of the ordinary derivative.

jackson integral.gloss: The series expansion ∫₀ᵃf(x),rm d_qx=(1-q),a∑ₖ₌₀ ᪲qᵏf(qᵏa). for real variable a and function of a real variable f(x).

jacob's ladder.gloss: A noncompact surface resembling a ladder made of handlebodies.

jacobi identity.gloss: Given a binary operation × defined on a set S which also has additive operation + and additive identity 0, the property that a × (b×c) + b × (c×a) + c × (a×b) = 0 for all a, b, c in S.

jacobi polynomial.gloss: Any member of a certain class of orthogonal polynomials.

jacobi symbol.gloss: A mathematical function of integer a and odd positive integer b, generally written (a/b), based on, for each of the prime factors pᵢ of b, whether a is a quadratic residue or nonresidue modulo pᵢ.

jacobian.gloss: A Jacobian matrix or its associated operator.
The determinant of such a matrix.

jacobian conjecture.gloss: A famous problem on polynomials in several variables.

jacobson radical.gloss: The operation that produces (from a given ring) the ideal of elements which annihilates all simple modules (over the given ring); the result of this operation. The Jacobson radical of a ring R is denoted J(R).

jagged.gloss: Of an array, having a different cardinality in each dimension, such that a representation on paper would appear uneven.

jagged array.gloss: An array of arrays in which the component arrays are of varying lengths.

jaggies.gloss: Jagged artifacts in raster graphics, such as those caused by resizing a bitmap image without preserving its aspect ratio.

jail.gloss: A kind of sandbox for running a guest operating system instance.

jailbreak.gloss: A modification to a closed platform's technical restrictions that enables installation or execution of software (or OS modification) the platform's original design was intended to prevent. Typical devices are iPhones and game consoles.
To modify the firmware of an electronic device, especially a mobile phone, in order to remove restrictions that prevent it from running unofficial software.

james-stein estimator.gloss: A particular estimator of the mean boldsymbol θ:=(θ₁,θ₂,…θₘ) for a multivariate random variable boldsymbol Y:=(Y_1,Y_2,…Y_m).

jank.gloss: Perceptible pause in the smooth rendering of a software application's user interface due to slow operations or poor interface design.

janky.gloss: Unresponsive (of a software application’s user interface), sluggish.

japh.gloss: A program written in Perl that outputs the text Just another Perl hacker, usually programmed in an obfuscated manner so that the output is not obvious until it is run.

jar hell.gloss: Problems with Java programs caused by incompatible versions of a JAR (Java archive).

javalike.gloss: Resembling the Java programming language or some aspect of it.

javascripted.gloss: Implemented in the JavaScript programming language.

javascripting.gloss: Programming in the JavaScript programming language.

jbod.gloss: Acronym of Just a Bunch of Disks, a collection of hard disks that are not configured according to RAID.
A hard disk enclosure for several disks, especially one lacking a RAID controller.

jefferson disk.gloss: Any of a set of stackable disks, each having the letters of the alphabet arranged in some sequence around its edge, used in a cipher system.

jeffreys prior.gloss: In Bayesian probability, a non-informative (objective) prior distribution for a parameter space; it is proportional to the square root of the determinant of the Fisher information matrix.

jellybean.gloss: of an electronic component, or software algorithm: generic, standard, vanilla, easy to find

jeos.gloss: Abbreviation of just enough operating system: one customised to the needs of a specific application, with other features excluded.

jet.gloss: an operation that takes a differentiable function f and produces a polynomial, the Taylor polynomial (truncated Taylor series) of f, at each point of its domain.

jeu de taquin.gloss: A construction that defines an equivalence relation on the set of skew standard Young tableaux.

jeu de taquin equivalent.gloss: Of tableaux: able to be transformed into each other by a sequence of jeu de taquin slides.

jeu de taquin slide.gloss: A transformation that moves around the numbers in a tableau according to the jeu de taquin construction, used to determine whether tableaux are equivalent.

jfif.gloss: Acronym of JPEG File Interchange Format.

jiffy.gloss: A unit of time defined by the frequency of its basic timer – historically, and by convention, 0.01 of a second, but some computer operating systems use other values.

jiggle mode.gloss: The editable state of a home screen, in which application icons, folders, and widgets oscillate to indicate that the user can rearrange or remove them.

jit.gloss: To perform a just-in-time operation (usually compiling).
To compile (program code for a virtual machine) immediately when needed, as part of the execution process.

jitter.gloss: A program or routine that performs jitting; a just-in-time compiler.

jmp.gloss: An unconditional jump, i.e., a transfer of the flow of program execution to a different point in the instruction stream without any conditions attached.

job.gloss: A task, or series of tasks, carried out in batch mode (especially on a mainframe computer).

job scheduler.gloss: A software application that is in charge of unattended background executions known for historical reasons as batch processing.

joblist.gloss: A list of tasks to be performed by the system.

jobname.gloss: The identifier assigned to a job by an operating system.

joe job.gloss: An act of e-mail spamming where the sender's identity and address are those of an innocent third party, intended either to tarnish that person's reputation or to flood that person's e-mail with bounces.

johnson solid.gloss: Any of a class of convex polyhedra that have regular faces but are not uniform (that is, not Platonic solids, Archimedean solids, prisms, or antiprisms).

join.gloss: To produce an intersection of data in two or more database tables.
An intersection of data in two or more database tables.
The act of joining something, such as a network.
The lowest upper bound, an operation between pairs of elements in a lattice, denoted by the symbol ∨.
The smallest linear space containing both of two given linear spaces.

join point.gloss: In aspect-oriented programming, a point at which advice (additional code) is triggered (a set of these constituting a pointcut).

joint entropy.gloss: The Shannon entropy of a "script" whose "characters" are elements of the Cartesian product of the sets of characters of the component scripts.

jones polynomial.gloss: A particular knot polynomial that is an invariant of an oriented knot or link which assigns to each oriented knot or link a Laurent polynomial in the variable t^(1/2) with integer coefficients.

jordan algebra.gloss: A non-associative algebra over a field whose product satisfies the axioms (i) xy=yx (the commutative law) and (ii) (xy)(xx)=x(y(xx)) (the Jordan identity).

jordan block.gloss: A Jordan block over a ring R (whose identities are the zero 0 and one 1) is a matrix composed of 0 elements everywhere except for the diagonal, which is filled with a fixed element λ ∈ R, and the superdiagonal, which is composed of ones.

jordan curve.gloss: A non-self-intersecting continuous loop in the plane; a simple closed curve.

jordan curve theorem.gloss: The theorem that states that a simple closed curve (Jordan curve) divides the plane into precisely two distinct areas.

jordan matrix.gloss: Any block diagonal matrix whose blocks are Jordan blocks.

jordanization.gloss: Conversion to, or representation as a Jordan curve.

jordanize.gloss: To convert to, or represent as a Jordan curve

journal.gloss: A chronological record of changes made to a database or other system; along with a backup or image copy that allows recovery after a failure or reinstatement to a previous time; a log.

journaling.gloss: The change log of the file system or database.

joyport.gloss: A port for connecting a joystick.

jpeg.gloss: An image using the JFIF image file format, containing an image compressed using JPEG compression.
To create or convert an image into a JPEG file.
To lossily compress an image file using the JPEG format with visible loss of quality.

jpegged.gloss: lossily compressed with the JPEG algorithm with visible loss of quality.

jsdk.gloss: Abbreviation of JavaServer Web Development Kit.

jsr.gloss: Initialism of Jump to Subroutine: (an assembler command).

jswdk.gloss: Abbreviation of JavaServer Web Development Kit.

jth.gloss: Occurring at position j in a sequence.

jtwi.gloss: Initialism of Java Technology for the Wireless Industry.

juice jacking.gloss: The act of stealing information from mobile devices by placing a data-stealing device that appears to be a charging station in a place where passers-by are likely to plug their devices into it.

jukebox.gloss: A software application capable of replaying tracks from a digital music collection.
An automated carousel for the storage and retrieval of tapes, CD-ROMs, etc.

julia set.gloss: In complex dynamics, a set consisting of values generated by a mathematical function such that an arbitrarily small perturbation can cause drastic changes in the sequence of iterated function values.

jumbo frame.gloss: An Ethernet frame with more than 1500 bytes of payload, the limit set by the IEEE 802.3 standard.

jumbogram.gloss: An Internet-layer packet exceeding the standard maximum transmission unit of the underlying network technology.

jump.gloss: To start executing code from a different location, rather than following the program counter.
A discontinuity in the graph of a function, where the function is continuous in a punctured interval of the discontinuity.
A change of the path of execution to a different location.

jump list.gloss: A kind of sorted linked list with additional pointers to connect data items that are various distances apart.
A pop-up list of tasks or documents associated with an application in the taskbar.

jump out.gloss: To emerge suddenly. To exit a loop, function, etc. ending its execution before it has reached its terminating condition.

jump point search.gloss: An optimization to the A* search algorithm for uniform-cost grids.

jump process.gloss: A type of stochastic process that has discrete movements, called jumps, with random arrival times, rather than continuous movement.

jump server.gloss: A hardened device on a network that spans two dissimilar security zones and provides a controlled means of access between them.

junction.gloss: A kind of symbolic link to a directory.
In the Raku programming language, a construct representing a composite of several values connected by an operator.

junction point.gloss: A kind of symbolic link to a directory.

junction table.gloss: A table whose rows represent connections between items in other tables.

junk email.gloss: Junk mail taking the form of email.

jurimetrics.gloss: The application of quantitative and statistical methods to law.

just-in-time.gloss: Taking place at the time when it is needed, and not in advance. Performing compilation of code on the client machine immediately before execution.

justifier.gloss: A machine, program or algorithm that justifies text by aligning it.

juxtaposition.gloss: The nearness of objects with little or no delimiter. An absence of operators in an expression.

jvm-specific.gloss: written specifically for the Java Virtual Machine

k.gloss: A kilobyte (more formally KB or kB).
A kilobit (more formally kb), especially in measuring Internet connection.
A single character message used as an acknowledgement (ACK), meaning "previous message received and understood."

k-adic.gloss: Of or pertaining to k-adic notation or the k-adic numbers.

k-adic notation.gloss: The bijective numeration of digits 1 through k inclusive that uses position in powers of k to encode an integer's expansion.

k-algebra.gloss: An algebra over a field; a ring with identity together with an injective ring homomorphism from a field, k, to the ring such that the image of the field is a subset of the center of the ring and such that the image of the field’s unity is the ring’s unity.

k-cell.gloss: A subset of k-dimensional Euclidean space which is obtained by taking the Cartesian product of k intervals (closed, open, or half-closed) which are subsets of the coordinate axes of the ambient Euclidean space.

k-d tree.gloss: A space-partitioning data structure for organizing points in a k-dimensional space, used in search algorithms etc.

k-function.gloss: A generalization of the hyperfactorial function in mathematics to real and complex numbers.

k-theory.gloss: The study of rings R generated by the set of vector bundles over some topological space or scheme;

The study of rings R generated by the set of vector bundles over some topological space or scheme;
(dated, obsolete) that part of algebraic topology comprising what is now called topological K-theory. that part of algebraic topology comprising what is now called topological K-theory.

kac-moody algebra.gloss: A Lie algebra, usually infinite-dimensional, that can be defined by generators and relations through a generalized Cartan matrix. They have applications in theoretical physics.

kakeya set.gloss: A set of points in Euclidean space that contains a unit line segment in every direction.

kaleidocycle.gloss: A flexible polyhedron connecting six tetrahedra (or disphenoids) on opposite edges into a cycle.

kan extension.gloss: A construct that generalizes the notion of extending a function's domain of definition.

kangaroo code.gloss: Poorly structured program code consisting of many jumps.

kap.gloss: Initialism of knowledge, attitude(s), and practice(s): a type of representative survey, originated in the 1950s, that examines the level of knowledge, beliefs, and behaviours of a population in the context of a specific topic.

kaprekar number.gloss: A non-negative integer, the representation of whose square in its base can be split into two parts that add up to itself (such as 297, whose square, 88209, can be split into 88 and 209, totalling 297).

karatsuba algorithm.gloss: A fast multiplication algorithm that reduces the multiplication of two n-digit numbers to at most n^(log ₂₃)≈n^(1.585) single-digit multiplications.

karatsuba multiplication.gloss: Multiplication by means of the Karatsuba algorithm.

karp reduction.gloss: A polynomial-time algorithm for transforming inputs to one problem into inputs to another problem, such that the transformed problem has the same output as the original.

kata.gloss: A short programming exercise to improve one's skills through practice and repetition.

kayles.gloss: A simple impartial game in combinatorial game theory, in which players take turns to knock out one pin or two adjacent pins from a line of imagined bowling pins.

kazhdan-lusztig polynomial.gloss: A member P_(y,w)(q) of a certain family of integral polynomials that are indexed by pairs of elements y, w of a Coxeter group W, which can in particular be the Weyl group of a Lie group.

kdd.gloss: Initialism of knowledge discovery in databases.

kebab.gloss: A menu icon of three vertical dots.

kebab button.gloss: A dropdown menu whose presence is indicated by a vertical ellipsis (⋮).

kebab case.gloss: The practice of writing identifiers using hyphens to separate words.

kebab icon.gloss: A dropdown menu whose presence is indicated by a vertical ellipsis (⋮).

kebab menu.gloss: A dropdown menu whose presence is indicated by a vertical ellipsis (⋮).

keith number.gloss: A repetitive Fibonacci-like integer which appears in a linear recurrence relation.

keller graph.gloss: Any of a certain family of graphs related to Keller's conjecture, such that the vertices of the Keller graph of dimension n are the 4ⁿ elements (m₁,...,mₙ) where each m is 0, 1, 2, or 3, and two vertices are joined by an edge if they differ in at least two coordinates and differ by exactly two in at least one coordinate.

kelly criterion.gloss: A formula used to determine the optimal size of a series of bets in order to maximize the logarithm of wealth.

kelvin function.gloss: Any of class of special functions, usually denoted as two pairs of functions berₙ(x), beiₙ(x), kerₙ(x) and keiₙ(x) with variable x and given order number n. The former two functions berₙ(x) and beiₙ(x) respectively correspond to the real part and the imaginary part of the Kelvin differential equation's solution that can be expressed with the Bessel function of the first kind Jₙ(x), and the latter kerₙ(x) and keiₙ(x) correspond to those that can be expressed with the modified Bessel function of the second kind Kₙ(x).

kempner series.gloss: A modification of the harmonic series, formed by omitting all terms whose denominator expressed in base 10 contains the digit 9.

kendall rank correlation coefficient.gloss: A measure of the ordinal association between two measured quantities.

kenotheme.gloss: An intersection of n hypersurfaces in an n-dimensional projective space

kepler solid.gloss: Any of several nonconvex regular polyhedra with regular pentagrammatic faces or vertex figures and which can be obtained by stellation of the dodecahedron or icosahedron.

keplerate.gloss: Any structure containing both Platonic and Archimedean solids, one inside the other.

kernel.gloss: The central part of many computer operating systems which manages the system's resources and the communication between hardware and software components.
The core engine of any complex software system.
The simplified input to an algorithm that has undergone kernelization.
A function used to define an integral transform.
The set of pairs of elements in the domain of f which are mapped to the same value; the equivalence relation x≡y⟺f(x)=f(y).

The set of elements of the domain of f which are mapped to an identity element. The set of elements of G which are mapped to the identity of H (usually written as 0 in an additive group and as 1 in a multiplicative group).
qualifiers: of a morphism f between algebraic structures

kernel.gloss: The set of elements of the domain of f which are mapped to an identity element. The set of elements of R which are mapped to the additive identity 0 of S.
qualifiers: of a morphism f between algebraic structures

kernel.gloss: The set of elements of the domain of f which are mapped to an identity element. The set of elements of M which are mapped to the additive identity 0 of N.
qualifiers: of a morphism f between algebraic structures

kernel.gloss: The equalizer of f and the zero morphism from X to Y, denoted operatorname kerf.
The equalizer of f and the zero morphism from X to Y, denoted operatorname kerf. The source of operatorname kerf, denoted operatorname Kerf.
The set of members of a fuzzy set that are fully included (i.e., whose grade of membership is 1).

kernel hacker.gloss: A developer who maintains the Linux kernel code.

kernel pair.gloss: A couple of morphisms which constitute the pullback of a given morphism along itself.

kernel panic.gloss: On Unix-derived operating systems, an action taken by the operating system when it cannot recover from a fatal error, where the system halts, displays an error, and dumps kernel memory to disk.

kernel space.gloss: The on-board RAM set aside specifically for kernel-related tasks.

kernelization.gloss: A technique for creating algorithms for fixed-parameter tractable problems, involving a preprocessing stage in which inputs to the algorithm are replaced by a smaller input, called a kernel.

kernelize.gloss: To produce, or to undergo kernelization

ket.gloss: A column vector, in Hilbert space, especially as representing the state of a quantum mechanical system; the complex conjugate transpose of a bra (a row vector); a ket vector. Symbolised by |...〉.

kettle lead.gloss: The similar-looking C13/C14 coupler lead, commonly used to power computer equipment.

kext.gloss: A loadable extension to the kernel of the macOS operating system.

key.gloss: An object designed to open and close a lock or to activate or deactivate something, especially a length of metal inserted into a narrow opening on the lock to which it is matched (keyed). A piece of information (e.g., a password or passphrase) used to encode or decode a message or messages.
Senses relating to a guide that identifies information. A value that uniquely identifies an entry in a container.
Senses relating to a guide that identifies information. In a relational database, a field used as an index into another table (not necessarily unique).
Senses relating to a set of features that modify the output of a device. One of several small, usually square buttons on a typewriter or computer keyboard, mostly corresponding to text characters.
Senses related to colors. A color to be masked or made transparent.
(more usually to key in) To enter (information) by typing on a keyboard or keypad.

key binding.gloss: A key or key combination configured to trigger an action when pressed.

key encapsulation mechanism.gloss: A mechanism for sharing a secret key securely between recipients, despite the presence of adversaries.

key exchange.gloss: An exchange of peers' keys at the initialization phase of connection.

key logger.gloss: Software or hardware designed to record keyboard entries, often for the purpose of stealing passwords or other sensitive data.

key off.gloss: To take something as a controlling input datum.

key set identifier.gloss: A value that is used to identify a key set.

key stretching.gloss: Techniques used to make a key more secure against brute force attacks by increasing the resources needed to test each possible key.

key-value.gloss: A pair consisting of a key (usually unique) and a value associated with the key.

keybit.gloss: A binary digit forming part of a cryptographic key.

keyboard.gloss: A set of keys laid out in a gridlike pattern, used for typing on a typewriter, computer, etc.

keyboard shortcut.gloss: A key, or more usually a combination of keys, on the keyboard of a personal computer that activates a specific, predefined function; a press (pressing) of such key(s).

keyboardable.gloss: Usable with a keyboard as the only input device.

keybounce.gloss: Multiple recorded keystrokes from a single press of a key on a computer keyboard due to poor electrical contact.

keychain.gloss: A digital repository for the storage of cryptographic keys.

keyclick.gloss: The sound produced by a keypress.

keycode.gloss: A code that represents a keypress.

keyfile.gloss: A file that contains encryption or license keys

keyframe.gloss: A complete video frame, used as a reference for subsequent interframes in video compression.

keygen.gloss: A small program used to generate a license key used to unlock a trial version of software illegitimately.

keyholder.gloss: One who or a device or component which holds a key for security reasons. An individual or organization with access to a cryptographic key.

keyholding.gloss: That stores or holds a cryptographic key.

keylock.gloss: A physical lock on the case of a computer, preventing use of the keyboard until unlocked.

keylogging.gloss: The logging of keystrokes, as with a key logger

keymapping.gloss: A mapping of keys on a keyboard to commands; a key binding.

keymask.gloss: A bitmask specifying which keypresses were made.

keyness.gloss: The statistical significance of a keyword's frequency in a given corpus, relative to a reference corpus.

keypair.gloss: A public key and its associated private key (in public-key cryptography).

keypath.gloss: A path to a file or other component that is critical to the installation of a given program.

keyphrase.gloss: A phrase used in encryption as a key, like a single keyword (password).

keypress.gloss: The buffered electrical signal resulting from such an event, sometimes distinguished from the release.

keypunch.gloss: A mechanical device whose keys are pressed, individually or in combination, to punch holes in punched cards or paper tape that correspond to particular characters.
An electric machine with a keyboard that has the same function.

keyring.gloss: A set of data holding linked encryption keys.

keyscan.gloss: The process of scanning the state of a keyboard to determine which keys are being pressed.

keyserver.gloss: In public key cryptography, the server that stores and distributes the public key files.

keyset.gloss: An input device whose few keys can be pressed in many combinations, often simultaneously, to enter different commands or characters.
A set of keys (unique identifiers) used to distinguish the rows of data being traversed by a cursor.

keysigning.gloss: The process of digitally signing someone else's public key using one's own.

keyspace.gloss: The notional space that contains all possible cryptographic keys.
A NoSQL object that includes column families.

keystore.gloss: A storage area for cryptographic keys.

keystream.gloss: A stream of random or pseudorandom characters that are combined with the plaintext to produce a ciphertext.

keystring.gloss: Any string of characters that has key (high) importance, such as a keyword or a keyphrase, but not necessarily a word in all senses of that term (as for example a phone number, an alphanumeric or numeric sequence, or string of symbols).

keystrip.gloss: A physical overlay for a computer keyboard, indicating the functions of certain keys within a particular software package.

keyswitch.gloss: A mechanical switch associated with a key on a keyboard.

keyword.gloss: Any word used as the key to a code.
Any word used in a reference work to link to other words or other information.
Any important word in a text or document, which may be linked to other words or other information, or listed in the metadata for searches to find.
A reserved word used to identify a specific command, function, etc.

kezboard.gloss: A computer keyboard whose keys are arranged in the qwertz layout.

khovanov homology.gloss: An oriented link invariant that arises as the homology of a chain complex. It may be regarded as a categorification of the Jones polynomial.

kibibit.gloss: Strictly, 2¹⁰ (1,024) bits, as opposed to a kilobit.

kibibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2¹⁰ (1,024) bytes, as opposed to a kilobyte.

kick.gloss: The act of restarting or resetting a watchdog timer.

kidnapped robot problem.gloss: The situation where an autonomous robot is carried somewhere and as a result has trouble determining its own location.

kill.gloss: To cause to assume the value zero.
To disconnect (a user) involuntarily from the network.

killbit.gloss: A setting that disables a specific web browser plug-in, typically to prevent a security vulnerability from being exploited.

killer poke.gloss: Any method of inducing physical harm to a computer or peripheral by software means, especially by inserting invalid values into a control register or by building up harmonic oscillations in a hard disk, etc.

killing field.gloss: A vector field on a Riemannian manifold (or pseudo-Riemannian manifold) that preserves the metric.

killing form.gloss: A symmetric bilinear form that plays a basic role in the theories of Lie groups and Lie algebras.

killing horizon.gloss: A geometrical construct used in general relativity and its generalizations to delineate spacetime boundaries without reference to the dynamic Einstein field equations.

kilobinary.gloss: Relating to the units prefixed kibi-, such as the kibibyte as opposed to the kilobyte.

kiloflop.gloss: A unit of computing power equal to 1,000 floating point operations per second

kiloword.gloss: A unit of storage capacity, equal to 1000 words.

kindless.gloss: Having no specific kind, unspecified, general.

kinetostatic.gloss: Relating to a pair of opposing kinematic vectors

king.gloss: A vertex in a directed graph which can reach every other vertex via a path with a length of at most 2.

kingmaker.gloss: A player who is unable to win but powerful enough to decide which of the other viable players will eventually win.

kink.gloss: A positive 1-soliton solution to the sine-Gordon equation.

kips.gloss: Abbreviation of thousand instructions per second.

kirby calculus.gloss: A method in geometric topology for modifying framed links in the 3-sphere using a finite set of moves (the Kirby moves).

kirby move.gloss: Any of the moves used in the Kirby calculus for modifying framed links in the 3-sphere.

kisrhombille.gloss: A uniform tiling of rhombic faces divided by central points into four triangles.

kissing number.gloss: For a given space, the maximum number of non-overlapping unit spheres that can be arranged in that space such that they each touch a common unit sphere.

kit.gloss: A full software distribution, as opposed to a patch or upgrade.

kitchen sink regression.gloss: A statistical regression which uses many possible independent variables to attempt to explain variance in a dependent variable.

kitchen table software.gloss: A set of computer programs developed by an entrepreneurial advanced amateur or self-employed professional computer programmer in their own home; software developed by a small business using the services of such programmers.

kite.gloss: A polygon resembling the shape of a traditional toy kite (sense 3): a quadrilateral having two pairs of edges of equal length, the edges of each pair touching each other at one end.

kleene algebra.gloss: A De Morgan algebra which also satisfies the inequation x∧∼x⩽y,∨∼y for all x and y, where "∼" here denotes the De Morgan involution.

kleene closure.gloss: The set of all strings of finite length made up of elements of a given set. (Then the Kleene closure is said to be of that given set. For a given set S, its Kleene closure may be denoted as S^*. The Kleene closure includes a string of zero length. Strings are equivalent to ordered tuples but written without the parentheses and commas.)

kleene plus.gloss: The plus symbol, +, used as an operator to concatenate one or more strings from a given set, widely used in regular expressions.

kleene star.gloss: The asterisk, *, used as an operator to concatenate zero or more strings from a given set, widely used in regular expressions.

kleenex testing.gloss: Software testing carried out with people who have never before seen or used the software.

klein bottle.gloss: The closed manifold obtained by identifying the boundary components of the annulus so that the resultant surface is nonorientable.

klein quadric.gloss: The lines of a 3-dimensional projective space, S, can be viewed as points of a 5-dimensional projective space, T. In that 5-space, the points that represent each line in S lie on a hyperbolic quadric, Q, known as the Klein quadric.

kleisli category.gloss: A category naturally associated to any monad T, and equivalent to the category of free T-algebras.

kloc.gloss: Abbreviation of thousand lines of code.

kludge.gloss: An amalgamated mass of unrelated parts.
A badly written or makeshift piece of software; a hack.

klunker.gloss: Alternative spelling of clunker; a dilapidated, worn-out, or noisy machine. An old, slow, or decrepit computer; a clunker.

knapsack.gloss: A set of values from which a subset is chosen.

kneser graph.gloss: A graph K(n, k) (alternatively KG_(n,k)), whose vertices correspond to the k-element subsets of a set of n elements, and where two vertices are adjacent iff the two corresponding sets are disjoint.

knightship.gloss: A spaceship, in a cellular automaton, which moves knightwise (i.e., moving two spaces along the x-axis for every space it moves along the y-axis [or vice versa], in the manner of a chess knight); a spaceship which moves with slope 2; a (2,1) spaceship.

knot.gloss: A non-self-intersecting closed curve in (e.g., three-dimensional) space that is an abstraction of a knot (in sense 1 above).

knot diagram.gloss: A representation in the plane of a knot, with no triple points.

knot theory.gloss: A branch of topology dealing with knots.

knowbot.gloss: a bot that roams a distributive network (especially the Internet) to gather or distribute information

knowledge graph.gloss: A knowledge base with an interlinked graph structure.

knowledge mining.gloss: An emerging discipline in artificial intelligence that uses a combination of intelligent services to quickly learn from large amounts of information.

known.gloss: A constant or variable the value of which is already determined.

known-plaintext attack.gloss: An attack on a cryptosystem that relies on the attacker's knowledge of not just some ciphertexts encrypted with that system and key, but also their corresponding plaintexts (cribs). More powerful than a ciphertext-only attack, but less powerful than a chosen-plaintext attack.

knuthian.gloss: Of or relating to the work, or theory developed from the work, of American computer scientist and mathematician Donald Knuth.

kochanek-bartels spline.gloss: A cubic Hermite spline with tension, bias and continuity parameters defined to change the behavior of the tangents.

kolakoski sequence.gloss: An infinite sequence of symbols {1,2} that is its own run-length encoding and the prototype for an infinite family of related sequences.

kolmogorov complexity.gloss: The complexity of an information object—such as a book or an image—informally defined as the length of the shortest program that produces that information object as output.

kolmogorov space.gloss: A topological space for which any pair of distinct points are also topologically distinct, i.e., there is an open set which contains one of the points but not the other one.

koszul duality.gloss: Any of various kinds of duality found in representation theory of Lie algebras, abstract algebras, and topology.

kriging.gloss: A regression technique used to interpolate data.

kripke frame.gloss: A set, whose elements are called nodes or worlds, together with a preordering relation for that set, called its accessibility relation.

kripke model.gloss: A Kripke frame together with any one of the following: (1) a function associating each of the frame's worlds to a set of prime formulae which are "true" for the given world, (2) a function associating each prime formula to a set of worlds for which the prime formula is "true", (3) a forcing relation between worlds and prime formulae. Additionally, there is a set of rules for deducing (from the given function or relation) what formulae are forced to be true by a given world. (The set of rules depends on which logic the Kripke model is being applied to, whether one of several modal logics or intuitionistic logic). For intuitionistic logic the forcing relation satisfies a persistence relation, namely, if world w forces proposition p, then all worlds accessible from w also force p.

kronecker delta.gloss: A binary function, written as δ with two subscripts, which evaluates to 1 when its arguments are equal, and 0 otherwise.
A unary function, written as δ with a single index, which evaluates to 1 at zero, and 0 elsewhere.

kronecker product.gloss: The ⊗ operation (the tensor product) when applied to two matrices.

kronecker symbol.gloss: (a/n) or (a|n), a generalization of the Jacobi symbol to all integers n.

kth.gloss: Occurring at position k in a sequence.

kube.gloss: An individual container of the Kubernetes orchestration system.

kummer ring.gloss: A ring obtained by adjoining a non-real complex pᵗʰ root of unity (where p is a prime number) to the ring of integers.

kummer surface.gloss: The Kummer variety of a two-dimensional abelian variety.

kummer variety.gloss: For a given abelian variety: its quotient by the map taking any element to its inverse.

kung fu.gloss: A mastery of or expertise in a skill A mastery of or expertise in computer programming, hacking, or cracking

kurepa tree.gloss: A tree (T, <) of height ω₁, each of whose levels is at most countable, and has at least ℵ₂ branches.

kurtosis.gloss: A measure of "heaviness of the tails" of a probability distribution, defined as the fourth cumulant divided by the square of the variance of the probability distribution.
Excess kurtosis: the difference between a given distribution's kurtosis and the kurtosis of a normal distribution.

kvm.gloss: Initialism of keyboard-video-mouse: a device allowing these input and output devices to be swapped between a series of server consoles, especially in a rack configuration.
Initialism of kilobyte virtual machine: a virtual machine derived from the Java virtual machine specification, written for small devices with limited memory.
Initialism of kernel-based virtual machine: a virtualization infrastructure for the Linux kernel that turns it into a hypervisor.

kwips.gloss: Initialism of kilo Whetstone instructions per second.

l-estimator.gloss: Any estimator that is a linear combination of order statistics of the measurements.

l-fuzzy.gloss: Relating to a generalized variant of the notion of fuzzy sets, with membership functions taking values in a (fixed or variable) algebra or structure L of a given kind, usually at least a poset or lattice.

l1.gloss: Short for first level in various contexts. The first-level cache of a processor, closer to the processor than the second-level cache.
Short for first level in various contexts. The physical layer in the seven-layer OSI network model.

l2.gloss: Short for second level in various contexts The second-level cache of a processor, farther away from the processor than the first level cache.
Short for second level in various contexts The data link layer in the seven layer OSI network model.

l3.gloss: Short for third level in various contexts The third-level cache of a processor, farther away from the processor than the second-level cache.
Short for third level in various contexts The network layer in the seven-layer OSI network model.

label.gloss: A user-defined alias for a numerical designation, the reverse of an enumeration.
A named place in source code that can be jumped to using a GOTO or equivalent construct.
A non-interactive control or widget displaying text, often used to describe the purpose of another control.

laceable.gloss: Of a bipartite graph: having a possible Hamiltonian path between any two vertices from different partite sets.

lacunary.gloss: Of, pertaining to, or having characteristics of a lacuna.

lacunary function.gloss: A function defined by a lacunary series, especially one which cannot be analytically continued outside its domain of convergence.

lacunary series.gloss: A series with arbitrarily large gaps between nonzero terms, usually a power series or trigonometric series.

ladder logic.gloss: A technique for describing and drawing electrical logic schematics.

ladder operator.gloss: An operator that either increases or decreases the eigenvalue of another operator.

ladderize.gloss: to sort the nodes of a tree graph on one level by the count of their subnodes (on all levels under the node)

lag time.gloss: The time delay (latency) between the action of the user and the reaction of the server supporting the task, which requires resending to the client.

lagfest.gloss: Something prone to lagging, or network delays.

laggy.gloss: Tending to lag, or respond slowly because of network latency.

lagrange polynomial.gloss: For a given set of points (x_j,y_j) with no two x_j values equal, the polynomial of lowest degree that assumes at each value x_j the corresponding value y_j, so that the functions coincide at each point.

lagrange's equations.gloss: A set of equations of motion of a mechanical system which relate the kinetic energy of the system to its generalized coordinates.

lagrange's interpolation formula.gloss: A formula which when given a set of n points (x_i,y_i), gives back the unique polynomial of degree (at most) n − 1 in one variable which describes a function passing through those points. The formula is a sum of products, like so: ∑ᵢⁿy_i∏_(j ne i)x-x_j/x_i-x_j. When x=x_i then all terms in the sum other than the iᵗʰ contain a factor x-x_i in the numerator, which becomes equal to zero, thus all terms in the sum other than the iᵗʰ vanish, and the iᵗʰ term has factors x_i-x_j both in the numerator and denominator, which simplify to yield 1, thus the polynomial should return y_i as the function of x_i for any i in the set 1,...,n.

lagrange's theorem.gloss: The theorem in group theory that for any finite group, the size (order) of any subgroup must be a divisor of that of the group itself.

lagrangian function.gloss: A function of the generalized coordinates and velocities of a dynamic system from which Lagrange's equations may be derived.

laguerre polynomial.gloss: A polynomial that is a solution to Laguerre's equation.

lah number.gloss: Any of a class of coefficients expressing rising factorials in terms of falling factorials.

lake of wada.gloss: Any of three disjoint connected open sets of the plane or open unit square with the counterintuitive property that they all have the same boundary.

lambda abstraction.gloss: A lambda term of the form (λx.t) where x is a variable and t another lambda term. Any free instance of x within t (considered by itself) then becomes bound by the λx. prefix. It is meant to represent an anonymous function.

lambda calculus.gloss: Any of a family of functionally complete algebraic systems in which lambda expressions are evaluated according to a fixed set of rules to produce values, which may themselves be lambda expressions.

lambda function.gloss: An anonymous function; a function that is defined in an inline, ad-hoc manner, and often doesn't have a name (not bound to an identifier).

lambda term.gloss: A well-formed formula in the language of a lambda calculus.

lambert series.gloss: A series taking the form S(q)=∑ₙ₌₁ ᪲a_n(qⁿ)/(1-qⁿ).

latch.gloss: To use a latch (kind of lightweight lock).

lateral area.gloss: The sum of the areas of the lateral (vertical) faces of a cylinder, cone, frustum, or the like.

lateral surface.gloss: All of the sides of the object, excluding its base and top (when they exist).

lathe.gloss: To produce a three-dimensional model by rotating a set of points around a fixed axis.

latin square.gloss: An n-by-n arrangement of n different integers such that each row, each column and each of the two diagonals contains each of the integers once and once only.

latus rectum.gloss: The chord passing through a focus of a conic section, parallel to the directrix and terminated both ways by the curve. It is the parameter of the principal axis.

launder.gloss: To obtain a pointer to an object created in storage occupied by an existing object of the same type, even if it has const or reference members.

law.gloss: A rule, such as: A statement (of relation) that is true under specified conditions; a mathematical or logical rule.

lax pair.gloss: In the theory of integrable systems, a pair of time-dependent matrices or operators that satisfy a corresponding differential equation, called the Lax equation.

lectic.gloss: Pertaining to a generalization of alphabetical order applied to sets such that, for each pair of sets, their relative ordering is the order obtained if you remove their common (shared) elements and compare the last element in each remaining subset.

legendre transformation.gloss: Given a function f(x,y,z,...) which is concave up with respect to x (i.e., its second derivative with respect to x is greater than zero), an involutive procedure for replacing x with another variable, say p=∂f/∂x thus yielding another function, say F=F(p,y,z,...). This new function contains all of the information of the original f encoded, as it were, within it so that ∂F/∂p=x and applying a similar transformation to F yields the original f. The formula is: F(p,y,z,...)=p·x(p)-f(x(p),y,z,...) where x must be expressed as a function of p. (Note: The concave upwardness means that ∂f/∂x is monotonically increasing, which means that p as a function of x is invertible, so x should be expressible as a function of p.)

line graph.gloss: A graph L(G) which is derived from a given non-oriented graph G such that the vertices of L(G) represent edges of G and so that a clique in L(G) represents a common end-vertex shared by a set of represented edges. (A star subgraph in G transforms into a clique in L(G).)

A graph L(G) which is derived from a given non-oriented graph G such that the vertices of L(G) represent edges of G and so that a clique in L(G) represents a common end-vertex shared by a set of represented edges. (A star subgraph in G transforms into a clique in L(G).) A graph which is the line graph (in the above sense) of some other graph.

line integral.gloss: An integral whose integrand's domain is a curve.

line noise.gloss: Spurious characters due to signal noise in a communications link.
Data that looks random, as when outputting a binary file as text.
Incomprehensible source code or other textual material (often due to terseness or overuse of operators).

line number.gloss: The sequential number indicating a particular line of text in a text file.
A number included at the beginning of a line of source code, dictating the order of execution of instructions in the program.

line of best fit.gloss: A line on a scatter plot that best defines or expresses the trend shown in the plotted points. It is chosen so that the sum of the squares of the distances from the points to the line is a minimum. It also illustrates the correlation (positive, negative, or zero correlation) between the plotted variables.

line of centers.gloss: A line joining centers of figures.

line of striction.gloss: The line on a skew surface that cuts each generator in that point of it that is nearest to the succeeding generator.

line plot.gloss: A plotting of data above an axis to show frequency of data in each category.

line printer.gloss: A high-speed impact printer, most often used by older mainframes, that prints an entire line in a single operation.

line segment.gloss: A part of a straight line bounded by two points.

line slip.gloss: A variant form of a sphere packing in a cylinder, differing from the uniform structure in missing certain lines that represent contacts between spheres when diagrammed.

linear.gloss: (of polynomials or polynomial equations) Having degree one; that is, being of the form a_1x_1+a_2x_2+⋯+a_nx_n+b, where each x_i is a variable. See also Linear polynomials on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
(of polynomials or polynomial equations) Involving only linear polynomials. See also Linear equation on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

(of functions or maps) An additive, homogeneous mapping; that is, a function f:V→W is linear if it distributes over vector addition (f( mathbf v+ mathbf w)=f( mathbf v)+f( mathbf w)) and respects scalar multiplication (f(c mathbf v)=cf( mathbf v)). If V and W are vector spaces over a field K, f may also be called a K-linear map. See also linear map on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
qualifiers: of a function between vector spaces

linear.gloss: (of functions or maps) A module homomorphism; that is, a group homomorphism that commutes with scalar multiplication. See also Module homomorphism on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
qualifiers: of a function over a module

linear algebra.gloss: The branch of mathematics that deals with vectors, vector spaces, linear transformations and systems of linear equations.

linear algebraic group.gloss: An algebraic group that is isomorphic to a subgroup of some general linear group.

linear combination.gloss: a sum, each of whose summands is an appropriate vector times an appropriate scalar (or ring element)

linear congruential generator.gloss: An algorithm that yields a sequence of pseudo-randomized numbers calculated with a discontinuous piecewise linear equation.

linear dependence.gloss: The state of being linearly dependent
A linear relation between some appropriate things

linear equation.gloss: A polynomial equation of the first degree (such as x = 2y - 7)

linear function.gloss: Any function whose graph is a straight line: f(x)=ax+b

Any function whose value on the sum of two elements is the sum of the values of the function on the two elements and whose value on the product of a scalar times an element is the scalar times the value of the function on the element: f(ax+by)=af(x)+bf(y)

linear functional.gloss: A linear mapping from a vector space to its field of scalars.

linear group.gloss: Any group that is isomorphic to a matrix group.

linear independence.gloss: the state of being linearly independent

linear logic.gloss: A logic in which two structural rules are missing from its sequent calculus: those for weakening and contraction; which has some extra logical connectives, so that it has both "additive" and "multiplicative" versions of the typical binary connectives and truth constants; and which has a pair of modal, "exponential" operators for resource management, to help make up for the loss of the two structural rules.

linear operator.gloss: An operator L such that for functions f and g and scalar λ, L (f + g) = L f + L g and L λf = λ L f.

linear pair.gloss: The two supplementary adjacent angles formed by two intersecting lines

linear programming.gloss: The branch of mathematics concerned with the minimization or maximization of a linear function of several variables and inequalities; used in many branches of industry to minimize costs or maximize production.

linear regression.gloss: A linear equation for deriving a single predicted value from one or more known explanatory values.

linear span.gloss: A linear subspace generated by all linear combinations of a given subset of vectors of a given vector space.

linear subspace.gloss: A subset of vectors of a vector space which is closed under the addition and scalar multiplication of that vector space.

linear sum.gloss: A linear subspace which is the linear span of the union of two subspaces (of some vector space).

linear time.gloss: The time complexity, denoted O(n), of an algorithm whose running time increases at most linearly with the size of the input.

linear transformation.gloss: A map between vector spaces which preserves the operations of vector addition and scalar multiplication.

linear triplet.gloss: The three supplementary adjacent angles formed by three intersecting lines

linearithmic.gloss: Taking up to time proportional to n log(n) to run on inputs of size n.

linearity.gloss: A relationship between several quantities which can be considered as proportional and expressed in terms of linear algebra, or any mathematical property of a relationship, operation or function that is analogous to such proportionality, satisfying additivity and homogeneity.

linearization.gloss: A linear approximation of a non-linear system

linearly dependent.gloss: Having a nontrivial linear combination which is zero.
qualifiers: of a set of vectors or ring elements

linearly independent.gloss: Of a set of vectors or ring elements, whose nontrivial linear combinations are nonzero.

linemode.gloss: A mode of interaction with a remote server where all incoming text characters are printed to the current line, without the possibility of updating the text of previous lines.

lineoid.gloss: the set of points in 3-dimensional space that are also points in 4-dimensional space

linestring.gloss: A curve with linear interpolation between points, used in geographic information systems e.g. to represent streets and rivers.

link.gloss: The connection between buses or systems.
A space comprising one or more disjoint knots.
To combine objects generated by a compiler into a single executable.

link editor.gloss: A program that links modules together, by resolving calls or references to external names, to form a single executable program

link farm.gloss: A website containing many hyperlinks, especially one designed to increase the index ranking of other websites to search engines.

link state.gloss: A class of routing protocol based on sending local status updates to every node in the network.

link-dead.gloss: Of a character in a multi-user dungeon: stuck in a frozen state, but still visible to other players, as a result of sudden disconnection by the user without logging out.

link/cut tree.gloss: A data structure that represents a forest (a set of rooted trees) and allows dynamic updates on the tree in logarithmic time.

linkage.gloss: The act or result of linking: the combination of multiple object files into one executable, library, or object file.

linkage editor.gloss: A utility program that combines load modules (typically of subroutines) etc. to produce an executable program

linkage section.gloss: The part of the data division of a COBOL program that describes the format of variables and constants passed to the program as parameters, either from JCL or from a calling program

linked list.gloss: A simple linear data structure, each of whose nodes includes a pointer to the next (and sometimes previous) node in the list, enabling traversal of the structure in at least one direction from any starting point.

linker.gloss: A computer program that takes one or more objects generated by compilers and assembles them into a single executable program.

linking number.gloss: A numerical invariant that describes the linking of two closed curves in a three-dimensional space.

linkware.gloss: Digital materials that can be used for free on the condition that the user links back to the creator's web site.

linmodem.gloss: A softmodem designed to work with Linux operating systems.

lint.gloss: To perform a static check on (source code) to detect stylistic or programmatic errors.

linter.gloss: A program or algorithm that performs linting.

linting.gloss: The process of using a software tool to analyse source code and identify possible programming problems.

linux.gloss: Any unix-like operating system that uses the Linux kernel.

linuxism.gloss: Any feature specific to the Linux operating system (usually in comparison to other UNIX-like systems like BSD).

liouville number.gloss: An irrational number x with the property that, for every positive integer n, there exist integers p and q with q > 1 and such that 0<|x-p/q|<1/(qⁿ).

lipschitz condition.gloss: A property which can be said to be held by some point in the domain of a real-valued function if there exists a neighborhood of that point and a certain constant such that for any other point in that neighborhood, the absolute value of the difference of their function values is less than the product of the constant and the absolute value of the difference between the two points.

lipschitz constant.gloss: (Of a real-valued real function f) The smallest constant K such that whenever x_1 and x_2 are in the domain of f, |f(x_1)-f(x_2)|≤K|x_1-x_2|.

lipschitz continuity.gloss: The property of being Lipschitz continuous.

lipschitz continuous.gloss: (Of a real-valued real function f) Such that there exists a constant K such that whenever x_1 and x_2 are in the domain of f, |f(x_1)-f(x_2)|≤K|x_1-x_2|.

liquid state machine.gloss: A kind of reservoir computer that uses a spiking neural network with nodes randomly connected to each other.

lisper.gloss: A person who programs in Lisp.

lispish.gloss: Characteristic or reminiscent of the Lisp programming language.

lisplike.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of the programming language Lisp.
