lissajous figure.gloss: A plane curve traced by a point which executes two perpendicular independent harmonic motions, the frequencies of which are in a simple ratio.

list.gloss: A codified representation of a list used to store data or in processing; especially, in the Lisp programming language, a data structure consisting of a sequence of zero or more items.

list box.gloss: A GUI widget that allows the user to select one or more items from a list contained within a static, multiple line text box.

list-based programming.gloss: A coding paradigm where a programming language treats lists (or sequences of data) as its primary building blocks.

listener.gloss: A function that runs in response to an event; an event handler.

listing.gloss: A printout of a program or data set.

listing number.gloss: Any of four topological invariants associated with a topological space. The smallest Listing number counts the number of connected components of a space, and is thus equivalent to the zeroth Betti number.

listserver.gloss: A server that distributes messages to members of an e-mail list.

listview.gloss: A user interface control that can display a series of icons, possibly with accompanying text captions.

listwashing.gloss: The removal of nonproductive addresses from a mailing list.

literal.gloss: An atomic formula (consisting of a propositional variable) or its negation.
A value, as opposed to an identifier, written into the source code of a computer program.

literate programming.gloss: A programming paradigm in which a program is given as an explanation of the program logic in a natural language (such as English), interspersed with snippets of macros and traditional source code, from which compilable representation can be generated.

little's law.gloss: A theorem which states that the long-term average number L of customers in a stationary system is equal to the long-term average effective arrival rate λ multiplied by the average time W that a customer spends in the system.

little-endian.gloss: Storing the most significant byte of a multibyte number at a higher address than the least significant byte; that is, "little end" first.

lituus.gloss: A curve with polar equation r²θ=a², where a is a constant.

live.gloss: Operational; in actual use rather than in testing etc. Of an object or value: that may potentially be used in the future execution of a program.

live cd.gloss: A storage medium, often a compact disc, that contains a complete operating system that can be booted off the medium without having to install it.

livelock.gloss: A state resembling deadlock in which various computational processes are constantly changing but never reach a point where any of them can proceed.
To enter a state of livelock.

livelocked.gloss: Unable to proceed because of livelock.

liveness.gloss: A set of properties of a concurrent system that require the system to make progress despite the fact that its concurrently executing processes may have to take turns in critical sections.

living standard.gloss: A technical specification that is continually developed, rather than being fixed at one point in time.

llc.gloss: Initialism of logical link control, one of the two functions of a NIC.

llvm.gloss: Initialism of Low Level Virtual Machine, a collection of modular and reusable compiler and toolchain technologies that are used to develop compiler front ends and back ends.

lmi.gloss: Initialism of log management and intelligence.

load.gloss: The process of loading something, i.e. transferring it into memory or over a network, etc.
To read (data or a program) from a storage medium into computer memory.
To transfer from a storage medium into computer memory.

load factor.gloss: The proportion of the buckets in a hash table which contain entries.

load module.gloss: The executable form of a program that is produced by a linkage editor, taking as input the output of a compiler and/or assembler

load time.gloss: The point at which a program is put into an executable state.
The amount of time taken to load something.

load-and-go.gloss: The assembly and loading into memory of a program as a single operation, without generating and saving an intermediate object program.

load-store architecture.gloss: A type of computer architecture in which instructions either load/store values between memory and CPU registers, or perform calculations on values in CPU registers, but cannot directly perform calculations on values in memory.

loader.gloss: A program that prepares other programs for execution.

loading screen.gloss: A graphical display shown while a program loads (e.g. from cassette tape or video games).

loaf.gloss: A particular still life configuration with seven living cells.

loafer.gloss: A particular orthogonal spaceship in Conway's Game of Life that moves at a speed of c/7, and the smallest such example.

local.gloss: Connected directly to a particular computer, processor, etc.; able to be accessed offline.
Having limited scope (either lexical or dynamic); only accessible within a certain portion of a program.
Applying to or satisfied by substructures understood as "near points;" in particular: Satisfied by at least one open neighborhood of every point.
Applying to or satisfied by substructures understood as "near points;" in particular: Satisfied by arbitrarily small open neighborhoods of every point.
Applying to or satisfied by substructures understood as "near points;" in particular: Satisfied by every finitely generated subgroup.
qualifiers: of a property of an infinite group

local.gloss: Detectable from the behavior of substructures understood to be "near points;" in particular: Such that the following conditions are equivalent: (1) P holds for R (M); (2) P holds for the localization R_p (M_p) for all prime ideals p of R; (3) P holds for the localization R_m (M_m) for all maximal ideals m of R.
qualifiers: of a property P of a ring R (or an R-module M)

local.gloss: Detectable from the behavior of substructures understood to be "near points;" in particular: Detectable from the behavior of the normalizers of the nontrivial p-subgroups.
qualifiers: of a property of a finite group

local area network.gloss: An interconnection of computers that are in relatively close proximity to each other, such as within a building.
A network on which all devices communicate using OSI model device layer addressing.

local maximum.gloss: A maximum within a restricted domain; a point on a function whose value is greater than the values of all other points near it, especially if another local maximum of greater value is known to exist.

local minimum.gloss: A point on a graph (or its associated function) whose value is less than all other points near it.

local ring.gloss: A commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal, or a noncommutative ring with a unique maximal left ideal or (equivalently) a unique maximal right ideal.
The non-routing segment of a token ring network.

local-first.gloss: Designed to store the user's data on the local computer, connecting to the cloud only when required for tasks such as backup or synchronization.

locale.gloss: The set of settings related to the language and region in which a computer program executes. Examples are language, currency and time formats, character encoding etc.

A partially ordered set with the following additional axiomatic properties: any finite subset of it has a meet, any arbitrary subset of it has a join, and distributivity, which states that a binary meet distributes with respect to an arbitrary join. (Note: locales are just like frames except that the category of locales is opposite to the category of frames.)

locale-aware.gloss: The automatic detection of a user's language and country settings, thereby supplying the corresponding content at the same URLs.

localhost.gloss: The computer being used locally, contrasted with remote computers elsewhere on a network.

localic.gloss: Relating to the category of locales.

localization.gloss: The act, process, or result of making a product suitable for use in a particular country or region.
The act, process, or result of adapting translated text to fit a local culture; domestication.
A systematic method of adding multiplicative inverses to a ring.
A ring of fractions of a given ring, such that the complement of the set of allowed denominators is an ideal.

localize.gloss: To adapt (a product or service) for use in a particular country or region, typically by translating text into the language of that country and modifying currencies, date formats, etc.
To adapt translated text to fit a local culture; to domesticate.
To produce (from a ring and an ideal in that ring) the ring of fractions, where the set of allowed denominators is the compliment of the given ideal.

localizer.gloss: A person who localizes (adapts a product for use in a particular country or region, or adapts translated text to fit a local culture).

locally.gloss: Within a sufficiently small sphere (or circle or interval) around a given point (sometimes, around any point).

locally compact.gloss: Of a topological space: such that, for every point of the space, there is a neighborhood of that point whose closure is compact.

locally compact group.gloss: A topological group whose underlying topology is both locally compact and Hausdorff.

locally finite.gloss: For which every vertex has finite degree.

locally indicable.gloss: Such that each of its nontrivial, finitely generated subgroups maps homomorphically onto ℤ.

locally small.gloss: Such that the hom class between any two objects is a set (and not a proper class).

location-agnostic.gloss: Not constrained to a particular location.

lock.gloss: A mutex or other token restricting access to a resource.

lock convoy.gloss: The undesirable situation where multiple threads of equal priority contend repeatedly for the same lock.

lock out.gloss: To prevent from accessing a data structure.

lock up.gloss: To cause (a program) to cease responding or to freeze.

lock-free.gloss: Not requiring the acquisition of a mutex (or other kind of) lock for synchronizing with other threads.

locked.gloss: Protected by a mutex or other token restricting access to a resource.

locker.gloss: An online storage service for files.

lockfile.gloss: A file whose existence, by convention, indicates that a particular resource is in use.

locking.gloss: The use of a lock or a mutex to restrict access to a part of the code to at most one process.

locking shift.gloss: A state-dependent encoding mechanism used in data communication (such as GSM SMS) and character encoding standards to switch between different character sets or windows.

lockout.gloss: A situation where the system is not responding to input.

lockup.gloss: A condition where a system stops responding to inputs; a freeze.

locus.gloss: The set of all points whose coordinates satisfy a given equation or condition.

lod.gloss: Initialism of logarithm of odds, a measure of likelihood calculated by taking the log of the ratio of the probability of a hypothesis being true given the observed data over the probability that the hypothesis is false.
Alternative letter-case form of lod (“logarithm of odds”).

loess.gloss: Acronym of locally estimated scatterplot smoothing.

log.gloss: Specifically, an append-only sequential record of events written to a file, display, or other data stream.

log in.gloss: To gain access to a computer system, usually by providing a previously registered username and password.

log out.gloss: To exit a user account in a computer system, so that one is not recognized until signing in again.

log spam.gloss: Excessive or irrelevant log entries, typically resulting from misconfiguration, that are unlikely to be read and serve only as clutter and waste storage space.

log-linear.gloss: Being or relating to a mathematical model that takes the form of a function whose logarithm is a linear combination of the parameters of the model, making it possible to apply (possibly multivariate) linear regression.

log-log.gloss: Describing a relationship (or a graph) between logarithmic quantities (or scales)

log-logistic.gloss: Whose logarithm has a logistic distribution

log-structured.gloss: Storing data in such a way that modifications are kept in a buffer rather than overwriting the previous version.

logarithm.gloss: For a number x, the exponent by which a given base number must be raised in order to obtain the power x. Written log _bx. For example, log ₁₀1000=3 because 10³=1000 and log ₂16=4 because 2⁴=16.

logarithmic decrement.gloss: The logarithm of the ratio of two successive amplitudes separated by one period for oscillators (second-order linear dynamical systems).

logarithmic derivative.gloss: Given a real or complex function f, the ratio of the value of the derivative to the value of the function, (f')/f, regarded as a function.

logarithmic function.gloss: Any function in which an independent variable appears in the form of a logarithm; they are the inverse functions of exponential functions

logarithmic integral.gloss: A special function written using the symbol li and defined as operatorname lix=∫₀ˣ(dt)/(ln t).

logarithmic spiral.gloss: A self-similar spiral curve which often appears in nature.

logarithmic trigonometric function.gloss: The logarithm of a trigonometric function

logfile.gloss: A file that serves as a log.

logic.gloss: The study of the principles and criteria of valid inference and demonstration.
The mathematical study of relationships between rigorously defined concepts and of mathematical proof of statements.
A formal or informal language together with a deductive system or a model-theoretic semantics.

logic bomb.gloss: A piece of code intentionally inserted into a software system that will set off a malicious function when specified conditions are met.

logic circuit.gloss: a chain of multiple logic gates

logic error.gloss: a case in which a programmer writes viable code that however produces undesired results

logic form.gloss: The representation of natural language sentences in first-order logic, where concept predicates are combined through shared arguments.

logic gate.gloss: A physical device, typically electronic, which computes a Boolean logical output (0 or 1) from Boolean input or inputs according to the rules of some logical operator.

logic programming.gloss: Programming with a paradigm that bases on formal logic

logical.gloss: Relating to the conceptual model of a system rather than its physical expression

logical address.gloss: The address at which an item appears to reside from the perspective of an executing application program.

logical block address.gloss: An address for accessing logical blocks on a secondary storage device, expressed as an integer from 0 to n−1, where n is the number of blocks available on the device. An address under the system of logical block addressing.

logical block addressing.gloss: A system for referring to blocks of a secondary storage device (usually, these are 512-byte chunks), whereby each is given an index from 0 to n−1, where n is the number of blocks available on the device.

logical clock.gloss: A mechanism for capturing chronological and causal relationships in a distributed system.

logical complement.gloss: The number, obtained by complementing every bit of a given number, which produces all ones when exclusive ored with the given number.

logical connective.gloss: A truth-valued function such as conjunction, disjunction, negation, and material implication.

logical constant.gloss: A word or phrase which has an invariant logical meaning and which is useful for forming argument forms.

logical form.gloss: A specific semantic version of a statement in a formal system, attempting to formalize something possibly ambiguous.

logicomathematical.gloss: Relating to logic and mathematics (or to mathematical logic)

login.gloss: Credentials: the combination of a user's identification and password used to enter a computer, program, network, etc.
The process or an instance of logging in.

logistic.gloss: Using sexagesimal fractions, especially in arithmetic or logarithms.
A logistic function or graph of a logistic curve.

logistic curve.gloss: An S-shaped curve that models the growth of many ecosystems.

logistic function.gloss: A function, the result of the division of two exponential functions, that gives rise to the logistic curve.

logit.gloss: The inverse of the sigmoid or logistic function used in mathematics, especially in statistics. The logit of a number p between 0 and 1 is given by the formula

logject.gloss: An object with embedded software capable of monitoring and recording, in some manner, its own activity and operation.

loglike.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of the log (logarithm) function.

loglikelihood.gloss: The likelihood of a model fitting a data set according to a logarithmic formula.

lognormal.gloss: Describing a logarithmic function that has a normal distribution.

logoff.gloss: The process or an instance of logging off.

logometric.gloss: Of or relating to a system of logarithms constructed to suit a system of ratios and measures.

logon.gloss: credentials: the combination of a user's identification and password used to enter a computer.

logout.gloss: The act or process of logging out.

logpoint.gloss: A point in program code at which a message is logged for debugging.

logseries.gloss: A class of continuous probability distributions developed in 1943 by the English statistician and biologist Ronald Fisher to fit some particular species distribution data sets.

logsumexp.gloss: A smooth maximum used by machine learning algorithms.

long.gloss: A long integer variable, twice the size of an int, two or four times the size of a short, and half of a long long.

long division.gloss: A procedure for dividing multidigit numbers, breaking down the division into a series of easier steps.

long filename.gloss: A filename in which the name, the file extension, or both exceed(s) the length permitted by the 8.3 filename format.

long integer.gloss: An integer with a width (in bits) that is at least equal to that of a standard integer on the same machine (usually 32 or 64 bits).

long long.gloss: A kind of integer variable, allowing a greater range of possible values than a long.

long mode.gloss: An operational mode of x86-64 computers which enables 64-bit addressing, running older 32-bit code in compatibility mode and foregoing support for real-mode applications entirely.

long polling.gloss: A technology where the client requests information from the server without expecting an immediate response.

long tail.gloss: The tail of a distribution that represents the rare occurrence of extreme values.

longword.gloss: A type of unsigned integer variable that is longer than a word (with the specific number of bits depending upon the system architecture).

look and feel.gloss: The combination of the visual design and behaviour of a user interface.

look development.gloss: The process of defining the final appearance of three-dimensional assets using shaders, textures, and lighting, especially as a cohesive design across a larger project.

lookahead.gloss: The analysis in advance of subsequent decisions that would be made if a particular branch of an algorithm was followed.

lookahead time.gloss: The amount of time from the point when an upcoming process is scheduled and resources are allocated for it, to the moment when it executes.

lookaside.gloss: The technique of searching for something in a precalculated cache before attempting a more time-consuming search elsewhere.

lookup table.gloss: A data structure created for the purpose of translating keys into values.

loop.gloss: A programmed sequence of instructions that is repeated until or while a particular condition is satisfied.
An edge that begins and ends on the same vertex.
A path that starts and ends at the same point.
A quasigroup with an identity element.

loop device.gloss: A pseudodevice that makes a file accessible as a block device.

loop invariant.gloss: an invariant that should be true on entry into a loop and is guaranteed to remain true on every iteration of the loop

loopoid.gloss: A nonassociative generalization of a groupoid

loopspace.gloss: A function space of continuous functions that map from the unit interval to a space from x₀ to x₁, all of which map 0 to x₀ and 1 to x₁.

loose coupling.gloss: A low-level interdependent coupling between program modules.

lorentz group.gloss: The group of all Lorentz transformations in spacetime.

lorentz invariant.gloss: A quantity that does not change due to a Lorentz transformation; a quantity that is independent of the inertial frame.

lorentz transformation.gloss: A transformation relating the spacetime coordinates of one frame of reference to another in special relativity.

loss function.gloss: A function which expresses numerically the loss produced by a decision or other event.

lossy.gloss: Of an algorithm for converting or compressing data, reducing the amount of information in data.

low poly.gloss: A 3D modeling technique in computer graphics that uses a relatively small number of polygons to construct a digital object or environment.

low surrogate.gloss: A code point in the range U+DC00 through U+DFFF (the Low Surrogates block), used in UTF-16 to encode the low 10 bits of the 20-bit offset above U+FFFF of the code point belonging to a supplementary character.

low-code.gloss: (of a development environment) Primarily involving a graphical user interface rather than a text-based one.
(of an application) Programmed using a low-code development environment.
The practice of developing applications via a low-code development environment.

low-level.gloss: Of, or relating to a program, or to code in which each statement corresponds to a single machine instruction.

low-level language.gloss: A computer language whose source code is a somewhat user-friendly version of a particular computer architecture's assembly language, containing no provisions for portability between architectures.

lowdimensional.gloss: Having or involving four or fewer dimensions

lower.gloss: To reduce operations to single machine instructions, as part of compilation of a program.

lower bound.gloss: A value that is less than or equal to every element of a given set of values.

lower camel case.gloss: The practice of writing identifiers by concatenating multiple component words, where each word excluding the first is capitalized.

lower set.gloss: A subset of a poset which contains any descending chain which starts at any element of itself.

lowest common denominator.gloss: The smallest positive integer which is a multiple of every denominator of several fractions.

loxodrome.gloss: A line on a surface (such as the Earth) that cuts all meridians at a constant angle (but not a right angle) – on Earth, the path followed by a ship or aircraft that maintains a constant course by the compass.

loxodromic.gloss: Preserving angles between curves, such as in a Möbius transformation that is not elliptic or parabolic.

lp space.gloss: Function spaces defined using a natural generalization of the p-norm for finite-dimensional vector spaces.

lpddr.gloss: Initialism of low-powered double data rate.

lqtm.gloss: Initialism of linear quantum Turing machine.

lr.gloss: Initialism of left to right, rightmost derivation in reverse.

lsp.gloss: Initialism of Liskov substitution principle, one of the SOLID programming principles.

lte.gloss: Initialism of lifting the exponent, a lemma used to calculate p-adic orders.

lth.gloss: Occurring at position l in a sequence.

lto.gloss: Initialism of Linear Tape-Open, an open standard computer storage tape format having a single spooled cartridge with half-inch tape.

lu.gloss: A matrix decomposition which writes a matrix as the product of a lower and upper triangular matrix, used in numerical analysis to solve systems of linear equations or find the inverse of a matrix.

lucas.gloss: Acronym of low-cost uncrewed combat attack system

lucas polynomial.gloss: Any member of a polynomial sequence which can be considered as a generalization of the Lucas numbers.

lucasian.gloss: Of or pertaining to Henry Lucas (c. 1610–1663), Member of Parliament for Cambridge University and founder of the Lucasian Chair of Mathematics.

luck.gloss: The results of a random number generator.

ludolphian number.gloss: Synonym of pi, particularly the 35-decimal approximation discovered by Ludolph van Ceulen

luggable.gloss: An early portable computer, similar to a desktop computer.
An early portable computer, heavier than the modern laptop.
A portable computer that can be easily carried and moved, but cannot easily be used during travel.

lumel.gloss: A texel in the texture map representing a lightmap.

lumpability.gloss: The extent to which a matrix is lumpable.

lunchbox.gloss: A luggable; an early laptop computer, usually a unit with a handle and a fold-out keyboard.

lune.gloss: A concave figure formed by the intersection of the arcs of two circles on a plane, or on a sphere the intersection between two great semicircles.

lune of hippocrates.gloss: A lune bounded by arcs of two circles, the smaller of which has as its diameter a chord spanning a right angle on the larger circle.

luser.gloss: A user (especially in IRC) who disobeys the rules of the servers that they are using and usually resorts to disruptive or offensive behavior.

lvalue.gloss: A value that can be treated as an address or storage location.

lyapunov exponent.gloss: In a dynamical system, a quantity that characterizes the rate of separation of infinitesimally close trajectories.

lychrel number.gloss: A natural number that cannot form a palindrome through the iterative process of repeatedly reversing its digits and adding the resulting numbers.

lyricon.gloss: A form of earcon or musicon that incorporates musically intoned speech.

lzo.gloss: Initialism of Lempel-Ziv-Oberhumer, a lossless data compression algorithm.

lévy flight.gloss: A type of random walk in which the increments are distributed according to a “heavy-tailed” distribution i.e. there are a significant number of large increments.

m1.gloss: The number two, as the first Mersenne prime.
Apple M1, a system on a chip designed by Apple which was introduced in 2020.

m2.gloss: The number three as the second Mersenne prime.
Apple M2, a system on a chip designed by Apple which was introduced in 2022.

m2m.gloss: Abbreviation of machine to machine, technologies that allow both wireless and wired systems to communicate with other devices of the same type.

mac.gloss: Initialism of media access control: the portion of Ethernet, Wi-Fi 802.11 wireless, Bluetooth, FDDI, ATM, and Fibre Channel networks that controls which hardware devices have access to the media over which signals are sent.

Initialism of multiply and accumulate, a hardware module found in digital signal processors which performs a multiplication and adds the result of that operation to an accumulator in the same cycle, used extensively in implementations of digital filters, transforms, and codecs.

mac address.gloss: Media Access Control address; a unique identifying number assigned to most network devices.

macdonald polynomial.gloss: Any of a two-parameter family of orthogonal polynomials indexed by a positive weight of a root system.

mach.gloss: Acronym of microservices, API-first, cloud-native, headless.

machin-like formula.gloss: Any of a number of variants or extensions of Machin's formula.

machine code.gloss: A system of instructions and data directly understandable by a computer's central processing unit.
Machine language instructions that can be executed directly by a computer's central processing unit.

machine epsilon.gloss: An upper bound on the relative approximation error due to rounding in floating-point arithmetic, denoted by the symbol ε.

machine instruction.gloss: Any of a set of discrete instructions, each with its own binary representation and associated assembly language mnemonic, that a CPU can execute; typically they involve the movement, comparison or manipulation of data.

machine language.gloss: The set of instructions that a particular computer is designed to execute; generated from an assembly language by an assembler, or from a high-level language by a compiler or interpreter.

machine translation.gloss: The production of instructions in a computer language that are equal in meaning to that in another language.

machine word.gloss: A unit of information of a standard number of characters, appropriate for a fixed wordlength computer.

machine-readable.gloss: Organised or formatted in a way that permits unambiguous interpretation by a program.

machoflops.gloss: A deceptively inflated measure of the speed of a computer, as used in marketing materials.

macintel.gloss: A Macintosh computer with an Intel CPU.

macintosh.gloss: A brand of personal computer manufactured by Apple Inc.

maclaurin polynomial.gloss: A truncated Maclaurin series; the sum of the first n terms of a Maclaurin series.

maclaurin series.gloss: Any Taylor series that is centred at 0 (i.e., for which the origin is the reference point used to derive the series from its associated function); for a given infinitely differentiable complex function f, the power series f(0)+(f'(0))/(1!)x+(f(0))/(2!)x²+(f'(0))/(3!)x³+⋯=∑ₙ₌₀ ᪲(f⁽ⁿ⁾(0))/(n!),xⁿ.

macro.gloss: A comparatively human-friendly abbreviation of complex input to a computer program.

macro expansion.gloss: The source code (assembler or other language) created by interpretation of a macro

macro language.gloss: A system for defining and processing macros.
An extension to an assembly language in which macroinstructions, containing a series of instructions, may be written.

macroassembler.gloss: An assembler that supports user-defined macros.

macroblock.gloss: A block of adjacent pixels, typically a rectangular 16×16 block

macroblocking.gloss: A visual artifact in compressed video etc. where similar adjacent pixels appear as a contiguous block of colour.

macrocomputer.gloss: A mainframe, as opposed to a microcomputer.

macrolanguage.gloss: Alternative spelling of macro language (“system for defining and processing macros”).

macrolike.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a macro.

macroparameter.gloss: Any parameter of a macro (normally written as macro parameter)

macroprogramming.gloss: The creation of macros and macroinstructions, and the writing of programs using them.

macroroutine.gloss: A routine implemented using one or more macros.

macrosimulation.gloss: simulation of a system as a whole, without simulating the behaviour of its individual components

macrosystem.gloss: A programming system in which small constructs (macros) represent groups of machine instructions.

macrovariable.gloss: A variable that may be modified by or within a macro

mactel.gloss: The computing environment of the Apple operating system running on an Intel CPU.

magic.gloss: Something producing successful and remarkable results, especially when not fully understood; an enchanting quality; exceptional skill. Complicated or esoteric code that is not expected to be generally understood.
Being a literal number or string value with no meaning or context, not defined as a constant or variable

magic circle.gloss: An arrangement of natural numbers on circles such that the sum of the numbers on each circle and the sum of numbers on diameter are identical.

magic constant.gloss: The sum of numbers in any row, column, or diagonal of a magic square.

magic cookie.gloss: A token or short packet of data passed between communicating programs, used to identify a particular event or transaction; the data is typically not meaningful to the recipient program and not usually interpreted until the recipient passes the data back to the sender or another program at a later time.

magic cube.gloss: By analogy with magic square, an n-by-n-by-n arrangement of n³ numbers such that the numbers in each row, in all columns (horizontal and vertical) and in all main diagonals (of which there are 6*n+4) each have the same sum.

magic number.gloss: A number which is manually entered into source code, rather than defined somewhere as a named constant; especially one which is arbitrary or lacks explanation.
A sentinel value which cannot occur in normal use, typically used as a placeholder (e.g. a fictitious date such as 2000-02-32).
A hash code, such as those used by some webmail servers to keep track of sessions.
A number or pattern in a binary file that identifies the filetype.

magic packet.gloss: A specially crafted packet that will turn on a computer with wake-on-LAN support if it is received by the computer's network card in standby mode.

magic square.gloss: An n-by-n arrangement of n² numbers such that the numbers in each row, in each column and along both diagonals all have the same sum.

magic string.gloss: A text input that is never expected to be received in normal conditions and that activates otherwise hidden functionality.

magic word.gloss: A string of text having some special function or purpose.

magma.gloss: A basic algebraic structure consisting of a set equipped with a single binary operation.

magnetic strip.gloss: A strip of magnetic material on which data is stored for later retrieval and reading by an electronic device.

magnetologic.gloss: Describing a device that uses magnetism to perform the logical operations normally performed using electronics

magnitude.gloss: A number, assigned to something, such that it may be compared to others numerically
Of a vector, the norm, most commonly, the two-norm.

maharam algebra.gloss: A complete Boolean algebra having a continuous submeasure (also known as a Maharam submeasure).

mahler measure.gloss: For a given polynomial p(z): a kind of height function defined as M(p)=|a|∏_(|αᵢ|>1)|αᵢ|=|a|∏ᵢ₌₁ⁿ max 1,|αᵢ|, where p(z) factorizes over the complex numbers ℂ as

mail bomb.gloss: A large number of e-mails sent to one destination, or an e-mail with a very large attachment, as a denial-of-service attack.

mail merge.gloss: A software product that uses a file (or database) of names and addresses, together with a template document, to produce multiple copies of a letter, each personally addressed to a different recipient.

mail slot.gloss: A designated storage location for interprocess messages.

mailbox.gloss: A folder or account for the storage of email; an electronic inbox or mailstore.

mailfile.gloss: A file that stores electronic mail.

mailstore.gloss: A structure in a file system that stores electronic mail.

main diagonal.gloss: The entries of a square matrix from the top left to the bottom right.

main memory.gloss: Volatile memory forming most of a computer’s primary storage, not including cache memory (central processing unit cache) and secondary storage (mass storage).

main menu.gloss: A list of principal options, usually presented to the user immediately upon the launch of a computer program or video game.

mainframe.gloss: A large, powerful computer able to manage very many simultaneous tasks and communicate with very many connected terminals; used by large, complex organizations (such as banks and supermarkets) where continuously sustained operation is vital.
A computer chassis that hosts and interconnects modules that perform various tasks.

mainline.gloss: To integrate (code, etc.) into the main repository for a software project, rather than separate forks.
The main repository for a software project, from which different versions (forks) may be split off.

maintenance.gloss: Software updates that fix bugs and improve stability rather than adding new features.

major.gloss: Occurring as the predicate in the conclusion of a categorical syllogism. (of a term)
Containing the major term in a categorical syllogism. (of a premise)

major axis.gloss: The longest diameter of an ellipse, running through the center and foci, with its ends being the widest points of the shape.

major premise.gloss: In a categorical syllogism, the premise whose terms are the syllogism's major term and middle term.

major term.gloss: In a syllogism, the term that is the predicate of the conclusion.

majorant.gloss: A function, or an element of a set, that dominates others or is greater than all others.

majoration.gloss: The establishment of conditions for an upper bound of an expression.

majorization.gloss: A preorder on vectors of real numbers.

make.gloss: A software utility for automatically building large applications, or an implementation of this utility.

make file.gloss: A configuration file that describes the steps involved in building an application from its source code.

malfatti circle.gloss: Any of the three circles inside a given triangle such that each circle is tangent to the others and to two sides of the triangle.

malfunction routine.gloss: Any program or subroutine responsible for troubleshooting problems.

malleability.gloss: A property of a cryptographic algorithms in which an adversary can alter a ciphertext such that it decrypts to a related plaintext.

malleable.gloss: In which an adversary can alter a ciphertext such that it decrypts to a related plaintext.

malloc.gloss: A subroutine in the C programming language's standard library for performing dynamic memory allocation.
To allocate memory using the C programming language malloc subroutine.

malnormal.gloss: Of, pertaining to, or exhibiting malnormality

malnormality.gloss: The property of a subgroup H of a group G where, for any x in G but not in H, H and Hˣ intersect in the identity element.

maltitude.gloss: Any of the four line segments perpendicular to the sides of a cyclic quadrilateral and passing through the opposite side's midpoint.

malvertisement.gloss: An advertisement, published on the Internet, that is infected with malicious code aiming to hijack the viewer's computer.

malvertising.gloss: Internet advertising whose real intention is to deliver malware to the viewer's computer.

malware.gloss: Software which has been designed to operate in a malicious, undesirable manner.

man.gloss: Initialism of Metropolitan Area Network, a large computer network usually spanning a city.

man page.gloss: A helpfile in Unix and Unix-like operating systems.

man-in-the-middle attack.gloss: A security attack in which someone intercepts the communication between a device and the server it is connected to, simulating the device to the server and simulating the server to the device.

managed bean.gloss: A regular Java Bean class that is registered with JSF, i.e. which is managed by the JSF framework, and contains the getter and setter methods, business logic, or even a backing bean.

managed code.gloss: Source code that will execute only under Microsoft's Common Language Runtime.

manager.gloss: A window or application whose purpose is to give the user the control over some aspect of the system.

mancova.gloss: Acronym of multivariate analysis of covariance, an extension of ANOVA methods to cover cases where there is more than one dependent variable and where the control of covariates is required.

mandelbox.gloss: A multidimensional fractal with a box-like shape, defined in a similar way to the Mandelbrot set.

mandelbrot set.gloss: the set of complex numbers c for which the orbit of 0 under iteration of the complex quadratic polynomial zₙ₊₁ = zₙ² + c remains bounded. The boundary of this set is a fractal.

mandelbrotian.gloss: Of or relating to the work, or theory developed from the work, of mathematician Benoit Mandelbrot.

mandelbug.gloss: A software bug whose behaviour appears to be chaotic.

mandelbulb.gloss: A three-dimensional analogue of the Mandelbrot set.

mangle.gloss: To modify (an identifier from source code) so as to produce a unique identifier for internal use by the compiler, etc.

manhattan distance.gloss: Synonym of taxicab distance (“the distance between two points on a grid, where the only path allowed is along horizontal and vertical lines”).

manifest.gloss: A file containing metadata describing other files.

manifest file.gloss: A file containing metadata for a group of accompanying files that are part of a set or coherent unit.

manifest typing.gloss: A typing where the software programmer explicitly identifies the type of each declared variable.

manifold.gloss: A Hausdorff topological space that looks locally like the "ordinary" Euclidean space ℝⁿ.
A polygon mesh representing the continuous, closed surface of a solid object

manipulative.gloss: A manipulable object designed to demonstrate a mathematical concept.

mann-whitney u test.gloss: A nonparametric test of the null hypothesis that the probability that a randomly selected value from one population is less than a randomly selected value from a second population is equal to the probability of being greater. It can be used to investigate whether two independent samples were selected from populations having the same distribution.

mantissa.gloss: The part of a common logarithm after the decimal point, the fractional part of a logarithm.
The significand; that part of a floating-point number or number in scientific notation that contains its significant digits.

manularity.gloss: labor-intensiveness, especially in contrast to automation.

many-sorted logic.gloss: A logic that directly supports classification of entities into disjunct sorts.

many-to-many.gloss: Having the property that many elements of one set may be assigned by the relationship to any element in the other set, and that a given element in the first set can also be assigned more than one member of the second set.
qualifiers: of a relationship between two sets

many-to-one.gloss: Having the property that many elements of one set may be assigned by the relationship to one element in the other set, and that a given element in the first set can be assigned by only one member of the second set.
qualifiers: of a relationship between two sets

many-valued logic.gloss: A kind of non-classical propositional calculus whose semantics makes use of more than two truth values.

map.gloss: A function, especially a function satisfying a certain property (e.g. continuity, linearity, etc.; see Usage notes).
To act as a function on something, taking it to something else.
To assign a drive letter to a shared folder.

maplet.gloss: A pair which is a member of a mapping.
An applet written in the computer algebra system Maple.

mapper.gloss: A software or hardware component that performs a mapping.

mapping.gloss: Assigning a PC to a shared drive or printer port on a network.
A function that maps every element of a given mathematical structure (eg: a set) to a unique element of another structure; a correspondence.

marching ants.gloss: An animated dotted line indicating which portion of an image is currently selected.

marching cubes.gloss: An algorithm for extracting a polygonal mesh of an isosurface from a three-dimensional scalar field.

marchitecture.gloss: A non-technical depiction of the architecture of a system, service, product line, or organization that has been simplified or made more conceptual for use in marketing communications.
An unfinished architecture that only exists as a figment of marketing.
An architecture whose design is dictated by marketing considerations.

margin of error.gloss: An expression of the lack of precision in the results obtained from a sample.

marginalize.gloss: To find a marginal distribution of a joint probability distribution.

marginalize out.gloss: The act of discarding a subset of random variables from a probability distribution to find the marginal distribution.

margolus neighborhood.gloss: A block cellular automaton neighborhood consisting of a two-by-two square of cells which shifts one cell diagonally each generation.

mark.gloss: Characteristic, sign, indication for measurement; visible impression. A characteristic or essential attribute; a differential.

mark and sweep.gloss: A form of garbage collection in which every accessible object in memory is flagged, leaving unflagged only those that are no longer reachable and can thus be discarded.

marker interface.gloss: A special type of interface without any constants or methods defined, and that is used just to mark a class.

marker interface pattern.gloss: A software design pattern in computer science, used with languages that provide run-time type information about objects.

marking.gloss: Any configuration of a Petri net with a number of marks or tokens distributed across it.

markov chain.gloss: A discrete-time stochastic process containing a Markov property.

markov jump process.gloss: A time-dependent variable that starts in an initial state and stays in that state for a random time, when it makes a transition to another random state, and so on.

markov partition.gloss: A tool used in dynamical systems theory, allowing the methods of symbolic dynamics to be applied to the study of hyperbolic systems. By using a Markov partition, the system can be made to resemble a discrete-time Markov process, with the long-term dynamical characteristics of the system represented as a Markov shift.

markov process.gloss: Any stochastic process for which the conditional probability distribution of future states depends only on the current state (and not on past states).

markov property.gloss: The memoryless property of Markov models, according to which the future states depend only on the current state and not those that preceded it.

markov renewal process.gloss: A class of random processes that generalize the class of Markov jump processes.

markovian.gloss: Exhibiting the Markov property, in which the conditional probability distribution of future states of the process, given the present state and all past states, depends only upon the present state and not on any past states.

markup.gloss: The notation that is used to indicate the meaning of the elements in an electronic document, or to dictate how text should be displayed.

markup language.gloss: A computer language using markup that tells the computer some traits of the content that is described by the markup tags.

marquee.gloss: In graphical editing software, a special selection tool, used to highlight a portion of an image.
To select (an object or region) with the marquee selection tool.

marshal.gloss: To serialize an object into a marshalled state represented by a sequence of bytes that can later be converted back into an object with equivalent properties.

marshalling.gloss: The process of transforming the memory representation of an object to a data format suitable for storage or transmission, which is typically used when data must be moved between different parts of a computer program, or from one program to another.

martian packet.gloss: A network packet whose declared source or destination IP address lies within a reserved address range unavailable for use on the public Internet.

martingale.gloss: A stochastic process for which the conditional expectation of future values given the sequence of all prior values is equal to the current value.

martingality.gloss: The condition of being like a martingale.

mashup.gloss: Something consisting of two or more elements combined together. A derivative work consisting of two or more pieces of (generally digital) media joined together, such as a video clip with a different soundtrack applied for humorous effect, or a map overlaid with user-supplied data.

mask.gloss: A pattern of bits used in bitwise operations; bitmask.
A two-color (black and white) bitmap generated from an image, used to create transparency in the image.
To set or unset (certain bits, or binary digits, within a value) by means of a bitmask.
To disable (an interrupt, etc.) by setting or unsetting the associated bit.

mask work.gloss: A type of three-dimensional image or pattern on a layer of materials used to design or manufacture a semiconductor chip.

masked man fallacy.gloss: A fallacy of inferring that since one knows (or does not know) something by one description, one must know (or not know) it by another, as in "I know who my father is. I do not know who the masked man is. Therefore, my father is not the masked man."

masonry layout.gloss: A tightly-packed columnar layout in which there are no identifiable rows, unlike a uniform grid.

mass function.gloss: A relationship that describes the mass distribution.

mass storage.gloss: Any form of data storage (non-volatile memory) with high capacity relative to that of the faster volatile memory of computers (of its time).

massive parallelism.gloss: The property of being massively parallel.

massively parallel.gloss: having many individual or distributed processing units and thus able to carry out many simultaneous calculations.

master.gloss: A device that is controlling other devices or is an authoritative source.

master boot record.gloss: A type of boot sector in the first few blocks of partitioned computer mass storage devices.

match.gloss: To be an example of a rule or regex.

match demo.gloss: a type of file that recreates a Video game Match using recorded information

match moving.gloss: A technique that allows the insertion of computer graphics into live-action footage with correct position, scale, orientation, and motion relative to the photographed objects in the shot.

match-merge.gloss: To merge sets of objects while excluding duplicates.

matchgate.gloss: A weighted planar graph having some external nodes

matching.gloss: A set of independent edges in a given graph, i.e. a set of edges which do not intersect, such that pairs of vertices are "matched" to each other one to one.

matching number.gloss: the number of edges in a maximum matching, often denoted ν=ν(G)

material.gloss: Of or relating to the matter of reasoning, as distinguished from the form of it, especially empirical.
An element of a design language associated with a certain style of rendering on the display.

material conditional.gloss: A type of conditional statement used in formal logic and defined as true whenever its antecedent is false or its consequent is true, and false when its antecedent is true and its consequent is false.

material nonimplication.gloss: The negation of material implication, such that for any two propositions P and Q, the material nonimplication from P to Q is true if and only if the negation of the material implication from P to Q is true.

materialization.gloss: The creation of a temporary table containing the results of a database query.

materialize.gloss: To perform materialization; to save the results of a database query as a temporary table or materialized view.

mathematical analysis.gloss: The mathematical study of functions, sequences, series, limits, derivatives and integrals.

mathematical economics.gloss: A sub-field of economics which aims at expressing economic theories with mathematical formulae.

mathematical formula.gloss: Synonym of formula (“any mathematical rule expressed symbolically”).

mathematical function.gloss: Synonym of function (“a relation in which each element of the domain is associated with exactly one element of the codomain”).

mathematical game.gloss: Any game featuring arithmetic or other branches of mathematics; a branch of recreational mathematics

mathematical induction.gloss: A method of proof which, in terms of a predicate P, could be stated as: if P(0) is true and if for any natural number n>0, P(n) implies P(n+1), then P(n) is true for any natural number n.

mathematical logic.gloss: A subfield of logic and mathematics consisting of both the mathematical study of logic and the application of this study to other areas of mathematics, exemplified by questions on the expressive power of formal logics and the deductive power of formal proof systems.

mathematical morphology.gloss: A theory and technique for the analysis and processing of geometrical structures, based on set theory, lattice theory, topology, and random functions.

mathematical semantics.gloss: A study of formal semantics of computer languages, such as denotational semantics.

mathematical space.gloss: A set (a "universe") that consists of selected mathematical objects that are treated as points, and selected relationships between them.

mathematical statistics.gloss: The study of statistics from a purely mathematical standpoint, using probability theory, measure theory, linear algebra and analysis.

mathematical structure.gloss: A set together with a collection of mathematical objects such as other sets, relations or operations which endow it with additional structure.

mathieu moonshine.gloss: A surprising correspondence between the coefficients of K3 surfaces and finite simple group known as Mathieu group M24.

matrically.gloss: By means of, or in the form of matrices

matricization.gloss: The operation that turns a tensor into a matrix.

matricize.gloss: To convert (a tensor) into a matrix by means of matricization.

matrix.gloss: A rectangular arrangement of numbers or terms having various uses such as transforming coordinates in geometry, solving systems of linear equations in linear algebra and representing graphs in graph theory.

matrix algebra.gloss: Generically, the arithmetic of matrices, involving matrix addition, scalar multiplication of matrices, matrix multiplication, and matrix inversion.
A matrix ring over a commutative ring.

matrix decomposition.gloss: A process by which a matrix (a rectangular table of numbers or abstract quantities that can be added and multiplied) is broken down into simpler numerical building blocks.

matrix group.gloss: Any group of invertible matrices over a specified field, with the group operation of matrix multiplication.

matroid.gloss: A structure that captures the essence of a notion of "independence" that generalizes linear independence in vector spaces and acyclicality in graphs.

matroidal.gloss: Of or pertaining to a matroid

mau.gloss: Initialism of media/multiple attachment unit: a connectivity device for a token ring network.

maxheap.gloss: A heap data structure with a "less than or equal to" comparison function.

maximal.gloss: Larger than any previous term in the sequence.
Such that no other element is greater (with respect to the given partial order).
qualifiers: of an element of a poset

maximal.gloss: The element of a set with the greatest magnitude.
Said of an ideal of a ring or a filter of a lattice: that it is as large as it can be without being trivial (improper).
Said of a set of well-formed formulas: that it is as large as it can be without being inconsistent; i.e. that for any well-formed formula φ, the set contains either φ or ~φ.

maximal ideal.gloss: An ideal which cannot be made any larger (by adjoining any element to it) without making it improper (i.e., equal to the whole of the containing algebraic structure).

maximax.gloss: A strategy or algorithm that seeks to maximize the maximum possible result (that is, that prefers the alternative with the chance of the best possible outcome, even if its expected outcome and its worst possible outcome are worse than other alternatives); often used attributively, as "maximax strategy", "maximax approach", and so on.

maximin.gloss: A rule to identify the worst outcome of each possible option to find one's best (maximum payoff) play.

maximization.gloss: The process of finding the maximum value of a function.

maximize.gloss: To expand (a window) to fill the main display area.

maximum.gloss: The greatest value of a set or other mathematical structure, especially the global maximum or a local maximum of a function.
An upper bound of a set which is also an element of that set.
The largest value of a batch or sample or the upper bound of a probability distribution.

maximum cut.gloss: A cut whose size is at least the size of any other cut; a partition of the graph's vertices into two complementary sets S and T, such that the number of edges between S and T is as large as possible.

maximum seek time.gloss: The amount of time required for a disk drive to seek through all possible tracks, from the innermost to the outermost or vice versa.

maximum throughput.gloss: The highest rate at which data can be transmitted or processed in a system over a given period of time.

maxipok.gloss: A strategy that aims to maximise the probability of an acceptable outcome.

maxitive.gloss: Describing a certain class of nonnegative functions of countable disjoint sets

maxplane.gloss: Describing a type of rotation in factor analysis.

maxterm.gloss: A sum that is a logical OR of a set of variables where each individual variable only appears once in the sum, either in complemented or uncomplemented form, so that the value of the sum becomes 0.

mb1.gloss: Initialism of mouse button 1, left mouse button.

mbaas.gloss: Acronym of mobile backend as a service.

mbps.gloss: megabit per second, a measure of data transfer rate

mca.gloss: Initialism of Micro Channel architecture (“a computer bus standard for connecting internal components”)

mcar.gloss: Initialism of missing completely at random.

mckinley.gloss: A processor of Intel’s first Itanium 2 brand, code-named McKinley.

mcmc.gloss: Initialism of Markov chain Monte Carlo.

mcts.gloss: Initialism of Monte Carlo tree search.

md5.gloss: Initialism of Message Digest 5, a cryptographic hash function.

md5-summed.gloss: Having had its MD5 checksum computed.

mdct.gloss: Initialism of modified discrete cosine transform.

meager.gloss: Of a set: such that, considered as a subset of a (usually larger) topological space, it is in a precise sense small or negligible.

meagre.gloss: Of a set: such that, considered as a subset of a (usually larger) topological space, it is in a precise sense small or negligible.

mealy machine.gloss: A finite-state machine whose output values are determined by both its current state and its current inputs.

mean.gloss: Any function of multiple variables that satisfies certain properties and yields a number representative of its arguments; or, the number so yielded; a measure of central tendency.

Any function of multiple variables that satisfies certain properties and yields a number representative of its arguments; or, the number so yielded; a measure of central tendency. The average of a set of values, calculated by summing them together and dividing by the number of terms.
Either of the two numbers in the middle of a conventionally presented proportion, as 2 and 3 in 1:2=3:6.

mean absolute deviation.gloss: In a set of data, the average of the absolute values of the deviations from a chosen central point.

mean hitting time.gloss: The average number of steps that a Markov chain takes to go from a specified starting state to a specified target state or set of states.

mean value theorem.gloss: Any of various theorems that saliently concern mean values.

meander.gloss: A self-avoiding closed curve which intersects a line a number of times.

meandric number.gloss: The number of distinct meanders of a given order.

meanless.gloss: Having no (mathematical) mean, or having a mean of zero.

measurable function.gloss: A function whose codomain is a topological space and domain is a measurable space, with the property that the inverse image of every open set in its codomain is a measurable set in its domain.
Any well-behaved function of real numbers between measurable spaces.

measurable set.gloss: A subset of a given measurable space which is a member of the σ-algebra of that space.

measurable space.gloss: A set with a σ-algebra defined on it.

measure.gloss: The act or result of measuring. A number which is contained in a given number a number of times without a remainder; a divisor or factor.

The act or result of measuring. A function which obeys a particular set of formal conditions, created to generalize and rigorize the notions of length, volume, and probability. Formally, a non-negative, countably additive set function on a sigma-algebra; see Measure (mathematics) on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

measure of central tendency.gloss: A measure of location for a batch, a sample, or a distribution characterizing a value around which are spread the members or the distribution.

measure of location.gloss: A single number used to characterize a batch, sample, or distribution or the position of an element of it.

measure space.gloss: A measurable space which has a positive measure defined on its σ-algebra.

measure theory.gloss: A branch of mathematical analysis, concerned with the theory of integration, that generalizes the intuitive notions of length, area and volume.

meatball.gloss: A menu icon of three horizontal dots.

mebibit.gloss: Strictly, 2²⁰ (1024², or 1,048,576) bits or 2¹⁰ (1024) kibibits, as opposed to a megabit.

mebibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2²⁰ (1024², or 1,048,576) bytes or 2¹⁰ (1024) kibibytes, as opposed to a megabyte.

mechanical mouse.gloss: A pointing device which uses a ball to detect movement.

medcouple.gloss: A scaled median difference between the two halves of a distribution.

media.gloss: Files and data comprising material viewable by humans, but usually not plain text; audiovisual material.

media player.gloss: A software application for the playback of audio or video files.
A hardware device that performs the same function, often also acting as a data storage device.

medial.gloss: Of or pertaining to a mean or average.

medial graph.gloss: A graph derived from a given plane graph such that this derived graph has a vertex corresponding to each edge of the given graph, and such that for every “angle” (consecutive trio of edge, vertex, edge) along the border of a face of the given graph there is a corresponding edge which connects the vertices corresponding to the two edges that are part of that “angle”.

median.gloss: A line segment joining the vertex of triangle to the midpoint of the opposing side.

A number separating the higher half from the lower half of a data sample, population, or probability distribution. The median of a finite list of numbers can be found by arranging all the observations from lowest value to highest value and picking the middle one (e.g., the median of {3, 3, 5, 9, 11} is 5). If there is an even number of observations, then there is no single middle value; the median is then usually defined to be the mean of the two middle values.
Having the median as its value.

median filter.gloss: A filter that replaces signal values in a neighbourhood with the median of that neighbourhood.

mediant.gloss: A rational number whose numerator is the sum of the numerators of two other given rational numbers and whose denominator is the sum of the denominators of those same two other rational numbers.

mediary.gloss: Storing data that is written by one process so that it can be read by another process.

mediatrix.gloss: A bisector, the line that is perpendicular to a line segment and intersects the line segment at its midpoint.

medical informatics.gloss: Informatics as applied to medicine: the application of information science and information technology to medical care and any other health care.

medium.gloss: The mean or middle term of a syllogism, that by which the extremes are brought into connection.

medoid.gloss: A mathematically representative object in a set of objects; it has the smallest average dissimilarity to all other objects in the set.

meet.gloss: The greatest lower bound, an operation between pairs of elements in a lattice, denoted by the symbol ∧.

mega menu.gloss: A complex menu that may incorporate subheadings, images, and other content.

megabinary.gloss: Relating to the units prefixed mebi-, such as the mebibyte as opposed to the megabyte.

megabit.gloss: One million (10⁶, or 1,000,000) bits or 1,000 kilobits. Equals 125,000 bytes (125 kilobytes).

megabyte.gloss: One million (10⁶, or 1,000,000) bytes or 1,000 kilobytes.

megademo.gloss: A large, long-running demo (audiovisual presentation), sometimes one that multiloads.

megaflop.gloss: megaflops (one million FLOPS, or floating point operations per second)

megaflops.gloss: a measure of the speed of a computer; one million floating point operations per second.

megagon.gloss: A polygon with one million sides.
A polygon with a vastly larger number of sides, used in the definition of Moser's number.

megahack.gloss: A massive hack of a computer system.

megamenu.gloss: A dropdown menu that expands into a relatively large and complex interface rather than a simple vertical list of commands.

megaprime.gloss: A prime number with at least one million decimal digits.

megaword.gloss: A unit of storage or capacity equal to 10⁶ (or 2²⁰) words

mellin transform.gloss: An integral transform that may be regarded as the multiplicative version of the two-sided Laplace transform.

melonic.gloss: Pertaining to a leading order graph.

melt.gloss: Acronym of metrics, events, logs, and traces.

mem.gloss: A memory access as part of processing.

member.gloss: One of the propositions making up a syllogism.
Either of the two parts of an algebraic equation, connected by the equality sign.
A file stored within an archive file.

member function.gloss: A function that belongs to a class and can be called on instances of the object defined by that class.

member variable.gloss: A variable that is associated with each instance of a class and can be accessed from all its methods.

membership.gloss: The fact of being a member of a set.

membership function.gloss: A generalization of the indicator function for a fuzzy set which assigns a truth value (0 or 1) to each element.

memberwise.gloss: In terms of members (items associated with class instances).

memcomputer.gloss: A computer that has very fast (even instantaneous) access to memory

memcomputing.gloss: computing by means of a memcomputer

memo.gloss: A record of partial results that can be reused later without recomputation.

memoization.gloss: A technique in which partial results are recorded (forming a memo) and then can be re-used later without having to recompute them.

memoize.gloss: To store (the result of a computation) so that it can be subsequently retrieved without repeating the computation.

memoizer.gloss: An algorithm or software component that memoizes.

memoried.gloss: Having a memory (of a given kind).

memory.gloss: The part of a computer that stores variable executable code or data (RAM) or unalterable executable code or default data (ROM).

memory balloon.gloss: A pool of memory in the system of memory ballooning.

memory ballooning.gloss: A technique used to eliminate the need to overcommit host memory used by virtual machines by letting each VM effectively "give back" unused pages of virtual memory.

memory barrier.gloss: An instruction that enforces an ordering constraint on memory operations issued before and after it.

memory card.gloss: A solid state digital memory storage format, commonly found on computers, digital cameras and cellphones.
A personal computer's expansion memory module that fits in a standard interface such as a PCI or ISA slot.

memory cell.gloss: A fundamental block of computer memory.

memory chip.gloss: A RAM, ROM, PROM, EPROM or EEPROM microchip that can be plugged into a personal computer to provide temporary or permanent memory.

memory core.gloss: A (semi-)permanent computer memory storage device that may be extracted, and may or may not be separate from the computer core.

memory hole.gloss: A fragment of physical address space which does not map to main memory.
Synonym of memory leak (“any of several faults in the memory allocation logic of a computer or program whereby parts of memory become hidden or unusable”).

memory leak.gloss: Any of several faults in the memory allocation logic of a computer or program whereby parts of memory become hidden or unusable.

memory page.gloss: A fixed-length contiguous block of virtual memory, representing the smallest division of a page table.

memory safety.gloss: Protection from software bugs and security vulnerabilities resulting from improper memory management, such as buffer overflows and dangling pointers.

memory stick.gloss: One of a series of memory devices manufactured by the Sony Corporation ranging in size from a USB drive down to a flash card.

A portable solid-state electronic flash memory data storage device equipped with a USB (or similarly specified) plug for direct connection to a corresponding port; a USB drive, thumb drive or pen drive.

memory unit.gloss: A component of a computer system used to store data, instructions and information.

memory-safe.gloss: Of a program or programming language, able to ensure memory safety.

memory-unsafe.gloss: Of a program or programming language, not memory-safe.

memoryless.gloss: Of a probability distribution, such that any derived probability from a set of random samples is distinct and has no information (i.e. "memory") of earlier samples.

menger sponge.gloss: A fractal curve, a three-dimensional generalization of the Cantor set and Sierpinski carpet, formed by repeated subdivision of a cube, and having infinite surface area and zero volume.

mensuration.gloss: The study of measurement, especially the derivation and use of algebraic formulae to measure the areas, volumes and different parameters of geometric figures.

menu.gloss: A list from which the user may select an operation to be performed, often done with a keyboard, mouse, or controller under a graphical user interface.

menu bar.gloss: A rectangular region of a graphical user interface where computer menus are housed.

menuing.gloss: The use of menus in a graphical user interface.

merate.gloss: Any of the independent quantities making up a holor.

mereological.gloss: Of or pertaining to mereology, a collection of axiomatic first-order theories dealing with parts and their respective wholes.

mereology.gloss: The discipline which deals with the relationship of parts with their respective wholes.

mereotopology.gloss: A theory combining mereology and topology, investigating relations between parts and wholes and boundaries between them.

merge.gloss: To combine two or more versions of a file into one file, especially using a version control system.

merge-purge.gloss: To combine two lists of data, removing any duplicate entries.

mergesort.gloss: A divide and conquer sorting algorithm that operates by dividing the items to be sorted into many small lists and gradually merging them together.
To sort with such an algorithm.

meridian.gloss: A line passing through the poles of any sphere; a notional line on the surface of a curved or round body (in particular, an eyeball).

meridiem.gloss: The property of a timestamp of being either a.m. or p.m.

merkle-patricia tree.gloss: A tree data structure that combines properties of Merkle trees and Patricia trees.

meromorphic.gloss: That is the ratio of two holomorphic functions (and so possibly infinite at a discrete set of points).

merotopy.gloss: The set of all subsets of a topological space such that, for some element in that space every neighbourhood of that element contains a member of the subset.

mersenne prime.gloss: A prime number which is one less than a power of two (i.e., is expressible in the form 2ⁿ-1; for example, 31=2⁵-1).

mersenne twister.gloss: A kind of pseudorandom number generator whose period length is chosen to be a Mersenne prime.

mesh.gloss: A network topology with each device connected to multiple other devices in lieu of a central switch. Redundancy on a mesh network prevents single points of failure.

mesh network.gloss: A communications network with at least two pathways to each node, forming a net-like organization. When each node is connected to every other node, the network is said to be fully meshed. When only some of the nodes are linked, switching is required to make all the connections and the network is said to be partially meshed, or partially connected.

meshable.gloss: Capable of being converted to a polygon mesh.

meshlet.gloss: A subset of a polygon mesh.

mesokurtic.gloss: Of a distribution: having kurtosis equal to that of a normal distribution; equivalently, having zero excess kurtosis.

mesokurtosis.gloss: The property of having kurtosis equal to that of a normal distribution; equivalently, having zero excess kurtosis.

mesologarithm.gloss: A logarithm of the cosine or cotangent.

message board.gloss: A system by which users may send, read and reply to public messages; an electronic bulletin board or forum.

message broker.gloss: An intermediary program that translates a message from the formal messaging protocol of the sender to the formal messaging protocol of the receiver in a telecommunication network where programs communicate by exchanging formally-defined messages.

message coupling.gloss: the loosest form of coupling that can be achieved by a state of decentralization

message queue.gloss: A queue onto which messages may be placed for delivery between components as part of interprocess communication.

message-driven bean.gloss: A type of Enterprise JavaBean (EJB) designed to process messages asynchronously, acting as a listener for Java Message Service (JMS) or JCA messages.

message-oriented middleware.gloss: Hardware or software infrastructure supporting sending and receiving of messages between distributed systems

messaging pattern.gloss: A network-oriented architectural pattern that describes how two different parts of a message pass system connect and communicate with each other.

meta key.gloss: A special key on some kinds of keyboard, used to activate keyboard shortcuts.

meta-analysis.gloss: Any systematic procedure for statistically combining the results of many different studies.
An analysis resulting from combining the results of diverse statistical studies.

meta-induction.gloss: The use of inductive reasoning to select the best choice from a number of different methods of prediction.

metaball.gloss: An n-dimensional object with an organic appearance, characterised by the ability to meld into others when in close proximity.

metabelianization.gloss: Conversion to, or viewing as metabelian form

metachannel.gloss: A transmission channel used for event notifications rather than actual data.

metacharacter.gloss: A character used to signify something other than its literal form, such as the asterisk when used as a wildcard.

metacircularity.gloss: The property of an interpreter that is written in the same programming language that it interprets, and that exploits homoiconicity to reuse the existing facilities of the parent interpreter rather than reimplementing them.

metaclassifier.gloss: A classifier that operates on other classifiers.

metacommand.gloss: A command that is not part of the language being written but serves as a directive to the interpreter or compiler.

metacompact.gloss: Of a topological space: such that every open cover has a point finite open refinement. That is, given any open cover of the topological space, there is a refinement which is again an open cover with the property that every point is contained only in finitely many sets of the refining cover.

metacompilation.gloss: A computation which involves metasystem transitions from a computing machine to a metamachine which controls, analyzes and imitates the work of the original machine.

metacompiler.gloss: A compiler used to construct compilers for other programming languages.

metacomputation.gloss: The transformation of computer programs based on their semantics.

metaconjecture.gloss: A conjecture that holds for most, but not all, conditions

metacube.gloss: A kind of computer architecture derived from the hypercube and intended for use with large-scale parallel systems.

metadata.gloss: Structured information about a file (date created, creator, software used to create, last modified, file format, file fingerprint, etc).

metadatabase.gloss: A database that serves to catalogue and classify other databases.

metadataset.gloss: A data set composed of metadata.

metadirectory.gloss: A directory service that lists other directory services.

metadynamics.gloss: An algorithmic method of simulating rare complex systems and for calculating the free energy associated with them

metafile.gloss: A file in any format that can store multiple types of data, typically a graphics file format.

metafinite.gloss: Describing a structure composed of a finite part, an infinite part, and a form of mapping between the two

metafunction.gloss: A function which calls all the other functions of a certain program; the only function that can be called independently.
A construct that performs a mapping between entities at compile time.

metagraph.gloss: A graphical representation of a set of objects and the morphisms relating them

metalanguage.gloss: Any similar language used to define a programming language

metalearning.gloss: A form of machine learning where automatic learning algorithms are applied to metadata about machine learning experiments, so that the machine learns how to learn.

metalog.gloss: A flexible continuous probability distribution designed for ease of use.

metamethod.gloss: A method belonging to a metatable.

metamodel.gloss: A model of the modelling process itself.

metanode.gloss: A node, in a graph, that represents a subgraph that is at a lower level of abstraction

metaobject.gloss: Any entity that manipulates, creates, describes, or implements others

metaoperator.gloss: In the Perl and Raku programming languages, an operator that can combine with other operators.

metapackage.gloss: A software package that contains no software itself, but serves to install a particular set of other packages.

metaparameter.gloss: A parameter that controls the value of one or more others.

metaphor.gloss: The use of an everyday object or concept to represent an underlying facet of the computer and thus aid users in performing tasks.

metaphysics.gloss: The metalogic of physics; the logical framework of physics.

metapipeline.gloss: A kind of pipeline that exploits nested parallelism.

metaplectic.gloss: Describing a specific form of symplectic group.

metaprogram.gloss: A computer program that writes or manipulates other programs as data, or does the work at runtime that would otherwise be done at compile time.

metaprogrammer.gloss: One who uses the technique of metaprogramming.

metaprogramming.gloss: The writing of computer programs that write or manipulate other programs or themselves as their data, or that perform operations at runtime that would typically be done at compile time.

metaprotocol.gloss: A protocol that dictates the form of other protocols.

metaregression.gloss: A form of subgroup analysis that is used to investigate heterogeneity across multiple trials

metasearch.gloss: A search technology that uses the results from a number of traditional search engines.
An individual search operation of this kind.
To perform a search of this kind.

metasequence.gloss: A sequence of characters having a similar role to a metacharacter.

metaserver.gloss: A hardware or software system that uses a group of other servers to obtain results

metaservice.gloss: An abstraction of the workflow in a network

metasoftware.gloss: Software that controls or manages other software.

metaspace.gloss: The conceptual space occupied by metaobjects.

metasprite.gloss: A sprite made up from a number of smaller hardware sprites that are moved together.

metastore.gloss: An area set aside in certain database systems for the storage of metadata.

metastring.gloss: A string of characters used as a placeholder for a variable data item.

metasurface.gloss: A generalization of the metaball, not necessarily spherical.

metasyntactic.gloss: Used in describing syntax; relating to metasyntax.
