metasyntactic variable.gloss: A conventional variable name used for an unspecified entity whose exact nature depends on context.

metatable.gloss: A table (of key-value pairs) associated with another object, which uses the functions (or other data) it contains to define the behaviour of that object under certain conditions.

metatheorem.gloss: A statement about theorems proven in a metalanguage.

metavariable.gloss: A symbol or string of symbols belonging to a metalanguage and standing for elements of some object language.

metaverse.gloss: A hypothetical future (counterpart or continuation of the) Internet, created by the convergence of virtually enhanced physical reality and physically persistent virtual space.

methuselah.gloss: A small pattern that takes many generations to stabilize.

metric.gloss: A function which satisfies a particular set of formal conditions, created to generalize the notion of the distance between two points. Formally, a real-valued function d on M×M, where M is a set, is called a metric if (1) d(x,y)=0 if and only if x=y, (2) d(x,y)=d(y,x) for all pairs (x,y), and (3) d obeys the triangle inequality.

metric space.gloss: Any set on which a metric is defined, giving a distance between any two elements.

metric-compatible.gloss: Of a font, having identical metrics as another font, enabling it to serve as a substitute for another font without affecting document layout.

metriplectic.gloss: Describing a structure, on a smooth manifold, that consists of a pair of tensors: a skew-symmetric Poisson tensor and a symmetric metric tensor.

metrizable.gloss: Of a topological space: for which a metric exists that will induce the original topology.

metrization.gloss: The process or result of metrizing a topological space.

metrize.gloss: To associate with an appropriate metric space.

metropolis light transport.gloss: The application of a variant of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm to the rendering equation for generating images from detailed physical descriptions of three-dimensional scenes.

mex.gloss: The mex of a subset of a well-ordered set is the smallest value from the whole set that does not belong to the subset.

meyer set.gloss: A set relatively dense X of points in the Euclidean plane or a higher-dimensional Euclidean space such that its Minkowski difference with itself is uniformly discrete. They are now best known as a mathematical model for quasicrystals.

meyniel graph.gloss: A graph in which every odd cycle of length five or more has at least two chords.

mfc.gloss: Initialism of multifunction centre, a printer-scanner combination, sometimes with a fax machine included.

mfcc.gloss: Initialism of Mel-scale Frequency Cepstral Coefficient.

mickey.gloss: The smallest distance that a computer mouse can move a cursor on a screen, which is used to measure the device's resolution or sensitivity.

micro-optimization.gloss: Optimization at the level of individual instructions and operations.

microaddress.gloss: A location or address within the control memory (microcode store) of a microprogrammed control unit, used to fetch or branch to a specific microinstruction.

microapp.gloss: A very small application, often one of a group that are integrated into a website

microarchitect.gloss: A person who designs a microarchitecture.

microarchitecture.gloss: The architecture of the data processing parts of a microcomputer.

microassembler.gloss: An assembler that operates on microcode.

microbenchmark.gloss: A benchmark designed to measure the performance of a very small and specific piece of code.

microbenchmarking.gloss: Measuring the performance of a small piece of code that executes in microseconds or nanoseconds.

microbrowser.gloss: Any relatively small web browser designed for use on a mobile phone or similar technology

microbundle.gloss: A kind of generalization of a vector bundle.

microcode.gloss: The collective microprograms in a CPU, used to run machine instructions.
To write or rewrite (program instructions) in microcode, typically to optimize performance.

microcomputer.gloss: A computer designed around a microprocessor, smaller than a minicomputer or a mainframe.
A microprocessor that is based on a single chip.

microcontroller.gloss: A microcomputer on a single chip, used to control some device such as an automobile engine or a toy.

microdata.gloss: Data concerning individuals in a trial, survey etc.

microdocument.gloss: A short subsection of a document.

microdrive.gloss: An early computer storage system using cartridges of looped tape.

microfacet.gloss: A tiny facet of the surface of an object being rendered, used in approximating reflections, etc.

microformal.gloss: "Thickened" using formal canonical relations between the cotangent bundles of smooth manifolds.

microformat.gloss: A simple data format that can be embedded in a webpage.

microinstruction.gloss: A hardware instruction in the CPU of a microprocessor; a software instruction in a microprogram

microinteraction.gloss: Any very small-scale interaction between a user and the system they are using.

microlibrary.gloss: A compact, minimalistic library (set of routines).

microlocal.gloss: Local with respect to both space and cotangent space.

microlog.gloss: A section of non-volatile memory used to record state information.

microoperation.gloss: Any of several simpler operations that form a more complex machine instruction

microoperative.gloss: Relating to, or implemented by means of microoperations

microprocessor.gloss: The entire CPU of a computer on a single integrated circuit (chip).

microprogram.gloss: A set of microinstructions in a CPU, used to implement machine instructions.

microroutine.gloss: A microscale routine, one written in microcode.

microsequencer.gloss: A device that generates addresses in a microprogram

microserver.gloss: A simple server requiring little or no configuration.

microservice.gloss: A small independent process that communicates with other processes, used to break down a complex task into many simpler components.

microsoft tax.gloss: The licence fee for the Microsoft Windows operating system software that is pre-installed on many home computer systems.

microsupport.gloss: A closed involutive cone in the cotangent bundle of codirections in which the cohomology of the object does not propagate.

microtexture.gloss: A small-scale texture used to produce fine detail.

microthread.gloss: A thread (typically one executed in parallel) in a microprocessor

microtrajectory.gloss: A microscopic trajectory (one of a series used in calculating a real trajectory)

microwalk.gloss: To walk using very small steps

midamble.gloss: A portion of data located in the middle of a file or stream.

midcircle.gloss: The circle (if one exists) that passes through the midpoint of each side of a given polygon, especially a triangle.

midclick.gloss: A point in time when the user is clicking something.
While the user is clicking something.

midcorrelation.gloss: A correlation between the medians of two populations

middle term.gloss: The term of a syllogism that appears in both the major premise and the minor premise, but not in the conclusion.

middle-click.gloss: To press the middle button on a computer mouse.
To activate an item on the screen by middle-clicking while the pointer is over it.

middlebox.gloss: A device in the Internet that provides transport policy enforcement, such as a firewall.

middleware.gloss: Software that functions at an intermediate layer between applications and operating system or database management system, or between client and server.

Networking software or hardware that is deployed in the middle of, as opposed to serviced by, a packet network to enhance or provide some network function, such as caching, filtering, or firewall functionality.

middleweight spaceship.gloss: A particular orthogonal spaceship in Conway's Game of Life, and the second smallest such example.

midframe.gloss: During a frame; before the completion of a discrete chunk of data.

midhinge.gloss: A measure of location of a batch or sample equal to the average of the first and third quartiles. Equivalently, it is the 25% trimmed mid-range.

midlet.gloss: An application that uses the Mobile Information Device Profile of the Connected Limited Device Configuration for the embedded Java environment.

midpoint.gloss: A point which divides a line segment into two lines of equal length.

midrise.gloss: Having a zero-valued classification threshold (analogous to a riser of a stairway).

midsphere.gloss: The sphere which, if it exists, is tangent to every edge of a given polyhedron and with respect to which the polyhedron's vertices are the inversion poles of the planes of the faces of its dual polyhedron (and vice versa).
The sphere, between two given spheres, by which each of the latter may be inverted into the other.

midsquare quadrilateral.gloss: A quadrilateral whose diagonals are perpendicular and of equal length, so that its four edges' midpoints form a square.

midstring.gloss: Within a string of text characters.
Within a string of text characters.

midtread.gloss: Having a zero-valued reconstruction level (analogous to a tread of a stairway).

migrate.gloss: To move computer code or files from one computer or network to another.

migration.gloss: Instance of changing a platform from an environment to another one.

migrator.gloss: A computer program that helps move objects between locations, e.g. from a legacy system to a new technology.

millicpu.gloss: A unit of CPU time equivalent to a thousandth of the work that can be done by one CPU core.

millile.gloss: Any of the values in a series that divides the distribution of individuals in that series into a thousand groups of equal frequency.

millipawn.gloss: One thousandth of the value of a pawn, especially for calculation purposes in computer chess.

mimd.gloss: Acronym of multiple instruction, multiple data.

mimic function.gloss: A function that modifies a file to make it assume the statistical properties of another file.

min-entropy.gloss: The smallest of the Rényi family of entropies, corresponding to the most conservative way of measuring the unpredictability of a set of outcomes, as the negative logarithm of the probability of the most likely outcome.

minaswan.gloss: Initialism of Matz is nice and so we are nice: a motto of the Ruby programming language community, in reference to the demeanor of Yukihiro Matsumoto (nicknamed Matz, born 1965), the Japanese computer scientist who designed the language.

mine.gloss: A machine or network of machines used to extract units of a cryptocurrency.

minesweep.gloss: To click or hover the cursor over inconspicuous areas to find a hidden link.

minesweeper.gloss: Any of various logic-based computer games in which the player has to discover the position of mines in a rectangular grid, based on numerical hints.

minheap.gloss: A heap data structure with a "greater than or equal to" comparison function.

mini tower.gloss: A relatively small tower case for a computer system.

minicomputer.gloss: A computer smaller than a mainframe, but larger than a microcomputer.

minidriver.gloss: A device-specific plug-in that connects to a generic utility that is supplied with the operating system to form a device driver.

minidump.gloss: A small core dump comprising 64 kilobytes of memory (on 32-bit systems) or 128 kilobytes (on 64-bit systems).

minification.gloss: The removal of white space and unnecessary characters from a web page's source code in order to reduce its size and improve download time.

minifier.gloss: A program that minifies, or removes unnecessary characters to make a document smaller.

minifloat.gloss: A floating-point number represented with very few bits (such as 8 or 16, when a more common size would be 32 or 64 bits).

minify.gloss: To remove white space and unnecessary characters from source code in order to reduce its size.

minilanguage.gloss: A relatively small and simple domain-specific language.

minimal.gloss: The smallest possible amount, quantity, or degree. Among elements of some collection, such that no other element is greater (with respect to some given partial order).

minimal ideal.gloss: A nonzero (two-sided) ideal that contains no other nonzero two-sided ideal.

minimal polynomial.gloss: For a given square matrix M over some field K, the smallest-degree monic polynomial over K which, when applied to M, yields the zero matrix.

minimal prime.gloss: A prime number whose digital representation contains no smaller subsequence that is also prime.

minimal recursion semantics.gloss: A computational semantic framework employed in typed feature structure formalisms.

minimal surface.gloss: Any surface that has the least possible surface area of those into which it could transform; typically the shapes of soap bubbles that span wire frames

minimax.gloss: A decision rule used for minimizing the maximum possible loss, or maximizing the minimum gain.

minimin.gloss: A strategy or algorithm that seeks to minimize the minimum possible result.

minimization.gloss: The process of finding the minimum value of a function.

minimize.gloss: To remove (a window) from the main display area, collapsing it to an icon or caption.

minimum.gloss: A lower bound of a set which is also an element of that set.
The smallest member of a batch or sample or the lower bound of a probability distribution.

minimum cut.gloss: A cut that is minimal in some metric.

minimum seek time.gloss: The amount of time required to move the head of a disk drive from one track to the next.

minimum spanning tree.gloss: A spanning tree that has minimum possible weight for a given graph.

miniport.gloss: A port that uses a lightweight driver that relies on built-in support from the operating system.

minisupercomputer.gloss: A computer capable of vector processing and small-scale multiprocessing, a cheaper alternative to a full supercomputer in the 1980s.

minkowski inequality.gloss: An inequality that establishes that the Lp spaces are normed vector spaces.

minkowski space.gloss: A four-dimensional real vector space equipped with an inner product of signature (−,+,+,+) or (+,−,−,−), in which special relativity is formulated

minkowski spacetime.gloss: A geometrically flat spacetime, i.e. one with zero curvature.

minkowski-bouligand dimension.gloss: A way of determining the fractal dimension of a set in a Euclidean space, or more generally in a metric space. It may be visualized by imagining the fractal lying on an evenly-spaced grid and counting how many boxes are required to cover the set. The dimension is then calculated by seeing how this number changes as the grid is made finer.

minor.gloss: Lesser, smaller in importance, size, degree, seriousness, or significance compared to another option Of or related to a minor, a determinate obtained by deleting one or more rows and columns from a matrix.

minor premise.gloss: The second premise in a categorical syllogism, whose subject is the minor term and whose predicate is the middle term.

minor term.gloss: The subject of the conclusion in a categorical syllogism.

minorant.gloss: A function, all of whose values are not greater than the corresponding values of another function.

minorate.gloss: To replace a term by its lower bound.

minorization.gloss: The action of forming a lower bound

minorize.gloss: To be or become a lower bound

minus-plus sign.gloss: the symbol ∓, meaning "minus or plus", used alongside the plus-minus sign to show that a negative value is to be taken where the positive value is indicated by the plus-minus sign, and vice versa (as in (x ± 1) / (x ∓ 2), which means (x + 1) / (x - 2) and (x - 1) / (x + 2).

mipmap.gloss: A precalculated, optimised collection of images accompanying a main texture, used to increase rendering speed and reduce aliasing artifacts.

mipmapping.gloss: The creation or use of mipmaps.

mips.gloss: Initialism of million instructions per second.

mirabolic.gloss: Being or relating to a subgroup of the general linear group GLₙ(k) that consists of automorphisms fixing a given non-zero vector in kⁿ. Its image in the projective general linear group is a parabolic subgroup consisting of all elements fixing a given point of projective space.

mirror.gloss: A website or server that contains replicated data from another site.
To create something identical to (a website, etc.).

mirror server journal.gloss: A mechanism used to maintain data consistency and support recovery by recording any changes that are made in data.

mirror symmetry.gloss: A relationship between Calabi-Yau manifolds where two such manifolds look very different geometrically but are nevertheless equivalent when employed as extra dimensions of string theory.

misclick.gloss: A click of a computer mouse that is inaccurate and therefore fails to perform the desired action.

misd.gloss: Acronym of multiple instruction, single data.

misfactor.gloss: To err when determining the factors of.

misfetch.gloss: An error that occurs when the wrong block of code is fetched in advance.

misproof.gloss: A mathematical proof that contains logical errors.

misrelay.gloss: The modification or dropping of routing packets, causing a disruption of communication between nodes in a network.

miss.gloss: The situation where an item is not found in a cache and therefore needs to be explicitly loaded.

missingness.gloss: The manner in which data are missing from a sample of a population.

mitchell-netravali filter.gloss: Any of a group of bicubic reconstruction filters often used for antialiasing or for scaling raster graphics.

mitm.gloss: Initialism of meet-in-the-middle attack: Cryptographic attack that attempts to find a value in each of the ranges and domains of the composition of two functions such that the forward mapping of one through the first function is the same as the inverse image of the other through the second function.

mitre.gloss: A square with one triangular quarter missing from the outside.

mittag-leffler distribution.gloss: Any member of two families of probability distributions defined with the Mittag-Leffler function.

mittag-leffler star.gloss: A set in the complex plane obtained by attempting to extend a given complex-analytic function along rays emanating from a given point.

mittag-leffler summation.gloss: Any of several variations of the Borel summation method for summing possibly divergent formal power series.

mittenpunkt.gloss: A triangle center defined as the symmedian point of the triangle formed by the centers of the three excircles.

mixed alphabet.gloss: The mapping from plaintext to ciphertext characters in a substitution cipher, when it is not merely a shift or reversal but an arbitrary reordering.

mixed initiative.gloss: A computer-human interaction in which either the computer or the human can take initiative and decide what to do next.

mixed number.gloss: A number consisting of a whole number and a fraction, such as 11½.

mixed raster content.gloss: An image that has been stored as multiple layers under different types of compression, typically a bitonal text and line-art layer, a foreground layer coloring the text and line-art layer, and a full-color background and image layer.

mixfix.gloss: Being or relating to a kind of operator that can combine any of the infix, prefix, postfix, and closed notations.

mixing.gloss: Of a stochastic process, to be asymptotically independent (in a precise mathematical sense).

mixingness.gloss: The quality or characteristic of being mixing.

mixtilinear.gloss: Containing, or consisting of, lines of different kinds (straight, curved, etc.).

mlm.gloss: Initialism of multi-level model or multi-level modeling.

mlse.gloss: Abbreviation of maximum likelihood sequence estimation.

mmb.gloss: Initialism of modular multiplication-based block cipher.

mnar.gloss: Initialism of missing not at random.

mnemonic.gloss: The human-readable, textual form of an assembly language instruction, not including operands.

mob programming.gloss: A software development approach where the whole team works on a single project at a single computer at the same time.

mobile-first.gloss: Designed primarily for mobile rather than desktop devices.

mock.gloss: A mockup or prototype; particularly, ellipsis of mock object, as used in unit testing.

mockable.gloss: Of which a mockup or prototype may be made.

mod.gloss: A module (file containing a tracker music sequence).

modal.gloss: Of, or relating to the modality between propositions.

modal logic.gloss: Any formal system that attempts to deal with modalities, such as possibility and necessity, but also obligation and permission.

modality.gloss: The classification of propositions on the basis on whether they claim possibility, impossibility, contingency or necessity; mode.

mode.gloss: A particular means of accomplishing something. A state of a system that is represented by an eigenfunction of that system. A state related to signals or vibrations.
A particular means of accomplishing something. A state of a system that is represented by an eigenfunction of that system. A wave pattern in the electromagnetic field.
A particular means of accomplishing something. One of various related sets of rules for processing data; more generally, any state of the system associated with certain behaviours.
The most frequently occurring value in a distribution.

model.gloss: An interpretation function which assigns a truth value to each atomic proposition.
An interpretation which makes a set of sentences true, in which case that interpretation is called a model of that set.

model theory.gloss: The study of the relationship between formal theories and their models.

model-view-presenter.gloss: A derivative of the model-view-controller (MVC) architectural pattern, where the presenter assumes the functionality of the "middle-man".

modeler.gloss: a computer program that simulates a physical system
a computer program that generates a three-dimensional representation of an object or system

modeless.gloss: Not modal; not having separate modes in which user input has different effects.
Not modal; not requiring immediate user interaction and thus allowing interaction with other widgets.

modeline.gloss: A status line in a text editor, displaying buffer-dependent information such as the current line number, file size, and filename.
A line of configuration within a text file, dictating the contents of the status line while that file is open for viewing or editing.

modeling.gloss: The construction and use of a computer model of a physical system.

modeling language.gloss: An artificial language used to express information, knowledge, or systems in a structured way defined by a consistent set of rules.

modem.gloss: A device that encodes digital computer signals into analog telephone signals and vice versa, allowing computers to communicate over a phone line.

modified harvard architecture.gloss: A variation of the Harvard computer architecture, allowing the contents of the instruction memory to be accessed as data.

modifier.gloss: A keyword that qualifies the meaning of other code.

modmin.gloss: A user on social media who is either a moderator or an administrator.

module.gloss: A section of a program; a subroutine or group of subroutines.

A file containing a music sequence that can be played in a tracker.

mom.gloss: Initialism of month-over-month/month-on-month; compared to the same time period in the previous month.

monad.gloss: A monoid object in the category of endofunctors of a fixed category.

monadic.gloss: having an arity of one (taking a single argument or operand)

monadic second-order logic.gloss: A formal deductive system which extends first-order logic by the ability to quantify over unary predicates over individual members of the universe of discourse.

moniamond.gloss: The polyiamond made up of a single triangle.

monic.gloss: Of a polynomial whose leading coefficient is one.

To alter the behaviour of a program by forcibly overriding aspects of the original code at runtime.

monocase.gloss: Supporting or consisting of only one case of letters; either all uppercase or all lowercase; (also), case insensitive, treating upper and lower case as being the same.

monodendron.gloss: A maximal connected subgraph of a dendrimer that shares only the coalescence node with a core.

monodromy.gloss: The globalization of local morphisms in category theory

monoexponential.gloss: Involving the exponent of a single variable
The exponent of a single variable

monofractal.gloss: Describing a system that is fractal in only one way.
A system that is fractal in only one way.

monogon.gloss: A one-dimensional object comprising one vertex and one (not necessarily straight) edge both of whose ends are that vertex.
A two-dimensional object comprising one vertex, one edge both of whose ends are that vertex, and one face filling in the hollow formed by that edge.

monogonal.gloss: Of or pertaining to a monogon.
That passes through exactly one vertex (of a polygon or polyhedron).

monohedrally.gloss: In a monohedral manner; involving only copies of the original tile (allowing for translation, rotation, and reflection).

monohedron.gloss: A solid figure with a single continuous surface (face) and no edges, such as a torus or spheroid.

monoid.gloss: A set which is closed under an associative binary operation, and which contains an element which is an identity for the operation.

monomino.gloss: A polyomino consisting of one square.

monomorphic.gloss: Taking only a single data type.

monostatic.gloss: A solid body with a single stable resting point.

monosyllogism.gloss: An argument expressed as a single syllogism

A function f : X→Y (where X and Y are posets with partial order "≤") with either: (1) the property that x ≤ y implies f(x) ≤ f(y), or (2) the property that x ≤ y implies f(y) ≤ f(x).

monotonic function.gloss: A function that either never decreases or never increases as its independent variable increases.

monotonic increasing.gloss: always increasing or remaining constant, and never decreasing; contrast this with strictly increasing

monotonically.gloss: In a monotonic manner, of a function that either never decreases or never increases as its independent variable increases.

monotonicity.gloss: Said of a positive measure: the property of a positive measure of a measure space, that given two measurable sets where the first set is contained in the second one, then the measure of the first set must be less than or equal to the measure of the second set.

monotony.gloss: The property of a monotonic function.

monotype.gloss: In the Hindley–Milner type system, a single specific data type.

monovariant.gloss: A variable whose value changes in one direction only (gets either larger or smaller)

monsterology.gloss: The study of the Monster group.

monstrous moonshine.gloss: The unexpected connection between the Monster group and modular functions, now known to relate to a certain conformal field theory having the Monster group as symmetries.

monte carlo method.gloss: Any of a class of techniques for estimating the solution of a numerical mathematical problem by means of a random artificial sampling experiment that simulates the problem.

moob.gloss: To rapidly adjust the evaluation of a position towards zero, indicating a likely draw.

moonshine.gloss: A branch of pure mathematics relating the Monster group to an invariant of elliptic functions.

moore machine.gloss: A finite-state machine whose output values are determined solely by its current state.

moore neighborhood.gloss: A neighborhood on a 2D square lattice consisting of a cell and its eight orthogonal and diagonal neighbors.

morally.gloss: Used to clarify that a statement is made in analogy, and every detail may not be strictly true.

morbus cyclometricus.gloss: A fascination with finding a way to square the circle (an impossible task in geometry).

morefold.gloss: Being greater than one in number; plural; multiple; multiplex; manifold.

morin surface.gloss: A halfway model of the sphere eversion, featuring fourfold rotational symmetry.

morita equivalence.gloss: A certain relationship defined between algebraic rings that preserves many ring-theoretic properties.

motor variable.gloss: A variable that can be a split-complex number.

motzkin number.gloss: For a given number n, the number of different ways of drawing non-intersecting chords between n points on a circle (not necessarily touching every point by a chord). They have diverse applications in geometry, combinatorics, and number theory.

moufang loop.gloss: A special kind of algebraic structure, similar to a group in many ways but not necessarily associative.

moufang plane.gloss: A type of projective plane whose every line is a translation line.

moufang polygon.gloss: A mathematical generalization of Moufang planes.

mouse.gloss: An input device that is moved over a pad or other flat surface to produce a corresponding movement of a pointer on a graphical display.

mouseover.gloss: The event of an on-screen pointer being over an on-screen shape.

mousework.gloss: Activities requiring the use of a mouse (input device).

moving average.gloss: A weighted average that is determined for a given data point based on its value and the past values.

mozillian.gloss: A member or supporter of Mozilla, a community that develops and supports free software.

mth.gloss: Occurring at position m in a sequence.

mucube.gloss: A regular skew apeirohedron with six squares around each vertex, formed by an infinite number of cubic cells (specifically, cubes missing two opposite faces each, around cubic empty spaces with no faces) in Euclidean 3D space.

mudhead.gloss: A dedicated participant in multi-user dungeons.

muffin.gloss: To transfer files between 13-sector and 16-sector Apple II diskettes, as with MUFFIN (Move Utility For Files In NewDOS.)

multenion.gloss: A tuple consisting of multiple numeric parts, such as a quaternion.

multi-armed bandit.gloss: An algorithm that allocates a fixed limited set of resources between competing alternative choices so as to maximize the expected gain, when each choice's properties are only partially known at the time of allocation, and may become better understood as time passes or allocations are made.

multi-start.gloss: Describing a multiple spiral that starts at the origin and divides the plane into multiple regions

multi-temporal.gloss: Of, relating to, or specifying multidimensional visual datasets, maps, or environment views captured across multiple distinct points in time, serving as the input corpus for vision-language models or predictive neural architectures to decode structural, environmental, or spatial changes.

multi-touch.gloss: Of a computer tablet or touch-screen interface, accepting more than one touch at the same time.

multiaddress.gloss: Of or pertaining to more than one address in memory.

multiaddressing.gloss: The availability of different addresses at the same network endpoint.

multiagent.gloss: Involving more than one agent (actor that can make decisions).

multialgebra.gloss: An algebra composed of a set and a family of multioperations on that set

multiapp.gloss: Involving or relating to several software applications.

multibit.gloss: Contained in more than one bit.

multiboot.gloss: Having several operating systems available, such that any of them can be selected each time the computer is booted.

multibooting.gloss: The use of a multiboot configuration.

multibuffering.gloss: The use of more than one buffer.

multibump.gloss: Having more than one bump (when visualised as a graph, etc.).

multibus.gloss: Involving or relating to more than one bus (electrical conductor or interface).

multibyte.gloss: Contained in more than one byte.

multicache.gloss: Having or relating to more than one cache.

multicast.gloss: The simultaneous transmission of data to several destinations on a network.

multicasting.gloss: The simultaneous transmission of data to several destinations on a network.

multicategory.gloss: A generalization of the concept of category that allows morphisms of multiple arity.

multichain.gloss: Of a Markov chain, consisting of two or more closed sets of recurrent states plus (optionally) a set of states that do not belong to any of the closed sets.

multicharacter.gloss: Consisting of more than one character (unit of text).

multicloud.gloss: Of or relating to more than one cloud, in the context of cloud computing.
The use of cloud computing services from multiple cloud providers.
An application or environment that operates across multiple cloud providers.
To use cloud computing services from multiple cloud providers simultaneously.

multicollinearity.gloss: A phenomenon in which two or more predictor variables in a multiple regression model are highly correlated, so that the coefficient estimates may change erratically in response to small changes in the model or data.

multicolumn.gloss: Of or pertaining to more than one column.

multicomplex.gloss: Of or relating to a class of number systems relating to the imaginary numbers. See Multicomplex number on Wikipedia.

multiconvex.gloss: Relating to multiple convex sets or variables

multicore.gloss: Combining two or more independent cores into a single package composed of a single integrated circuit

multicorn.gloss: The connectedness locus in the space of antiholomorphic unicritical polynomials; The set of parameters for which the Julia set is connected.

multicosimplicial.gloss: Pertaining to a generalization of a cosimplicial space to diagrams of spaces that are cosimplicial in each direction.

multicover.gloss: A combinatorial problem concerning the covering or inclusion of elements by a collection of shapes or sets.
A solution to a multicover problem.

multidegree.gloss: The tuple (properly though a multiset) of the degrees of defining hypersurfaces for a complete intersection.

multidesktop.gloss: Having or supporting more than one desktop.

multideviation.gloss: A generalization of standard deviation to higher orders.
A distance of more than two standard deviations from the mean.

multidifferential.gloss: Pertaining to any of various constructions based on multiple differential equations or operators.

multidigraph.gloss: A directed graph that is permitted to have multiple arcs connecting the same source and target nodes.

multidimensional.gloss: Having multiple dimensions (aspects). Having more than two dimensions.

multidimensional array.gloss: A data structure consisting of a vector of vectors, in the case of a 2-dimensional array, or, in the case of an N-dimensional array, a vector of multidimensional arrays of degree N minus 1, thereby allowing the simulation of a N-dimensional grid of storage locations using an underlying memory architecture in which storage is addressed in a linear fashion.
A data structure that has the semantics of an array of arrays, all of which may be indexed with values of any data type, usually with a supporting syntax built-into a programming language.
Any abstraction, usually a memory-resident data structure, that addresses storage locations via an N-dimensional coordinate space.

multidirectory.gloss: Of or pertaining to more than one directory (container structure in a file system).

multidistance.gloss: An extension of the concept of distance between a pair of points in n-dimensional space.

multidrop.gloss: Of a computer bus, having all components connected to the same set of electrical wires, each component listening for its own data and negotiating with the others in order to send.
A computer bus having all components connected in this manner.

multiextent.gloss: Consisting of more than one extent.

multifactor.gloss: Involving more than one distinct authentication mechanism, such as both a password and facial recognition.

multiflow.gloss: A flow function that operates on the set of edges (ordered pairs of vertices) on the intersection of two related directed graphs.

multiforest.gloss: Of or relating to more than one forest.

multifractal.gloss: Describing a system that is fractal in multiple ways

multigait.gloss: Having multiple gaits to adapt to the environment.

multigerm.gloss: A set of germs of a function that have distinct sources and a common target.

multigraph.gloss: A set V (whose elements are called vertices or nodes), taken together with a multiset E, each of whose elements (called an edge or line) is a cardinality-two multisubset of V.
A set V (as before), taken together with a multiset E, each of whose elements is a cardinality-two subset of V.

multigrid.gloss: A class of techniques for solving algebraic or differential equations that employs a hierarchy of discretizations
Relating to or utilising a multigrid method.

multihome.gloss: To use the technique of multihoming.

multihomed.gloss: Having network reliability increased by means of multihoming.

multihoming.gloss: A technique to increase the reliability of a network connection by means of additional, alternative network interfaces or IP addresses.

multihomogenous.gloss: Pertaining to a sum of terms whose monomials all have the same multidegree

multihop.gloss: Of a question-answering task or system, able to chain together multiple steps of reasoning.

multihopping.gloss: The transmission of data from multiple nodes of a mobile phone network to an individual mobile device simultaneously

multihypergraph.gloss: A set V (whose elements are called vertices or nodes), taken together with a multiset E, each of whose elements (called an edge or hyperedge) is a subset of V.

multijoin.gloss: Of or pertaining to more than one join (intersection of data).

multikey.gloss: A multi-element key into a data structure.

multilicence.gloss: A licence to have the same software on multiple devices

multilinear.gloss: That is linear in each variable separately.

multilinear form.gloss: Given a vector space V over a field K of scalars, a mapping Vᵏ → K that is linear in each of its arguments;

Given a vector space V over a field K of scalars, a mapping Vᵏ → K that is linear in each of its arguments;
(more generally) a similarly multiply linear mapping Mʳ → R defined for a given module M over some commutative ring R. a similarly multiply linear mapping Mʳ → R defined for a given module M over some commutative ring R.

multilingual notation.gloss: A system used in lexical resources to denote words or phrases in multiple languages.

multilingualization.gloss: The act of adapting or localizing something to, into, or for multiple languages

multilingualize.gloss: To adapt or localize something to, into, or for multiple languages.

multilist.gloss: A data structure comprising several lists.

multiloader.gloss: A piece of software that multiloads.

multilock.gloss: A lock that restricts access to more than one object.

multimagic.gloss: Of a magic cube: remaining magic even if all its numbers are replaced by their kth power.

multimagic square.gloss: A magic square that remains magic even if all its numbers are replaced by their kth powers for 1 ≤ k ≤ P.

multimap.gloss: A data structure that maps a single key to multiple values.

multimaster.gloss: Relating to more than one master.

multimedia.gloss: of, or relating to an application that can combine such media into an integrated package

multimemory.gloss: Having or relating to more than one memory.

multimodality.gloss: The presence of multiple modes or maxima in a statistical distribution.

multinacci.gloss: Describing a generalization of Fibonacci numbers

multinumber.gloss: A set with repeated elements that are indistinguishable from one another.

multioperation.gloss: A mapping f:Xⁿ→𝒫(X) for some n∈ℕ₀.

multipart.gloss: of computer printout that is printed in multiple copies on paper having two or four continuous sheets rolled together with interleaving carbon paper; after printing it is separated on a decollator

multipartition.gloss: To logically divide a hard disk into multiple partitions

multipathing.gloss: A network facility providing fault tolerance and load-spreading for network interface cards, each interface being assigned a static "test" IP address for diagnostic purposes.

multiperfect.gloss: Being a generalization of a perfect number. For a given natural number k, a number n is called k-perfect (or k-fold perfect) iff the sum of all positive divisors of n (the divisor function, σ(n)) is equal to kn.

multipermutation.gloss: A generalization of a permutation where every element can appear multiple times.

multiple.gloss: A whole number that is obtained by multiplying a specific whole number by another whole number.

multiple inheritance.gloss: The ability to inherit from more than one superclass in a single subclass.

multiplee.gloss: A partial product, i.e., the result of one step of a full multiplication algorithm.

multiplex.gloss: To combine several signals into one.

multiplexer.gloss: A device that combines several input signals into a single output signal.

multiplication sign.gloss: Any symbol (in particular ×, * or ·) used to denote the operation of multiplication.

multiplicative identity.gloss: An element of an algebraic structure, generally denoted 1, which is an identity for a multiplicative operation (generally denoted × or *, or by concatenation).

multiplicative operation.gloss: An operation of an algebraic structure playing a role analogous to multiplication.

multiplicity.gloss: The number of values for which a given condition holds.
The number of instances that can occur on a given end of a relationship.

multiply.gloss: An act or instance of multiplying.

multipoint.gloss: A collection of points treated as a single object.

multipolygon.gloss: A collection of polygons treated as a single object.

multipost.gloss: To post several copies of (a message) to different newsgroups.

multiprocessor.gloss: A computer that has multiple CPUs or execution units under an integrated control.

multiprogram.gloss: Having or employing multiple programs simultaneously

multiprogramming.gloss: The allocation of computing resources to more than one concurrent application, job, or user.

multipunch.gloss: To punch more than one hole in one column of a punch card, allowing a greater number of unique values to be represented per column.
An instance of more than one hole being punched in one column of a punch card.

multischema.gloss: Of or pertaining to more than one (database) schema.

multiserver.gloss: Involving or pertaining to more than one server.

multisession.gloss: To operate multiple simultaneous sessions, for example allowing many users to be active at one time.

multiset.gloss: A generalized type of set in which multiple occurrences of an element are permitted.

multislave.gloss: Relating to more than one slave.

multisurface.gloss: A collection of surfaces treated as a single object.

multisymplectic.gloss: symplectic in more than one way

multitable.gloss: Involving multiple tables (in various senses). Encompassing or affecting multiple tables.

multitaskable.gloss: Capable of being solved or executed using multitasking.

multitenancy.gloss: The situation in which a single instance of software, running in a server, serves multiple tenants

multitexture.gloss: Of or relating to multiple textures.

multitwist.gloss: An automorphism that induces a set of Dehn twists around a surface.

multitype.gloss: Relating to or consisting of multiple types

multiusing.gloss: multiuser capability; the ability of a computer system to process requests from multiple users at the same time

mumblage.gloss: Mumbled or imprecise remarks, especially remarks which are trivial or unreliable.

mutex.gloss: An object in a program that serves as a lock, used to negotiate mutual exclusion among threads.

mutual information.gloss: A measure of the entropic (informational) correlation between two random variables.

mv*.gloss: Any of various software design approaches involving a model and a view, such as MVC, MVP, or MVVM.

mvc.gloss: Initialism of model-view-controller, an architectural pattern used in software development.

mwips.gloss: Initialism of million Whetstone instructions per second.

mycielskian.gloss: A larger graph formed from a given undirected graph by a particular construction that preserves the property of being triangle-free but increases the chromatic number.

möbius group.gloss: The projective general linear group mathbf PGL(2,ℂ): the group of Möbius transformations on the Riemann sphere.
For a given dimension n, the group of projective transformations leaving a particular hypersphere invariant.

A one-sided surface formed by identifying two opposite edges of a square in opposite senses;
a narrow strip given a half twist and joined at the ends, forming a three-dimensional embedding of said surface. a narrow strip given a half twist and joined at the ends, forming a three-dimensional embedding of said surface.

n-ary.gloss: Of, or relating to, n entities (where n is an arbitrary or large number).

n-dimensional.gloss: Having an arbitrary number of dimensions.

n-dimensional space.gloss: A vector space having n vectors as its basis.

nagware.gloss: Software that displays a message requesting that the user register it.

naive.gloss: Intuitive; designed to follow the way ordinary people approach a problem.

nak.gloss: A negative ACK; a response indicating that a message was not fully received, or that there was a problem with the message.

name.gloss: An identifier, generally a unique string of characters.

name binding.gloss: the association of entities (data and/or code) with identifiers

named.gloss: An argument that is passed to a subroutine according to its name in the invocation code, rather than on its position; compare with positional.

named parameter.gloss: A parameter that is passed by name, rather than by position, in a function call.

named pipe.gloss: An extension to the anonymous pipe concept on Unix and Unix-like systems, used for interprocess communication.

namespace.gloss: A conceptual space that groups classes, identifiers, etc. in order to avoid conflicts with items in unrelated code that carry the same names.
To categorize by placing into a namespace.

namevoter.gloss: One who votes for an entry in a demoscene competition on the basis of its author or demogroup, rather than the actual merits of the work.

namevoting.gloss: Voting for an entry in a demoscene competition because of its author or demogroup rather than its actual merits.

naming collision.gloss: An error caused by two source code elements (such as variables or functions) having the same name as each other.

nan.gloss: Acronym of not a number, applied to numeric values that represent an undefined or unrepresentable value, such as zero divided by itself.
Alternative form of NaN (not a number)

nand.gloss: A binary operator composite of NOT AND; negation of AND function.

nano-com.gloss: The use of a very small subset of the Component Object Model, focused exclusively on the Application Binary Interface (ABI) aspects that enable function and method calls across independently compiled modules.

nanobot.gloss: A very small autonomous robot, typically the size of a biological cell, designed to work alone or in very large numbers to achieve some task.

nanocode.gloss: The microcode used in a nanoprocessor

nanoinstruction.gloss: A hardware instruction in the CPU of a nanoprocessor; a software instruction in a nanoprogram.

nanokernel.gloss: A particularly small or minimal microkernel.

napierian logarithm.gloss: The logarithm to the base e, named after John Napier.

napoleon point.gloss: Either of a pair of special points associated with a plane triangle. (See Wikipedia for detailed definitions.)

nappe.gloss: Either of the two parts of a double cone.

narayana number.gloss: Any of the triangular array of natural numbers defined by N(n, k), n = 1, 2, 3 ..., 1 ≤ k ≤ n, occurring in various counting problems.

narcissistic number.gloss: A number that, in a given base, is the sum of its own digits each raised to the power of the number of digits.

To convert to a data type that cannot hold as many distinct values.

narrowing conversion.gloss: A conversion from one data type to another where the new data type’s size is smaller than the old one’s, such that the conversion may result in loss of information.

narumi polynomial.gloss: Any of a group of polynomials sₙ(x) given by the generating function displaystyle ∑s_n(x)tⁿ/n!=(t/(log (1+t)))ᵃ(1+t)ˣ.

nat.gloss: Acronym of network address translation (“network address rewriting”).

native.gloss: Pertaining to the system or architecture in question.

native bundle.gloss: A self-contained package that includes all the necessary components required to build a native executable or shared library.

native code.gloss: source code written in a code readable by the processor

native support.gloss: a feature that already exists in the environment in which an application is run.
a feature that works out of the box, without the need to install extensions, rely on external modules, or program extensive specific code.

natively.gloss: Pertaining to the computer or architecture in question; without the use of emulation, etc.

natural.gloss: Existing in nature. Designating a standard trigonometric function of an angle, as opposed to the logarithmic function.
Existing in nature. Closed under submodules, direct sums, and injective hulls.

natural isomorphism.gloss: A natural transformation whose every component is an isomorphism.

natural join.gloss: A join between two tables on a field which has the same name.

natural key.gloss: A unique key formed from attributes that relate to the external world being modelled, rather than being an internally generated surrogate key.

natural logarithm.gloss: The logarithm in base e: either the function that given x returns y such that eʸ = x, or the value of y given by the function.

natural numbers object.gloss: An object which has a distinguished global element (which may be called z, for “zero”) and a distinguished endomorphism (which may be called s, for “successor”) such that iterated compositions of s upon z (i.e., sⁿ∘z) yields other global elements of the same object which correspond to the natural numbers (sⁿ∘z↔n). Such object has the universal property that for any other object with a distinguished global element (call it z’) and a distinguished endomorphism (call it s’), there is a unique morphism (call it φ) from the given object to the other object which maps z to z’ (ϕ∘z=z') and which commutes with s; i.e., ϕ∘s=s'∘ϕ.

natural transformation.gloss: A morphism between a pair of parallel functors such that if each object of the shared domain category subtends a correlated arrow — called a component — in the shared codomain (which arrow represents the difference between applying the second functor and the first functor to the correlated object) then each arrow of the shared domain subtends a commuting square — called a naturality square — between two components (correlated to the domain and codomain of the arrow).

natural user interface.gloss: A user interface for a computer that is effectively invisible, or becomes invisible to its users with successive learned interactions.

navbar.gloss: A bar, usually at the top of a web page, offering a number of links to help the user to navigate.

navigate.gloss: To move between web pages, menus, etc. by means of hyperlinks, mouse clicks, or any other mechanism.

navigation bar.gloss: A bar at the top of a graphical user interface containing links that allow users to move around the page and/or program

navigator.gloss: A user interface that allows navigating through a structure of any kind.

nbf.gloss: Initialism of nearest block first, a disk scheduling algorithm or approach

nbmr.gloss: Initialism of negative binomial multiple regression.

nc.gloss: Initialism of Nick's Class, the complexity class of decision problems solvable in polylogarithmic time using a polynomial number of processors.

near.gloss: Within the currently selected segment in a segmented memory architecture.

nearline.gloss: Having a level of availability somewhere between online and offline, typically using removable media.

nebentypus.gloss: The character χ, as applied to a modular form.

neededness.gloss: Dependency; the state of one segment of code requiring another segment to complete.

needle.gloss: A text string that is searched for within another string. (see: needle in a haystack)

nef.gloss: Of a line bundle on a complete algebraic variety over a field: such that the degree of its restriction to every algebraic curve in the variety is non-negative.

negabicomplex.gloss: Related to a bicomplex value by a power of -1.

negafibonacci.gloss: Of or pertaining to the Fibonacci sequence extended to negative indices.

negand.gloss: The proposition that is to be negated.

negate.gloss: To perform the NOT operation on.

negation.gloss: A proposition which is the contradictory of another proposition and which can be obtained from that other proposition by the appropriately placed addition, or insertion, of the word "not". (Or, in symbolic logic, by prepending that proposition with the symbol for the logical operator "not".)
The logical operation which obtains such (negated) propositions.

negative.gloss: Of a number: less than zero.
Of a number: less than zero. Less than zero degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit.
