operand.gloss: A quantity to which an operator is applied (in 3-x, the operands of the subtraction operator are 3 and x).

operating system.gloss: Software that is designed for controlling the allocation and the use of various hardware resources to tasks and remote terminals.

operating time.gloss: The time interval between the instant a request for service is received from a user and the instant of final release of all facilities by the user or either of two users.

operation.gloss: A procedure for generating a value from one or more other values (the operands).
A procedure for generating a value from one or more other values (the operands). A function which maps zero or more (but typically two) operands to a single output value.

operational calculus.gloss: The study of calculus from the perspective of the theory of operators.

operator.gloss: A function or other mapping that carries values defined on a domain into another value or set of values in a defined range.
The administrator of a channel or network on IRC.
A symbol that represents a construct in a programming language and differs from a normal function in its syntax.

operator theory.gloss: A branch of functional analysis, being the study of linear operators on function spaces.

operatorial.gloss: Of or pertaining to an operator

opinionated.gloss: Enforcing one particular approach instead of offering options and flexibility.

oplax.gloss: Pertaining to the dual of a lax monoidal functor.

oplock.gloss: An opportunistic lock on a file system object, used for caching purposes rather than to avoid modifications by multiple users at once.

opmask.gloss: A bit mask used to select elements in vector processing.

opmn.gloss: Abbreviation of Oracle Process Management and Notification.

opmonoidal.gloss: Having a natural family of distributive morphisms and an identity morphism that are coherent.

opposite.gloss: Something or someone opposite to something or someone else. An additive inverse.

opposite angle.gloss: Either of the angles directly opposite to each other when two lines intersect in a plane.

opposition.gloss: The difference of quantity or quality between two propositions having the same subject and predicate.

optical character recognition.gloss: The electronic identification and digital encoding of printed or handwritten characters by means of an optical scanner and specialized software.

optical disc.gloss: A modern data storage medium consisting of a flat disc read mechanically by illumination with laser light, including the Laserdisc, compact disc, DVD, and Blu-ray.

optical drive.gloss: A drive that reads optical media.

optical mouse.gloss: A mouse (pointing device) that uses a light source and a light detector (for example, an LED and an array of photodiodes) to detect movement, as opposed to the earlier mechanical mouse.

optimistic.gloss: Allowing other processes to perform transactions on the same data at the same time, and checking for conflicts only when changes need to be written back.

optimistic concurrency.gloss: A database model that allows multiple users to update data simultaneously without locking rows.

optimization.gloss: The reduction of a program or algorithm to its most efficient form, as during compilation, by removing unused portions of code and improving the speed or resource usage of others.

optimization problem.gloss: The problem of finding the "best" solution from all feasible solutions, given constraints defining which of the solutions are feasible, and a goal function defining which of the feasible solutions is the best one.

optimize out.gloss: To omit (some portion of program logic) through optimization, when it is found to be unused or unnecessary.

optimizer.gloss: A program that uses linear programming to optimize a process.
A compiler or assembler that produces optimized code.

option.gloss: To configure, by setting an option.

option type.gloss: A polymorphic type that represents encapsulation of an optional value.

optional.gloss: In various programming languages, a kind of variable that is assigned a specific data type but may or may not hold an actual value.

or.gloss: The binary operator inclusive or, true if one at least one of two inputs is true. In infix notation.

oracle.gloss: A theoretical entity capable of answering some collection of questions.

oracle machine.gloss: In computability theory, a form of theoretical Turing machine, able to solve even undecidable decision problems in a single operation.

orbifold.gloss: A topological space in which every small enough neighborhood is homeomorphic to a quotient of real space by the action of a finite group.

orbifoldized.gloss: Converted to, or considered as an orbifold

orbiform.gloss: A plane for which the distance between the points of contact of two nonequal parallel tangents at a circle is the same everywhere.

orbispace.gloss: A topological space or generalization of an orbifold.

orbit.gloss: A collection of points related by the evolution function of a dynamical system.
The subset of elements of a set X to which a given element can be moved by members of a specified group of transformations that act on X.

orchestration.gloss: The automated arrangement, coordination, and management of computer systems, middleware, and services.

orchestrator.gloss: A system that performs orchestration (automated configuration, deployment, etc.).

order.gloss: The number of elements contained within (the given object); formally, the cardinality (of the given object).
qualifiers: of a set or algebraic structure

order.gloss: The smallest positive natural number n such that (denoting the group operation multiplicatively) gⁿ is the identity element of G, if such an n exists; if no such n exists the element is said to be of infinite order (or sometimes zero order).
qualifiers: of an element g of a group G

order.gloss: The number of vertices in the graph (i.e. the set-theoretic order of the set of vertices of the graph).
The relation with which a partially ordered set is equipped.
The sum of the exponents of the variables involved in the expression.
The order of the leading monomial; (equivalently) the largest power of the variable involved in the given expression.
qualifiers: of a polynomial in one variable

order of magnitude.gloss: The class of scale or magnitude of any amount, where each class contains values of a fixed ratio (most often 10) to the class preceding it.

order of operations.gloss: The sequence in which the various operations in a mathematical expression are to be evaluated.

order statistic tree.gloss: A variant of the binary search tree (or more generally, a B-tree) that supports, in addition to insertion, lookup and deletion, the operations of Select (find the ith smallest element stored in the tree) and Rank (find the rank of element x in the tree, i.e. its index in the sorted list of elements of the tree).

order tree.gloss: A set that is the union of subsets (called segments), each of which is totally ordered, such that the segments fit together a certain way.

order type.gloss: In the context of sets equipped with an order (especially, the context of totally ordered sets), the characteristic of being a member of some equivalence class of such sets under the equivalence relation "existence of an order-preserving bijection".

ordered.gloss: Equipped with a partial or total order which, in any of several technical senses, respects the algebraic structure of the object (if such structure exists). See .

ordered field.gloss: A field which has an order relation satisfying these properties: trichotomy, transitivity, preservation of an inequality when the same element is added to both sides, and preservation of an inequality when the same strictly positive element is multiplied to both sides.

ordered integral domain.gloss: An integral domain which has a subset whose elements are said to be "positive", such that this subset is closed under addition, closed under multiplication, and all elements of the integral domain satisfy a law of trichotomy; namely, that either that element is in the said subset, or it is the zero (additive identity), or its product with −1 (the additive inverse of the multiplicative identity) belongs to the said subset.

ordered pair.gloss: An object containing exactly two elements in a fixed order, so that, when the elements are different, exchanging them gives a different object. Notation: (a, b) or ⟨a,b⟩.

ordered ring.gloss: A ring, R, equipped with a partial order, ≤, such that for arbitrary a, b, c ∈ R, if a ≤ b then a + c ≤ b + c, and if, additionally, 0 ≤ c, then both ca ≤ cb and ac ≤ bc.
A ring, R, equipped with a total order, ≤, such that for arbitrary a, b, c ∈ R, if a ≤ b then a + c ≤ b + c, and if, additionally, 0 ≤ c, then both ca ≤ cb and ac ≤ bc.

ordinal number.gloss: Such a number generalised to correspond to any cardinal number (the size of some set); formally, the order type of some well-ordered set of some cardinality a, which represents an equivalence class of well-ordered sets (exactly those of cardinality a) under the equivalence relation "existence of an order-preserving bijection".

ordinal variable.gloss: A variable with values whose order is significant, but on which no meaningful arithmetic-like operations can be performed.

ordinary differential equation.gloss: An equation involving the derivatives of a function of only one independent variable.

ordinate.gloss: The second of the two terms by which a point is referred to, in a system of fixed rectilinear coordinate (Cartesian coordinate) axes.
The vertical line representing an axis of a Cartesian coordinate system, on which the ordinate (sense above) is shown.
To subject to the mathematical operation of ordination.
Of a figure: having all its sides and angles equal.
Relating to an ordered series of ratios.

ordination.gloss: A statistical technique for ordering data from a large number of sites or populations by arranging the data as points in a multidimensional coordinate frame, in which patterns can be discerned; an instance of this.

organizer.gloss: A hand-held micro-computer that will perform specific tasks; can be used as an electronic diary, alarm clock, recorder of memos and notes, a portable database etc.

orientation.gloss: The choice of which ordered bases are "positively" oriented and which are "negatively" oriented on a real vector space.
The designation of a parametrised curve as "positively" or "negatively" oriented; the analogous description of a surface or hypersurface.

oriented.gloss: In any of various technical senses, admitting or being equipped with a notion of handedness (i.e. of distinguishing clockwise and anticlockwise). See Orientability on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

oriented graph.gloss: A directed graph having no opposite pairs of directed edges.

origin.gloss: The point at which the axes of a coordinate system intersect.

origin of coordinates.gloss: The point of intersection of coordinate axes, which represents the value of 0 for all coordinates.

orphan.gloss: To make unavailable, as by removing the last remaining pointer or reference to.

orphan off.gloss: To remove all links to (something), leaving it an orphan; to render a technical item (website, function, etc.) useless by removing references that call on it.

orthant.gloss: An n-dimensional generalization of the quadrant (in two-dimensional Cartesian space) and octant (in three-dimensional space).

orthobicupola.gloss: A bicupola in which the bases have the same orientation

orthobirotunda.gloss: A birotunda in which the bases have the same orientation.

orthocenter.gloss: One of the centers (UK:centres) of a triangle, defined as being the intersection of its three altitudes; in an acute triangle, it is inside the triangle; in an obtuse triangle, it is outside the triangle; in a right-angled triangle it is the vertex opposite the hypotenuse and so is on the triangle.

orthocentric.gloss: Having all three pairs of opposite edges perpendicular.
Of or relating to a set of four points in the plane, one of which is the orthocenter of the triangle formed by the other three.

orthochronous.gloss: Describing any Lorentz transformation or Galilean transformation which preserves the direction of time

orthocomplement.gloss: An element of an ortholattice which is the result of applying an orthocomplementation function to a given element (of that ortholattice) (of which it is said to be the orthocomplement).

orthocomplementation.gloss: An involution on a complemented lattice which is order-reversing and maps each element to a complement.

orthocupolarotunda.gloss: A cupolarotunda in which the bases have the same orientation.

orthodiagonal.gloss: Having diagonals that are perpendicular to each other.

orthodox file manager.gloss: A file manager program with a traditional textbased user interface.

orthodrome.gloss: A great circle, or part of one.

orthogon.gloss: A multi-dimensional figure in which all sides result in a right angle, typically surpassing the restrictions of 3 dimensions.

orthogonal.gloss: Of two objects, at right angles; perpendicular to each other.
Of a pair of vectors: having a zero inner product; perpendicular.
Of a square matrix: such that its transpose is equal to its inverse.
Of a linear transformation: preserving its angles.
Of grid graphs, board games and polyominoes: vertical or horizontal but not diagonal.
Of a pair of elements in an ortholattice: each less than or equal to the orthocomplement of the other.
Statistically independent, with reference to variates.
Of two or more aspects of a problem, able to be treated separately; of a design, exhibiting consistency and composability.

orthogonal complement.gloss: The set of all vectors which are orthogonal to a given set of vectors.

orthogonal group.gloss: For given n and field F (especially where F is the real numbers), the group of n × n orthogonal matrices with elements in F, where the group operation is matrix multiplication.

orthogonal matrix.gloss: A square matrix whose columns, considered as vectors, are orthonormal to each other. This implies that the transpose of such a matrix is also its inverse.

orthogonalization.gloss: The process of converting a set of functions or vectors into orthogonal ones.

orthohedron.gloss: A figure, somewhat like a cube but with two square faces and four rectangular faces

ortholinear.gloss: Of a keyboard, having keys that are aligned in a perfect grid.

orthomodular.gloss: Describing a lattice with the property that its every orthogonal pair is modular.

orthomorphism.gloss: A morphism that is also a permutation

orthonormal.gloss: Of a set of vectors, both orthogonal and normalized.
Of a linear transformation: that preserves both angles and lengths.

orthonormalization.gloss: A form of orthogonalization in which the resulting vectors are all unit vectors

orthonormalize.gloss: To make a set of vectors both orthogonal and normalized.

orthopair.gloss: A pair of orthogonal or disjoint subsets (of a given universe)

orthopedal.gloss: Orthogonal to the foot of a geometric figure.

orthoplex.gloss: A convex polytope analogous to an octahedron (3 dimensions) or 16-cell (4 dimensions).

orthoptic.gloss: The isoptic whose given angle is a right angle.

orthoradial.gloss: Relative to a grid of circles surrounding a point and lines starting at that point; such a graph has alternate circular and radial components

orthoscheme.gloss: A special kind of simplex whose vertices can be connected by a path such that every pair of edges in the path are at right angles to each other.

orthosymmetric.gloss: That has equal elements of the secondary diagonal.

orthotomic.gloss: imaginary; involving the square root of a negative number.
The line that joins the poles of the common chord on two orthotomic circles.
The envelope of the family of circles that have centers on a specified curve and which pass through a specified point.

orthotomic circle.gloss: A circle that cuts three other given circles at right angles.

orthotomy.gloss: The property of cutting at right angles.

orthotope.gloss: The generalization of a rectangle for higher dimensions, formally defined as the Cartesian product of intervals.

os-specific.gloss: written for a specific operating system

oscillating.gloss: Describing a function or divergent series that moves between multiple values.

oscillation.gloss: (of a function) defined for each point x in the domain of the function by inf diam(f(U))∣Uisaneighborhoodofx, and describes the difference (possibly ∞) between the limit superior and limit inferior of the function near that point.

oscillaton.gloss: A spherically-symmetric solution to an Einstein–Klein–Gordon equation

oscillator.gloss: A pattern that returns to its original state, in the same orientation and position, after a finite number of generations.

oscnode.gloss: A node of a plane curve where two branches meet with contact order 3.

osculant.gloss: Tangent, touching at a single point.
The point at which two tangent curves touch.
The condition that the solution to a set of simultaneous quantics, is also the solution of the corresponding set of tangential quantics.
a form of tacinvariant of hypersurfaces that have a point in common

osculate.gloss: To touch so as to have the same tangent and curvature at the point of contact.

osculating.gloss: Having three or more points coincident with another

osculating circle.gloss: The circle that has the same tangent, and the same curvature at the point on the curve.
qualifiers: for any point on a curve

osculation.gloss: A contact between curves or surfaces, at which point they have a common tangent.

osculatory.gloss: Relating to, or having the properties of, an osculatrix; capable of osculation.

osculatrix.gloss: A curve whose contact with a given curve at a given point is of a higher order (or involves the equality of a greater number of successive differential coefficients of the ordinates of the curves taken at that point) than that of any other curve of the same kind.

osi layer.gloss: Any of the seven layers of abstraction in the OSI model of communications systems: application, presentation, session, transport, network, data link, or physical.

ostrowski numeration.gloss: Either of two related numeration systems based on continued fractions: a non-standard positional numeral system for integers, and a non-integer representation of real numbers.

otopy.gloss: A type of vector field defined on an open set of such that every vector in the field is tangent to the corresponding point in the set.

otp.gloss: Initialism of one-time password: a password that is valid for only one login session or transaction.

otprom.gloss: Acronym of one-time programmable read-only memory.

out-of-band.gloss: Of a value returned by a function: not in its natural range of return values, but rather signaling an exception.

out-of-band signaling.gloss: A type of transmission technology in which signaling is separate from the data being transmitted, using one or more channels for transmitting data or voice information and one out-of-band channel for performing signaling functions.

out-of-tree.gloss: Located outside of a source tree.
Taking place outside of a source tree.

outbox.gloss: An electronic folder serving the same purpose, for electronic mail.

outbranch.gloss: One of several edges in a directed graph that has an endpoint in a specified vertex and for which the direction of the edge goes from the specified vertex to another vertex.

outcase.gloss: A condition that allows code to break out of a recursive routine.

outcode.gloss: A code used in the Cohen-Sutherland algorithm, indicating how a line should be clipped relative to the viewport.

outcome.gloss: The result of a random trial. An element of a sample space.

outcome variable.gloss: A dependent variable thought to change as a function of changes in a predictor variable.

outcrack.gloss: To surpass in cracking (security systems etc.).

outdegree.gloss: The number of edges directed out of a vertex in a directed graph.

outedge.gloss: An outgoing edge in a digraph, i.e. one that leaves a particular node.

outer automorphism.gloss: An automorphism which is not an inner automorphism.

outer join.gloss: A join yielding a set of records that combines every record from a set of tables.

outer measure.gloss: A measure-like function derived from some premeasure as follows: when it is applied to a set E, it yields the infimum of the premeasures of all possible premeasurable covers of E. More abstractly, a measure-like function whose domain is the power set of some underlying set, which has the properties of (1) yielding zero when applied to the empty set, (2) being monotonic (if A is subset of B then this function applied to A is less-than-or-equal to this function applied to B), (3) being subadditive (if A is a countable sum of Bⱼ's then this function applied to A is less-than-or-equal to the sum of the applications of this function to the Bⱼ's).

outer product.gloss: The tensor product of two vectors.

outer regular.gloss: (of a Borel set) That its measure is equal to the infimum of the measures of all open sets which contain it.

outer semidirect product.gloss: A group constructed from a specific relationship between two abstract groups, G₁ and G₂, given a certain homomorphism denoted φ.

outer totalistic.gloss: Having the state of each cell represented by a number, and the value of a cell dependent only on its current value along with the sum of the values of nearby cells.

outerplanar.gloss: Having a planar embedding such that the vertices lie on a circle and the edges lie inside that circle.

outerthickness.gloss: The minimum number of outerplanar subgraphs which a given graph can decompose into.

outlier.gloss: A value in a statistical sample which does not fit a pattern that describes most other data points; specifically, a value that lies 1.5 IQR beyond the upper or lower quartile.

outline.gloss: To optimize for size by replacing repeated code fragments with function calls.

outliner.gloss: A software system for organizing text into a hierarchy.

outlyingness.gloss: The measure, degree or quality of being an outlier.

output.gloss: That which is produced by something, especially that which is produced within a particular time period or from a particular effort. Data sent out of the computer, as to output device such as a monitor or printer, or data sent from one program on the computer to another.

That which is produced by something, especially that which is produced within a particular time period or from a particular effort. The terminal through which the data or power is delivered from the source, output terminal.
To send data out of a computer, as to an output device such as a monitor or printer, or to send data from one program on the computer to another.

output device.gloss: Any device that formats and presents data for display to a user; examples include printers and video monitors

outscriber.gloss: A magnetic recording device that serves as a buffer for data being transmitted from computer to printer, to reduce delays in printing.

ova.gloss: Abbreviation of Open Virtualization format Archive.

oval.gloss: In a projective plane, a set of points such that no three are collinear and there is a unique tangent line at each point.

overalign.gloss: To organise data with alignment greater that a compiler can handle

overarc.gloss: In a two-dimensional knot diagram, any arc which crosses over another segment of the knot.

overbound.gloss: To provide an upper bound to.

A Gaussian model of the (non-Gaussian) error distribution on a signal, which is conservative enough that the resulting confidence interval is guaranteed to be at least as wide as the actual confidence interval.

overburn.gloss: To record more than the usual available data capacity onto (an optical disc).

overcategory.gloss: Any functor into a specified base category.

overclock.gloss: To run a processor (CPU), or any electronic logic device, at a speed higher than is recommended by the manufacturer.

overclocker.gloss: A person who overclocks a computer.

overcomment.gloss: To annotate (code) with too many comments.

overcommit.gloss: Allocation of more resources than are actually available.

overcomplete.gloss: Describing a frame (in linear algebra) having a set of functions more than a basis

overcone.gloss: A morphism from a diagonal overfunctor to the base category of the overcategory.

qualifiers: of a system of linear equations

overdispersion.gloss: The presence of greater dispersion in a data set than would be expected according to the statistical model in use.

overdraw.gloss: To draw over the top of existing content.
The process by which, during the rendering of a three-dimensional scene, a pixel is replaced by one that is closer to the viewpoint, as determined by their Z coordinates.

overfactorization.gloss: The use or consideration of excessive factors in factor analysis.

overfilter.gloss: A morphological filter (idempotent operator) whose image is a superset of the domain.

overfit.gloss: To use a statistical model that has too many parameters relative to the size of the sample, leading to a good fit with the sample data but a poor fit with new data.

overfitting.gloss: The production of a statistical model that, due to an excess of parameters relative to the sample size, fits the sample data extremely well but fails to fit new data.

overflow.gloss: The situation where a value exceeds the available numeric range.
To (cause to) exceed the available numeric range.

overhead.gloss: Data or steps of computation used only to facilitate the computations in the system and not directly related to the actual program code or data being processed.

overindex.gloss: To attempt to access an element beyond the bounds of (an array).

overlap.gloss: Of sets: to have some elements in common.

overlay.gloss: A block of program code that is loaded over something previously loaded, so as to replace the functionality.

overlay scrollbar.gloss: A scrollbar that appears over content as a floating thumb, rather than enclosed within a track.

overlicensed.gloss: Having purchased more licences than are legally required.

overload.gloss: An overloaded version of a function.

overloaded.gloss: of a name, used for more than one variable or procedure etc; differentiated by the compiler based on context

overloop.gloss: An outer loop; A loop that contains an inner loop.

overmatching.gloss: Matching for an apparent mediator that actually is a result of the exposure.

overorder.gloss: A ring for which a specified subring R contains no nonempty socles and for which any R-module is of finite length.

overpaint.gloss: To erase by drawing graphics over the top.

overparameterize.gloss: To use an excessive number of parameters.
To increase the degree of the line of best fit to the point that the fit of the line decreases.

overpartition.gloss: An overpartition of n is a non-increasing sequence of natural numbers whose sum is n in which the first occurrence of a number may be overlined.

overpost.gloss: To breach security by overwriting data that is not intended for user input.

overprime.gloss: A prime number larger than some given natural number.

overpunch.gloss: To punch (some value or pattern) over an existing pattern on paper tape.

overrelaxation.gloss: A technique which, when applied iteratively, can solve certain types of matrix equation

overring.gloss: An overring B of an integral domain A is a subring of the field of fractions K of A that contains A, i.e. A#92;subseteqB#92;subseteqK.

oversample.gloss: An additional sample of a subpopulation, above and beyond the portion of a main sample that already belongs to that subpopulation.
To sample additional members of a subpopulation, above and beyond the members included in the main sample.

overscroll.gloss: A feature where content being scrolled goes beyond its end point and bounces back, giving the user visual feedback that the end has been reached.
To perform this kind of scrolling and bouncing effect.

oversegmentation.gloss: A division into too many segments, as when attempting to recognize parts of an image.

overstore.gloss: The overwriting of memory or data, especially when done in error.

overstrike.gloss: overtype (feature where input replaces existing characters instead of being inserted before them)

oversubscribe.gloss: To use the oversubscription technique in multithreading.
To use the oversubscription technique in a computer network.

oversubscription.gloss: A multithreading technique involving an extra thread that runs tasks when all other threads are blocked.
The practice of connecting multiple devices to the same switch port in a storage area network.

overtravel.gloss: The distance a pressed switch on a keyboard continues to move after its actuation.

overtype.gloss: A feature in wordprocessing whereby each typed character replaces the character after the cursor rather than being inserted before it.

overwrite.gloss: To destroy (older) data by recording new data over it.
The operation of destroying older data by recording new data over it.

overwriter.gloss: Software that writes over the contents or unused section of a data store to prevent recovery of sensitive information.

owl.gloss: Initialism of Web Ontology Language (The order of the letters is discussed at Web Ontology Language § Acronym.)

own.gloss: To illicitly obtain administrative access to a computer system, thereby having full access to all the files thereon (including executables).

p-adic.gloss: Of, pertaining to, (ultimately) derived from or defined in the context of p-adic numbers.

p-adic absolute value.gloss: A norm for the rational numbers, with some prime number p as parameter, such that any rational number of the form pᵏ(a/b) — where a, b and k are integers and a, b and p are coprime — is mapped to the rational number p⁻ᵏ and 0 is mapped to 0. (Note: any nonzero rational number can be reduced to such a form.)

p-adic norm.gloss: A p-adic absolute value, for a given prime number p, the function, denoted |..|ₚ and defined on the rational numbers, such that |0|ₚ = 0 and, for x≠0, |x|ₚ = p^(-ordₚ(x)), where ordₚ(x) is the p-adic ordinal of x; the same function, extended to the p-adic numbers ℚₚ (the completion of the rational numbers with respect to the p-adic ultrametric defined by said absolute value); the same function, further extended to some extension of ℚₚ (for example, its algebraic closure).
A norm on a vector space which is defined over a field equipped with a discrete valuation (a generalisation of p-adic absolute value).

p-adic number.gloss: An element of a completion of the field of rational numbers with respect to a p-adic ultrametric.

p-adic order.gloss: Of a positive integer n, the exponent of the highest power of p that divides n. Often denoted νₚ(n). For example, ν₂(48)=4.

p-adic ordinal.gloss: A function of rational numbers, with prime number p as parameter, which is defined for some non-zero integer x as the largest integer r such that pʳ divides x; is defined for some non-zero rational number a/b as the p-adic ordinal of a minus the p-adic ordinal of b; and is defined for 0 as infinity.

p-adic ultrametric.gloss: The ultrametric with prime number p as parameter defined as d_p(x,y)=|x-y|ₚ; i.e., such that the distance between two rational numbers is equal to the p-adic absolute value of the difference between those two numbers.

p-code.gloss: A very low-level code that is machine-independent and enables a compiled file to be run on different processor types.

p-complete.gloss: Describing any problem in the complexity class P to which there exists a polynomial time mapping from any other problem in P.

p-frame.gloss: A video frame which contains only information on the differences from previous frames

p-hacking.gloss: The practice of reanalysis of data until a desired result is obtained which is statistically significant.

p-value.gloss: In statistical significance testing, the probability of obtaining a test statistic at least as extreme as the one that was actually observed, assuming that the null hypothesis is true.

paamayim nekudotayim.gloss: The scope resolution operator :: in the PHP programming language.

paas.gloss: Acronym of platform as a service.

pachinko allocation.gloss: In machine learning and natural language processing, a suite of algorithms to determine the thematic structure of a collection of documents by modelling correlations between topics in addition to the word correlations that constitute topics.

pachner move.gloss: Any of a set of ways of replacing a triangulation of a piecewise linear manifold by a different triangulation of a homoeomorphic manifold.

pack.gloss: To put or bring things together in a limited or confined space, especially for storage or transport. To compress (data).

package.gloss: A piece of software which has been prepared in such a way that it can be installed with a package manager.

package format.gloss: A type of archive containing computer programs and additional metadata required by a package manager.

package management system.gloss: A package manager: the tool used by an operating system to manage software installation.

package manager.gloss: A computer program responsible for installing, updating and configuring other software, maintaining an index of installed programs and resolving their dependencies.

packager.gloss: A program that groups objects or data into a single file.

packed decimal.gloss: A storage mode that places two decimal digits into one byte, each digit occupying four bits. The sign occupies four bits in the least significant byte.

packer.gloss: A software program that compresses code or data.

packet.gloss: A small fragment of data as transmitted on some types of network, notably Ethernet networks (Wikipedia).
A protocol data unit of the Internet Protocol.
A message sent over a transport layer protocol.

packet switching.gloss: A means of directing digitally encoded information in a communication network from its source to its destination, in which messages may be divided into smaller entities called packets, each of which travels independently through the network in paths based on moment-to-moment routing decisions made by the nodes through which they pass.

packet tracer.gloss: A tool used to monitor, analyze and simulate network traffic by capturing data packets over a network.

packetization.gloss: The act or process of bundling data into packets according to a specific protocol

packetize.gloss: To form data into packets, or bundled units, according to a specific protocol

packing.gloss: The action of the verb. The spatial arrangement of objects, items or constituent parts.

pacs.gloss: Initialism of picture archiving and communication system.

pad.gloss: A random key (originally written on a disposable pad) of the same length as the plaintext.

paddable.gloss: Capable of being padded; said of a set whose strings can be transformed into infinitely many further strings in the set.

padding.gloss: Extra characters such as spaces added to a record to fill it out to a fixed length.
Extraneous text added to a message for the purpose of concealing its beginning, ending, or length.

padé approximant.gloss: The "best" approximation of a function by a rational function of given order. Under this technique, the approximant's power series agrees with the power series of the function it is approximating.

page.gloss: A screenful of text and possibly other content; especially, the digital simulation of one side of a paper leaf.
A block of contiguous memory of a fixed length.

page down.gloss: To scroll down to the next page of content.
A keyboard key that when pressed scrolls down to the next page of content.

page fault.gloss: An alert (such as an interrupt or exception) indicating that a page of memory was accessed without being loaded.

page flow.gloss: A directory of web application files that work together to implement a user interface feature.

page in.gloss: To transfer (memory contents) from auxiliary storage.

page out.gloss: To transfer (memory contents) to auxiliary storage.

page table.gloss: A data structure used by a virtual memory implementation to store the mappings between physical and virtual addresses.

page up.gloss: To scroll up to the previous page of content.
A keyboard key that when pressed scrolls up to the previous page of content.

pageable.gloss: Able to be divided into pages, or navigated as pages.
Able to be paged in and paged out.

pager.gloss: A computer program running in a text terminal, used to view (but not modify) the contents of a text file moving down the file one line or one screen at a time.

paginate.gloss: To separate (data) into batches, so that it can be retrieved with a number of smaller requests.

pagination.gloss: The separation of data into batches, so that it can be retrieved with a number of smaller requests.

paging.gloss: A transfer of pages between main memory and an auxiliary store, such as hard disk drive.

paging file.gloss: A region of secondary storage allocated by the operating system to function as virtual memory, extending physical RAM.

paint.gloss: Graphics drawn using an input device, not scanned or generated.
To draw an element in a graphical user interface.

paint bucket.gloss: A tool in some graphics editor applications that fills in a portion of the image with a certain color or pattern.

pair.gloss: to link two electronic devices wirelessly together, especially through a protocol such as Bluetooth.

pair of compasses.gloss: A technical drawing instrument consisting of two hinged legs, one typically equipped with a sharp metal point for anchoring and the other with a holder for a pencil or pen, designed to inscribe circles or arcs of an adjustable radius.

pair of pants.gloss: The orientable surface of genus zero having three boundary components.

pair programmer.gloss: A computer programmer who takes part in pair programming.

pair programming.gloss: A software development technique, part of extreme programming, in which two programmers work together at a single keyboard, one coding while the other observes and reviews. The roles are often switched at regular intervals.

pairing function.gloss: A process to uniquely encode two natural numbers into a single natural number.

pairwise disjoint.gloss: Let A_λ_(λ∈Λ) be any collection of sets indexed by a set Λ. We call the indexed collection pairwise disjoint if for any two distinct indices, λ,μ∈Λ, the sets A_λ and A_μ are disjoint.
qualifiers: of a collection of two or more sets

pajeetware.gloss: Software created by stereotypical Indians, especially when regarded as poor-quality.

palette.gloss: A visual selection of colours, tools, commands, etc.

palette swap.gloss: To change the color palette used to render a palettized image.
An image that is the same as another but rendered with a different colour palette.

palette window.gloss: A window often with miniaturized graphical user interface widgets housing a collection of related tools/commands for a particular task. The contemporary behavior is for the window to be a floating palette, floating over the main document window.

palettization.gloss: The act or process of palettizing.

palettize.gloss: To encode (an image) efficiently by mapping its pixels to a palette containing only those colours that are actually present in the image.

palimpsest.gloss: Memory that has been erased and re-written.

pancake number.gloss: In pancake sorting, the minimum number of flips required for a given number of pancakes.

pancake sorting.gloss: The mathematical problem of sorting a disordered stack of pancakes in order of size when a spatula can be inserted at any point in the stack and used to flip all pancakes above it.

pancyclic.gloss: Containing cycless of every possible length (from 3 to the order of the graph).

pandiagonal.gloss: Of a magic square: having the additional property that the broken diagonals, i.e. the diagonals that wrap round at the edges of the square, also add up to the magic constant.

pandiagonal magic square.gloss: A magic square with the additional property that the broken diagonals also summate to the magic constant.

pandigital.gloss: Containing at least one of every digit in a specified base.

pane.gloss: A portion of a user interface that typically makes up part of a larger window and may be docked or snapped into position.

panel.gloss: A type of GUI widget, such as a control panel.

panic.gloss: Ellipsis of kernel panic (“on Unix-derived operating systems: an action taken by the operating system when it cannot recover from a fatal error”); (by extension) any computer system crash.
To cause (a computer system) to crash.
Of a computer system: to crash.

paper cut.gloss: a paper cut bug: a bug which causes harm and would be easy to fix.

paper tape.gloss: An early sequential digital storage medium originally used with teletype machines, consisting of a long roll of paper, each character being encoded as a pattern of punched holes.

pappian.gloss: For which Pappus's hexagon theorem is valid.

parabicanonical.gloss: Pertaining to a linear system of divisors numerically equivalent to a bicanonical divisor, on a general type minimal surface.

parabola.gloss: The conic section formed by the intersection of a cone with a plane parallel to a tangent plane to the cone; the locus of points equidistant from a fixed point (the focus) and line (the directrix).

parabolaster.gloss: A curve analogous to a parabola; or of a higher degree.

parabolic.gloss: Of, or pertaining to, or in the shape of a parabola or paraboloid.

parabolism.gloss: The division of the terms of an equation by a known quantity that is involved in the first term.

paraboloid of revolution.gloss: A surface of revolution formed by revolving a parabola around its axis.

paracanonical.gloss: Pertaining to a curve in the linear system of a canonical divisor of an irregular surface and any point on that surface.

paracentric.gloss: A planar curve having the property that, when its plane is placed vertically, a body descending along it, by the force of gravity, will approach to, or recede from, a fixed point or centre, by equal distances in equal times.

paracompact.gloss: In which every open cover admits an open locally finite refinement.

paracompactification.gloss: A construction yielding a paracompact space.

paracomplete.gloss: Omitting the law of excluded middle, for example by introducing a third truth value.

paracomplex.gloss: Pertaining to the category of all metric spaces and all CW-complexes.

paracomposition.gloss: An extension of the paralinearization of non-smooth functions, used to flatten pairs of surfaces by changing variables.

paraconsistent.gloss: Dealing with contradictions in a discriminating way, in order to avoid acceptance of one from entailing acceptance of all contradictions.

paraconsistent logic.gloss: A particular formal logical system which allows some contradictions to be true without all contradictions or all statements becoming true; i.e. in which the principle of explosion does not hold.

paracontact.gloss: Having the property that every open cover has an open refinement that is locally finite.

paracontrolled distribution.gloss: A distribution d ∈ C^α is called paracontrolled by u ∈ C^α if there exists d′ ∈ Cᵝ such that d − d′ ≺ u ∈ C^(α+β).

paradifferential.gloss: Describing an extension of differential calculus that deals with nonlinear hyperbolic and similar functions.

paragraph.gloss: An offset of 16 bytes in Intel memory architectures.

parahoric.gloss: Describing a form of parabolic Iwahori subgroups.

paralinear.gloss: Consisting of the linear combination of different rate equations, each of which may or may not be linear.

qualifiers: said of a pair of lines

parallel.gloss: Involving the processing of multiple tasks at the same time.

parallel port.gloss: A physical interface capable of transmitting multiple bits of data simultaneously.

parallel postulate.gloss: An axiom in Euclidean geometry: given a straight line L and a point p not on L, there exists exactly one straight line parallel to L that passes through p; a variant of this axiom, such that the number of lines parallel to L that pass through p may be zero or more than one.

parallel transport.gloss: A way of transporting geometrical data along smooth curves in a manifold.

parallelepiped.gloss: A solid figure, having six faces, all parallelograms, all opposite faces being similar and parallel.

parallelepipedal.gloss: Having the form of a parallelepiped

parallelism.gloss: The use of parallel methods in hardware or software, so that several tasks can be performed at the same time.

parallelizable.gloss: Whose tangent bundle is a trivial bundle.

parallelize.gloss: To make to execute in parallel.

parallelizer.gloss: A process or algorithm that parallelizes code.

parallelogram.gloss: A convex quadrilateral in which each pair of opposite edges are parallel and of equal length.

parallelohedron.gloss: A polyhedron that can tessellate three-dimensional spaces with face-to-face contacts via translations.

parallelotope.gloss: A generalization of parallelogram and parallelepiped into a figure of arbitrary dimensionality.

paralogics.gloss: The study of paralogic rhetoric; the study of understanding language by successive approximation.

parameter.gloss: A variable that describes a property or characteristic of some system (material, object, event, etc.) or some aspect thereof. Any measured quantity of a statistical population that summarises or describes an aspect of the population.
An input variable of a function definition, that gets an actual value (argument) at execution time.
An actual value given to such a formal parameter.
In the ellipse and hyperbola, a third proportional to any diameter and its conjugate, or in the parabola, to any abscissa and the corresponding ordinate.

parameterization.gloss: The representation of physical characteristics or properties by parameters rather than as sui generis instances; usually and especially: Such parameterized representation in a computer model.

parameterize.gloss: To rewrite (a database query, etc.) as a template into which parameters can be inserted.

parameterless.gloss: Taking no parameters; having zero arity.

parametric.gloss: Of, relating to, or defined using parameters. In mathematics, this typically means related to parametrization / parametric equation.

parametric equation.gloss: A set of equations that defines the coordinates of the dependent variables (x, y and z) of a curve or surface in terms of one or more independent variables or parameters.

parametric polymorphism.gloss: A way to make a computer language more expressive, while maintaining full static type safety, by allowing a function or a data type to be written generically so that it can handle values identically without depending on their type.

parametrix.gloss: An approximation to a fundamental solution of a partial differential equation, and is essentially an approximate inverse to a differential operator.

paramodular.gloss: Pertaining to a pair (a, b) of set functions where a is supermodular, b is submodular, and they always satisfy the cross-inequality b(X) - a(Y) > b(X-Y) -a(Y-X) for all X, Y.

paramodulation.gloss: A technique for reasoning on sets of clauses where the predicate symbol is equality.

paraproduct.gloss: A non-commutative bilinear operator acting on functions that in some sense is like the product of the two functions it acts on.

paratactic.gloss: Of two lines in elliptic geometry: such that the perpendicular distance between them is constant from point to point.

paratopological group.gloss: A topological semigroup that is algebraically a group.

paraunitary.gloss: Of or relating to a kind of matrix that occurs in the construction of filter banks used in multirate digital systems.

paravector.gloss: A sum (in some algebras) of a scalar and a vector.

paravirtualization.gloss: An approximate virtualization in which the emulated operating system has been modified for convenience or efficiency.

paravirtualize.gloss: To modify an operating system or software driver to allow paravirtualization.

paraxial.gloss: Parallel to one or more axes of the coordinate system.

paren.gloss: A parenthesis (bracket used to enclose parenthetical material in text).

parent.gloss: The object from which a child or derived object is descended; a node superior to another node.
To provide a parent object for one or more other objects, which become the children.

parenthesis.gloss: Either of a pair of brackets, chiefly the round brackets "(" and ")" but occasionally also the square brackets "[" and "]", which are used together to enclose parenthetical material in a text. Either of a pair of brackets used to clarify an expression by grouping terms affected by a common operator, or to enclose the components of a vector or the elements of a matrix.

parentless.gloss: Having no parent in a data structure.

pareto distribution.gloss: A probability distribution such that for a random variable X with that distribution holds that the probability that X is greater than some number x is given by

A probability distribution such that for a random variable X with that distribution holds that the probability that X is greater than some number x is given by

pareto efficient.gloss: Describing a situation in which the profit of one party cannot be increased without reducing the profit of another.

pareto improvement.gloss: A change in the allocation of a resource to a set of individuals that is an improvement for at least one and no worse for any other.

pareto optimal.gloss: Describing a situation in which the profit of one party cannot be increased without reducing the profit of another.
Describing a strategy that cannot be made to perform better against one opposing strategy without performing less well against another.

parity.gloss: Senses related to classification into two sets. A set with the property of having all of its elements belonging to one of two disjoint subsets, especially a set of integers split in subsets of even and odd elements.
Senses related to classification into two sets. The classification of an element of a set with parity into one of the two sets.
Senses related to classification into two sets. The count of one-valued bits in a value, reduced to even or odd or zero or one.

parity bit.gloss: A bit (binary digit) used to indicate whether the number of bits in a given set with value of one is even or odd. Parity bits are used as a simple error detection code.

parity game.gloss: A type of game played on a directed graph whose nodes are coloured by priority.

parse.gloss: To split (a file or other input) into pieces of data that can be easily manipulated or stored.
To resolve (a string of code or text) into its elements to determine if it conforms to a particular grammar.
Of a string of code or text, sentence, etc.: to conform to rules of grammar, to be syntactically valid.
An act of parsing; a parsing.
The result of such an act; a parsing.

parse tree.gloss: An ordered, rooted tree (data structure) that represents the syntactic structure of a string according to some context-free grammar.

parselet.gloss: A small modular parsing object or routine (particularly in a Pratt parser) that handles a particular syntactic construct.

part.gloss: A portion; a component. A factor.

partial.gloss: Describing a property that holds only when an algorithm terminates.
Of or relating to a partial derivative or partial differential.
A partial derivative: a derivative with respect to one independent variable of a function in multiple variables while holding the other variables constant.
A fragment of a template containing markup.
To take the partial regression coefficient.

partial application.gloss: The process of fixing a number of arguments to a function, producing another function of smaller arity.

partial autocorrelation.gloss: Remaining correlation of two random variables in a stochastic process after intervening random variables have been accounted for.

partial dependency.gloss: An attribute of a relation that depends on a key but also on a part of such key; this is a violation of second normal form.

partial derivative.gloss: A derivative with respect to one variable of a function of several variables with the other variables held constant.

partial differential.gloss: an infinitesimal change in a variable in a partial derivative, or the result of partial differentiation

partial differential equation.gloss: A differential equation that involves the partial derivatives of a function of several variables.

partial evaluation.gloss: A technique for program optimization by specialization, so as to produce new programs which run faster than the originals while guaranteed to behave in the same way.

partial fraction.gloss: Any of several fractions to the sum of which a single fraction is equal.

partial function.gloss: A function whose domain is a subset of the set on which it is formally defined; i.e., a function f: X→Y for which values f(x) are defined only for x ∈ W, where W ⊆ X.

partial order.gloss: (informal) An ordering of the elements of a collection that behaves like that of the natural numbers by size, except that some elements may not be comparable (if all elements are comparable, it is called a total order); (formal) a binary relation that is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive.

partial out.gloss: To remove one variable (by giving it a fixed value) in order to identify any correlation between others
qualifiers: in a system of multiple variables

partial sum.gloss: The sum of the first n terms of an infinite series, where n is a finite number.

partially ordered.gloss: Equipped with a partial order; when the partial order is specified, often construed with by.

partially ordered set.gloss: A set that has a given, elsewhere specified partial order.
The ordered pair comprising a set and its partial order.

particle distribution function.gloss: A function that gives the number of particles per unit of volume of phase space.

particular.gloss: Forming a part of a genus; relatively limited in extension; affirmed or denied of a part of a subject.

particular integral.gloss: Any solution to a differential equation.

partition.gloss: An approach to division in which one asks what the size of each part is, rather than (as in quotition) how many parts there are.
A section of a hard disk separately formatted.
A division of a database or one of its constituting elements such as tables into separate independent parts.
A division of a data stream, such as a messaging queue or topic (often representing a unit of parallelism, and of fault tolerance).
A collection of non-empty, disjoint subsets of a set whose union is the set itself (i.e. all elements of the set are contained in exactly one of the subsets).

partition function.gloss: generalization of the definition of a partition function in statistical mechanics
function that represents the number of possible partitions of a natural number.

partition of unity.gloss: A collection of non-negative-valued functions defined on a topological space, such that every point has only finitely many nonzero values, and these sum to one.

partyplace.gloss: The venue where a demoparty is held.

pascal string.gloss: A string whose length is stored as a separate value.

pascal's triangle.gloss: A geometric representation of the binomial coefficients in a triangle, each entry being the sum of the two entries above.

pass.gloss: A run through a document as part of a translation, compilation or reformatting process.
A password (especially one for a restricted-access website).

pass by value.gloss: Alternative form of call by value.

passive attack.gloss: An attack in which the cryptanalyst cannot interact with any of the parties involved, attempting to break the system solely based upon observed data such as ciphertext.

passkey.gloss: A cryptographic key that is tied to specific devices or cloud accounts and is meant to be used instead of a password.

passphrase.gloss: A password that comprises a whole phrase.

passthrough.gloss: The act or process of passing through. As of a signal through a device or network.
The act or process of passing through. Allowing the use of some resource unchanged from one system to another.

password.gloss: A string of characters used to log in to a computer or network, to access a level in a video game, and so on; archetypally a word but nowadays often an alphanumeric string or a phrase.

password salting.gloss: A technique employed to protect passwords stored in a database by attaching a string of 32 or more characters and then hashing them.

password wallet.gloss: An application or mechanism which stores someone's passwords by encryption.

passwordable.gloss: Able to be protected with a password.

passwordless.gloss: Without a password; not requiring a password.

paste.gloss: To insert a piece of media (e.g. text, picture, audio, video) previously copied or cut from somewhere else.

pasteboard.gloss: A widget allowing multiple users to paste and share text or other items.

pata.gloss: Initialism of parallel ATA: a computer bus technology primarily designed for transfer of data to and from a hard disk.

patch.gloss: A piece of data intended to modify a computer file by replacing a part of it.
To make the changes a patch describes; to apply a patch to the files in question. Hence: To fix or improve a computer program without a complete upgrade.
To make the changes a patch describes; to apply a patch to the files in question. Hence: To make a quick and possibly temporary change to a program.

patch file.gloss: A text file or binary file that lists differences between two versions of a file.

patch panel.gloss: a series of network cable connection sockets.

patcher.gloss: A process or program that applies a software patch.

path.gloss: A human-readable specification for a location within a hierarchical or tree-like structure, such as a file system or as part of a URL.

A sequence of vertices from one vertex to another using the arcs (edges). A path does not visit the same vertex more than once (unless it is a closed path, where only the first and the last vertex are the same).
A continuous map f from the unit interval I=[0,1] to a topological space X.
To navigate through a file system directory tree (to a desired file or folder).

path length.gloss: The number of edges traversed in a given path in a graph.
The number of text characters in a path (file or resource specifier).

path of least resistance.gloss: The path or route by which an object can move while minimizing the amount of resistance on the object's movement.

path tracing.gloss: A Monte Carlo method of rendering images of three-dimensional scenes such that the global illumination is faithful to reality.

pathfind.gloss: To find the best route between two points.

pathfinding.gloss: The plotting by a computer application of the best route between two points.

pathion.gloss: A 32-dimensional hypercomplex number that is a nonassociative extension of a sedenion.

pathname.gloss: The full name of a computer file, including the names of any directories or subdirectories in the path needed to access it.

pathological.gloss: Having properties which are counterintuitive or difficult to handle.
Having properties that cause unusually bad behaviour, especially regarding correctness or performance.

pathwidth.gloss: A measure of a path decomposition of a graph.

patricia tree.gloss: A radix tree with radix of 2, meaning that each bit of the key is compared individually and each node is a two-way branch.

patristocrat.gloss: A cipher in which punctuation and word spacing are not retained.

pattern.gloss: A text string containing wildcards, used for matching.
Coherent or decorative arrangement. A sequence of notes, percussion etc. in a tracker module, usable once or many times within the song.
Coherent or decorative arrangement. A configuration of cells in a cellular automaton universe.

pattern language.gloss: A structured method of describing good design practices within a field of expertise.

pattern matching.gloss: The act of checking some sequence of tokens for the presence of the constituents of a pattern.

pattern word.gloss: A word in which some letter appears more than once, useful in solving a cryptogram.

pauli matrix.gloss: Any one of three complex matrices that arise in Wolfgang Pauli's treatment of spin in quantum mechanics.

pauli vector.gloss: A vector whose components are Pauli matrices; e.g., ⃑σ=σ₁̂i+σ₂̂j+σ₃̂k.

pavement.gloss: A paved surface; a hard covering on the ground.

payload.gloss: The functional part of a computer virus or another type of malware program, rather than the part that spreads it.

payment terminal.gloss: An electronic device which interfaces with payment cards to make electronic funds transfers.

payoff function.gloss: A mathematical function describing the award given to a single player at the outcome of a game.

paywall.gloss: A system that restricts access to content with a purchase or a paid subscription.
To restrict access to (a website or other resource) by means of a paywall.

payware.gloss: Software for which a payment is required.

pbp.gloss: Initialism of personal basis profile (of JavaME).

pbps.gloss: petabits per second, a measure of data transfer rate equal to 1000 terabits or 10¹⁵ bits per second.

pc card.gloss: A removable memory or I/O device that fits into an expansion slot on a notebook computer or a personal digital assistant (PDA). PC Cards are used primarily in notebook computers and PDAs. PC Card peripherals include Wi-Fi network cards, memory cards, modems, wired NICs, and hard drives.

pc speaker.gloss: A device found in most IBM PC compatible computers that allows simple beeps to be output.

pc-compatible.gloss: Of a computer, offering the compatibility of the IBM Personal Computer regarding software, and―to a lesser degree―hardware.

pcaas.gloss: Acronym of PC as a service.

pci.gloss: Initialism of Peripheral Component Interconnect, a type of expansion slot on a motherboard.

pcmcia.gloss: Initialism of people can't memorize computer industry acronyms.

pdf.gloss: Initialism of Portable Document Format, a standard for representing electronic documents, allowing them to be transmitted and reproduced accurately with the same printed layout.
Initialism of portable document format (“a document in PDF format”).
Alternative letter-case form of pdf (“probability density function”).

pdfify.gloss: To convert (a file) to PDF format.

pdfize.gloss: To convert (a file) to PDF format.

pdo.gloss: Initialism of persistent data object (“a data object not lost when the application exits”).
Initialism of persistent domain object (“a domain object not lost when the application exits”).
Initialism of PHP data object, a PHP extension to be used as a database abstraction layer.

peak.gloss: A local maximum of a function, e.g. for sine waves, each point at which the value of y is at its maximum.
To exceed the maximum signal amplitude of (a piece of equipment), resulting in clipping of the signal.

peakon.gloss: A soliton whose first derivative is discontinuous.

peano arithmetic.gloss: A set of axioms of first-order logic for the natural numbers specifying the operations of zero, successor, addition and multiplication, including a first-order schema of induction.

peano axiom.gloss: Any of a set of fundamental axioms describing the natural numbers and their relationships.

peano curve.gloss: A space-filling curve in the 2-dimensional plane.

peanosphere.gloss: the scaling limit of random planar maps equipped with a collection of loops coming from a critical FK model.

pearson distribution.gloss: A family of continuous probability distributions.

pebble.gloss: To place a pebble at (a vertex of a graph) according to certain rules, in a pebble game.

pebbler.gloss: One who or that which places pebbles at the vertex of a graph, according to certain rules; see pebble game.

pebcak.gloss: Chiefly used by technical support helpdesk staff: a problem experienced with a user's computer that is due to user error.

pebibit.gloss: Strictly, 2⁵⁰ (1024⁵, 1,125,899,906,842,624) bits or 2¹⁰ (1024) tebibits, as opposed to a petabit.

pebibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2⁵⁰ (1024⁵, 1,125,899,906,842,624) bytes or 2¹⁰ (1024) tebibytes, as opposed to a petabyte.

pedal curve.gloss: For a plane curve C and a given fixed point P, the locus of points X such that PX is perpendicular to a tangent to the curve passing through X.

pedestal server.gloss: A type of computer rack consisting of a box-like frame or a columnar support, and may include wheels for transportation.

pedipulator.gloss: A component mechanism which gives a robot the capability of walking; a robot having such a capability.

pedmas.gloss: An acronym used to help people remember the order of operations, in the PEDMAS order (cf. "please excuse my dear Aunt Sally").

peek.gloss: To retrieve (a value) from a memory address.

peekable.gloss: Of a stream or other sequence: from which the next value can be retrieved without advancing the pointer from its current position.

peekaboo card.gloss: A kind of punch card that could be used to find records matching several categories by aligning cards for the records and retaining those where a hole could be seen all the way through the stack of cards.

peephole optimization.gloss: An optimization that works by eliminating redundant instructions from a small area of source code.

peepholer.gloss: An algorithm or process that performs peephole optimization.

peer-to-peer.gloss: Connected as equal partners and able to share processing, control and access to data and peripherals; decentralized.

peercast.gloss: To transmit streaming media via a peer-to-peer network.

peirce arrow.gloss: The downward arrow symbol ↓ denoting the NOR operation.

pell number.gloss: An infinite sequence of integers that comprises the denominators of the closest rational approximations to the square root of 2.

pell's equation.gloss: The Diophantine equation x²-my²=1 for a given integer m, to be solved in integers x and y.

pen drive.gloss: A small electronic device used to store digital data, more portable and robust than a hard drive; a flash drive.

penalty function.gloss: Any function that applies constraints to a maximum or minimum problem

pencentric.gloss: Wholly or primarily operated by means of a pen or stylus.

pencil.gloss: A family of geometric objects with a common property, such as the set of lines that pass through a given point in a projective plane.

penetration test.gloss: A test of a computer system's access control, in which a user attempts to gain access to the system without the prescribed credentials.

pentachoron.gloss: A four-dimensional object analogous to a tetrahedron, constructed out of five tetrahedra.

pluripolar.gloss: Being a subset of the values which a plurisubharmonic function takes to −∞.

plurisubharmonic.gloss: Describing a generalization of subharmonic functions

plus-minus sign.gloss: the symbol ±, meaning "plus or minus", used to indicate the precision of an approximation (as in "The result is 10 ± 0.3", meaning the result is anywhere in the inclusive range from 9.7 to 10.3), or as a convenient shorthand for a quantity with two possible values of opposing sign and identical magnitude (as in "The roots of the equation x²-4=0 are ±2").

plycount.gloss: The total number of moves in a game, counting each player's move as 1.

plücker coordinate.gloss: Any of six homogeneous coordinates assigned to a line in projective 3-space, used in geometric algebra and computer graphics.

plücker embedding.gloss: A method of realizing the Grassmannian Gr_k(V) of all k-dimensional subspaces of an n-dimensional vector space V as a subvariety of a projective space.

plücker matrix.gloss: A special skew-symmetric 4×4 matrix that characterizes a straight line in projective space, and is defined by six Plücker coordinates with four degrees of freedom.

plücker relation.gloss: Any of a group of simple quadratic relations that are satisfied by the Plücker embedding.

pmmu.gloss: Initialism of paged memory management unit.

png.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of PNG; Portable Network Graphics, an open protocol for digital images.

pochhammer symbol.gloss: The notation (x)ₙ, where n is a non-negative integer, which depending on the context represents either the rising factorial or the falling factorial.

pocket computer.gloss: A small portable computer with a screen capable of displaying only a few lines of text.

pod slurping.gloss: The illicit copying of data from an unattended personal computer by plugging in a portable storage device

podule.gloss: An expansion mechanism for ARM-based computer systems, generally a Eurocard-compatible printed circuit board that plugs into a backplane inside the machine.

poeaa.gloss: Initialism of Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture.

poincaré map.gloss: The intersection of a periodic orbit in the state space of a continuous dynamical system with a certain lower-dimensional subspace (the Poincaré section), transversal to the flow of the system.

poincaré recurrence time.gloss: Of certain systems, the total amount of time required for the system to revert to a state that is almost identical to its current state.

poincaré space.gloss: An n-dimensional topological space with a distinguished element µ of its nth homology group such that taking the cap product with an element of the kth cohomology group yields an isomorphism to the (n − k)th cohomology group.

point.gloss: A small dot or mark. A decimal point (now especially when reading decimal fractions aloud).
A small dot or mark. A zero-dimensional mathematical object representing a location in one or more dimensions; something considered to have position but no magnitude or direction.
To separate an integer from a decimal with a decimal point.
To direct the central processing unit to seek information at a certain location in memory.

point at infinity.gloss: Any point added to a space to achieve projective completion.

point elasticity.gloss: The ratio of the relative change in a function's output with respect to the relative change in its input, for infinitesimal changes at a certain point.

point function.gloss: Any function whose values are points

point group.gloss: A group of isometries leaving a fixed point.

point mass.gloss: A probability distribution with unity probability mass at one specific outcome, and zero probability mass everywhere else.

point of contact.gloss: A person who is associated with a defined Internet entity.

point of inflection.gloss: A point on a curve at which the sign of the curvature changes; at this point the second derivative of the underlying function will be zero, but positive on one side and negative on the other.

point of tangency.gloss: The point where a tangent line and its curve meet

point release.gloss: A software release that is only slightly different from a previous version and thus having the same major version number, only differing in minor version number (after the decimal point).

point source.gloss: The abstract concept of a singularity emitting a flux or flow. A source with infinitesimal dimensions in space.

point-and-click.gloss: With which the user interacts by pointing and clicking, using a mouse or similar device.

point-and-drool.gloss: Synonym of point-and-click (implying that such a user interface is preferred by unintelligent, technically incompetent people)

point-free.gloss: Employing or relating to tacit programming.

point-set topology.gloss: The general field of topology, not restricting attention to specific classes of spaces, and not using algebraic topology.

pointclass.gloss: A collection of sets of points (ordinarily understood to be elements of some perfect Polish space), characterized by some sort of definability property.

pointcut.gloss: In aspect-oriented programming, a set of join points specifying when advice should run during execution.

pointed.gloss: That has a named, but otherwise arbitrary, point (called the basepoint) that remains unchanged during subsequent discussion and is kept track of during all operations.

pointee.gloss: The data or object referenced by a pointer.

pointel.gloss: Any of the eight vertices of a voxel.

pointer.gloss: Anything that points or is used for pointing. A variable that holds the address of a memory location where a value can be stored.
Anything that points or is used for pointing. An icon that indicates the position of the pointing device, such as a mouse.

pointerlike.gloss: Like a pointer (variable holding a memory address).

pointing device.gloss: Any device, such as a mouse or trackball, used to control an on-screen pointer or cursor.

pointing stick.gloss: An isometric joystick used as a pointing device.

pointless.gloss: Point-free; employing the tacit programming paradigm.

pointless topology.gloss: An approach to topology that avoids mentioning points.

pointlessness.gloss: The quality of not mentioning points.

pointwise.gloss: Occurring or true for each point of a given set.

pointy.gloss: In the Raku programming language: being a block or subroutine that acts as a closure accepting a list of parameters (denoted by the pointed arrow symbol ->).

poison.gloss: To place false or malicious data into (a cache, etc.) as part of an exploit.

poison message.gloss: A message that causes processing to fail, and thus remains in the message queue and prevents processing of further messages.

poison queue.gloss: A special message queue into which poison messages are diverted, to prevent them from blocking the system.

poisson distribution.gloss: Any of a class of discrete probability distributions that express the probability of a given number of events occurring in a fixed time interval, where the events occur independently and at a constant average rate; describable as a limit case of either binomial or negative binomial distributions.

poisson process.gloss: A stochastic process in which events occur continually and independently of one another.

poissonian.gloss: Of or pertaining to the Poisson distribution.

poissonization.gloss: Analysis of a multivariate combinatorial distribution by turning interdependent variables into independent Poisson distributions.

poke.gloss: To modify the value stored in (a memory address).
The storage of a value in a memory address, typically to modify the behaviour of a program or to cheat at a video game.

pola.gloss: Initialism of principle of least astonishment.

polar.gloss: Of or having a pole or polarity, as: Of a coordinate system, specifying the location of a point in a plane by using a radius and an angle.
The line joining the points of contact of tangents drawn to meet a curve from a point called the pole of the line.

polar axis.gloss: A fixed line, usually horizontal, used in polar coordinates and from which an angle coordinate is measured.

polar cone.gloss: Relative to a set S in Rⁿ, the set of points y such that the inner product of x and y is not positive for any point x in S.

polar coordinates.gloss: The coordinates of a point in a plane, measured as its Cartesian distance from the origin and the angle measured counterclockwise from the x-axis to a line joining the point to the origin.
A system of coordinates using such measurements to indicate position.

The coordinates of a point in three-dimensional space, measured as its Cartesian distance from the origin, the angle measured from the z-axis to a line joining the point to the origin, and the angle measured counterclockwise from the x-axis to this line.

polar equation.gloss: An equation defining a curve in terms of radius and angle.

polarity.gloss: An indicator of the positivity or negativity of a literal. ᵂᵖ

pole.gloss: A fixed point relative to other points or lines.
For a meromorphic function f(z), any point a for which f(z)→∞ as z→a.

policer.gloss: A software component that enforces a security policy.

polish notation.gloss: A notation for arithmetic (and logical) formulae in which operations (respectively, quantifiers and operands) are written immediately before their operands, used to avoid the need for parentheses; for example, 3 * (4 + 7) is written as * 3 + 4 7 and A AND B is written as AND A B.

polish space.gloss: A separable, completely metrizable topological space

poll.gloss: To (repeatedly) request the status of something (such as a computer or printer on a network).

poller.gloss: a task or process that periodically checks for a condition being satisfied, such as the availability of new data

polling.gloss: A technique that continually interrogates a peripheral or service to see if it has data to transfer.

poloid.gloss: A closed loop that has been twisted in a third dimension.

polyabolo.gloss: A polyform made by joining right isosceles triangles edge to edge in various arrangements.

polyache.gloss: A mathematical function defined in terms of the sums of powers. (See reference for details.)

polyalgorithm.gloss: A set of algorithms together with rules for choosing when to use each one.

polyare.gloss: Any pattern formed from a polyomino by removing half of each square such that the squares are still joined

polybius square.gloss: A grid used for fractionating plaintext characters so that they can be represented by a smaller set of symbols.

polychoral.gloss: Of, pertaining to or derived from a polychoron.

polychoric.gloss: Of or pertaining to the relationship between two latent variables, each assumed to have a normal distribution and associated with an ordinal variable.
Of, pertaining to or derived from a polychoron.

polyconvexity.gloss: A generalization of the notion of convexity for functions defined on spaces of matrices.

polycount.gloss: The total number of polygons found in a three-dimensional model.

polycube.gloss: A polyform made by joining one or more cubes face to face in various arrangements.

polycycle.gloss: A planar countably locally-finite graph in which all interior vertices have the maximum vertex degree and all interior faces are polygons with the same number of faces.

polydivisible.gloss: Describing an integer whose first digits are divisible by the numbers of digits concerned

polydrafter.gloss: A polyform made by joining N-2 triangles edge to edge in various arrangements, each of these triangles being a right triangle with angles 30°, 60° and 90°.

polyexponential.gloss: A function of multiple exponential terms.

polyfill.gloss: An algorithm to fill a polygon with a particular color.

polyfold.gloss: A metrizable space together with an equivalence class of sc-smooth structures.

polyform.gloss: A plane or solid figure constructed by joining together identical polygons edge to edge.

polygamma function.gloss: A meromorphic function on ℂ, defined as the (m+1)-th derivative (for a given order m) of the logarithm of the gamma function.

polygenic.gloss: having an infinite number of derivatives at a point (otherwise it is monogenic)

polyglot.gloss: A file that can be interpreted validly as multiple formats.
A program written to be valid in multiple programming languages.

polygon.gloss: A plane figure bounded by edges that are all straight lines.
The boundary of such a figure.
A figure comprising vertices and (not necessarily straight) edges, alternatingly.
Such a figure and its interior, taken as a whole.

polygon mesh.gloss: A collection of vertices, edges and faces that defines the shape of a polyhedral object.
