polygon soup.gloss: An arbitrary collection of polygons with no particular distinguishing traits, thus possibly difficult to decompose for rendering.

polygon-circle graph.gloss: A graph (set of connected points) in which each vertex corresponds to a convex polygon circumscribed in a common circle, and in which (graph) vertices are adjacent iff their corresponding polygons intersect geometrically.

polygonality.gloss: The state of being a polygon, the degree to which an object is polygonal.

polygonhood.gloss: The state of being a polygon.

polygonization.gloss: The subdivision of a plane into polygons

polygonize.gloss: To subdivide a plane into polygons.

polygonness.gloss: The state of being a polygon.

polyhe.gloss: A pattern constructed from a polyhex by removing half of each hexagon such that they remain connected

polyhedral.gloss: Of, pertaining to or derived from a polyhedron.
Having multiple planar faces or facets.

polyhedron.gloss: A solid figure with many flat faces and straight edges.

polyhex.gloss: A polyform made by joining one or more regular hexagons edge to edge in various arrangements.

polyhierarchy.gloss: A hierarchical relationship (tree) in which at least one child has more than one parent

polyiamond.gloss: A polyform made by joining one or more equilateral triangles edge to edge in various arrangements, with every polyiamond corresponding to a polyhex.

polykay.gloss: A statistic that is a certain kind of linear combination of sample moments. (See reference for details.)

polykite.gloss: A polyform constructed from quadrilaterals obtained from the superimposition of a triangular and hexagonal grid.

polyline.gloss: A continuous line composed of one or more line segments.

polylogarithm.gloss: A function of complex numbers related to logarithms.

polyloglog.gloss: Relating to a polynomial involving loglog terms

polymorphic.gloss: Having or relating to the ability to take multiple data types for a single parameter.

polymorphic iteration.gloss: The use of an iterator class or interface to enable traversal over the members of any type of collection for which there is a corresponding descendant of that iterator by code which need not know the type of the collection.

polymorphism.gloss: The property of certain typed formal systems of allowing for the use of type variables and binders/quantifiers over those type variables; likewise, the property of certain expressions (within such typed formal systems) of making use of at least one such typed variable.

polynomial.gloss: An expression consisting of a sum of a finite number of terms, each term being the product of a constant coefficient and one or more variables raised to a non-negative integer power, such as a_nxⁿ+a_n-1xⁿ⁻¹+...+a_0x⁰.
Able to be described or limited by a polynomial.

polynomial basis.gloss: A basis of a polynomial ring (said ring being viewed either as a vector space over the field of coefficients or as a free module over the ring of coefficients).

Specifically, a basis, of the form {1, α, ..., αⁿ⁻¹}, of a finite extension F_(qⁿ) of a Galois field F_q, where α is a primitive element of F_(qⁿ) (i.e., a root of a degree-n primitive polynomial over F_q).

polynomial equation.gloss: Any algebraic equation in which one or both sides are in the form of a polynomial.

polynomial form.gloss: A linear combination of powers of an indeterminate (or products of powers of more than one indeterminate), with coefficients belonging to an integral domain or a field. (The indeterminate is thought of as an element extraneous to the set of coefficients, instead of as a variable element of it (as in the case of polynomial functions), just as, say, the square root of negative one is an element extraneous to the set of integers when it is adjoined to them to form the domain of Gaussian integers. The indeterminate forms a free commutative monoid, to which all powers of it belong, and the unity of it can also show up implicitly in the constant term of a polynomial form.)

polynomial function.gloss: Any function whose value is the solution of a polynomial; an element of a subring of the ring of all functions over an integral domain, which subring is the smallest to contain all the constant functions and also the identity function. (If the polynomial is multivariate then there is a different identity function corresponding to each variable.)

polynomial ring.gloss: A ring (which is also a commutative algebra), denoted K[X], formed from the set of polynomials (usually of one variable, in a given set, X), with coefficients in a given ring (often a field), K.

polynomial time.gloss: The complexity class where the runtime can be bounded (from above) by a polynomial in the input size.

polynomiograph.gloss: A two-dimensional coloured image, prepared using polynomiography, that is the representation of a polynomial

polynomiography.gloss: An iterative process used to create two-dimensional coloured images (polynomiographs) that are the representations of polynomials

polynormal.gloss: Such that its closure under conjugation by any element of the parent group can also be achieved via closure by conjugation by some element in the subgroup generated.

polyomino.gloss: A plane polyform made by joining one or more squares edge to edge in various arrangements; a similar polyform made from triangles or hexagons (or any polygon that can tile a plane)

polypaint.gloss: A feature allowing the user to "paint" color directly onto the polygons of a three-dimensional model without first creating a texture map.

polyplet.gloss: An object, similar to a polyomino, made by attaching squares joined at their edges or corners

polyquadratic.gloss: Involving multiple quadratic equations or functions

polyrepo.gloss: A software project in which different components are located in separate code repositories which can be versioned individually (as opposed to a monorepo in which all the code exists within a single repository).

polysaturated.gloss: Having the property that for some cardinality, all subsets of that cardinality or smaller map to another element of the subset.
qualifiers: of an internal binary mapping on a countably infinite set

polyserial.gloss: Relating to the correlation between multiple continuous variables

polysingularity.gloss: The condition of a function or equation that has multiple singularities

polyspectrum.gloss: A higher-order spectrum of a multivariate stationary time series

polystick.gloss: A figure made by joining line segments of equal length end to end at right angles.

polysyllogism.gloss: A number of propositions that, together, constitute a sequence of syllogisms

polytomous.gloss: Of a variable: having more than two categories.

polytope.gloss: A geometric shape (of any number of dimensions) which is fully enclosed and has flat sides, making it a member of the generalized class of shapes which includes the two-dimensional polygon and three-dimensional polyhedron; (formally) a finite region of n-dimensional space bounded by hyperplanes.

polytorus.gloss: The set of all vectors of a given dimension such that each element of the vector is within a radius r of the corresponding element of a central vector.

polytree.gloss: a graph with at most one undirected path between any two vertices. In other words, a directed acyclic graph (DAG) for which there are no undirected cycles either.

polytrope.gloss: A particular solution to an equation concerning self-gravitating, polytropic fluid

polytype.gloss: In the Hindley–Milner type system, a data type containing variables bound by one or more ∀ (for-all) quantifiers.

polyvariadic.gloss: Supporting a variable but nonzero number of arguments.

polyzeta.gloss: A complex function related to zeta functions

pon.gloss: Initialism of passive optical network, technology and standards for fiber-optic broadband access.

pong.gloss: A packet sent in reply to a ping, thereby indicating the presence of a host.

pons asinorum.gloss: A method for finding the middle term of a syllogism in Aristotlean analytics.
A proposition in Euclid stating that the angles at the base of an isoceles triangle are equal.

pontryagin product.gloss: A product on the homology of a topological space induced by a product on the topological space.

pool.gloss: A set of resources that are kept ready to use.

pop.gloss: The removal of a data item from the top of a stack.
To remove (a data item) from the top of a stack.

pop out.gloss: To appear on the screen as a temporary window or menu.

pop-in.gloss: A performance issue in three-dimensional graphics, causing objects or textures to "pop" suddenly into view as they are loaded, rather than smoothly moving into view.

popout.gloss: A user interface element that opens a small separate section in front of the main content.

populate.gloss: To fill initially empty items in a collection.

population.gloss: A count of the number of residents within a political or geographical boundary such as a town, a nation or the world. The number of living cells in a pattern.
A group of units (persons, objects, or other items) enumerated in a census or from which a sample is drawn.
The act of filling initially empty items in a collection.

population mean.gloss: The mean (usually arithmetic, but possibly geometric) of all members of a population or all possible values from which a sample can be taken, as opposed to a sample mean.

popup blocker.gloss: A piece of software that prevents pop-up advertisements from being displayed.

porcelain.gloss: The set of Git commands, such as `git commit` or `git checkout`, which control the high-level state of the repository, each typically combining the behaviour of multiple plumbing commands.

porism.gloss: A proposition affirming the possibility of finding such conditions as will render a certain determinate problem indeterminate or capable of innumerable solutions.

port.gloss: A logical or physical construct in and from which data are transferred. Computer port on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
A female connector of an electronic device, into which a cable's male connector can be inserted.
A number that delimits a connection for specific processes or parts of a network service.
To adapt, modify, or recode to work on a different platform.
A program that has been adapted, modified, or recoded so that it works on a different platform; the act of this adapting.
A set of files used to build and install a binary executable file from the source code of an application.

port forwarding.gloss: The forwarding of a network port from one device to another; especially, such forwarding when done to provide an external user with access to a port on a private IP address.

port knocking.gloss: A means of securing ports on a firewall by requiring the host to attempt to connect to a prespecified sequence of closed ports before being allowed access to the desired port.

port replicator.gloss: A device used to quickly connect multiple peripherals to a laptop through a single interface, typically through a USB port.

port triggering.gloss: A configuration option on a NAT-enabled router that controls communication between internal and external host machines on an IP network.

portability.gloss: The quality of being portable. The ability of a program (or software system) to execute properly on multiple hardware platforms.

portable.gloss: Of software: able to be run on multiple hardware or operating systems.
Of a program: able to be copied directly from one machine to another without the use of an installer.

portable computer.gloss: A microcomputer powered by batteries with an integral display screen and integral input device (such as a keyboard) that can be used on the move.

portable executable.gloss: A file format used for executable programs, DLLs, fonts, etc. in Microsoft Windows and some other operating systems.

portal.gloss: A connecting window between volumes, in portal rendering.

portal rendering.gloss: An algorithm for determining the visibility of objects in a three-dimensional world, based on partitioning the space into polygonal, generally convex regions that can be used to form generalizations about the visibility of objects within those regions.

portation.gloss: The act of porting software between hardware or operating system platforms.

porter.gloss: One who ports software (makes it usable on another platform).

porter-duff compositing.gloss: A technique for image compositing using an alpha channel.

portmapper.gloss: A software service that maps programs to the ports they will use to communicate over a network.

portrait.gloss: A print orientation where the vertical sides are longer than the horizontal sides.

portscan.gloss: To scan (a network host) in order to detect open ports.
The scanning of a network host in order to detect open ports.

portscanner.gloss: A software program that performs portscans.

portsweep.gloss: A portscan that connects to numerous host computers in search of a specific open port rather than scanning a single computer for any open port.

posedness.gloss: The condition of being posed in the stated manner

posetal.gloss: Of, pertaining to, or being a poset.

posit.gloss: A number format representing a real number consisting of a sign bit, a variable-size "regime" part (which modifies the exponent), up to two exponent bits, and a fraction part, proposed as a more efficient alternative to IEEE 754 floats in AI applications.

position vector.gloss: Of a point, a vector going from the origin to that point; equivalently, the transpose of the point.

position-independent code.gloss: Code that is able to execute correctly regardless of its memory address.

position-independent executable.gloss: An executable (a program) that is able to run correctly regardless of what memory address it is loaded into.

positional.gloss: An argument that is passed to a subroutine according to its position in the invocation code, rather than on its name; compare with named.

positional parameter.gloss: a parameter that is passed by position, rather than by name, in a function call

positioning time.gloss: Random-access time: the time required to move the hard disk arm to the desired cylinder (seek time) and for the desired sector to rotate under the disk head (rotational latency).

positive.gloss: Greater than or equal to zero.

positive linear functional.gloss: A kind of linear functional which yields a non-negative scalar when given a non-negative function as parameter.

positive logic.gloss: A logical system or fragment thereof not containing a negation operator.

positive measure.gloss: A function whose domain is a σ-algebra, whose codomain is [0,∞], and which is countably additive.

positive recurrence.gloss: the quality of being positive recurrent.

positive recurrent.gloss: recurrent with finite expected return time.

positive zero.gloss: A signed magnitude representation of zero in which the sign bit indicates a positive number.

positive-definite.gloss: Said of a real, square matrix: that the product of it with a column vector on its right side and the transpose of that column vector on its left side is greater or equal to zero, only equaling zero if the vector itself is zero.
Said of a quadratic form: that the application of it to a tuple is greater or equal to zero, only equaling zero if the tuple itself is zero.

positive-sum.gloss: Pertaining to a game or situation where overall benefits to all participants can increase.

positone.gloss: of a particular kind of eigenvalue problem involving a nonlinear function on the reals that is continuous, positive, and monotone.

positroid.gloss: A matroid of a real matrix with nonnegative maximal minors

posology.gloss: In the works of English philosopher Jeremy Bentham (1748–1832): the study of quantity; mathematics.

possibilistic.gloss: Of, pertaining to or derived using possibility.

post.gloss: To successfully perform a power-on self-test.

post-build.gloss: After the build step that creates an executable program from source code.

post-decrement.gloss: A decrement operation that takes place after evaluation of the expression that contains the variable being decremented.
To perform such an operation upon.

post-increment.gloss: An increment operation that takes place after evaluation of the expression that contains the variable being incremented.
To perform such an operation upon.

post-pc.gloss: After the decline of the personal computer in favour of mobile devices.

post-wimp.gloss: Belonging to user interface designs that move away from the traditional windows, icons, menus and pointer in an attempt to find something better.

postamble.gloss: Closing statements of a computer program; final or closing part of data.

postback.gloss: The transmission of data back to the same web page by means of HTTP POST.

postcardware.gloss: A software product whose author requests as payment a postcard from the user's hometown.

postcompose.gloss: To apply (an operation) after another operation has occurred.

postcondition.gloss: A condition that must be met immediately after execution of some piece of code.

postcritical.gloss: Pertaining to the set of all images of the critical points of a function.

postdominance.gloss: The property of a node that postdominates another.

postdominate.gloss: A node z postdominates a node n if all paths to the exit node of the graph starting at n must go through z

posterior.gloss: The probability that a hypothesis is true (calculated by Bayes' theorem).

posterior probability.gloss: The probability of an event given the knowledge of occurrence of other events that bear on it: P( A | B ) as contrasted to P( A ), where A is the sought event and B is the sign or symptom event.

postfiller.gloss: In text processing systems, a pattern of text that is expected to occur after the portion of interest.

posting.gloss: A message posted to a computerized bulletin board, a newsgroup, a blog, etc.

postmultiply.gloss: To multiply (the elements of a vector or matrix) by a following factor

postorder.gloss: Of a tree traversal, recursively visiting the left and right subtrees before the root.

postpend.gloss: To append at the end of a text string.

poststate.gloss: A modified state that exists after executing an operation.

postulation.gloss: Something self-evident that can be assumed as the basis of an argument.

posynomial.gloss: A function of the form f(x_1,x_2,…,x_n)=∑ₖ₌₁ᴷc_kx_1^(a_1k)⋯x_n^(a_nk), where all the coordinates x_i and coefficients c_k are positive real numbers, and the exponents a_ik are real numbers.

potato.gloss: Metaphor for a person or thing of little value. An underpowered computer or other device, especially when small in size.

potato paradox.gloss: A calculation having a counterintuitive result: "Fred brings home 100 kg of potatoes, which consist of 99% water. He then leaves them outside overnight so that they consist of 98% water. What is their new weight?" The surprising answer is 50 kg.

pov.gloss: Initialism of percentage of volume, a type of securities trading algorithm.

pow.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of PoW (“proof of work”).

power.gloss: A product of equal factors (and generalizations of this notion): xⁿ, read as "x to the power of n" or the like, is called a power and denotes the product x×x×⋯×x, where x appears n times in the product; x is called the base and n the exponent.
The probability that a statistical test will reject the null hypothesis when the alternative hypothesis is true.

power button.gloss: A button that switches an electrical device on or off. A button that switches the computer on or off (or, on more recent models, often enables sleep mode).

power function.gloss: A function where the independent variable is raised to a particular real number power.

power law.gloss: A mathematical relationship in which the magnitude of something is proportional to a fixed power of the magnitude of something else (i.e. the relationship takes the form f(x)=axᵏ).

power mac.gloss: A family of personal computers designed, manufactured, and sold by Apple Computer, Inc. from 1994 until 2006.

power series.gloss: Any infinite series of the general form ∑ᵢ₌₀ ᪲a_i(x-c)ⁱ.

power set.gloss: The set whose elements comprise all the subsets of S (including the empty set and S itself).

power tower.gloss: A chain of exponentiations, or raising to powers, of the form a^(aa...); tetration.

power user.gloss: A person who makes heavy use of computers, running many applications and capable of using advanced functionality.
A computer user who seeks and uses products having the most features and the fastest performance.

power wall.gloss: The rapidly increasing loss of efficiency due to overheating as the power/speed of a CPU increases.

power-associative algebra.gloss: An algebra such that every subalgebra generated by one element is associative.

power-cycle.gloss: To turn a device off and then back on again, usually to restore proper function by forcing a malfunctioning or unresponsive device to reset or reinitialize, or as a step in troubleshooting the device.

powerful number.gloss: A positive integer m such that for every prime number p dividing m, p² also divides m. Equivalently, it is the product of a square and a cube.

powerlike.gloss: Of or resembling power or the use of power.

powerpointer.gloss: One who creates or delivers a presentation using PowerPoint or a similar Web-based slideshow product.

powerpointlessness.gloss: The senseless and excessive use of PowerPoint as a communication medium, characterized by an overreliance of superficial visual effects, such as animated transitions, which detract from the clarity and substantive quality of the presentation.

powerstructure.gloss: An analog of a power set in the context of mathematical structuralism.

powerwash.gloss: The process of resetting a Chromebook or any other ChromeOS device to its factory settings, by deleting all data from the unit.

ppa.gloss: Initialism of Personal Package Archive, a software repository for managing source packages in Ubuntu.

ppd.gloss: Initialism of pixels per degree (“a measurement of the visual fidelity of a virtual reality headset”).

ppe.gloss: Initialism of PCBoard programming executable: a software component used to extend the features of a bulletin board system.

ppmcc.gloss: Initialism of Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient.

ppu.gloss: Initialism of physics processing unit, a dedicated microprocessor designed to handle the calculations of physics.

practical number.gloss: Any positive integer having the property that all smaller integers can be represented as sums of distinct divisors of it

practice.gloss: The ongoing pursuit of a craft or profession, particularly in medicine or the fine arts. An easy and concise method of applying the rules of arithmetic to questions which occur in trade and business.

pragma.gloss: A compiler directive; data embedded in source code by programmers to indicate some intention to a compiler.

pragmat.gloss: A pragma, or compiler directive, in the ALGOL 68 programming language.

pre-abelian category.gloss: An additive category in which all kernels and cokernels exist.

pre-alpha version.gloss: A program or application that is not feature-complete and is not usually released to the public. Developers are usually still deciding on what features the program should have at this stage of software development. This stage comes before the alpha version, and is the first software development stage given to a program.

pre-decrement.gloss: A decrement operation that takes place prior to evaluation of the expression that contains the variable being decremented.
To perform such an operation upon.

pre-echo.gloss: A digital audio compression artifact where a (typically percussive) sound is heard before it should occur.

pre-hilbert space.gloss: An incomplete metric space with an inner product.

pre-hook.gloss: A section of code that runs immediately before a hook call.

pre-increment.gloss: An increment operation that takes place prior to evaluation of the expression that contains the variable being incremented.
To perform such an operation upon.

pre-render.gloss: To render (a complex image) in advance.

preadditive category.gloss: A category which is enriched over the category Ab of abelian groups; that is, each hom-set is equipped with an abelian group structure, and composition is distributive over the group operations of each hom-set.

prealgebra.gloss: A particular form of Lie algebra; also applied analogously to other types of algebra.

prealgebraic.gloss: Of or relating to a prealgebra.

preassociative.gloss: Prior to association into an aggregation

prebuffer.gloss: To place into a buffer in preparation for later retrieval or playback.

precalculus.gloss: A course, or set of courses, that includes (specifically) trigonometry and algebra at an appropriate level to prepare students to study calculus.

precanonical.gloss: In raw form, before conversion to a canonical form.

precedence rule.gloss: A set of rules specifying the order in which parts of an expression are parsed, especially when parentheses are not present.

prechart.gloss: Part of a chart that must be traversed with a successful outcome in order for the main chart to have a successful outcome.

precisification.gloss: The process of making a statement more precise.

precisify.gloss: To make precise; to make more precise.

precision.gloss: The number of significant digits to which a value may be measured reliably.

precisive.gloss: Exactly limiting by cutting off all that is not absolutely relevant.

precompact.gloss: Forming a relatively compact subspace; Having a closure that is compact.
Totally bounded; Having a cover that consists of finitely many finite subsets.

precompiler.gloss: A program or algorithm that precompiles.

precomplete.gloss: Having a certain property that is analogous to completeness but weaker.

precompose.gloss: To apply (an operation) before another operation occurs.

precomposed.gloss: Describing a character that can also be represented an equivalent string of other characters (typically a letter and a diacritical mark).

precomposition.gloss: A form of pullback where a function of a variable y can be rewritten as a function of x if y itself is a function of x.

preconditioner.gloss: A matrix that has a smaller condition number than another.

preconfigure.gloss: To set up or configure a software system or hardware device with standard settings before selling or implementing it.

precover.gloss: A generalization of a cover in which the kernel may contain a non-zero pure subgroup.

predecessor.gloss: A vertex having a directed path to another vertex

predeclaration.gloss: A declaration made in advance; forward declaration.

predeclare.gloss: To declare some source code element (such as a class) in advance of its full description, so that other preceding parts of the code can refer to it.

predecoding.gloss: The process of partially decoding machine instructions prior to their storage in the instruction cache, typically to identify instruction boundaries, classify instruction types, and facilitate faster or parallel decoding during execution.

predefined function.gloss: Any of a set of subroutines that perform standard mathematical functions included in a programming language; either included in a program at compilation time, or called when a program is executed

predesignate.gloss: Having its quantity indicated by a verbal sign, as with "all", "none", etc.

predicable.gloss: One of the five most general relations of attributes involved in logical arrangements, namely, genus, species, difference, property, and accident.

predicament.gloss: That which is predicated; a category.

predicate.gloss: A term of a statement, where the statement may be true or false depending on whether the thing referred to by the values of the statement's variables has the property signified by that (predicative) term.
An operator, expression, or function that returns either true or false.
To assert or state as an attribute or quality of something.

predicate calculus.gloss: The branch of logic that deals with quantified statements such as "there exists an x such that..." or "for any x, it is the case that...", where x is a member of the domain of discourse.

predicate logic.gloss: The generic term for symbolic formal systems like first-order logic, second-order logic, many-sorted logic or infinitary logic.

predication.gloss: The act of making something the subject or predicate of a proposition.
The parallel execution of all possible outcomes of a branch instruction, all except one of which are discarded after the branch condition has been evaluated.

predicativism.gloss: A philosophical position that definitions of concepts can only use other concepts that don't depend on the concept being defined.

predictand.gloss: That which is to be predicted.

prediction.gloss: A probability estimation based on statistical methods.

predictive.gloss: Simulated data generated from a statistical model, based on the estimates for the real data.

predictive parser.gloss: A recursive descent parser that does not require backtracking.

predictive text.gloss: A system for inputting text on a device where individual buttons correspond to several characters that attempts to guess which word was intended (typically out of a writable vocabulary), as opposed to a system where disambiguation is achieved through repeated presses of the same key.
A system, as in a word processor, that attempts to predict and autocomplete the text being typed.

predictive texting.gloss: The composition of messages using predictive text.

predictor variable.gloss: An independent variable that may be used to predict the value of another, especially in statistical regression

predimension.gloss: The result of a function on a group of sets, where the function satisfies three conditions: (1) it returns 0 for the empty set; (2) if one set is contained in another set, the function always returns a value that is less than or equal to the result for the containing set; (3) the result for the union of two sets is less than or equal to the sum of the results for each of those sets individually minus the result for their intersection.

predual.gloss: An object whose dual space is some other specified object.

preemption.gloss: An act or process that preempts; a preventive or forestalling action; as: The temporary interruption of a task without its cooperation and with the intention of resuming it at a later time.

preexponent.gloss: Any factor that multiplies an exponential function

preexponential.gloss: Describing any factor that multiplies an exponential function

prefab.gloss: A reusable object in a video game world.

preferences.gloss: The user-specified settings of parameters in interactive computer software

preferential attachment.gloss: A positive feedback cycle where the more connected nodes in a graph are more likely to receive new links.

prefetch.gloss: To load data or instructions in anticipation of their need

prefetcher.gloss: A system or process that prefetches data.

prefiller.gloss: In text processing systems, a pattern of text that is expected to occur before the portion of interest.

prefix.gloss: Something placed before another An initial segment of a string of characters.

prefix coding.gloss: A coding system that uses (typically variable-length) codes that are distinguished by their "prefix property", which requires that there is no code word in the system that is a prefix (initial segment) of any other code word in the system.

preflight.gloss: Serving to confirm that requests can be accepted, before sending an actual request.

prefork.gloss: To fork (a process) in advance, so that additional similar processes are immediately available if required later.

prefundamental.gloss: Given a group G that acts on a set P, a subset P is prefundamental for G if, for any g in G, gB is in B only if g is 1.

pregroupoid.gloss: A category together with its inversion.

prehomogeneous.gloss: Having an automorphism group with an open orbit.

preimage.gloss: For a given function, the set of all elements of the domain that are mapped into a given subset of the codomain; (formally) given a function ƒ : X → Y and a subset B ⊆ Y, the set ƒ⁻¹(B) = {x ∈ X : ƒ(x) ∈ B}.

preimage attack.gloss: An attack on a cryptographic hash function that is able to find a preimage for a hash; that is, it is able to determine (faster than by brute force) some input that results in a known hash when passed through the algorithm.

preindesignate.gloss: Having no sign expressing quantity; indefinite.

preinitialization.gloss: A phase prior to initialization, when something is preinitialized.

preinitialize.gloss: To preprepare (a data structure, etc.) so that it is ready to be initialized.

prejacent.gloss: A proposition laid out previously; a proposition from which another proposition is inferred.

preloaded.gloss: Of software, already installed on a personal computer at the time of purchase.

prelude.gloss: A standard module or library of subroutines and functions to be imported, generally by default, into a program.

premarginalization.gloss: marginalization prior to some other procedure

premaster.gloss: To make a master copy of (data) on a hard disk before writing it to optical disc.

premature optimization.gloss: The act of wasting resources on optimising source code that does not represent a significant bottleneck.

premetric.gloss: Any of several specific generalizations of a metric.

premise.gloss: Any of the first propositions of a syllogism, from which the conclusion is deduced.

premise indicator.gloss: A word or phrase that signals a premise in an argument, such as: as, for, since, because, given that, inasmuch as, for the reason that, etc.

premouse.gloss: A generalization of a mouse that is not necessarily iterable.

premultiply.gloss: To multiply a matrix or quaternion by a preceding factor noncommutatively

prenex.gloss: Of a formula, having all of its quantifiers at the beginning.
The initial part of a prenex formula where all of the formula's bound variables are bound by logical quantifiers.

prenex normal form.gloss: A way of expressing a formula of predicate logic such the formula consists of a prenex and a matrix, with the prenex preceding the matrix.

preoptimization.gloss: An advance optimization; an instance of preoptimizing.

preorder.gloss: A binary relation that is reflexive and transitive.
Such that, recursively, the root is visited before the left and right subtrees.
qualifiers: of a traversal of a tree

prepaging.gloss: The loading of memory pages before they are needed, so as to avoid page faults.

prepared statement.gloss: A database query that has parameters which are replaced by values when it is executed, instead of the values being part of the statement itself.

preparser.gloss: A software component that performs parsing in advance.

prepass.gloss: A prior pass of an algorithm or process, sometimes as an optimization to handle simpler cases.

prepend.gloss: To attach (an expression, phrase, etc.) to another, as a prefix.

prepender.gloss: A software component that prepends data to a computer file.

prepopulate.gloss: To populate (form fields, a database, etc.) in advance.

prepotential.gloss: A vector superfield in supersymmetry theory

preprimitive.gloss: Of a variety: not itself primitive, but whose proper subvarieties are all primitive.

preprocessor.gloss: program that processes its input data to produce output that is used as input to another program

preprojective.gloss: Exhibiting a generalization of being projective, in which some, but not every surjective homomorphism splits.

prequantization.gloss: The process of finding a quantum analog of a classical system by introducing a quantization condition.

preradical.gloss: A subfunctor of the identity functor in the category of left modules over a ring with identity.

preread.gloss: An operation in which data is read in advance of its being needed.

preregular.gloss: In which any two topologically distinguishable points can be separated by neighbourhoods

presburger arithmetic.gloss: A set of axioms of first-order logic for the natural numbers specifying the operations of zero, successor, and addition, including a first-order schema of induction, without multiplication.

preseeding.gloss: a way to set answers to questions asked during the installation process, without having to manually enter the answers while the installation is running.

preselection.gloss: The process of a jury selecting entries to be shown in a competition when there are too many entries for the audience or schedule. The term preselection is often used with the opposite meaning in demoscene context, i.e. selecting entries not to be shown.

presemifield.gloss: A finite algebra satisfying all the axioms for a skew field except multiplicative associativity and the existence of a multiplicative identity.

presentation.gloss: The specification of a group by generators and relators.

presentation logic.gloss: The logic that is concerned with the style or manner in which domain and business objects are displayed to users of the software.

presentation software.gloss: A computer software package used to display information, normally in the form of a slideshow.

presented.gloss: Having a specified presentation, or a presentation with specified properties.

presenter.gloss: A small handheld device used to remotely control a computerised slide show.
A conceptual layer in GUI-based software that assumes the functionality of the "middleman".

preshared.gloss: Shared between the communicating parties by some secure channel before it needs to be used.

presheaf.gloss: An abstract mathematical construct which associates data to the open sets of a topological space, generalizing the situation of functions, fiber bundles, manifold structure, etc. on a topological space (but not necessarily in such a way as to make the local and global data compatible, as in a sheaf). Formally, A contravariant functor ℱ whose domain is a category whose objects are open sets of a topological space (called the base space or underlying space) and whose morphisms are inclusion mappings. The image of each open set under ℱ is an object whose elements are called sections, and are which are said to be over the given open set; the image of each inclusion map A→B under ℱ is a morphism ℱ(B)→ℱ(A), called the restriction from B to A and denoted operatorname res_(B,A) or |_(B,A).

presignature.gloss: An intermediate value used in forming a signature, unrelated to the contents of the message being signed.

prestack.gloss: The category c is called a prestack over a category C with a Grothendieck topology if it is fibered over C and for any object U of C and objects x, y of c with image U, the functor from objects over U to sets taking F:V→U to Hom(F*x,F*y) is a sheaf.

prestate.gloss: The state that exists before an operation.

presymplectic.gloss: prior to the introduction of symplectic geometry

pretopology.gloss: The field of study of pretopological spaces (in plural for different prespaces).
A filter subset or a preclosure operator which acts as a distinct prespace (pre-topological space).

pretty.gloss: Matching commonly accepted principles of formatting and syntax, for the sake of readability.

pretty-print.gloss: To display code in a pretty fashion, matching commonly accepted principles of formatting and syntax, for the sake of readability.

pretty-printer.gloss: A computer program that performs pretty-printing.

pretzel knot.gloss: A pretzel link which is a knot.

pretzel link.gloss: A link with a standard projection comprising several tangles, each a braid on two strands, with the tangles arranged in some cyclic order.

pretzelosity.gloss: The condition of having the knotted form of a pretzel

prevariety.gloss: A ringed space that has a finite open cover by affine varieties

preview.gloss: A facility for viewing and checking a document or photo, or changes to it, before saving or printing it.
To show something in advance, a facility for viewing and checking a document or photo, or changes to it, before saving or printing it.

preview-quality.gloss: A type of resolution that is visible in icons, thumbnails, or previews of operations such as scans and printing.

previewer.gloss: A program that provides a preview of a document or other work.

prewarm.gloss: To initialize with the illusion of prior activity.

prewarmed.gloss: Initialized with the illusion of prior activity.

prewellordering.gloss: A binary relation that is transitive, total, and well-founded.

prewhiten.gloss: To modify (a data set) to make the samples statistically independent, analogous to white noise.

prewrite.gloss: A write operation that is buffered instead of being applied directly to the database.

prg.gloss: Initialism of post/redirect/get, a design pattern for web applications.

primal.gloss: To take part in primal therapy.

primality.gloss: The condition of being a prime number.

primary ideal.gloss: Given a commutative ring R, any ideal I such that for any a,b ∈ R, if ab ∈ I then either b ∈ I or aⁿ ∈ I for some integer n > 0.

primary key.gloss: In the design of a database table, the primary key (abbreviated PK) is selected among the non-empty set of candidate keys. The PK is a column (or an irreducible group of columns) able to identify every row of the table.

primary storage.gloss: The volatile memory of a computer directly accessible by the central processing unit; the main memory together with cache memory (and processor registers).

prime.gloss: Having exactly two integral factors: itself and unity (1 in the case of integers).
Such that if it divides a product, it divides one of the multiplicands.
Having its complement closed under multiplication.
Such that the annihilator of any nonzero submodule is equal to the annihilator of the whole module.
A prime element of a mathematical structure, particularly a prime number.
To mark with a prime mark.

prime constellation.gloss: An ordered set of prime numbers having a constant difference between successive elements

prime factor.gloss: A factor of a given integer which is also a prime number.

prime factorization.gloss: The factorization of a positive integer into its constituent prime numbers.

prime field.gloss: A field that contains no proper subfields.

prime formula.gloss: A well-formed formula which has not been made by combining simpler well-formed formulas by means of logical connectives.

prime gap.gloss: The difference between two successive prime numbers.

prime ideal.gloss: Any (two-sided) ideal I such that for arbitrary ideals P and Q, PQ⊆I⟹P⊆I or Q⊆I.

prime number.gloss: Any natural number greater than 1 that cannot be formed by multiplying two smaller natural numbers.
Any natural number (including 1) that is divisible only by itself and 1.

prime number theorem.gloss: Any theorem that concerns the distribution of prime numbers.

prime reciprocal magic square.gloss: A magic square using the decimal digits of the reciprocal of a prime number.

prime ring.gloss: Any nonzero ring R such that for any two (two-sided) ideals P and Q in R, the product PQ = 0 (the zero ideal) if and only if P = 0 or Q = 0.
Synonym of prime subring. A ring which is equal to its own prime subring.

prime subring.gloss: The image of the natural homomorphism from ℤ into R, which is the unique homomorphism mapping 1_ℤ to 1_R. Equivalently, the intersection of all subrings of R.

prime triplet.gloss: An ordered set of three prime numbers in which the smallest and largest of the three differ by six.

primeness.gloss: The quality of being prime, or a prime number.

primitive.gloss: A data type that is built into the programming language, as opposed to more complex structures.
Any of the simplest elements (instructions, statements, etc.) available in a programming language.
A function whose derivative is a given function; an antiderivative.
Not derived from another of the same type

primitive element.gloss: An element that generates a simple extension.
An element that generates the multiplicative group of a given Galois field (finite field).
Given a modulus n, a number g such that every number coprime to n is congruent (modulo n) to some power of g; equivalently, a generator of the multiplicative field of integers modulo n.
An element that is not a positive integer multiple of another element of the lattice.

An element x ∈ C such that μ(x) = x ⊗ g + g ⊗ x, where μ is the comultiplication and g is an element that maps to the multiplicative identity 1 of the base field under the counit (in particular, if C is a bialgebra, g = 1).
qualifiers: of a coalgebra over an element g

primitive element.gloss: An element of a free generating set of a given free group.

primitive polynomial.gloss: A polynomial over an integral domain R such that no noninvertible element of R divides all its coefficients at once; (more specifically) a polynomial over a GCD domain R such that the greatest common divisor of its coefficients equals 1.
A polynomial over a given finite field whose roots are primitive elements; especially, the minimal polynomial of a primitive element of said finite field.

primitive recursion.gloss: The operator ρ, that creates a new function from two functions g, and h, such that

primitive recursive.gloss: Of a function, capable of being constructed from the zero function, successor function, and projection functions, by a finite number of applications of composition and recursion.

primitive root.gloss: For a given modulus n, a number g such that for every a coprime to n there exists an integer k such that gᵏ ≡ a (mod n); a generator (or primitive element) of the multiplicative group, modulo n, of integers relatively prime to n.

primitive type.gloss: A data type provided by a programming language as a basic building block, such as integer, character or Boolean.

primordial element.gloss: A particular kind of a vector in a vector space.

primorial.gloss: Any number belonging to the integer sequence whose nth element is the product of the first n primes.

A unary operation, denoted by the postfix symbol # and defined on the nonnegative integers, which maps 0 to 1, 1 to 1, and each subsequent number to the product of all primes less than or equal to it; the value mapped to by said operation for a given input.

primorial prime.gloss: A prime number that is one more or one less than a primorial. For example, 31 is a primorial prime, since 6# + 1 = 31.

principal.gloss: Chosen or assumed among a branch of possible values of a multi-valued function so that the function is single-valued.

principal ideal.gloss: An ideal I in an algebraic object R (which could be a ring, algebra, semigroup or lattice) that is generated by a given single element a ∈ R; the smallest ideal that contains a.

principal ideal domain.gloss: An integral domain in which every ideal is a principal ideal.

principal ideal ring.gloss: A commutative ring in which every ideal is a principal ideal.
A noncommutative ring in which every left ideal is a principal ideal and so is every right ideal.

principal part.gloss: A polynomial approximation of a power series, made up of monomials whose indices lie in the Newton diagram of the power series and which occur with the same coefficients as in the original power series.
The portion of a Laurent series that has negative exponents.

principal root.gloss: A complex number which, when raised to the power of n, yields the radicand of its nth degree radical, and which has the greatest real part among all such numbers, and positive imaginary part in case of equality of the real parts.

principal square root.gloss: The positive square root of a number; the positive number which, when squared, yields the original number.

principal ultrafilter.gloss: An ultrafilter such that every set belonging to it is the superset of some fixed singleton set.

principle of indifference.gloss: A rule for assigning epistemic probabilities, according to which, in the absence of any relevant evidence, agents should distribute their credence (or 'degrees of belief') equally among all the possible outcomes.

print.gloss: To display a string on the terminal.

print server.gloss: A server that processes print jobs and sends them to one or more printers.

printable.gloss: Of a text character: having a visual representation, unlike the control characters.

printer.gloss: A device, usually attached to a computer, used to print text or images onto paper; an analogous device capable of producing three-dimensional objects.

printer buffer.gloss: A hardware or software device that stores a stream of data to be printed until a printer is ready to process it.

printer-friendly.gloss: Of a document or layout, suitable for printing, without any extraneous formatting, images, etc.

prior probability.gloss: The probability of an event obtained without the knowledge of occurrence of other events that bear on it.

priority queue.gloss: An abstract data type similar to a regular queue or stack abstract data type.

prism.gloss: A polyhedron with parallel ends of the same polygonal shape and size, the other faces being parallelogram-shaped sides. An object having the shape of a geometrical prism (sense 1).

A polyhedron with parallel ends of the same polygonal shape and size, the other faces being parallelogram-shaped sides. A cutting (“open passage at a level lower than the surrounding terrain, dug for a canal, railway, or road to go through”) or an embankment shaped like a prism (sense 1) or a number of prisms, such that its volume can be easily calculated.
A polyhedron with parallel ends of the same polygonal shape and size, the other faces being parallelogram-shaped sides. A crystal in which the faces are parallel to the vertical axis.

A polyhedron with parallel ends of the same polygonal shape and size, the other faces being parallelogram-shaped sides. A transparent block in the shape of a prism (sense 1), typically with triangular ends, used to reflect or refract light.

A polyhedron with parallel ends of the same polygonal shape and size, the other faces being parallelogram-shaped sides. A transparent block in the shape of a prism (sense 1), typically with triangular ends, used to reflect or refract light. A spectrum produced by light being refracted through a prism.

prismatoid.gloss: Any polyhedron whose vertices all lie in either of two parallel planes

prismoid.gloss: A prismatoid that has planar sides, and the same number of vertices in both of its parallel planes.

private key.gloss: The unpublished key in asymmetric cryptography.

privatize.gloss: To render (a variable, etc.) private in scope.

privilege.gloss: An ability to perform an action on the system that can be selectively granted or denied to users.

probabilistic.gloss: Of, pertaining to, or derived using probability.

probabilistically checkable proof.gloss: A reasonable proof of a computational theorem or conjecture obtained via a randomized algorithm.

probabilistics.gloss: A branch of statistics that deals with probabilities

probability.gloss: A number, between 0 and 1, expressing the precise likelihood of an event happening.

probability box.gloss: A quantitative characterization of an imperfectly known probability distribution.

probability density function.gloss: Any function whose integral over a set gives the probability that a random variable has a value in that set.

probability distribution.gloss: A distribution of all possible values of a random variable together with an indication of their probabilities.

probability mass function.gloss: A function that gives the relative probability that a discrete random variable is exactly equal to some value.

probability measure.gloss: A mathematical measure on a probability space that can take on values between 0 and 1, with 0 corresponding to the empty set and 1 to the entire space.

probability space.gloss: A measurable space having a unit measure

probability theory.gloss: The mathematical study of probability (the likelihood of occurrence of random events in order to predict the behavior of defined systems).

probable error.gloss: The half-range of an interval about a central point for the distribution, such that half of the values from the distribution will lie within the interval and half outside.

probit.gloss: A unit, derived from a standard normal distribution, used in measuring the responses to doses.

problematic.gloss: Only affirming the possibility that a predicate be actualised.

probvious.gloss: Able to be shown to hold with very high confidence via heuristic arguments, but not formally provable.

procedural.gloss: Generated by means of a procedure, rather than being designed.

procedure.gloss: A subroutine coded to perform a specific task, which is not permitted a return value when distinguished from a function.

procedure call.gloss: A statement that invokes a procedure in a program.

procedure division.gloss: The part of a COBOL program containing all the instructions that the computer is to execute

process-oriented.gloss: Of or pertaining to a programming paradigm that separates the concerns of data structures and the concurrent processes that act upon them.

processing.gloss: The act of retrieving, storing, classifying, manipulating, transmitting etc. data, especially via computer techniques.

processing unit.gloss: An electrical component (digital circuit) that performs operations on an external data source, usually memory or some other data stream.

procrustean assignment.gloss: A form of assignment to fixed-length string variables in which a shorter value is padded to the necessary length while a longer one is truncated.

prodiscrete.gloss: Isomorphic to the limit of a filtered projective system of discrete groups.

produce.gloss: To extend an area, or lengthen a line.

product.gloss: Anything that is produced; a result. Any operation or a result thereof which generalises multiplication of numbers, like the multiplicative operation in a ring, product of types or a categorical product.

product owner.gloss: In the Scrum framework, the manager of the product backlog, responsible for maximizing the value of the product.

product ring.gloss: A ring that is the direct product of rings.

product topology.gloss: The topology of the Cartesian product of two or more topological spaces which is generated from a basis whose elements are Cartesian products of open subsets of the original spaces, such that for each such Cartesian product only a finite quantity of such subsets are proper.

production.gloss: A rewrite rule specifying a symbol substitution that can be recursively performed to generate new symbol sequences. (More information on Wikipedia.)
The environment where finished code runs, as opposed to staging or development.

productionable.gloss: ready to be placed into a production environment

productive.gloss: A type of set of natural numbers, related to mathematical logic; a set S is productive if there exists a total recursive function f such that ∀x∈ℕ,~~W_x⊆S⇒f(x)∈A⧵W_x, where W_x is a recursive function whose Gödel number is x.

productization.gloss: The act of modifying something, such as a concept or a tool internal to an organization, to make it suitable as a commercial product.

profile.gloss: To measure the performance of various parts of (a program) so as to locate bottlenecks.

profiler.gloss: A software program that measures the performance of different portions of another program in order to locate bottlenecks.

profinite.gloss: Describing certain topological groups formed from finite groups

profinite group.gloss: A topological group that is isomorphic to the inverse limit of some inverse system of discrete finite groups; equivalently, a topological group that is also a Stone space.

profunctor.gloss: A generalization of a relation in category theory

proggie.gloss: A program, especially (historical) an externally produced hacking tool used to attack other users on early America Online services.

progid.gloss: Abbreviation of programmatic identifier (string that represents the underlying Clsid).

program counter.gloss: A register that stores the address of the current (or next) instruction to be carried out by the processor.

program slicer.gloss: A software analysis tool that displays data links and related characteristics to enable a programmer to track the effects of proposed changes.

program trading.gloss: High-volume and high-speed buying and selling of investment securities, such as stocks and bonds, which is initiated and executed by brokerage firms' computer programs that continually monitor market conditions.

programmatically.gloss: Through program code, rather than through a user interface.

programmed function key.gloss: A function key whose function can be assigned by the user or by a program.

programmer art.gloss: Crude or ugly visuals created by a developer as placeholders.

programming.gloss: The act of writing a computer program.

programming in the large.gloss: Designing a complex software system as a composition of smaller parts.

programming in the small.gloss: Writing individual lines of code in a programming language.

programming language.gloss: A code of reserved words and symbols used in computer programs, which give instructions to the computer on how to accomplish certain computing tasks.

programming style.gloss: The conventions and patterns used in writing source code, resulting in a consistent and readable codebase.

progress bar.gloss: A bar that indicates the progression of a task by gradually filling its empty space with solid colour.

progression.gloss: A sequence obtained by adding or multiplying each term by a constant.

progressive scan.gloss: A method of displaying or transmitting an image or film in which all horizontal lines of a frame are drawn in sequence.

progressive web application.gloss: A type of application software delivered through the web, built using common web technologies including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WebAssembly.

project.gloss: To draw straight lines from a fixed point through every point of any body or figure, and let these fall upon a surface so as to form the points of a new figure.

projection.gloss: An image of an object on a surface of fewer dimensions.
An idempotent linear transformation which maps vectors from a vector space onto a subspace.
A transformation which extracts a fragment of a mathematical object.
A morphism from a categorical product to one of its (two) components.

projection matrix.gloss: A transformation matrix whose associated transformation is a projection.
A matrix that maps a vector of response (dependent variable) values to a vector of fitted or predicted values.

projectionless.gloss: In which 0 and 1 are the only projections.

projective.gloss: Of or related to projective geometry: Invariant under projective transformations.
qualifiers: of a property of a geometric object

projective.gloss: Of or related to projective geometry: Defined in or inhabiting a projective space.

In a technical sense, general (but not necessarily so general as to be free); involving such objects: Such that there is another (left) R-module N with M⊕N a free R-module. Equivalently, projective in the category of modules (see below).
qualifiers: of a (left) module M over a ring R

projective.gloss: In a technical sense, general (but not necessarily so general as to be free); involving such objects: Such that, given an epimorphism e:E→X and morphism f:P→X, f factors through e; that is, there exists a morphism ̃f:P→E with e∘̃f=f.
qualifiers: of an object P in a category

projective.gloss: In a technical sense, general (but not necessarily so general as to be free); involving such objects: Such that every epimorphism from a profinite group onto G has a right inverse which is a homomorphism.
In a technical sense, general (but not necessarily so general as to be free); involving such objects: Such that every object in the resolution is projective.
A projective member of a category.

projective frame.gloss: The projection onto an n − 1 dimensional hyperplane (which is extended so as to be projective) of a set of n + 1 affinely independent n-dimensional points (called an affine frame).

projective geometry.gloss: The branch of mathematics that investigates those properties of figures that are invariant under homographies, special kinds of spaces called projective spaces, and the geometric structures that inhabit them.

projective limit.gloss: Synonym of limit (“the cone of a diagram through which any other cone of that same diagram can factor uniquely”)

projective module.gloss: A module which is a direct summand of a free module.

projective plane.gloss: A plane in which any pair of distinct points determine a line and any pair of distinct lines intersect at a point.

projective space.gloss: A kind of geometrical space in which only relation(s) of incidence between points and lines matter; in such a space distances or angles do not matter and parallelism (as in an affine space) does not matter either.

projective variety.gloss: A Zariski closed subvariety of a projective space; the zero-locus of a set of homogeneous polynomials that generates a prime ideal.

projectivise.gloss: The process of transforming a mathematical object into its projective form, often by embedding it into a projective space.

projectivization.gloss: A process (more formally, a mapping) that, given a vector space, specifies an associated projective space; (loosely) the projective space so specified.

projectivize.gloss: The process of transforming a mathematical object into its projective form, often by embedding it into a projective space.

projector.gloss: An operator that forms a projection.

prolate cycloid.gloss: A cycloid where the distance from the point to the center of the rolling circle is longer than the radius of the circle itself, instead of having the point on the circumference.

prologue.gloss: A component of a computer program that prepares the computer to execute a routine.

promax.gloss: Describing a type of rotation in factor analysis.

promiscuous.gloss: The mode in which an NIC gathers all network traffic instead of getting only the traffic intended for it.

promise.gloss: A placeholder object representing the eventual result of an asynchronous operation.

promote.gloss: To treat (a value) as a more capable data type or as having higher priority.

prompt.gloss: A reminder or cue. A sequence of characters that is displayed to indicate that a computer is ready to receive input.
To request (a user) to provide input or do something on a computer.

pronic.gloss: Being the product of two consecutive integers.

pronilfactor.gloss: An ergodic nilspace X/R(X) such that there exists an element x of X and a homomorphism H such that (H,X) is a nilsystem.

pronormal.gloss: Such that each of its conjugates is conjugate to it already in the subgroup generated by it and its conjugate.

proof.gloss: A sequence of statements consisting of axioms, assumptions, statements already demonstrated in another proof, and statements that logically follow from previous statements in the sequence, and which concludes with a statement that is the object of the proof.
A process for testing the accuracy of an operation performed. Compare prove, transitive verb, 5.

proof by contradiction.gloss: The proof of a statement adduced by deriving a contradiction from the statement's negation.

proof by example.gloss: A logical fallacy consisting of providing one or more examples as a proof of a more general statement.

proof by exhaustion.gloss: The indirect verification or falsification of a statement by the verification or falsification of each of the finite number of cases which arise therefrom.

proof of concept.gloss: A proof of technology or pilot project.

proof of work.gloss: A form of cryptographic proof in which a prover proves to verifiers that a certain amount of a specific computational effort has been expended.

proof system.gloss: A set of axioms and a set of inference rules which are jointly used to deduce tautologies, thereby providing proofs of them.

propagate.gloss: To take effect on all relevant devices in a network.
To cause to take effect on all relevant devices in a network.

propelinear.gloss: A code C is propelinear if, for every codeword x in C, there exists a coordinate permutation Pₓ such that x + Pₓ (C) = C and, for any codewords x, y, z, and c in C, if x + Pₓ(y) = z, then P_z(c) is the composition of the permutations Pₓ and P_y(c).

proper.gloss: Suitable. Such that the preimage of every compact set is compact.
Suitable. Continuous, mapping closed sets to closed sets, and such that the preimage of every point is compact.
Suitable. Separated, of finite type, and universally closed.
Suitable. Such that unique morphism from the variety to k is proper (as above).
qualifiers: of a variety over a field k

proper.gloss: Suitable. Such that every closed ball is compact.
Possessed, related. Being strictly part of some other thing (not necessarily explicitly mentioned, but of definitional importance), and not being the thing itself.
Possessed, related. Eigen-; designating a function or value which is an eigenfunction or eigenvalue.
Accurate, strictly applied. Not being a set.

proper class.gloss: A class which is not a set.

proper divisor.gloss: A divisor of a number which is not the number itself.

proper inclusion.gloss: The state of being a proper subset; a subset relation in which a set A is a subset of a set B but A is not equal to B.

proper subset.gloss: a set that is a subset of the set, but not equal to it.

properly included.gloss: Being a proper subset; having the property that every element of a set A is also an element of a set B, and A is not equal to B.

properness.gloss: The state or condition of being proper (of a proper fraction, proper subset, etc.).

property.gloss: An editable or read-only parameter associated with an application, component or class; especially (object-oriented programming) one that encapsulates an underlying variable.

property bag.gloss: A collection of properties and their values, similar to an associative array or hash table.

proplet.gloss: A basic element of a proposition.

proportion.gloss: A statement of equality between two ratios.
The "rule of three", in which three terms are given to find a fourth.

proportional.gloss: At a constant ratio (to). Two magnitudes (numbers) are said to be proportional if the second varies in a direct relation arithmetically to the first. Symbol: ∝.

proposition.gloss: The content of an assertion that may be taken as being true or false and is considered abstractly without reference to the linguistic sentence that constitutes the assertion; (Aristotelian logic) a predicate of a subject that is denied or affirmed and is connected by a copula.
An assertion so formulated that it can be considered true or false.
An assertion which is provably true, but not important enough to be called a theorem.

propositional constant.gloss: One of a set of letters or symbols which are assigned fixed truth values independently of any interpretation or valuation, and each of which qualifies as a prime formula of their language.

propositional function.gloss: An expression containing algebraic symbols that serve to represent words or other elements of a sentence or proposition

propositional logic.gloss: A formal deductive system in which formulae representing propositions can be formed by combining atomic propositions using logical connectives.

propositional variable.gloss: A variable that can either be true or false.

propositionalization.gloss: The transformation of a relational dataset into a propositional one.

proregular.gloss: Having the property that the inverse systems of the Koszul cohomology modules satisfy the Inverse limit#Mittag-Leffler condition.)

prosleptic.gloss: Being or involving a particular kind of proposition in a syllogism. (See Wikipedia article.)

prospectivity.gloss: A projective relationship between a line and itself by projecting onto an intersecting line from a point on another line that intersects at the same point, and then back on to the first line from a different point on the first intersecting line.

prosyllogism.gloss: A syllogism that is preliminary or logically essential to another syllogism.
The conclusion of such a syllogism, which becomes a premise of the following syllogism.

protasis.gloss: A clause that expresses a contingent element in a conditional sentence.

protected.gloss: Having the protected access modifier, indicating that a program element is accessible to subclasses but not to the program in general.

protected mode.gloss: An operational mode of x86-compatible CPUs, in which software can use features such as virtual memory, paging, and safe multitasking.

protection.gloss: An instance of a security token associated with a resource (such as a file).

protestware.gloss: Software subverted to serve the ends of a political protest, for example by deleting files or displaying propaganda messages.

proteus effect.gloss: A phenomenon in which the behavior of an individual, within virtual worlds, is changed by the characteristics of their avatar.

proth number.gloss: Any number of the form k·2ⁿ + 1, where k is odd, n is a positive integer, and 2ⁿ > k.

proth prime.gloss: A Proth number that is prime.

protoadditive.gloss: Having the property that the result when applied to x + y is less than or equal to the sum of the result when applied to x plus the result when applied to y, for all values x and y in the domain.

protocol.gloss: A set of formal rules describing how to transmit or exchange data, especially across a network.

protocol stack.gloss: Synonym of stack (“an implementation of a protocol suite (a set of protocols forming a layered architecture)”).

protothetic.gloss: A particular theory of the relationships between propositions

protothread.gloss: A lightweight stackless thread used in concurrent programming.

prototile.gloss: Any of the minimal set of non-congruent shapes from which a larger set of shapes, some of which may be congruent, can be produced.

prototrace.gloss: A trace containing temporary placeholder variables.

prototype.gloss: A declaration of a function that specifies the name, return type, and parameters, but none of the body or actual code.

prototype extension.gloss: An extension, enrichment or continuation of a declaration of a function.

prototype pattern.gloss: A creational design pattern that determines the type of objects to create by a prototypical instance, which is cloned to produce new objects.

prototype-based.gloss: making inheritance possible by cloning objects instead of instantiating them from classes

prototype-based language.gloss: A programming language in which behaviour reuse (or inheritance) is performed via cloning existing objects that serve as prototypes.

prototype-based programming.gloss: A programming style, where inheritance is achieved by using existing objects by means of delegation that act as prototypes.

prototype-based scripting language.gloss: A programming language that uses prototypes to allow objects to inherit properties and methods from other objects.

prototype-oriented.gloss: Of or pertaining to a style of object-oriented programming that uses existing objects as prototypes to reuse behavior.

prototype-oriented programming.gloss: A programming paradigm that encapsulates states and operations inside "prototypes" to design applications and computer programs.

provector.gloss: A contravariant operator formed by substituting signs of partial differentiation for the facients of a quantic.

provenance.gloss: The copy history of a piece of data, or the intermediate pieces of data used to compute a final data element, as in a database record or web site (data provenance).
The execution history of computer processes which were used to compute a final piece of data (process provenance).

provision.gloss: To supply (a user) with an account, resources, etc. so that they can use a system; to install the necessary software on a bare-bones system so it can be used for a specific purpose.

provisioner.gloss: One who or that which provisions (sets up an account, resources, etc.).

provisioning.gloss: The installation of software on a system, especially when automated.

proxy.gloss: An interface for a service, especially for one that is remote, resource-intensive, or otherwise difficult to use directly.
To function as a server for a client device, but pass on the requests to another server for service.

proxy pattern.gloss: A structural design pattern that is implemented as a class functioning as an interface for a network connection, a large object in memory, a file, or some other resource that is expensive or impossible to duplicate.

proxy server.gloss: A hardware server that acts as an intermediary between a user and another server, usually on the Internet.

proxyless.gloss: Without the use of a proxy.

prune.gloss: To remove unnecessary branches from a tree data structure.

pruning.gloss: A method of enumeration that allows the cutting out of parts of a decision tree.

prvalue.gloss: An rvalue that is not an xvalue.

pseudo-3d.gloss: The use of 2D sprites with effects such as perspective, parallax and shading to simulate three dimensions.
Rendered with 2D sprites using effects such as perspective, parallax and shading to simulate three dimensions.

pseudo-anosov.gloss: Pertaining to the generalization of Anosov diffeomorphism of the torus introduced by William Thurston.

pseudo-complement.gloss: The relative pseudo-complement of a given element (of a Heyting algebra) with respect to the least element — the "zero" of that algebra.

pseudo-edge.gloss: The connection between vertices in a pseudo-Hamiltonian-connected graph.

pseudo-english.gloss: A structured artificial language that uses English words in order to be more user friendly for English speakers.

pseudo-localization.gloss: The practice of using fake localization strings during development, intended to test the software's capability of handling multilingual text.

pseudo-polynomial time.gloss: A time algorithm whose running time is a polynomial in the numeric value of the input, but not necessarily in the length of the input.

pseudo-rhombicuboctahedron.gloss: A convex polyhedron that resembles the rhombicuboctahedron but has a different arrangement of faces and lower symmetry. It is specifically the elongated square gyrobicupola, a Johnson solid.

pseudo-type.gloss: A data type that can be only used in certain places, for example as the argument to a function.

pseudoalgorithm.gloss: A description of a process that resembles, but is not in fact, an algorithm, as for example by being written in vague pseudocode.

pseudoaligner.gloss: A tool that rapidly assigns sequencing reads to transcripts (or genes) without performing base-by-base alignment.

pseudoanalytical.gloss: Relying on simplifying assumptions in order to create a less complex alternative to a full analytical approach.

pseudoangle.gloss: The equivalent of an angle (or solid angle) in a non-Euclidean space

pseudoapproximation.gloss: An approximation where the error of approximation is greater than ε because calculation of a true approximation is not feasible.

pseudoblock.gloss: A construct that resembles a block of source code but is not a true block.

pseudocircle.gloss: The finite topological space X consisting of four distinct points { a, b, c, d } with the non-Hausdorff topology a,b,c,d,a,b,c,a,b,d,a,b,a,b,∅.

pseudoclass.gloss: A construct in code that behaves like a class but is not a true class.

pseudocode.gloss: A description of a computer programming algorithm that uses the structural conventions of programming languages but omits detailed subroutines or language-specific syntax.
Any format or language that resembles a programming language but is not.

pseudocodeword.gloss: The result obtained when a decoder fails to converge on a codeword, but instead converges on some other code structure.

pseudocoding.gloss: The expression of an algorithm in pseudocode.

pseudocollarable.gloss: Such that there exists a neighborhood that is homeomorphic to a product, but this homeomorphism may not preserve all the desired structures or conditions that a true collar neighborhood would.

pseudocolouring.gloss: The assignment of arbitrary colours to the grey levels of a monochrome image; used especially in thermography

pseudocolumn.gloss: A column that yields a value when selected, but is not an actual column of the table.

pseudocomplex.gloss: Relating to the square root of ±1

pseudoconcave.gloss: (said of a function) differentiable and decreasing in any direction where it has a negative directional derivative.

pseudoconformal.gloss: That appears to conform, but in practice does not.

pseudoconsciousness.gloss: A state or condition that is not consciousness but seemingly or nearly approaches it or simulates it.

pseudocontractive.gloss: Satisfying the equation ||Tx - Ty|| <= ||x - y|| - α * ||x - y||² where T is the mapping that is pseudocontractive, x and y are points in the metric space, ||.|| denotes the norm in the metric space, and α is a constant.

pseudoconvex.gloss: Of a function: differentiable and increasing in any direction where it has a positive directional derivative.

pseudocorrelation.gloss: An approximation to a cross-correlation made using Monte Carlo methods

pseudocount.gloss: A number added to a number of observations so as to change a generated probability to one obtained by prior knowledge.

pseudocubic.gloss: describing a rhombohedral structure that is almost cubic

pseudodata.gloss: Data that is artificially generated in order to test a program; test data.

pseudodevice.gloss: An entry in a file system that acts like a physical device without having the corresponding hardware.

pseudodifferential.gloss: Describing an extension to differential calculus that deals with Fourier transforms and similar structures.

pseudodifferential operator.gloss: An extension of the differential operator, used in the theory of partial differential equations and quantum field theory.

pseudodigraph.gloss: A graph that resembles a directed graph but violates one of the normal rules, as for example by including a directed loop.

pseudodimension.gloss: The largest cardinality (or infinite) of a set of points (in a function class) that can be shattered.

pseudodirectory.gloss: A virtual directory entry that does not represent a directory on the underlying file system on disk, instead being automatically generated to represent some other objects in the form of files (for example '/proc' in Linux).

pseudodistance.gloss: A pseudometric having some characteristics of distance

pseudodivision.gloss: Any of several methods of division that employ addition and shifting of digits.

pseudoeffective.gloss: Having a nonnegative intersection product with every ample divisor and numerically eventually free if the intersection product with every positive divisor is non-negative.

pseudoelement.gloss: An object in code that behaves like an HTML element but is not a true element.

pseudofile.gloss: A file that does not represent a file on the underlying file system on disk, but instead is automatically generated to represent some other object in the form of a file (for example '/proc/cpuinfo' in Linux).

pseudofinite.gloss: Of a field: both quasi-finite (perfect with a unique extension of every positive degree) and pseudo algebraically closed (every absolutely irreducible variety over the field has a point defined over the field).

pseudoforest.gloss: an undirected graph in which every connected component has at most one cycle
