pseudofunctor.gloss: A mapping between categories that is just like a functor except that f(x∘y)=f(x)∘f(y) and f(1)=1 do not hold as exact equalities but only up to coherent isomorphisms.

pseudograph.gloss: A graph that may contain loops as well as multiple edges between vertices

pseudographical.gloss: Having the appearance of graphics, though actually text-based.

pseudographics.gloss: An approximation of graphics achieved through the use of text characters.

pseudogroup.gloss: An algebraic structure having elements that are homeomorphisms between subsets of a space

pseudohandle.gloss: A special value that can be treated as a handle (e.g. to identify a process) but is not a true handle.

pseudohermitian.gloss: Having the Hermitian properties except that the eigenvalues may be complex and the eigenvectors need not be orthogonal.

pseudoideal.gloss: The set of all lower bounds of the set of all upper bounds of a subset of a partially ordered set

pseudoinstruction.gloss: A command that resembles, but is not in fact, a machine instruction, such as a special directive or a command that is mapped to a sequence of real instructions.

pseudointerface.gloss: A software component that acts like a network interface but is not a true interface.

pseudointersection.gloss: A set for which the number of elements that are not in the intersection (of two infinite sets) is finite.

pseudoinverse.gloss: Any of several structures, similar to inverses, related to complex matrices

pseudoinversion.gloss: An operation that approximates an inversion; A reversal of the ends while maintaining a constant central region.

pseudoisotropic.gloss: That is isotropic in the three physical dimensions but not in some higher dimension

pseudolanguage.gloss: A means of describing an algorithm in human terms, without the use of a true programming language.

pseudolikelihood.gloss: An approximation to the joint probability distribution of a collection of random variables.

pseudoline.gloss: A curve that shares certain topological properties with a line.

pseudolocalization.gloss: The testing of software for internationalization compliance using modified versions of the original text (with the use of foreign script etc.) rather than genuine translations.

pseudolongitudinal.gloss: Not actually longitudinal, but treated that way.

pseudomeasure.gloss: A distribution that can be extended to a continuous functional.

pseudomedian.gloss: A measure of centrality for data sets and populations, which agrees with the median where the data are symmetric.

pseudometric.gloss: Describing a generalization of a metric space in which the distance between two distinct points can be zero.

pseudomoment.gloss: A numerical entity that combines the properties of moments and metrics

pseudomonad.gloss: A weak generalization of a monad on a Gray-category or 2-category (or more generally a weak 2-category) 𝒞 consists of a 2-functor (in particular, if it is a functor on a weak 2-category, it is a pseudo-functor) T:𝒞→𝒞 equipped with pseudonatural transformations μ:T²→T and η:Id→T which satisfy the monad laws up to coherent invertible modifications.

pseudomonoid.gloss: A structure similar to a monoid that supports associativity and an identity element, but does not include all the constraints that are required to qualify as a monoid.

pseudomultiplication.gloss: Any of several methods of multiplication that employ addition and shifting of digits

pseudonamespace.gloss: A false namespace achieved by other means.

pseudonumerical.gloss: Being a factor-object of an algebraically numerical object.

pseudonymization.gloss: The replacement of all data (in a database etc) that identifies a person with an artificial identifier or pseudonym.

pseudonymize.gloss: To depersonalize or anonymize (data); a procedure by which the most identifying fields within a data record are replaced by one or more artificial identifiers, or pseudonyms.

pseudoparallelism.gloss: The execution of parallel processes on a unicore system.

pseudoperfect.gloss: Of a number, having proper divisors, some or all of which sum to the number itself.

pseudoperiod.gloss: A solution function that is not technically periodic, but nevertheless displays repetitive behavior.

pseudopolynomial.gloss: A function where f(n+k) ≡ f(n) (mod k) for all integers n ≥ 0, k ≥ 1.

pseudopopulation.gloss: A subset of a population used in simulations

pseudoprime.gloss: An integer that possesses at least one characteristic of a prime number without actually being prime. The characteristic is typically chosen to make such "false primes" very rare.
A Fermat pseudoprime; a composite integer n satisfying bⁿ⁻¹≡1(mod n) for some integer b such that b > 1.

pseudoproper.gloss: Describing any system that has some proper characteristics.

pseudoprotocol.gloss: Something that can be accessed in the manner of a protocol but is not in fact a protocol.

pseudoquotient.gloss: A value in pseudodivision more or less corresponding to the quotient in normal division.

pseudoradical.gloss: The intersection of the set of nonzero prime ideals of a ring.

pseudorational.gloss: Able to be expressed as the convolution ratio of distributions with compact support.

pseudoreflection.gloss: An invertible linear transformation of a finite-dimensional vector space such that it is not the identity transformation, has a finite (multiplicative) order, and fixes a hyperplane.

pseudoreflexive.gloss: Inducing a topological isomorphism between the domain and its image.

pseudorelational.gloss: Having certain elements of a relational database.

pseudoremainder.gloss: A value in pseudodivision more or less corresponding to the remainder in normal division.

pseudoreplicate.gloss: Any of a group of interdependent data that are mistakenly treated as independent.

pseudoreplication.gloss: The exaggeration of the statistical significance of a set of measurements resulting from treating the data as independent observations when they are in fact interdependent.

pseudorepresentation.gloss: Given a group G and a commutative ring R, a tuple of maps (a,d,x), where a,d:G→R and x:GxG→R, are a pseudorepresentation if they satisfy the relations one would expect if a(g) and d(g) were the diagonal entries of a two dimensional representation |a(g)b(g)|\|c(g)d(g)| and if x was given by x(g,g^′)=b(g)c(g^′).

pseudoresidual.gloss: The difference between the observed value and the median.

pseudorhombic.gloss: describing a structure that is almost rhombohedral

pseudoring.gloss: Any of various variants of a ring.

pseudoroot.gloss: A value that appears to be a root of a polynomial equation but that is not actually a root, such as one obtained when factors cancel out in the process of solving the equation.

pseudoselector.gloss: A kind of selector that identifies something not explicitly labelled in the document markup.

pseudosequence.gloss: An apparent sequence used as a key in data compression

pseudospectral.gloss: Describing a class of numerical analysis methods related to spectral methods

pseudospectrum.gloss: A set containing the spectrum of an operator and the numbers that are "almost" eigenvalues.

pseudosphere.gloss: A surface generated by rotating a tractrix about its asymptote; a tractricoid
Any of various surfaces with constant negative Gaussian curvature.

pseudospinor.gloss: A pseudospin analog of a spinor.

pseudospoofing.gloss: The use of a Sybil attack.

pseudostate.gloss: An entity that resembles, but is not in fact, a state in a state machine or similar.

pseudostatement.gloss: A construct resembling a statement that is not a true statement.

pseudosyllogism.gloss: A false syllogism, one that is not logically coherent.

pseudotensor.gloss: A quantity that transforms like a tensor under a proper rotation but gains an additional change of sign under an improper rotation.

pseudoterminal.gloss: A pair of pseudodevices that can communicate with each other without the hardware that a true device would require.

pseudotriangle.gloss: Any subset of a plane that lies between any three mutually tangent convex sets

pseudotriangulation.gloss: The partitioning of the plane into pseudotriangles

pseudotype.gloss: Something resembling, or having certain characteristics of, a data type.

pseudoumbilical.gloss: Umbilical in the direction of the mean curvature vector field everywhere.

pseudovalue.gloss: Something that resembles a value but is not a true value or does not really belong to the set of data being studied.

pseudovariable.gloss: A named value that acts like a variable but is not a true variable.

pseudovariety.gloss: A class of algebras of a given signature, closed under the taking of homomorphic images, subalgebras and finitary direct products.

pseudovector.gloss: A quantity that transforms like a vector under a proper rotation but gains an additional change of sign under an improper rotation

pseudowire.gloss: An emulation of a point-to-point connection over a packet-switching network.

psi function.gloss: A function of a complex variable obtained by differentiating the logarithm of a gamma function; the digamma function

pspo.gloss: Initialism of professional scrum product owner.

psu.gloss: Initialism of primary sampling unit, a sampling unit in the first stage of a polyetapic sampling.

psvm.gloss: Abbreviation of public static void main(String[] args), the declaration for the entry-point method of a Java program.

ptal.gloss: Acronym of please take a look: please review and comment on the proposed change to software source code.

ptb.gloss: Initialism of public test build, public test branch.
Initialism of packet too big, an IPv6 error message.

pua.gloss: Initialism of Private Use Area (the ranges of Unicode code points reserved for private use).

public key.gloss: One of the two keys used in asymmetric cryptography, which is published to others.

public key certificate.gloss: A certificate that uses a digital signature to bind together a public key with an identity — used to verify that a public key belongs to a particular person.

publish.gloss: To make (information such as an event) available to components that wish to be notified (subscribers).

publisher.gloss: A system or component that allows other components (subscribers) to receive notifications of something, such as an event.

puck.gloss: A pointing device with a crosshair.

puffer.gloss: A finite pattern that moves like a spaceship but leaves a trail of debris.

pull.gloss: To retrieve source code or other material from a source control repository.

pull request.gloss: A request to a repository maintainer to pull in and merge a proposed source code or other change.

pull-down.gloss: A dynamic menu; a list of options in a computer application which appears below a heading when it is selected, and remains only as long as the user needs it.
The conversion of video footage to a higher frame rate by duplicating certain frames.

pullback.gloss: The limit of a cospan: a Cartesian square or “pullback square”.

Within a Cartesian square (which has a pair of divergent morphisms and a pair of convergent morphisms) the divergent morphism which is directly opposite to a given one of the convergent morphisms, said to be “along” the convergent morphism which is between that pair of opposite morphisms. (The pullback is said to be “of” the given morphism.)

pump.gloss: To pass (messages) into a program so that it can obey them.

pumping lemma.gloss: A lemma which states that for a language to be a member of a language class any sufficiently long string in the language contains a section that can be removed or repeated any number of times with the resulting string remaining in the language, used to determine if a particular language is in a given language class (e.g. not regular).

pumpking.gloss: A Perl user working on shared source code who has been temporarily designated as the only person who is allowed to make changes.

punch card.gloss: A card that can have holes or notches cut in it, especially one for storing data, that can be sorted according to combinations of holes present or absent. Such a card, the size of a US dollar bill and having 80 columns of 12 rows, used in early mainframe computers.

punch out.gloss: To extract data from a computer by the use of a keyboard.

punched card.gloss: A punch card (especially one that has had holes punched in it).

punched tape.gloss: Synonym of paper tape (“an early sequential digital storage medium originally used with teletype machines, consisting of a long roll of paper, each character being encoded as a pattern of punched holes”).

punctual.gloss: Existing as a point or series of points.

punctured interval.gloss: A neighborhood of a point in a space with an order, minus the point itself.

punctured neighborhood.gloss: A neighborhood of a point, minus the point itself.

pup.gloss: Acronym of potentially unwanted program, software that most computer users do not want on their computers, such as adware.

puppetize.gloss: To configure (a system) using the Puppet software configuration management tool.

pure name.gloss: A name that reveals no usable information about the entity it identifies.

purely imaginary.gloss: Of a number, having real part equal to zero.

pursuit curve.gloss: A geometrical model which simulates the path taken by a pursuer in the course of its pursuit.

push.gloss: To add (a data item) to the top of a stack.
To publish (an update, etc.) by transmitting it to other computers.
The addition of a data item to the top of a stack.

push time.gloss: The time when a remote server sends an unsolicited update.

push-scrolling.gloss: A form of scrolling that is triggered whenever the user's text cursor, player character, etc. approaches the border of the screen, so as to keep it more or less central.

pushalong.gloss: A pattern that attaches to the front of a spaceship, moving along with it.

pushdown.gloss: Describing a stack in which items are removed in a LIFO manner from the end at which they were added.
The relegation of the transformation or processing of data to the originating datasource.

pushdown automaton.gloss: An automaton with finitely many states that can also use one unbounded stack of memory; the automaton may only push, pop, or read the top of the stack. Abbreviation: PDA.

pushforward.gloss: The differential of a smooth map between smooth manifolds.

pushout.gloss: The colimit of a pair of morphisms which share the same domain.

pwd.gloss: Unix command to print the working directory

pyramid.gloss: A solid with triangular lateral faces and a polygonal (often square or rectangular) base.

pyramid of doom.gloss: The presence of many levels of nested indentation in source code, making it difficult for a person to read.

pyramidal number.gloss: A number that represents the number of items in a pyramid having a given number of sides and layers

pyritohedral.gloss: Having the shape of a pyritohedron.

pyritohedron.gloss: An irregular dodecahedron, the faces of which are identical but irregular pentagons.

pythagorean field.gloss: A field in which every sum of two squares is a square.

pythagorean quadruple.gloss: A set of four positive integers a, b, c, and d, for which a²+b²+c²=d²

pythagorean triangle.gloss: A triangle whose sides form a Pythagorean triple, such as 3, 4, 5.

pythagorean trigonometric identity.gloss: The equality sin (x)²+ cos (x)²=1, holding for all real and complex x, equivalent to the application of the Pythagorean theorem to the unit circle.

pythagorean triple.gloss: A set of three positive integers a, b and c, for which a²+b²=c².

pythonesque.gloss: Typical of, or suited to, the Python programming language.

pythonic.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of Pythonic (“using the idioms of the Python programming language”).
Using the idioms of the Python programming language.

pythonist.gloss: A programmer who uses the Python programming language.

q-analog.gloss: A generalization of a theorem, identity or expression that involves a new parameter q that returns the original theorem, identity or expression in the limit as q → 1. They have applications in the study of fractals and the entropy of chaotic dynamical systems.

q-learning.gloss: A model-free reinforcement learning algorithm to learn a policy telling an agent what action to take under what circumstances.

q.e.d..gloss: Initialism of quod erat demonstrandum (“what was to be proved; what was to be demonstrated”): placed at the end of a mathematical proof to show that the theorem under discussion is proved.

qbic.gloss: Acronym of query by image content.

qhd.gloss: Initialism of quarter high definition (“960x540 pixels”).

qic.gloss: Initialism of quarter-inch cartridge: a tape storage format having a dual spooled cartridge with a quarter-inch wide tape.

qr decomposition.gloss: A decomposition of a matrix into a product of a unitary matrix (orthogonal matrix) and an upper-triangular matrix.

qrng.gloss: Abbreviation of quantum random number generator.

quadball.gloss: A rounded cube used to approximate a sphere.

quadbit.gloss: Four bits (binary digits), half a byte; a nibble.

quadkey.gloss: A key into a quadtree data structure.

quadlet.gloss: A word consisting of four bytes.

quadrable.gloss: Of a plane figure, for which quadrature is possible.

quadragesimal.gloss: Of, related to, or based on the number forty.

quadral.gloss: A set of points with all the combinatorial properties of a quadric (a quadric being the set of points of PG(n, q) whose coordinates satisfy a quadratic equation).
Of or relating to quadral polynomials.

quadrangle.gloss: Synonym of quadrilateral (“a polygon with four sides”).

quadrangulation.gloss: A graph embedded in a surface such that every face is a quadrangle.

quadrant.gloss: One of the four regions of the Cartesian plane bounded by the x-axis and y-axis.
One fourth of a circle or disc; a sector with an angle of 90°.

quadrantal.gloss: Of or relating to a quadrant, or included in the fourth part of a circle.

quadrate.gloss: A plane surface with four equal sides and four right angles; a square; hence, figuratively, anything having the outline of a square.

quadratic.gloss: Of a polynomial, equation or function, second-degree: involving the second power (square) of a variable but no higher powers, as ax²+bx+c.
A quadratic polynomial, function or equation.

quadratic equation.gloss: A polynomial equation of the second degree; an equation that can be rearranged in standard form as ax²+bx+c=0, where x is an unknown value, a, b, and c are known numbers, and where a does not equal zero.

quadratic form.gloss: A homogeneous polynomial of degree 2 in a given number of variables.
A scalar quantity of the form εᵀΛε, where ε is a vector of n random variables, and Λ is an n-dimensional symmetric matrix.

quadratic formula.gloss: The formula x=(-b±√(b²-4ac))/(2a) for finding roots of the quadratic equation.

quadratic function.gloss: Any function whose value is the solution of a quadratic polynomial

quadratic integer.gloss: A number (real or complex) which is a solution to an equation of the form x²+Bx+C=0 for some integers B and C. For example 42, or 2+3i, or 1+√(-3)/2.

quadratic mean.gloss: A type of average, calculated as the square root of the mean of the squares, i.e. Q=√x_1²+x_2²+...+x_n²/n.

quadratic reciprocity.gloss: The mathematical theorem which states that, for given odd prime numbers p and q, the question of whether p is a square modulo q is equivalent to the question of whether q is a square modulo p.

quadratic residue.gloss: For a given positive integer n, any integer that is congruent to some square m² modulo n.

quadratic surd.gloss: An irrational number that is the solution of a quadratic equation of the form ax²+bx+c=0, where a, b, and c are integers and a ≠ 0.

quadratic time.gloss: A time algorithm in which given an input of size n, the number of steps required to complete a task is the square of n.

quadratization.gloss: An approximation of a system obtained by quadratizing it.

quadratize.gloss: To approximate a system with a quadratic system.

quadratrix.gloss: A curve having ordinates which are a measure of the area (or quadrature) of another curve.

quadrature.gloss: The act or process of constructing a square that has the same area as a given plane figure, or of computing that area.
The calculation of a definite integral by numerical means.
The act or process of solving an indefinite integral by symbolic means.

quadrature of the circle.gloss: The problem, proposed by ancient Greek geometers, of using a finite ruler-and-compass construction to make a square with the same area as a given circle.

quadravigesimal.gloss: A number system with base twenty-four, using the digits 0–9 and A–N (or Greek α-ω without numerals).
A number expressed in the quadravigesimal system.

quadric.gloss: A surface or curve whose shape is defined in terms of a quadratic equation.
Of or relating to the second degree; quadratic.

quadrify.gloss: To convert into one or more quadrilaterals.

quadrilinear.gloss: Having, or bounded by, four lines.

quadrille.gloss: A square tiling of the plane.

quadrinomial.gloss: An expression consisting of four terms.

quadriquadric.gloss: A curve that is the complete intersection of two quadric surfaces.

quadrisecant.gloss: A line that passes through four points of the curve.

quadrisector.gloss: A line or curve that quadrisects something.

quadrivalent.gloss: Having all of its vertices of degree four.

quadruple-click.gloss: The action of pushing the button on a mouse four times in quick succession.
To push the button on a mouse four times in quick succession.

quadtree.gloss: A treelike data structure each of whose nodes has up to four children, most often used to partition a two-dimensional space by recursively subdividing it.

quadword.gloss: A numerical value of four times the magnitude of a word, typically used in the same contexts as the fossilized 16-bit sense of "word" and thus 64 bits.

quaject.gloss: An object-like data structure containing both data and code (or pointers to code), typically used as an abstraction to manage self-modifying code.

qualifier.gloss: A marker that qualifies or modifies another code element.

qualitative research.gloss: A type of research that aims to gather and analyse non-numerical (descriptive) data in order to gain an understanding of individuals' social reality, including understanding their attitudes, beliefs, and motivation.

quality of life.gloss: Features or improvements designed to make software easier to use without changing the main functionality.

quandle.gloss: A rack, scriptstyle Q,, such that scriptstyle ∀a;∈;Q a triangleright a=a or equivalently a triangleleft a=a.

quantale.gloss: A kind of partially ordered algebraic structure that generalizes locales (point free topologies) as well as various multiplicative lattices of ideals from ring theory and functional analysis.

quantaloid.gloss: A category enriched over the category Sup of suplattices.

quantic.gloss: A homogeneous polynomial in two or more variables.

quantification.gloss: A limitation that is imposed on the variables of a proposition.

quantificational logic.gloss: The logic of sentences involving quantifiers, predicates, and names; the branch of logic that investigates the properties that arguments, sentences, and sets of sentences have in virtue of their quantificational structure.

quantifier.gloss: An operator, such as the universal quantifier (written as ∀) or the existential quantifier (∃), used in predicate calculus to indicate the degree that predicate is true for a specified set.
A symbol or symbols in a regular expression indicating the number of characters to be matched.

quantify.gloss: To relate a statement (called a predicate) to a given set using a quantifier—either for all (denoted ∀) or there exists (denoted ∃).

quantile.gloss: One of the class of values of a variate which divides the members of a batch or sample into equal-sized subgroups of adjacent values or a probability distribution into distributions of equal probability.

quantion.gloss: A form of quaternion used to explain the electroweak theory on curved spacetime.

quantitative research.gloss: A type of research that aims to gather and analyze numerical data in order to broadly and through quantification promote the objective empirical investigation of observable phenomena.

quantity.gloss: Indicates that the entire preceding expression is henceforth considered a single object.

quantization.gloss: The process of approximating a continuous signal by a set of discrete symbols or integer values

quantize.gloss: To associate a given set of numbers with a set of numeric values in another encoding or numerical system (e.g. in a discrete mathematics).

quantoid.gloss: The left hand side of a linear differential equation whose right hand side is zero.

quantum.gloss: The amount of time allocated for a thread to perform its work in a multithreaded environment.
A definite portion of a manifoldness, limited by a mark or by a boundary.
Involving quanta, quantum mechanics or other aspects of quantum physics. Relating to a quantum computer.

quantum advantage.gloss: The ability of a quantum algorithm to solve a computational problem in a greatly reduced time period, as compared to using a conventional computer.

quantum bogosort.gloss: A hypothetical sorting algorithm which generates a random permutation of its input (like in bogosort) using a quantum source of entropy, checks if the list is sorted, and, if it is not, destroys the universe. Assuming that the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics is true, this algorithm will result in at least one surviving universe where the input was successfully sorted in O(n) time (thus making it faster than quicksort).

quantum computing.gloss: The use of quantum mechanical phenomena to transcend classical time complexity limitations in computing.

quantum cryptography.gloss: The science of exploiting quantum mechanical properties to perform cryptographic tasks.

quantum logic.gloss: A form of non-classical logic which has been abstracted out of quantum mechanics.
A set of events that is closed under a countable disjunction of countably many mutually exclusive events.ᵂᴾ

quarantine.gloss: An isolation of one program, drive, computer, etc. from the rest of a computer network to limit the damage from a bug, computer virus, etc.
The program, drive, computer, etc. thus isolated.

quark.gloss: An integer that uniquely identifies a text string.

quartal.gloss: Of base four; using only four unique digits.

quarter circle.gloss: A quarter of a circle. The shape formed from an arc that is a quarter of the circumference of a circle.

quartic.gloss: Of or relating to the fourth degree.
An algebraic equation or function of the fourth degree.
A curve describing such an equation or function.

quartic function.gloss: Any function of a polynomial whose greatest exponent is 4.

quartile.gloss: Any of the three points that divide an ordered distribution into four parts, each containing a quarter of the population.
Any one of the four groups so divided.

quartimax.gloss: Describing an orthogonal rotation that maximizes the squared loadings for each variable rather than each factor.

quasi-compact.gloss: In which has every open cover has a finite subcover.

quasi-derivative.gloss: A particular generalization of the derivative of a function between two Banach spaces.

quasi-invariant.gloss: Preserving a specified property under transformation.

quasi-projective.gloss: Locally closed with respect to the Zariski topology on projective n-space; isomorphic to such a set.
Comprising an open subscheme of a projective scheme

quasi-transitive.gloss: Such that its vertex set can be partitioned into finitely many sets, so that there exists an automorphism mapping a vertex to another vertex if and only if the two vertices belong to the same set in that partition.

quasi-zero-dimensional.gloss: Refers to a complex topological space that behaves similarly to a zero-dimensional space.

quasiabelian.gloss: Having properties similar to an abelian structure

quasianalytic.gloss: Belonging or relating to a generalization of the class of real analytic functions based upon the fact that, if f is an analytic function on an interval [a,b] ⊂ R, and at some point f and all of its derivatives are zero, then f is identically zero on all of [a,b].

quasibarrelled.gloss: For which every barrelled bornivorous set in the space is a neighbourhood of zero.

quasibialgebra.gloss: A generalization of a bialgebra that allows for a weaker form of coassociativity.

quasibinomial.gloss: Describing a generalisation of binomial distributions

quasicircle.gloss: A Jordan curve in the complex plane that is the image of a circle under a quasiconformal mapping of the plane onto itself.

quasicoherent.gloss: Belonging to a generalization of coherent sheaves, including the locally free sheaves of infinite rank.

quasiconcave.gloss: said of a function, if the inverse image of any set of the form (a,∞) for that function is a convex set.

quasicontinuous.gloss: Having some characteristics of a continuous function, system etc

quasicontinuum.gloss: A system that behaves as a continuum in most but not all respects.

quasiconvex.gloss: said of a function, if the inverse image of any set of the form (-∞,a) for that function is a convex set.

quasicyclic.gloss: Describing a certain type of cyclic group or cyclic code

quasideterminant.gloss: The equivalent of a determinant in matrices that have noncommutative entries

quasidiagonal.gloss: Having an approximate unit consisting of projections which is quasicentral.

quasidisorder.gloss: The condition of an apparently disordered system that has an underlying order.

quasidisordered.gloss: Apparently disordered, but having an underlying order.

quasidistribution.gloss: A quantum state described in terms of phase-space quasiprobability densities.

quasidynamical.gloss: Describing a system that has some characteristics of a dynamical system

quasifield.gloss: An algebraic structure (Q,+,·) where + and · are binary operations on Q, much like a division ring, but with some weaker conditions.

quasigeodesic.gloss: Of a map f: textbf R→Y, having constants K>0 and C>0 such that 1/Kd(x,y)-C<d(f(x),f(y))<Kd(x,y)+C.

quasigroup.gloss: An algebraic structure, resembling a group, whose arithmetic may not be associative

quasiharmonic.gloss: Describing any system that has some harmonic (periodic) characteristics

quasiidentity.gloss: A kind of Horn clause, a generalization of identities.

quasiisometry.gloss: An equivalence relation that is an isometry when viewed at a large scale

quasilattice.gloss: A non-periodic structure that exhibits long-range order without translational symmetry.

quasilocal.gloss: Describing a ring that is not Noetherian

quasimeasure.gloss: A nonnegative increasing semiadditive set function defined on a ring of sets that is continuous above the origin and takes its values in the extended domain of real numbers.

quasimeromorphic.gloss: Describing a mapping that has some characteristics of a meromorphic one

quasimetric.gloss: A structure that satisfies most, but not all, axioms of a metric

quasimode.gloss: A mode that remains activated only through some constant action on the part of the user, such as holding down a certain key on the keyboard.

quasimodular.gloss: Being the holomorphic part of an almost holomorphic modular form.

quasinilpotent.gloss: Of a bounded operator over a Hilbert space, having a spectrum containing only 0.

quasinorm.gloss: A function that has all the properties of a norm except the triangle inequality

quasiperiodic.gloss: Such that an increment of a variable leads to a multiplication by some function.

quasipoisson.gloss: describing a generalisation of a Poisson distribution

quasipositive.gloss: Describing a matrix, all of whose elements are nonnegative except for those on the main diagonal

quasipotential.gloss: A complex function of momentum and energy applied to an individual attractor in a complex system of multiple attractors

quasiquote.gloss: To enclose (a text fragment within source code) in a special markup that allows it to be separately parsed to yield a computed output value.

quasirandom.gloss: Apparently random, but produced by a non-random algorithm (typically from a given "seed")

quasireflexive.gloss: Of a relation ~ on a set S: such that every element that is related to some element is also related to itself, i.e. ∀x,y∈S: x~y ⇒ x~x ∧ y~y.
Of a Banach space X: such that the quotient X ′′ / J(X) has finite dimension d. (It is then said to be "quasireflexive of order d".)

quasiregular.gloss: That is semiregular with regular faces of precisely two types that alternate around each vertex.
Such that 1 − r is a unit (has a multiplicative inverse).
qualifiers: of an element r of a ring

quasiregular.gloss: Having certain properties in common with holomorphic functions of a single complex variable.
qualifiers: of a mapping from a multi-dimensional space or manifold to an equivalent space

quasiregular.gloss: That is the result of a required adjustment of an induced representation that would, unadjusted, give rise to (only) a quasi-invariant measure.

quasiregular polyhedron.gloss: A uniform polyhedron with two types of faces that alternate around each vertex.

quasireversibility.gloss: A property of some queues, differing from reversibility in that a stronger condition is imposed on arrival rates and a weaker condition is applied on probability fluxes.

quasiseparable.gloss: That becomes disconnected when a suitable subgraph is removed

quasisimple.gloss: Being a perfect central extension of a simple group S.

quasisplit.gloss: Describing a polynomial or group etc that has some characteristics of a split system.

quasisymmetry.gloss: A mapping that preserves shape but allows size to change in a well-defined manner.

quasithin.gloss: Of a group: being a finite simple group that resembles a group of Lie type of rank at most 2 over a field of characteristic 2.

quasitopological.gloss: Semitopological, and such that the function mapping elements to their inverses is also continuous.

quasitoric.gloss: Describing a smooth 2n-dimensional manifold that admits a smooth, locally standard action of an n-dimensional torus, with orbit space an n-dimensional simple convex polytope.

quasitrivial.gloss: Trivial in a restricted sense or to some limited extent.

quasiuniform.gloss: Somewhat uniform; partially uniform. Having some but not all of the characteristics of a uniform structure.

quasivariety.gloss: Any of a class of algebraic structures generalizing the notion of variety by allowing equational conditions on the axioms defining the class.

quater-imaginary.gloss: Of or relating to a nonstandard numeral system using the imaginary number 2i (= √–4) as its base.

quaternion.gloss: A type of four-dimensional hypercomplex number consisting of a real part and three imaginary parts (real multiples of distinct, independent square roots of −1 denoted by i, j and k); commonly used in vector mathematics and as an alternative to matrix algebra in calculating the rotation of three-dimensional objects.

quaternion algebra.gloss: A particular kind of algebra, generalizing the classical quaternions: a four-dimensional central simple algebra over a field.

quaternionic.gloss: Of or pertaining to a quaternion

quebibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2¹⁰⁰ (1024¹⁰, 1,267,650,600,228,229,401,496,703,205,376) bytes or 2¹⁰ (1024) robibytes, as opposed to a quettabyte.

quefrency.gloss: The inverse of the distance between successive lines in a Fourier transform, measured in seconds.

query.gloss: A set of instructions passed to a database.
To pass a set of instructions to a database to retrieve information from it.

query language.gloss: Any of several generalized computer languages in which users may extract data from selected records in a database.

query plan.gloss: The sequence of steps used to execute a given query in a SQL-based database.

query processing.gloss: Processing of a specific set of instructions for extracting particular data.
Processing to extract data from a database and present it for use.

quesitive.gloss: Of or relating to an unknown quantity.

quettabit.gloss: One nonillion (10³⁰) bits. SI symbol: Qb.

quettabyte.gloss: One nonillion (10³⁰) bytes. SI symbol: QB.

queue.gloss: A data structure in which objects are added to one end, called the tail, and removed from the other, called the head (in the case of a FIFO queue). The term can also refer to a LIFO queue or stack where these ends coincide.
To add to a queue data structure.

queue up.gloss: To enqueue (something): to add (it) to a queue.

queueing theory.gloss: The study of the behaviour of queues, and of stochastic processes on which they are modelled.

queuer.gloss: A process, etc. that places data items on a queue.

queuing.gloss: The act of placing something in a queue.

qugate.gloss: The kind of logic gate used in quantum computing.

quiche-eater.gloss: In computer programming circles, a person far removed from practice and concerned only with academic matters, unwilling to "get their hands dirty".

quickselect.gloss: A sorting algorithm related to quicksort, but with limited recursion.

quicksort.gloss: A sorting algorithm that operates by recursively partitioning the items to be sorted into two sets.
To sort with such an algorithm.

quickstart.gloss: A guide or manual intended to get a user rapidly acquainted with a program or system.

quiesce.gloss: To pause or reduce the activity of (a device or application), for example to prepare it for backups or other maintenance.

quiesce time.gloss: The amount of time required to render a computer system inactive, or the amount of time between periods of inactivity.

quindecagon.gloss: A polygon with fifteen sides and fifteen angles.

quine.gloss: A program that produces its own source code as output.

quinquangle.gloss: Synonym of pentagon (“a polygon with five sides and five angles”).

quinquesect.gloss: To divide (a quantity, angle etc.) into five equal parts.

quintate.gloss: The set of the series of integers that occur between a multiple of five and the next (exclusive of those multiples).

quintic.gloss: Of or relating to the fifth degree, such as a quintic polynomial which has the form ax⁵+bx⁴+cx³+dx²+ex+f=0 (containing a term with the independent variable raised to the fifth power).

quintic function.gloss: Any function of a polynomial whose greatest exponent is 5.

quintile.gloss: Any of the quantiles which divide an ordered sample population into five equally numerous subsets.

quintinomial.gloss: Any expression that has five terms.

quintuple-click.gloss: The action of pushing the button on a mouse five times in quick succession.
To push the button on a mouse five times in quick succession.

quippian.gloss: A degree 5 class 3 contravariant of a plane cubic.

quiver.gloss: A multidigraph, especially in the context of representation theory.

quorum.gloss: The minimum number of votes that a distributed transaction has to obtain in order to be allowed to perform an operation in a distributed system.

quote.gloss: To mark an S-expression argument for self-evaluation by the interpreter in Lisp.

quotient.gloss: By analogy, the result of any process that is the inverse of multiplication as defined for any mathematical entities other than numbers.
A mathematical structure formed by identifying elements within a larger one.
To identify elements within a mathematical structure so as to create a quotient.

quotient group.gloss: A group obtained from a larger group by aggregating elements via an equivalence relation that preserves group structure.

quotient map.gloss: A surjective, continuous function from one topological space to another one, such that the latter one's topology has the property that if the inverse image (under the said function) of some subset of it is open in the function's domain, then the subset is open in the target space.

quotient ring.gloss: For a given ring R and ideal I contained in R, another ring, denoted R / I, whose elements are the cosets of I in R.

quotient set.gloss: the set consisting of all equivalence classes

quotient space.gloss: A space obtained from another by identification of points that are equivalent to one another in some equivalence relation.

quotition.gloss: An approach to division in which one asks how many parts there are, rather than (as in partition) what the size of each part is.

quotron.gloss: A computer system or service that provides stock market quotations

qvt.gloss: Initialism of Query/View/Transformation, a standard for model transformation in a certain model-driven architecture.

qwan.gloss: Acronym of quality without a name, referring to a more metaphysical attribute that expresses elegancy of code.

qwerty.gloss: A standard layout of keys on a keyboard for typing, in which the leftmost keys of the top lettered row are Q-W-E-R-T-Y.
A keyboard with such a layout.

qwertz.gloss: A style of keyboard layout used in some European countries.

qwertzu.gloss: Synonym of qwertz (“a style of keyboard layout used in some European countries”).

qwertzuiop.gloss: Synonym of qwertz (“a style of keyboard layout used in some European countries”).

qword.gloss: A quadword: four words, typically used in the same contexts as the fossilized 16-bit sense of "word" and thus 64 bits.

r* tree.gloss: A kind of R-tree used for indexing spatial information.

r+ tree.gloss: A kind of R-tree used for geospatial data.

r-module.gloss: The monoid action of a ring R on an abelian group.

r-pentomino.gloss: A particular five-square polyomino. The methuselah based on this polyomino that, in Conway's Game of Life, has a lifespan of 1,103 generations.

r-tree.gloss: A kind of tree data structure used to group objects by nearness of location, representing them by their minimum bounding rectangles in the next higher level of the tree.

raas.gloss: Initialism of ransomware as a service.

rabbit.gloss: A large element at the beginning of a list of items to be bubble sorted, and thus tending to be quickly swapped into its correct position. Compare turtle.

rabin fingerprint.gloss: A fingerprint using polynomials over a finite field.

rabin-karp algorithm.gloss: A string-searching algorithm that uses hashing to find an exact match of a pattern string in a text.

race.gloss: A race condition; a bug or problem that occurs when two or more components attempt to use the same resource at the same time.

race condition.gloss: A flaw in a system or process whereby the output or result is unexpectedly and critically dependent on the sequence or timing of other events.

rack.gloss: A set with a distributive binary operation whose action on the set is invertible.

rackware.gloss: Low-cost software sold in shops, generally hung on display racks.

racy.gloss: Involving a data race or a race condition.

rademacher distribution.gloss: A discrete probability distribution where a random variate has a 50% chance of being +1 and a 50% chance of being -1.

radial.gloss: Of, or relating to a radius (line joining to a geometric centre).
Of, or relating to a radius (line joining to a geometric centre). Moving or acting along a radius.

radial curve.gloss: Any of a family of curves that are the loci of points that have a defined relationship between a fixed point and the centre of curvature at each point on another curve

radial distribution function.gloss: A function which specifies the average density of atoms, molecules etc in three dimensions from a given point.

radian.gloss: In the International System of Units, the derived unit of plane angle: the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc of its circumference equal in length to the radius of the circle.

radiant.gloss: A straight line proceeding from a given point, or fixed pole, about which it is conceived to revolve.

radical.gloss: Relating to a radix or mathematical root.

Given an ideal I in a commutative ring R, another ideal, denoted Rad(I) or √I, such that an element x ∈ R is in Rad(I) if, for some positive integer n, xⁿ ∈ I; equivalently, the intersection of all prime ideals containing I.
Given a ring R, an ideal containing elements of R that share a property considered, in some sense, "not good".
The intersection of maximal submodules of a given module.
The product of the distinct prime factors of a given positive integer.

radical axis.gloss: The line containing the locus of points from which the segments respectively tangent to two given circles have equal length.

radical center.gloss: A point at which the radical lines of three circles meet.

radical ideal.gloss: An ideal I within a ring R that is its own radical (i.e., for any r ∈ R, if rⁿ ∈ I for some positive integer n, then r ∈ I).

radical line.gloss: The line containing the locus of points from which the segments respectively tangent to two given circles have equal length.

radical plane.gloss: The plane containing the circle formed by the intersection of two spheres (or whose points have equal power with respect to two non-intersecting spheres)

radicand.gloss: The number or expression whose square root or other root is being considered.

radio button.gloss: Any of a group of widgets in a graphical user interface that is used to select one of a group of options; the selection of any one deselects the others.

radiosity.gloss: A three-dimensional rendering system that simulates all reflections from objects in the scene.

radius.gloss: A line segment between any point of a circle or sphere and its center.
The length of this line segment.
The minimum eccentricity of any vertex, for a given graph.
Initialism of Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service.

radius of curvature.gloss: The radius of the osculating circle at the point on the curve
qualifiers: for any point on a curve

radius vector.gloss: Of a point, a vector going from the origin to that point; equivalently, the transpose of the point.

radix.gloss: The number of distinct symbols used to represent numbers in a particular base, as ten for decimal.

radix point.gloss: The character used to separate the integer and fractional part of a number in a digital representation of a number, regardless of the base used.

radix sort.gloss: Any of various sorting algorithms in which items are processed according to the value of each digit or character in turn

radix tree.gloss: A space-optimized trie data structure in which each node that is the only child is merged with its parent.

radon measure.gloss: A measure on the σ-algebra of Borel sets of a Hausdorff space that is locally finite and inner regular.

radon point.gloss: A point in the intersection of convex hulls specified by Radon's theorem.

radon transform.gloss: An integral transform which takes a function defined on the plane to a function defined on the (two-dimensional) space of lines in the plane, whose value at a particular line is equal to the line integral of the function over that line.

raft.gloss: To dock (toolbars, etc.) so that they share horizontal or vertical space.

ragdoll.gloss: A model consisting of a set of connected rigid bodies that can collapse in a loose, natural manner.

ragdoll physics.gloss: Physics based around ragdolls (models consisting of a set of connected rigid bodies that can collapse in a loose, natural manner).

ragged.gloss: Of a data structure: having uneven levels.

ragged array.gloss: An array of arrays in which the component arrays are of varying lengths.

raid.gloss: Acronym of Redundant Array of Inexpensive (or Independent) Disks.

raii.gloss: Initialism of Resource Acquisition Is Initialization, a popular design pattern in object-oriented programming that ties resources to the lifespan of associated objects to prevent resource leakage.

rail fence cipher.gloss: A transposition cipher in which the plain text is written in a zigzag fashion diagonally up and down on successive "rails" of an imaginary fence, and then the characters are read off in rows to obtain the ciphertext.

raim.gloss: Initialism of redundant array of independent memory.

rainbow.gloss: Of or pertaining to rainbow tables.

rainbow table.gloss: A table of surjective functions used to decrypt a text that was coded using a hash table.

raise.gloss: To instantiate and transmit (an exception, by throwing it, or an event).

rake.gloss: A type of puffer train that leaves behind a stream of spaceships as it moves.

ram disk.gloss: A virtual disk, implemented in software, that stores its contents in random access memory.

ram pack.gloss: A hardware module containing RAM for use by another device.

ramanujan graph.gloss: A regular graph whose spectral gap is almost as large as possible, making it an excellent spectral expander. Such graphs are relevant to diverse branches of pure mathematics.

ramanujan prime.gloss: A prime number that satisfies a result proven by Srinivasa Ramanujan relating to the prime-counting function.

ramanujan summation.gloss: A technique for assigning a value to an infinite divergent series, not summation in the traditional sense, but having useful mathematical properties.

ramanujan's sum.gloss: A function, usually denoted c_q(n), of two positive integer variables q and n, defined by the formula c_q(n)=∑_(1<a≤q atop (a,q)=1)e^(2πi tfrac aqn),, where (a, q) = 1 means that a only takes on values coprime to q. It is used in the proof of Vinogradov's theorem.

ramifiable.gloss: Capable of being subdivided into branches.

ramified forcing.gloss: The original form of forcing, starting with a model M of set theory in which the axiom of constructibility, V = L, holds, and then building up a larger model M[G] of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory by adding a generic subset G of a partially ordered set to M, imitating Kurt Gödel's constructible hierarchy.

ramsey number.gloss: Any one of a certain set of numbers which are guaranteed to exist by Ramsey's theorem; a positive integer which is a certain function of some given multiset of positive integers, where that "certain function" is that which yields the minimal number guaranteed to exist by Ramsey's theorem.

ramsey sentence.gloss: A formal logical reconstruction of a theoretical proposition, attempting to draw a line between science and metaphysics by replacing non-observable theoretical terms with observational terms.

ramsey theory.gloss: A branch of mathematics which deals with patterns that inevitably arise in sufficiently large sets (i.e., subsets of some structure).

ramsey's theorem.gloss: A (version of a) theorem concerning the existence of cliques in a labelled complete graph. The theorem that any graph labelling (with colours) of a sufficiently large complete graph contains monochromatic cliques.

A (version of a) theorem concerning the existence of cliques in a labelled complete graph. The theorem that any graph labelling (with colours) of an infinite complete graph contains at least one infinite monochromatic clique.

ramseyan.gloss: Of or relating to Frank Ramsey (1903-1930), British economist, mathematician, and philosopher.

random.gloss: Involving an outcome which is impossible to predict, but which may be represented by a probability distribution; in the ideal case, involving outcomes which are equally likely.
Pseudorandom; mimicking the result of random selection.

random access.gloss: The ability to access any element of a sequence in real time, without having to seek through preceding elements.

random access memory.gloss: Computer memory, usually volatile, that stores program and data values during operation and in which each word of memory may be directly (randomly) accessed.
Computer memory, usually volatile, that stores program and data values during operation and in which each word of memory may be directly (randomly) accessed. Main memory.

random forest.gloss: A structure composed of a collection of decision trees with controlled variance

random function.gloss: A function whose formula is always the same, but whose initial value is chosen at random from a set of possible values (its domain).
A function chosen at random from a set of functions.
A function that returns a random or pseudo-random value that is distributed according to a specific probability distribution associated with the function.

random sample.gloss: A sample randomly taken from an investigated population.

random sequence.gloss: A sequence of identically distributed random variables.

random variable.gloss: A quantity whose value is random and to which a probability distribution is assigned, such as the possible outcome of a roll of a dice.
A measurable function from a sample space to the measurable space of possible values of the variable.

random walk.gloss: A stochastic path consisting of a series of sequential movements, the direction (and sometime length) of which is chosen at random.

random walker.gloss: An object taking a random walk.

random-access.gloss: Capable of being accessed in any order, not required to be sequential.

randomized algorithm.gloss: Any algorithm that uses randomness as part of its logic.

randomized polynomial time.gloss: The complexity class of problems for which a probabilistic Turing machine exists with certain properties.

randomly.gloss: By random access; at any point at a given time; not sequentially.

randomness.gloss: A type of circumstance or event that is described by a probability distribution.

range.gloss: The set of values (points) which a function can obtain.
The length of the smallest interval which contains all the data in a sample; the difference between the largest and smallest observations in the sample.
A sequential list of values specified by an iterator.

rangefree.gloss: That is not dependent on a range

rank.gloss: The dimensionality of an array (computing) or tensor.
The maximal number of linearly independent columns (or rows) of a matrix.
The maximum quantity of D-linearly independent elements of a module (over an integral domain D).
The size of any basis of a given matroid.

rank of apparition.gloss: Given a positive integer m and a divisibility sequence Sₖ, the smallest index k such that Sₖ is divisible by m;

Given a positive integer m and a divisibility sequence Sₖ, the smallest index k such that Sₖ is divisible by m;
such an index for some generalisation of the concept (for example to allow multiple ranks of apparition for a given m). such an index for some generalisation of the concept (for example to allow multiple ranks of apparition for a given m).

rank sum.gloss: The sum of ranks of members of a sample population

rank-deficient.gloss: Not having full rank; having a rank (dimension) less than the number of columns and the number of rows.

rao-blackwellization.gloss: The procedure of applying the Rao–Blackwell theorem to an estimator.

rao-blackwellize.gloss: To apply the Rao–Blackwell theorem to an estimator.

rao-blackwellized.gloss: Of an estimator, being the result of Rao-Blackwellization.

raster.gloss: A bitmap image, consisting of a grid of pixels, stored as a sequence of lines.

raster graphics.gloss: A data file or structure representing a generally rectangular grid of pixels, or points of colour, on a computer monitor, paper, or other display medium.

raster mask.gloss: A greyscale bitmap that controls the alpha channel of another bitmap.

rasterize.gloss: To convert (an image) into a grid of points, such as a bitmap, for display or printing.

rat.gloss: To hack someone with a remote-access Trojan.

rat's nest.gloss: Something that is excessively complicated, entangled, or disorderly (either physically or metaphorically). A software or hardware system whose design lacks organized structure, making it difficult to understand and maintain.

ratchet.gloss: A mechanism for generating a new unique key for each message by moving forward in a sequence.

rate limit.gloss: The maximum number of requests in a given timeframe that are able to be made to a server that uses rate limiting.

rate limiter.gloss: A piece of software that performs rate limiting.

rate limiting.gloss: The process of limiting the number of requests made to a server so as to avoid overloading it.

rate of change.gloss: A value that results from dividing the change in a function of a variable by the corresponding change in the variable

A value that results from dividing the change in a function of a variable by the corresponding change in the variable Also, the instantaneous rate of change, the limit of such value as the change approached zero.

rateless.gloss: Describing a family of codes whose higher rate codes have codewords that are prefixes of those of the lower rate codes.

ratelessly.gloss: In a rateless manner; in a manner that employs a rateless code.

ratio formalis.gloss: the formal grounds for something; the essential attributes of matter as they appear in the mind or in a definition.

ratio scale.gloss: A scale of measurement of data having a fixed zero value, which permits the quantitative comparison of differences of values.

ratio variable.gloss: A variable with the features of interval variable and, additionally, whose any two values have meaningful ratio, making the operations of multiplication and division meaningful.

rational.gloss: Comprising, or expressible as, a ratio Of a number, capable of being expressed as the ratio of two integers.
Comprising, or expressible as, a ratio Of an algebraic expression in indeterminates, or more generally a function: capable of being expressed as the ratio of two polynomials.
Comprising, or expressible as, a ratio Of a variety: (informally) geometrically simple almost everywhere; (formally) birationally equivalent to projective space
Comprising, or expressible as, a ratio Of a function between varieties: acting as a morphism on an open subset of its domain.

Comprising, or expressible as, a ratio Of a point on an algebraic variety over a field: whose coordinates belong to the field in question (in contrast to those points of the variety which are only defined over the algebraic closure of the base field).
A rational number: a number that can be expressed as the quotient of two integers.

rational function.gloss: Any function expressible as the quotient of two (coprime) polynomials (and which thus has poles at a finite, discrete set of points which are the roots of the denominator).

rational number.gloss: A number that can be expressed as the ratio of two integers.

rational numbers.gloss: The set of numbers that can be expressed as a ratio of integers, often denoted with the bold letter Q, or the blackboard bold letter ℚ.

rationalization.gloss: The simplification of an expression without changing its value.

rationalize.gloss: To remove radicals, without changing the value of an expression or the roots of an equation.

ratiuncule.gloss: A ratio very close to unity.

ravel.gloss: In the APL programming language: to reshape (a variable) into a vector.

ravelled.gloss: Of a variable in the APL programming language: which has been reshaped into a vector.

ravelling.gloss: gerund of ravel In the APL programming language: the act of reshaping a variable into a vector.

ravioli code.gloss: Overly structured program source code, with many small sections, functions, etc. that should be combined.

raw.gloss: Initialism of read after write, a kind of data hazard.

raw data.gloss: Data that has not been analyzed or processed.

ray.gloss: A line extending indefinitely in one direction from a point.

ray casting.gloss: The calculation of intersections between a ray and a surface.

ray marching.gloss: An advanced form of ray tracing in which the imaginary light rays are not merely computed where they intersect with solid parts of the model, but also sampled and modified as they pass through space.

ray tracing.gloss: A technique that produces realistically shaded images by projecting imaginary light rays to determine which parts of an object should be illuminated.

raycaster.gloss: A program or algorithm that performs ray casting.

rayleigh quotient.gloss: A formula used in the min-max theorem to find exact eigenvalues, and in eigenvalue algorithms to obtain an eigenvalue approximation from an eigenvector approximation; it has applications in quantum mechanics.

rbf.gloss: Abbreviation of radial basis function, a type of equation used to approximate a vector field, used in neural networks.

rdbms.gloss: Initialism of relational database management system.

rdma.gloss: Initialism of remote direct memory access

rdram.gloss: Initialism of Rambus dynamic random-access memory.

re.gloss: Initialism of recursively enumerable; the class of decision problems for which a “yes” answer can be verified by a Turing machine in a finite amount of time. See more at RE (complexity) on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

reachability.gloss: The extent to which a node in a graph is reachable from others

reachable.gloss: That may be reached from another node in a graph by passing along one or more lines

reactive programming.gloss: A declarative programming paradigm where changes to values are automatically propagated, without the need for explicit reassignment.

read.gloss: To fetch data from (a storage medium, etc.).

read receipt.gloss: An automatic response, often containing a timestamp, which notifies the sender of an e-mail or instant message that the message was opened.

read-around ratio.gloss: In cathode-ray-tube storage systems, the number of times that a value can be read from a given cell without corrupting adjacent stored values.

read-only.gloss: Unalterable, capable of being read but not written.

read-only access.gloss: A permission to access files or directories where the user is only allowed to read or view, not to make changes.

read-only memory.gloss: A computer memory chip that stores values but does not allow updates, in which the values are nonvolatile in that they are retained even when the computer is unpowered.

read-through.gloss: A cache that will fetch information from the original source when asked for information that is not yet cached.

read-write.gloss: Supporting both read and write operations.

readahead.gloss: The operation of reading data from a storage medium in advance so that it is immediately available when requested.

readback.gloss: The act of reading data back from a location where it has been stored.

readers-writers problem.gloss: Any of a class of problems in which many concurrent threads of execution try to access the same shared resource at one time, with constraints on which threads may read from and write to the resource.

readme.gloss: A text file meant to be read before taking any significant action with the items it accompanies.

readout.gloss: The information output from a computer in a readable form.

readset.gloss: The set of records read from a database, typically by a single transaction

readtable.gloss: In Lisp and related languages, a data structure specifying how text characters are to be interpreted syntactically.

ready queue.gloss: A data structure that holds a process that is ready to run, but is unable to do so because the CPU is already occupied.

real.gloss: Being either a rational number, or the limit of a convergent infinite sequence of rational numbers: being one of a set of numbers with a one-to-one correspondence to the points on a line.

real analysis.gloss: The branch of mathematics dealing with the real numbers and related structures.

real axis.gloss: The horizontal line in the complex plane, every point on which corresponds to a real number.

real function.gloss: A function whose range is a subset of the set of real numbers.

real line.gloss: The real number system, viewed as a line.

real mode.gloss: The default operational mode of x86-compatible CPUs, offering direct software access to all memory and peripherals but without the advanced features of protected mode.

real number.gloss: The limit of a convergent sequence of rational numbers, whether the limit is a rational number such as 2, -5, or 2/7 or whether the limit is an irrational number such as the square root of two or the circumference of the circle whose radius is one.

real number line.gloss: A geometric representation of the real number system.

real number system.gloss: The complete Archimedean ordered field (of real numbers).

real numbers.gloss: The smallest set containing all limits of convergent sequences of rational numbers.

real part.gloss: Of a complex number a + bi, the value a.

real plane.gloss: The Cartesian product of two real lines.

real programmer.gloss: An archetypal highly skilled programmer, who eschews abstractions and convenient modern tools and methods of programming, instead preferring to use a manually-optimised low-level language or program directly in machine code for maximum performance.

real projective plane.gloss: A three-dimensional vector space over the field of real numbers in which one-dimensional linear subspaces are considered as “points” and two-dimensional linear subspaces are considered as “lines”. Equivalently, a sphere in which pairs of antipodal points are considered as “points” and great circles are considered as “lines”.

real storage.gloss: The physical main memory, or RAM, of a computer.

real time.gloss: The duration required by a computer system to complete a particular task.

real valued.gloss: Used to describe a mathematical entity, like a function, that takes values from the real numbers (as opposed to, for instance, from the complex numbers).

real vector space.gloss: A vector space over the field of real numbers.

real-time.gloss: Of a system: that responds to events or signals within a predictable time after their occurrence; specifically in which the response time must be within the maximum allowed, but is typically synchronous.

real-valued.gloss: Having only real values: having as its codomain the set of real numbers or a subset thereof.

realia.gloss: Physical objects in a library collection that do not fit into traditional categories of media, whose media are the objects themselves, as opposed to their informational content, such as artifacts, tools, memorabilia, and naturally-occurring specimens.

reality gap.gloss: The difference between a simulation and reality.

realize.gloss: To obtain an entity from (an abstract group or structure).

realm.gloss: A grouping of equally trusted computers managed together on a network.

reap.gloss: To terminate a child process that has previously exited, thereby removing it from the process table.

reason.gloss: A cause: A premise placed after its conclusion.

rebase.gloss: To modify core data from which other data is derived in such a way that the final meaning is unchanged.
To change the base address of.
To integrate changes by appending them to another commit or branch, rather than pulling or merging in changes from a branch.

rebin.gloss: To divide (data) into a different set of bins, or interval groupings.

reboot.gloss: To execute a computer's boot process, effectively resetting the computer and causing the operating system to reload, commonly after a system failure.

rebucket.gloss: To recategorize (data) into a different set of buckets.

recent.gloss: A recently viewed or accessed item.

reciprocal.gloss: Used to denote different kinds of mutual relation; often with reference to the substitution of reciprocals for given quantities.

reciprocal lattice.gloss: A conceptual lattice in reciprocal (or momentum) space that corresponds to a given Bravais lattice in realspace.

reciprocant.gloss: A contravariant expressing a certain condition of tangency; a differential invariant.

reciprocity law.gloss: A generalization of the law of quadratic reciprocity to arbitrary monic irreducible polynomials with integer coefficients.

reclock.gloss: To modify the clock speed of.

recomment.gloss: To convert (a portion of source code, configuration, etc.) back to a comment, so that it no longer takes effect.

reconvolution.gloss: A second or subsequent convolution, typically performed after deconvolution

record.gloss: A set of data relating to a single individual or item.
A data structure similar to a struct, in some programming languages such as C and Java based on classes and designed for storing immutable data.

recordset.gloss: A data structure consisting of a group of database records.

recovery cd.gloss: A CD-ROM distributed with a computer and containing copies of the software originally installed on the computer's hard drive, allowing the end user to restore the system to its factory state.

recreational mathematics.gloss: Any use of mathematics or logic whose primary purpose is recreation, though often with more serious characteristics.

rectagraph.gloss: A triangle-free connected graph where any two vertices have 0 or 2 common neighbors.

rectahedron.gloss: A six-sided polyhedron whose faces are all rectangular (like a brick, shoe box or matchbox)

rectangle.gloss: Any quadrilateral having opposing sides parallel and four right angles.

rectangular cuboid.gloss: A special case of a cuboid with rectangular faces in which all of its dihedral angles are right angles.

rectangular hyperbola.gloss: A hyperbola where the two asymptotes intersect at a right angle.

rectangular number.gloss: A number which is the product of two consecutive integers.
A composite number; or a composite number which is not a square; or a composite number which is neither square nor heteromecic.

rectanguloid.gloss: A rectangular object; A three-dimensional form related to the rectangle

rectification.gloss: The determination of a straight line whose length is equal to a portion of a curve.

The truncation of a polyhedron by replacing each vertex with a face that passes though the midpoint of each edge connected to the vertex; an analogous procedure on a polytope of dimension higher than 3.

rectify.gloss: To determine the length of a curve included between two limits.

recur.gloss: Synonym of recurse (“to execute a procedure recursively”).
Often in the form recurring following a number: of a numeral or group of numerals in a decimal fraction: to repeat indefinitely.

recurrence relation.gloss: an equation that recursively defines a sequence; each term of the sequence is defined as a function of the preceding terms.

recurrence time.gloss: The moment in time between two successive occurrences in which a Markov process enters any given state.

recurring.gloss: Of a decimal: having a set of digits that is repeated indefinitely.

recursion.gloss: The act of defining an object (usually a function) in terms of that object itself.
The invocation of a procedure from within itself.

recursion theory.gloss: A branch of mathematical logic studying computable functions and Turing degrees, concerned with questions such as "What does it mean for a function on the natural numbers to be computable?" and "Can noncomputable functions be classified into a hierarchy based on their level of noncomputability?".

recursive.gloss: Having to do with an object (typically a function or formula) which is defined in terms of the object itself.
Having to do with an algorithm, program, subroutine, procedure, function, or other block of code that calls itself.
Having to do with a function which can be computed by a theoretical model of a computer in a finite amount of time.
Having to do with a set whose characteristic function is recursive (sense 4).

recursive descent.gloss: A kind of top-down parsing involving a set of mutually recursive procedures, each of which implements one of the non-terminals of the grammar, so that the structure of the parser program closely mirrors that of the grammar.

recursive function.gloss: Any function that uses recursion and can call itself until a certain condition is met.
Any function whose value may be obtained using a finite number of operations using a precisely specified algorithm.

recursively enumerable.gloss: Of a set, such that there exists a deterministic algorithm which will list all the items in the set and no others.

recycle bin.gloss: In Microsoft Windows, a storage location for deleted files, from which they can be retrieved or permanently deleted.

red forest.gloss: A forest (group of domains) having high security and limited access, used for administrative purposes.

red-black tree.gloss: A type of self-balancing binary search tree, typically used to implement associative arrays.

redefine.gloss: To define again or differently. To define a previously defined area of storage etc. in a different manner, e.g. changing it from textual to numeric.

rederive.gloss: To derive again, especially by using a different method

redevelop.gloss: To develop again or differently. To reprogram (an app).

redex.gloss: Something to be reduced according to the rules of a formal system.

redimension.gloss: To resize (an array or similar data structure) so as to change its dimensionality; to reallocate.

redirect.gloss: To substitute an address or pointer to a new location.
To send to a new location by substituting an address or pointer.
The substitution of one address or identifier for another one, so as to navigate to a different location.

redistributable.gloss: Of a software component, allowable to be redistributed by a third party as part of its own software.
A software component that can be redistributed.

redmondian.gloss: Of or pertaining to the computing company Microsoft.

redraw.gloss: An update to the screen display.

reduce.gloss: To simplify an equation or formula without changing its value.
To express the solution of a problem in terms of another (known) algorithm.
To convert a syllogism to a clearer or simpler form.

reduced algebra.gloss: An algebra over a reduced ring.

reduced ring.gloss: A ring R that has no nonzero nilpotent elements; equivalently, such that, for x ∈ R, x² = 0 implies x = 0.

reduced row echelon form.gloss: The form of a row-reduced matrix which is in row echelon form.

reduced word.gloss: A word that contains no redundant pairs.

reducer.gloss: A function that takes state and action as arguments and returns the next state of the app.

reducible.gloss: Able to be factored into polynomials of lower degree, as x²-1.
Able to be factored into smaller integers; composite.
Containing a sphere of codimension 1 that is not the boundary of a ball.

reductio ad absurdum.gloss: The method of disproving a statement by assuming the statement is true and, with that assumption, arriving at a blatant contradiction.

reduction.gloss: The rewriting of an expression into a simpler form.
A transformation of one problem into another problem, such as mapping reduction or polynomial-time reduction.

redundant.gloss: Containing duplicate pathways to send a message.

redundant array of independent disks.gloss: A system using multiple hard drives for the sharing or replication of data in order to increase data integrity, fault-tolerance or throughput.

ree group.gloss: A group of Lie type over a finite field constructed from an exceptional automorphism of a Dynkin diagram that reverses the direction of the multiple bonds, generalizing the Suzuki group.

reeb component.gloss: A solid torus whose boundary is a leaf of a foliation of the ambient 3-dimensional manifold.

reebless.gloss: (of a foliation) Not containing a Reeb component.

reentrancy.gloss: The state or condition of being reentrant.

reentrant.gloss: That may be executed more than once at a time either by different threads, or because of recursion.

rhetorical induction.gloss: reasoning from specific examples to general laws

rhizic.gloss: Relating to the root of an equation.

rhizoristic.gloss: Relating to the separation of the roots of an equation.

rhombic dodecahedron.gloss: A convex polyhedron that has 12 congruent rhombic faces, 24 edges and 14 vertices of two types (eight 3-edge and six 4-edge) and is a Catalan solid.

rhombic triacontahedron.gloss: A convex polyhedron that has 30 congruent rhombic faces, 60 edges and 32 vertices of two types (twenty 3-edge and twelve 5-edge) and is the Catalan solid dual to the icosidodecahedron.

rhombicosidodecahedron.gloss: An Archimedean solid with 62 regular faces (20 triangles, 30 squares, and 12 pentagons), 60 vertices and 120 edges.

rhombicuboctahedron.gloss: An Archimedean solid with eight triangular and eighteen square faces; the small rhombicuboctahedron.

rhombidodecahedron.gloss: A nonconvex uniform polyhedron with square faces and sharing symmetry of a dodecahedron.

rhombiform.gloss: In the shape of a rhombus.

rhombihexahedron.gloss: Either of two concave polyhedra: the great rhombihexahedron and the small rhombihexahedron.

rhombitrihexagonal.gloss: Relating to a semiregular tiling of the Euclidean plane with one triangle, two squares, and one hexagon on each vertex.

rhombitruncated icosidodecahedron.gloss: An Archimedean solid composed of 122 faces, 120 vertices, and 240 edges.

rhombus.gloss: A parallelogram having all sides of equal length.
A parallelogram having all sides of equal length. The rhombus diamond, as one of the suits seen in a deck of playing cards ( or ).

rhu.gloss: Initialism of radioisotope heater unit, a device that generates heat from the natural decay of radioactive material.

ribbon.gloss: A toolbar that incorporates tabs and menus.

ribbonlength.gloss: The length of a ribbon (in a ribbon knot)

riccati equation.gloss: Any first-order ordinary differential equation that is quadratic in the unknown function.

ricci calculus.gloss: A formal system in which index notation is used to define tensors and tensor fields and the rules for their manipulation; the theory of tensor calculus as developed by Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro, which formed the foundation of the modern theory.

rice.gloss: An instance of customization of a user interface.
To customize the user interface of a computer system, e.g. a desktop environment. (derived from rice out)

rice distribution.gloss: The probability distribution of the magnitude of a circular bivariate normal random variable with potentially non-zero mean.

rich.gloss: Elaborate, having complex formatting, multimedia, or depth of interaction.

rich internet application.gloss: A Web application that has many of the characteristics of desktop application software, like domain logic.
An applet or Web Start application.

rich text.gloss: Text that has been enhanced with formatting, multimedia, etc., such as Microsoft's Rich Text Format or the enriched text format used in electronic mail.

richlet.gloss: A small Java program that creates all the necessary components for a given page in response to a user's request.

ricing.gloss: The act of customizing the user interface of a computer system.

riemann.gloss: Pertaining to German mathematician Bernhard Riemann.

riemann integral.gloss: A type of integral whose computation involves dividing the interval of integration into smaller sub-intervals, summing sample values of the integrand inside those sub-intervals multiplied by their lengths, and letting the number of sub-intervals tend to infinity.

riemann space.gloss: A subset of Euclidean space in which tensors are used to describe distance, angle, and curvature

riemann sphere.gloss: The complex numbers extended with the number ∞; the complex plane (representation of the complex numbers as a Euclidean plane) extended with a single idealised point at infinity and consequently homeomorphic to a sphere in 3-dimensional Euclidean space.

The 2-sphere embedded in Euclidean three-dimensional space and often represented as a unit sphere, regarded as a homeomorphic representation of the extended complex plane and thus the extended complex numbers.
