riemann sum.gloss: A certain kind of approximation of an integral by a finite sum that is calculated by dividing the interval of integration into smaller sub-intervals and summing sample values of the integrand inside those sub-intervals multiplied by their lengths.

riemann surface.gloss: A one-dimensional complex manifold; a generalization of the complex plane.

riemann zeta function.gloss: The function ζ defined by the Dirichlet series ζ(s)=∑ₙ₌₁ ᪲1/(nˢ)=1/(1ˢ)+1/(2ˢ)+1/(3ˢ)+1/(4ˢ)+⋯, which is summable for points s in the complex half-plane with real part > 1; the analytic continuation of said function, being a holomorphic function defined on the complex numbers with pole at 1.

riemann-lebesgue lemma.gloss: A lemma, of importance in harmonic analysis and asymptotic analysis, stating that the Fourier transform or Laplace transform of an L1 function vanishes at infinity.

riemann-stieltjes integral.gloss: A generalization of the Riemann integral, serving as a precursor of the Lebesgue integral and a means of unifying equivalent forms of statistical theorems that apply to discrete and continuous probability.

riemannian.gloss: Of or relating to the work, or theory developed from the work, of German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, especially to Riemannian manifolds and Riemannian geometry.
One who uses or supports the work of German mathematician Bernhard Riemann.

riemannian geometry.gloss: The branch of differential geometry that concerns Riemannian manifolds; an example of a geometry that involves Riemannian manifolds.

riffle shuffle.gloss: A permutation that models the outcome of a riffle shuffle; the operation of dividing an ordered set into two equal subsets and then alternately listing sequences of elements from each subset that have a common specified length.

rig.gloss: A personal computer, typically one modified for looks.
An algebraic structure similar to a ring, but without the requirement that every element have an additive inverse.

right.gloss: Of an angle, measuring 90 degrees, or one quarter of a complete rotation; the angle between two perpendicular lines.
Of a geometric figure, incorporating a right angle between edges, faces, axes, etc.

right angle.gloss: Half of the angle formed by a single straight line, equivalent to 90 degrees.

right coset.gloss: A copy of a subgroup, multiplied on the right by some element from the parent group.

right eigenvalue.gloss: An eigenvalue corresponding to the right transform of a given linear operator; i.e. λ such that rm Au=λu.

right eigenvector.gloss: An eigenvector corresponding to the right transform of a given linear operator; i.e. u such that rm Au=λu.

right ideal.gloss: A subset of a ring which is closed under right-multiplication by any element of the ring.

right identity.gloss: An element of a structure that produces an identity mapping when applied on the right.

right inverse.gloss: For a given morphism f : X → Y, its right inverse (if it has one) is a morphism s : Y → X such that f∘s= mbox id_Y.

right outer join.gloss: A join yielding a set of records for two tables, where all rows of the "right" table are enlisted with all rows of the "left" table, even if the join condition does not find any matching row on the "left".

right shift.gloss: A bit shift to the right, in which all of the bits of an operand are shifted by a given number of positions to the right.
The right shift operator; often given as >> or >>>
To perform a right shift bitwise operation.

right stochastic matrix.gloss: A square matrix whose rows consist of nonnegative real numbers, with each row summing to 1. Used to describe the transitions of a Markov chain; its element in the i'th row and j'th column describes the probability of moving from state i to state j in one time step.

right total.gloss: Of a binary relation, to have every element of the right set occur at least once: ∀b∈B∃a∈A:(a,b)∈R⊆A×B

right trapezoid.gloss: A trapezoid with two adjacent right angles

right triangle.gloss: A triangle having a right angle as one of its interior angles.

right-click.gloss: To press the right-hand button on a computer mouse.
To activate (an item on the screen) by right-clicking while the pointer is over it.

right-drag.gloss: To drag an item using the right mouse button.

rigidification.gloss: A form of isomorphism applied between line bundles.

rimm.gloss: Initialism of Rambus in-line memory module.

ring.gloss: A planar geometrical figure included between two concentric circles.
A hierarchical level of privilege in a computer system, usually at hardware level, used to protect data and functionality (also protection ring).

A network topology where connected devices form a circular data channel. All computers on the ring can see every message, and there are no collisions, and a single point of failure will occur if any part of the ring breaks.

An algebraic structure which consists of a set with two binary operations: an additive operation and a multiplicative operation, such that the set is an abelian group under the additive operation, a monoid under the multiplicative operation, and such that the multiplicative operation is distributive with respect to the additive operation.
An algebraic structure as above, but only required to be a semigroup under the multiplicative operation, that is, there need not be a multiplicative identity element.
A family of sets that is closed under finite unions and set-theoretic differences.
A family of sets closed under finite union and finite intersection.

ring homomorphism.gloss: A function from one ring to another one which preserves the structure of the additive operation, the structure of the multiplicative operation, the zero element (additive identity), and, if there is one, the unity element (multiplicative identity).

ring isomorphism.gloss: A ring homomorphism which is also a bijection.

ring of fractions.gloss: A ring whose elements are fractions whose numerators belong to a given commutative unital ring and whose denominators belong to a multiplicatively closed unital subset D of that given ring. Addition and multiplication of such fractions is defined just as for a field of fractions. A pair of fractions a/b and c/d are deemed equivalent if there is a member x of D such that x(ad-bc)=0.

ring sum normal form.gloss: The form of a Boolean formula expressed using only the operators and constants of a Boolean ring (XOR, AND, 0, 1), some variables and possibly also coefficients, and without using any parentheses.

ring topology.gloss: A network topology in which, in the physical case, every node of a network is connected to exactly two other nodes: one node designated as upstream and the other as downstream. A given node receives data from its upstream node and sends data to its downstream node.

ring-theoretic.gloss: Of or relating to ring theory.

ringoid.gloss: A small preadditive category (so named because a ring can be viewed as a preadditive category with a single object).

rip.gloss: To copy data from a CD, DVD, Internet stream, etc., to a hard drive, portable device, etc.
Data or audio copied from a CD, DVD, Internet stream, etc. to a hard drive, portable device, etc.
Data or audio copied from a CD, DVD, Internet stream, etc. to a hard drive, portable device, etc. Ellipsis of high quality rip.
Something ripped off or stolen; a work resulting from plagiarism.

rip box.gloss: A high end computer used for "ripping" (decoding) DVDs and converting them into various formats, using ripping and encoding software.

riplock.gloss: A deliberate slowdown in the transfer rate when reading data from a DVD, so as to reduce the amount of noise from the drive.

ripper.gloss: Software that extracts content from files or storage media.

ripple carry.gloss: The situation where a logic circuit uses multiple full adders to add n-bit numbers, with each full adder taking the output of the previous one as an input.

riro.gloss: Acronym of rubbish in, rubbish out.

risc.gloss: Acronym of reduced instruction set computer.

riskware.gloss: Software that may pose a risk to a computer on which it is installed.

ritz series.gloss: A generalization of a Fourier series extended to situations in which a displacement field has an arbitrary time dependence while still maintaining its spatial periodicity.

rldram.gloss: Initialism of reduced latency dynamic random access memory.

rng.gloss: An algebraic structure satisfying the same properties as a ring, except that multiplication need not have an identity element.

road map.gloss: A structured representation of objects to display a development plan, used in business for strategic planning and communications.

roam.gloss: To use a network or service from different locations or devices.
To transmit (resources) between different locations or devices, to allow comparable usage from any of them.

roamable.gloss: Supporting roaming (the use of a network or service from different locations or devices).

roaming.gloss: The use of a network or service from different locations or devices.
Using the OS service of manipulating folders and documents from different PC devices by a registered user.

robibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2⁹⁰ (1024⁹, 1,237,940,039,285,380,274,899,124,224) bytes or 2¹⁰ (1024) yobibytes, as opposed to a ronnabyte.

robin boundary condition.gloss: A type of boundary condition that specifies a linear combination of the value of a function and the value of its derivative at the boundary of a given domain.

robin hood hashing.gloss: A scheme for resolving hash collisions that favors the displacement of the element that is farthest from its home location.

robinson arithmetic.gloss: A finitely axiomatized fragment of first-order Peano arithmetic, lacking the axiom schema of mathematical induction.

robinson-schensted correspondence.gloss: A bijective correspondence between permutations and pairs of standard Young tableaux of the same shape. It has applications in combinatorics and other areas.

robomoderate.gloss: To robotically moderate (a discussion forum, etc.).

robomoderation.gloss: Robotic moderation (of a discussion forum, etc.).

robomoderator.gloss: A robotic moderator (of a discussion forum, etc.).

robot.gloss: A bot, software designed to perform a task.

robust.gloss: Resistant or impervious to failure regardless of user input or unexpected conditions.
Not greatly influenced by errors in assumptions about the distribution of sample errors.

rogue.gloss: Malware that deceitfully presents itself as antispyware.

rogue access point.gloss: An unauthorized access point installed on a WLAN.

rolap.gloss: Acronym of Relational Online Analytical Processing.

role-based.gloss: based on a special given role to access a content; used usually in cloud computing, databases, or other complex systems.

role-oriented.gloss: Of or pertaining to a form of computer programming which aims at expressing objects in terms that are analogous to a human conceptual understanding of the world.

role-oriented language.gloss: A programming language that uses a paradigm aiming at expressing things in terms analogous to human conceptual understanding of the World by using roles.

roll.gloss: To apply (one line or surface) to another without slipping; to bring all the parts of (one line or surface) into successive contact with another, in such a manner that at every instant the parts that have been in contact are equal.
To throw dice. To generate a random number.
To perform an operation similar to a bit shift, but with the bit that "falls off the end" being wrapped around to the other end.
To create a customized version of; often followed by one's own.
An operation similar to a bit shift, but with the bit that "falls off the end" being wrapped around to the other end.

roll one's own.gloss: To create something of which an analogue is commercially available.

rollback.gloss: A return to a prior state by undoing some operation, especially of policy or price changes. An operation which returns a database, or group of records in a database, to a previous state (normally to the previous commit point).
To return to the previous state.

rollback netcode.gloss: A type of netcode that prioritizes the inputs of a local player and predicts the inputs of a remote player, rolling back to a previous state when the remote player's inputs differ from the prediction.

rolling backup.gloss: A form of backup where newer data periodically overwrites older data.

rollover.gloss: A graphic element that changes its appearance when the cursor moves over it.
A keyboard feature where each key is scanned independently, so that multiple simultaneous keypresses always register correctly.

rollover cable.gloss: A kind of cable used to connect consoles to computers, having the pinouts on one end reversed with respect to the other.

rollup.gloss: A collection of software updates distributed as a single package.

rom.gloss: The nonvolatile internal storage, often a solid-state drive, on a mobile device or computer.

romable.gloss: Able to execute from read-only memory.

roman.gloss: Of or related to the Latin alphabet or roman numerals.

roman font.gloss: A font that is upright, as opposed to oblique or italic.
A font supporting the characters of the Latin alphabet.

roman surface.gloss: A self-intersecting mapping of the real projective plane into three-dimensional space, with an unusually high degree of symmetry.

ronnabit.gloss: One octillion (10²⁷) bits. SI symbol: Rb.

ronnabyte.gloss: One octillion (10²⁷) bytes. SI symbol: RB.

rook polynomial.gloss: A generating polynomial of the number of ways to place non-attacking rooks on a generalized form of chessboard.

root.gloss: The single node of a tree that has no parent.

In UNIX terminology, the first user account with complete access to the operating system and its configuration, found at the root of the directory structure; the person who manages accounts on a UNIX system.
The highest directory of a directory structure which may contain both files and subdirectories.
To get root or privileged access on (a computer system or mobile phone), often through bypassing some security mechanism.

root mean square.gloss: The square root of the arithmetic mean of the squares of a set of numbers or values.

root of unity.gloss: An element of a given field (especially, a complex number) x such that for some positive integer n, xⁿ = 1.

root system.gloss: A configuration of vectors in a Euclidean space satisfying certain geometrical properties, fundamental in the theory of Lie groups and Lie algebras.

rooted.gloss: Having a root (superuser) account that has been compromised.

rooted tree.gloss: A tree in which one vertex has been designated as the root.

rooter.gloss: A type of malware that obtains and runs using privileged access, bypassing normal security systems.

rootfinder.gloss: An algorithm for finding roots of an equation.

rootfinding.gloss: The process of finding the root of an equation.

rootless.gloss: Without (the use of) a root user account.

rop.gloss: A Render Output unit or raster operations pipeline.

rope.gloss: A data structure resembling a string, using a concatenation tree in which each leaf represents a character.

rose.gloss: Any of various flower-like polar graphs of sinusoids or their squares.
A graph with only one vertex.

rose curve.gloss: Any plane curve that consists of loops (petals) emanating from a central point.

roster.gloss: A bracketed list that shows the elements of a set.
To show the elements of a set by listing them inside brackets.

rotation.gloss: An operation on a metric space that is a continuous isometry and fixes at least one point.

rotational.gloss: Having non-zero curl somewhere, i.e. not irrotational

rotational symmetry.gloss: The property a shape has when it looks the same after some rotation by a partial turn.

roto-homothety.gloss: The composition of a rotation and a homothety about a common point.

rotoidal.gloss: Having the form of a rotoid

rotoinversion.gloss: The combination of a rotation and an inversion in a point on the axis.

rotopulsator.gloss: Any of a class of solutions to the n-body problem, in a curved space, whose configuration rotates during the motion.

rotor.gloss: A quantity having magnitude, direction, and position.
The set of cells within an oscillator that switch between being alive and dead over the course of the oscillator's period.

rotor machine.gloss: An mixed electronic and mechanical stream cipher composed of a series of wheels, widespread use from the 1920s–1970s.

rotoreflection.gloss: rotation (about an axis) and reflection (in a plane perpendicular to that axis)

rototill.gloss: To make extensive and pervasive changes to a piece of code without altering its functionality.

rototranslation.gloss: Any rigid transformation (Euclidean isometry) that involves rotation and translation

rotozoomer.gloss: An animated visual effect in which a bitmap is scaled and rotated.

rotunda.gloss: A form of cupola that has pentagons rather than squares or rectangles.

rough number.gloss: A k-rough number; a positive integer whose prime factors are all greater than or equal to k.

roulette.gloss: The locus of a point on a plane curve that rolls without slipping along another fixed plane curve.

round.gloss: A rounded relief or cut at an edge, especially an outside edge, added for a finished appearance and to soften sharp edges.

round angle.gloss: An angle of 360 degrees; a full circle.

round off.gloss: To change (a number) to an approximation having fewer significant digits.

round robin.gloss: Senses relating to something with a round shape, or which goes around. A method of making use of several similar subsystems, assigning tasks to each of them in turn (for example, sending data to a destination down several communication links in turn to achieve greater combined speed).

round trip.gloss: The export and eventual reimport of a file, data, etc. without loss of fidelity.

round-trippable.gloss: Able to be exported and later reimported without loss of fidelity.

rounded.gloss: Describing a number that has been changed to its nearest desired value.

rounded down.gloss: Of a real number, converted to an integer by having its fractional component removed.

rounded up.gloss: Of a real number: converted to an integer by having 0.5 added to it, and the result being rounded down.

rounding error.gloss: The difference between the result of a calculation using exact arithmetic and finite-precision, rounded arithmetic.

roundoff.gloss: The act of rounding off a number.

roundtrip.gloss: To export (a file, data, etc.) and eventually import it again without loss of fidelity.

route.gloss: A specific entry in a router that tells the router how to transmit the data it receives.

route redistribution.gloss: The exchange of routing information, on a router, between different routing protocols.

routine.gloss: A set of instructions designed to perform a specific task; a subroutine.

routing.gloss: A method of finding paths from origins to destinations in a network such as the Internet, along which information can be passed.

row echelon form.gloss: The stepped appearance of a matrix that has undergone Gaussian elimination with the result that the leading coefficient or pivot (that is, the first nonzero number from the left) of a nonzero row is to the right of the pivot of the row above it.

row space.gloss: The vector space generated by all the row vectors of a matrix.

row vector.gloss: A 1×n matrix that represents a vector.

row-equivalence.gloss: A relation between two matrices of the same size, such that every row of one matrix is a linear combination of the rows of the other matrix, and vice versa. It is an equivalence relation.

row-reduced.gloss: Said of a matrix which has undergone row reduction; i.e., of a matrix which has a 1 as the leading entry of each one of its non-zero rows and which has zeroes as all the other entries of any column containing such a leading entry (of any non-zero row).

rowmotion.gloss: A certain operation on the order ideals (or antichains) of a finite poset.

rowset.gloss: A set of rows of data.

rowstore.gloss: A database storage method that organizes data by rows, storing all fields of a record together. This design is best for transactional workloads where entire records are frequently accessed or modified.

royalty-free.gloss: Of software, content, or materials, licensed for use after a one-time payment or fee, with no additional royalties required per use, reproduction, or distribution.

rref.gloss: Initialism of reduced row echelon form.

rsa number.gloss: Any of the large semiprime numbers to be factored in the RSA Factoring Challenge, a competition from 1991 to 2007 encouraging research into computational number theory.

rss.gloss: Initialism of residual sum of squares.

rtx.gloss: A brand of graphics processing units developed by Nvidia featuring ray tracing technology.

rubber duck.gloss: To act as a sounding board for a programmer that is debugging their code, facilitating rubber duck debugging.

rubber duck debugging.gloss: The practice in which a programmer attempts to solve a bug by explaining their code to an inanimate object, such as a rubber duck.

rubber-hose cryptanalysis.gloss: The extraction of cryptographic secrets by coercion or torture.

rubberbanding.gloss: A technique in which one point or object moves while attached to another point or object, as when dragging out a new shape in a drawing program.

rubyist.gloss: A user of the Ruby programming language.

rugged.gloss: Designed to reliably operate in harsh usage environments and conditions.

rule.gloss: A determinate method prescribed for performing any operation and producing a certain result.

rule-based.gloss: Based on a series of simple "if-then" rules.

ruled.gloss: Being a scroll; being such that through every point of S there is a straight line that lies on S.

ruled surface directrix.gloss: A guiding curve from which a ruled surface is generated by moving a straight line.

run.gloss: A literal or figurative path or course for movement relating to: The execution of a program or model

run ahead.gloss: To execute (code) in advance, anticipating a likely upcoming need for the result.

run book.gloss: A set of procedures prepared by an administrator for the day-to-day maintenance and exception handling of an IT system; (loosely) such a set of procedures for a job whether IT-specific or not.

run time.gloss: The stage during which a program is executing.
The amount of time during which a program is executing.
A software component designed to support the execution of computer programs.

run-length encoding.gloss: A simple data compression scheme in which sequences of the same item are replaced by one such item and a count (so for example the text BBBBB is stored as a single B with count of 5).

run-time.gloss: Of, relating to, or happening during run time.

runahead.gloss: The speculative execution of code that may or may not be required to execute, so that the results are available in advance if that branch is in fact subsequently taken.

runcic.gloss: Having the vertices of a runcinated polytope.

runcicantellated.gloss: Generated or modified by a runcicantellation.

runcicantellation.gloss: The simultaneous state of runcination and cantellation.

runcicantitruncated.gloss: Generated or modified by a runcicantitruncation.

runcinated.gloss: Generated or modified by a runcination.

runcination.gloss: An operation in any dimension that cuts a regular polytope at its faces, its edges and its vertices, creating a new facet in place of each face, each edge and each vertex.

runcitruncated.gloss: generated or modified by a runcitruncation

runge-kutta method.gloss: Any of an important family of implicit and explicit iterative methods for the approximation of solutions of ordinary differential equations.

runlength.gloss: The length of a sequence of repeated characters in a string

runlevel.gloss: Any of a set of modes of operation in certain operating systems, defining the state of the machine after boot.

running time.gloss: Of an algorithm, the length of time required for it to run as a function, depending on the number of operations executed.

runspace.gloss: In Microsoft PowerShell, an isolated environment in which a script or command executes.

runt.gloss: An Ethernet packet that does not meet the medium's minimum packet size of 64 bytes.

rupert.gloss: Having or relating to the property of being able to pass through a copy of itself.

russian copulation.gloss: A method of rearranging plaintext before encryption by breaking it into two parts and inverting their order, so as to conceal obvious headers, salutations, signatures, etc.

russification.gloss: The process of making anything Russian. Enabling a computer system to work with the Russian Cyrillic alphabet.

rustacean.gloss: A user of the Rust programming language.

rvalue.gloss: Any value that is not an lvalue.

rvalue reference.gloss: In C++, a reference which is bound to an rvalue.

rényi entropy.gloss: A quantity that generalizes various notions of entropy, including Hartley entropy, Shannon entropy, collision entropy, and min-entropy.

s plane.gloss: The complex plane on which Laplace transforms are graphed; a mathematical domain where processes are viewed in the frequency domain rather than the time domain; used as a graphical analysis tool in engineering and physics.

s-box.gloss: A basic component of symmetric-key algorithms, which performs substitution, transforming one set of bits into another.

s-t cut.gloss: A cut that requires the source and the sink to be in different subsets, and its cut-set only consisting of edges going from the source's side to the sink's side.

s.m.a.r.t..gloss: Acronym of self-monitoring, analysis and reporting technology: a monitoring system included in computer HDDs and SSDs in order to detect and report various indicators of drive reliability with the intent of anticipating imminent hardware failures.

saas.gloss: Acronym of software as a service.

saass.gloss: Acronym of software as a self-service.
Acronym of service as a software substitute.

sad number.gloss: Any number that is not a happy number.

saddle.gloss: Something resembling a saddle (sense 1) in appearance or shape. Synonym of saddle point (“a point in the range of a smooth function, every neighbourhood of which contains points on each side of its tangent plane”).

saddle point.gloss: A point in the range of a smooth function, every neighbourhood of which contains points on each side of its tangent plane.
Such a point in the graphical representation of the possible outcomes of a game.

safe.gloss: Of a programming language, type-safe or more generally offering well-defined behavior despite programming errors.

safe mode.gloss: A troubleshooting mode of many operating systems in which most advanced functions are not activated.

safe navigation operator.gloss: A binary operator that returns its second argument, unless the first argument is null, in which case it returns null; used to simplify code that would otherwise need multiple explicit checks for nullity.

safe prime.gloss: A prime number of the form 2p+1, where p is also a prime (the latter is called a Sophie Germain prime).

sagitta.gloss: The distance from a point in a curve to the chord; also, the versed sine of an arc; so called from its resemblance to an arrow resting on the bow and string.

sail curve.gloss: A catenary-generated curve in the form of a cross-section of a sail filled by wind.

sak.gloss: Initialism of secure attention key (such as ctrl+alt+delete for Windows operating systems) (not in general use but used in topic-relevant online discussions).

salami attack.gloss: An attack against a system that consists of many minor actions (such as stealing small amounts of funds from multiple bank accounts) and is thus relatively difficult to detect.

salient.gloss: Denoting any angle less than two right angles.

salinon.gloss: A particular figure bounded by four semicircles.

salt.gloss: A sequence of random data added to plain text data (such as passwords or messages) prior to encryption or hashing, in order to make brute force decryption more difficult.
To add filler bytes before encrypting, in order to make brute-force decryption more resource-intensive.

saltus.gloss: The difference between the right limit and the left limit of a function at a given point.

salvage.gloss: To modify (a false proposition) to create a true proposition.

samegrade.gloss: Synonym of sidegrade (“switch to a different but equivalent product”).

sample.gloss: A subset or portion of a population that is systematically selected for measurement, observation, or questioning, with the objective of generating statistical information that accurately reflects the characteristics of the entire population.
To reduce a continuous signal (such as a sound wave) to a discrete signal.
To make or show something similar to a sample.

sample function.gloss: Any function used to obtain a set of samples from a given population

sample mean.gloss: Given a random sample mathbf x₁,…, mathbf x_N from an n-dimensional random variable mathbf X, a mean defined as

sample path.gloss: Any set of possible values to which the appropriate random variables determined by a stochastic process might map a given point in the sample space, taken over all values of the index space (often regarded as time).

sample point.gloss: A point in the sample space representing some concrete non-decomposable result of an individual experiment.

sample space.gloss: The set of all possible outcomes of a game, experiment or other situation.

samplesize.gloss: The size (number of units) of a sample.

sampling.gloss: The analysis of a group by determining the characteristics of a significant percentage of its members chosen at random.
The measurement, at regular intervals, of the amplitude of a varying waveform in order to convert it to digital form.

sampling error.gloss: The error caused by observing a sample instead of the whole population.

sandbox.gloss: An isolated area where a program can be executed with a restricted portion of the resources available.
To restrict (a program, etc.) by placing it in a sandbox.

sandboxable.gloss: Able to be run in a sandbox (isolated and restricted environment).

sandpile.gloss: Any of several models in which a series of connected nodes interact with their neighbours according to fixed rules.

sandwich testing.gloss: A hybrid form of integration testing that combines top-down and bottom-up approaches.

sanitize.gloss: To filter (text) to ensure it does not contain any characters that will cause problems for or be interpreted in an adverse way by the receiving system.
To remove sensitive or personal data from (a database or file).

sanitizer.gloss: A program to detect errors in code, usually integrated into a compiler.

sargable.gloss: Able to use indexes to speed up execution.

sarmo.gloss: Abbreviation of sense and react to military objects; A technology methodology for automated weapons response.

sash.gloss: A draggable vertical or horizontal bar used to adjust the relative sizes of two adjacent windows.

satellite assembly.gloss: A compiled library file that contains culture-specific resources, such as translated text, images, or audio for a software application without containing any executable code.

satf.gloss: Initialism of shortest access time first, a disk scheduling algorithm or approach

satisfiability.gloss: The property of being able to be satisfied.

satisfy.gloss: To cause (a sentence) to be true when the sentence is interpreted in one's universe.

saturated.gloss: Equal to a union of equivalence classes of ≡; such that if x∈S and x≡y then y∈S.
qualifiers: with respect to an equivalence relation ≡

saturated.gloss: Equal to a union of equivalence classes of ≡; such that if x∈S and x≡y then y∈S. Saturated with respect to the equivalence relation x≡y⟺f(x)=f(y) (the kernel, noun sense 10, of f).
qualifiers: with respect to a function f
with respect to an equivalence relation ≡

saturation.gloss: The smallest set containing S which is saturated with respect to the equivalence relation or function.
qualifiers: with respect to an equivalence relation or function

saturation.gloss: A form of arithmetic in which all operations are limited to a fixed range of values. See Saturation arithmetic.

save.gloss: To put aside; to avoid. To write (a file) to disk or other storage medium.
The act, process, or result of saving data to a storage medium.

save as.gloss: To enter a dialog box where the user can specify a new filename to save the current document under.

save down.gloss: To write a computer file to disk.

savepoint.gloss: A point during a transaction at which changes are committed, and to which the user can roll back if necessary.

savestate.gloss: A file that contains an emulator's or virtualizer's state at the moment it was saved to disk. The file contains the contents of the memory, registers and other pertinent data that allows the user to resume the application from the moment the file was created.

saw tooth.gloss: Describing a function or waveform that consists of repeated triangular transitions when graphed.

sawtooth.gloss: A pattern whose living cell population reaches new peaks infinitely many times before dropping to a fixed value after each peak.

sawtooth wave.gloss: A function or waveform that repeatedly ramps upwards (usually linearly) and then sharply drops.

sbom.gloss: Initialism of software bill of materials, the inventory of components used to build a software artifact.

scada.gloss: Acronym of supervisory control and data acquisition, an electrical network typically containing at least IED's, RTU's, and a master station equipped with an HMI; used to monitor and control process automation systems, such as those used by electrical and water utilities.

scaffolder.gloss: A software tool that creates the basic framework or template for a new project.

scaffolding.gloss: Source code etc. that is incomplete and serves as a basis for further development.

scag.gloss: To destroy the data on a disk, either by corrupting the file system or by causing media damage.

scagnostic.gloss: A heuristic used to automatically analyse variables in a large dataset in order to determine which scatterplots are to be visualised in a scatterplot matrix.

scalable.gloss: Able to greatly increase in capacity, with relative ease.

scalar.gloss: Consisting of a single value (e.g. integer or string) rather than multiple values (e.g. array).
A quantity that has magnitude but not direction.

scalar curl.gloss: The coefficient of k in the three-dimensional curl of a two-dimensional vector field.

scalar field.gloss: A function that assigns a scalar value to every point in space.
The field (algebraic structure) for which scalar multiplication is defined for a given vector space; field of scalars.

scalar function.gloss: Any function whose domain is a vector space and whose value is its scalar field

scalar multiplication.gloss: Multiplication of a vector by a scalar (which belongs to the vector space's field of scalars).
multiplication of a module element by a ring element

scalar product.gloss: The product of two vectors computed as the sum of the corresponding elements of the vectors, or, equivalently, as the product of the magnitudes of the vectors and the cosine of the angle between their directions.

scalar triple product.gloss: The dot product of one of the three vectors with the cross product of the other two.

scalar-valued.gloss: Taking values in K; having codomain K.
qualifiers: of a function on a vector space V over a field K

scale.gloss: To tolerate significant increases in throughput or other potentially limiting factors.

scale invariance.gloss: a feature of objects or laws that do not change if length scales (or energy scales) are multiplied by a common factor.

scale out.gloss: To scale up (a system) by adding more servers or nodes.

scalebound.gloss: Of an object: for which characteristic elements of scale, such as length and width, are few in number and each with a clearly distinct size.

scaled copy.gloss: A copy of a figure in which every length in the original is multiplied by the same scale factor.

scalefree.gloss: Describing any property that is independent of scale.

scalene.gloss: Having sides all unequal in length.

scalene triangle.gloss: A triangle having each of its three sides of different lengths.

scalenohedron.gloss: A polyhedron having twelve sides, each in the form of a scalene triangle, that is topologically equivalent to a hexagonal bipyramid and whose middle section can be said to inscribe a rhombohedron.

scaling.gloss: The expression of the terms of an equation using powers of nondimensional quantities.

scalogram.gloss: A visual representation of a wavelet transform, having axes for time, scale, and coefficient value, analogous to a spectrogram

scamware.gloss: Software that fraudulently fails to do what it is claimed to do.

scan.gloss: To examine sequentially, carefully, or critically; to scrutinize; to behold closely. To inspect, analyse or go over, often to find something.
To look about for; to look over quickly. To perform lexical analysis; to tokenize.
To create an image of something with the use of a scanner.
To read with an electronic device.
The result or output of a scanning process.

scan line.gloss: A single row of pixels in a raster graphics image.

scanbed.gloss: The flat surface of a scanner on which a document is placed to be scanned.

scancode.gloss: A numeric code transmitted by a computer keyboard to indicate which keys are currently being pressed.

scannerless.gloss: Performing tokenization and parsing in a single step, using a single formalism to express both the lexical and the phrase-level structure of the language.

scanout.gloss: The conversion of image data in computer memory to a series of lines for output to a raster display.

scareware.gloss: Software that attempts to scare the user into compliance, as by displaying false warnings of virus infection.

scatter plot.gloss: A type of display using Cartesian coordinates to display values for two variables for a set of data.

scatter/gather.gloss: Being or relating to a form of I/O by which a single procedure call sequentially writes data from multiple buffers to a single data stream, or reads data from a stream into multiple buffers.

scea.gloss: Initialism of Sun Certified Enterprise Architect.

scedastic.gloss: related to the variance of (statistical) errors

scedasticity.gloss: The distribution of error terms. Error terms are distributed either randomly and with constant variance (homoscedasticity) or with some kind of pattern (heteroscedasticity).

scenegraph.gloss: A data structure representing a graphical scene.

schedule.gloss: An allocation or ordering of a set of tasks on one or several resources.

scheduler.gloss: An operating system component responsible for allocating several resources, most commonly the use of processors by different concurrent processes or threads.

schelling point.gloss: Synonym of focal point (“solution used in the absence of communication”).

schema.gloss: A formal description of the structure of a database: the names of the tables, the names of the columns of each table, and the data type and other attributes of each column.

A formula in the metalanguage of an axiomatic system, in which one or more schematic variables appear, which stand for any term or subformula of the system, which may or may not be required to satisfy certain conditions.

schematic variable.gloss: A variable that appears in an axiom schema and ranges over formulas, distinguished from the variables of the axiom schema that are quantified over and that range over the individuals of the universe of discourse.

scheme.gloss: A mathematical structure that generalizes the notion of an algebraic variety in several ways, such as taking account of multiplicities and allowing "varieties" defined over any commutative ring. Formally, a locally ringed space that admits a covering by open sets, each of which is isomorphic to an affine scheme (i.e. the spectrum of some commutative ring).

scheme theory.gloss: The branch of mathematics that concerns schemes (locally ringed spaces admitting coverings by open sets, each isomorphic to the spectrum of some commutative ring).

schemer.gloss: A person who programs in Scheme.

schemoid.gloss: A generalization of an association scheme from the point of view of small categories.

schensted insertion.gloss: The insertion step of the Schensted algorithm.

schiffler point.gloss: A certain type of triangle center. A triangle △ABC with the incenter I has its Schiffler point at the point of concurrence of the Euler lines of the four triangles △BCI, △CAI, △ABI, △ABC.

schizophrenic number.gloss: An irrational number with persistent patterns in its decimal expansion that give it the appearance of a rational number.

schlegel diagram.gloss: A projection of a polytope from n-dimensional space to n-1 dimensions through a point beyond one of its faces; especially such a projection (itself represented in 2 dimensions) of a 3- or 4-dimensional polytope.

schlicht.gloss: univalent (analytic and one-to-one) in a given region, sometimes qualified with the stipulation that the function is 0 at 0 and has a slope there equal to 1 (see Koebe function)

schlockware.gloss: Software that is of shoddy or inferior quality.

schläfli double six.gloss: A configuration of 30 points and 12 lines. The lines can be partitioned into two subsets of six: each line is disjoint from (skew with) the lines in its own subset of six lines, and intersects all but one of the lines in the other subset of six lines. Each of the 12 lines of the configuration contains five intersection points, and each of these 30 intersection points belongs to exactly two lines, one from each subset.

schläfli symbol.gloss: A notation that recursively encodes certain properties of a specified regular polytope or tessellation.

scholium.gloss: A note added to a proof as amplification.

schroedinbug.gloss: A software bug which begins to manifest only when somebody debugging the code finds out that it should not work at all.

schröder number.gloss: The number of possible lattice paths from the southwest corner (0, 0) of an n × n grid to the northeast corner (n, n), using only single steps north, northeast or east, and not rising above the southwest–northeast diagonal.

schubert calculus.gloss: A branch of algebraic geometry concerned with solving certain types of counting problem in projective geometry; a symbolic calculus used to represent and solve such problems.

schur decomposition.gloss: A matrix decomposition allowing one to write complex square matrices as similar to a triangular matrix whose diagonal elements are the eigenvalues of the original matrix.

schur function.gloss: A holomorphic function in the Schur class.

schwarz lantern.gloss: A polyhedral approximation to a cylinder (formed by stacked rings of isosceles triangles, arranged within each ring in the same pattern as an antiprism), used as a pathological example of the difficulty of defining the area of a smooth (curved) surface as the limit of the areas of polyhedra.

schwarz-christoffel mapping.gloss: A conformal map of the upper half-plane or the complex unit disk onto the interior of a simple polygon; used in minimal surfaces, hyperbolic art, and fluid dynamics.

schönhardt polyhedron.gloss: The simplest non-convex polyhedron that cannot be triangulated into tetrahedra without adding new vertices.

scientific calculator.gloss: An electronic calculator that can handle trigonometric, exponential and often other advanced functions, and can show its output in scientific notation and sometimes in hexadecimal, octal or binary.

scientific computing.gloss: The use of computing to solve scientific and engineering problems, especially by means of simulation, or the construction of mathematical models of physical, chemical or biological processes

scientific notation.gloss: a method of writing, or of displaying real numbers as a decimal number between 1 and 10 followed by an integer power of 10
an alternative format of such a decimal number immediately followed by E and an integer

scissor congruence.gloss: The property of two polygons that have the property of being decomposable into finitely many polygons that are pairwise congruent.

scjd.gloss: Initialism of Sun Certified Java Developer.

scjp.gloss: Initialism of Sun Certified Java Programmer.

scleronomic.gloss: Of a mechanical system whose constraint equations do not explicitly contain or are not dependent upon time.

scleronomy.gloss: A mechanical system whose constraint equations do not explicitly contain or are not dependent upon time.

scmp.gloss: Initialism of software configuration management plan.

scope.gloss: The region of program source code in which a given identifier is meaningful, or a given object can be accessed.
The shortest sub-wff of which a given instance of a logical connective is a part.
To limit (an object or variable) to a certain region of program source code.

scope block.gloss: the region of a computer program where a name binding is valid

scoped enumeration.gloss: In C++, an enumeration that automatically defines its own name as a scope.

scoping.gloss: the act of adding a scope

scorefile.gloss: A file containing criteria for assigning a score to each email message received, for purposes of filtering out spam, etc.

scott topology.gloss: A topology on a partially ordered set, consisting of the Scott-open subsets of that set.

scott-continuous.gloss: Given two partially ordered sets P and Q, a function f: P → Q between them is Scott-continuous if it preserves all directed suprema.

scott-open.gloss: Of a subset O of a partially ordered set P: such that it is an upper set and is inaccessible by directed joins, i.e. all directed sets D with supremum in O have non-empty intersection with O.

scrape.gloss: To extract data by automated means from a format not intended to be machine-readable, such as a screenshot or a formatted web page.

scraper.gloss: A program or process that scrapes data, such as a screen-scraper.

scraping.gloss: Automated collection of data, data scraping.

scratch.gloss: Relating to a scratchpad, a data structure or recording medium attached to a machine for testing or temporary use.

scratch tape.gloss: A tape that is only temporarily needed for data storage and that can therefore be reused.

scratcher.gloss: A user of the Scratch visual programming language.

scratchpad.gloss: A piece of temporary memory to hold details of a current conversation, usually scratchpad memory.

screaming snake case.gloss: The practice of writing identifiers in all caps using underscores to separate words.

scree plot.gloss: A graph of the eigenvalues of factors

screen.gloss: A surface on which various forms or formats of information are displayed. The visualised data or imagery displayed on a computer screen.

screen mask.gloss: A tool that follows the mouse or touch input and helps eliminate distractions on a page.
A protective layer that guards against dust and moisture in an LED display.

screen memory.gloss: A portion of computer memory storing the graphics currently displayed on the screen.

screen motion capture.gloss: The digital recording, by software, of a moving image displayed upon a screen in order to allow manipulation and playback.

screen name.gloss: a string of characters used to identify a user of a bulletin board, e-mail etc; a pseudonym used for online communication.

screen of death.gloss: A screen or a message indicating an unrecoverable error or failure.

screen reader.gloss: A software application that speaks aloud information from a computer display, for users with impaired vision.

screen scraping.gloss: A form of web scraping in which a program visually captures and processes data from a webpage.

screen share.gloss: To transmit the content of one's computer screen (or a portion of it) to another device.

screen tearing.gloss: A phenomenon where the image on a screen appears to horizontally "tear" in two due to lack of synchronization between the video feed and the display's refresh rate.

screen-scrape.gloss: To extract data from (a source such as a webpage) by picking it out from among the human-readable content.

screen-scraper.gloss: A piece of software that screen-scrapes.

screenlet.gloss: A visual widget or small application that can be placed on the desktop.

screenname.gloss: a string of characters used to identify a user of a bulletin board, e-mail etc; a pseudonym used for online communication.

screensaver.gloss: A computer program that displays aesthetic patterns or images when the computer is not being used, originally intended to prevent screenburn.

screenshot.gloss: An image of computer or smartphone screen output at a given moment in time.
To take a screenshot of something.

screenshottable.gloss: Of which a screenshot may be taken.

screenshotter.gloss: A computer program that takes screenshots.

screenspace.gloss: The space available on a screen display.

screw.gloss: A straight line in space with which a definite linear magnitude termed the pitch is associated. It is used to express the displacement of a rigid body, which may always be made to consist of a rotation about an axis combined with a translation parallel to that axis.

script.gloss: A file containing a list of user commands, allowing them to be invoked once to execute in sequence.

script editor.gloss: A software program or feature for editing source code.

script monkey.gloss: A hacker who has no talent other than for using other people's scripts.

script out.gloss: To simplify or automate a process using scripts (a file containing a list of user commands, allowing them to be invoked once to execute in sequence).

scriptability.gloss: The ability to be driven programmatically as well as interactively.

scriptable.gloss: That can be extended or automated through scripting.
Something that can be extended or automated through scripting.

scripter.gloss: A programmer who uses a scripting language.

scriptlet.gloss: A small script, especially a section of Java code embedded in JavaServer Pages code.

scroll.gloss: The incremental movement of graphics on a screen, removing one portion to show the next.
To change one's view of data on a computer's display by moving in gradual increments, typically using an input device or touch screen.

scroll bar.gloss: A graphical widget in the form of a horizontal or vertical bar, on the edges of a personal computer screen, that is used to move scrollable text or images.

scroll lock.gloss: A key on a standard extended keyboard, originally causing the arrow keys to scroll a window rather than moving a cursor, now sometimes used for other purposes.

scroll wheel.gloss: A hard plastic or rubbery disc on a computer mouse, used for scrolling.

scrollable.gloss: of text or images on a screen, that may be moved by the user to bring other parts of them into view

scrollback.gloss: The part of a scrolling display that precedes the current line or section.

scrolling.gloss: The continuous movement of text or images on a display screen in either a horizontal or vertical direction.

scrolltext.gloss: Text displayed in an animated scrolling message, common in early demos.

scrolly.gloss: A scrolling message, especially one used in a demo to convey news, commentary, greetings, etc.

scrub.gloss: To eliminate or remove (something); to render (something) unretrievable. To eliminate or correct (data) from a set of records to bring it inline with other similar datasets.

scrubber.gloss: A horizontal bar allowing the user to set the playback position.

scrum.gloss: In agile software development (specifically Scrum or related methodologies), a daily meeting in which each developer describes what they have been doing, what they plan to do next, and any impediments to progress.

scrum master.gloss: In the Scrum framework, a facilitator of a developer team, who is accountable for removing impediments to the ability of the team to deliver the product goals and deliverables.

scsu.gloss: Initialism of Standard Compression Scheme for Unicode.

sculpt.gloss: A modification that can be applied to an object, like a texture, but changes the object's shape rather than its appearance.

scutoidal.gloss: Of, pertaining to, or having the shape of a scutoid.

sd-wan.gloss: Acronym of software-defined wide area network.

sdhc card.gloss: A type of flash memory card with storage capacities ranging from 4 to 32 gigabytes.

sdr.gloss: Initialism of system of distinct representatives.

sdv.gloss: Initialism of software-defined vehicle / software-driven vehicle.

seadrone.gloss: A robotic drone boat capable of operating on the open seas. They may be optionally crewed, remotely controlled, or, autonomous.

seam carving.gloss: A technique for resizing images so as to preserve the main contents by selectively removing less important regions, as defined by "seams" (approximately horizontal or vertical paths of pixels).

search and replace.gloss: A function in text editors and word processors where a string of characters is replaced by another.

search as you type.gloss: An autocomplete feature when used to search for something.

search box.gloss: A text box for the input of text to be searched for in a database, on the Internet, etc.

search engine.gloss: An application that searches for, and retrieves, data based on some criteria, especially one that searches the Internet for documents containing specified words.

search history.gloss: A record of one's queries for a search engine.

search result.gloss: A hyperlink generated by a search engine in response to a query.

search space.gloss: The set of all possible points of an optimization problem that satisfy the problem's targets or goals.

search term.gloss: The word or phrase that a user searches for, e.g. in a search engine.

search tree.gloss: A tree (data structure) set up to facilitate searching.

search-engine.gloss: To look up on a search engine.
To use a search engine; to look things up on a search engine.

search-oriented architecture.gloss: A software-architectural approach that is focused on a search engine.

searchability.gloss: The extent to which, or ease with which something may be searched.

seasonalize.gloss: To offset (data) to compensate for seasonal variations.

secant.gloss: A straight line that intersects a curve at two or more points.
In a right triangle, the reciprocal of the cosine of an angle. Symbol: sec

secant method.gloss: An iterative numerical method for finding a root of an equation f(x)=0, using a succession of roots of secant lines to better approximate the root.

second derivative.gloss: The derivative of the derivative of a function.

second normal form.gloss: A stage in the normalization of a relational database in which it is in first normal form and every non-key attribute is dependent upon the entire primary key.

second preimage attack.gloss: An attack on a cryptographic hash function that is able to find a second preimage for a hash and its preimage; that is, given a hash and an input that has that specific hash, it is able to find (faster than by brute force) another input with the same hash.

second-class continuation.gloss: A type of continuation whose use is limited or restricted and that cannot be stored, passed around, etc. as freely as other types of value.

second-class object.gloss: An entity of which the value can be passed as a parameter, but that can neither be returned from a function, nor be assigned to a variable. (Used by Raphael Finkel, the first-class object does not need to have run-time constructability according to his definition.)

second-countable.gloss: Such that its topology has a countable base, said of a topological space.

second-level domain.gloss: A domain that is immediately subordinate to a top-level domain (whose name appears after it, with a period separating the two).

second-order.gloss: Denoting the second in a numerical sequence of models, languages, relationships, forms of logical discourse etc.

secondary storage.gloss: The nonvolatile memory of a computer, not directly accessible by the central processing unit.

secret sharing.gloss: Any method for distributing a secret amongst a group of participants, each of whom is allocated a share; the secret can be reconstructed only when a sufficient number of shares (possibly of different types) are combined.

secretary problem.gloss: The problem of selecting the best out of n applicants for a position, under the condition that all applicants are interviewed in random order, the quality of the applicants is not known before interviewing, and once rejected an applicant cannot be recalled.

section.gloss: A cross-section (image that shows an object as if cut along a plane). A function that generalizes the notion of the graph of a function; formally, a continuous right inverse to the projection map of a fiber bundle.
A cross-section (image that shows an object as if cut along a plane). A right inverse of a morphism in some category

sector.gloss: Part of a circle, extending to the center; circular sector.
A portion of a sphere or ball defined by a conical boundary with apex at the center of the sphere.
A fixed-sized unit (traditionally 512 bytes) of sequential data stored on a track of a digital medium.

securable.gloss: A resource that can be secured.

secure by design.gloss: designed from the ground up to be secure

security system.gloss: A similar software system that prevents unauthorised access.

sedenion.gloss: A 16-dimensional nonalternative extension of an octonion with one real part and 15 imaginary parts, each a real multiple of a distinct, independent square root of −1.

see.gloss: Initialism of single-event effect (a temporary or permanent fault caused by an ionizing radiation particle or ray striking a computer chip).

seed.gloss: The initial state, condition or position of a changing, growing or developing process; the ultimate precursor in a defined chain of precursors. The initialization state of a pseudorandom number generator or similar system.

seed number.gloss: Synonym of seed (“generation”); a pseudorandom number generator or a code that generates a game's world or environment.

seeder.gloss: A process that seeds a random number generator.

seek.gloss: To move to a specified location (particularly of a disk drive or similar device).
To navigate through a data stream.
The operation of navigating through a stream.

seek time.gloss: The measurement of time required for the head assembly on the actuator arm of a hard drive to travel to the track of the disk where the data will be read or written.

seekable.gloss: Through which one can seek back and forth; not purely sequential.

segfault.gloss: To cause or experience a segmentation fault.

segment.gloss: A portion. A straight path between two points that is the shortest distance between them; a line segment.
A portion. The part of a circle between its circumference and a chord (usually other than the diameter).
A portion. The part of a sphere cut off by a plane.
A portion. Any of the pieces that constitute an order tree.
A region of memory or a fragment of an executable file designated to contain a particular part of a program.

segment descriptor.gloss: A part of the segmentation unit, used for translating a logical address to a linear address.

segment tree.gloss: A data structure that is used to store information about intervals (segments) and perform range queries, or queries on a set of intervals, in logarithmic time.

segmentation fault.gloss: A software error that occurs when a program attempts to access a memory location that it is not permitted to access.

seifert fiber space.gloss: A fiber bundle whose fiber is the circle and whose base space is a two-dimensional orbifold.

seifert fibered space.gloss: Alternative spelling of Seifert fiber space.

seifert fibre space.gloss: Alternative spelling of Seifert fiber space.

seifert fibred space.gloss: Alternative spelling of Seifert fiber space.

sel.gloss: Initialism of single-event latchup (a destructive internal short circuit produced by a particle of ionizing radiation striking a CMOS computer chip).

selberg sieve.gloss: A technique for estimating the size of sifted sets of positive integers that satisfy a set of conditions expressed by congruences.

select.gloss: To obtain a set of data from a database using a query.

selectable.gloss: An item that can be selected by the user.

selection.gloss: A set of data obtained from a database using a query.
A list of items on which user operations will take place.
A unary operation that denotes a subset of a relation.
The stage of a genetic algorithm in which individual genomes are chosen from a population for later breeding.

selection sort.gloss: A sorting algorithm that divides the input list into two sublists — items already sorted, and items not yet sorted — and gradually transfers elements from one list to the other.

selector.gloss: A matching expression in a stylesheet determining which elements in the markup are affected by a style.
A pointer to a structure describing a segment of memory.

self-affinity.gloss: The condition of a fractal whose pieces are scaled by different amounts in the x and y directions, so that self-similarity becomes apparent only after an anisotropic transformation.

self-balancing.gloss: Of a data structure: able to maintain a small height (number of levels) regardless of insertions and deletions.

self-commutator.gloss: Given a bounded linear operator B and its adjoint B^*, the self-commutator is B^*B-BB^*.

self-contradiction.gloss: A statement that contains a contradiction, or a premise from which one could be derived.

self-delete.gloss: Of code, to overwrite itself upon completion, usually with 0x00 or 0xFF bytes that represent an unwritten region.

self-documenting.gloss: Written and structured in such a way that it can be understood without consulting separate documentation.

self-dual.gloss: Of a vector space, isomorphic to its dual space.
Of a proposition that is equivalent to its dual.
Of a graph or polyhedron, being the dual of itself.

self-elevation.gloss: elevation of one's own user privilege level (usually to run software that requires a higher privilege level)

self-encrypting.gloss: Automatically encrypting data without user intervention.

self-evaluation.gloss: The property of constants to be evaluated immediately as their respective values without further look up or transformation.

self-executing.gloss: Consisting of a complete executable package that takes some action with the included data, rather than a pure data file requiring some additional tool to read it.

self-hosting.gloss: Of software: capable of generating new versions of itself.

self-interpreter.gloss: A metacircular interpreter where the host programming language is also the language being interpreted.

self-selection.gloss: A form of nonprobability sampling bias in which individuals select themselves into a group.

self-signed.gloss: Of a security certificate: signed by the same entity whose identity it certifies; signed with its own private key.

self-signing.gloss: The use of self-signed security certificates.

selfdistributive.gloss: Having the property (of an operation) of being distributive with respect to itself. Thus, an operator ◦ is left selfdistributive iff x◦(y◦z) = (x◦y)◦(x◦z), and is right selfdistributive iff (x◦y)◦z = (x◦z)◦(y◦z), for all x, y, z.

selfinjective.gloss: injective with itself (in a higher dimension)

sem.gloss: Initialism of standard error of the mean.

semacode.gloss: A machine-readable two-dimensional barcode used primarily to code website addresses.

semantic analysis.gloss: The phase in which a compiler adds semantic information to the parse tree and builds the symbol table.

semantic versioning.gloss: A versioning scheme where each release is given a three-part version number of the form major.minor.patch. The major number is incremented to indicate a breaking change, minor for new non-breaking features, and patch for other non-breaking changes.

semantic-oriented programming.gloss: A software paradigm where code is defined, parsed, and executed based on its underlying meaning or intent rather than rigid syntax.

semantics.gloss: The meaning of computer language constructs, in contrast to their form or syntax.

semaphore.gloss: A bit, token, fragment of code, or some other mechanism which is used to restrict access to a shared function or device to a single process at a time, or to synchronize and coordinate events in different processes.

semi-complete.gloss: of or pertaining to a graph in which, for any two vertices u, v in the graph, there is another vertex w which is adjacent to both u and v (i.e. u,w,v is a path in that graph).

semi-decidable.gloss: Of a set, such that there is a deterministic algorithm such that (a) if an element is a member of the set, the algorithm halts with the result "positive", and (b) if an element is not a member of the set, (i) the algorithm does not halt, or (ii) if it does, then with the result "negative".

semi-infinite.gloss: Involving a finite number of variables but an infinite number of constraints, or vice versa.

semi-markov process.gloss: A generalization of the Markov chain in which the distribution of the amount of time that the process spends in a given state is permitted to be nonexponentially (generally) distributed.

semi-naive.gloss: Predominantly naive but including modifications that improve efficiency.

semi-norm.gloss: A function denoted ∥v∥ that maps a vector v to a non-negative value such that ∥cv∥ = |c|.∥v∥, where c is a scalar, and ∥v + w∥ ≤ ∥v∥ + ∥w∥ (the triangle inequality); the condition that ∥v∥ = 0 implies that v = 0 is not required, but when it holds, the semi-norm is a norm.

semi-transitive.gloss: Such that there exists a finite vertex set so that for any vertex there exists another vertex in that finite set and an injective homomorphism of the graph that maps the second vertex to the first vertex.

semialgebra.gloss: A class that is closed under intersection and semiclosed under set difference

semialgebraic.gloss: Describing any algebraic system in which only real roots are investigated.

semiample.gloss: Having a positive multiple that is generated by global sections.

semiangle.gloss: an angle of half a given size

semiartinian.gloss: Of a module _RM: such that, for every M→N epimorphism, where N≠0, the socle of N is essential in N.

semiautomaton.gloss: a multiplicative operation of a monoid on a set

semiaxis.gloss: A line segment, joining the centre of a figure to an edge, that forms half of an axis of symmetry.

semibent.gloss: Having a Walsh transform that contains only the values {0, ±2(n+1)/2}, when n is odd.

semibounded.gloss: Having either an upper or a lower bound, but not both

semicalibrated.gloss: A condition where a differential form on a Riemannian manifold satisfies certain properties related to calibration.

semiclairvoyant.gloss: Relating to a form of parallel processing algorithm given approximate advance information about the problem, but not fully clairvoyant.

semicoercive.gloss: Continuous and symmetric but with a nonzero kernel.

semicomputable.gloss: Semidecidable (for decision problems), can be approximated from either above or below by a computable function (for optimization and numerical problems).

semiconcentric.gloss: Having the form of concentric semicircles

semiconjugate.gloss: Describing each of the equal line segments into which the conjugate axis of a hyperbola is divided by the centre of symmetry

semiconnected.gloss: Containing a directed path from u to v or a directed path from v to u for every pair of vertices u, v.

semicontinuous.gloss: (of a function) That it is continuous almost everywhere, except at certain points at which it is either upper semi-continuous or lower semi-continuous.

semiconvergent.gloss: A kind of fraction. If (h_n-1)/(k_n-1), (h_n)/(k_n) are successive convergents, then any fraction of the form (h_n-1+ah_n)/(k_n-1+ak_n), where a is a nonnegative integer and the numerators and denominators are between the n and n+1 terms inclusive, is a semiconvergent.
For which the limit lim _(k→∞) bold Tᵏ exists.

semiconvex.gloss: Having the property that for every compact subset of the domain, there exists a constant C such that f(x) + ½C|x|² is convex on the subset.

semicoroutine.gloss: A type of coroutine with limited control over its execution flow that can yield values multiple times, suspending its execution and allowing the caller to resume it later. However, unlike full coroutines, semicoroutines do not specify where the execution will continue after yielding; control is always returned to the caller.

semicovariant.gloss: A covariant form of a cumulant

semicovering.gloss: A projection that has the property that for any projection onto its image, it is possible to find a corresponding projection onto its domain such that locally constant regions about a point projected onto the image have locally constant images in the domain.

semicreative.gloss: A type of set of natural numbers, related to mathematical logic.

semicritical.gloss: Related to a differential equation and its criticoids.

semicubical.gloss: Of or relating to the square root of the cube of a quantity.

semicuspidal.gloss: Pertaining to a singularity that is not smooth.

semicyclic.gloss: Describing a polygon that is inscribed within a circle and has one of its sides being the diameter

semidecidability.gloss: Alternative spelling of semi-decidability (“property of being semi-decidable”).

semidefinite.gloss: Describing a bilinear form, over a vector space, that is either always nonnegative or always nonpositive.

semidirect.gloss: That has the nature of, or has a nature that derives from or is analogous to, a semidirect product.

semidirect product.gloss: A generalisation of direct product such that, in one of two equivalent definitions, only one of the subgroups involved is required to be a normal subgroup.

semielliptic.gloss: In the theory of partial differential equations, designating a partial differential operator satisfying a positivity condition slightly weaker than that of being an elliptic operator. This produces a curved line progressively slightly straighter than an ellipse, such as that of an automotive leaf spring.

semifactual.gloss: A conditional with a false antecedent and a true consequent.

semifield.gloss: An algebraic structure with two binary operations, addition and multiplication, similar to the field but with some axioms relaxed.

semifinite.gloss: (Of a measure space) in which every nonzero measurable set has a subset with finite nonzero measure

semiflat.gloss: Having the property that, given a morphism (f: X→Y), for every point y in Y, the fiber over y behaves like a flat family of schemes over the base (Y).

semiflow.gloss: A form of matrix annuler in a Petri net.

semigroup.gloss: Any set for which there is a binary operation that is closed and associative.

semigroup homomorphism.gloss: a function that preserves semigroup structure

semigroupoid.gloss: A form of partial algebra in category theory.

semiheap.gloss: A variety of heap that is required to satisfy only the para-associative law and need not obey the identity law.

semihereditary.gloss: Of a ring: hereditary for finitely generated submodules.

semihypergroup.gloss: Any hypergroup for which the reproduction axiom is valid.

semijoin.gloss: A type of join in relational algebra, denoted by ⋉ or ⋊.

semilattice.gloss: A partially ordered set that either has a join (a least upper bound) for any nonempty finite subset (a join-semilattice or upper semilattice) or has a meet (or greatest lower bound) for any nonempty finite subset (a meet-semilattice or lower semilattice). Equivalently, an underlying set which has a binary operation which is associative, commutative, and idempotent.

semilength.gloss: The value of n for a Dyck path that begins at the origin (0,0) and ends at the coordinate (2n,0).

semilinear.gloss: Describing equations involving both linear and nonlinear objects
Having characteristics intermediate between linear and nonlinear

semilocal.gloss: Describing a ring that has a finite number of maximal ideals

semilogarithmic.gloss: Having one logarithmic scale and one arithmetic/linear scale.

semiloopoid.gloss: A nonassociative generalization of a semigroupoid

semilow.gloss: Such that there exists a nonempty intersection (with another set) that is low.

semimajor.gloss: Of or pertaining to the semimajor axis, the long axis of an ellipse

semimajor axis.gloss: Half of the major axis of a circle or ellipse.
Half of the distances between the two branches of a hyperbola.

semimartingale.gloss: A form of probability process that is the sum of a martingale and another form of process

semimean.gloss: Pertaining to half the length of the middle axis on an ellipse (halfway between the major and minor axes).
The result obtained by taking either the largest or smallest half of the values and calculating the mean.

semimeasure.gloss: A function that assigns a non-negative number to each element of a set that is subadditive.

semimeridian.gloss: The intersection of a surface of revolution and a half-plane through its centre

semimetric.gloss: A metric that does not satisfy the triangle inequality

semiminor.gloss: Describing each of the two segments of the minor axis of a conic section at both sides of the center of the conic section.

semiminor axis.gloss: Half of the minor axis of a circle or ellipse.

semimodule.gloss: A mathematical construct that resembles a module, except that the underlying abelian group is replaced with an abelian semigroup, so the elements do not necessarily have inverses.

seminormal.gloss: Being a commutative reduced ring in which, whenever x, y satisfy x³=y², there is s with s²=x and s³=y.
Of a subgroup A of a group G, having a subgroup B such that AB = G, and for any proper subgroup C of B, AC is a proper subgroup of G.

seminumerical.gloss: Having some aspects that are numerical and others that are not.

semiorder.gloss: A type of order that is not wholly comparable

semiordinate.gloss: Half a chord bisected by the transverse diameter of a conic.

semiorthogonal.gloss: Having the property that every subcategory is in the set of orthogonal subcategories of every higher order subcategory.
Either columnwise orthogonal (having the property that M'M is an identity matrix) or rowwise orthogonal (having the property that MM' is an identity matrix).

semiparabola.gloss: One branch of a parabola, terminating at the principal vertex of the curve.

semiparabolic.gloss: Having the form of a semiparabola.

semiparametric.gloss: Having some, but not all, components that are parametric

semipartial.gloss: Being or relating to a form of partial correlation that holds the third variable constant for either X or Y but (unlike a partial correlation) not both.

semiperfect.gloss: Of a ring over which every finitely generated left module has a projective cover.
Of an integer equal to the sum of all or some of its proper divisors.

semiperfect number.gloss: A number which is the sum of some, or all, of its proper divisors.

semiperimeter.gloss: Half of the perimeter (sum of the lengths of the sides) of a polygon. The term is typically applied to triangles, cyclic quadrilaterals, and regular polygons.

semipermutable.gloss: That commutes with every subgroup whose order is relatively prime to its own.

semipositive.gloss: Having a dual that is nonnegative.
Having all elements nonnegative where at least one is positive.

semipositone.gloss: an eigenvalue problem that would be a positone eigenvalue problem except that the nonlinear function is not positive when its argument is zero.

semiprimality.gloss: The condition of being a semiprime

semiprime.gloss: A natural number that is the product of two (not necessarily distinct) prime numbers.
That has properties derived directly or by extension from a semiprime.

semiprimitive.gloss: In a technical sense, described by its simple modules. Formally: Having trivial Jacobson radical.

semiprojection.gloss: A function f of rank k, where k is greater than or equal to three, such that for some index i between one and k (inclusive), f(x₁, x₂, ... xₖ) = xᵢ whenever |{x₁, x₂, ... xₖ}| < k.

semiqueen.gloss: A queen (chess piece) that can only move or attack in one (but not the opposing) direction

semiregular.gloss: Whose regular open sets form a base.
Uniform (isogonal and isotoxal) with regular faces of two or more types, such that each vertex is surrounded by the same polygons in the same order.
qualifiers: of a polyhedron or tessellation of the plane

semiregular polyhedron.gloss: A polyhedron whose faces are all regular polygons, two or more having a different amount of sides, and each vertex having the same arrangement of polygons.

semiregular tessellation.gloss: A tessellation of the plane by two or more different convex regular polygons.

semireliable.gloss: Partly or somewhat reliable; having a fair degree of reliability.

semiring.gloss: An algebraic structure similar to a ring, but without the requirement that each element must have an additive inverse.

semiset.gloss: In set theory, a semiset is a proper class that is a subclass of a set.

semisimple.gloss: In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. Containing a collection of simple objects such that all objects in the category are direct sums of these simple objects.
In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. In which each submodule is a direct summand; equivalently, equal to a direct sum of simple submodules.
In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. Semisimple as a module over itself; equivalently, such that all (left) modules are semisimple.

In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. Semisimple as a module over itself; equivalently, such that all (left) modules are semisimple. Semiprimitive: having trivial Jacobson radical.

In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. For which every invariant subspace has an invariant complement, equivalent to the minimal polynomial being squarefree.
In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. Being a direct sum of simple Lie algebras.
In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. Being a direct sum of simple representations (also known as irreducible representations).
qualifiers: of a linear representation of a group or algebra

semisimple.gloss: In any of several technical senses, decomposable into sub-objects that have a simple structure. Being a linear algebraic group whose radical of the identity component is trivial.

semispace.gloss: Either of two regions making up a space.

semisquare.gloss: A right isocoles triangle, or such figure of which two form a square.

semistable.gloss: Describing a form of elliptic curve having congruent roots

semistandard.gloss: Of a Young tableau: having the entries weakly increasing along each row and strictly increasing down each column.

semistationary.gloss: Having the same properties over time, although possibly showing different behavior in stability intervals.

semistrict.gloss: Having some, but not all, characteristics of a strict system, category etc.
