semisum.gloss: half the result of an addition

semisymmetrization.gloss: The act or process of making semisymmetric

semitangent.gloss: The tangent of half an arc.

semitopological.gloss: Having a topology such that, for each c in G, the two functions G → G defined by x↦xc and x↦cx are continuous.

semitotalistic.gloss: Totalistic only on the outer planes.

semivalue.gloss: A function on a vector space of all coalitional games which verifies linearity, anonymity, positivity, and inessential games.

semivariance.gloss: A measure of the dispersion of those values that fall below the mean or target value of a data set

semivariation.gloss: Variation that only considers certain parts of a function or a stochastic process, typically focusing on only the positive or only the negative changes rather than all changes.

semivariogram.gloss: A function of the spatial dependence of semivariance; a graph of this function.

send.gloss: An icon (usually on a computer screen and labeled with the word "Send") on which one clicks (with a mouse or its equivalent) or taps to transmit an email or other electronic message.
Alternative letter-case form of send (email icon)

sense.gloss: One of two opposite directions in which a vector (especially of motion) may point. See also polarity.
One of two opposite directions of rotation, clockwise versus anti-clockwise.

sensitivity.gloss: The probability, in a binary classification test, of a true positive being correctly identified.

sentence.gloss: A formula with no free variables.
Any of the set of strings that can be generated by a given formal grammar.

sentiment analysis.gloss: The use of computers to process natural language in an attempt to identify and extract information about the writer's affective state.

sentinel.gloss: A unique value recognised by a computer program for processing in a special way, or marking the end of a set of data.

separable.gloss: Able to be brought to a form where all occurrences of the dependent and the independent variable are on opposite sides of the equal sign.
Any of several technical senses relating to the behavior of polynomials or objects over which polynomials can be defined: Having no repeated roots (where roots are considered in an algebraic closure)

Any of several technical senses relating to the behavior of polynomials or objects over which polynomials can be defined: Having no repeated roots (where roots are considered in an algebraic closure) Such that none of the irreducible factors of P have a repeated root.

Any of several technical senses relating to the behavior of polynomials or objects over which polynomials can be defined: Such that the minimal polynomial of every element of E is a separable polynomial.
qualifiers: of an algebraic field extension E/F

separable.gloss: Any of several technical senses relating to the behavior of polynomials or objects over which polynomials can be defined: Satisfying any of several technical conditions on the center of the algebra which generalize the situation of field extensions; see Separable algebra on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
qualifiers: of an algebra over a ring

separable extension.gloss: A finite (and thereby algebraic) extension of a base field such that every element of the extension is the root of a separable polynomial over the base field.

separable polynomial.gloss: A polynomial over a given field that has distinct roots in the algebraic closure of said field (the number of roots being equal to the degree of the polynomial).

separate.gloss: A printing of an article from a periodical as its own distinct publication and distributed independently, often with different page numbers.

separation constant.gloss: a constant that may be introduced upon separation of variables

separation of concerns.gloss: The process of separating a computer program into distinct features that overlap functionally as little as possible.

separatrix.gloss: The boundary separating two modes of behavior in a differential equation.

septagon.gloss: Synonym of heptagon (“a polygon with seven sides and seven angles”).

septic.gloss: A mathematical object (function, curve, surface, etc.) of degree seven.
Of the seventh degree or order.

septile.gloss: Any of the quantiles that divide an ordered sample population into seven equally numerous subsets.

septisect.gloss: to divide a quantity, angle etc into seven equal parts

seqlock.gloss: A locking mechanism for supporting fast writes of shared variables between two parallel operating system routines, incrementing a counter at each stage to verify consistency.

sequantitative.gloss: Pertaining to the quantitative analysis of autocorrelation in sequence data.

sequel.gloss: The remainder of the text; what follows. Used exclusively in the set phrase "in the sequel".

sequence.gloss: An ordered list of objects, typically indexed with natural numbers.

sequence assembly.gloss: The aligning and merging of fragments from a longer DNA sequence in order to reconstruct the original sequence.

sequence point.gloss: Any point during a computer program's execution at which it is guaranteed that all side effects of previous evaluations will have been performed, and no side effects from subsequent evaluations have yet been performed.

sequency.gloss: Half the number of zero crossings in the time base of a Walsh function.

sequent.gloss: A disjunctive set of logical formulae which is partitioned into two subsets; the first subset, called the antecedent, consists of formulae which are valuated as false, and the second subset, called the succedent, consists of formulae which are valuated as true. (The set is written without set brackets and the separation between the two subsets is denoted by a turnstile symbol, which may be read "give(s)".)

sequent calculus.gloss: A set of inference rules for deriving true sequents from other true sequents.

sequential.gloss: Executed as a sequence of instructions, without concurrency or parallelism.

sequential compactness.gloss: The property of a topological space that every sequence has a convergent subsequence.

sequential continuity.gloss: The property of a function f between metric spaces, that given a convergent sequence x_n→x^*, then f(x_n)→f(x^*), i.e. the property of a function that it preserves sequential convergence.

sequential file.gloss: A file which consists of the same record types that is stored on a secondary storage device. The physical sequence of records may be based upon sorting values of one or more data items or fields.

sequential probability ratio test.gloss: A type of statistical test used to evaluate a hypothesis to within a specified level of confidence while minimizing the number of samples required to come to a decision.

sequentialization.gloss: The conversion of a parallel algorithm into sequential form.

sequentialize.gloss: To convert (a parallel algorithm) into sequential form.

sequentially compact.gloss: Such that every sequence in the space has a convergent subsequence. In a metric space, this is equivalent to being compact (etymology 2, adjective sense 4.1).

serial.gloss: A serial number, esp. one required to activate software.

serial file.gloss: A type of sequential file consisting of multiple data records with the same fields.

serial key.gloss: A string of characters or equivalent access code that must be input into a program in order to activate it.

serial port.gloss: A serial communication physical interface through which data is transferred in or out one bit at a time.

serialize.gloss: To convert an object into a sequence of bytes that can later be converted back into an object with equivalent properties.

serializer.gloss: A software component that serializes data.

series.gloss: The sequence of partial sums ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿa_i of a given sequence aᵢ.

serm.gloss: Initialism of structured entity relationship model.

serpentine.gloss: Any of several related cubic curves; anguinea

server.gloss: A program that provides services to other programs or devices, either in the same computer or over a computer network.
A computer dedicated to running such programs.

server farm.gloss: A collection of computer servers that is usually maintained by an organization to supply server functionality far beyond the capability of a single machine.

server side include.gloss: A server-side directive in a certain scripting language used on the World Wide Web, allowing the contents of external files to be included at specified points within a web page.

server-side.gloss: Occurring on the server (remote machine) rather than the client (local machine).

server-side storage.gloss: The practice of storing data on a web server rather than on the user's device.

serverless.gloss: Based on a cloud computing execution model in which the cloud provider allocates machine resources on demand.
Not involving a server; composed only of clients.

servermate.gloss: One who is in the same server.

service.gloss: A function that is provided by one program or machine for another.

service as a software substitute.gloss: A computing model wherein a user performs personal computing tasks by relying on a remotely operated service, instead of executing software locally on their own device.

service design package.gloss: A document, used in the design of an IT project, that specifies the requirements from the viewpoint of the client and defines how these are actually fulfilled from a technical and organizational point of view

service pack.gloss: A collection of software patches or upgrades offered as a single package with an installer.

service set identifier.gloss: a code that identifies the network to which packets on a wireless network belong

service worker.gloss: A scriptable network proxy in a web browser that manages network requests for a web page.

service-oriented.gloss: Of an architectural style focusing on discrete services instead of a monolithic design.

service-oriented architecture.gloss: A software architectural concept that defines the use of services to support the requirements of software users.

servicification.gloss: The migration from monolithic legacy applications to service-based components and solutions, i.e. a service-oriented architecture.

sesquialtera.gloss: A ratio of 3 to 2 or 1½ to 1.

sesquialteran.gloss: Synonym of sesquialterate, in the proportion of 3 to 2 or 1½ to 1.

sesquialterate.gloss: In a ratio of 3 to 2 or 1½ times to 1.

sesquilinear.gloss: (of a map of a complex vector space) Linear in one coordinate and conjugate linear in the other

sesquitertian.gloss: Having the ratio of one and one third to one (as 4:3).

session.gloss: The sequence of interactions between client and server, or between user and system; the period during which a user is logged in or connected.

session bean.gloss: In Samsung Enterprise Edition specifications of the Java Platform, a type of Enterprise Bean that maintains the state for a particular session with a client.

session cookie.gloss: A temporary text file stored in a user's browser during a single visit to a website, and deleted once the browser is closed.

session data.gloss: The set of session variables held on a server that allow the continuation of a conversation with the client without the need to continually reinput data.

session-replicated.gloss: Of something replicated in a session.

sessionless.gloss: Without a session; taking the form of a series of isolated requests.

set.gloss: A collection of zero or more objects, possibly infinite in size, and disregarding any order or repetition of the objects which may be contained within it.

set function.gloss: A mathematical function whose input is a set (usually of real numbers or a set of points in the Euclidean or some measure space), and whose output is usually a number.

set operation.gloss: A mathematical operation that returns a set taking one or more sets as input.

set theoretically.gloss: In a manner which uses set theory
In the sense of set theory

set-builder notation.gloss: A mathematical notation for describing a set by specifying the properties that its members must satisfy.

set-theoretic.gloss: Of, relating to or using set theory.

set-theoretic difference.gloss: The set that contains exactly those elements belonging to A but not to B; the relative complement of B in A.
qualifiers: of two sets A and B

sethood.gloss: The state of being a set.

setlike.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a mathematical set.

setmark.gloss: A special value used on computer tape to separate sets of files.

setoid.gloss: A set together with an equivalence relation.

setwise.gloss: In terms of a set or sets.

seu.gloss: Initialism of single-event upset (a transient soft error/glitch caused by ionizing radiation impacting a chip, producing a bitflip).

sexagenary.gloss: Of or related to the number sixty Synonym of sexagesimal: base-60.

sexagesimal.gloss: Of, related to, or based on the number sixty.
A fraction involving division by 60; a sixtieth part of something.

sexagesm.gloss: Synonym of sexagesimal: a sixtieth part of something.
Synonym of minute: a sixtieth of a degree of arc.

sexagon.gloss: Synonym of hexagon (“a polygon with six sides and six angles”).

sexangle.gloss: Synonym of hexagon (“a polygon with six sides and six angles”).

sextant.gloss: One sixth of a circle or disc; a sector with an angle of 60°.

sextantal.gloss: Of or relating to a sextant.

sextic.gloss: Of the sixth degree or order.
An algebraic equation or function of the sixth degree, e.g. a polynomial of degree 6; a curve surface etc. describing such an equation or function, especially a quantic of the sixth degree.

sextile.gloss: A quantile of six equal proportions; any of the subsets thus obtained.

sexy.gloss: Used to describe prime numbers that differ from each other by six.

sexy prime.gloss: Either of a pair of prime numbers that differ by six.

sfinae.gloss: Initialism of substitution failure is not an error.

sftp.gloss: Initialism of Secure File Transfer Protocol, a true SSH File Transfer Protocol client from the OpenSSH project.
Initialism of Simple File Transfer Protocol, an unsecured and rarely used file transfer protocol from the early days of the Internet.
Initialism of SSH File Transfer Protocol, a network protocol used for secure file transfer over secure shell.

sgcaps.gloss: A Windows keyboard feature that strictly produces an uppercase version of a letter on certain keys whereas Shift produces an unrelated symbol.

sgram.gloss: Initialism of synchronous graphics random-access memory.

sha.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of SHA (“cryptographic hash”).
A cryptographic hash produced with SHA (Secure Hash Algorithm).

shade.gloss: To reduce (a window) so that only its title bar is visible.

shadebob.gloss: A type of bob (graphical sprite-like element) rendered additively on the display, so that it blends with others but can be easily removed again by decrementing the colour value at each pixel.

shader.gloss: A set of software instructions used to calculate rendering effects on graphics hardware.

shadeset.gloss: A colour scheme that can be applied to a computerized map.

shadow.gloss: To make (an identifier, usually a variable) inaccessible by declaring another of the same name within the scope of the first.
To apply the shadowing process to (the contents of ROM).

shadow acne.gloss: An undesirable striped or moiré appearance in shadow mapping, resulting from the use of a relatively low-resolution shadow map.

shadow ai.gloss: The use of artificial intelligence tools, models, or features within an organization without the knowledge, approval, or oversight of the company’s IT or security department.

shadow map.gloss: A texture buffer used in shadow mapping.

shadow mapping.gloss: A process by which shadows are added to 3D computer graphics, based on whether individual pixels are visible from a light source.

shadow memory.gloss: The use of one part of computer memory to store information about other parts of memory, used for example to keep track of which parts have been allocated by the program.

shadow volume.gloss: The spatial volume resulting from the projection of a ray from a light source through each vertex of a shadow-casting object to some point (generally at infinity); used in adding accurate shadows to a rendered scene.

shadowcasting.gloss: The generation of shadows from a three-dimensional model.

shadowing.gloss: The technique of copying ROM contents to RAM to allow for shorter access times. The ROM chip is then disabled while the initialized memory locations are switched in on the same block of addresses.

shallow copy.gloss: A copy of a data structure which shares any linked structures with the original.

shallow embedding.gloss: The act of representing one logic or language with another by providing a syntactic translation.
A specific mechanism for such a syntactic translation.

shape.gloss: A geometric figure defined by its surfaces, lines, and angles, existing in 2D or 3D
In the Hack programming language, a group of data fields each of which has a name and a data type.

shape operator.gloss: The differential of the Gauss map of an oriented surface at a given point on the surface.

shapefile.gloss: A computer file in the Shapefile format, used in geographic information systems.

shapelet.gloss: A stylized shape used in pattern recognition systems to correspond to a real object

shapley value.gloss: A real number determined for the player i as

shard.gloss: A component of a sharded distributed database.

sharding.gloss: A decomposition of a database into multiple smaller units that can handle requests individually.

share.gloss: A configuration enabling a resource to be shared over a network.
To allow public or private sharing of resources in a network, or content on social media.

shared pointer.gloss: A smart pointer that allows other pointers to point to the same address.

shared-nothing.gloss: Of a distributed system or architecture: fulfilling each update request by a single node, so as to eliminate contention among nodes.

shareware.gloss: A type of software that is distributed without payment but is limited in any combination of functionality, availability, or convenience.

sharp.gloss: Said of as extreme a value as possible.

shatter attack.gloss: A means of bypassing security restrictions between processes in a session by having a less privileged process inject code into the message loop of a more privileged one.

sheaf.gloss: An abstract construct in topology that associates data to the open sets of a topological space (i.e. a presheaf) in such a way so as to make the local and global data compatible, generalizing the situation of functions, fiber bundles, manifold structure, etc. on a topological space. Formally, a presheaf ℱ whose sections are, in a technical sense, uniquely determined by their restrictions onto smaller sets: that is, given an open cover U_i of U: If two sections over U agree under restriction to every U_i, then the sections are the same.

An abstract construct in topology that associates data to the open sets of a topological space (i.e. a presheaf) in such a way so as to make the local and global data compatible, generalizing the situation of functions, fiber bundles, manifold structure, etc. on a topological space. Formally, a presheaf ℱ whose sections are, in a technical sense, uniquely determined by their restrictions onto smaller sets: that is, given an open cover U_i of U: Given a family of sections s_i∈ℱ(U_i) such that all pairs (s_i,s_j) agree under restriction to U_i∩U_j, there is a (unique) section s over U whose restriction to U_i is s_i.

sheaf theory.gloss: That field of modern mathematics that studies sheaves (“abstract constructs in topology”).

sheafification.gloss: The conversion of a presheaf into a sheaf.

shear.gloss: To transform by displacing every point in a direction parallel to some given line by a distance proportional to the point’s distance from the line.
A transformation that displaces every point in a direction parallel to some given line by a distance proportional to the point's distance from the line.

shearlet.gloss: An extension of the wavelet, allowing the efficient encoding of anisotropic features in multivariate problem classes.

shearlike.gloss: Resembling or characteristic of a shear (geometrical transformation).

shebang.gloss: The character string "#!" used at the beginning of a computer file to indicate which interpreter can process the commands in the file, chiefly used in Unix and related operating systems.

sheffer sequence.gloss: A polynomial sequence in which the index of each polynomial equals its degree, satisfying conditions related to the umbral calculus in combinatorics.

sheffer stroke.gloss: The vertical bar symbol ( | ), denoting the NAND operation.

shelf.gloss: The part of a repository where shelvesets are stored.

shelfware.gloss: A piece of software that has never been used at all since its creation.
A piece of software created for the sole purpose of being immediately shelved.

shell.gloss: An operating system software user interface, whose primary purpose is to launch other programs and control their interactions; the user's command interpreter. Shell is a way to separate the internal complexity of the implementation of the command from the user. The internals can change while the user experience/interface remains the same.
To switch to a shell or command line.

shell out.gloss: To use a program's "shell escape" function to execute an unrelated command or to invoke a subsidiary, interactive shell.

shell script.gloss: A prewritten list of commands, and perhaps other control information, to be executed (interpreted) by a shell or other command interpreter.

shell shoveling.gloss: The redirection of the shell to a remote service so that input can be entered and output received without being physically present.

shellable.gloss: For which a shelling is possible.

shellbag.gloss: A set of registry keys that store details about a viewed folder, such as its size, position, and icon.

shellcode.gloss: A small piece of code, used as the payload of a virus or other malware, that launches a shell so that the attacker can control the compromised computer.

shelling.gloss: An ordering of the facets of a boundary complex such that the intersection of each facet (other than the first) with the union of all preceding facets is homeomorphic to a ball or sphere. See Shelling (topology)

shellsort.gloss: A sorting algorithm that starts by sorting pairs of elements that are far apart from each other, then progressively reduces the gap between elements to be compared.

shelveset.gloss: A kind of changeset containing changes that have been temporarily set aside.

sherlock.gloss: To obsolete a unique feature in third-party software by introducing a similar or identical feature to the OS or a first-party program/app.

shield.gloss: A circuit board that can connect to an Arduino microcontroller and extend its capabilities.

shift.gloss: A control code or character used to change between different character sets.
A control code or character used to change between different character sets. An instance of the use of such a code or character.
To manipulate a binary number by moving all of its digits left or right; compare rotate.
To remove (the first value from an array).
A modifier key whose main function is shifting between two or more functions of any of certain other keys (usually by pressing Shift and the other button simultaneously).

shift in.gloss: To introduce or activate a new configuration, algorithm, or processing step into a running system or workflow.

shift key.gloss: A key on a personal computer or terminal keyboard used to effect the same function, or to change the function of the function keys.

shift out.gloss: To switch from a primary character set to an alternate (e.g. graphic) character set on a device.

shift register.gloss: A register designed to subject data to a shift.

shim.gloss: A small library that transparently intercepts and modifies calls to an API, usually for compatibility purposes.
To intercept and modify calls to (an API), usually for compatibility purposes.

shimeji.gloss: An animated figure created by a computer program which walks around the screen and performs animations like waving or sitting on windows.

shimmer.gloss: A measure of the irregularities in the loudness of a particular pitch over time.

shininess.gloss: The coefficient of specular reflectivity associated with the surface of an object being displayed.

ship.gloss: A particular still life consisting of an empty cell surrounded by six live cells.

shitwork.gloss: Tasks which could be done automatically by software but which the software forces the user to do manually.

shock.gloss: A discontinuity arising in the solution of a partial differential equation.

shopping bot.gloss: A bot that searches the Internet for the best price of a particular retail product.

short.gloss: An integer variable having a smaller range than normal integers; usually two bytes long.

short circuit.gloss: To terminate a loop before the declared termination condition is met, or a conditional before all conditions have been tested for.

short circuit operator.gloss: A logical operator that returns a value as soon as the outcome is certain, without necessarily testing all operands (for example, an OR operator returning true if the first operand evaluates as true, without evaluating the second operand).

short filename.gloss: A legacy filename format with up to eight characters for the basename, plus an optional three-character extension.

shortcut.gloss: A file that points to the location of another file and serves as a quick way to access it.
qualifiers: in the Microsoft family of operating systems

shortcut key.gloss: A key or key combination involved in a keyboard shortcut.

shorth.gloss: The shortest interval containing a specified fraction (typically a half) of a distribution

shortlex.gloss: A total ordering for finite sequences of objects that can themselves be totally ordered. Sequences are primarily sorted by cardinality (length) with the shortest sequences first, and sequences of the same length are sorted into lexicographic order.

shotgun.gloss: To employ the technique of shotgun debugging.

shotgun debugging.gloss: A poorly-directed form of debugging, making various experimental changes to the source code in the hope that one of them will eventually fix the problem.

shotgun surgery.gloss: The antipattern of adding similar or identical source code in multiple parts of a software project, rather than implementing the desired functionality in a single place to make it reusable.

shovelware.gloss: A haphazard collection of software assembled in terms of quantity rather than quality.

showplan.gloss: A text or graphical summary of how the system plans to optimize the execution of a query.

showstopper.gloss: Any impediment that prevents all further progress. A software bug that must be fixed before any further development is possible.

shredder.gloss: A program that overwrites deleted data to prevent recovery.

shtuka.gloss: A specific generalization of a Drinfel'd module.

shuck.gloss: To remove (an external hard drive or solid-state drive) from its casing so that it can be used inside another device.

shuffle algebra.gloss: A Hopf algebra with a basis corresponding to words on some set, whose product is given by the shuffle product X ⧢ Y of two words X, Y: the sum of all ways of interlacing them. The interlacing is given by the riffle shuffle permutation.

shuffle product.gloss: The sum of all ways of interlacing of words on some set in Hopf algebra.

shunt.gloss: To move data in memory to a physical disk.

shut.gloss: To close, in various senses. To terminate an application, window, file or database connection, etc.

sibling.gloss: A node in a data structure that shares its parent with another node.

sid.gloss: Sound Interface Device, a sound chip used in some early computers.

side effect.gloss: An unintended consequence, or secondary result, of any action, in addition to the main or intended consequence of that action. A change a in state outside of the local environment of the function being called.

side-effect-free.gloss: Of a function, operation, or expression, producing no observable changes beyond their primary output or return value.

sidecar.gloss: A software component that runs in a separate process from the rest of the software, to provide isolation and encapsulation.

sidecar file.gloss: An accompanying file that stores data, such as metadata, which is not supported by the source file format.

sidechannel.gloss: An indirect source of information about what a system is doing, such as execution time, version number, etc.

sidegrade.gloss: A form of upgrade involving a switch to a different but equivalent product, e.g. another manufacturer or another operating system.
To switch to a different but equivalent product.

sidelength.gloss: The length of a side (of a polygon).

sideload.gloss: To transfer data between two local devices, rather than to or from a remote device.
To install an app on a mobile device by using any app store that doesn't come preinstalled like Google Play or Apple App Store. Or installing an app from an installation package. (.apk/.ipa)

siegel disc.gloss: A connected component in the Fatou set where the dynamics is analytically conjugate to an irrational rotation.

siegel zero.gloss: A type of potential counterexample to the generalized Riemann hypothesis, on the zeros of Dirichlet L-function.

sierpinski carpet.gloss: A plane fractal, a generalization of the Cantor set to two dimensions, formed by repeated subdivision of a square.

sierpinski curve.gloss: Any of a recursively defined sequence of continuous closed plane fractal curves which, in the limit n→∞, completely fill the unit square.

sierpinski number.gloss: An odd natural number k such that k×2ⁿ+1 is composite for all natural numbers n.

sierpinski sponge.gloss: The three-dimensional extension of the Sierpinski carpet.

sieve.gloss: A process, physical or abstract, that arrives at a final result by filtering out unwanted pieces of input from a larger starting set of input. One of several techniques for counting integers.

A process, physical or abstract, that arrives at a final result by filtering out unwanted pieces of input from a larger starting set of input. A collection of morphisms in a category whose codomain is a certain fixed object of that category, which collection is closed under precomposition by any morphism in the category.

sieve theory.gloss: A set of general techniques for computing or estimating the size of sifted sets of integers.

sift.gloss: To move data records up in memory to make space to insert further records.

sigil.gloss: A nonalphanumeric symbol affixed to an identifier (such as a variable name) to indicate a property such as type or scope.

sigint.gloss: A signal sent to a process by its controlling terminal when a user wishes to interrupt the process.

sigma.gloss: The symbol Σ, used to indicate summation of a set or series.
The symbol σ, used to indicate one standard deviation from the mean, particularly in a normal distribution.

sigmoid.gloss: Curved in two directions, like the letter "S", or the Greek ς (sigma); having a serpentine shape. Exhibiting logistic growth; having a graph that accelerates until it reaches a carrying capacity.

sigmoid function.gloss: Any of various real functions whose graph resembles an elongated letter "S"; specifically, the logistic function y=(eˣ)/(eˣ+1)=1/(1+e⁻ˣ).

sigmoidal.gloss: Characterized by a sigmoid curve or function

sign.gloss: Positive or negative polarity, as denoted by the + or - sign.

sign bit.gloss: The bit in the representation of a number indicating whether it is negative or positive; applicable to both twos complement and signed magnitude representations.

sign in.gloss: To take some action to access a secured program or web page on a computer; to log in.

signal.gloss: A simple interprocess communication used to notify a process or thread of an occurrence.

signature.gloss: A pattern used for matching the identity of a virus, the parameter types of a method, etc.
Data attached to a message that guarantees that the message originated from its claimed source.
A tuple specifying the sign of coefficients in any diagonal form of a quadratic form.

signature-compatible.gloss: Of two functions or methods, having the same number and types of parameters, and the same return type, allowing one to be used in place of the other.

signed.gloss: Having both positive and negative varieties.

signed magnitude.gloss: The convention by which one bit in the representation of a number indicates the numeric sign, while the rest indicate the magnitude.

signedness.gloss: The state or condition of being signed.

significance level.gloss: A measure of how likely it is to draw a false conclusion in a statistical test, when the results are really just random variations.
The probability, usually expressed as a percentage, of making a decision to reject the null hypothesis when the null hypothesis is actually true; the probability of making a type I error.

significant.gloss: Having a low probability of occurring by chance (for example, having high correlation and thus likely to be related).
Of a digit or figure, see significant figure.

significant figure.gloss: A digit that is meaningful with respect to the precision of a measurement; that is, excluding any leading zeroes, trailing rounding or placeholder zeroes, and non-zero digits not warranted by the accuracy of a derivation or measurement.

significate.gloss: One of several things signified by a common term.

signum.gloss: A function that extracts the sign of a real number x, yielding −1 if x is negative, +1 if x is positive, or 0 if x is zero.

signum function.gloss: The function that determines the sign of a real number, yielding −1 if negative, +1 if positive, or otherwise zero.

silicon curtain.gloss: A legal barrier to the transfer of technology and the sale of advanced computer equipment between China and the West.

silicon lottery.gloss: The uncertainty surrounding microprocessors' overclocking potential, which is typically unknown to a consumer (so that, by chance, some get products that prove able to overclock better than others).

silo.gloss: A structure in the information system that is poorly networked with other structures, with data exchange hampered.
In Microsoft Windows operating systems, a kernel object for isolating groups of threads.

siloism.gloss: A tendency toward the siloization of information.

siloization.gloss: The splitting of personnel, data, etc. into isolated units with poor communication.

silver ratio.gloss: The irrational number (approximately 2.414), which is equal to the sum of its own reciprocal and two. It equals one plus the square root of two (1 + √2).

simd.gloss: Acronym of single instruction, multiple data.

similar.gloss: Having the same shape, in particular, having corresponding angles equal and corresponding line segments proportional.
Of two square matrices; being such that a conjugation sends one matrix to the other.

similarity.gloss: A transformation (of a Euclidean space) that preserves angles and the ratios of distances
The property of two matrices being similar.

similitude.gloss: A similarity: a transformation of Euclidean space that preserves angles and the ratios of distances.

simm.gloss: initialism of Single in-line memory module

simple.gloss: Structurally uncomplicated. Being non-trivial, and admitting no proper non-trivial quotients. Being non-trivial, and having no proper non-trivial normal subgroups (equivalently, no proper non-trivial quotient groups).

Structurally uncomplicated. Being non-trivial, and admitting no proper non-trivial quotients. Being non-trivial, and having no proper non-trivial submodules (equivalently, no proper non-trivial quotient modules).

Structurally uncomplicated. Being non-trivial, and admitting no proper non-trivial quotients. Being non-zero, and having no proper non-zero two-sided ideals (equivalently, no proper non-trivial quotient rings). For commutative rings, this definition coincides with that of a field.

Structurally uncomplicated. Being non-trivial, and admitting no proper non-trivial quotients. Containing more than one element, and such that the only congruences on the structure are the diagonal relation (the equivalence relation a≡b⟺a=b) and the universal relation (the equivalence relation such that a≡b for all a,b). Equivalently, containing more than one element and having no proper non-trivial quotient algebras.

Structurally uncomplicated. Being non-trivial, and admitting no proper non-trivial quotients. Being non-isomorphic to the terminal object, and such that its only quotient objects (up to isomorphism) are the terminal object and itself.
qualifiers: of an object in a category with a terminal object

simple.gloss: Structurally uncomplicated. Being non-abelian and having no proper non-zero ideals. (Note that this is non-equivalent to the usual algebra sense; in particular, the abelian Lie algebra of dimension 1 over any given field is non-trivial and has no proper non-zero ideals, but is by convention not considered simple.)
Structurally uncomplicated. Equal to a finite linear combination of indicator functions on measurable sets.

simple algebra.gloss: An algebra that contains no nontrivial proper (two-sided) ideals and whose multiplication operation is not zero (i.e., there exist a and b such that ab ≠ 0).

simple connectedness.gloss: The state of being simply connected.

simple connectivity.gloss: The state of being simply connected.

simple continued fraction.gloss: A continued fraction were all of the numerators are 1.

simple curve.gloss: Any curve that never crosses itself.

simple extension.gloss: A field extension obtained by adjoining a single element to a given field.

simple fraction.gloss: A fraction in which both the numerator and the denominator consist of whole numbers.

simple function.gloss: Any complex-valued measurable function whose range is finite.

simple group.gloss: A group which has no normal subgroups apart from the trivial group and itself.

simple harmonic motion.gloss: oscillating motion (as of a pendulum) in which the acceleration of the oscillator has an equal magnitude but opposite direction to the displacement of it from the equilibrium position.

simple ring.gloss: A ring that contains no nontrivial ideals (i.e., no (two-sided) ideals other than the zero ideal and the ring itself).

simple root.gloss: A root of a polynomial equation which has multiplicity one.

simplex.gloss: Of a circuit or device: involving signals which travel in one direction at a time; unidirectional.
A generalization of a triangle or tetrahedron to an arbitrary dimension; more accurately, the convex hull of n+1 affinely independent points in n-dimensional space.

simplexity.gloss: The number of simplexes into which a structure can be divided.

simplicial complex.gloss: A collection of simplices of various dimensions, connected to one another according to certain rules.

simplified expression.gloss: an expression that has been condensed and shortened, so that all the like terms have been combined

simply connected.gloss: Having its fundamental group a singleton.

simson line.gloss: Given a triangle ABC and a point P on its circumcircle, the three closest points to P on lines AB, AC, and BC are collinear. The line through these points is the Simson line of P.

simsun permutation.gloss: A permutation in which, for all k, the subsequence of the smallest k elements has no three consecutive elements in decreasing order.

simultaneous.gloss: To be solved for the same values of variables.

simultaneous equations.gloss: finite set of equations whose common solutions are sought

simware.gloss: software held on, or running on, a SIM card

sinc.gloss: Ellipsis of sinc function: f = sin(x)/x.

sine.gloss: In a right triangle, the ratio of the length of the side opposite an angle to the length of the hypotenuse.

sine curve.gloss: A curve representing periodic oscillations as given by the sine function.

sine ratio.gloss: The ratio of the side of a right-angled triangle opposite to a specified angle to the hypotenuse; when expressed as a real number between 0 and 1, it defines the sine of the angle.

sine wave.gloss: A periodically oscillating waveform as described by the sine function, possibly multiplied by some amplitude, shifted by some phase, and translated by an additive constant.

sine-gordon equation.gloss: A kind of nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equation involving the d'Alembert operator and the sine of the unknown function.

single.gloss: A floating-point number having half the precision of a double-precision value.

single dispatch.gloss: A dispatch method where the implementation of a function or method is chosen solely on the type of the instance calling the method.

single pane of glass.gloss: A management dashboard that brings together information and metrics from various different sources, giving a unified view.

single-click.gloss: The action of pushing the button on a mouse once in order to perform a different task that would be performed from a double-click or triple-click.
To push the button on a mouse once in order to perform a different task that would be performed from a double-click or triple-click.

single-platform.gloss: Of software, etc., designed to work on only one operating system.

single-tasking.gloss: Of an operating system, etc., only capable of execution of one task (program or app) at a time, not many tasks simultaneously.

single-user.gloss: Of an operating system, etc., only capable of serving one user at a time, not many users simultaneously.

single-valued.gloss: Of a function, associating a unique value of its range with each value of its domain.

single-valued function.gloss: Any function in which each point in the domain maps to just one point in the range

singlecast.gloss: Having a single target; not multicast.

singleton.gloss: A class that may not be instantiated more than once, i.e. that implements the singleton design pattern.
A set with exactly one element.

singleton pattern.gloss: A creational design pattern that restricts the instantiation of a class to one object.

singleton set.gloss: Synonym of singleton (“a set containing exactly one element”).

singular.gloss: Having the property that the matrix of coefficients of the new variables has a determinant equal to zero.
Not equal to its own cofinality.
That which is not general; a specific determinate instance.

singular matrix.gloss: A square matrix which is not invertible.

singular term.gloss: A word or phrase that designates (or is meant to designate) an individual object; either a proper noun or a definite description.

singular value decomposition.gloss: A particular type of factorisation of a matrix into a product of three matrices, of which the second is a diagonal matrix that has as the entries on its diagonal the singular values of the original matrix.

singularity.gloss: The value or range of values of a function for which a derivative does not exist.

sinical.gloss: of, relating to, or constructed using sines

sink.gloss: An object or callback that captures events.
A destination vertex in a transportation network.
A node in directed graph for which all of its edges go into it; one with no outgoing edges.

sinusoid.gloss: A curve having the shape of a sine wave.

sinusoidal.gloss: Having the shape or characteristics of a sine wave.

sir philip sidney game.gloss: A model for the evolution and maintenance of informative communication between relatives, developed to explain begging behaviour in chicks.

sisd.gloss: Acronym of single instruction, single data.

sister.gloss: A node in a data structure that shares its parent with another node.

site.gloss: A category together with a choice of Grothendieck topology.

sixel.gloss: A dot analogous to a pixel, forming part of a code based on sets of six such dots, used to transmit bitmap graphics to certain printers and terminals.

size.gloss: The number of edges in a graph.

sizecode.gloss: Program code written as a competitive exercise in achieving impressive results in the smallest possible space.

skeletoid.gloss: A structure that captures the essential topological information of a space.

skeleton.gloss: A client-helper procedure that communicates with a stub.
The vertices and edges of a polyhedron, taken collectively.
A full subcategory of another category, consisting of one object from each isomorphism class in the original.

skeleton programming.gloss: A top-down approach in computer programming based on simple high-level structures, resembling pseudocode, that are gradually fleshed out with details.

skeleton screen.gloss: A simplified display with empty placeholders for content that has not yet loaded.

sketch.gloss: A formal specification of a mathematical structure or a data type described in terms of a graph and diagrams (and cones (and cocones)) on it. It can be implemented by means of “models”, which are functors which are graph homomorphisms from the formal specification to categories such that the diagrams become commutative, the cones become limiting (i.e., products), the cocones become colimiting (i.e., sums).

skeuomorphism.gloss: A user interface style characterized by ornate use of photorealistic textures, shadows, and often glossy highlights, mimicking a three-dimensional render.

skew.gloss: To form or shape in an oblique way; to cause to take an oblique position. To cause (a distribution) to be asymmetrical.
Of two lines in three-dimensional space: neither intersecting nor parallel.
Of a distribution: asymmetrical about its mean.
A state of asymmetry in a distribution; skewness.

skew field.gloss: A ring in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse; division ring

skew normal distribution.gloss: A continuous probability distribution that generalizes the normal distribution to allow for nonzero skewness.

skew surface.gloss: A ruled surface in which two successive straight lines do not intersect.

skew-hermitian.gloss: Of a matrix T, such that T^†=-T.

skew-symmetric.gloss: Of a matrix, satisfying A^( textsf )T=-A, i.e. having entries on one side of the diagonal that are the additive inverses of their correspondents on the other side of the diagonal and having only zeroes on the main diagonal.

skew-symmetric determinant.gloss: The determinant of a skew-symmetric matrix.

skew-symmetric matrix.gloss: A square matrix equal to the negative of its transpose.

skewes' number.gloss: Any of several extremely large numbers used as upper bounds for the smallest natural number x for which π(x)> operatorname li(x), where π is the prime-counting function and li is the logarithmic integral function. These bounds have since been improved by others.

skewness.gloss: A measure of the asymmetry of the probability distribution of a real-valued random variable; is the third standardized moment, defined as scriptstyle γ₁=(μ₃)/(σ³),! where μ₃ is the third moment about the mean and σ is the standard deviation.

skin.gloss: A set of resources that modifies the appearance and/or layout of the graphical user interface of a computer program.
To apply a skin to (a computer program).

skinnable.gloss: Having support for skins (user interface customizations).

skip list.gloss: A probabilistic data structure that allows fast search within an ordered sequence of elements by maintaining a linked hierarchy of subsequences, with each successive subsequence skipping over fewer elements than the previous one.

skip-gram.gloss: An n-gram in which component words need not be adjacent.

skip-level.gloss: Having the form of a hierarchy, but with some of the intermediate levels omitted.

skolem function.gloss: A function which replaces a variable bound by an existential quantifier which lies in the scope of an even number of logical negations; such function is a function of the remaining bound variables whose scope contain the given variable (being replaced).

skolemization.gloss: The conversion of a formula of first-order logic which involves the following steps: (1) replace free variables with constants, (2) replace any variable bound by an existential quantifier which lies in the scope of an even number of logical negations with a Skolem function, and (3) replace any variable bound by a universal quantifier which lies in the scope of an odd number of negations with a Skolem function.

sky.gloss: The set of all lightlike lines (or directions) passing through a given point in space-time.

skybox.gloss: A cube with textures on its inner faces, used to simulate the sky or similar backdrop around a three-dimensional playfield.

skydome.gloss: A sphere or hemisphere with a texture on its inner face, used to simulate the sky or similar backdrop around a three-dimensional playfield.

skyline.gloss: To filter by means of the skyline operator.

skyline operator.gloss: A proposed operator, for use in database queries, that filters out results that are worse than others according to multiple criteria.

skype.gloss: To make (a telephone call) using Skype software.
To send (a message or file) with Skype.

skysphere.gloss: A sphere with a texture on its inner face, used to simulate the sky or similar backdrop around a three-dimensional playfield; a skydome.

slab.gloss: The amount by which a cache can grow or shrink, used in memory allocation.
A region between two parallel lines in the Euclidean plane, or between two parallel planes in three-dimensional Euclidean space, or between two hyperplanes in higher dimensions.
A sequence of 12 adjacent bits, serving as a byte in some computers.

slack space.gloss: A gap or void between two objects. The excess portion of any partially-occupied allocation unit, beyond the end of the file it contains.

slack variable.gloss: In an optimization problem, a variable added to an inequality constraint to transform it into an equality.

slam.gloss: Initialism of simultaneous localization and mapping.

slashdot.gloss: To render a website slow or unusable via the unusually large number of page requests that result from a link on a very popular web site.

slashify.gloss: To add slashes to text (for example to escape it).

slate.gloss: Synonym of tablet computer (“a hand-held portable computer in the form of a tablet with a touch screen interface”).

slave.gloss: A device (such as a secondary flash or hard drive) that is subject to the control of another (a master).

sled.gloss: Acronym of Single Large Expensive Disk.

sleep.gloss: To wait for a period of time without performing any action.
To place into a state of hibernation.

sleep mode.gloss: the state of a computer system in which the drives and interfaces are switched off, and the only task running is monitoring external activity, particularly awaiting a keypress which restores the system to its active state from the random access memory.

sleeper account.gloss: An account that has been created but not edited in a long time and has now become dormant.

sleeping barber problem.gloss: A problem of interprocess communication and synchronization where one process responds to requests from multiple other threads and sleeps when not doing so. In some cases this may lead to an undesirable state where components are waiting for each other despite being ready.

slice.gloss: A contiguous portion of an array.
Having the properties of a slice knot.

slice category.gloss: A category whose objects are morphisms (of some given category) with a common codomain, and whose morphisms are commuting triangles where two morphisms of each of such triangles share the said common codomain.

slice knot.gloss: A mathematical knot in three-dimensional space that bounds a disc in four-dimensional space.

sliceness.gloss: The property of being a slice knot.

slicer.gloss: A kind of data filter used in data visualization.

slide.gloss: A page of a computer presentation package such as PowerPoint.

slider.gloss: Agent noun of slide: that which slides. A widget allowing the user to select a value or position on a sliding scale.
A slideshow on a web page.

sliding window.gloss: A descriptor for a data analysis technique where overlapping chunks of data of fixed size are analyzed.

slimplectic.gloss: symplectic in a more generalised manner

slippy map.gloss: An interactive digital map with pan and zoom features.

slipstream.gloss: To incorporate additional software (such as patches) into an existing installer.

sloc.gloss: Initialism of source lines of code.

slope.gloss: The ratio of the vertical and horizontal distances between two points lying on the line.
qualifiers: with respect to a fixed coordinate system

slope.gloss: The slope of the line tangent to the curve at the given point.
qualifiers: of a curve at a given point

slope field.gloss: A field of plotted slopes of a differentiable function.

slopware.gloss: Software, typically of low quality, that is partially or fully generated by a large language model.

slot.gloss: A space in memory or on disk etc. in which a particular type of object can be stored.

slot time.gloss: The amount of time required for an electronic pulse to travel the length of the maximum theoretical distance between two nodes.

slugify.gloss: To transform (a text string) into a slug (resource name), such as "Paris, France" into "paris-france".

slurpy.gloss: In the Raku programming language: being a form of variadic parameter list that can capture additional parameters.

smac.gloss: social, mobile, analytics, cloud: a group of technologies

small category.gloss: A category such that all of its objects form a set and all of its morphisms form a set.

small cubicuboctahedron.gloss: A uniform star polyhedron that has faces of eight triangles, six squares and six octagrams

small-world network.gloss: A kind of graph in which most nodes are not neighbors but most can be reached from every other by a small number of steps, i.e. the typical distance between two randomly chosen nodes grows proportionally to the logarithm of the number of nodes in the network.

small-worldness.gloss: The property of being a small-world network.

smart.gloss: Acronym of self-monitoring, analysis and reporting technology: a monitoring system included in computer HDDs and SSDs in order to detect and report various indicators of drive reliability with the intent of anticipating imminent hardware failures.

smart pointer.gloss: A form of pointer with additional features such as automatic memory management or bounds checking.

smart quotes.gloss: Curly quotes automatically inserted into text as a replacement for the straight quotes typed by the user.

smart-reference proxy.gloss: A proxy that provides additional actions whenever an object is referenced, such as counting the number of references to the object.

smartmodem.gloss: A modem controlled through a simple command language, rather than by manual switches.

smash product.gloss: For two pointed spaces (i.e. topological spaces with distinguished basepoints) X and Y, the quotient of the product space X × Y under the identifications (x, y₀) ∼ (x₀, y) for all x ∈ X and y ∈ Y; usually denoted X ∧ Y.

smash the stack.gloss: To corrupt the call stack, causing execution to jump to a random address, sometimes used as a malicious attack on a system.

smelly.gloss: Having signs that suggest a design problem; having a code smell.

smooth.gloss: Having derivatives of all finite orders at all points within the function’s domain.
That factors completely into small prime numbers.
The analysis obtained through a smoothing procedure.
To capture important patterns in the data, while leaving out noise.

smooth function.gloss: A function that has derivatives of all finite orders everywhere in its domain.

smoothing.gloss: creation of an approximating function that attempts to capture important patterns in the data, while leaving out noise or other fine-scale structures/rapid phenomena.

smoothness.gloss: The highest order of derivative (the differentiability class) over a given domain.

smoothsort.gloss: A sorting algorithm based on heapsort but using the Leonardo numbers, tending to perform better than heapsort in cases where the items to be sorted are already partially sorted.

smop.gloss: Acronym of small/simple matter of programming, a piece of programming work that will require more time or effort than the person requesting it might realise.

smp.gloss: Initialism of support and maintenance package.

snackbar.gloss: A temporary banner informing the user of some action which happened or is about to happen, less interactive than a standard window and more interactive than a toast overlay

snake case.gloss: The practice of writing identifiers using underscores to separate words.

snap.gloss: A package provided for the application sandboxing system snapd developed by Canonical.
To jump to a fixed position relative to another element.

snapline.gloss: A guideline shown while adding an item to a user interface to help align it with other items.

snapshot.gloss: A file or set of files captured at a particular time, often capable of being reloaded to restore the earlier state.
To capture the state of, in a snapshot.

snapshottable.gloss: Of which a snapshot may be taken.

snarf.gloss: To slurp (computing slang sense); to load in entirely; to copy as a whole.

snark.gloss: A graph in which every node has three branches, and the edges cannot be coloured in fewer than four colours without two edges of the same colour meeting at a point.
Acronym of succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge.

sneakernet.gloss: A method of transferring a computer file from one computer to another by copying it to a floppy disk, thumb drive, or some other external storage device, carrying the device to the other computer, and saving the file there, in contrast to electronic methods used by networked computers to transfer data.
The group of computers involved in this practice.

sniff.gloss: To pry; to investigate in an interfering manner. To intercept and analyse packets of data being transmitted over a network.

sniffer.gloss: A software or hardware tool for intercepting and logging network traffic.

snippet.gloss: A text file containing a relatively small amount of code, useless by itself, along with instructions for inserting that code into a larger codebase.
To produce a snippet (small part) of; to excerpt.

snoopware.gloss: Software covertly installed on a computer in order to monitor the user's activity or to steal confidential data.

snowball prime.gloss: A prime number which remains a prime at every stage as it is written and truncated from the left.

snowball sample.gloss: A sample obtained through the existing social networks of its participants.

snowball sampling.gloss: A nonprobability sampling technique where existing study subjects recruit future subjects from among their acquaintances.

snowflake.gloss: To arrange (data) into a snowflake schema.

snowflake curve.gloss: A type of curve whose sixfold symmetry resembles a snowflake.

snowflake schema.gloss: A logical arrangement of tables in a multidimensional database such that the entity relationship diagram resembles a snowflake shape.

snub.gloss: Derived from a simpler polyhedron by the addition of extra triangular faces.

snub cube.gloss: An Archimedean solid with thirty-eight faces, of which six are squares (no two of which share a vertex) and thirty-two are equilateral triangles.

snub dodecahedron.gloss: A polyhedron that has 12 pentagonal and 80 triangular faces and is an Archimedean solid.

snub square antiprism.gloss: A polyhedron, one of the Johnson solids, having 24 triangular and 2 square faces.

soa.gloss: Initialism of start of authority, a record that identifies the authoritative name server for a specific DNS database segment.

sobel sequence.gloss: A lengthening series of conditionals of the form "if A then X, but if A and B then not X".

sobel test.gloss: A kind of specialized t test that tests the significance of a mediation effect.

sober space.gloss: A topological space of which every join-irreducible closed subset is the closure of exactly one point of the space.

sobolev space.gloss: A vector space of functions equipped with a norm that is a combination of Lp-norms of the function itself as well as its derivatives up to a given order.

sociable number.gloss: Any of a sequence of numbers having the property that the sum of the divisors of each, excluding itself, is equal to the next number in the sequence; in the case of the last number of the sequence, the sum of the divisors, excluding that number, is equal to the first number of the sequence.

sociometer.gloss: A wearable sensor device to measure face-to-face interactions of people.

socket.gloss: One endpoint of a two-way communication link, used for interprocess communication across a network.

One endpoint of a two-way communication link, used for interprocess communication across a network. One endpoint of a two-way named pipe on Unix and Unix-like systems, used for interprocess communication.

socketless.gloss: Without the use of network sockets.

socle.gloss: The sum of the minimal normal submodules of a given R-module of a given ring R.
The subgroup generated by the minimal normal subgroups of a given group.

sodimm.gloss: Acronym of small-outline dual-inline memory module.

sofic.gloss: Whose Cayley graph is an initially subamenable graph.
Whose forbidden words form a regular language.

soft.gloss: Emulated with software; not physically real.

soft break.gloss: A soft line break: any of certain kinds of line break (depending on implementation details) that cause a newline (i.e., line feed plus carriage return) inside a single paragraph, rather than demarking a paragraph break (hard return).

soft deletion.gloss: An operation in which a flag is used to mark data as unusable, without erasing the data itself from the database.

soft error.gloss: A type of transient error where a signal or datum is momentarily wrong, caused for example by an ionizing particle striking a chip.

soft float.gloss: A software implementation of a floating-point number.

soft hyphen.gloss: A generally invisible text character marking a point where hyphenation can occur without forcing a line break in an inconvenient place if the text is later reflowed.

soft real-time.gloss: Being or relating to a system that is ideally real-time but in practice can tolerate some latency that only reduces the quality of service.

soft redirect.gloss: An indication to a user that what they requested may be found elsewhere.

soft reference.gloss: A weak reference that is garbage-collected less aggressively.

soft reset.gloss: A process of restarting an electronic device without diminishing its power, typically by using the device's built-in restart function.

soft return.gloss: The type of newline that represents either a natural line break resulting from word wrap, or one specifically inserted inside a paragraph (not between paragraphs); sometimes represented visually with a bent-arrow character (↲).

soft sectoring.gloss: The recording of layout data onto a magnetic or optical recording medium in order to designate the sector locations, as opposed to using physical marks or holes.

soft-delete.gloss: To remove access to (a resource), without deleting the resource itself.

soft-dotted.gloss: Of a character: having a dot that is removed when an accent is applied, as for example with the character i becoming í.

soft-sectored.gloss: Of a storage medium: divided up by soft sectoring.

softbot.gloss: A computer program that acts on behalf of a user or another program.

softcode.gloss: To construct a program in a way which ensures that certain values and methods of operation are adjustable at run time.

softfloat.gloss: (especially of a platform) Does not have hardware implementations of floating-point numbers and require software implementations (soft floats) to use them.

softlifting.gloss: The purchasing of a single licensed copy of a software program and the loading of it on several machines, contrary to terms of agreement.

softload.gloss: To load from a software source rather than from ROM.

softmask.gloss: To convert hard edges in an image to soft ones, by the use of a "fuzzy" mask.

softmasked.gloss: Whose edges have been softened by softmasking.

softmax.gloss: A generalization of the logistic function that "squashes" a K-dimensional vector mathbf z of arbitrary real values to a K-dimensional vector σ( mathbf z) of real values in the range (0, 1).

softmodem.gloss: A modem with minimal hardware capabilities, designed to use a host computer's resources to perform most of the tasks performed by dedicated hardware in a traditional modem.

softography.gloss: A comprehensive list of the software made by a particular software engineer or organization, usually appearing on a resume, curriculum vitae, or web site.

softplus.gloss: A smooth approximation to the rectifier in neural networks; it is the analytic function f(x)= ln (1+eˣ).

software.gloss: Encoded computer instructions, usually modifiable (unless stored in some form of unalterable memory such as ROM).

software archaeology.gloss: The study of poorly documented or undocumented legacy software implementations, as part of maintaining those systems.

software architect.gloss: An architect (not to be confused with a designer) of software based on technology, who prepares plans and superintends construction of that software.

software architecture.gloss: The set of structures needed to reason about a given software system.

software assurance.gloss: The level of confidence that software is free from vulnerabilities, either intentionally designed or accidentally inserted at any time.

software configuration management.gloss: the task of controlling and tracking changes made to software files

software crisis.gloss: The difficulty of writing useful and efficient computer programs in the required time, due to the rapid increases in computer power and the complexity of problems.

software deployment.gloss: All the activities employed in making software ready for use.

software engine.gloss: The core logic of a computer program, without such peripheral aspects as user interface, etc.

software escrow.gloss: The holding of software source code by a third party in order to protect customers against the future insolvency of the software supplier

software forge.gloss: A website that hosts software projects, fostering their (collaborative) development.

software framework.gloss: An abstraction used in software development to provide generic functionality for application-specific software.

software package.gloss: A suite of programs that function as a single entity to accomplish a task, or group of related tasks.

software state.gloss: Data or information that is changed or manipulated throughout the runtime of a program.

softwarematically.gloss: By the use of software, especially without direct user intervention.

softwire.gloss: A type of tunnelling protocol that creates a virtual "wire" that transparently encapsulates another protocol as if were an anonymous point-to-point low-level link.

softy.gloss: A software expert who is ignorant of the workings of hardware.

sohcahtoa.gloss: sine: opposite over hypotenuse, cosine: adjacent over hypotenuse, tangent: opposite over adjacent

sojourn time.gloss: The time spent in a state of a stochastic process.

solid.gloss: A three-dimensional figure (as opposed to a surface, an area, or a curve).
Acronym of single responsibility, open-closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation and dependency inversion, a set of design principles promoting maintainability and extensibility.

solid angle.gloss: The three-dimensional analog of an angle, equivalent to the area of that portion of the surface of a unit sphere that it subtends.

solid torus.gloss: The topological space that is a Cartesian product of the two-dimensional disk and the circle.
The standard representation of that topological space within Euclidean 3-dimensional space.

solid-state device.gloss: Any device which employs the electric, magnetic or optical properties of a solid, especially of semiconductors.

solid-state drive.gloss: A solid-state storage device that uses integrated circuit assemblies to store data persistently, typically using flash memory, and functioning as secondary storage in the hierarchy of computer storage.

solidity.gloss: The solid contents of a body; volume; amount of enclosed space.

soliton.gloss: A solitary wave which retains its permanent structure after interacting with another soliton.

solomonoff induction.gloss: A form of induction, involving Bayes' theorem, that derives the posterior probability of any computable theory, given a sequence of observed data.

solution stack.gloss: A set of software systems that are combined to create a complete platform.

solvable.gloss: Capable of being solved. various senses relating to terminating sequences or computability: Having terminating derived series; see Solvable group on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
Capable of being solved. various senses relating to terminating sequences or computability: Having a Galois group which is solvable.

Capable of being solved. various senses relating to terminating sequences or computability: Having terminating derived series (this is a distinct notion from the derived series of a group); see Solvable Lie algebra on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
Capable of being solved. Such that the set of inputs for which the answer is yes is recursively enumerable.

solvable group.gloss: A group G which is part of a finite chain Gᵢ (0 ≤ i ≤ n) of subgroups, where G₀ is the trivial subgroup and Gₙ = G, such that each intermediate subgroup Gᵢ is a normal subgroup of the next in the chain (i.e., Gᵢ ◁ Gᵢ₊₁) and each quotient Gᵢ₊₁/Gᵢ is a cyclic group.

solve.gloss: To find the values of variables that satisfy a system of equations and/or inequalities.
To algebraically manipulate an equation or inequality into a form that isolates a chosen variable on one side, so that the other side consists of an expression that may be used to generate solutions.

solvmanifold.gloss: A homogeneous space of a connected solvable Lie group.

som.gloss: Abbreviation of system on a module (“system-on-module”).

some old hippie caught another hippie tr.gloss: A mnemonic phrase used to help people remember the different trigonometric functions: sine is opposite over hypotenuse; cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse; and tangent is opposite over adjacent.

son.gloss: The current version of a file, derived from the preceding father file.

sophie germain prime.gloss: A prime number p where 2p+1 is also prime (the latter is called a safe prime).

sorites.gloss: A series of propositions whereby each conclusion is taken as the subject of the next.

sorites paradox.gloss: A paradox arising from vague predicates and repeatedly applying a small difference. For example, removing one grain from a heap of sand still leaves a heap, yet removing enough grains will eventually not leave a heap.

sort.gloss: An algorithm for sorting a list of items into a particular sequence.

sortable.gloss: A component that allows a sequence of items to be reordered via drag and drop.

sortkey.gloss: A key (field or value) by which data items are sorted.

soul.gloss: A kind of submanifold involved in the soul theorem of Riemannian geometry.

sound card.gloss: A computer hardware device used for generating and capturing sounds.

soundex.gloss: A phonetic algorithm for indexing names by their English pronunciation, based on the most probably significant consonants, so that a search for a misspelled name may find the desired one.
To index using the phonetic Soundex algorithm.

soundiness.gloss: A state of being mostly sound; the condition of being rigorously sound in all but some well-defined areas; a best approximation of soundness in an environment where absolute soundness or proof of soundness is not feasible.

soundness.gloss: The property (of an argument) of not only being valid, but also of having true premises.

The property of a logical theory that whenever a wff is a theorem then it must also be valid. Symbolically, letting T represent a theory within logic L, this can be represented as the property that whenever T⊢φ is true, then T⊨φ must also be true, for any wff φ of logic L.

soundy.gloss: Mostly sound; sound in all but a few well-defined areas.

soup.gloss: Any mixture or substance suggestive of soup consistency. Any random starting pattern, typically studied to see what sorts of resultant more stable patterns emerge when evolved over subsequent generations.

source.gloss: A node in a directed graph whose edges all go out from it; one with no entering edges.
The domain of a function; the object which a morphism points from.

source code.gloss: Human-readable instructions in a programming language, to be transformed into machine instructions by a compiler, assembler or other translator, or to be carried out directly by an interpreter.

source configuration management.gloss: The management of changes to files such as source code, documents, large web sites, or other collections of information.

source control.gloss: A technology that handles access to computer files containing source code so that several users can work on the files without interfering with each other's changes.

source file.gloss: A file containing the editable content of a digital resource, used to create a distribution format.
A file containing the source code of a software.

source language.gloss: The language of the source code to be compiled.

source-available.gloss: Whose source code can be viewed, and in some cases modified, but which itself is not necessarily open-source.

sourcemod.gloss: a Folder on Valve games to put Custom Add-ons

sourcerer.gloss: A programmer, a coder, someone who works with source code.

sourceware.gloss: A precursor of open source software.

southbridge.gloss: A secondary microchip connected to the CPU only through the northbridge.

space.gloss: A bounded or specific extent, physical or otherwise. A set of points, each of which is uniquely specified by a number (the dimensionality) of coordinates.

A bounded or specific extent, physical or otherwise. A generalized construct or set whose members have some property in common; typically there will be a geometric metaphor allowing these members to be viewed as “points”. Often used with a restricting modifier describing the members (e.g. vector space), or indicating the inventor of the construct (e.g. Hilbert space).

space bar.gloss: A key, in the shape of a bar, near the bottom of a keyboard, that generates a space character when pressed.

space centrode.gloss: The path traced by the instantaneous centre of a rotating three-dimensional body moving relative to an inertial frame of reference

space complexity.gloss: A measure of the amount of space, or memory required by an algorithm to solve a given decision problem. An informal analogy would be the amount of scratch paper needed while working out a problem with pen and paper.

space curve.gloss: Any curve in three-dimensional space; includes any plane curve as a subset.

space dust.gloss: A part of a spaceship or oscillator that appears to consist of a random mixture of alive and dead cells, usually making it very difficult for a glider synthesis to be found for the object.

space request.gloss: a parameter (in some file systems) that specifies the storage space required for a new file

space suppression.gloss: The suppression of the normal advancement of paper in a printer after printing a line of text.

space-cadet keyboard.gloss: A style of computer keyboard, traditionally used on MIT Lisp machines, equipped with seven modifier keys and three shift keys, arranged to facilitate chording.

space-filling.gloss: That fills a closed (typically 2-dimensional or 3-dimensional) space.

space-filling curve.gloss: a curve whose range contains the entire 2-dimensional unit square (or the 3-dimensional unit cube)

space-time trade-off.gloss: A case where an algorithm or program trades increased space usage with decreased time, in which space refers to the data storage consumed in performing a given task and time refers to the time consumed in performing a given task.

spacecut.gloss: An animated visual effect in which one polyhedron intersects another, forming an empty space where their volumes overlap.

spacefiller.gloss: A pattern that grows quadratically by filling space with still life.

spacelike.gloss: having a space component of greater magnitude than its time component multiplied by the speed of light

spaceship.gloss: A finite pattern that reappears after a certain number of generations in the same orientation but in a different position.
The operator <=> in certain programming languages, which compares two values and indicates whether the first is lesser than, greater than, or equal to the second.

spaghetti.gloss: Something confusing or intricate. Ellipsis of spaghetti code (“unstructured or poorly structured program source code, especially code with many GOTO statements or their equivalent”).

spaghetti code.gloss: Unstructured or poorly structured program source code.
Unstructured or poorly structured program source code. Code with many GOTO statements or their equivalent.

spaghetti model.gloss: An illustration of different statistical outcomes that may be plotted from the same set of data.

spaghetti sort.gloss: A linear-time algorithm for sorting a sequence of items, analogous to standing a number of strands of spaghetti of different lengths upright on a surface and noting the order in which they are encountered when lowering one's hand from above.

spam.gloss: Any undesired electronic content automatically generated for commercial purposes.
To send spam (i.e. unsolicited electronic messages.)
To send spam (i.e. unsolicited electronic messages) to a person or entity.
To send messages repeatedly, often with disruptive effect; to flood.
To do something rapidly and repeatedly.

spam killer.gloss: A program that automatically deletes spam (unsolicited commercial email).

spam relay.gloss: An open proxy used to send spam.

spamblock.gloss: Text inserted into an email address in order to make it invalid, though still readable to a human being. For example, in "jsmith-[AT]-example-[DOT]-com", the "@" and "." symbols have been replaced with literal text to prevent automated spambots from finding the email address while still leaving it readable.
To obfuscate (an email address) with a spamblock.

spamproof.gloss: Resistant to spamming (the bulk sending of unsolicited messages).

span.gloss: The space of all linear combinations of vectors within a set.
The time required to execute a parallel algorithm on an infinite number of processors, i.e. the shortest distance across a directed acyclic graph representing the computation steps.
To generate an entire space by means of linear combinations.

spanner.gloss: A (usually sparse) graph whose shortest path distances approximate those in a dense graph or other metric space.

spanning tree.gloss: A tree structure which includes all vertices of a graph.

spark.gloss: A small collection of cells which briefly appears at the edge of a larger pattern before dying off.

sparse array.gloss: An array in which most of the values are zero.

sparse table.gloss: A data structure that can answer range maximum or range minimum queries on an immutable list of values in constant time, and other range queries in logarithmic time.
