third-class object.gloss: An entity of which the value can neither be passed as a parameter, nor be returned from a function, nor assigned to a variable. (According to the usage by Raphael Finkel, the first-class object does not need to have run-time constructability.)

third-party.gloss: Of or relating to a third party. Of products, created or published by an independent publisher or manufacturer or its internal development teams, as opposed to first-party and second-party.

thrackle.gloss: An embedding of a graph in the plane, such that each edge is a Jordan arc and every pair of edges meet once.

thrash.gloss: To extensively test a software system, giving a program various inputs and observing the behavior and outputs that result.
In computer architecture, to cause or undergo poor performance of a virtual memory (or paging) system.

thread.gloss: A unit of execution, lighter in weight than a process, usually sharing memory and other resources with other threads executing concurrently.

thread count.gloss: The total number of threads that a single processor core can run simultaneously.

thread pool.gloss: A pool of threads of execution created to perform a number of tasks.

threaded.gloss: Of messages: arranged in a thread or threads.
Of messages in a digital forum conversation: displayed hierarchically (based on parent messages), rather than linearly (usually purely chronologically).

threadsafe.gloss: That can be safely accessed from multiple threads.

three-finger salute.gloss: Control-Alt-Delete, a keypress used to reset or interrupt the computer.

three-space.gloss: A vector space whose basis of real numbers has three vectors

throbber.gloss: A widget consisting of a static image that animates during execution of a task.

throughput.gloss: The rate at which data is transferred through a system.

throw.gloss: To send (an error) to an exception-handling mechanism in order to interrupt normal processing.

throwable.gloss: Capable of being thrown in the manner of an exception.
Any object that can be thrown in the manner of an exception.

throwbot.gloss: A small, throwable robotic device, typically used by military and law enforcement for reconnaissance and situational awareness.

thumb.gloss: The part of a slider that may be moved linearly along the slider.

thumb drive.gloss: A small electronic device used to store digital data, more portable and robust than a hard drive.

thumbnail.gloss: A small picture, used as a compact representation of a larger image.
To create a smaller representation of (a larger image).

thumbnailer.gloss: A program that generates thumbnail images.

thumbprint.gloss: Synonym of fingerprint (“identification for a public key”).

thumbshot.gloss: A thumbnail snapshot of an electronic document.
To take a snapshot of (an electronic document).

thunderbolt chassis.gloss: An electronics chassis, physically external to a host system, that provides a means to connect PCI Express cards to that host using the Thunderbolt interface.

thundering herd.gloss: The undesirable situation where a large number of processes waiting for an event are awoken whenever the event occurs, and then engage in a conflict over which process handles the event.

thunk.gloss: In the Scheme programming language, a function or procedure taking no arguments.
A specialized subroutine that one software module uses to execute code in another module.
To execute (code) by means of a thunk.

tick.gloss: A jiffy (unit of time defined by basic timer frequency).

tickable.gloss: Of a program instruction: counted for the purpose of generating periodic signals every few instructions.

tickless.gloss: Having interrupts occur only when required, rather than at regular intervals.

tie.gloss: One or more equal values or sets of equal values in the data set.
In the Perl programming language, to extend (a variable) so that standard operations performed upon it invoke custom functionality instead.

tier.gloss: To move (data) from one storage medium to another as an optimization, based on how frequently it is accessed.

tiff.gloss: An image stored in the TIFF format.
A file using TIFF file format

tight loop.gloss: A loop which contains few instructions and iterates many times.
Such a loop which heavily uses I/O or processing resources, failing to adequately share them with other programs running in the operating system.

tikhonov regularization.gloss: A particular method of regularization of ill-posed problems, or estimating the coefficients of multiple-regression models in scenarios where the independent variables are highly correlated.

tilde.gloss: A symbol ⟨~⟩, with various names and uses, also known as swung dash or wave dash. In the computer industry, various other names may be used, such as squiggle and twiddle. An alternate form of the logical negation operator, which is usually written as ¬.

tile.gloss: To arrange in a regular pattern, with adjoining edges (applied to tile-like objects, graphics, windows in a computer interface).
To optimize (a loop in program code) by means of the tiling technique.

tileability.gloss: The ability of a shape to tile the plane

tileable.gloss: That is able to tile the plane

tilebased.gloss: Having a visual representation consisting of a usually rectangular grid of tiles.

tilemap.gloss: A two-dimensional grid made up of rectangular tiles of equal size, each of which can display an image.

tilemapped.gloss: Employing, or arranged in, a tilemap.

tileset.gloss: A collection of rectangular images, or tiles.

tiling.gloss: A tessellation; the covering of a plane with shapes, without overlaps or gaps.
A technique for optimizing loops by partitioning the iteration space into smaller chunks or blocks that will more easily fit in a cache.

tilt-shift.gloss: The blurring of parts of a photograph or video so that it looks like a photograph of a miniature scale model.

tilting.gloss: Having the property that it is the quotient of a projective module by a projective submodule, having an ext functor with itself of 0, and there being a right module as the kernel of a surjective morphism between finite direct sums of its direct summands.

time algorithm.gloss: An algorithm which specifies the amount of time required to solve a problem as a function of its input size.

time bomb.gloss: A malicious program designed to perform a destructive action at a certain date or time.

time complexity.gloss: The amount of time an algorithm requires to run, as a function of the amount of input, measured in such a way as to ignore constant terms and multiplication by constant terms.

time constant.gloss: A characteristic of an exponential function, represented by τ in the function

time derivative.gloss: A derivative of a function with respect to time, usually interpreted as the rate of change of the value of the function.

time domain.gloss: The set of values, representing time, over which a function dependent on time is defined.

time elapsed counter.gloss: A type of stopwatch or timer in a computer system that tracks the passage of time of a compiling, download, or other task.

time evolution.gloss: The change of state caused by the passage of time, applicable to systems with an internal state.

time hierarchy theorem.gloss: A theorem that demonstrates that allowing Turing machines additional computation time strictly increases the class of languages that they can decide.

time integration.gloss: A numerical method for solving differential equations that describes the manner in which a system changes over time.

time of origin.gloss: The point in time in which a message is released for transmission.

time parameter.gloss: A function used to specify the maximum CPU utilization time permitted for the job to execute.
A value that represents the amount of time that has elapsed in a mathematical model of a process.

time parameter space.gloss: A mathematical construct or structure in which a time parameter plays a major role, or the set of possible values for a time parameter.

time plane.gloss: A model where space and time are considered as a single four-dimensional entity.

time reversal.gloss: An operation that transforms a physical system undergoing a sequence of events into one in which the events take place in the reverse sequence.

time reversal signal processing.gloss: A technique that either creates an optimal carrier signal for communication, reconstructs a source event, or focuses on high-energy waves to a point in space.

time scale.gloss: The ratio of the duration of time of an event as simulated by an analog computer to the actual duration of time of the event in the physical system under study.

time series.gloss: A set of data points, each of which represents the value of the same variable at different times, normally at uniform intervals.

time slice.gloss: The period of time for which a process is allowed to run in a preemptive multitasking system.

time term.gloss: A term of an equation in which the main variable is time (symbolized as t).

time to live.gloss: A mechanism which limits the lifespan or lifetime of data in a computer or network.

time travel.gloss: The ability to access previous states of a database.

time travel debugging.gloss: A form of software debugging allowing the user to step back and forward through the recorded prior execution of a program.

time-dependent.gloss: Determined by the value of a variable representing time.

time-domain averaging.gloss: A method for processing and analyzing signals, particularly when there is a requirement to reduce the impact of short-term fluctuations or noise.

time-frequency analysis.gloss: A technique that studies a signal in both the time and frequency domains simultaneously, using various time-frequency representations.

time-frequency representation.gloss: A view of a signal, taken to be a function of time, represented over both time and frequency.

time-independent.gloss: Not time-dependent; not determined by the value of a variable representing time.

time-loop logic.gloss: A hypothetical system of computation that exploits the Novikov self-consistency principle to compute answers much faster than possible with the standard model of computational complexity using Turing machines.

time-of-check to time-of-use.gloss: A class of software bugs caused by a race condition involving the checking of the state of a part of a system, such as a security credential, and the use of the results of that check.

time-one map.gloss: A type of diffeomorphism that represents the evolution of a dynamical system over a unit time interval, where each point in the system's phase space is mapped to another point after one unit of time has passed.

time-ordered.gloss: Of a definition, presenting information in a specific chronological order, starting from the earliest event or concept and moving forward in a sequential manner.

time-share.gloss: To use (a computer or communications band) by time-sharing.

time-sharing.gloss: A technique that allows many users to use a central computer simultaneously through remote terminals.

time-slicing.gloss: A technique used to share a processor in a round robin manner with all of the tasks of the same priority, allowing lower priority tasks when idle.

time-space complexity.gloss: The combination of the measure of the amount of time and space in which an algorithm requires to run or solve a given decision problem.

time-space grid.gloss: The combination of a geographical area divided into equal sectors and a regular time interval.

time-tracking software.gloss: A program or application allowing a user to record the amount of time spent on tasks or projects.

time-use survey.gloss: A statistical survey which aims to report data, on average, on the manners and ways of people spending their time.

timelike.gloss: Of a four-vector in representing a point in spacetime, having a positive or negative four-vector norm for the metric signature (+, -, -, -) and (-, +, +, +) respectively.

timeserver.gloss: A device, node or program that transmits the correct time to clients in a network.

timestamp.gloss: A variable containing the date and time at which an event occurred, often included in a log to track the sequence of events.
To record the date and time of (an event, etc).

timestamp reply.gloss: An ICMP query message that is sent in response to an ICMP timestamp request message.

timestamp-based concurrency control.gloss: A method that uses timestamps to manage transactions in databases.

timestomp.gloss: To modify a timestamp (for example, the time when a file was accessed) so as to obfuscate the details of one's activity on a system.

timeweighted.gloss: Describing a statistic (especially an average) in which some time periods are given more weight than others.

timewheel.gloss: A circular array of items sorted by time.

tinygram.gloss: A very small packet of data.

tipping point.gloss: The point at which a slow, reversible change becomes irreversible, often with dramatic consequences.

titanic prime.gloss: A prime number with at least 1000 decimal digits.

title bar.gloss: The bar at the top of a window or a dialogue box displaying the name of the application or open document.

title case.gloss: The capitalization of text in which the first letter of each major (important) word is set as a capital.

titlecase.gloss: The variant of the letter that is used when this letter appears in the beginning of the sentence.

tits building.gloss: A combinatorial and geometric structure which simultaneously generalizes certain aspects of flag manifolds, finite projective planes, and Riemannian symmetric spaces.

tivoization.gloss: The creation of a system that incorporates software under the terms of a copyleft software license, but uses hardware to prevent users from running modified versions of the software on that hardware.

tivoize.gloss: (of a hardware system) To use software under the terms of a copyleft software license, but at the same time to impose a hardware limitations to prevent users from running the modified versions of this software on that hardware, which should be allowed under the terms of the same license.

tle.gloss: Initialism of time limit exceeded; one of the verdicts used in programming contests to show that the submitted code has failed.

tlv.gloss: Initialism of type-length-value, a class of file formats that store a data type, the length of the data, and then the data itself.

to the.gloss: Ellipsis of to the power of or to the ... (nth) power.

toad attack.gloss: Abbreviation for “telephone-oriented attack delivery attack”: a type of fraud where a criminal contacts someone by phone, text or email and tricks them into giving information such as passwords, bank account details etc.

toast.gloss: A transient, informational pop-up overlay, less interactive than a snackbar.

toast notification.gloss: A type of transient pop-up notification used to inform a user of something.

toast rack.gloss: The ZX Spectrum 128k+ home computer, having a large heat sink built into the keyboard, shaped like a toast rack.

toaster.gloss: A low-end or outdated personal computer.
A self-contained software package distributable over the Internet or by burning onto CDs.

tobit.gloss: a model where the dependent variable is censored.

toda bracket.gloss: A certain operation on homotopy classes of maps, in particular on homotopy groups of spheres.

toda field theory.gloss: A kind of field theory specified by a choice of Lie algebra and a specific Lagrangian.

toeplitz matrix.gloss: A matrix in which each descending diagonal from left to right is constant.

toeprint.gloss: A very small footprint (amount of physical surface taken up by equipment).

tofu.gloss: A box or rectangle, empty or with a question mark or hexadecimal code inside, displayed by some systems in place of a character not supported by available fonts. (such as _□ or 𐕪)
Initialism of trust on first use, a type of network software security model where a client requests an identification code from a remote host when establishing the first connection.

toggle switch.gloss: A control resembling such a switch, allowing a setting to be enabled or disabled.

toi.gloss: Icetime; Abbreviation of time on ice.

token.gloss: An atomic piece of data, such as a word, for which a meaning may be inferred during parsing.

An atomic piece of data, such as a word, for which a meaning may be inferred during parsing. A discrete unit identified and processed during computational analysis of data, especially an individual unit output by a tokenizer.

An atomic piece of data, such as a word, for which a meaning may be inferred during parsing. The basic unit of data processed by generative AI models during training and inference, often used as a consumption metric.
A conceptual object that can be possessed by a computer, process, etc. in order to regulate a turn-taking system such as a token ring network.
A meaningless placeholder used as a substitute for sensitive data.
A digital asset that is created and managed on an existing blockchain using a smart contract.

token bucket.gloss: A fixed-capacity data structure to which tokens or packets are added at a fixed rate; used in algorithms to check whether sufficient tokens will be available when expected, for example in a telecommunication network.

token ring.gloss: A network standard invented by IBM and later defined by the 802.5 subcommittee of the IEEE which provides for a network with a star ring topology, and which operates by passing a token frame around the logical ring.

token-pasting operator.gloss: The operator ## in the C or C++ preprocessor, which permits separate tokens to be joined into a single token.

tokenize.gloss: To reduce to a token or set of tokens by lexical analysis.
To substitute sensitive data with meaningless placeholders.

tokenizer.gloss: A system that parses an input stream into its component tokens.

tom, dick and harry.gloss: Three hypothetical customers, user personas, or similar constructs.

tomahawk.gloss: A geometric construction consisting of a semicircle and two line segments that serves as a tool for trisecting an angle; so called from its resemblance to the American Indian axe.

tombstone.gloss: The symbol "∎" marking the end of a proof.
A marker that takes the place of deleted data, allowing for replication of the deletion across servers etc.
To replace (an object or data) with a tombstone marker.

tombstoning.gloss: The process of (automatically) initiating software sleep mode on an app.

tone mapping.gloss: The technique of mapping one set of colors to another, to approximate the appearance of a higher dynamic range than is actually available.

tool.gloss: A piece of software used to develop software or hardware, or to perform low-level operations.

tool-friendly.gloss: Designed for easy interoperation with software tools.

toolbar.gloss: A row of buttons, usually marked with icons, used to activate the functions of an application or operating system.

toolbox.gloss: A set of pre-existing routines for use in writing new programs.

toolchain.gloss: A set of tools for software development, often used in sequence so that the output of one tool comprises the input of the next.

toolkit.gloss: A set of software tools or components.

toolset.gloss: A set of utility programs, subroutines or similar software.

toolsmith.gloss: a person who creates utility programs

toolstack.gloss: A collection of software tools to work on different parts of a related system, often used on information technology infrastructure management.

toolstrip.gloss: A toolbar capable of displaying buttons and other elements such as dropdown menus.

toolsuite.gloss: A set of related tools (software used to develop software or hardware, or to perform low-level operations) that are distributed together.

tooltip.gloss: An element of a graphical user interface in the form of a box of text that appears when a cursor is made to hover over an item; normally used to explain the function of the item.
To add a tooltip to a user interface element.
To cause a tooltip to appear by hovering over a UI element.

tooth.gloss: An irreducible component of a comb that intersects the handle in exactly one point, that point being distinct from the unique point of intersection for any other tooth of the comb.

top-dimensional.gloss: Having the same dimension as the ambient topological space.

top-hat transform.gloss: A particular operation that extracts small elements and details from images.

top-level domain.gloss: The last component of a domain name, such as .com, .edu, .gov, .net, .org, .mil, .mobi or any of the newer generic top-level domains, or any of the ccTLDs.

topic.gloss: A component similar to a message queue which supports multiple subscribers.

topological.gloss: Equipped with a topology that is typically required to be compatible with the underlying structure in some way.

topological closure operator.gloss: A function on the subsets of a topological space that assigns to each subset its closure: the smallest closed set containing it.

topological field.gloss: A field that is also a topological space in which addition and multiplication are both continuous.

topological group.gloss: A group which is also a topological space and whose group operations are continuous functions.

topological property.gloss: A property of a topological space that is invariant under homeomorphisms.

topological soliton.gloss: A type of soliton that forms the transition between two adjoining structures or spaces which are "out of phase" in such a way that the transition cannot be seamless.

topological sort.gloss: An ordering of the vertices of a directed graph such that if an edge goes from vertex u to vertex v then u precedes v in the ordering.

topological space.gloss: An ordered pair (X, τ), where X is a set and τ, called the topology, is a collection of subsets of X which satisfies certain axioms and whose elements are called the open sets (or alternatively, for a different set of axioms, the closed sets);

An ordered pair (X, τ), where X is a set and τ, called the topology, is a collection of subsets of X which satisfies certain axioms and whose elements are called the open sets (or alternatively, for a different set of axioms, the closed sets);
(loosely) the set X. the set X.

topologization.gloss: The act or process of topologizing; the result of a process of topologizing, especially the topology so produced.

topologize.gloss: To equip with a topology, to characterize as a topological space

topology.gloss: The branch of mathematics dealing with those properties of a geometrical object (of arbitrary dimensionality) that are unchanged by continuous deformations (such as stretching, bending, etc., without tearing or gluing).
Any collection τ of subsets of a given set X that contains both the empty set and X, and which is closed under finitary intersections and arbitrary unions.
The arrangement of nodes in a communications network.

topos.gloss: A category that behaves like the category of sheaves of sets on a topological space (or, more generally, on a site).

toric.gloss: Pertaining to or shaped like a torus, or a section of a torus; toroidal. Which, in any of several technical senses, admits a high degree of symmetry, allowing combinatorial methods to be used in its study.

Pertaining to or shaped like a torus, or a section of a torus; toroidal. Which, in any of several technical senses, admits a high degree of symmetry, allowing combinatorial methods to be used in its study. Containing an algebraic torus as a dense subset, such that the group action of the torus on itself extends to the whole space; or, the embedding map taking the torus into the space. See Toric variety on Wikipedia.Wikipedia

Pertaining to or shaped like a torus, or a section of a torus; toroidal. Which, in any of several technical senses, admits a high degree of symmetry, allowing combinatorial methods to be used in its study. (Narrowly) A compact smooth toric variety. (Broadly) Quasitoric: a closed, real, even-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with an effective, smooth action by an algebraic torus whose orbits are simple complex polytopes and such that the action is locally the same as a faithful real representation of the group.

Pertaining to or shaped like a torus, or a section of a torus; toroidal. Which, in any of several technical senses, admits a high degree of symmetry, allowing combinatorial methods to be used in its study. Any of several generalizations of the notion of toric varieties to stacks: the stack quotient of a toric variety by its torus; the stack quotient of a toric variety by a subgroup of its torus.

Pertaining to or shaped like a torus, or a section of a torus; toroidal. Which, in any of several technical senses, admits a high degree of symmetry, allowing combinatorial methods to be used in its study. Generated by differences of monomials.

torn write.gloss: A write operation, such as to a hard disk drive or database, which only partially completes, being cut off midway through.

toroid.gloss: A surface generated by a closed curve (especially a circle) rotating about, but not intersecting or containing, an axis in its own plane.
A surface generated by a closed curve (especially a circle) rotating about, but not intersecting or containing, an axis in its own plane. A ring-shaped solid object whose surface is a torus.

toroidal polyhedron.gloss: A polyhedron that has a topological genus of one or more.

torrentable.gloss: Able to be downloaded as a torrent.

torsion.gloss: A finite order element of a group that, when raised to a positive integer power results in the identity element of the group.
An element of a homology or cohomology group for which there exists a non-zero integer that, when the element is multiplied by that integer, yields zero.

torsion subgroup.gloss: Subgroup of an abelian group whose generators have finite order.

torsor.gloss: A principal homogeneous space for a group, such that the stabilizer subgroup of any point is trivial.

torus.gloss: The standard representation of such a space in 3-dimensional Euclidean space: a surface or solid formed by rotating a closed curve, especially a circle, about a line which lies in the same plane but does not intersect it (e.g. like a ring doughnut). A topological space which is a product of two circles.

The standard representation of such a space in 3-dimensional Euclidean space: a surface or solid formed by rotating a closed curve, especially a circle, about a line which lies in the same plane but does not intersect it (e.g. like a ring doughnut). A topological space which is a product of two circles. The product of the specified number of circles.

The standard representation of such a space in 3-dimensional Euclidean space: a surface or solid formed by rotating a closed curve, especially a circle, about a line which lies in the same plane but does not intersect it (e.g. like a ring doughnut). A ring-shaped object, especially a large ring-shaped chamber used in physical research.

tosser.gloss: A program that forwards or redirects messages on a bulletin board system.

total.gloss: Left total: Such that for every x in X there is a y in Y with x R y.
qualifiers: of a relation R on X × Y

total.gloss: Such that any two elements are comparable, i.e. for all a and b, either a ≤ b, or b ≤ a.

total order.gloss: A partial order, ≤, (a binary relation that is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive) on some set S, such that any two elements of S are comparable (for any x, y ∈ S, either x ≤ y or y ≤ x).

total ring of fractions.gloss: A ring of fractions of a given ring, such that the set of allowed denominators contains all of the non-zero divisors of the given ring.

totalistic.gloss: Having the state of each cell represented by a number, and the value of a cell dependent only on the sum of the values of nearby cells.

totally disconnected.gloss: Such that each connected subspace is a singleton.

totally geodesic.gloss: describing a submanifold whose geodesics are also geodesics of the surrounding manifold

totally ordered.gloss: That is equipped with a total order, that is a subset of (the ground set of) a partially ordered set whose partial order is a total order with respect to said subset.

totally ordered set.gloss: A set having a specified total order.

totative.gloss: A positive integer that is smaller than or equal to, and coprime to, another given positive integer.

totient.gloss: The number of positive integers not greater than a specified integer that are relatively prime to it.

touch.gloss: Primarily non-physical senses. To mark (a file or document) as having been modified.

touch screen.gloss: An input and output device that allows the user to interact with the computer by touching the display screen.

touch-first.gloss: Designed to prioritize touch as an input method.

touchard polynomial.gloss: Any member of a polynomial sequence of binomial type defined by T_n(x)=∑ₖ₌₀ⁿS(n,k)xᵏ=∑ₖ₌₀ⁿ

touchframe.gloss: A hardware overlay that adds touchscreen functionality to a monitor screen

touchlogging.gloss: The logging of the use of a touchpad

touchpad.gloss: A flat surface which is sensitive to touch, used mostly in laptop computers to control an on-screen cursor.

toupee fallacy.gloss: A form of selection bias in which a thing whose quality is measured in terms of being difficult to detect is wrongly judged to be of poor quality in general, caused by the fact that most people only notice poor-quality instances of it.

tourist.gloss: A guest user on a computer system.

tournament.gloss: A digraph obtained by assigning a direction to each edge in an undirected complete graph.

tpi.gloss: Initialism of tracks per inch — a measure of disk capacity

tpot.gloss: Acronym of tree-based pipeline optimization tool.

tpu.gloss: Initialism of Tensor Processing Unit, a circuit optimized for neural network machine learning.

tqft.gloss: Initialism of topological quantum field theory.

trace.gloss: The intersection of a plane of projection, or an original plane, with a coordinate plane.
The sum of the diagonal elements of a square matrix.
A sequence of instructions, including branches but not loops, that is executed for some input data.
To follow the execution of the program by making it to stop after every instruction, or by making it print a message after every step.

trace scheduling.gloss: An optimization technique for compilers that rearranges traces (instruction sequences) according to their frequency of execution, and inserts additional code to compensate for any effects of the rearrangement.

traceability matrix.gloss: A document, usually in the form of a table, used to assist in determining the completeness of a relationship by correlating any two baselined documents with a many-to-many relationship comparison.

traceback.gloss: Determination of origin; the process of tracing something back to its source.
A stack trace (in some programming languages)

tracee.gloss: A program or a process that is being traced.

tracelet.gloss: A short fragment of the trace of execution of a computer program, used in automated systems that attempt to understand and optimize source code.

tracepoint.gloss: A kind of breakpoint that performs a custom action.

tracer.gloss: A process that traces something, such as the path of execution of a program during debugging.

traceroute.gloss: The route taken by packets over an IP network.
To measure the route taken by packets over an IP network and any delays in transit.

tracial.gloss: Of or pertaining to the trace of a projection.

traciator.gloss: A natural isomorphism of a functor (F) such that F(x⊗y)→F(y⊗x).

track.gloss: A circular (never-ending) data storage unit on a side of magnetic or optical disk, divided into sectors.
To create a musical recording (a track). To create music using tracker software.

trackback.gloss: A method to keep track of links to content, especially blog entries.

trackball.gloss: A pointing device consisting of a ball housed in a socket

trackbar.gloss: A widget allowing the user to select a value on a sliding scale.

tracker.gloss: A type of computer software for composing music by aligning notes or samples on parallel timelines.
A musician who writes music in a tracker.
A computer program that monitors something.
A computer program that monitors something. Server software that coordinates peers in the BitTorrent protocol.

trackerscene.gloss: The informal subculture that produces and shares music composed in tracker software.

trackloader.gloss: A custom software loading technique that streams data directly from the tracks of a floppy disk, bypassing the operating system.

trackmo.gloss: A demo that is loaded directly from the physical tracks of a floppy disk instead of loading through the file system.
A demo whose visual effects follow a set timeline synchronized with a continuous soundtrack, much like a music video.

trackpoint.gloss: An individual record within a GPS of a visited location.

trackwheel.gloss: A small wheel, incorporated into a mouse or smartphone, that controls scrolling.

tractable.gloss: Sufficiently operationalizable or useful to allow a mathematical calculation to proceed toward a solution.
Algorithmically solvable fast enough to be practically relevant, typically in polynomial time.

tractricoid.gloss: A surface formed by revolving a tractrix about its asymptote.

tractrix.gloss: A curve that satisfies the following property: that segment of the tangent line that lies between the point of tangency and a fixed line has length independent of the point of tangency chosen.

traffic light.gloss: In Conway's Game of Life, an arrangement of four blinkers that are orthogonally equidistant from a central point.

trail.gloss: A walk in which all the edges are distinct.

trailer.gloss: The final record of a list of data items, often identified by a key field with an otherwise invalid value that sorts last alphabetically (e.g., “ZZZZZ”) or numerically (“99999”); especially common in the context of punched cards, where the final card is called a trailer card.
The last part of a packet, often containing a check sequence.

train.gloss: Connected sequence of people or things. A software release schedule.

train track.gloss: A set of curves lying in a surface, meeting one another at their respective endpoints in a specific way that resembles railroad tracks.

training.gloss: The process by which two modems determine which protocol and speed to use; handshaking.

trajectoid.gloss: A solid shape that traces a periodic trajectory when rolled down a slope.

tramp data.gloss: Data which is passed via one function to another, and not otherwise used by the first.

trampoline.gloss: Any of a variety of looping or jumping instructions in specific programming languages.
Any of a variety of indirection techniques in specific programming languages.
To rewrite (computer code) to use trampoline instructions.

transaction.gloss: An atomic operation; a message, data modification, or other procedure that is guaranteed to perform completely or not at all (e.g. a database transaction).

transaction time.gloss: The time during which a fact stored in the database, represented by all the information in a row, is considered to be true and in effect.

transactional memory.gloss: A concurrency control mechanism analogous to database transactions for controlling access to shared memory.

transactionality.gloss: The degree to which a database or other system is transactional.

transceiver.gloss: A device that performs transmitting and receiving functions, especially if using common components.

transcendence.gloss: The property of being a transcendental number.

transcendence degree.gloss: Given a field extension L / K, the largest cardinality of an algebraically independent subset of L over K.

transcendental.gloss: Of an element of an extension field: not algebraic, that is, not the root of any polynomial that has positive degree and rational coefficients; also, of an extension field: that contains elements which are not algebraic.
Of a function or number: not algebraic.
A thing which is transcendental (all adjective senses). An element of an extension field, an extension field, a function, or a number which is not algebraic.

transcendental function.gloss: Any function that is algebraically independent of its variable(s); a function which does not satisfy a polynomial equation whose coefficients are themselves polynomials.
A meromorphic function on the complex plane that is not a rational function.

transcendental number.gloss: any irrational number that is not an algebraic number

transcendental number theory.gloss: The branch of number theory that deals with transcendental numbers.

transclude.gloss: To replace a template or other input with its rendered text, such as when parsing wikitext.

transclusion.gloss: The inclusion of part of one hypertext document in another one by means of reference rather than copying.

transcompilation.gloss: The translation of source code in one programming language into source code for another programming language.

transcompiler.gloss: A translating compiler that takes the source code of a programming language as its input and outputs the source code into either another programming language or an older version of the same language.

transcribe.gloss: To transfer data from one recording medium to another.

transcriber.gloss: A device or program that transcribes data.

transdimensional.gloss: Applicable to multiple dimensionalities; Having components or subspaces of different dimension.

transducer.gloss: A state machine that generates output based on a given input.

transduction.gloss: Particularly in the discipline of artificial intelligence, a form of inference, according to which the response appropriate to a particular known case, also is appropriate to another particular case diagnosed to be functionally identical. This contrasts with induction, in which general rules derived from past observations are applied to future cases as a class (compare also analogy).

The improvement of an electronic logic network by reduction of redundant components in an initial version, using an established pruning procedure, then applying permissible functions for transformation of the network into a workable form. Thereafter the transformation and reduction may be repeated till no worthwhile further improvement results.

transfer function.gloss: a mathematical representation of the relation between the input and output of a linear time-invariant system

transfinite induction.gloss: An extension of mathematical induction to well-ordered sets of transfinite cardinality, such as sets of ordinal numbers or cardinal numbers.

transfinite number.gloss: Any cardinal or ordinal number which is larger than any finite, i.e. natural number; often represented by the Hebrew letter aleph (ℵ) with a subscript 0, 1, etc.

transflection.gloss: A transfiguration consisting of reflection about a line combined with translation along the same line.

transflective.gloss: Of a liquid crystal display: that reflects and transmits light.

transform.gloss: To subject to a transformation; to change into another form without altering the value.
An operation (often an integration) that converts one function into another.

transformation.gloss: The replacement of the variables in an algebraic expression by their values in terms of another set of variables; a mapping of one space onto another or onto itself; a function that changes the position or direction of the axes of a coordinate system.

transformation matrix.gloss: A matrix (of dimension n×m) that represents some linear transformation from ℝᵐ→ℝⁿ.

transient.gloss: having a positive probability of being left and never being visited again.
A module that generally remains in memory only for a short time.

transiso.gloss: Pertaining to a graph on a finite group whose vertices are the subgroups of a specified order and for which two vertices are adjacent if the sets of all normalized right transversals for each corresponding subgroup contain at least one common element.

transition function.gloss: A function from (state, input symbol) to state describing what state to move to on receiving a given input in a given state.

transition matrix.gloss: A square matrix whose rows consist of nonnegative real numbers, with each row summing to 1. Used to describe the transitions of a Markov chain; its element in the ith row and jth column describes the probability of moving from state i to state j in one time step.

transitive.gloss: Having the property that if an element a is related to b and b is related to c, then a is necessarily related to c.
qualifiers: of a relation on a set

transitive.gloss: Such that, for any two elements of the acted-upon set, some group element maps the first to the second.
Such that, for any two vertices there exists an automorphism which maps one to the other.
Of a set of dice: not having the intransitive property.

transitive closure.gloss: The smallest binary relation on X that includes R and is transitive.
qualifiers: of a binary relation R on a set X

transitive closure.gloss: The smallest transitive set that contains X.

transitive dependency.gloss: An attribute of a relation that depends on a key but also on a third attribute which is not a key; this is a violation of third normal form.
In a computer program, library called by another dependency.

transitive set.gloss: Any set X such that for any x ∈ X, if y ∈ x then y ∈ X; equivalently, such that if x ∈ X and x is not an urelement then x ⊆ X.

transjective.gloss: Corresponding to shifts of preprojective and preinjective modules.

translate.gloss: Senses relating to a change of position. To move (something) from one place or position to another; to transfer. In Euclidean geometry: to transform (a geometric figure or space) by moving every point by the same distance in a given direction.

Senses relating to a change of position. To move (something) from one place or position to another; to transfer. To map (the axes in a coordinate system) to parallel axes in another coordinate system some distance away.
In Euclidean spaces: a set of points obtained by adding a given fixed vector to each point of a given set.

translation.gloss: The act of translating, in its various senses: A motion or compulsion to motion in a straight line without rotation or other deformation.

The act of translating, in its various senses: A relation between two mathematical figures such as a straight line where the coordinates of each point in one figure is a constant added to the coordinates of a corresponding point in the other figure.

translational bioinformatics.gloss: The branch of bioinformatics that uses genomic data as its source

translationary.gloss: Pertaining to the shifting of coordinate axes.

translator.gloss: A person or thing that translates meaning from one language into another, particularly A machine that converts inputs into a pattern of holes on a punch card.
A person or thing that translates meaning from one language into another, particularly A program that converts commands from one computer language into another.

translogarithmic.gloss: Describing functions that are both transcendental and logarithmic

transmission function.gloss: The mathematical function of an electromagnetic wave is a measure of the change undergone by the amplitude of the wave as it propagates in a given direction, which is also called the propagation constant.

transmission time.gloss: The amount of time from the beginning until the end of a message transmission.

transmoding.gloss: Conversion of one media form to another, for example text to audio.

transnormal.gloss: Having the property that for any pair of points (x, y) in a Riemannian manifold where x belongs to the normal subspace at y, the normal subspaces at points x and y coincide.

transnormalization.gloss: The transformation of raw data such that the resulting cumulative distribution is normal.

transnumeration.gloss: The transformation of numerical data in a meaningful way, for example by representing it in a table or graph.

transparency.gloss: Sufficient accuracy to make the compressed result perceptually indistinguishable from the uncompressed input.

transparent.gloss: Having the property of transparency, i.e. sufficiently accurate that the compressed result is perceptually indistinguishable from the uncompressed input.
Not noticeable because it happens automatically or in the background; invisible.

transpose.gloss: To move (a term) from one side of an algebraic equation to the other, reversing the sign of the term.
To rearrange elements in a matrix, by interchanging their respective row and column positional indicators.
To reverse the direction of every edge of (a graph).
Created by transposing a specified matrix.
Created by transposing a specified graph.
The matrix derived from performing a transpose operation on a given matrix.
A graph whose every edge has had its direction reversed.
The process of rearranging elements in a matrix, by interchanging their respective row and column positional indicators.

transposition.gloss: The act or process of transposing or interchanging.

transposition cipher.gloss: An encryption method that rearranges the order of the plaintext letters.

transputer.gloss: A single chip with CPU, memory and communications capability, used in grids to form parallel processing computers.

transrecursive.gloss: Being or relating to a type of operator used in hypercomputation.

transseries.gloss: A series (sequence of partial sums of a given sequence) in which members of the sequence from which the series is defined are defined by a transcendental function.

transvectant.gloss: An invariant formed from n invariants in n variables using Cayley's Ω process.

transvection.gloss: A kind of linear mapping which leaves all points on one axis fixed, while other points are shifted parallel to the axis by a distance proportional to their perpendicular distance from the axis

transversal.gloss: A line which traverses or intersects any system of other lines transversely. A line intersecting a pair of parallel lines.
A set containing one member from each of a collection of disjoint sets.

transversality.gloss: A property of two intersecting submanifolds, where at every intersection point, their separate tangent spaces at that point together generate the tangent space of the ambient manifold at that point.

transverse.gloss: (of an intersection) Not tangent, so that a nondegenerate angle is formed between the two things intersecting. (For the general definition, see Transversality (mathematics) on Wikipedia.Wikipedia )
The longer, or transverse, axis of an ellipse.

trap.gloss: An exception generated by the processor or by an external event.
To capture (e.g. an error) in order to handle or process it.

trapdoor.gloss: A secret method of obtaining access to a program or online system; a backdoor.
The special information that permits the inverse of a trapdoor function to be easily computed.
To subvert (a cryptographic scheme) by means of a secret parameter that makes the trapdoor function easy to compute.

trapdoor function.gloss: A function that is easy to compute in one direction but difficult to compute in the opposite direction (finding its inverse) without special information.

trapezium.gloss: A quadrilateral with two sides parallel.
A quadrilateral with two sides parallel. A quadrilateral with two sides parallel and two sides non-parallel.
A four-sided polygon with no parallel sides and no sides equal; a simple convex irregular quadrilateral.

trapezohedron.gloss: Any of a class of polyhedra that have kite-shaped faces and are dual polyhedra of antiprisms.

trapezoid.gloss: A (convex) quadrilateral with two (non-adjacent) parallel sides.
A convex quadrilateral with no sides parallel.

trapezoidal rule.gloss: A method of finding an approximate value for a definite integral, based on dividing the area under the graph of the function into a series of strips, each of which is approximately a trapezoid, and summing the area of all the trapezoids to approximate the area.

trash.gloss: Temporary storage on disk for files that the user has deleted, allowing them to be recovered if necessary.

trashbox.gloss: An electronic folder for deleted electronic mail.

travelling salesman problem.gloss: The problem in combinatorial optimization in which, given a number of cities and the costs of travelling from one to the other, it is required to determine the cheapest route that visits each city once and then returns to the initial city.

traversable.gloss: Any object that can be navigated by traversal.

traverse.gloss: A line lying across a figure or other lines; a transversal.
To visit all parts of; to explore thoroughly.

tray.gloss: A notification area used for icons and alerts.
A type of retail or wholesale packaging for CPUs where the processors are sold in bulk and/or with minimal packaging.

trbl.gloss: Acronym of top, right, bottom, left, the order in which the sides of elements are defined.

treap.gloss: A type of randomized binary search tree where nodes are labelled with randomly chosen priority values and which is simultaneously a heap on those priorities.

tree.gloss: A connected graph with no cycles or, if the graph is finite, equivalently a connected graph with n vertices and n−1 edges.
A recursive data structure in which each node has zero or more nodes as children, but does not share children with other nodes.
A display or listing of entries or elements such that there are primary and secondary entries shown, usually linked by drawn lines or by indenting to the right.
An extremely fast-growing function based on Kruskal's tree theorem.

tree diagram.gloss: A visual representation used to represent a probability space.

tree kernel.gloss: A tree data structure based on the more general concept of the positive-definite kernel, used in the parsing and classification of sentences.

tree shaking.gloss: In JavaScript, automatic dead code elimination during the build.

tree-maker.gloss: A software program that constructs family trees.

treeable.gloss: That can be represented as a tree (graph)

treebank.gloss: A database (corpus) of sentences which are annotated with syntactic information, often in the form of a tree.
To parse and annotate sentences according to a treebank.

treelength.gloss: A measure of the size or complexity of a tree.

treelist.gloss: A user interface control that displays a list of items in an expandable hierarchy.
A list of trees (the data structure).

treeness.gloss: The condition of being a tree; acyclicity and connectedness.

treeplot.gloss: A graphical representation of a tree (data structure)

treespace.gloss: A space whose components are trees.

treetope.gloss: A multi-dimensional generalisation of a roofless polyhedron

treewidth.gloss: The width (maximum number of nodes or leaves at any level) of a tree.

trefoil knot.gloss: A knot formed by joining the two loose ends of a overhand knot to form a knotted loop; the simplest non-trivial knot.

trellis.gloss: A kind of graph, used in communication theory and encryption, whose nodes are ordered into vertical slices by time, with each node at each time connected to at least one node at an earlier and at least one node at a later time.

trend.gloss: A line drawn on a graph that approximates the trend of a number of disparate points; the shift over time represented by such a curve on a graph.

trendlessness.gloss: The absence of any particular trend.

triacontadigon.gloss: A polygon with thirty-two sides and thirty-two angles.

triacontakaitetragon.gloss: A polygon with thirty-four sides and thirty-four angles.

triacontatetragon.gloss: A polygon with thirty-four sides and thirty-four angles.

triadic.gloss: Of or relating to a triad. Having an arity of three; taking three arguments or operands.

triage.gloss: The process of prioritizing bugs to be fixed.

triakis icosahedron.gloss: A Catalan solid with 60 isosceles triangle faces, 90 edges and 32 vertices, being the dual of the truncated dodecahedron.

triakis octahedron.gloss: A Catalan solid with 24 isosceles triangle faces, 36 edges and 14 vertices, being the dual of the truncated cube.

triakis tetrahedron.gloss: A Catalan solid with 12 isosceles triangle faces, being the dual of the truncated tetrahedron.

trial division.gloss: A simple method of finding the divisors of an integer, or establishing if the integer is prime, by selecting a set of smaller integers and seeing if there is a zero remainder upon division by each one

triality.gloss: A relationship between three vector spaces.

triamond.gloss: A polyiamond made up of three triangles.

triangle.gloss: A polygon with three sides and three angles.

triangle group.gloss: A group that can be realized geometrically by sequences of reflections across the sides of a triangle.

triangle inequality.gloss: The inequality that states that the magnitude of the sum of two vectors is less than or equal to the sum of the magnitudes of the vectors.
The inequality that states that the distance between two points is less than or equal to the sum of the distances between the first two points and some third point.
Either of the above two inequalities, considered as one of the axioms which a function must satisfy to be a norm or metric respectively.

triangle postulate.gloss: An axiom that states that the sum of the angles in a triangle equals two right angles, equivalent to the parallel postulate.

triangle wave.gloss: A function or waveform that alternately ramps linearly upwards and then downwards.

triangle-free.gloss: Of an undirected graph in which no three vertices form a triangle of edges.

triangular hebesphenorotunda.gloss: A polyhedron, one of the Johnson solids, whose faces are composed of 13 triangles, 3 squares, 3 pentagons, and 1 hexagon.

triangular matrix.gloss: A square matrix in which all the items on one side of the main diagonal are zero.

triangular number.gloss: Any integer that is the sum of n natural numbers from 1 to n.

triangulation.gloss: A subdivision of a planar object into triangles, and by extension the subdivision of a higher-dimension geometric object into simplices.

triangulo-triangular.gloss: Being or relating to a pentatope number.

triaugmented.gloss: Having a square pyramid attached to each of three equatorial faces.

triaxial.gloss: Having three planes of symmetry (e.g. having the shape of a scalene ellipsoid) and thus two axes of rotation

triaxial ellipsoid.gloss: An ellipsoid whose three perpendicular axes of symmetry each have unique lengths.

tribool.gloss: A variable that behaves similar to a Boolean, but allows three values instead of two.

tribrid modeller.gloss: A CAD system that is capable of modelling three-dimensional objects as combinations of surfaces, solids and polygons

tricategorical.gloss: Of or pertaining to a tricategory.

tricategory.gloss: A 3-dimensional category, continuing the pattern of bicategory.

trichotomous.gloss: Such that, for all x and y in X, and for a binary relation R, exactly one of xRy, yRx or x=y holds.

trichotomy.gloss: the property of an order relation whereby, given an ordered pair of elements (of a given algebraic structure), exactly one of these is true: the first element is 'less than' the second one, the second is 'less than' the first, or the two elements are equal.

triclustering.gloss: The simultaneous clustering of three independent rows or columns of a three-dimensional matrix

tricomplex number.gloss: The equivalent of a complex number in three dimensions

triconnected.gloss: Of a connected graph: needing three vertices removed for it to become disconnected.

tricuspal.gloss: Consisting of, or relating to, three cusps.

tricylinder.gloss: A solid formed by three intersecting cylinders.

tridecagon.gloss: A polygon having thirteen sides and thirteen angles.

tridecagonal.gloss: Having thirteen sides and angles, similar to a tridecagon.

trident.gloss: A curve of third order of the form

tridiagonal.gloss: Having nonzero elements only in the main diagonal and the diagonals directly above and below it.

tridiagonality.gloss: The condition (of a matrix) of being tridiagonal

tridiagonalization.gloss: The formation of a tridiagonal matrix

trie.gloss: An ordered tree data structure that is used to store an associative array where the keys are usually strings.

trifan.gloss: A set of triangles connected at a single point.

trifid cipher.gloss: A classical cipher that extends the earlier bifid cipher with the use of trigrams.

trigamma function.gloss: The second of the polygamma functions, after the digamma function.

trigger.gloss: An SQL procedure that may be initiated when a record is inserted, updated or deleted; typically used to maintain referential integrity.

trigintaduonion.gloss: A 32-dimensional hypercomplex number that is a nonassociative extension of a sedenion.

trigonometric.gloss: of, relating to, or constructed using trigonometry

trigonometric cofunction.gloss: Either of a pair of trigonometric functions that have equal values when their arguments are complementary angles, e.g. sine and cosine.

trigonometric function.gloss: Any function of an angle expressible as the ratio of two of the sides of a right triangle that has that angle (e.g., sine), or that subtracts 1 from such a ratio or subtracts such a ratio from 1 (e.g., coversed sine).

trigonometric identity.gloss: A trigonometric equation that is true for all values of the input variable for which both sides of the equation are defined.

trigonometric series.gloss: Any series of the form 1/2A_o+ displaystyle ∑ₙ₌₁ ᪲(A_n cos nx+B_n sin nx).

trigonometry.gloss: The branch of mathematics that deals with the relationships between the sides and angles of (in particular) right-angled triangles, as represented by the trigonometric functions, and with calculations based on said relationships.

trigram.gloss: An n-gram consisting of three items from a sequence.

trigraph.gloss: A three-character sequence used to enter a single conceptual character.

triharmonic.gloss: Describing a class of sixth-order partial differential equations which arises in areas of continuum mechanics

trihedral.gloss: Having three plane faces that meet at a common point

trihedron.gloss: A geometric figure composed of three planes meeting at a single vertex.

trihexagonal.gloss: Pertaining to a semiregular tiling of the Euclidean plane with two triangles and two hexagons alternating on each vertex.

trilemma.gloss: An argument containing three alternatives, jointly exhaustive either under any condition(s) or under all condition(s) consistent with the universe of discourse of that argument, that each imply the same conclusion.

trilinear.gloss: Linear (preserving linear combinations) in each variable.
qualifiers: of a function in three variables

trilinear.gloss: A triple (x, y, z) of the algebraic distances of a point to each side of a surrounding triangle

trilobular.gloss: Having a shape that is broadly triangular but is rounded, with three lobular segments conjoined.

trilogarithm.gloss: The form of polylogarithm having a base of three

trimagic.gloss: Of a magic cube: remaining magic even if all its numbers are replaced by their kth power for 1 ≤ k ≤ 3.

trimagic square.gloss: A magic square that remains magic when all of its numbers are replaced by their cubes.

trimean.gloss: A measure of a probability distribution's location defined as a weighted average of the distribution's median and its two quartiles.

trinarization.gloss: Conversion of a tree to one with at most three children per node

trinomial.gloss: An expression consisting of three terms.

triomino.gloss: Alternative form of tromino (“a polyomino consisting of three squares connected edge to edge”)

triple.gloss: A sequence of three elements or 3-tuple.

triple equals.gloss: The symbol ===, consisting of three consecutive equal signs.

triple fault.gloss: An exception thrown by the CPU while trying to handle a double fault, typically resulting in immediate rebooting.
To cause a triple fault to happen.

triple point.gloss: A point where a curve or surface intersects itself along three arcs.

triple-click.gloss: The action of pushing the button on a mouse three times in quick succession in order to perform a different task that would be performed from a single-click or double-click.
To push the button on a mouse three times in quick succession in order to perform a different task that would be performed from a single-click or double-click.

triplestore.gloss: A database designed for the storage and retrieval of RDF (Resource Description Framework) metadata in the form of triples representing predicates.

triprimality.gloss: The condition of being a triprime number

triprime.gloss: A number with exactly three prime factors.

trisect.gloss: to divide a quantity, angle etc into three equal parts

trisectability.gloss: Ability to be divided into three equal angles using a compass and straightedge.

trisectible.gloss: Able to be divided into three equal angles using a compass and straightedge.

trisection.gloss: The act of division of something (such as an angle, line segment, or circle) into three parts, especially three equal parts.

trisection point.gloss: Either of two points which trisect a given line segment.

trisector.gloss: A line or curve that trisects something.

Someone who believes to have found a way to construct an angle one-third the size of an arbitrary angle using only an unmarked straightedge and compass (this is known to be impossible; see Angle trisection § Proof of impossibility on WikipediaWikipedia ).

trispectrum.gloss: A certain type of statistic used to analyze nonlinear interactions

tristate.gloss: A variable, etc. that can take any of three distinct values.

tristrip.gloss: A strip formed by joining triangles.

trit.gloss: The ternary equivalent of a bit; a fundamental unit of information that may take any of three distinct states.

tritangent.gloss: A line that is tangent to a curve at three points.

trivariate.gloss: Having or involving exactly three variables.

trivial.gloss: Of, relating to, or being the simplest possible case.
Of, relating to, or being the simplest possible case. Containing only one element; having an underlying set which is a singleton.
qualifiers: of an algebraic structure or ideal thereof

trivial absolute value.gloss: An absolute value (or norm) for a field which is defined to be equal to one for any element of the field other than the field's zero, for which it is defined to be equal to zero.

trivial functional dependency.gloss: A functional dependency of an attribute on a superset of itself.

trivial group.gloss: The unique group (up to isomorphism) consisting of a single element (which is the identity element).

trivial solution.gloss: The answer ⃑x=⃑0 to a linear system A⃑x=⃑0.

trivial topology.gloss: A topology consisting only of the empty set and the underlying set.

trivialism.gloss: The theory that every proposition and its negation is true.

trivialist.gloss: A proponent of trivialism, the metaphysical and logical theory that all propositions are true.

trixel.gloss: A triangle assigned a single color based on the colors of the pixels inside it, used in medical imaging systems.

trochoid.gloss: The curve traced by a point on a circle as it rolls along a straight line

troglodyte.gloss: A person who chooses not to keep up to date with the latest software and hardware.

trojan.gloss: Malware that appears to perform or actually performs a desired task for a user while performing a harmful task without the user's knowledge or consent.
To infect (a system) with a trojan.

tromino.gloss: A polyomino consisting of three squares connected edge-to-edge.

trope.gloss: Mathematical senses. A tangent space meeting a quartic surface in a conic.
Mathematical senses. The reciprocal of a node on a surface.

tropical geometry.gloss: A recent branch of geometry that can be described as a piecewise linear version of real algebraic geometry.

troubleshooter.gloss: A software program or routine that attempts to diagnose a problem with the system.

true.gloss: Of the state in Boolean logic that indicates an affirmative or positive result.

true color.gloss: graphics with 24 bits of storage per pixel, allowing for up to 16,777,216 different colors

true lover's knot.gloss: A particular knot of eight crossings.

truel.gloss: A duel fought between three people.

truncate.gloss: To shorten (a decimal number) by removing trailing (or leading) digits.
To replace a corner by a plane (or to make a similar change to a crystal).

truncated cube.gloss: A polyhedron with eight triangular and six octagonal faces that is an Archimedean solid and can be constructed by truncating a cube at each vertex along each adjoining edge.

truncated cuboctahedron.gloss: An Archimedean solid that is isogonal and has twenty-six regular faces (twelve square, eight hexagonal and six octagonal); a great rhombicuboctahedron.

truncated dodecahedron.gloss: An Archimedean solid with thirty-two regular faces (twelve decagons and twenty triangles) and ninety edges.

truncated icosahedron.gloss: A polyhedron that has thirty-two faces (12 regular pentagons and 20 regular hexagons) and 60 vertices and 90 edges, and is one of the Archimedean solids.

truncated tetrahedron.gloss: A convex polyhedron, with four triangular and four hexagonal faces, that is an Archimedean solid and can be constructed by truncating a regular tetrahedron at each vertex by one-third the length of each adjoining edge.

truncation.gloss: The removal of the least significant digits from a decimal number.
An operation in any dimension that cuts a regular polytope at its vertices, creating a new facet in place of each vertex.

truncus.gloss: A curve in the Cartesian plane consisting of all points (x,y) satisfying an equation of the form f(x)=a/(x+b)²+c where a, b, and c are given constants.

trunk.gloss: In software projects under source control: the most current source tree, from which the latest unstable builds (so-called "trunk builds") are compiled.

trust.gloss: Affirmation of the access rights of a user of a computer system.

trust anchor.gloss: An authoritative entity that is assumed to be trustable.

trustless.gloss: Which does not need any trust, or a trusted third party.

trustlet.gloss: A trusted process or application in certain types of secure system.

truststore.gloss: A storage area for trusted cryptographic certificates issued by a certificate authority.

truth function.gloss: A Boolean function whose value is interpreted as truth or falsity

truth table.gloss: A table showing all possible truth values for an expression, derived from the truth values of its components.

truth tree.gloss: A variation of a truth table in which any node (representing a statement) has branches if and only if other statements (true or false) may be derived from it

truth value.gloss: A value indicating to what extent a statement is true; in classical logic, these are the values "true" and "false".

truth-functional.gloss: Of or relating to a truth function; having a truth value that depends solely on the truth values of its components.

truth-functional logic.gloss: The logic of truth-functional combinations of simple sentences; the branch of logic that investigates the properties that arguments, sentences, and sets of sentences have in virtue of their truth-functional structure.

truthiness.gloss: The property of being truthy, i.e. evaluating to true in a Boolean context.

truthset.gloss: A set of all true values

truthy.gloss: Evaluating to true in a Boolean context.

try.gloss: A block of code that may trigger exceptions the programmer expects to catch, usually demarcated by the keyword try.

tryte.gloss: The ternary equivalent of a byte.

tschirnhaus transformation.gloss: A type of mapping on polynomials that may be defined by means of field theory as the transformation on minimal polynomials implied by a different choice of primitive element.

tschirnhausen cubic.gloss: A plane curve defined, in its left-opening form, by the polar equation r=a sec ³(θ/3) where sec is the secant function.

tsr.gloss: Initialism of terminate and stay resident: a type of DOS program that can continue to run all the time, once it is loaded, even while other programs are running.

tss.gloss: Initialism of total sum of squares.

tst.gloss: Initialism of ternary search tree: a type of trie.

tty.gloss: A command line interface or terminal emulator.

tub file.gloss: A technique used to speed the generation of datafiles on a punch card, involving multiple copies of frequently used cards that were prepunched and stored in trays arranged by index.

tufu.gloss: Initialism of trust upon first use.

tui.gloss: Initialism of text-based user interface or terminal user interface.

tuio.gloss: Initialism of Tangible User Interface Objects.

tukey lambda distribution.gloss: A continuous, symmetric probability distribution defined in terms of its quantile function, typically used to identify an appropriate distribution.

tunable.gloss: A setting that can be configured.

tunnel.gloss: A wrapper for a protocol that cannot otherwise be used because it is unsupported, blocked, or insecure.
To transmit something through a tunnel (wrapper for an insecure or unsupported protocol).

tunnel broker.gloss: A service that provides a network tunnel.

tunneling.gloss: A feature of the file system that allows files to preserve certain properties, such as creation date, even after being deleted and recreated.

tupelize.gloss: To place data in a tuple.

tuple.gloss: A single row in a relational database.
A set of comma-separated values passed to a program or operating system as a parameter to a function call.
A fixed-size container data type similar to a list that can hold different types of elements.

tuply.gloss: in a way relating to tuples.

turbo.gloss: Causing or relating to increased speed.

turbofish.gloss: A syntactic element in Rust, ::<>, with arguments between < and >, that specifies the generic arguments of a function in an expression.

turboload.gloss: A software mechanism that loads data from cassette tape more rapidly than usual, saving time and making software piracy more difficult.

turing complete.gloss: Equivalent in power to a universal Turing machine; equivalently, functionally complete.

turing computable function.gloss: Any function whose value may be computed using a Turing machine.

turing degree.gloss: A measure of the level of algorithmic unsolvability of the decision problem of whether a given set of natural numbers contains any given number.

turing equivalent.gloss: Capable of computing precisely the same set of functions as a Turing machine can compute.

turing instability.gloss: The property of a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system in which a steady state that is stable in the corresponding nonspatial system is able to, under certain parameter constraints, become unstable in the spatial system containing a particular wavelength.

turing jump.gloss: In computability theory, an operation that assigns to each decision problem X a successively harder decision problem X′ with the property that X′ is not decidable by an oracle machine with an oracle for X.

turing machine.gloss: An abstract computing machine that has a finite number of possible internal states and operates on an infinite memory tape by first reading a symbol from a cell in the tape, and then, deterministically, based on that symbol and the machine’s state, writing a symbol in that cell, moving to a neighboring cell, and/or changing state.

turing pattern.gloss: A pattern, found in nature, that arises naturally and autonomously from a homogeneous, uniform state, through instability.

turing reduction.gloss: A reduction that solves a problem if the solution to another problem is already known, i.e. an algorithm that could be used to solve A if it had available to it a subroutine for solving B.

turing switch.gloss: A logical construction modelling the operation of the network switch, just as in theoretical computer science a Turing machine models the operation of a computer.

turing tape.gloss: The infinitely long memory tape on which a Turing machine would operate, consisting of individual cells that can be read or written.

turing tarpit.gloss: The situation in which a programming language is only minimally Turing complete, so that "everything is possible but nothing is easy".

turingery.gloss: A manual cryptanalysis technique used in breaking the Lorenz cipher during World War II, based on deducing the wheel settings of the machine that did the encryption.

turmite.gloss: A two-dimensional variant of a Turing machine in which the head has an orientation in addition to a position and state.

turn.gloss: A movement of an object about its own axis in one direction that continues until the object returns to its initial orientation. A unit of plane angle measurement based on this movement.

turn-by-turn navigation.gloss: A feature of GPS devices, particularly smartphones, that continuously gives directions as the person or vehicle approaches navigation points.

turnaround time.gloss: The amount of time required to complete a process or fulfill a request.

turning number.gloss: A version of winding number in which the number of rotations is counted with respect to the tangent of the curve rather than a fixed point.

turning point.gloss: A maximum or minimum on a graph.

turnstile.gloss: The ⊢ symbol used to represent logical entailment (deducibility relation), especially of the syntactic type; i.e., syntactic consequence. (Such symbol can be read as "prove(s)" or "give(s)". )

turtle.gloss: Senses resembling a turtle in shape or movement A type of robot having a domed case (and so resembling the reptile), used in education, especially for making line drawings by means of a computer program.
Senses resembling a turtle in shape or movement An on-screen cursor that serves the same function as a turtle for drawing.
Senses resembling a turtle in slowness A small element towards the end of a list of items to be bubble sorted, and thus tending to take a long time to be swapped into its correct position.

turtle graphics.gloss: Vector graphics generated by a turtle that moves according to relative coordinates on a Cartesian plane, as in the Logo programming language.

turán graph.gloss: A complete multipartite graph T(n,r) formed by partitioning a set of n vertices into r subsets, with sizes as equal as possible, and connecting two vertices by an edge if and only if they belong to different subsets.

tutorial.gloss: A video or text guide or instruction about a specific topic (generally a how-to).

tutte matrix.gloss: A matrix used to determine whether all of the edges of a graph can be traversed without visiting a vertex more than once.

tv tuner.gloss: A hardware component that allows a computer to receive television signals.

tv typewriter.gloss: A kind of video terminal that could be used with a standard television set.

tweak.gloss: An additional input to a block cipher, used in conjunction with the key to select the permutation computed by the cipher.

tweak freak.gloss: A person who modifies software or hardware in order to enhance its performance beyond their normal and acceptable standards.

tweakable.gloss: Of a block cipher: accepting a second input (the "tweak"), used in conjunction with the key to select the permutation computed by the cipher.

tweener.gloss: A person or thing that is between two categories, classes or age groups. A computing device that is smaller than a traditional laptop, but larger than a PDA.

twiddle.gloss: To flip or switch two adjacent bits (binary digits).
To be in an equivalence relation with.

twigil.gloss: A character prepended to a variable name to indicate its scope.

twin prime.gloss: Either of a pair of prime numbers that differ by two.

twip.gloss: A unit of measure equal to one twentieth of a point.

twist morphism.gloss: An isomorphism between a pair of products which have the same components but in swapped order, which isomorphism commutes with the two associated product diagrams.

twistor.gloss: Any of the complex-valued coordinates in twistor theory, which maps the geometric objects of conventional 3+1 space-time into geometric objects in a four-dimensional space, twistor space, with metric signature (2,2), a proposed path to a theory of quantum gravity.

twistorian.gloss: A mathematician who specializes in twistor theory.

twisty.gloss: A collapsible element having a marker such as a small triangle that rotates between horizontal and vertical positions to indicate whether the content is currently hidden or expanded.

twit.gloss: To ignore or kill file (a user on a bulletin board system).

two seconds to black.gloss: The situation where a computer monitor displays a correct screen image when first switched on, but then quickly blanks out, typically associated with capacitor problems.

two's complement.gloss: The number obtained by complementing every bit of a given number and adding one. A number and its complement add to 2ⁿ, where n is the word size of the machine.

The convention by which bit patterns with high bit 0 represent positive numbers from 0 to 2ⁿ⁻¹-1 directly, while bit patterns with high bit 1 represent negative numbers from −1 to -2ⁿ⁻¹, n being the word size of the machine, and the numeric complement of a number is its two's complement.

two-norm.gloss: A measure of length given by "the square root of the squares." Denoted by ||·||₂, the two-norm of a vector ⃑v= is ||⃑v||₂=√(a_1²+a_2²+⋯+a_n²). The two norm of an m×m matrix A is defined by max _(⃑v≠⃑0)(||A⃑v||₂)/(||⃑v||₂) where ⃑v is an m-dimensional vector that is not the zero vector.

two-sided.gloss: Whose salient properties apply when (the specified object) appears on either side of a given binary operator.
That is necessarily or absolutely different than the respective coordinate alethic or temporal modality as well as its opposite.

two-sided ideal.gloss: A subset of a ring which is both a left ideal and a right ideal. Commonly referred to simply as an ideal, but referred to as two-sided ideal for emphasis.

two-start.gloss: Describing a double spiral that starts at the origin and divides the plane into two
Describing a construction of two helices that wrap around the same cylinder; if infinite, would divide the surface of the cylinder into two

two-way.gloss: Of a table, etc., having or involving exactly two variables; bivariate.

tychonoff space.gloss: Any completely regular topological space that is also a Hausdorff space.

type.gloss: A tag attached to variables and values used in determining which kinds of value can be used in which situations.

A part of the partition of the object domain of a logical theory (which due to the existence of such partition, would be called a typed theory). (Note: this corresponds to the notion of "data type" in computing theory.)

type class.gloss: A type system construct that supports ad hoc polymorphism (independent of the type hierarchy), first pioneered in Haskell.

type coercion.gloss: changing an entity from one data type to another according to explicit or implicit rules.

type conversion.gloss: changing an entity from one datatype to another according to explicit or implicit rules.

type erasure.gloss: A compile-time process by which explicit data type annotations are removed from a program, before run-time execution.

type hint.gloss: An instance of type hinting: the specification of a data type in an otherwise untyped language.
