type hinting.gloss: The specification of data types in an otherwise untyped language, to indicate variables having a particular type.

type i error.gloss: Rejecting the null hypothesis when the null hypothesis is true.

type ii error.gloss: Accepting the null hypothesis when the null hypothesis is false.

type inference.gloss: The automatic deduction of the type of an expression in a programming language.

type juggling.gloss: In the PHP programming language, the automatic treatment of variables as a certain data type depending on the context in which they are used.

type punning.gloss: The circumvention of the system of data types in a programming language in order to achieve an effect that would be difficult or impossible to achieve within the bounds of the formal language.

type safety.gloss: The extent to which a programming language is type-safe.

type system.gloss: A way programming language classifies values and expressions into types (data types), how it can manipulate those types, and how they interact.

type theory.gloss: A branch of mathematical logic and theoretical computer science concerned with types.

type-in.gloss: A program listing, printed in a magazine, etc., to be inputted and run by the reader.

type-safe.gloss: Not susceptible to the class of programming errors that could lead to items of one data type being incorrectly treated as another type.

typeahead.gloss: A feature of computer software (and some typewriters) that enables the user to continue typing regardless of program or computer operation, the keystrokes being queued as necessary when the system is busy.

typecast.gloss: The modification of the data type of a variable or object.
To cast (change of data type of a variable or object).

typecheck.gloss: To verify whether a given value belongs to a certain data type.

typechecker.gloss: A system or algorithm that verifies values against their required data types, according to the type system of the language.

typechecking.gloss: The process of verifying whether a given value belongs to a certain data type.

typedef.gloss: A statement that declares a name for a data type.
A name that has been declared by such a statement.

typeful.gloss: Not typeless; having the concept of types; typed.

typelessness.gloss: The state or condition of being typeless; lack of fixed data types.

typescript.gloss: A file containing a replay of commands typed into a terminal, which can then be automatically typed by a program later on.

typestate.gloss: Information stored with a variable indicating its current data type.

typewriter-paired.gloss: Of a keyboard: having the layout of shifted keys corresponding to those of electric typewriters.

typing.gloss: Assignment or classification by type. The assignment of data types for variables.

t₂.gloss: Such that any two points have disjoint neighborhoods.

u-substitution.gloss: A method of integration in which a function of a variable is replaced with a new variable, conventionally called u.

uae.gloss: Initialism of unrecoverable application error (the standard Microsoft Windows error message in Win16)

uaf.gloss: Initialism of use after free: a class of software vulnerability where memory is erroneously used again after being deallocated.

ub.gloss: Initialism of undefined behavior, behavior not defined in the language standard.

ubuntero.gloss: A user of the Ubuntu operating system.

ucaas.gloss: Acronym of unified communications as a service.

ucas.gloss: Initialism of uncrewed combat aerial system, unmanned combat aerial system, uncrewed combat aircraft system, or, unmanned combat aircraft system

ucav.gloss: Initialism of unmanned/uncrewed combat aerial vehicle.

uce.gloss: Initialism of unsolicited commercial email; spam.

ufcs.gloss: Initialism of Uniform Function Call Syntax.

uiid.gloss: Initialism of unique instrument interface document.

ulam spiral.gloss: A graphical depiction of the set of prime numbers, constructed by writing the positive integers in a square spiral and specially marking the primes.

ulp.gloss: The value that the least significant digit of a floating-point number represents, used as a measure of accuracy in numeric calculations.

ultrabook.gloss: A very lightweight and thin portable computer the areal size of a notebook computer or subnotebook.

ultradifferentiable.gloss: Having all derivatives over an open set bounded by an indexed value in an ultradistribution (times a constant).

ultradifferential.gloss: A generalization of a differential that is calculated over an ultradistribution.

ultradiscrete.gloss: Describing any discrete system whose dependent variables also take discrete values

ultradiscretization.gloss: The transformation of a discrete system into an ultradiscrete one

ultraelliptic.gloss: Being or relating to a kind of hyperelliptic line integral involving a polynomial of degree 5 or 6.

ultrafilter.gloss: A proper filter which has a law of dichotomy for complements.
A filter (subset of a poset) that is maximal as a set with respect to the definition of proper filter.

ultrafinitism.gloss: A form of finitism that is even more extreme in that it denies those constructs whose construction cannot be physically performed (such as a number that no human could have time to calculate).

ultrafunction.gloss: A type of generalized non-Archimedean function

ultragraph.gloss: A generalization of a directed graph in which the source of an edge is a set of vertices rather than a single vertex.

ultraholomorphic.gloss: Holomorphic and such that all derivatives are uniformly bounded by a constant multiple of the argument that can be associated with the order of the derivative.

ultrahomogeneous.gloss: Such that every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures extends to an automorphism of itself.

ultralocal.gloss: Whose properties are influenced by its immediate neighbours only

ultramatricial.gloss: Isomorphic to a countable direct limit of matricial algebras.

ultrametric.gloss: Describing a metric whose triangle inequality has the stronger form d(x,z)< max d(x,y),d(y,z).

ultrametrics.gloss: The study and use of ultrametric systems

ultrapeer.gloss: In a peer-to-peer network, a peer capable of routing requests and responses from others rather than always adopting a direct client-server connection.

ultrapolynomial.gloss: A power series in several variables P:Kᵈ→K (with K a field) of the form P(x)=Σ_(α∈ℕᵈ)c_αx^α whose coefficients are bounded in some specific sense.

ultrapower.gloss: The special case of an ultraproduct where all factors are equal.

ultraproduct.gloss: A quotient of the direct product of a family of structures

ultraradical.gloss: A root of the polynomial x⁵ + x + a, where a is a complex number.

ultrasparsifier.gloss: A form of sparsifier that makes a graph particularly sparse.

ultraspherical.gloss: Related to or involving a Gegenbauer polynomial.

ultratotal.gloss: That quantifies more than the total quantity.

umbilical.gloss: Such that the curvatures of normal sections are all equal to each other.

umbilicus.gloss: One of the foci of an ellipse or other curve.
A point of a surface at which the curvatures of the normal sections are all equal to each other.

umbra.gloss: An element of the umbral calculus.

umbral.gloss: Of or relating to umbral calculus.

umbral calculus.gloss: An area of study around the surprising similarity between seemingly unrelated polynomial equations and certain shadowy techniques used to "prove" them.

umbral moonshine.gloss: A mysterious connection between Niemeier lattices and Ramanujan's mock theta functions; a generalization of the Mathieu moonshine phenomenon connecting representations of the Mathieu group M24 with K3 surfaces.

unacked.gloss: Not having been sent an ACK message (acknowledgement of a packet or a message received from a network).

unacquire.gloss: To lose or get rid of; reverse the possession or acquisition of; unget

unaddress.gloss: To delete or forget the address of some entity.

unadvertisement.gloss: The withdrawal of an earlier notification.

unadvise.gloss: To instruct the system to cease providing internal notifications of some kind.

unanchor.gloss: To release from a fixed position and allow to be moved.

unapply.gloss: To undo an apply operation; to remove (something previously applied).

unapprove.gloss: To rescind the approval of something; to mark as no longer approved; reject.

unarc.gloss: To extract (a file) from a compressed archive in ARC (file format).

unarchive.gloss: To extract from a digital archive.
To remove from an archived state.

unarchiver.gloss: A program or algorithm that unarchives.

unarion.gloss: An element in the bottom level of associative composition algebra, which is an element in a field

unary.gloss: Of an operation, function, procedure, or logic gate, taking exactly one operand, argument, parameter, or input; having domain of dimension 1.
The unary, or bijective base-1, numeral system.
Unary coding, an entropy encoding for natural numbers.

unary operation.gloss: An operation taking one operand, such as the square, factorial or absolute value operation.

unary operator.gloss: A symbol representing unary operation; an operator taking one operand.

unassign.gloss: To remove or undo the assignment of.

unassigned.gloss: Without a value assigned to it.

unassociate.gloss: To remove an association (of e.g. a computer with a network, or a file type with an application program); to disassociate.

unassociated.gloss: Not associated, as: Having no statistical association.

unattended installation.gloss: An installation that does not require user interaction.

unauthorize.gloss: To withdraw authorization or permissions from.

unauthorized term.gloss: A term discouraged by a controlled vocabulary in favor of its authorized synonym, such as pitch in favor of frequency.

unbalanced.gloss: of an expression having different numbers of left and right parentheses

unbatch.gloss: To split a batch into parts

unbind.gloss: To disable some kind of connection in software, such as a key binding.

unbinned.gloss: Not divided into bins (intervals into which data is placed)

unbless.gloss: To convert (a previously blessed object) back to a simple reference.

unblind.gloss: To convert (a blind signature) back to the unblinded state (as opposed to the blinded state).

unbox.gloss: To retrieve (a value of a primitive type) from the object in which it is boxed.

unbrick.gloss: To repair a device that was bricked (rendered inoperative).

unbrickable.gloss: Unable to be bricked (rendered inoperative through incorrect configuration).

unbuffer.gloss: To release or flush from a buffer.

unbuffered.gloss: That operates without a hardware or software buffer.

uncanny valley.gloss: A range of appearances, mannerisms, or behaviors of a humanoid figure that are subtly different from a human and thereby cause feelings of discomfort, such as fear or revulsion.

uncastable.gloss: That cannot be cast (converted to other data types).

uncertainty.gloss: A parameter that measures the dispersion of a range of measured values.

unchecked.gloss: Of a check box: not checked (ticked or enabled).

unchecked exception.gloss: An exception that is not declared in the signature of a method, but results in an abort with a stack trace.

uncia.gloss: A numerical coefficient in a binomial.

unclose.gloss: To undo the act of closing; to restore (something closed).

uncode.gloss: To remove the code or coding from.

uncolorable.gloss: That cannot be colored with fewer than a specified number of colors

uncomment.gloss: To convert (text that has been commented out) back into source code so that it will no longer be ignored by the compiler or interpreter.

uncommit.gloss: To undo a change that had been applied.

uncommitted.gloss: Not yet written to disk and logged.
qualifiers: of an update to a database etc.

uncompress.gloss: To restore a compressed file to its normal size.

unconcatenate.gloss: To undo the process of concatenation.

unconditional.gloss: A conditional-like structure expressing that the consequent holds true regardless of the particular value of the antecedent.

unconfidence.gloss: The complement of confidence; the probability that something is not the case.

uncook.gloss: To repair (an MP3 audio file) that has been damaged ("cooked") by being converted through a text format and having line breaks applied to it.

uncountable.gloss: Incapable of being put into one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers or any subset thereof.

uncountable set.gloss: A set, containing infinite number of elements, whose elements can not be mapped one-to-one to the natural numbers. A set with a cardinality greater than that of the set of natural numbers.

uncountably.gloss: In a way that is incapable of being put into one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers or any subset thereof.

uncrop.gloss: To undo the cropping of (an image).

uncurry.gloss: To reverse the operation of currying.

undecagon.gloss: A polygon with eleven sides and eleven angles.

undecic.gloss: Of the eleventh order or degree

undecidable.gloss: Incapable of being algorithmically decided in finite time. For example, a set of strings is undecidable if it is impossible to program a computer (even one with infinite memory) to determine whether or not specified strings are included.

(of a WFF) logically independent from the axioms of a given theory; i.e., that it can never be either proved or disproved (i.e., have its negation proved) on the basis of the axioms of the given theory. (Note: this latter definition is independent of any time bounds or computability issues, i.e., more Platonic.)

undeclaration.gloss: The act of undeclaring something previously declared.

undeclare.gloss: To revoke the declaration of (a variable, namespace, etc.) so that it is no longer available.

undefine.gloss: To remove the definition of; to return to an undefined state.

undefined.gloss: That does not have a logically sound meaning within a specific formal system and is thus not assigned an interpretation.
That behaves unreliably due to dependence on an uninitialized value or inconsistently ported code.

undelete.gloss: To recover (a file, record, etc.) from a deleted state; restore.

undeploy.gloss: To undo the deployment of; to revert to a state prior to deployment of.

underactuate.gloss: To make less easily actuated or responsive.

underarc.gloss: In a two-dimensional knot diagram, any arc which crosses under another segment of the knot.

underbound.gloss: To provide a lower bound to.

underclock.gloss: To modify (a CPU) by the use of underclocking.

underclocking.gloss: The deliberate reduction of the speed of a CPU, often to reduce power consumption.

undercomment.gloss: To annotate (code) with too few comments.

undercommented.gloss: Having inadequate documentation in the form of comments in source code.

undercomplete.gloss: Describing a frame (in linear algebra) having a set of functions less than a basis

undercoverage.gloss: Insufficient coverage (inadequate representation in a sample)

undercross.gloss: The strand or segment in a knot diagram that passes beneath another at a crossing; i.e., the under‑crossing strand in a knot projection. As distinguished from the overcrossing or over‑strand in knot projections

utility program.gloss: Any of a large range of software, often included with the operating system, that runs specific tasks associated with the computer or its environment.

uudecode.gloss: To decode (previously uuencoded data) back into its original binary form.

uuencode.gloss: To encode (binary data) into a text-based format for transmission.

uuoc.gloss: Initialism of useless use of cat, a usage of the cat command which can be avoided.

uv.gloss: The axes of a two-dimensional texture, as opposed to those (X, Y, Z) of the three-dimensional model to which it is applied.

vaccine.gloss: A software program which protects computers against, or detects and neutralizes, computer viruses and other types of malware; an antivirus.

vacuous truth.gloss: A proposition which is true only because it is a conditional statement with a necessarily false premise, or which asserts a property of all elements of an empty domain of discourse.

vacuously.gloss: Because of being a vacuous truth.

vacuum.gloss: To optimise a database or database table by physically removing deleted tuples.

valence.gloss: For a correspondence T on a curve: a number k such that the divisors T(P)+kP are all linearly equivalent.

valency.gloss: The number of edges connected to a vertex in a graph.

valid.gloss: Of a formula or system: such that it evaluates to true regardless of the input values.
Of an argument: whose conclusion is always true whenever its premises are true.

valid time.gloss: The time period during which a database fact is valid in the modeled reality.

valuation.gloss: An assignment of truth values to propositional variables, with a corresponding assignment of truth values to all propositional formulas with those variables (obtained through the recursive application of truth-valued functions corresponding to the logical connectives making up those formulas).
A structure, and the corresponding assignment of a truth value to each sentence in the language for that structure.
A measure of size or multiplicity.
A map from the class of open sets of a topological space to the set of positive real numbers including infinity.

valuation function.gloss: A function which assigns a truth value to every well-formed formula, which is identical to the model's interpretation function when applied to atomic propositions, and which otherwise assigns a truth value recursively depending on the formula's top logical connective and the truth values of the subformulae surrounding that logical connective.

valuation ring.gloss: An integral domain D such that for every element x of its field of fractions F, at least one of x or x⁻¹ belongs to D.

value.gloss: Any definite numerical quantity or other mathematical object, determined by being measured, computed, or otherwise defined.

value restriction.gloss: In a functional language, inference of a polymorphic type only for syntactic values (values that can be evaluated at compile time) to ensure that a program is type-safe.

value type.gloss: A data type that represents a value directly, rather than a pointer or reference to something else.
A data type having deep-copy semantics.

valueness.gloss: The quality of being a value or a value type.

vampire number.gloss: A composite natural number with an even number of digits that can be factored into two natural numbers (called "fangs") each with half as many digits as the original number, and where the two factors contain precisely all the digits of the original number, in any order, counting multiplicity.

van emde boas tree.gloss: A tree data structure that implements an associative array with keys of up to m bits. It can perform all operations in a time proportional to the log of the size of its largest element, or equivalently with an upper bound equal to the logarithm of 2 multiplied by m.

vanishing fraction.gloss: A fraction which reduces to the form 0/0 for a particular value of the variable which enters it, usually in consequence of the existence of a common factor in both terms of the fraction, which factor becomes 0 for this particular value of the variable.

vanishing ideal.gloss: An ideal consisting of all polynomials (belonging to a certain polynomial ring) which zero out within a given algebraic variety.

vaporware.gloss: An advertised product, often computer software, the launch of which has not happened yet and might not ever happen.

vararg.gloss: Any of the arguments to a variadic function.

varchar.gloss: A text field of indeterminate length in a database, as opposed to the traditional fixed-length field.

varentropy.gloss: The variance of the surprisal of a random variable; a measure of uncertainty in the amount of information provided by knowing the value of the random variable (usually in units such as bits).

variabilize.gloss: Rewrite (a database query, etc.) as a variable.

variable.gloss: A quantity that may assume any one of a set of values.
A named memory location in which a program can store intermediate results and from which it can read them.

variable binding.gloss: the association between a variable name (identifier) and its value.

variable-length array.gloss: An array whose length is determined by a variable at run time.

variadic.gloss: Taking a variable number of arguments; especially, taking arbitrarily many arguments.
A function that takes a variable number of arguments.

variance.gloss: The second central moment in probability; the square of the standard deviation.

variant.gloss: A variable that can hold any of various unrelated data types.

variation.gloss: An infinitesimal perturbation applied to a function, typically denoted δf, used to probe how a functional changes.
The corresponding first-order change in a functional induced by such a perturbation, typically denoted δJ[f] and called the first variation.

variation ratio.gloss: the proportion of cases not in the mode

variety.gloss: A collection or number of different things. In universal algebra: an equational class; the class of all algebraic structures of a given signature, satisfying a given set of identities.

A collection or number of different things. Ellipsis of algebraic variety (“the set of solutions of a given system of polynomial equations over the real or complex numbers; any of certain generalisations of such a set that preserves the geometric intuition implicit in the original definition”).

variety of algebras.gloss: Synonym of variety (“an equational class in universal algebra”).

varifold.gloss: A certain generalization of a differentiable manifold

varignon parallelogram.gloss: The parallelogram involved in Varignon's theorem, whose corners are the midpoints of the sides of an arbitrary quadrilateral.

varimax.gloss: Describing a rotation that maximizes the sum of the variances of the squared loadings, often used in surveys to see how groupings of questions measure the same concept.

variogram.gloss: A function of the spatial dependence of variance; a graph of this function

varray.gloss: An array whose number of elements can vary, up to a pre-defined maximum.

varying.gloss: A kind of variable, used by a fragment shader, that interpolates values across a primitive, so as to produce gradient effects etc.

vaultable.gloss: Able to be stored in a vault.

vaxherd.gloss: A sysadmin who works with VAX computers.

vaxocentrism.gloss: The incorrect assumption that certain behaviours and memory storage conventions of the VAX (a computer system of the 1970s) are applicable on all computer architectures.

vber.gloss: A programmer who uses the Visual Basic language.

vector.gloss: A directed quantity, one with both magnitude and direction; the signed difference between two points.
A directed quantity, one with both magnitude and direction; the signed difference between two points. Any member of a (generalized) vector space.

A directed quantity, one with both magnitude and direction; the signed difference between two points. An ordered tuple, originally one representing a directed quantity, but by extension any one-dimensional matrix.
A directed quantity, one with both magnitude and direction; the signed difference between two points. A chosen course or direction for motion, as of an aircraft.
A kind of dynamically resizable array.

A kind of dynamically resizable array. A memory address containing the address of a code entry point, usually one which is part of a table and often one that is dereferenced and jumped to during the execution of an interrupt.
A kind of dynamically resizable array. A graphical representation using outlines; vector graphics.
To redirect to a vector, or code entry point.

vector algebra.gloss: The branch of mathematics that deals with vectors and operations on them.

vector bundle.gloss: A fiber bundle for which the fiber is a vector space.

vector calculus.gloss: The branch of mathematics that covers the differentiation and integration of vector fields, primarily in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

vector clock.gloss: An array of logical clocks used to determine the partial order of events in a distributed system and detect causality violations.

vector field.gloss: a function mapping a subset of ℝⁿ into a subset of ℝⁿ

vector function.gloss: Any function whose range is n-dimensional

vector graphics.gloss: Geometrical primitives based upon mathematical equations to represent images in computer graphics, contrasted with raster graphics.

vector image.gloss: An image file where the image’s elements (such as lines, circles and subimages) are stored as individual objects, as opposed to a raster or bitmap which stores the image’s pixels.

vector product.gloss: a vector with the size given by the product of two vectors computed as the product of the magnitudes of the vectors and the sine of the angle between their directions, and directed perpendicular to the given two vectors, with positive orientation.

vector space.gloss: A set of elements called vectors, together with some field and operations called addition (mapping two vectors to a vector) and scalar multiplication (mapping a vector and an element in the field to a vector), satisfying a list of constraints; equivalently, a module over a field.

vector sum.gloss: The vector whose initial and final points are those of a series of other vectors laid end to end.

vectorial.gloss: Of or pertaining to a vector.

vectorize.gloss: To convert an image into a vector graphics format.
To convert a program that operates on scalar values into the equivalent program operating on vectors, usually as an optimization step inside the compiler (automatic vectorization).

vectorlike.gloss: Having some characteristics of a vector.

vee.gloss: A unit of vertical spacing, typically corresponding to the height of an ordinary line of text.

vel.gloss: The ∨ symbol used to represent the inclusive or, which is a logical connective.

velary.gloss: Relating to a curve representing the motion of a sail blown by the wind.

velct.gloss: Abbreviation of Velocity Energy-efficient and Link-aware Cluster-Tree, a cluster and tree based topology management protocol for mobile wireless sensor networks (MWSNs).

vend.gloss: To provide or export functionality, especially from an API.

vendor.gloss: To bundle third-party dependencies with the source code for one's own program.
As the software vendor, to bundle one's own, possibly modified version of dependencies with a standard program.

venn diagram.gloss: A diagram representing some sets by contours of closed shapes, such as circles or ellipses (and sometimes also the universal set as a rectangle enclosing all of these shapes), and indicating the relationships between the sets: by overlapping the shapes to show that the corresponding sets have a non-empty intersection, and by possibly (but not necessarily) enclosing all of the sets (which are proper subsets of the universal set) within a universal set (represented typically by a rectangle); such that the total number of simply connected regions is 2ⁿ, where n is the number of depicted sets which are proper subsets of the universal set.

ventile.gloss: Any of the nineteen points that divide an ordered distribution into twenty parts, each containing one twentieth of the population.
Any one of the twenty groups so divided.

verb.gloss: A named command that performs a specific operation on an object.

verbose.gloss: Producing detailed output for diagnostic purposes.

verifiable.gloss: A statement or observation that can be verified.

verification.gloss: The operation of testing the equation of a problem, to see whether it truly expresses the conditions of the problem.

verifier.gloss: A device used to verify that a punched card had been punched correctly.

verlet integration.gloss: A numerical method used to integrate Newton's equations of motion, frequently used to calculate trajectories of particles in molecular dynamics simulations and computer graphics.

verlet list.gloss: A data structure in molecular dynamics simulations that can efficiently maintain a list of all particles within a given cut-off distance of each other.

veronese embedding.gloss: The embedding of the projective plane given by the complete linear system of conics.

veronese surface.gloss: An algebraic surface in five-dimensional projective space, realized by the Veronese embedding.

veronese variety.gloss: A generalization of the Veronese surface to higher dimensions.

versal.gloss: An ornamental letter that begins a section.

versatile.gloss: Having varied uses or many functions.

version.gloss: A particular revision (of software, firmware, CPU, etc.).
To keep track of (a file, document, etc.) in a versioning system.

version control.gloss: A system responsible for managing modifications and additions to digital works, giving each revision a time-stamp and showing its difference to the previous revision.

version number.gloss: A unique number or set of numbers assigned to a specific version of software, firmware, file, etc.

versioned.gloss: Subject to versioning; of which more than one version may be stored.

versioned object base.gloss: An individual database in the versioning software ClearCase.

versioning.gloss: The use of versions as a means of distinguishing similar items.

versionitis.gloss: A situation in which there are many different (and possibly incompatible) versions of the same software, file or document.

versionless.gloss: Without a version or versions; not associated with a specific version of something.

vertex.gloss: An angular point of a polygon, polyhedron or higher order polytope. The common point of the two rays that form an angle.
An angular point of a polygon, polyhedron or higher order polytope. The point at which an axis meets a curve or surface.
A point on the curve with a local minimum or maximum of curvature.
One of the elements of a graph joined or not by edges to other vertices.
A point in 3D space, usually given in terms of its Cartesian coordinates.

vertex angle.gloss: An angle associated with a vertex of an n-dimensional polytope.

vertex cover.gloss: a set of vertices which touch all the edges of a graph

vertex figure.gloss: The figure exposed when a corner of a polyhedron or polytope is sliced off.

vertex form.gloss: a quadratic equation in the form y=a(x-h)²+k

vertical alignment.gloss: A style of liquid crystal display (LCD) that is naturally stored in an upright vertical position, producing a black image until an electrical current is introduced.

vertical angle.gloss: Any of the opposite angles formed by intersecting lines (and hence, meeting at their vertices).
The angle at the apex of an isosceles triangle or cone.

vertical mouse.gloss: A computer mouse that stands upright, with buttons on the side, designed to reduce strain on the user's wrist.

very-large-scale.gloss: Of a system, containing hundreds of thousands of transistors on a single integrated circuit.

vexillary permutation.gloss: A permutation μ of the positive integers containing no subpermutation isomorphic to the permutation (2143); in other words, there do not exist four numbers i < j < k < l with μ(j) < μ(i) < μ(l) < μ(k).

vfat.gloss: Initialism of virtual file allocation table: the method used by Windows 9x and Windows NT to allow the use of long filenames on FAT16 and FAT32 file systems while still providing 8.3 aliases of these filenames for backwards compatibility with systems not supporting long filenames.

vhd.gloss: Initialism of video high density, a videodisc format.
Initialism of virtual hard disk, a disk image file format used by Microsoft Virtual PC.
Initialism of volumetric haptic display, a display that about informs touch instead of vision.

vibe.gloss: To vibe code; to accomplish with the help of generative AI.

vibe coder.gloss: Someone who generates source code by repeatedly prompting a large language model, and has a very limited awareness of how the code actually functions; someone who engages in vibe coding.

vibe coding.gloss: A method of programming in which a developer generates code by repeatedly prompting a large language model, while having a very limited awareness of how the code actually functions.

vibe debugging.gloss: The debugging of program code by repeatedly prompting a large language model, while having a very limited awareness of how the code actually functions.

vibecode.gloss: To program by repeatedly prompting a large language model rather than understanding how the code functions.

vicious circle.gloss: A fallacy in which the premise is used to prove a conclusion which is then used to prove the premise.

video board.gloss: A board that outputs video to a screen; a graphics card.

video card.gloss: A piece of hardware installed into a personal computer to allow it to send video signals to an external output device such as a monitor or projector.

video shifter.gloss: A device in a computer that takes video data from the CPU and converts it to a serial bitstream in order to generate an output signal.

view.gloss: A virtual or logical table composed of the result set of a query in relational databases.
The part of a computer program which is visible to the user and can be interacted with.

view model.gloss: A framework that defines a coherent set of views to be used in the construction of an enterprise architecture, software architecture, or system architecture.
An abstraction of a view, especially in the context of the MVVM architectural pattern.

viewer.gloss: A program that displays the contents of a file.

viewlet.gloss: In certain content management systems, a region of a page where customizable content can be rendered.

viewport.gloss: A typically rectangular region representing the range or area currently visible (within a window, screen, etc.).
To clip (an image or region) so that it fits in a viewport.

vigintile.gloss: Any of the values in a series that divides the distribution of individuals in that series into twenty groups of equal frequency.

vignette.gloss: A hardware deficiency (even occurring in most expensive models) of a computer display wherein the picture slants towards a colour or brightness towards the edges especially if viewed from an angle.

vincentization.gloss: The technique of averaging three or more subjects' estimated or elicited quantile functions in order to define group quantiles from which F can be constructed.

vinculum.gloss: A horizontal line placed over a complex number or expression to denote its complex conjugate.
A horizontal line drawn over two letters to denote the line segment joining them.
A horizontal line placed over a symbol or expression to denote logical negation (complement).

viral.gloss: Of the nature of an informatic virus; able to spread copies of itself to other computers.

virtual.gloss: Operating using a computer and/or online rather than physically present.
Simulated in a computer and/or online.
Of a class member: capable of being overridden with a different implementation in a subclass.
A virtual (adjective sense 3.3) member function of a class.

virtual 8086 mode.gloss: A mode allowing the execution of real mode applications that are incapable of running directly in protected mode while the processor is running a protected mode operating system.

virtual address.gloss: The identification of a location in virtual memory that is mapped by the operating system into a location in real storage and thus appears to an application program to be an absolute address.

virtual data room.gloss: A data room that is accessible online by connecting remotely.

virtual desktop.gloss: A desktop (visual workspace) offering more space than the physical screen would usually allow, controlled either by scrolling or by switching between screenfuls.

virtual disk.gloss: A file, such as a RAM disk or disk image, that emulates a physical disk.

virtual drive.gloss: A software component that emulates a physical disk drive.

virtual machine.gloss: A software emulation of a computer that runs in an isolated partition of a real computer.
A computer system that is implemented in software rather than hardware and that runs bytecode.

virtual memory.gloss: An abstraction implemented by hardware and the operating system that allows a process to access a virtual address space, such as one that is larger than the available physical memory, by translating virtual addresses to physical memory locations.

virtual piano.gloss: An online software application designed to simulate playing a piano (or other keyboard instrument) on a personal computer, mobile device or a tablet computer.

virtual private network.gloss: A network set up for use by a limited number of individuals, such as employees of a company, operating over a large area. The network typically uses encryption to keep information secure.

virtual private server.gloss: A virtualized server cohosted with other virtual server instances on the same hardware.

virtual reality.gloss: A computer technology that simulates a real or imagined environment so that the user can interact with it as if physically present.

virtualist.gloss: An artist who specializes in art on the Internet or in virtual reality.

virtualization.gloss: Creating a virtual version of common computing hardware at the same abstraction level.

virtualize.gloss: To run a program in virtual storage.
To simulate (or make virtual) some effect or condition on a computer.

virtually.gloss: Of a subgroup of finite index.
Of a covering space of finite degree.

virus.gloss: A type of malware which can covertly transmit itself between computers via networks (especially the Internet) or removable storage such as disks by inserting its code into other executable files, often causing damage to systems and data; also computer virus.

visibility.gloss: The scope within which a variable, function, etc. is able to be accessed directly.

visitor.gloss: The object in the visitor pattern that performs an operation on the elements of a structure one by one.

visitor pattern.gloss: A behavioural design pattern that separates an algorithm from an object structure on which it operates.

visual angle.gloss: The angle formed by two rays of light, or two straight lines drawn from the extreme points of an object to the center of the eye.

visual programming language.gloss: A programming language that lets users create programs by manipulating program elements graphically rather than by writing code.

visual servoing.gloss: The control of a robot by using visual feedback.

vlan.gloss: Initialism of virtual local area network.

vlb.gloss: Initialism of VESA Local Bus, an expansion bus for i486 PCs.

vliw.gloss: Initialism of very long instruction word: an explicitly created set of processor instructions to be executed simultaneously.

voice assistant.gloss: A computer program that performs general tasks by responding to voice commands.

voice command.gloss: A spoken instruction to a computer.

void.gloss: Of a function or method, that does not return a value; being a procedure rather than a function.

voigt notation.gloss: A means of representing a symmetric tensor by reducing its order.

volatile.gloss: Of a variable etc., having its associated memory immediately updated with any changes in value.
Of memory, whose content is lost when the computer is powered down.
A variable that is volatile, i.e. has its associated memory immediately updated with any change in value.

volatile memory.gloss: Computer memory (such as RAM) that requires a constant electrical charge to maintain its contents.

volatility.gloss: The state of not retaining data in the absence of power.

voldemort type.gloss: A data type that is unspeakable.

volterra integral equation.gloss: A special kind of integral equation, having applications in demography, the study of viscoelastic materials, and actuarial science.

volume.gloss: An accessible storage area with a single file system, typically resident on a single partition of a hard disk.
The sum of the degrees of a set of vertices.

von neumann architecture.gloss: A computer architecture that uses the same buses to access both program instructions and data on which to be operated.

von neumann machine.gloss: A computer that implements the von Neumann architecture.

von neumann neighborhood.gloss: A neighborhood on a 2D square lattice consisting of a cell and its four orthogonal neighbors.

voodoo programming.gloss: A slapdash approach to programming involving guesswork or plagiarism rather than proper analysis and comprehension.

voronoi diagram.gloss: A diagram that assigns a set of points in a plane to an equal number of cells, such that each point p is inside a cell consisting of all regions closer to p than to any other point.

voronoi formula.gloss: An equality involving Fourier coefficients of automorphic forms, with the coefficients twisted by additive characters on either side.

voronoi pole.gloss: The vertices in a Voronoi diagram that are farthest from the point defining a cell.

vorticity.gloss: A property of a fluid flow related to local angular rotation; defined as the curl of the flow's velocity field.

votesheet.gloss: A form to be filled in by voters to indicate their preference among various choices in various categories.

voxel.gloss: The three-dimensional analogue of a pixel; a volume element representing some numerical quantity, such as the color, of a point in three-dimensional space, used in the visualization and analysis of three-dimensional (especially scientific and medical) data.

voxelate.gloss: To represent something as an array of voxels.

voxelization.gloss: The conversion of an image or model into voxels.

voxelize.gloss: To convert (an image or model) into voxels.

voxelscape.gloss: A three-dimensional landscape constructed from voxels.

voxmap.gloss: A three-dimensional array of voxels, analogous to a bitmap of pixels.

vram.gloss: Initialism of video random access memory (“random access memory used by graphics processing units”).
video memory (an area of a computer's memory used to hold data used by a graphics processing unit)
Initialism of Video RAM, a variant of DRAM invented in 1980 and used to store the framebuffer in some graphics adapters.

vsl.gloss: Initialism of Value of Statistical Life, a measure of the monetary value of reducing the statistical likelihood of death in a population by a given amount.

vtable.gloss: A table of memory pointers to different implementations of a virtual function.

vu meter.gloss: Any animated graphical representation of the volume of sound or music (often subdivided across channels).

vulnerability.gloss: A specific weakness in the protections or defences that (literally or figuratively) surround someone or something. A weakness which allows an attacker to reduce a system's security.

vulnerable.gloss: More likely to be exposed to malicious programs or viruses.

w-buffer.gloss: A kind of inverted z-buffer, storing inverse depth values, which has some advantages for interpolation and precision scaling.

w-shingling.gloss: In natural language processing, a set of unique "shingles" (contiguous subsequences of tokens in a document) that can be used to gauge the similarity of documents.

waas.gloss: Acronym of workplace as a service.

wabbit.gloss: A self-replicating computer process that (unlike a virus or worm) does not infect host programs or documents and remains on the local computer rather than spreading across networks of computers.

wad.gloss: Acronym of where's all the data?, commonly used when referring to the video game Doom.

wagon.gloss: A kind of prefix used in de Bruijn notation.

wai.gloss: Acronym of works as intended: current situation is what was intended and thus not subject to change.

wait state.gloss: Any of several instances in which a computer's processor cannot execute instructions (either for the entire computer, or just for a specific task) until an I/O operation completes, or until an interrupt is resolved.

wait-free.gloss: Involving no busy-wait loops or locks for synchronizing with other threads. Able to act immediately without waiting on others.

waiting time.gloss: The total amount of time in which a process spends in a ready queue before it reaches the CPU.

wake word.gloss: A word or phrase that activates a dormant device when spoken by the user.

wake-on-lan.gloss: A networking standard that allows a computer to be turned on or awakened by a network message.

wake-sleep algorithm.gloss: A certain unsupervised learning algorithm for neural networks, having separate "wake" and "sleep" phases that attempt to connect the layers of neurons in alternating directions.

wakelock.gloss: A lock that can be acquired by software for the purpose of preventing the mobile device from going into a locked standby state during a particular operation.

waker.gloss: In the Rust programming language, a handle that "wakes up" a task by notifying its executor that it is ready to be run.

wald test.gloss: A test that assesses constraints on statistical parameters based on the weighted distance between the unrestricted estimate and its hypothesized value under the null hypothesis, where the weight is the precision of the estimate.

walk.gloss: A sequence of alternating vertices and edges, where each edge's endpoints are the preceding and following vertices in the sequence. Compare path, trail.

walking skeleton.gloss: An initial, bare-bones implementation of a system or application which provides only the basic core functionality, in order to be able to demonstrate a minimal working product to be further fleshed out later.

walkthrough.gloss: The process of inspecting algorithms and source code by following paths through the algorithms or code as determined by input conditions and choices made along the way.

walktrap.gloss: An algorithm for identifying communities in large networks using random walks.

wall clock.gloss: The measure of wall time, the actual amount of time taken from the start to the end of an operation.

wall time.gloss: The actual time of day, as would be seen on a wall clock; contrasted with the (possibly inaccurate) time according to a computer system.
The actual amount of time taken from the start to the end of an operation, as opposed to CPU time, which only includes the periods of time during which the CPU was processing instructions.

wall-sun-sun prime.gloss: A (hypothetical) prime number p such that p² divides F_π(p), where F_n is the Fibonacci sequence and π(p) is the pth Pisano period (the period length of the Fibonacci sequence reduced modulo p).

wallace tree.gloss: An efficient hardware implementation of a digital circuit that multiplies two integers.

wallcrossing.gloss: A discontinuous change across a codimension wall of marginal stability.

wallpaper.gloss: An image or tiled pattern used as the background of a computer desktop.

wallpaper group.gloss: A mathematical group that classifies two-dimensional repeating patterns based on their symmetries.

walrus operator.gloss: The operator := that assigns values to variables in certain programming languages, such as Python.

walsh function.gloss: In harmonic analysis, any of a complete orthogonal set of functions that can be used to represent any discrete function.

wandering set.gloss: In dynamical systems and ergodic theory, a formalization of a certain idea of movement and mixing.

wang tile.gloss: A square tile with a colour on each side. Possible sets of such tiles are studied to determine whether they can tile the plane (arranged with like colours touching, and without rotations or reflections) and whether this can be done in a periodic pattern.

war.gloss: Initialism of write after read, a kind of data hazard.

wardialer.gloss: A program that dials every telephone number in a particular area searching for computers, or trying to guess passwords.

warm.gloss: To prepopulate (a cache) so that its contents are ready for other users.

warm boot.gloss: The restarting of a computer that was already running, rather than switched off.

wart.gloss: Any of the prefixes used in Hungarian notation.

warwalking.gloss: The act of walking around with a wireless device to find an access point for a wireless network.

wasd.gloss: A set of four keys on a keyboard used as directions to control player characters in certain video games. (W, A, S and D represent up, left, down and right, respectively.)

watchdog timer.gloss: An electronic or software timer used to detect and recover from computer malfunctions by generating a timeout signal if it is not periodically reset by the system.

watchpoint.gloss: A debugging mechanism whereby execution is suspended every time a specified memory location is modified; or, any of various similar such mechanisms.

waterfall model.gloss: A sequential software development process in which development is seen as flowing steadily downwards (like a waterfall) through the phases of requirements analysis, design, implementation, testing, integration, and maintenance.

watering hole attack.gloss: A computer attack strategy, in which the victim is a particular group (organization, industry, or region), and the attacker guesses or observes which websites the group often uses and infects one or more of them with malware.

watermark.gloss: A value stored in a datafile to ensure its integrity, so that if the file's contents are changed then the watermark will no longer match the contents.
A default hint caption displayed in a text box prior to the user inputting any text.

wave mechanics.gloss: The mathematical basis for quantum mechanics in which light and subatomic particles have the characteristics of both waves and particles.

wave vector.gloss: A vector whose direction is that of the direction of propagation of a wave, and whose magnitude is inversely proportional to its wavelength

wavefield.gloss: A mathematical description of the amplitude of a wave throughout such an area or space.

waveform.gloss: The shape of a wave function represented by a graph showing some dependent variable as function of an independent variable.

wavelet compression.gloss: A method of data compression, especially of images, that uses mathematical functions.

wavelet matrix.gloss: A type of data structure that represents a sequence of or the process of sorting elements while allowing query operations.

wavelet series.gloss: A wavelet-generated representation of a square-integrable function.

wavenumber.gloss: A measure of the number of waves in unit distance; inversely proportional to its wavelength.

waw.gloss: Initialism of write after write, a kind of data hazard.

weaire-phelan structure.gloss: A three-dimensional structure representing an idealized foam of equal-sized bubbles, with two different shapes.

weak.gloss: Having a narrow range of logical consequences; narrowly applicable. (Often contrasted with a strong statement which implies it.)

well-behavedness.gloss: The quality or condition of being well-behaved.

wellpowered.gloss: in which each object has only a set of pairwise nonisomorphic subobjects

wellsean.gloss: Having a structure within which both polygonality and connectivity are fractional.

whetstone.gloss: A single instruction of the Whetstone benchmark, often expressed as a value per second.

while loop.gloss: A section of computer code in which an instruction or group of instructions is repeated only while a certain condition continues to be met.

whisker.gloss: A graphic element that shows the maxima and minima in a box plot.

whiteness.gloss: The quality of being white noise.

whitenization.gloss: The calculation of a weighted average over all possible values of a quantity that is only known down to an interval, as opposed to a precise value.

whiteout.gloss: The simulated erasure of a file, etc. on a read-only volume.

whittle likelihood.gloss: An approximation to the likelihood function of a stationary Gaussian time series.

whnf.gloss: Initialism of weak head normal form.

widget.gloss: Any one of the components of a computer application's graphical user interface, such as a Cancel button or text input box that a user interacts with.

wiener filter.gloss: A filter that takes a statistical approach to filtering out noise that has corrupted a signal.

windowable.gloss: Capable of being displayed in a window.

windowed.gloss: Occupying only a part of the screen (in a window.)

windowing.gloss: The use of a graphical user interface divided into windows.

windowlike.gloss: Resembling a window (a rectangular area displaying the output of a program).

worklet.gloss: A small piece of functionality encapsulating a single task.

wormable.gloss: (of a computer flaw or a bug) Capable of being turned into a network worm.

wormhole.gloss: A location in a monitor program containing the address of a routine, allowing the user to substitute different functionality.

wpgma.gloss: Initialism of Weighted Pair Group Method with Arithmetic Mean.

wrap.gloss: To make functionality available through a software wrapper.

wrap around.gloss: To move (text or other content) to the beginning of the next line when unable to fit it at the end of the current line.

wrapping.gloss: The breaking of a section of text into lines so that it will fit into the available width of a display area.

wreath product.gloss: A combination of two groups based on their semidirect product, denoted as ≀.

write.gloss: To record data mechanically or electronically.

write blocker.gloss: A hardware device that allows a computer to read a peripheral such as a hard disk without making any changes to its contents, useful in cyberforensics etc.

write once, read many.gloss: A data storage device in which information, once written, cannot be modified.

write over.gloss: To save a piece of data in place of other data; to overwrite.

write-only.gloss: Capable of being written but not read.

wrong-endian.gloss: Stored in big-endian format on a little-endian machine, or vice versa.

wronskian.gloss: A determinant that is related to the linear independence of a set of solutions of a linear differential equation.

wtf.gloss: A bafflingly bad or unwise design decision.

wts.gloss: want to show (generally preceding a theorem that will subsequently be proved)

xacml.gloss: Initialism of eXtensible Access Control Markup Language.

xenobot.gloss: An artificial construct built from cells extracted from Xenopus embryos, and designed to move, consume, and build piles.

xps.gloss: Initialism of transmit packet steering, a scaling technique for network traffic processing.

xpu.gloss: Any unit of computing hardware designed to accelerate a particular workload, often used in artificial intelligence applications.

yottabyte.gloss: One septillion (10²⁴, or 1,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000) bytes or 1,000 zettabytes.

young diagram.gloss: A finite collection of boxes, or cells, arranged in left-justified rows, with the row lengths in non-increasing order. Listing the number of boxes in each row gives a partition λ of a non-negative integer n, the total number of boxes of the diagram.

young symmetrizer.gloss: An element of the group algebra of the symmetric group, constructed in such a way that, for the homomorphism from the group algebra to the endomorphisms of a vector space V^(⊗n) obtained from the action of S_n on V^(⊗n) by permutation of indices, the image of the endomorphism determined by that element corresponds to an irreducible representation of the symmetric group over the complex numbers.

young tableau.gloss: A diagram obtained by filling in the boxes of the Young diagram with symbols from some alphabet, usually required to be a totally ordered set.

your mileage may vary.gloss: It may work differently in your situation, or be different in your experience.

yp.gloss: Initialism of Yellow Pages, a network protocol invented by Sun Microsystems.

z score.gloss: The number of standard deviation units away from the mean a particular value of data lies.

z-axis.gloss: The axis on a graph of at least three dimensions that is usually drawn vertically and usually shows the range of values of a variable dependent on two other variables or the third independent variable.

z-buffer.gloss: A buffer for the purpose of tracking the relative depths of different objects in a scene and determining which are closer to the observer than others.

z-culling.gloss: The elimination of certain objects from the display that should not be rendered because they are behind objects that are closer to the viewer.

z-direction.gloss: The direction aligned with the z-axis of a coordinate system.

z-fighting.gloss: A phenomenon in three-dimensional rendering where two or more primitives have similar values in the z-buffer, causing flickering as one is displayed varyingly behind or in front of the other.

z-intercept.gloss: A point at which a line crosses the z-axis of a Cartesian grid.

z-order.gloss: The order in which objects should be drawn in order to display correctly.
A property of a graphical object that indicates its position in the z-order.

z-test.gloss: Any statistical test for which the distribution of the test statistic under the null hypothesis can be approximated by a normal distribution.
A comparison to determine which object should be at the front of the z-buffer.

z-transform.gloss: A transform that converts a discrete time-domain signal into a complex frequency-domain representation.

zariski topology.gloss: Originally, a topology applicable to algebraic varieties, such that the closed sets are the variety's algebraic subvarieties; later, a generalisation in which the topological space is the set of prime ideals of a commutative ring and is called the spectrum of the ring.

zariski-riemann space.gloss: A locally ringed space of a subring k of a field K, whose points are valuation rings containing k and contained in K. They generalize the Riemann surface of a complex curve.

zebibyte.gloss: Strictly, 2⁷⁰ (1024⁷, 1,180,591,620,717,411,303,424) bytes or 2¹⁰ (1024) exbibytes, as opposed to a zettabyte.

zeddy.gloss: The Sinclair ZX81, an early British home computer.

zeno.gloss: Requiring or involving an infinite number of intervals within a finite time.

zeno machine.gloss: A hypothetical computational model, related to Turing machines, that would be capable of carrying out computations involving a countably infinite number of algorithmic steps.

zenzizenzic.gloss: The fourth power of a number; the biquadrate.

zenzizenzizenzic.gloss: The eighth power of a number.

zenzizenzizenzizenzike.gloss: The sixteenth power of a number.

zequals.gloss: A technique for simplifying mental approximations by reducing each number to one significant figure followed by zeroes.
Is equal to, after performing such a reduction.

zermelo set theory.gloss: An early and influential axiomatisation of set theory.

zermelo-fraenkel set theory.gloss: An axiomatic system that was proposed in the early 20th century in order to formulate a theory of sets free from paradoxes such as Russell's paradox, and became the standard form of axiomatic set theory.

zermelo-fraenkelian.gloss: Of or relating to Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory.

zero.gloss: A value of the independent variables of a function, for which the function is equal to zero.
The additive identity element of a monoid or greater algebraic structure, particularly a group or ring.

zero crossing.gloss: A point where a function's graph intersects the x-axis, meaning the function's output (or sign) changes from positive to negative, or vice-versa, passing through zero; used in signal processing, electronics, and audio analysis for tasks like frequency measurement, noise reduction, and differentiating sound types, as it marks significant transitions in waveforms and data.

zero divisor.gloss: An element a of a ring R for which there exists some nonzero element x ∈ R such that either ax = 0 or xa = 0.
A nonzero element a of a ring R for which there exists some nonzero element x ∈ R such that either ax = 0 or xa = 0.

zero filling.gloss: The process of overwriting storage space, memory, or data arrays with binary zeros. (0s).

zero ideal.gloss: The ideal containing only the element zero.

zero locus.gloss: The set of points (usually in affine or projective space, but more generally in the domain of the function) where the given polynomial (or function) takes the value zero.

zero matrix.gloss: A matrix whose entries are all zero.

zero mode.gloss: An eigenvector that has a vanishingly small eigenvalue

zero morphism.gloss: A morphism which is both a constant morphism and a coconstant morphism.

zero object.gloss: An object which is both an initial object and a terminal object.

zero one infinity rule.gloss: The rule that a database, a user interface, etc. should allow for either zero, one, or an indefinite number of an entity.

zero out.gloss: To fill with zeros, replacing any previous contents.

zero vector.gloss: A vector 0 in a vector space V such that for any v∈V, 0+v=v; a vector whose value in every dimension is zero; i.e., ⃑0=<0,0,…,0>.

zero-based.gloss: Of an array or list: such the first element of the array or list is called the zeroth.

zero-day.gloss: Of warez, released less than a day after the official product release.

zero-dimensional.gloss: Having zero dimensions; having no extent in any direction.
Having a base consisting of clopen sets.

zero-knowledge.gloss: Describing situations in which the veracity of a statement may be shown to be true without revealing any other information.

zero-knowledge proof.gloss: An interactive method for one party to prove to another that a (usually mathematical) statement is true, without revealing anything other than the veracity of the statement.

zero-length.gloss: Having a length of zero; containing no elements, text characters, etc.

zero-one law.gloss: The fact that, in some circumstances, the probability of an event can only be zero or one and not any intermediate value.

zero-order hold.gloss: A mathematical model of the practical signal reconstruction done by a conventional digital-to-analog converter, describing the effect of converting a discrete-time signal to a continuous-time signal by holding each sample value for one sample interval.

zero-sum.gloss: Of a system, where all gains are offset by exactly equal losses.

zero-sum game.gloss: A game (or a similar political or economic system) in which the gains of some players must equal the losses of others.

zero-width.gloss: Adding no additional width to a line of text.

zeroaxial.gloss: Having an axis composed of zeroes.

zerogon.gloss: A hypothetical polygon with no vertices.

zerogonal.gloss: Of or pertaining to a zerogon.

zerohedron.gloss: A hypothetical polyhedron with no faces.

zeroization.gloss: The act or process of zeroizing. The erasure of sensitive parameters from a cryptographic module to prevent their disclosure if the equipment is captured.

zeroth.gloss: In the initial position in a sequence whose elements are numbered starting at zero; the ordinal number corresponding to zero.

zeta.gloss: A mathematical function, formally known as the Riemann zeta function.

zeta function.gloss: function of the complex variable s that analytically continues the sum of the infinite series ∑ₙ₌₁ ᪲1/(nˢ) that converges when the real part of s is greater than 1.

zeta value.gloss: The value of a particular zeta function

zetetics.gloss: A branch of algebra which relates to the direct search for unknown quantities.

zettabit.gloss: One sextillion (10²¹, or 1,000,000,000,000,000,000,000) bits or 1,000 exabits.

zettabyte.gloss: One sextillion (10²¹, or 1,000,000,000,000,000,000,000) bytes or 1,000 exabytes.

zeuthen-segre invariant.gloss: A certain invariant of complex projective surfaces.

zf.gloss: Initialism of Zermelo-Fraenkel (set theory): a particular axiomatic formulation of set theory without the axiom of choice.

zfc.gloss: Initialism of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with Choice; the standard axiomatization of set theory, including the axiom of choice.

zhegalkin polynomial.gloss: A Boolean-valued polynomial formed as a XOR-sum (or "ring sum") of conjunctions.

zigamorph.gloss: The text character with hexadecimal value 0xff, when used as a string separator or terminator.

ziggurat algorithm.gloss: An algorithm for pseudorandom number sampling, relying on an underlying source of uniformly-distributed random numbers as well as computed tables.

zilde.gloss: In the APL programming language, the symbol ⍬ (a zero crossed by a tilde), representing an empty numeric vector.

zinbiel algebra.gloss: The Koszul dual concept to a Leibniz algebra.

zip.gloss: Synonym of convolution (“a type of mapping function”).
To compress (one or more computer files) into a single and often smaller file, especially one in the ZIP format.
To subject to the convolution mapping function.

zip bomb.gloss: A malicious zip file designed to produce a very large output, and consume a great deal of processing resources, during decompression.

zip disk.gloss: A disk of the kind that can be read and written by a Zip drive.

zip drive.gloss: A storage device, similar to a floppy disk drive but using disks with a much larger capacity (100, 250, or 750 MB, compared to a normal floppy disk capacity of 1.44 MB).

zip up.gloss: To convert a computer file into a smaller package.

zipper.gloss: A technique for arbitrarily traversing an aggregate data structure and updating its contents. See zipper (data structure).

zoi.gloss: Initialism of Zero One Infinity, a rule of thumb in software suggesting that arbitrary limits on the number of entity instances are not allowed.

zombie.gloss: A process or task which has terminated but has not been removed from the list of processes, typically because it has an unresponsive parent process.
A computer affected by malware which causes it to do whatever the attacker wants it to do without the user's knowledge.

zombie client.gloss: Computer software that takes directions from a remote computer and uses the infected computer to perform malicious tasks as directed.

zombie computer.gloss: A computer connected to the Internet that has been compromised by a hacker by means of a computer virus, computer worm, or Trojan horse program and can be used to perform malicious tasks under the remote direction of the hacker.

zombie master.gloss: A command and control center that guides and directs a zombie computer or zombie network.

zombie network.gloss: A network or collection of compromised computers or hosts that are connected to the Internet.

zombie path.gloss: A path that is no longer valid or accessible because the target has been moved or deleted.

zombie process.gloss: A child process that has terminated but is still listed in the process table, having not yet been reaped by its parent process.

zombie program.gloss: Any computer program that has been revived or reinstalled by an operating system and is very difficult to uninstall.

zombie software.gloss: A program or application which has been maintained beyond its expiration date or end-of-life status.

zombie user.gloss: A logged in or registered user that should no longer exist but has not been fully deleted from the system.

zombied.gloss: In a zombie state (said either of a zombie process or of a computer covertly controlled by malware).

zombify.gloss: To take control of (a computer) in order to use it covertly and illicitly.

zone.gloss: That collection of a domain's DNS resource records, the domain and its subdomains, that are not delegated to another authority.
A logical group of network devices on AppleTalk (an obsolete networking protocol).
The curved surface of a frustum of a sphere, the portion of surface of a sphere delimited by parallel planes.

zone punch.gloss: A hole punched (normally in the top two or three positions) of a punched card in addition to another in order to designate a different (sometimes related) character or to add a plus or minus sign

zonogon.gloss: A polygon having an even number of sides and whose pairs of opposite sides are parallel and equal

zonohedron.gloss: A special case of convex polyhedron, in which every face of the polyhedron is a polygon with point symmetry.

zonoid.gloss: A limit of a vector sum of line segments

zonotope.gloss: A polytope formed by the Minkowski sum of a zonohedron's line segments in any dimension.

zonotopic.gloss: Of, pertaining to or composed of zonotopes.

zoom box.gloss: A clickable box that maximizes a window to fill the screen or (clicked a second time) restores the window to its previous size and position.

zroupoid.gloss: A generalization of a De Morgan algebra that defines a Boolean algebra using only implication and a constant.

zwnj.gloss: Initialism of zero-width non-joiner (“non-printing character used to avoid ligatures”).

étale.gloss: Such that the natural homomorphism is an isomorphism.

α-cut.gloss: An approach to transforming a fuzzy membership function into a basic belief assignment.

δ-box.gloss: A k-cell which is a Cartesian product of half-closed intervals which are closed at their infima and open at their suprema, and such that the infimum of each interval is the coordinate of a given point (called "the corner" of the δ-box), and the length (i.e., measure) of each interval is equal to (the given value) δ.

μ-completion.gloss: A σ-algebra which is obtained as a "completion" of a given σ-algebra, which includes all subsets of the given measure space which simultaneously contain a member of the given σ-algebra and are contained by a member of the given σ-algebra, as long as the contained and containing measurable sets have the same measure, in which case the subset in question is assigned a measure equal to the common measure of its contained and containing measurable sets (so the measure is also being completed, in parallel with the σ-algebra).

π-system.gloss: A non-empty collection of subsets of a given set Ώ that is closed under non-empty finite intersections.

σ-algebra.gloss: A collection of subsets of a given set, such that the empty set is part of this collection, the collection is closed under complements (with respect to the given set) and the collection is closed under countable unions.

σ-compact.gloss: That is expressible as a countable union of compact sets.
qualifiers: of a set in a topological space

σ-finite measure.gloss: A set, in a measurable space, that is expressible as a countable union of sets of finite measure.

ℝ-order tree.gloss: An order tree whose segments are homeomorphic to segments of the real line and that is the union of countably many segments.
